Violent clashes in North East Delhi, India, between Hindu and Muslim protesters over the Citizenship Amendment Act continues leaving 13 people dead and at least 150 injured.
Steve Hasker, former company president of American data firm Nielsen Holdings, is appointed CEO of Thomson Reuters effective March 15.

Bob Iger steps down as CEO of The Walt Disney Company, and is succeeded by Bob Chapek, former chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products. Iger will continue to serve the company's "creative endeavors" as executive chairman.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: 93 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in Italy, bringing the number to 322. Four more virus-related deaths are confirmed, bringing the death toll to eleven.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Two people from Lombardy, Italy, living in Austria's state of Tyrol, test positive for coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia
text: Croatia confirms its first case of coronavirus. The patient had stayed in Milan, Italy, from 19 to 21 February, and was hospitalised in Zagreb, Croatia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran's deputy health minister, Iraj Harirchi, tests positive for coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: A member of the Iranian Parliament, Mahmoud Sadeghi, states on Twitter that he has been infected with the virus.
sources: New York Times via MSN News

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Hundreds of guests are locked down in a hotel in Tenerife, Spain, after a visiting Italian doctor tested positive for the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The first case on the peninsula and the fourth in the country is confirmed in Barcelona, Catalonia. The wife of the Italian doctor becomes the fifth infected in Spain. A sixth case is reported in Villarreal.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland
text: Switzerland confirms its first case of coronavirus: a case in Ticino, on the border with Italy.
Algeria confirms its first case of the coronavirus. The patient is an Italian man who arrived in the country a week ago.
Canada's largest airline Air Canada suspends all flights to China until April in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The Swedish Foreign Ministry summons the Chinese ambassador after the Chinese government sentences bookseller and Swedish citizen Gui Minhai to ten years in prison for espionage.
A man was revealed to have been arrested the previous day for attempting to blow up a car in The Pentagon parking lot.
Aimee Anne Duffy, a Welsh singer who goes by Duffy, reveals she was raped, drugged and held hostage over some days resulting in her disappearance from the limelight in recent years.
German Health Minister Jens Spahn declines to run for leadership of the ruling Christian Democratic Union party, and endorses North Rhine-Westphalia Minister-President Armin Laschet for the position.

The Saudi government appoints former energy minister Khalid A. Al-Falih to head a new investment ministry replacing the General Investment Authority, and sacks the media minister, among other changes to the cabinet.

Former Liberal Democrats leader David Steel resigns from the party and announces he will leave the UK House of Lords after a report accused him of “abdicat[ing] his responsibility” when he supported the knighthood of former party whip Cyril Smith, who is accused of child molestation.
Violent clashes between Hindu and Muslim protesters over the Citizenship Amendment Act continue in North East Delhi, India, leaving 27 people dead and at least 180 injured.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey's MoD says two Turkish troops were killed in an airstrike in Syria's Idlib Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey's MoD claims 114 Syrian Army troops were "neutralized" in retaliation. An air defense system, a ZU-23-2 AA gun, an antitank weapon, 3 Tanks, an ammunition vehicle and 2 engineering vehicles were destroyed while 3 tanks were captured.
Bob Weighton, aged 111, of Alton, Hampshire, England, is named the oldest living man in the world after the death of Chitetsu Watanabe of Japan at the age of 112.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: 102 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in Italy, bringing the number to 424. Another virus-related death is confirmed, bringing the death toll in the country to 12.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: In Josefstadt, Vienna, students at Albertgasse high school have been prohibited from leaving the school after one of their instructors was flagged as potentially carrying the virus since he had recently returned from a trip to Northern Italy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: In California, San Francisco declares a public emergency. Santa Clara and San Diego counties have made similar declarations.
The first case in Latin America is confirmed by the Ministry of Health of Brazil in São Paulo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece confirms its first case in Thessaloniki.
Romania and Georgia report their first cases.
A 62-year-old man in Seville becomes the first non imported infected case of coronavirus in Spain.

Six prisoners are shot dead by Papua New Guinea Police as they escape from prison in Western Highlands Province. They were among 100 inmates who escaped during a mass breakout. Scores of others are captured.

Germany repeals its 2015 ban on advertisements for professional assisted suicide practices, after finding that its prohibition violated the German Constitution. Passive human euthanasia itself has been legal in the republic since 2014.

Six people, including the shooter, are killed in a mass shooting at the Molson Coors Beverage Company in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States. The perpetrator, who committed suicide, was an employee who was fired earlier in the day.

The re-election campaign of U.S. President Donald Trump files a libel suit against The New York Times over a 2019 editorial piece that accused the Trump campaign of striking a deal with Russia during the 2016 presidential election.

The Spanish and Catalan government meets for the first time after breaking the talks one year ago in the named "Dialogue Board" as a way to solve the constitutional and political crisis between both governments that erupted in 2017.

The U.S. House of Representatives votes 410–4 to pass the Emmett Till Antilynching Act, which designates lynching a federal crime. This is the first time that anti-lynching legislation has ever passed Congress.

Astronomers at the Catalina Sky Survey in Arizona, United States, say an object known as has been captured by Earth's gravitational field and has been in orbit since 2017, becoming a temporary natural satellite of Earth. The Minor Planet Center confirms the findings and says "no link to a known artificial object has been found", implying the object is an asteroid.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Syrian opposition groups backed by Turkey recapture the strategic city of Saraqib, lift the siege on four Turkish observation points and cut the M5 highway.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: A Turkish sniper kills a Syrian lieutenant colonel in Syria's Tell Abyad countryside.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Three Turkish soldiers are killed in Syrian Army attacks in Idlib, bringing the number of Turkish soldiers killed in Syria to 21.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: 36 Syrian Army troops and 25 Turkish-backed rebels are killed, bringing the total death toll in Idlib since December to 1,186 opposition fighters and 1,136 Syrian government soldiers.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Airstrikes kill at least 33 Turkish troops and injures 39 others in Jabal Zawiya, Idlib Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey says it has 'neutralized' 1,709 Syrian government elements in Idlib since 10 February 2020 and that it has destroyed 55 tanks, 3 helicopters, 18 armored vehicles, 29 howitzers, 21 military vehicles, 4 Docka anti-aircraft guns, 6 ammunition depots and 7 mortars in the operations.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey opens its border with Syria and allows Syrian refugees free passage to Europe effective immediately for the next 72 hours.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkish Foreign Minister Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu and NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg hold talks amid the escalation in Idlib with Syria and Russia.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Twitter, Facebook and Instagram are blocked in Turkey, while YouTube and WhatsApp are partially restricted. It is understood that the measures are intended to protect details surrounding troop and equipment deployments.
A cyber attack in Australia forces the cancellation of wool sales across the country.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average enters correction territory after plunging 700 points at opening.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Markets are on pace for their worst week since the 2008 financial crisis.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Vice President for Family Affairs Masoumeh Ebtekar is infected with the novel coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: 236 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in Italy, bringing the number to 655. Five more virus-related deaths are confirmed, bringing the death toll in the country to seventeen. Forty-five people recovered from the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: A woman is diagnosed with the coronavirus after a possible person-to-person transmission. It would be the first case of transmission in the United States with no known contacts to overseas cases.
Saudi Arabia temporarily suspends entry to the kingdom for the Umrah Islamic pilgrimage and visits to al Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Medina due to fears over the spread of the deadly novel coronavirus.
Saudi Arabia blocks all foreign pilgrims from entering the country. This block happens just before the Ramadan fasting.
Prime Minister of Japan Shinzo Abe announces that all junior and high schools will be asked to close from March 2 until their upcoming spring break to help fight the coronavirus pandemic.
Estonia confirms their first case.
Greece confirms its second and third cases and cancels all Carnival-related events.
The first case in San Marino is confirmed.

The decision to build a third runway at Heathrow Airport is found to be unlawful by the Court of Appeal because the British government did not take into account its commitments under the Paris Agreement to combat climate change.
A senior Turkish official tells Reuters that Turkey "will no longer stop Syrian refugees from reaching Europe".

Astronomers discover the largest known explosion ever in the history of the Universe, which occurred in the Ophiuchus galaxy cluster. It replaces MS 0735.6+7421. As space and ground telescopes that study radio emissions improve (which are better than X-ray observations for detecting these), more similar explosions, or "giant radio fossils", may be found.
sources: Astrophysics via arXiv at Cornell University

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkey calls for the establishment of a no-fly zone over Syria.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: NATO holds an emergency meeting after Turkey formally triggers Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkish MoD states that last night 329 Syrian Army troops were "neutralized" and asserts that five helicopters, 23 tanks, 10 armored vehicles, 23 artillery and howitzers, five ammunition trucks, one SA-17 and one SA-22 air defense systems, three ammunition depots, two inventory depots and one headquarters building belonging to Syria's military were destroyed.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Russia deploys two frigates, Admiral Makarov and Admiral Grigorovich, armed with Kalibr cruise missiles to the Eastern Mediterranean off the Syrian coast.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkey deploys MIM-23 Hawk surface-to-air missiles to its border with Syria.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: A Turkish drone strike kills 11 Syrian government soldiers on the M5 highway near Idlib.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Syrian attacks on Marat al-Nasan leave more Turkish soldiers wounded, some of them seriously.

Roman Polanski wins three César Awards, also for best director, for his movie An Officer and a Spy (French: J'accuse). Several women walk out in protest. Les Misérables wins four Césars, one of them for best film.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Global stock markets have lost US$6 trillion in value over the last six days.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average drops 800 points at opening, continuing the worst week since the financial crisis of 2007–08. This week, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has dropped 13% and 4,000 points.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Geneva Motor Show is cancelled due to the Swiss ban on gatherings larger than 1000 people.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The ITB Berlin, the world's largest tourism trade fair, is cancelled after authorities imposed the restriction that each participant would have to prove they are not a risk.

American investment management firm Elliott Management Corporation buys a significant stake in Twitter, and announces it will seek to make several changes to their management, including possibly replacing CEO Jack Dorsey.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: 464 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in Italy, bringing the number to 888. Four more virus-related deaths are confirmed, bringing the death toll in the country to 21.
Belarus, Monaco, Iceland, Azerbaijan, New Zealand, Lithuania, Mexico and Nigeria confirm their first cases of coronavirus.
Cyprus closes four of its checkpoints along the border with Northern Cyprus for the first time since 2003 due to coronavirus concerns. The checkpoints are expected to be reopened within a week.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), European migrant crisis
text: Nearly 300 migrants including Syrians arrived in Edirne province, Turkey, on the border with Greece in a bid to go to Europe. Another group of migrants arrived on the coast of Ayvacik in Çanakkale, western Turkey, and wanted to go to the Greek island of Lesbos by boats. Turkish officials announced that the security forces will not intervene to prevent the crossing of any migrants, including those from Syria and other countries like Afghanistan and Iran.
Chinese Olympic Swimmer Sun Yang is banned from swimming for eight years after being found guilty of doping by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco temporarily block the Remain-in-Mexico policy.
Guinea's president Alpha Condé announces a postponement of both the general election and referendum slated for March 1. A new date isn't given yet.
Hong Kong Police arrest entrepreneur Jimmy Lai, owner of the newspaper Apple Daily, and former lawmakers Yeung Sum and Lee Cheuk-yan for their involvement in anti-government protests.
Pope Francis, in tandem with IBM and Microsoft, calls for AI technologies that risk violating human rights, such as facial recognition software, to be regulated.
A meteor explodes over Croatia. The Croatian Astronomical Union say the meteor disintegrated at an altitude of at least 30 kilometers above sea level. The meteor was likely roughly 2 meters across.

context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), Afghan peace process
text: American and Afghan Taliban leaders will meet at the Sheraton Grand Doha Resort & Convention Hotel in Doha, Qatar, ahead of a signing ceremony to bring an end to the 18-year war in Afghanistan, which is now the longest war in U.S. history. Taliban deputy leader Sirajuddin Haqqani says "everyone is tired of war, it has exhausted everyone", while the longest-serving NATO Commander in Afghanistan, General John Nicholson, describes the situation as a "stalemate".

context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), Afghan peace process
text: The U.S. and the Taliban sign a deal.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: A Turkish soldier is killed and six more are wounded by Syrian government artillery shelling near Taftanaz.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkish bombing overnight kills 48 Syrian government troops and 14 members of the Lebanese Hezbollah, and also destroys 13 military vehicles. According to local sources, among the killed were 11 officers including a general, a brigadier general, and a colonel.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkey says it has destroyed a chemical warfare facility at a scientific research center in As-Safira, south of Aleppo with surface-to-surface missiles. Syrian Government said Turkish statement regarding the chemical warfare facility was not true.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkey releases footage of targeting Syrian equipment including a Pantsir-S1.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Turkish media said that drone and missile strikes targeted Syrian Kuweires and Abu al-Duhur military airbases in Aleppo Governorate, saying a hangar was destroyed.
The United Arab Emirates suspends all extracurricular school activities and orders nurseries closed until further notice as measures to prevent the spreading of the virus.
An elderly woman traveling from Spain becomes the first case of coronavirus in Ecuador.
The first case of COVID-19 is confirmed in Ireland, Qatar and Luxembourg.
A 78-year-old man evacuated from the Diamond Princess becomes the first death from coronavirus in Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The first death from coronavirus in the United States is confirmed after a man dies in a hospital in the Seattle area.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. announces new travel restrictions to Iran and increased warnings against traveling to South Korea and Italy.
Eighty migrants cross to Aegean Islands Lesbos and Samos overnight after Turkey opens its border with Greece.

Turkish President Recep Erdoğan says 18,000 refugees have crossed into Europe as of this morning and that 25,000–30,000 more may cross today. Erdoğan reiterates that Turkey cannot handle another refugee wave from Syria and that it will keep its borders open.
Voters in Slovakia head to the polls to elect the members of the country's National Council.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, 2020 South Carolina Democratic primary
text: Former Vice President Joe Biden wins the South Carolina primary.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, 2020 South Carolina Democratic primary
text: Businessman Tom Steyer suspends his presidential campaign, after coming in a distant third.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey launches an operation in Syria's Idlib Governorate codenamed Operation Spring Shield.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Two Syrian Air Force Su-24 jet aircraft are shot down by Turkish Air Force F-16s using air-to-air missiles over the Syria–Turkey border, while a Turkish drone is shot down by Syrian government forces in Idlib.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Syrian state media says the Syrian Air Defense Force has downed three Turkish drones used to hit Syrian Army and air bases.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkish drone and artillery strikes target Aleppo International Airport.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkish drone strikes target the Hama Military Airport.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkish drone strikes kill 19 Syrian Government troops in the past 24 hours, raising the total killed by Turkey in the past 3 days to 93 Syrian Government troops and 14 Hezbollah fighters.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: The Syrian Army launches an operation in the southern city of Al-Sanamayn, Daraa Governorate, after "armed militants" attempted to take over the majority-Sunni city. The operation is reportedly still ongoing as gunmen still hold western parts of the city.
Afghan president Ashraf Ghani rejects a clause in the U.S.–Taliban deal setting the release of Taliban prisoners ahead of intra-Afghan talks scheduled for March 10.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea halts religious services and closes churches as the infected toll surpass 3,700.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Armenia
text: Armenia confirms its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic confirms its first three cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scotland confirms its first case of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino
text: San Marino reports its first death.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)
text: A nursing home in Kirkland, Washington locks down due to fears of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Florida
text: Florida confirms its first two cases, and Governor Ron DeSantis declares a public health emergency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Republic confirms its first case.

context: European migrant crisis, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present)
text: Turkish Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu says 76,358 migrants have left Turkey from Edirne Province as of this morning towards Europe.

context: European migrant crisis, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present)
text: Greece deploys its military on the border with Turkey to prevent thousands of migrants from entering the European Union, and suspends all asylum applications for a month while also vowing to deport any migrants who enter Greek territory illegally.

Syria and Libya's Tobruk-based government led by Aguila Saleh Issa agree to establish diplomatic relations following a high level visit to Syrian Foreign Minister Walid Muallem. Both governments agree to counter "Turkish aggression" in the region.

Muhyiddin Yassin is sworn in as the Prime Minister of Malaysia, succeeding Mahathir Mohamad. ([https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-muhyiddin-yassin-swearing-in-prime-minister-12485960 CNA])
Former South Bend, Indiana mayor Pete Buttigieg suspends his presidential campaign.
Parliamentary elections are held in Tajikistan.
Luis Lacalle Pou is sworn in as the new President of Uruguay and succeeds leftist Tabaré Vázquez.
Houthi forces capture the city of Al Hazm, the capital of Al Jawf Governorate in Yemen.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Syrian rebels backed by Turkey recapture four towns and villages from the Syrian government forces in Idlib, raising the number of towns and villages recaptured since February 24 to 30.

context: Syrian Civil War, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)
text: Syrian government forces backed by Russian airstrikes recapture the city of Saraqib four days after its capture by the rebels.

context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), Afghan peace process
text: The Taliban say there will be no intra-Afghan talks if about 5,000 of their prisoners are not released.

context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), Afghan peace process
text: The Taliban announce the end of the period of reduction in violence. They say they will not attack foreign troops, but continue their operations against Kabul government troops. According to Belga news agency, it is unclear what the announcement means for the U.S.–Taliban agreement signed on February 29.
Hellenic Police border guards open fire on migrants attempting to illegally enter Greece by crossing the border from Turkey, killing a Syrian man.
The Hellenic Army's IV Army Corps announces a 24-hour snap military drill on the border with Turkey, and warns civilians to stay away from the area.
A soldier was killed and two injured after Islamic State-linked militants opened fire against them. Two terrorists were also killed.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Japan Sumo Association announces its spring tournament in Osaka will take place with no spectators.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rebounds 1,294 points to end its seven day decline.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia confirms its first case of the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: Andorra reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports its two first cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports its first case in Moscow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia confirms its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)
text: Two dozen more cases are reported in the U.S., bringing the total number of infected Americans to 102. Four deaths also occur in the state of Washington, bringing the total death toll in the U.S. to six. Washington and Florida issue state emergencies.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Federation of Municipalities call for all mayors to remain vigilant with the threat of the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador
text: Ecuador reports its first cases in Guayaquil.
The United Kingdom and the European Union start post-Brexit trade talks. Last week, each side publicly set its negotiating mandate.

North Korea fires two short-range projectiles from the coast of Wonsan before landing in the sea dividing the Korean Peninsula and Japan. Japan's Defence Ministry says it had not detected any projectile landing in its territory and that no ship or aircraft in the area had been damaged.

The head of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya Ghassan Salamé resigns citing stress and health concerns. In a statement on Twitter, Salamé says he has been frustrated with foreign powers, particularly France and Russia for covertly backing Khalifa Haftar's forces in the civil war.

A hostage situation occurs at the V-Mall in San Juan, Philippines. The suspect, a disgruntled security guard, took about 60 to 70 people hostage and shot and injured another security guard. The crisis is resolved after ten hours, with the suspect being arrested following an official apology and the resignation of his bosses for alleged corruption.
Industrial Associations Federation's president Ramón Porfirio Báez announces the election crisis is beginning to hurt the economy.
Former Santo Domingo mayor Roberto Salcedo Sr. resigns from the government and the Dominican Liberation Party.
People of Guyana head to the polls to elect the members of their National Assembly.
Israelis head to the polls for the third time in less than a year.
Minnesota Senator Amy Klobuchar suspends her presidential campaign, and joins fellow former contenders Pete Buttigieg and Beto O'Rourke in announcing their endorsement of Joe Biden.
MSNBC political anchor Chris Matthews resigns over criticism of making sexist comments and comparing Bernie Sanders' campaign to the Nazi invasion of France.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: A Syrian Air Force L-39 jet aircraft is shot down by a Turkish Air Force F-16 near the Syria–Turkey border. ,

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Turkey says it will deploy its domestically-produced surface-to-air missile HISAR to Syria's Idlib Governorate next week.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Syrian government sources say a Turkish drone was shot down by the Syrian Air Defense Force near Idlib; subsequent footage shared by the source shows drone to be a Bayraktar TB1.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Four Turkish soldiers are killed and seven are wounded in Tranbeh, west of Saraqeb by Syrian Army shelling; some are transferred to Turkish hospitals in Reyhanlı by helicopter.

context: Syrian civil war, Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020), Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Twenty-six Syrian Army troops are killed by Turkish ground and drone strikes, raising the number of pro-Syrian government forces killed by Turkey in the past five days to 139.

The GNA government says all flights from Mitiga International Airport, the only functioning airport in the capital Tripoli, will be shifted to Misrata Airport after Libyan National Army forces struck the airport with rockets.
Australian news agency Australian Associated Press (AAP) announces it will be closing down at the end of June, after 85 years of operation.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: In an emergency move, its first since 2008, the U.S. Federal Reserve cuts the federal funds rate by 0.5%, to a range between 1 and 1.25%.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. stocks extend their drop in response to the cuts.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: Three tornadoes, two at least EF 3 in strength, rip through downtown Nashville and surrounding towns, killing 25 people.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The state of Tennessee declares a state of emergency over the outbreak.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: John C. Tune Airport sustained major damage from the outbreak.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: President Trump announces he will visit Tennessee on Friday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea declares "war" on the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia
text: Myanmar turns a Silversea Cruises cruise ship away due to fears of coronavirus, a government spokesman says.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan announces it will cancel ceremonies marking the anniversary of the 2011 earthquake and tsunami as a precaution against the spread of coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Ukraine reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Spanish authorities announce that the first death from COVID-19 in the country occurred in Valencia on February 13.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Liechtenstein reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran says it will release 54,000 prisoners in an effort to prevent the spread of COVID-19 in overcrowded jails. Only inmates who test negative for COVID-19 will be allowed to leave prison and those sentenced to longer than five years will not be freed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)
text: Two people who died in the Seattle area on February 26 are found to have died from COVID-19, bringing the total death toll in the state of Washington to nine.

A Twitter human resources official advises that Twitter employees work at home to prevent exposure to Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. He adds that telecommuting will be mandatory for employees based in the Twitter offices in Hong Kong, Japan, and South Korea.
Argentina reports its first case.
Chile confirms its first case of COVID-19 in the Maule region.
Turkish interior minister says over 130,000 refugees have crossed into Greece in the past four days.

A court in Kazakhstan orders the early release of Mukhtar Dzhakishev, the former CEO of state nuclear firm Kazatomprom, who had been sentenced to 14 years in prison for corruption in 2010. Upon his release he will have served more than 11 years in prison.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, 2020 Republican Party presidential primaries
text: Voters in 14 U.S. states and American Samoa go to the polls in this year's Super Tuesday.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, 2020 Republican Party presidential primaries
text: Former Vice President Joe Biden is the night's big winner with victories in ten states, while Senator Bernie Sanders wins four and former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg wins American Samoa.

context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), Afghan peace process
text: The United States Armed Forces says it has carried out its first airstrike against the Taliban since a peace deal was signed in Doha, Qatar.

context: Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War
text: The Syrian Air Defense Force engages "hostile objects" over the central Homs Governorate and southern Quneitra Governorate. Syrian state media says Israel is behind the attacks.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The National Weather Service reports 11 tornadoes touched down resulting in 25 confirmed deaths. Eighteen people remain unaccounted for.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: 140 buildings were destroyed with thousands damaged. 44,000 people are without electric power.
Mount Merapi in Java, Indonesia erupts, forcing the airport in Surakarta to close.
Wallis and Futuna turns away a German cruise ship due to fears of coronavirus, and says that it is studying the possibility of denying another ship entry.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy says all schools and universities will close from March 5 through March 15 to stop the spread of the virus, as the country confirms a total of 3,090 cases and 107 COVID-19-related deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports its second death in Basque Country, an 82-year-old man, as infected toll rises to more than 210.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Hungary confirms first two COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Slovenia confirms its first case of COVID-19. The patient had recently travelled home from Morocco, passing through Italy on the way, and is now in isolation at the Ljubljana University Medical Centre.
The first in-person use of the CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing tool is conducted, intended to reverse a genetic mutation causing Leber congenital amaurosis, a form of inherited blindness.

context: Canada–Iran relations, Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752
text: Canadian Foreign Minister François-Philippe Champagne urges Iran to allow access to the flight recorders of the Ukrainian passenger plane that was shot down in January.
Egypt executes top Ansar al-Sharia militant Hisham al-Ashmawy, a former special forces officer who was convicted over several high-profile attacks, the country's military spokesman said.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) bans the use of electroshock devices for aversive conditioning on patients with mental disorders. The Judge Rotenberg Educational Center in Massachusetts, the last U.S. institution that still uses electroshock devices to punish patients, say they will challenge the federal ban in court.
After a poor performance on Super Tuesday, former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg suspends his presidential campaign and endorses former Vice President Joe Biden.

Avoiding questions about lower-than-expected GDP growth in his first year as President of Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro invites an impersonator to the restricted press section around the Planalto Palace to answer the questions in his stead. The comedian also distributed bananas (in reference to the name given in Brazil to the bras d'honneur) to the attending journalists.
Oleksiy Honcharuk and his government are voted out by the Verkhovna Rada after less than six months in office. President Volodymyr Zelensky proposes Denys Shmygal as Prime Minister.
Egypt reopens the Pyramid of Djoser after a 14-year restoration. The pyramid is deemed the oldest stone structure of its size in the world.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: British airline Flybe collapses into administration with the loss of 2,000 jobs after failing to secure financial support. The airline says the impact of the coronavirus pandemic is partly to blame for its collapse. Flybe provided more than half of UK domestic flights outside London.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average drops again almost 1,000 points over coronavirus fears.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The National Weather Service confirms 13 tornadoes occurred.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The tornado in Putnam County, Tennessee, is upgraded to an EF4, becoming the strongest tornado of the outbreak.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The EF3 tornado that went through Davidson, Wilson, and Smith counties was confirmed on the ground for , becoming the second longest path a tornado has taken in Tennessee.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: Every person is accounted for at the end of the day, after three people were missing previously. Official death toll from the outbreak is 25.
At least nine people, of whom four are children, are killed and 60 are injured when a fire at a bakery spreads to a crowded market in a refugee camp in the Gaza Strip.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: Officials in Republika Srpska reports the first case of COVID-19 in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The Italian government postpones the constitutional referendum, originally scheduled for 29 March.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The first death from COVID-19 is confirmed in England, after a woman in her 70s with underlying health conditions dies at Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading, Berkshire, as the number of confirmed cases of the virus rises to over 100.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iranian Islamic Consultative Assembly member and former Ambassador to Syria, Hossein Sheikholeslam, dies after becoming infected with COVID-19. Iran suspends its parliament indefinitely.
The International Criminal Court overturns on appeal a previous decision to block an investigation into war crimes allegedly committed by U.S. troops, the Taliban and the Afghan government.

A court in Russian-controlled Crimea sentences a Jehovah's Witness to six-years imprisonment for activities of a banned extremist organization, part of a crackdown that activists say violates religious freedom.
The Republican-controlled Arizona House of Representatives passes a bill banning transgender females from women's sports.

context: 2020 Dominican Republic municipal elections, 2020 Dominican Republic protests
text: The pots-and-pans protest continue in front of Pontificia Universidad Católica Madre y Maestra where the meeting of the Economic and Social Council with the political parties was to take place.

After failing to win any states on Super Tuesday, Massachusetts U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren suspends her presidential campaign, leaving Hawaii U.S. Representative Tulsi Gabbard as the only woman left in the race.

context: War in Afghanistan > 6 March 2020 Kabul shooting
text: At least 32 people are killed and 81 are injured when gunmen attack a ceremony in Kabul, Afghanistan. Afghan politician Abdullah Abdullah was present and escapes unharmed. ISIL claims responsibility for the attack.
Two suicide bombers on a motorcycle detonate their explosives near the United States embassy in Tunis, Tunisia, killing a policeman and wounding five others.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: U.S. President Donald Trump approves a disaster declaration for all areas affected by the tornadoes.

context: United States tornado outbreak of March 2–3, 2020
text: The National Weather Service concludes the EF3 tornado that went through Davidson, Wilson, and Smith counties in Tennessee was confirmed on the ground for , becoming the second longest path a tornado has taken in Tennessee.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia
text: Bhutan confirms its first COVID-19 case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia
text: Serbia reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City
text: The Vatican City reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Florida
text: Florida confirms its first two deaths from the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Oklahoma
text: Oklahoma confirms its first case of COVID-19 in Tulsa County.
The Committee on the Rights of the Child of the United Nations condemns the government of the Cook Islands for criminalizing homosexual sex.

Police in Georgetown, Guyana, surround the nation's election commission after there are accusations that the elections results were altered to help incumbent President David A. Granger win the election.

SpaceX successfully launches a Dragon spacecraft in orbit to resupply the International Space Station. This marks the last launch of a Dragon spacecraft, soon to be replaced by Dragon 2, and the 50th successful recovery of a Falcon 9 first stage booster.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on basketball
text: An NCAA Division III men's basketball tournament matchup at the Johns Hopkins University between Yeshiva and WPI is played without spectators after a student at Yeshiva University has tested positive for the coronavirus, making it the first U.S. sporting event to do so over coronavirus concerns.

Lebanon says it will default on a eurobond repayment and pursue restructuring its debt. The country has never before defaulted. Lebanon's government debt is about 170% of its yearly gross domestic product.
A hotel being used for quarantining those with COVID-19 collapses in Quanzhou, Fujian, China. Ten people were killed and twenty-three are trapped. Thirty-eight have been rescued alive.
Twenty-two people are killed and more than 70 are injured when a tank truck, two buses and another vehicle collide in the road between Damascus and Homs, in Syria.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Malta reports its first case of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Bulgaria reports its first two cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Nicola Zingaretti, the President of Lazio since 2013 and Secretary of the Democratic Party since 2019, confirmed he has contracted the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia
text: The Maldives report its first two confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Newly elected member of parliament Fatemeh Rahbar dies after contracting COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: A 50-year-old man is arrested for breaching quarantine and traveling to two crowded bars in Gamagōri after testing positive for COVID-19 the day prior. He reportedly told family members he intended to spread it and bragged to bar employees that he had tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina
text: The Ministry of Health of Argentina confirmed the country's first death due to COVID-19, a 64-year-old man who had traveled to Paris who also had other health conditions. This marks the first death due to COVID-19 in Latin America.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Paraguay
text: Paraguay reports its first case of COVID-19.

A spokesman for politician Abdullah Abdullah announces he will hold a parallel presidential inauguration ceremony next week after he declares himself the winner of the election. Incumbent President Ashraf Ghani was declared the winner.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: The first COVID-19 death is confirmed in Canada.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Women in Mexico march despite COVID-19 concerns and protests being cancelled in other parts of the world due to concerns over the spread of the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Women protest femicides in all major cities in Mexico, despite raise of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California, COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut
text: Connecticut confirms its first case of COVID-19 in Wilton, which is believed to have been contracted during a trip to California.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Albania
text: Albania reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova
text: Moldova reports its first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Chief of Staff of the Italian Army Salvatore Farina tests positive for COVID-19 and self-isolates, as well as President of Piedmont Alberto Cirio.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte extends the quarantine lockdown, to cover all the region of Lombardy and 14 other northern provinces, affecting over a quarter of the national population.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: The number of virus-related deaths in Italy rise to 366, while the confirmed cases are 7,375.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: Inmates at several prisons in Italy revolt with reports of riots at prisons in Modena, Foggia, Naples, Frosinone and Alessandria due to fears the coronavirus lockdowns will end visits from relatives. At least eight inmates, six in Modena, have died of overdose after assaulting the prison's pharmacy, while about 20 escaped in Foggia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: President of Portugal Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa self-isolates after a COVID-19 case is confirmed in a school he visited a few days ago.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Three new COVID-19 cases are registered in Russia (one is in Kaliningrad Region, one is in Belgorod Region, one is in Moscow Region). All of them visited Italy within the past 14 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Twenty-seven people have died from methanol poisoning in Iran after rumors that drinking alcohol can help cure the coronavirus infection, state news agency IRNA reported on Monday.
California U.S. Senator and former presidential candidate Kamala Harris endorses former Vice President Joe Biden in his campaign for the Democratic nomination for the presidency.
Civil rights activist Jesse Jackson endorses Vermont U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders in his campaign for the Democratic nomination for the presidency.

Following the death of 25-year-old Ingrid Escamilla, who was killed by her boyfriend in February, women march against violence against women in Mexico's capital on International Women's Day, ahead of the 24-hour female strike scheduled for Monday.

context: 2020 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Final
text: Australia wins the tournament, beating India by 85 runs, to win their fifth title.
Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok survives an assassination attempt in Khartoum. No one has claimed responsibility.

context: War in Afghanistan, Politics of Afghanistan
text: Ashraf Ghani is sworn in as the President of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan amidst a rocket attack claimed by ISIL. Abdullah Abdullah proclaims himself as President as well.

context: Libyan Civil War, Turkish military intervention in the Second Libyan Civil War, 2019–20 Western Libya offensive
text: Nearly 40 Syrian mercenaries recruited by the Turkish Army have fled to Italy, raising the number of Syrian fighters who fled from Libya to Europe to nearly 200.
Two United States troops are killed in a raid against ISIL in Iraq.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Black Monday, 2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war
text: Oil prices plummet after Saudi Arabia cut its official selling prices over the weekend.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Black Monday, 2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war
text: Before markets open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average futures posted a 1,300-point drop due to the coronavirus and a fall in the price of oil. The drop would be the most points the Dow has dropped in a single day.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Black Monday, 2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average plummets 1,800 points on opening, 500 points lower than pre-market futures trading.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom's largest retailer Tesco say they will be restricting the sale of essential food and household items in response to fears of mass panic buying.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The 2020 BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells) is canceled due to coronavirus fears. This is one of the first major sporting events in the United States to be canceled over the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The number of confirmed cases in Italy rose to 9,172, while the death toll rose to 463.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte extends the lockdown from Northern Italy to the whole country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: Riots continue at several prisons in Italy after family visitations were suspended due to the coronavirus pandemic. Inmates took two prison guards hostage in Modena during an attempted escape, while inmates at San Vittore Prison in Milan overpowered guards and occupied the roof. Prisons in Pavia and Rebibbia are set on fire, allowing some prisoners to escape.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: The Minister of Health of Cyprus confirms the first two cases in the island; one a health professional who visited United Kingdom and the other a 25-year-old man who had traveled from Italy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The first two COVID-19 deaths are confirmed in Germany.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The French Minister of Culture Franck Riester announces he is infected with COVID-19, as five members of the National Assembly join the 1,412 cases in the Republic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The President of the Community of Madrid Isabel Díaz Ayuso orders the suspension of classes "at all educational levels" between 11 March until 30 March, as the region reports more than 500 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland cancels all the Saint Patrick's Day parades.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: In order to combat the spread of coronavirus, Israel orders all arrivals from abroad, regardless of country, to self-quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia suspends all schools, universities and other educational institutions until further notice in response to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The infection rate is reduced, but South Korean president Moon Jae-in said it was "too early to be optimistic".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. Senator Ted Cruz and U.S. Representative Paul Gosar self-quarantine themselves after having made contact at CPAC with a man confirmed to have been infected with COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. Representative Matt Gaetz announces that he will quarantine for 14 days after making contact at the CPAC with a man who tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships
text: The Grand Princess cruise ship, with at least 21 people aboard who've tested positive for COVID-19, has docked at the Port of Oakland, California, to continue to the next step in the quarantining measures process. The ship was carrying more than 2,000 passengers, as well as 1,100 crew members. The Grand Princess had been idling about offshore since Thursday (March 5). Disembarking American passengers are being put under mandatory 14-day quarantine at military bases in California, Texas or Georgia. Foreign passengers are being sent to their home countries for the completion of the quarantine.
North Korea fires three projectiles from the coast of Sondok into the sea, according to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff.

text: President of Brazil Jair Bolsonaro tests negative for the disease, and decries news outlets that reported he had received an initial positive test result.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine's Ministry of Healthcare reports the country's first death from COVID-19, a 71-year-old woman from Radomyshl.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Guinea
text: Guinea confirms its first case of COVID-19, an EU employee traveling to Conakry.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Sudan
text: Sudan confirms its first case and death from COVID-19, a man in his 50s who had recently visited the United Arab Emirates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia confirms its first case of COVID-19, a 48-year-old Japanese woman coming from Burkina Faso.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: Guadeloupe confirms its first case of COVID-19, a 36-year-old woman returning from a cruise with relatives who recently visited Metropolitan France.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya
text: Kenya confirms its first case of COVID-19, a 27-year-old Kenyan woman travelling from the United States through London.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan closes all land borders, shuts down schools for three weeks, limits international flights, and discourages any large public gatherings in an attempt to prevent the spread of the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman
text: Oman suspends tourist visas, sporting events, and non-class student activities to slow the spread of the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: Venezuela suspends all incoming flights from Europe, supends all student activities and public gatherings to slow the spread of the coronavirus after the first two cases in the country were confirmed by the vice president.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Guatemala
text: Guatemala confirms its first case of COVID-19, is a Guatemalan who returned from Italy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Quebec company Medicago announces it has found a COVID-19 vaccine candidate, and hopes to begin human testing this summer.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada will suspend sessions of Parliament until at least April 20.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada Prime Minister Justin Trudeau says that his wife Sophie Grégoire Trudeau's symptoms remain "mild" after testing positive COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. President Donald Trump declares a national emergency in response to the pandemic. This will allow up to $50 billion of federal money for relief efforts.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: After 32 cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in Illinois, Governor J. B. Pritzker bans gatherings of 1,000 or more people for 30 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Four hundred United States National Guard and Air National Guard personnel are activated in six states to help contain the coronavirus: Florida, Iowa, Louisiana, New York, Rhode Island and Washington.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: After 41 cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in Pennsylvania, Governor Tom Wolf orders all K–12 schools to close from March 16–29.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan confirms it now has 25 cases of COVID-19, more than double than reported the previous day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado
text: 72 confirmed cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in Colorado, while the state's first death from the virus, identified as an 80-year-old woman, has been reported in El Paso County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut
text: Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont orders the closing of all schools for at least two weeks, beginning March 16.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Delaware
text: Delaware Governor John Carney orders the closing of all public schools in the state due to coronavirus concerns.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: The Prime Minister Xavier Espot announces in a special public appearance that orders the closure of all public establishments except basic stores, pharmacies and gas stations during two weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania
text: After Senator tested positive for COVID-19, becoming the first Romanian high-ranking official with the disease, interim government headed by Prime Minister Ludovic Orban self-isolates for 14 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo
text: Kosovo reports its first two cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland declares a state of epidemic emergency late on Friday, bans all foreigners from entering the country, and Polish citizens returning from abroad will be placed under a 14-day quarantine. The country closes all restaurants, pubs, clubs and casinos. From March 14, gatherings of more than 50 people will be banned. From March 15, international air and rail connections will be suspended.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: President Nikos Anastasiadis, in a special televised appearance, announces the closing of all borders except for nationals for 15 days since 15 March.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, aftermath of the Christchurch mosque shootings
text: Ahead of the one-year anniversary of two far-right terror attacks on mosques in Christchurch that killed 51 people, Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announces the cancellation of a national remembrance service as a precaution due to the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland
text: Icelandic government orders the closure of all universities and secondary schools and ban public gathering of 100 or more people for four weeks.

Katerina Sakellaropoulou is sworn in President of Greece in the Hellenic Parliament and becomes the first woman to hold the office, succeeding Prokopis Pavlopoulos. Amid the COVID-19 pandemic in Greece, she suspends the protocol ceremony for the inauguration scheduled for Saturday 14 and no handshakes are allowed.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > 2020 Louisiana Democratic primary
text: After 36 cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in Louisiana, Secretary of State Kyle Ardoin postpones its primary elections from April 4 until June 20.

context: 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries, COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Florida, Arizona, Illinois, and Ohio will proceed having Democratic Party primaries despite the coronavirus outbreak. Ohio Democratic Party chairman David Pepper said that the Ohio primaries will go on as planned.
The USMCTA has passed the Canadian Senate after passing the third reading in the House of Commons earlier, Canadian Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland says.
Astronomers discover 139 new "minor planets" in the Solar System that are beyond the orbit of Neptune, which helps boost odds of finding Planet Nine.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 Formula 1 season
text: Formula 1 officially cancels the 2020 Australian Grand Prix, then later announces the postponement of the Bahrain and Vietnam Grands Prix.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The Premier League holds an emergency meeting after Arsenal F.C. manager Mikel Arteta and Chelsea F.C. player Callum Hudson-Odoi both test positive for COVID-19. The current season is suspended until April 3, along with the English Football League and FA Women's Super League.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 Masters Tournament
text: Augusta National Golf Club postpones the 2020 Masters Tournament.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 IndyCar Series
text: IndyCar, the organizer of the IndyCar Series, cancels all events through the end of April.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 Boston Marathon
text: Mayor Marty Walsh announces that the 124th annual running of the Boston Marathon, originally scheduled for April 20, will take place on Monday, September 14 instead.
Canadian national Édith Blais and her Italian partner Luca Tacchetto are found alive in Mali after escaping from their captors. The pair were abducted in Burkina Faso on December 15, 2018.
A second rocket attack this week hits the Camp Taji base in Baghdad Governorate, Iraq, wounding three United States troops.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Apple Inc. says it will close all of its stores outside China for two weeks in response to the coronavirus pandemic, according to its CEO Tim Cook.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Solomon Islands bans all travelers from China, South Korea and Japan. Health minister Dickson Mua also says that the country has suspended flights to Brisbane, Australia, and banned all civil servants from overseas travel in an effort to contain COVID-19.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: American Airlines says it will suspend long haul international flights from March 16 until May 6.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Walmart says all of its stores will reduce their hours to 6:00 a.m. until 11:00 p.m. local time until further notice in response to the pandemic. Several other chains have already done so.
A group of researchers in the Netherlands have found antibodies that can be used to combat COVID-19.
Scientists from Imperial College London say that a vaccine could be tested soon.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain > Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Jet2.com planes return to the United Kingdom after the airline cancelled flights to Balearic Islands and Canary Islands.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain > 2020 Spain coronavirus lockdown
text: Spain officially places the entire country in a lockdown for two weeks after declaring a Status Alarm the day before.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Javier Solana, former Secretary General of NATO and former High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, has been hospitalized since Wednesday after testing positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain's Ministry of Health reports more than 1,500 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in a single day, including over a thousand in the capital Madrid.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: María Begoña Gómez Fernández, spouse of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, tests positive for coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: A newborn baby tests positive for COVID-19 at North Middlesex University Hospital in Edmonton, London, becoming the youngest known victim of the disease in the United Kingdom. The child's mother has also tested positive for the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: NHS England reports 10 more deaths from the coronavirus, doubling the number of deaths in the UK to 21. All patients were aged over 70 and had underlying health conditions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, 2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown
text: Italy's Ministry of Health reports 250 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date. The Mayor of Bergamo Giorgio Gori says churches are now being used to store dead bodies as the city's morgues are full.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, 2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown
text: Air pollution in Northern Italy drops following the coronavirus lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino
text: The Government of the Republic of San Marino orders a nationwide quarantine until April 6.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Abdelkader Aamara, Minister of Equipment, Transport and Logistics and Deputy tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia
text: Namibia reports its first two cases of COVID-19. President Hage Geingob says he imposes a travel ban to and from Qatar, Ethiopia and Germany for 30 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda confirms the country's first case of coronavirus, an Indian citizen who arrived in the country on March 8 from Mumbai.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports 1,365 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 97 more deaths, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date, bringing the total to 12,729 confirmed cases and 611 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Budi Karya Sumadi, the Indonesian Minister of Transportation, tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Syria
text: Syria's government closes all schools and cancels public events until April 2, to prevent the spread of the virus. Syrian Minister Imad al-Azab rejects claims the government is covering up cases and says the new measures are "precautionary".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. President Donald Trump confirms he has been tested for COVID-19, after coming into contact with Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro's Press Secretary last week, who has been diagnosed with the disease. President Trump's results were negative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: A total of 16 U.S. states have closed all of their schools as of this date.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo reports his state has confirmed 613 cases of COVID-19, with two deaths today.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Contra Costa County bans gatherings over 100 people, effective March 15. This is more than twice as strict as Governor Gavin Newsom's ban of crowds of 250 or more people earlier in the week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports eight more confirmed cases of COVID-19 since yesterday, for a total of 33.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)
text: After 66 cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in Georgia, Governor Brian Kemp declares a public health emergency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado
text: In an unprecedented move, Colorado Governor Jared Polis orders the closure of all downhill ski areas for a week, citing coronavirus concerns.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern imposes a 14 day mandatory quarantine to everyone arriving in New Zealand, including diplomats, tourists and returning citizens, but excluding those coming in from Pacific Island nations, and bans all cruise ships from entering the nation until at least June 30.

context: 2020 United States presidential caucuses in the Northern Mariana Islands, 2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries
text: U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders wins the Northern Mariana Islands Democratic caucuses.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: The Bath Half Marathon is expected to go as planned despite the coronavirus.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 in UFC
text: The Ultimate Fighting Championship events will go as planned despite the coronavirus.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 XFL season
text: A player on the Seattle Dragons tests positive for the coronavirus.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > COVID-19 pandemic in Hubei
text: Wuhan Zall F.C. is expected to leave Spain and return to Wuhan, where the coronavirus was originated.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, 2019–20 NBA season
text: Detroit Pistons power forward Christian Wood reportedly tests positive for COVID-19.
Fans attend the Vive Latino in Mexico City despite coronavirus concerns.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: In an emergency move, less than two weeks after the previous unscheduled intervention, the Fed drops its benchmark rate a full percentage point. It announces a $700 billion quantitative easing program, sets reserve requirements for thousands of banks to zero and lowers other lending rates. The set of measures appears as its biggest ever in a single day.
A pipeline explosion causes a fire and destroys dozens of buildings in Lagos, Nigeria, killing at least 15 people.
Malta's Navy rescues 112 migrants from a sinking boat in the Mediterranean Sea.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan confirms the Central Asian country's first case of COVID-19, an Uzbek citizen who had recently returned from France. All schools, colleges and universities are ordered to close for three weeks, while all public events are cancelled.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The number of confirmed cases of COVID-19 in Italy jumps to 24,747, while the death toll rose to 1,809 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Noted Italian architect Vittorio Gregotti dies in Milan, at age 92, after contracting coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa
text: The Republic of the Congo reports its first case of coronavirus, a 50-year-old man who arrived in the country on an Ethiopian Airlines flight from Paris.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran's Ministry of Health and Medical Education reports 1,209 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 113 more deaths, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date, bringing the total to 13,938 confirmed cases and 724 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan
text: Kazakhstan declares a state of emergency over the coronavirus pandemic. The presidential decree from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev imposes a national quarantine and restricts both entry and departures from the country to all except diplomats and individuals invited by the government.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina
text: President Alberto Fernández reinforces security at the borders and bans all travelers from hard-hit countries that spent at least 14 days there. In addition, he says he is considering a national quarantine and suspension of school classes.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 pandemic in Palestine
text: The Jerusalem Islamic Waqf announces the closure of the Al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock to upend contamination of the holy sites from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 pandemic in Palestine
text: The corruption trial of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, originally slated to open on March 17, has been delayed to May 24 due to restrictions on public gatherings enacted to stop coronavirus spread.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary reports its first death from COVID-19, a 75-year-old man.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom's Department of Health and Social Care reports 232 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 14 more deaths. The UK government says a "wartime-style" mobilisation will be enforced in the coming weeks to tackle the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, 2020 Spain coronavirus lockdown
text: Spain's Ministry of Health reports 2,000 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 105 more deaths, as the country enters a nationwide lockdown.
