text: Austria reports 6,211 new cases in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: President Nicos Anastasiades announce a curfew from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time and orders bars, cafés, restaurants and cultural venues to close at 10:30 p.m. beginning November 6 and until the end of this month.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen announces the extermination of the country's minks (around 15 million) after a mutated version of the coronavirus spreads to humans, reasoning mutations pose a risk to the efficacy of future COVID-19 vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports 2,646 new cases in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day record since the pandemic began and bringing the nationwide total to 46,892.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó tests positive for COVID-19 after arriving in Thailand for an official visit.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: A new lockdown is announced for four Italian regions: Lombardy, Piedmont, Aosta Valley, and Calabria. In two other regions, Apulia and Sicily, stricter measures will be imposed. The measures will start on November 6.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte also signs a decree that would impose a nationwide curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time beginning tomorrow. Under new nationwide restrictions, museums will be closed and shopping centers will close on the weekend.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania; COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
text: Lithuania declares a three-week lockdown starting from November 7 to curb the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports 24,692 new infections and 373 deaths in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day record of both cases and deaths since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports 19,768 new infections and 389 deaths in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day record of both cases and deaths since the pandemic began, bringing the nationwide totals to 1,693,454 cases and 29,217 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines records 987 new infections in the past 24 hours, the lowest single-day record since July 14, bringing the total to 388,137. The lowest figure is attributed to the 12 testing laboratories that failed to submit their reports on time.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco reports 5,745 new infections and 82 deaths in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day record of both cases and deaths since the pandemic began, bringing the nationwide totals to 235,310 cases and 3,982 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 4,101 new cases of COVID-19, a new single-day record.
Novavax signs an agreement with the Australian government to supply 40 million doses of their NVX-CoV2373 vaccine candidate to the country during the first half of 2021.

context: United States withdrawal from the Paris Agreement
text: The United States officially withdraws from the Paris Agreement.

French Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin declares that the Turkish ultranationalist group Grey Wolves has been outlawed, stating they "[incite] discrimination and hatred and [are] involved in violent actions". The decision follows a string of high-profile attacks against the Armenian community in Lyon in recent weeks that have been attributed to the group.

context: War crimes in the Kosovo War
text: Former President of Kosovo and Kosovo Liberation Army spokesman Jakup Krasniqi is transferred to the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in the The Hague to face trial on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity during the Kosovo War.

context: 2020 United States elections > 2020 United States presidential election
text: The outcome of the 2020 United States presidential election is still undetermined. Incumbent President Donald Trump declares victory despite not reaching the required 270 electoral votes needed to win. Former Vice President Joe Biden, having more projected electoral votes, says, "We're on track to win this election." Trump has sued in several states, claiming, without providing evidence, widespread voter fraud.

context: 2020 United States elections > 2020 United States election protests
text: Protesters took to the streets for a second night in a row as the presidential election inched closer to results. Protests and marches were underway in cities such as Philadelphia, Detroit and Chicago. The National Guard was mobilized in Portland and arrests were made in Minneapolis and New York City, with police confiscating weapons.

context: 2020 United States elections > 2020 Puerto Rican status referendum
text: In a nonbinding resolution, 52% of Puerto Ricans vote to make the island into a U.S. state.
Astronomers announce the discovery of the first fast radio burst (FRB) signal detected in the Milky Way galaxy. The signal is believed to be coming from a magnetar.

context: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War > 2020 bombardment of Stepanakert
text: Azerbaijani forces shell the Artsakh capital of Stepanakert and several other cities, including Shusha and Martuni, using heavy artillery. A journalist in the capital told Reuters, "The air raid siren hasn't stopped all day". Reporters Without Borders calls on the United Nations and Azerbaijan to allow the evacuation of civilians, including 80 local and foreign journalists.
The strategic Lachin corridor is closed by Armenian forces as Azerbaijani troops advance within a few kilometres south of Shusha.

The Ethiopian National Defense Force declares it is "at war" with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which controls the northern Tigray Region. TPLF Chairman Debretsion Gebremichael says fighting with federal troops is taking place in western Tigray.
Tigray officials say Ethiopian Air Force fighter jets have bombed areas near the regional capital Mekele.

Movement Towards Socialism (MAS) spokesperson Sebastian Michel announces that Bolivia's President-elect Luis Arce was attacked with dynamite while he was in a meeting at the party's headquarters in La Paz. No injuries were reported.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia falls into a recession for the first time since the 1997–98 Asian financial crisis after its economy contracts 3.49% in the third quarter.
The death toll from former Hurricane Eta rises to 18 as dozens of people are assumed buried in their homes in San Cristóbal Verapaz, Guatemala.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England, COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
text: England enters a four-week lockdown, with all non-essential shops, pubs, restaurants, hospitality venues, places of worship, and leisure facilities closing until at least December 2. All indoor cross-household mixing is banned, and people can only meet one person from another household outside. Unlike the first lockdown, schools and universities will remain open.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab self-isolates for two weeks under government and NHS rules after recently being in "close contact" with someone who tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France registers a record 58,046 new cases over the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 1.6 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: Paris bans delivery and takeaway services for prepared food and alcohol between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. local time starting tomorrow in an attempt to stem the worsening spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Prime Minister Stefan Löfven self-isolates after a person close to him came into contact with another individual who tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Sweden reports 4,034 new infections, a single-day record for the pandemic. Meanwhile, the death toll surpasses 6,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Danish authorities impose a lockdown that orders bars, restaurants, public transport, and public indoor sports closed between tomorrow and December 3 in seven North Jutland municipalities, to potentially help prevent a coronavirus mutation in minks from spreading to humans.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announces a three-week nationwide lockdown starting November 7 in an attempt to curb the spread of COVID-19. All retail stores will close, and travel between regions will be banned, while authorities will reintroduce a system obliging citizens to send text messages to a government number to leave home to work, shop, visit a doctor, or exercise. Secondary schools will close and introduce distance learning while kindergartens and primary schools will stay open.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy registers a record 34,505 new cases over the past 24 hours, pushing the cumulative case total to 824,879. In addition, the country reports 445 deaths, the highest number in a single day since May 2 and pushing the death toll to 40,192, becoming the sixth country to register more than 40,000 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway
text: Prime Minister Erna Solberg announces new restrictions limiting the number of guests to visit a household to five, ordering bars to close at midnight as of November 7, and ordering people to avoid unnecessary travel. In addition, a new rule is introduced that visitors must have proof of a negative COVID-19 test if they want to visit the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports a record 27,143 new infections and 367 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total since the pandemic began to 466,679 cases and 6,842 deaths, respectively.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin announces an extension of the remote learning period for secondary school students in grades 6–11 until November 22, as the city's COVID-19 situation worsens.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports 368 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day number since late April, as many parts of the country report a record number of deaths, exceeding levels reported in the first wave of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus
text: President Alexander Lukashenko bans Belarusian citizens from returning from abroad, with the exception of those in Russia, to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: China temporarily bans travellers arriving from many countries including Belgium, France, the Philippines, and the United Kingdom due to concerns over the growing spread of COVID-19 in those countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Prime Minister Hun Sen and four Cabinet ministers quarantine after they met with Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó, who tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut
text: Connecticut issues a statewide public health advisory due to the rise of COVID-19 cases, urging residents to limit non-essential trips outside the home between 10:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. EST with the exception of those who are essential workers who must leave their home to work and anyone who has to leave their house on an emergency basis for medical care, medical supplies, food or groceries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 5,710 new cases of COVID-19, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy says that the state is preparing to announce new steps to combat the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama
text: Alabama Governor Kay Ivey announces that the statewide mask mandate and safer-at-home order will be extended to December 11.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States reports 121,054 new cases of COVID-19 in a single day, a new record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics
text: Colombia's House of Representatives abruptly ends its session and asks lawmakers to quarantine after a member tested positive for COVID-19.

The United Nations General Assembly approves a resolution sponsored by Cuba, Egypt, Kuwait, Morocco, Nicaragua, Oman, Qatar, and Palestine condemning Israeli forces' use of violence against Palestinians. 139 nations voted in favor of the resolution and nine voted against: Australia, Canada, Guatemala, Hungary, Israel, the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, Nauru, and the United States.

context: 2020 United States presidential election, 2020 United States election protests
text: Protests continue in several U.S. cities, including New York City, Washington, D.C., and Minneapolis. Several clashes with police result in arrests.

context: 2020 United States presidential election, 2020 United States election protests
text: Facebook bans a large group called "Stop the Steal", which was used by supporters of President Donald Trump to organize protests against the election results.

context: 2020 United States presidential election, 2020 United States election protests
text: Police, acting on a tip, investigate an alleged plot by a group to attack the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia, where votes are being counted in the city. Two men have been taken into custody, and a weapon has been recovered.

context: War crimes in the Kosovo War
text: The President of Kosovo Hashim Thaçi resigns to face charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague. Thaçi says he is resigning to "protect the integrity of the presidency of Kosovo". Speaker of the Assembly Vjosa Osmani assumes the office as Acting Kosovar President.
U.S. Attorney David Anderson confirms that United States seized US$1 billion worth of bitcoin from an account tied to the former darknet market Silk Road earlier this week.

Voters in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines head out to elect the members of their House of Assembly. Incumbent prime minister Ralph Gonsalves of the Unity Labour Party is seeking a fifth consecutive term while his main opponent Godwin Friday of the New Democratic Party aims at a change of government.

context: Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 anti-lockdown protests in the United Kingdom
text: Police have arrested at least 104 protesters during "Million Mask March" in central London. A large police presence remains in place near Trafalgar Square where the protest was dispersed shortly after 07:00 p.m. GMT.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed accuses the Tigray People's Liberation Front of "criminal hubris and intransigence," claiming they rejected the federal government's efforts at "mediation, reconciliation, dialogue". Sudan closes its borders with Ethiopia and the United Nations calls for immediate de-escalation of tensions and peaceful resolution to the conflict.
The Afghan military recaptures Kandahar Province's Arghandab District, killing 200 Taliban members in the process.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia unveils an RM322.5 billion expansionary 2021 Budget to boost its domestic economic activity, according to government reports, as it grapples with the economic fallout of the pandemic and rising political uncertainty.

Former Hurricane Eta, now a tropical depression, leaves more than 50 people dead in Guatemala after causing flooding and landslides. It is expected to regain strength and head to Cuba and the coast of Florida this weekend.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C. > White House COVID-19 outbreak
text: White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows tests positive for COVID-19. Four other White House aides and a Trump campaign staffer have also tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona
text: Sierra Vista, Arizona announces that it will reinstate their mask mandate amid a rise of cases in Cochise County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado
text: Denver is expected to implement a curfew for residents and nonexempt businesses as an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts
text: The restrictions, mask mandate, and stay-at-home order is expected to take effect in Massachusetts amid a rise of cases in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan surpasses 200,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: Texas surpasses one million confirmed cases of COVID-19, becomes the first state in the US and world's first subnational to surpass that milestone.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France registers a record of 60,486 new cases over the past 24 hours. The record number of new cases pushes the nationwide total to 1.66 million, the fifth-highest in the world.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The number of daily cases in Germany hits a new record of 21,506 over the last 24 hours, the highest single-day increase since the beginning of the pandemic, according to data released by the Robert Koch Institute.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy registers 37,809 new cases in the past 24 hours, its single-day record since the start of the pandemic. In addition, the country reports 446 new deaths, the highest single-day number since April as four Italian regions enter lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia
text: Latvia declares a four-week lockdown from November 9 to slow the spread of COVID-19. Under the new rules, social contact is discouraged and a maximum of ten people from no more than two households will be allowed to gather inside. Restaurants can serve only takeaway food and shops will limit the number of people inside.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports a record 445 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll since the pandemic began to 7,287 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa declares a state of health emergency that will come into force next week to allow the government to impose further restrictions. These measures will be discussed at an extraordinary Cabinet meeting tomorrow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania
text: Romania imposes a nationwide nighttime curfew and closes all schools for 30 days beginning November 9 after the number of daily infections surges over the past two weeks. All shops will close by 9:00 p.m. and people will have to stay home from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time. It also widens the compulsory use of face masks to all outdoor spaces across the country and orders all indoor farm produce markets to close.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports 20,582 new infections in the past 24 hours, its single-day record since the pandemic began, bringing the cumulative nationwide total to 1.73 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi reports a record 7,178 new cases in the past 24 hours, pushing its cumulative case total to 423,381.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports 1,755 new infections in the past 24 hours, its single-day record since the pandemic began, bringing the cumulative nationwide total to 38,189 cases.
China condemns U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo's decision yesterday to remove the militant group East Turkestan Islamic Movement from his department's list of designated foreign terrorist groups.
The European Union announces sanctions against President Alexander Lukashenko, his son Viktor, police chief Ivan Tertel, and Chief of Staff Igor Sergeenko.
Surangel Whipps Jr. wins the election for President after Raynold Oilouch concedes his defeat. Whipps is the brother-in-law of outgoing President Tommy Remengesau Jr.

Incumbent prime minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Ralph Gonsalves wins a historic fifth consecutive mandate. His ruling Unity Labour Party also gains additional seats in the House of Assembly.

Former Hurricane Eta, now a tropical depression, moves toward Cuba after regaining strength. The government of the Bahamas issues a tropical storm watch while a state of emergency is declared in Miami-Dade County, Florida, as the state also prepares for the impact of the storm. The storm left at least 100 people dead in Central America.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Illinois reports 12,348 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. This brings the cumulative cases total to 477,978.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri
text: Missouri reports 4,559 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. This is because the state "de-duplicates" individuals who have already received a test prior to the 7-day period.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan records 6,225 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports 919 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,132 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases in the province to 82,825. It is the largest single-day increase in cases since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria reports a record 8,421 new infections in the past 24 hours, raising its nationwide case total to 147,220.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: Prime Minister Zoran Tegeltija tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a new record of 86,852 new confirmed cases in the last 24 hours while the total COVID-19 deaths surpasses 40,000 as Prime Minister Jean Castex warns that the second wave has "brutally" and "violently" arrived in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The number of daily confirmed cases in Germany hits a new record of 23,399 over the last 24 hours, according to data released by the Robert Koch Institute, bringing the nationwide total to 642,488. It is the third consecutive day that the country reported a record number of daily cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports a new record of 39,811 new confirmed cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 902,490 cases. Lombardy remained the hardest hit region, reporting 11,489 new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary reports a record 107 new fatalities in a single day, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,357 while the country also surpasses 100,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19 after a record 5,318 cases were reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland surpasses 500,000 cases of COVID-19 after a record 27,875 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports a new record of 10,746 new confirmed cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 450,934 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia
text: Georgia announces a curfew in Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi, Rustavi, Zugdidi, Gori and Poti between 10:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. local time beginning November 9, amid a surge in COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a single-day record of 9,450 new cases in the last 24 hours, prompting President Hassan Rouhani to announce new restrictions that all non-essential businesses must close at 6:00 p.m. local time for a month starting November 10.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports 1,502 new cases in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since July 30, pushing the cumulative infections total to 341,753 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: The number of daily confirmed cases in Morocco surges by a record 5,836 cases, bringing the nationwide total to 252,185.

Police arrest opposition leader and former prime minister Pascal Affi N'Guessan for creating a parallel government after the victory of incumbent Alassane Ouattara in the election. Prosecutors are seeking terrorism charges against more than a dozen opposition leaders who boycotted the election and created a transitional council.

context: Human rights in the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates overhauls its legal system to loosen restrictions on alcohol consumption, permit cohabitation, and criminalize honor killings, among other changes.

All major U.S. networks project that Joe Biden has been elected President of the United States after winning Pennsylvania. Kamala Harris will become the first female Vice President of the United States. This marks the first time since 1992 that an incumbent president's challenger has won the election over the incumbent president, when Bill Clinton defeated George H. W. Bush.
President Donald Trump is refusing to concede to Biden and has vowed to challenge the results in court, alleging widespread electoral fraud.
Fijian Prime Minister Frank Bainimarama is the first leader to congratulate Democratic presidential nominee Joe Biden, despite no official result being announced at the time.
After a first round in October, voters in Egypt head once again to the polls to elect their members of parliament.

In horse racing, American thoroughbred racehorse Authentic wins the Breeders' Cup Classic at the Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Kentucky, U.S, which was held with limited spectators due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

context: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado > 2020 Mozambique attacks
text: Islamist militants are reported to have beheaded over 50 people in a massacre at a village in Cabo Delgado Province.

context: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War > Battle of Shusha (2020)
text: The Azerbaijani military says it has captured the city of Shusha in Nagorno-Karabakh. Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev says "We have won this victory on the battlefield, not at the negotiating table". Armenia and Artsakh leaders deny the loss of the city but say "fierce fighting" is ongoing inside the city.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed abruptly sacks and replaces the Chief of General Staff of the Ethiopian military General Adem Mohammed, Foreign Minister Gedu Andargachew and the head of intelligence Demelash Gebremichael.

In a televised address, Ahmed accuses Tigray's regional leaders of "preparing for war" against the federal government since 2018, saying the group had siphoned federal development funds to buy weapons and train militias.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,328 new infections, marking a new single-day record for a second day in a row.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec
text: Quebec reports 1,397 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began and surpasssing previous record one month ago.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota
text: Minnesota reports 5,908 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Utah
text: Utah governor Gary Herbert declares a state of emergency and ordered a statewide mask mandate in an attempt to stem a surge of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi reports the highest single-day spike of 7,745 new cases of COVID-19, taking the capital’s total to 438,529 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: The Education Ministry orders all schools across the country to close as part of the implementation of a conditional movement control order in most states from tomorrow until the end of the academic year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia surpasses 40,000 cumulative cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports 459 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, its single-day record since the pandemic began, raising the nationwide death toll to 38,291.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Albania
text: Albania reports 501 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record and becomes the first time the country reports more than 500 cases in a single day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports 35 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record, pushing the nationwide death toll to 734.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Prime Minister Antonio Costa announces that Portugal will impose a localized nighttime curfew from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m., in 121 municipalities across the country, affecting 70% of the population, beginning tomorrow. People will also be prevented from leaving their homes between 1:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. on Saturdays and Sundays.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victorian Premier Daniel Andrews announces a lift on restrictions of the travel limit in Melbourne and the "ring of steel" separating the city from Regional Victoria from 11:59 p.m AEDT tonight. He also announces that gyms, theatres and cinemas will reopen tomorrow, and more people will be allowed in hospitality and religious venues. It is also the first time that all of Victoria has been on the same restriction level since late June.
The number of confirmed worldwide COVID-19 cases surpasses 50 million. The United States remains the country with the most confirmed cases, accounting for 20% of all cases worldwide.

Voters in Myanmar head to the polls. State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy is expected to win the election, despite international accusations of genocide and persecution of the Rohingya minority, who were also stripped of their voting rights in 2015.
Luis Arce is sworn in as President of Bolivia, succeeding Jeanine Áñez.

Turkish Finance Minister Berat Albayrak announces his resignation on social media due to "health reasons". It comes two days after the chief of the Turkish Central Bank was fired by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.
Japanese prince Fumihito is officially made heir to the Chrysanthemum Throne. The crowning ceremony had been delayed by seven months due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Fra' Marco Luzzago is elected the new Lieutenant of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta. The Order also postpones election for Grand Master.
Virgin Hyperloop makes its initial run with human passengers, achieving a top speed of 107 mph (172 kph) using magnetic levitation.

A Russian Mil Mi-24 helicopter is shot down by the Azerbaijani Armed Forces over Armenia, near the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. Russia says two crew members are killed. Azerbaijan apologizes, extends condolences, and offers to pay compensation.
Artsakh officials in Nagorno-Karabakh confirm the loss of Shusha to Azeri forces. Many civilians in Shusha have fled, and fighting is closing on the region's capital, Stepanakert.

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announces he has signed a deal with Azerbaijan and Russia to end the war by Tuesday morning. A Kremlin spokesman confirms the deal. Later, Azerbaijan's president Ilham Aliyev says a "trilateral agreement" has been signed. President of Russia Vladimir Putin says Russian peacekeepers will be deployed. The agreement cedes several districts to Azerbaijan, including the Lachin District. The agreement will also establish a transport corridor through Armenia, linking Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan.
The peace deal is met with anger in Armenia as thousands protest against it in the capital Yerevan with some protesters storming the parliament building.
Hours after signing of the deal, Ararat Mirzoyan, the president of Armenia's National Assembly, is pulled from his car and attacked by an angry mob of protesters.

Unidentified gunmen using grenades and automatic weapons attacked an army post in western Baghdad, killing 11 people, including soldiers. Both the military and police have launched a manhunt for the gunmen.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average opens at an all-time record high – a 1,500-point surge in reaction to Pfizer's results in testing its COVID-19 vaccine.
In the United States, a biannual Federal Reserve report mentions, for the first time, climate change as a risk for the stability of the financial system.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Albania
text: Albania announces that it will impose a second nationwide lockdown on November 11 in an attempt to curb the worsening spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium
text: Belgium surpasses 500,000 total confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports a record 41 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, raising its death toll to 825.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Prime Minister Viktor Orbán announces that a curfew will be implemented between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m local time and orders restaurants and bars to close. Meanwhile, the curfew also prohibits gatherings of more than ten people, reintroduces online learning for high schools and universities, and sports events will be held only behind closed doors. The measures, which last for an initial 30 days, will be voted on in the National Assembly tomorrow and come into force on November 11.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports 21,798 new infections in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since they began, thus bringing the cumulative nationwide total to 1.79 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: President Volodymyr Zelensky and two top government officials test positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a record 10,463 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total since the pandemic began to 692,949 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Hokkaido reports a record 200 new cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines reports 108 new deaths in the past 24 hours, its highest total since October 23, thus bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,647.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine
text: Maine reports 204 new infections, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: Governor Phil Murphy announces new restrictions in the state amid rising cases. Restaurants and bars will be ordered to close indoor services by 10:00 p.m. local time, casinos will be closed, and high school and indoor youth sports will be suspended. The restrictions will take effect on Thursday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Ben Carson tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: President-elect Joe Biden announces a 12-person coronavirus task force as part of his transitional team.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States becomes the first country in the world to surpass ten million cumulative COVID-19 cases, according to data from Johns Hopkins University.
Pfizer and BioNTech say that their potential vaccine is 90% effective at preventing COVID-19 infections.

A soldier kills an officer with an axe and then proceeds to shoot two more officers dead at a base near Voronezh, in southern Russia. The suspect has been detained and an investigation launched, though officials have said they are looking into the suspect's mental health state.

context: 2020 United States presidential election > Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election
text: President Donald Trump's re-election campaign files lawsuits in Nevada, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin and Georgia, alleging electoral fraud.

context: Second impeachment process against Martín Vizcarra
text: President of Peru Martín Vizcarra is impeached by the Congress of Peru. Manuel Merino replaces him as interim president.

President Trump tweets that he has fired Secretary of Defense Mark Esper. Esper had prepared a letter of resignation in the wake of the recent presidential election. National Counterterrorism Center director Christopher C. Miller has been named acting secretary.

Former President of Bolivia Evo Morales returns back to his country a day after his economic minister Luis Arce was sworn in as the new President. He was forced out of the country last year following unrest over his decision to run for a third term.

context: Aftermath of the Falklands War > Land mines in the Falkland Islands
text: The Falkland Islands are declared land mine-free, 38 years after the end of the war.

State-affiliated TV reports that Ethiopian Armed Forces have seized Humera Airport in the Tigray Region. Hundreds have been killed since the intervention broke out last week as the African Union calls for an immediate end to the conflict. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed ordered airstrikes and an offensive after an alleged attack on a federal military base by forces of the Tigray People's Liberation Front.

context: European Union competition law, criticism of Amazon
text: The European Union files antitrust charges against Amazon, accusing the company of abusing its position as the top online retailer in France and Germany by using data from sellers to determine what offers to make and what products to launch for their own branded goods. The antitrust commission also opens a second investigation into similar charges against Amazon.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Illinois reports 12,623 new confirmed and probable cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the beginning of the pandemic. In addition, the number of cumulative cases surpasses 500,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 6,473 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: Texas reports 10,865 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin reports 7,073 new cases and 66 deaths in the past 24 hours, new single-day records since the pandemic began. In addition, the positivity rate reaches a record high of 35.37%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Iowa
text: Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds extends the state of emergency and announces new restrictions on public gatherings amid a rise of cases in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota
text: Minnesota Governor Tim Walz announces new restrictions amid a rise of cases in the state. Indoor and outdoor gatherings will have a 10-person limit, bars and restaurants will close indoor dining service at 10 p.m. CST, and indoor capacity will be reduced to 50% of people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: 61,964 hospitalizations are reported in the United States, a new record high surpassing the previous record on April 15 and the first time that there are more than 60,000 Americans hospitalized for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,388 new cases of COVID-19 infections in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bosnia and Herzegovina
text: Bosnia and Herzegovina announces a nighttime curfew between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. local time beginning tomorrow as part of a measure to reduce the spread of COVID-19. It also will limit indoor and outdoor gatherings to 30 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria
text: Bulgaria reports 107 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record and the first time the country has reported more than 100 deaths since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen halts a plan to kill more than 15 million minks in Denmark to contain a coronavirus mutation due to opposition from MPs to pass a bill that would authorize the slaughter.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports 580 new fatalities in the past 24 hours, the highest daily total since April 14, as more regions across the country face new restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin announces that the city will limit operating hours at clubs, bars and restaurants for two months between November 13 until January 15, 2021. Under the new rules, these establishments will not be allowed to serve customers from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. local time. However, the restrictions do not apply to take-away services.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, COVID-19 vaccine
text: The Health Ministry announces that Spain will receive 20 million vaccine doses from Pfizer and BioNTech by early 2021.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports 532 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since May 12, bringing its death toll to 49,770. Meanwhile, weekly deaths surpass 1,000 for the first time since June.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran imposes new restrictions that order restaurants and non-essential businesses in Tehran to close at 6:00 p.m. local time for the next month, in order to curb the worsening spread of COVID-19 that threatens to overwhelm hospitals.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon, COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
text: Caretaker Prime Minister Hassan Diab announces a two-week full lockdown from November 14 - 30, after localized lockdown measures fail to stem the surge of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestinian chief negotiator Saeb Erekat dies at the age of 65 due to complications from COVID-19.

The defendant in the attack that killed 10 people pleads "not criminally responsible" for the incident saying he has a mental illness. Under Canadian law, his lawyers will have to prove that he has a mental illness that kept him from understanding either what he was doing, or that what he was doing was wrong.

Citizens of Jordan cast their votes in a general election after the country's House of Representatives was dissolved in September. The election takes place during a rapid surge of new COVID-19 infections.
A bomb explodes at a Remembrance Day ceremony attended by foreign diplomats in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Several people are wounded.
Hurricane Eta restrengthens into a category 1 hurricane as it reaches the Gulf Coast of Florida.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: Texas Governor Greg Abbott announces that the state is expected to deploy resources to Lubbock and El Paso to help combat the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: El Paso County judge Ricardo Samaniego announces that the stay-at-home order will be extended to December 1 as cases continue to increase.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas
text: Arkansas reports 1,962 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Illinois reports 12,657 new infections, a new single-day record as the number of hospitalized patients reaches an all-time high of 5,042, surpassing the previous record set in April.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo announces a 10:00 p.m. EST curfew for bars, restaurants, and gyms in the state from November 13 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina
text: North Carolina reports 3,119 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record, as the positivity rate rises to 7.9%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Ohio Governor Mike DeWine reinstates a statewide mask mandate with penalties for businesses. He also says that the state might close restaurants, bars, and fitness centers if cases continue to increase.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Vermont
text: Vermont reports 72 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The number of people who hospitalised due to COVID-19 in the United States reaches 65,368, a new record for second day a row.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,426 new infections, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany reports 261 new fatalities, according to the Robert Koch Institute. This is the highest number of deaths in a single day since April, raising the nationwide death toll to 11,767.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: The Greek government announces that it will impose a nationwide overnight curfew from 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time, beginning November 13. This comes as the National Public Health Organization reports a record 2,752 new cases and 43 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy surpasses one million total COVID-19 cases, becoming the third country in the European Union to surpass that milestone. In addition, the country also reports 623 new deaths, the highest single-day total since April 6.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports 432 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, raising its nationwide death toll to 31,593. It is first time that the country has reported more than 400 deaths and is also a new single-day record for that figure since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The number of deaths from COVID-19 in Spain surpasses 40,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey announces a nationwide indoor smoking ban in a bid to halt the rising number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports 50,385 total COVID-19 deaths since the start of the pandemic, becoming the first country in Europe to surpass 50,000 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports the first domestic case of COVID-19 from a truck driver who infected his wife and two other relatives after three weeks of quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a record 11,780 new infections and 462 fatalities in the past 24 hours, raising its nationwide totals since the beginning of the pandemic to 715,068 cases and 39,664 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports 1,708 new infections in the last 24 hours, which is the highest daily total since August as it considers new measures to combat the rising number of cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines surpasses 400,000 total COVID-19 cases, becoming the second country in Southeast Asia after Indonesia to reach that milestone.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Vanuatu
text: Vanuatu reports its first case of COVID-19 after a citizen who was repatriated from the United States tested positive while in quarantine.

context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic; COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong, COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) announces that a "travel bubble" between Singapore and Hong Kong will begin on November 22 with 200 passengers per day. Passengers on these flights will not be subjected to a two-week quarantine.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Teodoro Locsin Jr. announces the government's decision to suspend the termination of the Visiting Forces Agreement with the United States for at least another six months.
Kahairi Saadallah pleads guilty to three murders and three attempted murders.

A general election is held in Belize amidst a prolonged economic crisis. Patrick Faber of the ruling United Democratic Party is challenged by Johnny Briceño, the candidate of the oppositional People's United Party. Dean Barrow, Prime Minister of Belize for the past 12 years, decided to not run again for office.
Prince and Prime Minister Khalifa bin Salman Al Khalifa dies at the age of 84 after holding the office since 1970. He is succeeded by Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa.

context: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests; Legislative Council of Hong Kong
text: Four Hong Kong pro-democracy activists, Alvin Yeung, Dennis Kwok, Kwok Ka-ki and Kenneth Leung, are stripped of their seats following a decision by China's National People's Congress Standing Committee. 15 pro-democracy legislators announced their resignations shortly after the announcement, also declaring "that 'One Country, Two Systems' has come to an end". Critics fear this will turn the legislature into a rubber stamp for pro-Beijing policies.
Several officers are injured after far-right protestors clash with police in Warsaw, after thousands defied public gathering restrictions to participate in the annual Independence Day march.
President-elect Joe Biden announces Ron Klain as his incoming White House Chief of Staff.

Amnesty International reports that massacres are taking place in the Tigray Region of Ethiopia after a conflict broke out last week. Amnesty cites witnesses blaming the Tigray People's Liberation Front for the "horrific tragedy" taking place as airstrikes continue to hit the region after Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed blamed the political group of committing war crimes. Amnesty's report could not identify the perpetrators of the massacres.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announces a $35.14 billion package to stimulate the economy by boosting jobs, consumer demand, manufacturing, agriculture and exports hit by the COVID-19 pandemic. She said the package includes 9 billion rupees ($121 million) for development of a vaccine by the government’s biotechnology department.
Hurricane Eta makes landfall as a tropical storm near Cedar Key, Florida.

The International Organisation for Migration says at least 74 people have died after their boat, which was carrying more than 120 people, capsized off the coast of Libya. The Libyan Coast Guard has rescued 47 survivors.
Typhoon Vamco makes landfall in Luzon in the Philippines and causes flooding in Metro Manila killing at least seven people. In Marikina alone, around 40,000 homes were fully or partially submerged.

A helicopter carrying Multinational Force and Observers (MFO) peacekeepers crashes near Sharm el-Sheikh, South Sinai Governorate, Egypt. Seven people are killed, including five Americans, a French national and a Czech national. One crew member, an American, survived and was medically evacuated to an Israeli hospital.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Chicago Mayor Lori Lightfoot issues a new stay-at-home advisory that asks people to leave the house only for work, school or other essential reasons. It is scheduled to take effect for 30 days beginning at 6:00 a.m. CST on November 16.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Illinois reports 12,702 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California surpasses one million cases of COVID-19, becoming the second state after Texas to reach that milestone.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 6,940 new cases, a new single-day record, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 236,225.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota
text: Minnesota reports 7,228 new cases, a new single-day record, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 201,795.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Nationally, more than 150,000 cases are reported, setting a world record for a third consecutive day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta Premier Jason Kenney announces new restrictions that will suspend indoor group fitness programs, team sports, group performance activities, limit the number of people who attend weddings and funeral services to 50 and reduce operating hours for restaurants, bars and pubs in the areas that are under enhanced status from tomorrow until November 27. It comes after Alberta reports a record 860 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia reports a record 1,130 new cases in the last two days. This number includes 536 on Wednesday and 594 on Thursday. In addition, there are a record 155 people that have been hospitalized because of the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports a record 1,575 new cases in the last 24 hours, raising its seven-day average to 1,299 cases and the cumulative cases in the province to 89,784.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Nationwide, 4,981 new cases are reported in Canada in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi reports a record 8,593 new cases in the last 24 hours, taking the total number of confirmed cases in the capital to 459,975.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh has tested positive, only days after being released from prison.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran surpasses 40,000 total COVID-19 deaths after 457 new fatalities are reported in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Japan surges to a record high of 1,651 cases in the last 24 hours as Economy Minister Yasutoshi Nishimura warned of more stringent measures if the number of cases continues to rise.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports 1,808 new infections in the last 24 hours, the highest since July 30, raising its nationwide total to 349,992 cases, according to data from the National Command and Operation Centre.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine surpasses 500,000 total COVID-19 cases after a record 11,057 new cases are reported in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: President Volodymyr Zelensky is hospitalized after he contracted COVID-19 earlier this week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia
text: Croatia reports 3,082 new cases over the past 24 hours, a new single-day record, raising the total number of cases to 75,922.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports 3,316 new cases and 50 deaths over the past 24 hours, a new single-day record for both cases and deaths since the pandemic began, taking the nationwide totals to 66,637 cases and 959 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports 636 new deaths, the highest single-day total since April 6, which brings the nationwide death toll to 43,559.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 439 new fatalities in the past 24 hours, raising the nationwide death toll to 32,032.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports 33,470 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began, taking the nationwide total to 1.29 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands
text: President David Kabua states that the Marshall Islands are COVID-free again after the US Army workman who had tested positive is no longer contagious. Initially, two US Armed Forces personnel had tested positive for the virus and have both recovered.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: COVID-19 Response Minister Chris Hipkins asks New Zealanders who work in the Auckland CBD to stay home if possible from tomorrow after a new case was found in the city.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco reports 6,195 new cases, a new single-day record since the beginning of the pandemic, taking the nationwide total to 276,821 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships
text: In a first cruise since March, five passengers aboard the SeaDream I cruise ship have tested positive for COVID-19.

context: Legality of cannabis > Cannabis in Israel
text: Justice Minister Avi Nissenkorn announces that Israel will begin a nine-month process to legalise and regulate recreational use of cannabis.

Belgium expels five far-right Danish activists associated with Rasmus Paludan, ahead of a planned Quran burning event in Molenbeek-Saint-Jean, Brussels. The area has a large Muslim community and it was feared that the Quran burning could spark civil unrest. Asylum Secretary Sammy Mahdi said the group is a "serious threat to public order".
William Vollmar, who formerly worked as a doctor in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, was sentenced to up to 20 years in prison after pleading no contest to sexual assault charges.
The People's United Party wins Belize's latest general election, ending the United Democratic Party's rule after 12 years. Johnny Briceño will be sworn in as the next Prime Minister of Belize.

context: War in Afghanistan > November 2020 Afghanistan attacks
text: A car bombing leaves at least four soldiers dead and five others injured in Paghman District, Kabul Province.

Cross-border shelling between Indian and Pakistani troops kill 15 people, including ten civilians, and five security personnel. The Indian Army says it foiled an "infiltration attempt from Pakistan" in northern Kashmir whereas the Pakistan Army claims it responded to "unprovoked and indiscriminate firing" from India.
The United Nations says that war crimes might have been committed in the Tigray Region of Ethiopia.

context: Aftermath of the 1998 United States embassy bombings
text: An intelligence official says that Abdullah Ahmed Abdullah, Al-Qaeda’s second-in-command, accused of helping to mastermind the 1998 bombings of two United States embassies in Africa, was killed in Iran in August by Israeli operatives.
sources: The New York Times via The Sydney Morning Herald

text: Polisario Front declares war on Morocco accusing Rabat of breaking the 1991 ceasefire.

The death toll from the landfall of Typhoon Vamco in the Philippines rises to 53, according to the national police, with at least 22 still missing. The provinces of Cagayan and Isabela in northern Luzon are the most affected, mainly caused by floodwaters from the Magat Dam.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: Illinois registers 15,415 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record, breaking a national record that was previously set by Florida on July 12, when that state reported 15,299 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland
text: Maryland reports 1,869 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 8,516 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada
text: Nevada Governor Steve Sisolak tests positive for COVID-19. He says he is symptom-free but will quarantine at his home for ten days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York
text: New York reports more than 5,000 new cases for the first time since April, when the state registers 5,401 cases. The positivity rate also reaches 2.65 percent.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota
text: North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum issues a statewide face mask mandate and impose several business restrictions in an effort to contain the spread of COVID-19. The new executive order will take effect tomorrow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Oregon
text: Oregon Governor Kate Brown announces a statewide two-week "freeze" starting November 18, which will limit restaurants and bars to take-out only and close gyms, indoor and outdoor recreational facilities.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: More than 130 Secret Service agents have been ordered to isolate or quarantine because they tested positive for the coronavirus or had close contact with infected co-workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin reports 7,777 new cases, a new single-day record. The state also surpasses 300,000 total confirmed cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Nationwide, more than 180,000 cases reported in the United States, a new world record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia reports a record of 617 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing its total number of cases to 20,985.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi reports 104 new fatalities on Thursday, the highest single-day figure since the beginning of the pandemic, bringing the overall death toll to 7,332.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Indonesia reports a record 5,444 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 457,735 cases. Central Java reports the highest number of new cases, with 1,362 new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia, COVID-19 vaccine
text: President Joko Widodo states that the country has sought emergency authorization to start a mass vaccination programme by the end of the year using CoronaVac and the Sinopharm vaccine. He also said that health workers, military and police will be the first to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea begins to fine people and operators who fail to wear masks in public. Under the new rules, people caught without masks in public venues face fines of up to 100,000 won (US$90), while the operators of those places face fines of up to three million won (US$2,700).

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Germany surges to a record 23,542 cases over the past 24 hours, according to data from the Robert Koch Institute.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Italy surges to a record of 40,902 cases, pushing the nationwide total to 1.1 million cases as the government designates the Tuscany and Campania regions as high-risk "red zones".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal surpasses 200,000 cumulative cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom

context: COVID-19 pandemic > After a series of briefings against Prime Minister Boris Johnson and his wife, two of his Special Advisers Dominic Cummings and Lee Cain (also Downing Street Director of Communications left their roles in Number 10 Downing Street > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 21,983 new cases in the past 24 hours, pushing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 1.88 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > After a series of briefings against Prime Minister Boris Johnson and his wife, two of his Special Advisers Dominic Cummings and Lee Cain (also Downing Street Director of Communications left their roles in Number 10 Downing Street > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Sweden, whose government took a lighter approach to the pandemic, including not enforcing lockdowns, reports 5,990 new cases, a new single-day record that pushes the nationwide total to 177,395 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > After a series of briefings against Prime Minister Boris Johnson and his wife, two of his Special Advisers Dominic Cummings and Lee Cain (also Downing Street Director of Communications left their roles in Number 10 Downing Street > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland; COVID-19 vaccine
text: Switzerland begins reviews of Moderna's potential vaccine candidate.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > After a series of briefings against Prime Minister Boris Johnson and his wife, two of his Special Advisers Dominic Cummings and Lee Cain (also Downing Street Director of Communications left their roles in Number 10 Downing Street > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Ukraine surges to a record of 11,787 cases, pushing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 512,652 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Prime Minister Scott Morrison announces that all states and territories in Australia will reopen their borders by Christmas, with the exception of Western Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: The Auckland CBD reopens after contact tracing of a new case revealed it was linked to a known case from a border isolation facility, reversing an earlier call for people to work from home.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships
text: Seven passengers on SeaDream Yacht Club's SeaDream I cruise ship test positive for COVID-19, forcing the cruise line to cancel the remainder of the sailing and return the ship to a port in Barbados.
Ace Magashule, a top official of the African National Congress, is expected to face 21 charges of corruption in Bloemfontein, South Africa.

Federal prosecutors in Stuttgart state court charge 11 people with membership of the "" far-right terror organization, allegedly planning to effect "conditions similar to civil war" by killing Muslims and attacking mosques so as to "shake the state and the social order" and eventually overthrow the German government.

Twenty-one lawmakers from staunchly conservative Islamic parties, the Prosperous Justice Party (PKS) and the Development Unity Party (PPP), re-initiate their argument at the parliament to have the Bill on the Prohibition of Alcoholic Drinks passed into law. The bill has stalled in parliament ever since it was initiated by the same group in 2015.

A major police operation is conducted at the headquarters of Ubisoft Montreal following reports of a hostage situation. The employees remaining in the building are safely evacuated. Later, the police tell the local media that it was a false alarm. Police sources deem the 911 call that triggered the incident a hoax.

Recently unsealed court documents reveal that a teenager had been arrested last year for plotting an attack on an unidentified school in the Tasman District of New Zealand. He was in possession of an AR-15 style rifle, a modified shotgun, and homemade explosives. The suspect had pleaded guilty to charges of unlawful possession of restricted weapons and objectionable material and had been sentenced to two years of supervision.
Protesters gather in Belarus to mourn the death of 31-year-old protester Raman Bandarenka, who died in a hospital in Minsk after being beaten by security forces.

Early results show Myanmar's ruling National League for Democracy winning an absolute majority in the country's latest general election. The election is called unfair by the oppositional Union Solidarity and Development Party and is criticised by rights groups for alleged voter suppression and the political disenfranchisement of the Rohingya minority.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: The Egyptian Football Association announces that Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah has tested positive for COVID-19 shortly before Egypt's 2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier match against Togo.

Explosions are reported in the Eritrean capital Asmara amid reports of a missile attack from Tigray, Ethiopia. The Eritrean government confirms missiles were launched at the capital but said that they missed and instead landed in the countryside. The attack comes just hours after the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) threatened to target Eritrea.

The TPLF launched missiles at Gondar Airport and Bahir Dar Airport in Amhara Region, Ethiopia. A spokesman for the TPLF says, "As long as the attacks on the people of Tigray do not stop, the attacks will intensify".
Hundreds of people cross the Tekezé River on small boats into Sudan, fleeing the escalating fighting in Tigray. There are now around 8,000 refugees stranded on the Ethiopia–Sudan border.
The Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic declares war on Morocco, formally ending a 29-year truce.

Around 468,000 people are to be evacuated in Vietnam ahead of the landfall of Typhoon Vamco, which has already killed 53 people in the Philippines. Prime Minister Nguyễn Xuân Phúc warns people of the seriousness of the storm.

Tropical Storm Iota strengthens in the Caribbean Sea and is expected to intensify in the coming hours, threatening many parts of Central America, including Belize, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama and Colombia. The storm is expected to grow into a hurricane.
A fire breaks out in a hospital in Piatra Neamț, Romania, killing at least 10 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports 1,026 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba
text: Manitoba reports a record 15 new fatalities, including 11 deaths that are linked to Maples Long Term Care Home in Winnipeg, bringing the death toll to 152.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports a new single-day record of 1,581 cases, bringing the total number of cases in the province to 92,761.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec
text: Quebec reports a new single-day record of 1,448 cases, bringing the total number of cases in the province to 122,634.
