context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan
text: Saskatchewan reports a new single-day record of 308 cases, bringing the total number of cases in the province to 1,691.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota
text: Minnesota reports 8,703 new cases, a new single-day record as seven-day positivity rate reaches 15 percent.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: New Jersey reports a new single-day record of 4,395 new cases, surpassing the previous record set in April during the first wave of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota
text: North Dakota reports 2,278 new cases, a new single day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington
text: Washington state reports 2,323 new cases in the past 24 hours, a single-day record since the start of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico surpasses one million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Chancellor Sebastian Kurz announces a two-week national lockdown effective November 17. All schools, non-essential services and shops will be closed, and people will be told not to meet anyone from outside their household as the number of cases continues to rise.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Education Minister Niki Kerameus announces the closure of kindergartens, primary schools, and childcare centers across the country for two weeks beginning November 16 as part of tightened lockdown measures aimed to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland surpasses 10,000 deaths from COVID-19 after a record 548 new deaths are reported in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 22,702 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 1.9 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports a record 12,524 new confirmed cases, bringing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 525,176 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: The government announces that Iran will impose stricter restrictions beginning November 21. In Tehran and about 100 other towns and cities which are classified as "red zone" or "Level 3", non-essential businesses will close and cars will not be allowed to enter or leave the city.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports 1,731 new confirmed cases, a new record for the third consecutive day, as many prefectures such as Osaka and Chiba report record numbers of daily cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports 205 new confirmed cases, exceeding 200 for the first time since September, according to data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Western Australia reopens its hard border for the first time in seven months after it was closed due to restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

context: Foreign relations of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic
text: Guyana withdraws its recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR) following the military clashes in Guerguerat. Guyana's Foreign Minister Hugh Todd says his country will "support the efforts of the United Nations to achieve a peaceful and mutually acceptable solution".
Thousands of supporters of President Donald Trump protest the results of the 2020 United States presidential election in Washington, D.C.

Pope Francis issues an appeal to authorities in Ivory Coast to establish a climate of mutual trust and dialogue in the West African nation, where controversial elections have led to violence and a mass exodus from the country.

Fifteen Asia-Pacific nations sign the world's largest free-trade agreement in Vietnam. It replaces the Trans-Pacific Partnership, from which the administration of Donald Trump withdrew the United States in early 2017.

Iota becomes Hurricane Iota and is forecast to hit Central America. Nicaragua issues hurricane warnings near the border with Honduras while Honduras also issues warnings, whereas Colombia issues a warning to the islands of San Andrés and Providencia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Kentucky
text: Kentucky reports 3,303 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: After several days of record highs for new cases, Governor Gretchen Whitmer issues an order closing several types of business and services, including high schools and universities, for three weeks, effective November 18.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: New Jersey reports 4,540 new cases over the past 24 hours, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)
text: Governor Jay Inslee announces that bars, restaurants, and gyms in the state will no longer be able to operate indoor services. In addition, indoor social gatherings are prohibited. The new restrictions will take effect on November 17 at 12:01 a.m. PST and remain in effect for four weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. surpasses 11 million cases of COVID-19, just six days after surpassing ten million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba
text: Manitoba reports a record 494 new confirmed cases, bringing the total number of cases in the province to 10,947.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses 300,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh
text: Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, who tested positive for COVID-19 yesterday, tests negative within a day. Despite this, he and senior secretary Mostafa Kamal Uddin remain in isolation.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports 12,543 new infections of COVID-19, a new record, as well as 459 fatalities, bringing the death toll of the worst-hit country in the Middle East to 41,493.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: The municipal health commission in Jinan finds coronavirus on imported beef and tripe from Brazil, New Zealand, and Bolivia, as well as on packaging for these products, as China ramps up testing on imports of frozen foods.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports 2,443 new confirmed cases, the highest single-day total in four months, bringing the total number of cases to 356,904.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency reports 208 new confirmed cases, the highest single-day total since early September and the eighth consecutive day of triple-digit increases, bringing the total number of cases to 28,546.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy
text: A lockdown is imposed in the Italian regions of Campania and Tuscany, bringing the number of regions in lockdown in the country to six. Nine more regions are under strict restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Health Minister Maksym Stepanov tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson self-isolates after meeting with Ashfield MP Lee Anderson, who later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: South Australia reports four new cases through community transmissions linked to a supermarket and a hospital in the northern suburbs of Adelaide, leading to fears of a second wave in the state. In response, Western Australia reimposes hard border controls with South Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Eswatini
text: Prime Minister Ambrose Mandvulo Dlamini tests positive for COVID-19.
Worldwide, a record 660,905 new cases are reported over the weekend, according to the World Health Organization's COVID-19 dashboard.
Michigan State Representative, Matt Maddock and a group of representatives began impeachment hearings for Michigan Governor, Gretchen Whitmer.
A Belarusian human rights group says that over 500 people have been arrested during protests against President Alexander Lukashenko.
The second round of presidential elections takes place in Moldova.
Pro-European Union candidate Maia Sandu defeats pro-Russian incumbent Igor Dodon to be elected the first female President of Moldova.
Brazilians attend polling stations all over the country to elect mayors and city councillors in an election deemed to be a test of President Jair Bolsonaro's popularity.
Two-thirds of mayoral candidates openly supported by Bolsonaro are defeated in the first round of elections, including São Paulo candidate Celso Russomanno.
Incumbent president Donald Trump admits in a Twitter post that Joe Biden won the election. He follows up with a later tweet reaffirming his refusal to concede the election.
President Manuel Merino resigns five days after taking office as two demonstrators are shot dead and most of his Cabinet step down.

SpaceX successfully launches its Crew Dragon spacecraft carrying three NASA astronauts, Michael S. Hopkins, Victor J. Glover, Shannon Walker and JAXA astronaut Soichi Noguchi to the International Space Station. It is the first crewed operational flight of a Crew Dragon spacecraft and the first night launch in the United States since STS-130.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation
text: Korean Air announces that it will acquire Asiana Airlines for 1.8 trillion KRW (US$1.6 billion) to help the South Korean airline industry continue to grow amid uncertainties during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Hurricane Iota strengthens into a category 5 hurricane as it approaches Nicaragua.
An LP gas truck explodes on Federal Highway 15D in Nayarit, Mexico, killing at least 14 people. Most of the victims died inside their vehicles.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania > COVID-19 pandemic in Philadelphia
text: Philadelphia bans nearly all indoor gatherings, both public and private, between November 20 and January 1 as part of new restrictions in the wake of a spike in COVID-19 cases. In addition, high schools will be reverted to remote learning, restaurants will only be allowed to have takeaway or delivery, and businesses like movie theaters, arcades, and bowling alleys are ordered closed again.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Governor Gavin Newsom announces that he has pulled an "emergency brake", which means that starting the following day, California will implement more closures and stricter restrictions, which will cover 41 counties containing 94% of the state's population.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan surpasses 8,000 confirmed deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico
text: New Mexico begins its two-week lockdown announced by Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham on November 13 in an attempt to curb COVID-19 infections. Under the latest public health order, people are being asked to stay at home, and only essential businesses will remain open.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: Texas surpasses 20,000 total confirmed deaths from COVID-19 and becomes the state with the second-highest number of reported deaths in the United States, behind only New York.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: U.S. Representatives Cheri Bustos of Illinois and Tim Walberg of Michigan announce they have tested positive for COVID-19. Additionally, Representative Mark Pocan of Wisconsin said publicly he was isolating after a possible exposure to the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports a record 91 new fatalities in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Nunavut
text: Chief Medical Officer Dr. Michael Patterson announces that Nunavut will close all non-essential services, businesses and organizations, as well as schools and daycare centres for two weeks beginning November 18, due to a spike in COVID-19 cases in the territory.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 22,778 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases to 1.95 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Buryatia becomes the first Russian republic to return to a lockdown, as it closes restaurants, shopping malls, and other places of public gathering for two weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The number of hospitalized patients in France reaches an all-time high of 33,497.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 91 new fatalities, bringing the nationwide death toll to 3,472.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Prime Minister Stefan Löfven announces a ban on public gatherings of more than eight people beginning November 24, as part of measures aimed to curb the spread of COVID-19 in Sweden.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a record 13,053 new cases and 486 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases in the worst-hit country in the Middle East to 775,121 and the nationwide death toll to 41,979.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Prime Minister Imran Khan announces a temporary ban on political rallies and gatherings of more than 300 people in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19 in Pakistan.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The Northern Territory, Queensland, and Tasmania announce that their borders with South Australia are indefinitely closed, as the state's second wave reaches 17 cases.

Moderna's preliminary results show their vaccine candidate is 94.5% effective at preventing COVID-19 infections. The results also suggest that in cases of COVID-19 infection after vaccination, the vaccine appeared to prevent severe illness.

Russian President Vladimir Putin approves the construction of a new Russian Navy facility in Sudan. The naval base will be built near Port Sudan on the Red Sea coast, and will hold up to 300 military and civilian personnel.

Iraq hangs 21 convicted terrorists and murderers at the Nasiriyah Central Prison in Nasiriyah, Dhi Qar Governorate. The interior ministry did not provide details of the crimes of those executed but stated they were all convicted under a 2005 counter-terrorism law.

Plaintiffs aligned with President Donald Trump's re-election campaign and the GOP announces that they will drop lawsuits in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan, and Georgia challenging ballots and attempting to block the states from certifying their election results.
Retirees protest in Minsk, marking the 100th straight day protests broke in Belarus since President Alexander Lukashenko won his 6th term in a widely rejected election.

context: War in Afghanistan > Taliban insurgency > November 2020 Afghanistan attacks
text: The Taliban kill at least 12 police officers and injure 10 others in Jurm District, Badakhshan Province.

context: War in Afghanistan > Taliban insurgency > Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan
text: The Pentagon announces a partial withdrawal of 2,000 more U.S. troops from Afghanistan by mid-January. The withdrawal will reduce the number of U.S. military personnel stationed in Afghanistan from 4,500 to 2,500.

The Grand National Assembly of Turkey approves President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's request to deploy Turkish Army peacekeepers to monitor a ceasefire agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan in Nagorno-Karabakh.
Armenia and Azerbaijan exchange the bodies of at least 200 people killed in clashes in Nagorno-Karabakh. The exchange was overseen by Russian peacekeepers, according to the Red Cross.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed vows a "final and crucial" offensive after a three-day deadline to the leaders of the Tigray Region to surrender has expired. Abiy also confirms that airstrikes are being carried out but defines them as "precision-led and surgical", denying claims of civilian casualties.

The bodies of 29 people are found in the Virunga National Park, Democratic Republic of the Congo after they were "executed en masse". The interior ministry of North Kivu province has blamed the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and added that six other civilians were killed in a nearby village on Tuesday.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japanese economy grew at annualized rate of 21.4% in July-September quarter after two consecutive quarters of contraction due to the pandemic, driven by rise of private spending and exports.

Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel engine cars by 2030, as part of a government plan to reach a net zero emissions climate target in the United Kingdom by 2050. The sale of hybrid vehicles will also be banned by 2035.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Idaho
text: Idaho reports 1,781 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: U.S. Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico
text: New Mexico reports a record 2,112 new cases, bringing the statewide total to 67,559 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania
text: Health Secretary Rachel Levine announces that out-of-state travelers will be required to either quarantine or present a negative COVID-19 test to enter the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Ohio Governor Mike DeWine orders a night time curfew from 10:00 p.m. until 5:00 a.m. EST in an attempt to slow the spread of COVID-19. The curfew will begin on November 19 and will last for three weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin reports a record 92 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the death toll to 2,741. In addition, a record 318 hospitalizations are also reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine
text: Maine reports 246 new cases of COVID-19, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Pfizer announces that they have launched a pilot delivery program for their potential vaccine in Rhode Island, Texas, New Mexico, and Tennessee.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia reports a record 717 new cases and 11 deaths in the last 24 hours, bringing the provincial death toll to 310 and the total number of cases to 23,661.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon announces that 11 local authorities, including Glasgow, are to be placed into the highest level of restrictions (Level 4) for three weeks beginning at 6:00 p.m. GMT on November 20. The Level 4 status for the 11 areas will remain in effect "for a limited time".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports 598 new fatalities, the highest single-day total since May.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark > Cluster 5
text: The Minority government of Denmark, held by Social Democrats, agrees with four left-leaning and center parties to support a law proposal that would allow for the culling of 15 million minks across the country over concerns about a mutated version of the virus that has spread among the animals. The proposed law also bans mink farming until the end of next year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 442 new fatalities and 22,055 recoveries over the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 33,931 and nationwide recoveries to 1.47 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria
text: The number of total confirmed cases in Bulgaria surpasses 100,000, as the country sets a new record for daily deaths, with 152 fatalities reported in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reported 45,422 new cases in the last 24 hours, surpassing two million total confirmed COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports 731 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since April 3, bringing the nationwide death toll to 46,464.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports 435 new fatalities, the highest daily increase in the second wave of the pandemic, bringing the death toll in the country to 41,688.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announces the closure of schools for the remainder of the semester and introduces a nationwide weekend curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 a.m. local time. Restrictions for senior citizens over 65 years of age will also be expanded to include people under 20 years of age, allowing them to go outside only from 10:00 a.m to 4:00 p.m.. The new restrictions also order the closure of coffeehouses and cinemas, and for all sports events to be held without fans.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a record 13,352 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 788,473 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan reports a record 6,454 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 155,993 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The government will increase social distancing rules in the Seoul Capital Area to Level 1.5 amidst a surge in COVID-19 cases. The new protocols will be enforced for Seoul and Gyeonggi Province beginning November 19, as well as in Incheon beginning November 23.

context: Iran–Saudi Arabia relations, Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict
text: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Adel al-Jubeir says that his country "reserves the right to arm itself with nuclear weapons if Iran cannot be stopped from making one."

Belarus opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya calls on European leaders to impose sanctions on supporters of President Alexander Lukashenko after police used tear gas, rubber bullets and stun grenades to disperse protesters.

context: 2020 United States presidential election > Presidential transition of Joe Biden
text: President-elect Joe Biden and Vice President-elect Kamala Harris attend an unofficial security briefing from a team consisting of former advisers to both the Obama and Trump administrations. The briefing stems from the Trump administration's refusal to cooperate with the Biden-Harris transition team.

President Donald Trump fires Chris Krebs, the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), which oversaw the security of the 2020 election. Deputy Director Matthew Travis, who had expected to become acting director, is forced to resign. Krebs and the CISA have refuted Trump's accusations of voter fraud, calling the election the "most secure in American history". Trump has called Krebs' statements "highly inaccurate".

Apple Inc. releases the first Mac computers with Apple Silicon M-series ARM64 processors including the MacBook Air, MacBook Pro 13-inch, and Mac Mini with M1 chip which marks a major performance boost over x86 Intel equipped Macs.

The Solomon Islands Cabinet passes a ban on the use of social media platform Facebook in the country, citing public misuse of the platform, and a need for stricter cybercrime legislation and regulation. Communications Minister Peter Shannel Agovaka says the ban does not require parliament's approval, and will be enforced once operators "establish a firewall" to block Facebook.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration clears Boeing's 737 MAX to fly again, provided that all planes receive modifications to their software and wiring and that all pilots receive additional training.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation
text: Norwegian Air Shuttle files for bankruptcy protection in Ireland for two subsidiaries: Norwegian Air International and Arctic Aviation Assets as part of a restructuring of the business due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Fitch Ratings downgrades Zambia's government debt to RD (restricted default) after the country failed to pay a Eurobond coupon on Friday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: Mayor Bill de Blasio stated that public schools across New York City will temporarily close after the 7-day average positivity rate reaches 3%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Columbus Health Commissioner Dr. Mysheika Roberts and Franklin County, Ohio Health Commissioner Joe Mazzola issue stay-at-home advisories for residents of Columbus and Franklin County. People living in these areas are also advised to avoid travelling in and out of the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania
text: Pennsylvania reports a new single-day record of 6,339 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases in the state to 281,852.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin reports a record of 7,989 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases in the state to 331,837.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota
text: Minnesota Governor Tim Walz imposes several new restrictions on businesses and indoor gatherings in response to a surge in new cases. It begins on November 20 and lasts for four weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The number of confirmed deaths in the United States reaches 250,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. military reported a record high number of COVID-19 cases with 1,314 new cases on Tuesday, according to data from the Department of Defense.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia reports a record 762 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the province's total number of cases to 24,423.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Tokyo reports a new single-day record of 493 new cases, surpassing the previous record set in August and bringing the cumulative number of cases in the prefecture to over 35,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Nationwide, 2,203 new cases are reported in Japan. It is the first time that the country has reported more than 2,000 cases since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: The number of patients who recovered from COVID-19 in Indonesia exceeds 400,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports a record 13,421 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 801,894 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan reports a record 7,933 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cumulative total to 163,926 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia surpasses 50,000 total confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency reports 313 new cases in South Korea in the past 24 hours, surpassing 300 for the first time. It is also the highest single-day figure since August 29, taking the nationwide total to 29,311 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestine reports a record 1,268 new confirmed cases in the last 24 hours, half of them in Gaza, as officials in both the Palestinian Authority and Hamas resist calls to impose a second general lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Beginning December 1, Taiwan will require almost all visitors to have negative COVID-19 tests before arriving in the country due to an increase in imported cases. The government will also increase the number of places where people must wear masks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark > Cluster 5
text: Danish Agriculture Minister Mogens Jensen (politician) resigns following criticism of illegal government order to cull 15-17 million minks after the discovery of a mutated version of the coronavirus at some of the country's mink farms.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports 753 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since April 3, bringing the nationwide death toll to 47,217.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland surpasses 2,000 total deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports a record of 603 new fatalities in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 11,451.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 456 new fatalities in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 34,387. In addition, a record 25,179 recoveries are reported, outnumbering new cases for the first time since September 16.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Attorney General Dolores Delgado tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine surpasses 10,000 total deaths from COVID-19 after a record 256 new fatalities are reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
text: South Australian Premier Steven Marshall announces a six-day "circuit breaker" lockdown across the state beginning at midnight due to a growing number of COVID-19 cases in Adelaide. Unlike previous lockdowns in Australia, outside exercise and takeaway food will be prohibited. The lockdown will be followed by eight days of "lesser restrictions".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Samoa
text: Prime Minister Tuilaepa Aiono Sailele Malielegaoi confirms the first case of COVID-19 in the country from a sailor who returned from Auckland, New Zealand. Malielegaoi said the sailor tested positive Wednesday night but that a second confirmation test from this morning was negative. He added that they were concerned that the man could be contagious, though he is in isolation.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Authorities close a boarding school in Matabeleland North Province after at least 100 students tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa
text: The total number of confirmed cases in Africa surpasses two million. South Africa remains the continent's highest number of reported COVID-19 cases at over 750,000.

Malaysian Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Khairy Jamaluddin signed an agreement with his Chinese counterpart Wang Zhigang to cooperate on the development of a safe and efficacious vaccine, as part of efforts to combat the COVID-19 pandemic.
Pfizer formally ends its vaccine trial with a 95% success rate and will submit a regulatory approval "within days".
The Democratic Republic of the Congo declares the end of an almost six-month long Ebola outbreak in the Équateur Province.

context: Iran–United States relations, United States sanctions against Iran
text: Iran says that it will return to the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, better known as the "Iran Deal", if President-elect Joe Biden lifts sanctions imposed by President Donald Trump.

context: Iran–United States relations, United States sanctions against Iran
text: The United States imposes sanctions against the Mostazafan Foundation, a foundation controlled by Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, over alleged human rights abuses.

Three Republican members of the Michigan House of Representatives have introduced a resolution calling for the impeachment of Governor Gretchen Whitmer over her new mitigation measures against the COVID-19 pandemic in the state. Other members of the Michigan Republicans, including high-ranking members of the Michigan House, criticize the resolution.

Taiwan's broadcast regulator denies the renewal of the broadcast license of CTi News channel, citing alleged interference by its major shareholder Tsai Eng-meng. This is the first time ever that Taiwan shuts down a television news channel. The opposition party Kuomintang calls it an attack on press freedom.
Violeta Bermúdez becomes the new Prime Minister of Peru.
In basketball, the Minnesota Timberwolves select Anthony Edwards with the first overall pick in the draft, after the draft was delayed due to COVID-19.

Federal troops seize the town of Shire Inda Selassie from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) as government forces advance on the Tigray Region's capital Mekelle. There are conflicting reports of the status of Axum, with both sides claiming to control the town. TPLF leader Debretsion Gebremichael says his forces will never surrender and calls on all Tigrayans, including children, to mobilize and take up arms.
Thousands of more people flee into Sudan from Ethiopia's Tigray Region, according to international aid workers.

context: War in Afghanistan, Australian involvement in the War in Afghanistan
text: The Australian Defence Force's special report into war crimes in Afghanistan is released to the public, revealing that 39 civilians and prisoners had been killed unlawfully by special forces since 2001. Chief of the Defence Force Angus Campbell issues an apology to the Afghan people and promises significant reform.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Los Angeles County reports 5,031 new cases, the highest single-day total since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Governor Gavin Newsom orders a curfew (limited stay-at-home order) for all 41 counties in the purple tier of the state's Blueprint for a Safer Economy reopening system; these counties include more than 90% of the state population. The order will be in effect from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. PST beginning November 21.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland
text: Maryland reports a record 2,910 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases since the beginning of the pandemic to 174,733.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Franklin County, Ohio is elevated to the state's purple-level amid COVID-19 concerns, becoming the first county in the state to do so.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Miami Valley Gaming announces that they will change their operating hours due to the statewide curfew imposed by Governor Mike DeWine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania
text: Pennsylvania reports a record 7,126 new cases in the last 24 hours, surpassing 7,000 new cases for the first time since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: Texas reports a record 12,293 new cases in the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, there are 147,030 active COVID-19 cases across the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Utah
text: Utah Governor Gary Herbert issues a new public health order that will no longer require Utahns to limit social gatherings to only people in their households on Thanksgiving, even as the state reports a record 3,968 new cases in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: A record 185,759 new cases are reported in the United States, according to Johns Hopkins University.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports a record 1,105 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total cases in the province to 42,797 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba
text: Manitoba is expected to tighten their restrictions on stores and social gatherings in an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico exceeds 100,000 deaths, becoming the fourth country to do so after Brazil, the United States, and India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark > Cluster 5
text: The health ministry stated that a new, mutated strain of the coronavirus stemming from mink farms in the country is "most likely" extinct, amid fears that the new strain could compromise COVID-19 vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland
text: The Northern Ireland Executive agrees to implement a two-week tougher lockdown beginning November 27. All non-essential retail, close contact services, places of worship and cafés will close after being allowed to reopen tomorrow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia surpasses two million total COVID-19 cases after a record 23,610 new cases are reported. It also reports a record 463 new fatalities in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia resumes the vaccination of new volunteers in an trial for its flagship Sputnik V vaccine after a short pause at the end of October.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece, COVID-19 pandemic in Albania
text: The Greek government announces a closure of its border crossing with Albania in Krystallopigi beginning tomorrow morning and will also test all people entering the country through its land borders as part of efforts to contain the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine recommends the owners of three mink farms in Ireland to cull their mink to halt the potential spread of a mutated form of the coronavirus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports a record of 637 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll in the country to 12,088.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports a record 257 new fatalities and 13,357 new cases in the past 24 hours, taking the nationwide death toll to 10,369 and the total number of cases to 583,510.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government reports a new single-day record of 534 new cases and raise its virus alert in the prefecture to the highest of four levels for the first time since September, indicating that "infections are spreading".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 2,388 new cases, according to official figures. It comes as the country is on "maximum alert" and many prefectures such as Osaka, Aichi, and Hokkaido report record numbers of new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: President Rodrigo Duterte agrees to provide an advance payment to pharmaceutical companies developing a COVID-19 vaccine in order to secure millions of vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The number of new confirmed cases in South Korea reaches a three-month high of 343 cases, bringing the nationwide total to 29,654 cases, according to data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victoria Premier Daniel Andrews announces a closure of the state's border with South Australia for 48 hours beginning at 11:59 p.m. AEDT tonight. The "hard border" between the two states will be replaced by a permit system beginning at midnight on November 21.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands
text: Just days after announcing that the country was free of COVID-19 again after two infected people recovered, the Marshall Islands reports three new cases from a repatriation flight of Marshallese citizens in Hawaii.
AstraZeneca’s vaccine candidate shows promise in older adults. Late-stage trials are expected to be released by Christmas.

context: Israel–United States relations, Palestine–United States relations, Syria–United States relations
text: Mike Pompeo visits settlements in the Israeli-occupied territories of West Bank and Golan Heights, making him the first United States Secretary of State to do so.

context: George Floyd protests, 2020–2021 United States racial unrest > George Floyd protests in Chicago
text: A lawsuit is filed against the Chicago Police Department, accusing them of brutally attacking and falsely arresting protesters during demonstrations against the killing of George Floyd.
At least 19 people are killed in Uganda during protests triggered by the arrest of presidential candidate Bobi Wine.
President-elect Joe Biden wins Georgia, after the state completed its hand recount, making him the first Democrat to win the state since Bill Clinton in 1992.

Citing safety concerns, the National Science Foundation announces that the 57-year-old Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico will be decommissioned. Earlier this month, a second cable supporting the 900-ton instrument platform snapped. The platform is suspended 450 feet (137 meters) above the fixed radio dish, which is 1,000 feet (305 meters) in diameter.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launches rockets at Bahir Dar, capital of Ethiopia's Amhara Region, raising fears that the conflict could grow into a wider war. Amhara Region authorities report that the "illegal" TPLF group "launched a rocket attack around 1:40 am" but that the attack caused no damage.

A sealed copy of the 1990 Nintendo Entertainment System game Super Mario Bros. 3 sells for , the most ever paid for a video game. It features rare alternate cover art with the word Bros. on the left instead of the center.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in Canada, Federal aid during the COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canadian Conservative MP Kelly McCauley demands an audit, alleging that more than 800,000 ineligible people received Canada Emergency Response Benefit money from the Canada Revenue Agency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company
text: The Walt Disney World theme park in Orlando announces that they will bring back their Park Hopper ticket on January 1, 2021, with restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona > COVID-19 pandemic in the Navajo Nation
text: Navajo Nation reports 351 new infections in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: Donald Trump Jr., son of outgoing President Donald Trump, tests positive for COVID-19. His spokesperson says that he is asymptomatic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: U.S. Senator Rick Scott of Florida tests positive for COVID-19. He is expected to continue working from his house in Naples.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports a record 13,005 new cases in the last 24 hours. In addition, 4,750 people are hospitalized, the first time the state has seen such numbers since August.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Ohio reports a record 8,808 new cases, bringing the total number of cases in the state to 335,423.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: Newark Mayor Ras Baraka issues a ten-day stay-at-home advisory starting the day before Thanksgiving on November 25 until December 4. The city also will close streets into Ironbound District to non-residents at 8:00 p.m. to 3:00 a.m. EST in the zip code 07105 on Friday and Saturday to enforce an existing curfew.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Utah
text: Utah reports a record 4,588 new cases in the last 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Governor Tony Evers issues a new public health order that requires people aged five or older to wear a face mask when they are indoors or in an enclosed space with anyone outside their household or living unit. The mandate is effective immediately and will expire after 60 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan reports 9,779 new cases, a new one-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire
text: New Hampshire Governor Chris Sununu implements a new statewide mask mandate amid rise of cases in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario > COVID-19 pandemic in the Regional Municipality of Peel, COVID-19 pandemic in Toronto
text: Ontario Premier Doug Ford announces that Toronto and the Peel Region will be placed in a "lockdown" tier, meaning that most non-essential businesses will be closed and non-essential retail stores and food establishments will be limited to takeout and curbside pick-up or delivery. These new measures will begin on November 23.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario surpasses 100,000 total cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports a record 1,155 new cases in the last 24 hours. In addition, the number of active cases in the province reaches 10,655, the highest number since the pandemic began in March.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain > COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid
text: Madrid will close its borders with other regions between December 4 and 14 in an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19 over the December holiday week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Germany reaches a record high of 23,648, according to the Robert Koch Institute, bringing the nationwide total to 879,564 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: The Portuguese Assembly of the Republic approves a 15-day extension of the state of emergency beginning November 24 in order to allow a continuation of measures aimed to stop the spread of COVID-19. The current state of emergency will expire on November 23.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 24,318 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total since the beginning of the pandemic to 2,039,926 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Sweden reports a record of 7,240 new confirmed cases in the last 24 hours, according to the Public Health Agency of Sweden, bringing the nationwide total since the beginning of the pandemic to 208,295 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports a record 141 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 12,084.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports a record 14,575 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 598,085.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The number of new confirmed cases in South Korea reaches a three-month high of 363 cases. The country now has more than 30,000 total cases, according to data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: In response to a spike in COVID-19 cases, Prime Minister Chung Sye-kyun asks people to avoid year-end social gatherings and only leave their house for essential reasons.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Secretary for Food and Health Sophia Chan announces the suspension of classes for students in Grades one to three in primary schools for two weeks beginning November 23 due to an increase in new COVID-19 cases in Hong Kong.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: India surpasses nine million total cases of COVID-19, becoming the second country in the world to reach that milestone after the United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record of more than 2,400 new cases, according to official figures. It comes as many prefectures such as Osaka and Hokkaido report record numbers of new cases, prompting governors across the country to raise the alarm.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestine reports a record 1,472 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 81,294.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: South Australian Premier Steven Marshall announces an immediate easing of restrictions surrounding exercise, with further restrictions to be eased by the end of the week, blaming the state's brief hard lockdown on an infected individual who lied to contact tracers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil surpasses six million total confirmed cases of COVID-19, becoming the third country to do so after India and the United States.

Pfizer and BioNTech apply for an emergency use authorization from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for their vaccine. If the application is approved, the vaccine will likely be limited and rolled out in phases.

Japan's Kagawa Prefecture will cull 850,000 chickens at two poultry farms after the country reported its first bird flu outbreak in more than two years. It will be the sixth and seventh cases of avian flu in the prefecture and the biggest culling to be done at once.

Leaders from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation host a virtual summit in Malaysia to seek ways to revive their economies. U.S. President Donald Trump participates in the event for the first time since 2017.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest > Kenosha unrest shooting, Kenosha unrest
text: Kyle Rittenhouse, a 17-year-old who was charged with first-degree homicide for his involvement in a shooting in Kenosha, Wisconsin, is released on bond.

context: List of mass shootings in the United States in 2020 > Mayfair Mall shooting
text: Eight people are injured in a mass shooting at Mayfair Mall in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, leading to an emergency response. The shooter remains at large.

The Ethiopian Broadcasting Authority suspends the press license for Reuters's Ethiopia correspondent, and issues warnings to those representing the BBC and Deutsche Welle, for their alleged biased coverage of the Tigray conflict.
Over 5,000 protesters gather in Minsk to mourn the death of Roman Bondarenko, a 31-year-old protester who died from brain trauma after being arrested by police last week.

context: War in Afghanistan > November 2020 Afghanistan attacks
text: A rocket attack on residential areas in the Afghan capital Kabul kills at least eight people and injures 31 others. The Islamic State claims responsibility for the attack.

context: War in Afghanistan > Afghanistan–United States relations, Afghan peace process
text: Secretary of State Mike Pompeo meets with the Taliban and the Afghanistan government in Doha, Qatar to negotiate a peace deal.

Federal troops capture the city of Adigrat near the Eritrean border in Ethiopia's Tigray Region. Ethiopian government forces are now within 116 km (72 miles) of the heavily defended Tigrayan capital Mekelle. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) says Adigrat has experienced "heavy bombardment", but does not confirm the loss of the city.
Ethiopia rejects the African Union's offer to mediate an end to the conflict.

The TPLF report the deaths of nine civilians during the military assault on Adigrat. The Ethiopian government has denied targeting civilians and both the government and military could not be reached for comment.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts, COVID-19 pandemic in Maine, COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire
text: Massachusetts announces that they will remove New Hampshire and Maine from their low-risk travel list for contracting COVID-19. Individuals returning to Massachusetts from those states will be required to fill out a travel form, quarantine, or present a negative COVID-19 test.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports 15,442 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began as curfew begins in most counties.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan surpasses 300,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi
text: Mississippi reports a new daily record of 1,972 cases, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 142,401.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey
text: New Jersey surpasses 300,000 cases after reporting a new daily record of 4,679 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Oregon
text: Oregon reports a record 1,509 new cases, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 63,688.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: U.S. Senator Kelly Loeffler is expected to quarantine after testing positive for COVID-19 and receiving an inconclusive result.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 12 million cases of COVID-19, just six days after surpassing 11 million cases. New cases reach record highs in recent days, with more than 200,000 cases being reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration grants an emergency use authorization for Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' antibody cocktail to treat COVID-19 patients. The cocktail was previously given to President Donald Trump during his hospitalization for COVID-19 last month.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick
text: New Brunswick reports 23 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began as Premier Blaine Higgs warns that tighter restrictions will be rolled out if the increase in cases continues.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,588 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan
text: Saskatchewan reports 439 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. The province now has 6,237 total confirmed cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Tokyo reports a record 539 new cases in the past 24 hours, according to a statement from the metropolitan government, bringing the cumulative total since the pandemic began to 37,317 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Due to rising COVID-19 cases across the country, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga announces the suspension of the government-promoted "Go To Travel" campaign in areas with high infection rates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record of more than 2,500 new cases, according to official figures released by the government. It is the fourth time that Japan has reported a record number of cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran imposes tougher restrictions in Tehran and other cities as the country battles a third wave of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Senior Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob announces that the government will lift the conditional movement control order (CMCO) in Kedah, Melaka, Terengganu and Johor tomorrow but will place Kelantan under the CMCO until December 6. He also announces that foreign workers in some regions will have to undergo mandatory COVID-19 swab tests.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports the highest single-day total for both daily cases and deaths since mid-July, when 2,843 new cases and 47 new deaths are reported in the last 24 hours. This brings the cumulative number of cases to 371,508 and the nationwide death toll to 7,603.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The number of new confirmed cases in South Korea in the last 24 hours reaches a three-month high of 386. The country now has 30,403 total cases and more than 500 total deaths, according to data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic surpasses 7,000 total deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a record 24,822 new cases and 467 deaths in the last 24 hours, bringing the number of cases to 2,064,748 and the death toll to 35,778.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion
text: Mourners pay respects to the former head of the Serbian Orthodox Church Patriarch Irinej in Belgrade following his death due to COVID-19. Many mourners did not wear face masks or practice social distancing, and some kissed the glass shield that was covering the patriarch's body despite warnings from the Serbian government and epidemiologists.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports a new record of 5,532 new cases in the last 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set in April. The country now has 440,805 total confirmed cases since the pandemic began as a curfew takes effect.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports a new single-day record of 14,580 cases, bringing the nationwide total to 612,665 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile
text: Chile surpasses 20,000 total deaths from COVID-19, including suspected and confirmed cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong, COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: Singapore and Hong Kong postpone their air travel bubble agreement for two weeks amid a rise in COVID-19 cases in Hong Kong, which reported 43 new cases in the past 24 hours.
World leaders at the virtual G20 summit in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, call for a united response to the COVID-19 pandemic and discuss the global economic crises and climate change.
Russian President Vladimir Putin tells G20 leaders that his country is ready to provide their Sputnik V vaccine to other countries who need it.
Lobsang Sangay, the leader of the exiled Central Tibetan Administration, visits the White House, marking their first meeting in 60 years.
Sixty-nine inmates escape from a prison in Baabda District, Lebanon. Five of them are killed in a car crash while being pursued by security forces.

The second round of parliamentary elections is held in Georgia. After the first round in late October caused controversy, the political opposition called to boycott the run-off votes, leaving the candidates of the ruling Georgian Dream to run uncontested.
More than 7,000 people gather in Guatemala City to protest the recent budget bill. The National Congress building is also set on fire.

A federal judge dismisses a lawsuit filed by President Donald Trump's re-election campaign to block the certification of Pennsylvania's election results, saying it was "an attempt to violate the Constitution".

SpaceX successfully launches the European Space Agency's satellite altimeter Copernicus Sentinel-6 from Vandenberg Air Force Base. The satellite will monitor global sea levels with high accuracy, enhance weather forecasting, and provide detailed information on ocean currents to support ship navigation near coastlines.

Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) names Algerian Islamist Abu Obaida Yusuf al-Annabi as its new leader, following the death of Abdelmalek Droukdel during the Battle of Talahandak in June. Al-Annabi has been on the U.S. "international terrorist" blacklist since September 2015, and he has regularly appeared in jihadist propaganda videos.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed issues an ultimatum to the leaders of the Tigray People's Liberation Front, giving the group 72 hours to surrender before federal forces begin a ground offensive to capture the region's capital Mekelle. The Ethiopian military says Mekelle will be "encircled" and "shown no mercy".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Rajasthan
text: Rajasthan reports 3,260 new cases, a new single-day record since the pandemic began and bringing the total confirmed cases in the state to 243,936.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Osaka reports 490 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan surpasses 2,000 total COVID-19 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports 59 new deaths in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day total since July and bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,662.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The government will increase social distancing rules in the Seoul Capital Area to Level 2 and both North and South Jeolla Province to Level 1.5 beginning November 24 amidst a third wave of COVID-19 cases. In level 2, gatherings involving more than 100 people are banned, some high-risk facilities will be closed, and restaurants cannot operate dine-in services after 9:00 p.m.. Cafes and coffee shops are only allowed to offer takeout and delivery services. Also, indoor sports facilities must close at 9:00 p.m..

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates, COVID-19 testing
text: The Dubai Health Authority (DHA) begins to introduce saliva tests to detect active COVID-19 infections in children between the ages of 3 and 16 in all DHA facilities and DHA-run screening centers across Dubai. These tests are more than 90% accurate, making them a viable alternative to nasal swab tests which are uncomfortable and harder to use to test children.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: French authorities orders the culling of 1,000 minks in the Eure-et-Loir region after lab analyses detected a mutated version of SARS-CoV-2 in one farm. All animal products in that farm will be destroyed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez states that Spain will begin a comprehensive COVID-19 vaccination programme in January and expects to have vaccinated a substantial part of the population within three months.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports 6,017 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new record for the second consecutive day and bringing the nationwide total to 446,882 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: South Australia further eases restrictions imposed earlier in the week, ending a stay at home order but maintaining limits on public and private gatherings and quotas at businesses.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta
text: Alberta reports 1,584 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new one-day record since the pandemic began and highest number of daily cases on Sunday than any other provinces and territories.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Los Angeles County public health officials announces a suspension of outdoor dining at restaurant for three-weeks starting from November 25 at 10:00 p.m. PST due to rise of new infections in the U.S. largest county.
World leaders at the G20 summit in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, close the summit with calls for a coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic and support for vaccinations for everyone.
The United States withdraws from the Treaty on Open Skies.

Several people are arrested, including a 15-year-old boy, in connection with Friday's mass shooting at the Mayfair Mall in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, which injured eight people. The shooting followed an altercation between two groups, according to police.
Faisal Mekdad is appointed as Foreign Minister of Syria, succeeding Walid Muallem, who died last Monday.

Voters in Burkina Faso head to the polls in an election marred by a dramatic surge of terrorist attacks within the recent years. Incumbent President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré of the People's Movement for Progress seeks another term while he is challenged by two main opponents, Zéphirin Diabré of the Union for Progress and Reform and Eddie Komboïgo of the Congress for Democracy and Progress.

context: War in Afghanistan > Civilian casualties in the war in Afghanistan (2001–2021)
text: According to Save the Children, over 26,000 children have been killed in the Afghanistan war from 2005 to 2019.

context: Second Saudi–Yemeni War, Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict
text: The Iranian-backed Houthis say they attacked a Saudi Aramco oil terminal in Jeddah with a new type of Quds cruise missile. Saudi Arabia acknowledges the attack.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports 20,654 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Ohio reports a new single-day record of 11,885 new cases. This number is likely inflated because of a two-day backlog from multiple labs.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland
text: Maryland is expected to send state troopers to enforce restrictions in the state for Thanksgiving.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba
text: Manitoba reports a record 540 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total confirmed cases to 13,087 and pushing the five-day positivity rate tests to 14%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 1,589 new cases, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Nationwide, a record 5,713 new cases reported in Canada in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide confirmed cases to 337,555.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces that gyms, bars, and non-essential shops across England will be allowed to reopen when the lockdown ends on December 2. The three-tiered regional measures will return at the same time, but with tighter rules.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy surpasses 50,000 total deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia reports a new single-day record of 25,173 cases, bringing the nationwide total since the beginning of the pandemic to 2.11 million cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: King Felipe VI voluntarily quarantines for 10 days after being in close contact with someone who later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports a record 6,713 new cases and 153 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 453,535 confirmed cases and 12,511 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia > COVID-19 pandemic in Selangor
text: The government announces that it will temporarily close 28 Top Glove factories in Klang in stages to enable the Health Ministry to conduct COVID-19 screening and quarantine workers. This comes as the world's largest surgical glove maker sees an increase in infections among factory workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: The number of new confirmed cases in Malaysia increases by a record 1,884 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases to 56,659. 1,203 of these cases are from Selangor due to an increase in new infections in workplaces in the Klang Valley.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia surpasses 500,000 total confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand's Cabinet extends a COVID-19 state of emergency for 45 days until January 15, 2021.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The land border between New South Wales and Victoria reopens after 137 days of closure. People will now be able to travel between the two states without permits.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victoria eases restrictions, allowing larger public and private gatherings, larger capacity quotas for businesses, and relaxing of the mask mandate so that masks will only be required in settings where social distancing is impractical. Chief Health Officer Brett Sutton states that he is confident there will be no community transmission in the state.

AstraZeneca and University of Oxford's vaccine showed 90% efficacy when it was given to 2,741 people as a half-dose followed by a full dose and 62% efficacy when two full doses were given to 8,895 people.

Israeli media reports that, on Sunday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly flew to Neom in Saudi Arabia for a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
