context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: British Columbia reports their first case of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from a man in Island Health who returned from the United Kingdom on December 15 and tested positive on December 19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec
text: Quebec reports 6,783 cases and 110 deaths between 24 and 26 December, bringing the total number of cases to 192,655 and deaths to 8,023.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. surpasses 19 million cases of COVID-19, having averaged 185,000 daily cases over the past week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman
text: Oman officially begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine. The country is the last Gulf Cooperation Council member state to begin vaccinations. Health Minister Ahmed Al-Saidi is one of the first citizens to receive a dose of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman
text: The Supreme Committee decides to reopen Oman's land, sea, and air borders on December 29 after closing them on December 21 due to fears of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2. All travellers must show a negative PCR test within 72 hours before entering the country and must have valid health insurance. In addition, all travellers must quarantine for seven days and take another test after completing their quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 6,983 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 583,676.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Jordan reports their first two cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a couple who travelled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia announces that they will lift their flight ban on non-Saudis leaving the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea extends its current social distancing measures aimed at reducing the spread of COVID-19 until January 3, as record numbers of new cases are being reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria begins administering the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine tozinameran to its citizens. An 84-year-old woman becomes the first Austrian to be vaccinated against COVID-19 at the Medical University of Vienna.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine tozinameran, with Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and World War II veteran Emilie Řepíková among the first people to get vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece officially begins a vaccination programme against COVID-19, with ICU nurse Efstathia Kambissiouli, President Katerina Sakellaropoulou and Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis among the first people to get vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Norway reports its first cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2, after two people who travelled from the United Kingdom earlier in December test positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Portugal reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom in Madeira.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania
text: Romania begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine tozinameran. The first person vaccinated is a 26-year-old doctor from Bucharest.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: The European Union begins a mass vaccination campaign against COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazilian Vice President Hamilton Mourão tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay
text: Uruguay reported a record of 11 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 158.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa surpasses one million cases of COVID-19, becoming the first African country to reach this milestone.
Seven people are killed and seven others injured in a mass stabbing in Kaiyuan, Liaoning, China. The attacker has been arrested.
Authorities officially identify the perpetrator of Friday's suicide bombing in Nashville, Tennessee, as 63-year-old Anthony Quinn Warner and conclude that he had been acting alone.

Citizens in Niger head to the polls to elect their President in their first democratic power transfer since the country's independence from France. The election comes amidst a growing Islamist insurgency as Mohamed Bazoum is the favourite to succeed incumbent Mahamadou Issoufou, who is stepping down after serving two five-year terms.
Elections in the Central African Republic are underway, after a campaign marred by violence between government and rebel forces.
The Solar Orbiter spacecraft makes its closest approach to Venus.

Two knife-wielding assailants kill a police officer and wound another in Grozny, Chechnya. The attackers are shot dead while trying to seize weapons. It is the second attack against police in the city in recent months; in October, two officers were killed by militants.

context: Aftermath of the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
text: An Azerbaijani soldier is killed and another injured in a shooting in Nagorno-Karabakh. Azerbaijan blames the attack on "an Armenian armed group"; all the six attackers are shot dead.
Three French Army troops are killed when their armoured personnel carrier hits a roadside bomb in Hombori, Mali.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States House of Representatives passes the CASH Act, a bill that increases direct payments from $600 to $2,000, with a vote of 275–134. The bill is expected to head to the United States Senate for a vote.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders announces that he will filibuster a Senate vote to override President Donald Trump's veto of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 if the Senate doesn't vote on providing $2,000 direct payments to Americans.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism, COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka reopens the island for tourism after closing it for nine months.

Russian-led consortium Nord Stream AG says it has completed the construction of the Nord Stream 2 natural gas pipeline in Germany's exclusive economic zone in the Baltic Sea. The U.S. had previously threatened to impose wider sanctions on the project if work continued.

The Russian-flagged fishing trawler Onega capsizes near the Novaya Zemlya archipelago in the Barents Sea. 17 fishermen are missing and presumed dead, while two have been rescued. Search and rescue operations in the area have been suspended due to strong winds and low temperatures.
A power outage lasting several hours affects over 10 million people in Mexico, including in the capital Mexico City.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium
text: Belgium officially begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19, with a 96-year-old Flemish man from Antwerp becoming the first person to receive Pfizer-BioNTech's tozinameran vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Finland, Variant of Concern 202012/01, 501.V2 variant
text: Finland reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom, after a person who travelled from Western Europe tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Finland, Variant of Concern 202012/01, 501.V2 variant
text: A separate, second variant from South Africa is also reported in Finland, after two people tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain surpasses 50,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland, 501.V2 variant
text: Switzerland reports its first two case of new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from South Africa after two people tested positive for COVID-19 despite having no clear traveling history to South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 41,385 new cases in the past 24 hours. It is the first time that the country has reported more than 40,000 cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi announces that the country will ban all international travellers for two weeks starting January 1, citing concerns over new variants of SARS-CoV-2. Government officials are exempt from this ban.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Transport Minister Yuichiro Hata, who died yesterday, tested positive for COVID-19. He is the first Japanese lawmaker to die from the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Saudi Arabia extends the suspension of all international commercial flights, as well as all entry through land and sea ports for another week due to concerns about the new variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: South Korea reports its first cases of a more infectious variant of SARS-CoV-2, after three South Korean nationals who arrived from the United Kingdom tested positive for COVID-19, including an elderly man who has since died.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Alberta reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who travelled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses 15,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: President Cyril Ramaphosa announces that the country will move from level 1 to level 3 from midnight until January 15. This means that all alcohol sales are banned, wearing of masks in public places is compulsory, most gatherings other than funerals are banned, and the nationwide curfew will be extended from 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. local time.
Novavax announces it will begin phase 3 trials of its vaccine candidate in the United States and Mexico.

context: European Union–United Kingdom relations, trade negotiation between the UK and the EU
text: European Union ambassadors unanimously approve the EU–UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement with the United Kingdom.
The European Union announces that it is close to reaching an investment deal with China. The deal would immensely impact the global economy, especially with the U.S.-China trade war.
The United States Forces Japan announces that American troops in the country will begin vaccinations and prioritize front-line medical workers.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest, Andre Hill protests
text: Officer Adam Coy, who fatally shot Andre Hill was fired. Coy had failed to follow the required protocol by not turning on his body camera and failed to aid the dying man. Hill's killing was the second police-involved shooting in Columbus, Ohio in weeks, setting off renewed protests against the authorities for excessive use of force.

A court in China sentences a citizen journalist to four years in prison for "picking quarrels and provoking trouble" while reporting during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic earlier this year in Wuhan. The journalist's lawyer says that they will probably appeal the verdict. ,

A court in Saudi Arabia sentences women's rights activist Loujain al-Hathloul to five years and eight months in prison on grounds of "various activities prohibited by the anti-terrorism law". The verdict comes despite pressure from international organizations to release her.
The United States House of Representatives votes 322–87 to override President Donald Trump's veto of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell blocks an attempt by Senate Democrats to increase the direct payments from $600 to $2,000. However, McConnell also said that the Senate will consider a process to provide $2,000 in stimulus checks to Americans, a measure that is supported by both Democrats and President Donald Trump.

The first commercial Boeing 737 MAX flight in the United States since worldwide groundings began in March 2020 occurs. The flight, between New York City's LaGuardia Airport and Miami International Airport, was operated by American Airlines.

A magnitude 6.4 earthquake strikes Petrinja, Croatia, destroying half of the town. Several other cities in the country are also affected. At least seven people are killed, five of whom were in Glina, one in Petrinja, and one in Žažina. Several others are also injured.
The Krško Nuclear Power Plant in neighboring Slovenia, which produces around 20 percent of the country's electricity, is shut down as a precaution. Preventive inspections at the plant are ongoing.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C. > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: Vice President-elect Kamala Harris and her husband Doug Emhoff receive the Moderna vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: President-elect Joe Biden announces that three more officials will join his COVID-19 Advisory Board.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California extends a regional stay-at-home order in Southern California and the San Joaquin Valley due to rise of hospitalizations in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Colorado reports the United States' first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom. The patient is a man in his 20s who is in isolation in Elbert County and has no travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Louisiana
text: Republican U.S. congressman-elect Luke Letlow of Louisiana's 5th congressional district, who was scheduled to be sworn-in to the upcoming 117th United States Congress on January 3, 2021, dies from COVID-19 complications after previously testing positive for the disease, becoming the first member-elect of the U.S. House of Representatives to die before taking office since former astronaut Jack Swigert.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Kentucky
text: Governor Andy Beshear announces that the state will extend its mask mandate for another 30 days after reporting 2,990 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports a record 2,553 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, along with 1,939 new cases yesterday, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the province to 175,908.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Quebec reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who had been in contact with a family member who travelled from the United Kingdom on December 11 and tested positive for COVID-19 on December 13.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland
text: Northern Ireland reports a record 1,566 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the country to 68,762.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: A record 53,135 new cases are reported in the United Kingdom in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland reports a record 1,546 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 88,439.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland officially begins a vaccination programme against COVID-19 using Pfizer-BioNTech's tozinameran vaccine, with a 79-year-old woman from Dublin becoming the first person to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Belarus begins vaccinations with Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Denmark extends its hard lockdown until January 17 due to substantial increases in numbers of cases and hospitalizations in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 40 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 859.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: United States Forces Korea begins a vaccination programme against COVID-19 using the Moderna vaccine. Healthcare providers and first responders are among those who will initially receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: India reports six cases of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 in individuals who travelled from the United Kingdom and are now in isolation.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan, 501.V2 variant
text: Japan reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from South Africa in a 30-year old woman who arrived in Japan on December 19 and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Pakistan reports its first cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom. The patients are three people who travelled from the UK to Sindh and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines extends its travel ban to 19 "flagged" countries and territories from midnight until January 15 in order to prevent new variants of SARS-CoV-2 from entering the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The United Arab Emirates reports the first case of new variant of SARS-CoV-2 originated from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, 501.V2 variant
text: Queensland reports Australia's first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from South Africa in a woman who arrived in the state on December 22 and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Samoa
text: The government of Samoa suspends travel from the United Kingdom and South Africa in response to a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in those countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Argentina begins a vaccination campaign using the Russian Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Chile reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a resident of Panguipulli who traveled from Madrid on December 23.

The United Kingdom and Vietnam sign a free trade agreement, which will take effect on December 31, following a meeting between UK Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab and his Vietnamese counterpart Pham Binh Minh at the State Guest House in Hanoi, Vietnam.
The United States Department of Justice announces it will not charge the two Cleveland police officers who killed Tamir Rice.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest, Killing of Breonna Taylor
text: The Louisville Metro Police Department announces that they will fire Joshua Jaynes and Myles Cosgrove, two of the officers involved in the botched raid of Breonna Taylor's home.

The Investigative Committee of Russia accuses opposition leader and anti-corruption activist Alexei Navalny of fraud for allegedly using public funds from his organization for personal needs. The accusation comes after the federal prison service demanded that Navalny report to its office today or face jail time.
Jonathan Pollard, a convicted spy who spent 30 years in prison in the United States for spying, returns to Israel.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics > COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria
text: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune returns to Algeria following treatment in Germany for COVID-19 since November.

context: Abortion in Argentina > Voluntary Interruption of Pregnancy Bill
text: The Senate begins to debate the legalization of abortion up until the 14th week of pregnancy. If passed, Argentina will become the third Latin American country to allow abortion to be performed on demand, after Cuba and Uruguay. The Catholic Church opposes the move. The bill has already been approved by the lower house.

At least 25 people are killed and more than 110 others wounded in an attack at the Aden International Airport, shortly after a plane carrying the newly formed government arrived from Saudi Arabia. Prime Minister Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed is taken to safety along with the Saudi ambassador and all remaining government members. The Houthis are blamed for the attack, but the group has denied responsibility. Another blast was later reported at the presidential palace, where the cabinet was meeting.

Syrian state media reports that an ambush on a bus near Palmyra killed at least 37 people. A senior military defector in the region says that the bus was transporting Syrian Army troops and pro-government militia from Deir ez-Zor to the Tiyas Military Airbase.
A landslide in the village of Gjerdrum, Viken, Norway, leaves at least ten people injured and buries several houses. Ten people are missing.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports its first case of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom in a patient from Southern California.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports a record 442 deaths on Tuesday, bringing the statewide death toll to 24,987.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Los Angeles County surpasses 10,000 deaths from COVID-19 and is averaging 150 daily deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama
text: Outgoing U.S. Senator Doug Jones of Alabama announces he will quarantine at his home after his wife tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Colorado authorities announce the possible discovery of a second case of the SARS-CoV-2 variant from the United Kingdom in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota
text: North Dakota records 96 hospitalizations in the past 24 hours, making it the first time since September 24 that there have been less than 100 hospitalizations in the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario > COVID-19 pandemic in Toronto
text: Toronto reports a record of 1,069 cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports a record 2,923 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the province to 178,831.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in El Salvador, COVID-19 vaccine
text: El Salvador approves a vaccine made by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scotland reports a record 2,045 new cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom approves a vaccine made by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for use in the country. Health Secretary Matt Hancock says that the rollout of this vaccine will begin on January 4.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic reports a record 16,329 new cases in the past 24 hours as the positivity rate reaches a new record of 48.5%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany reports a record 1,129 deaths in the past 24 hours, according to data from the Robert Koch Institute, marking the first time that the country has surpassed 1,000 daily deaths since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Taoiseach Micheál Martin confirms that the country will close all non-essential retail under full level 5 restrictions that will remain in place for at least one month and will also delay the reopening of schools until January 11. Authorities also agree to extend travel bans to South Africa and the United Kingdom until January 6.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Malta reports its first three cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom. Two of the cases are reported in people who travelled from the UK, while the third is still being investigated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey receives their first shipment of three million doses of Sinovac's CoronaVac.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine signs an agreement to buy up to 1.8 million doses of Sinovac's CoronaVac. Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal says the first shipment of vaccines could arrive in February.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Taiwan reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 after a teenager who returned from the United Kingdom on Sunday tested positive for COVID-19 the following day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: As a result of this case, Taiwan will ban all non-resident foreigners from entering the country beginning on January 1. Legal residents, as well as people given special permission, and the spouses and children of Taiwanese nationals will be excluded from this ban.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: India extends their suspensions of flights from the United Kingdom until January 7 in order to prevent the spread of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: Singapore officially begins its vaccination campaign against COVID-19, with healthcare workers being among the first to receive the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine tozinameran.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand imposes a ban on large gatherings and events in controlled zones across the country in order to reduce the number of cases. 250 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina
text: Argentina approves a vaccine made by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for use in the country, becoming the second country after the UK to approve this vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia
text: Bolivia signs a deal with Russia's Russian Direct Investment Fund to secure 2.6 million Sputnik V vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Zambia, 501.V2 variant
text: Health Minister Chitalu Chilufya confirms Zambia's first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from South Africa and also confirms that a second wave of the pandemic has emerged.

context: United States–European Union relations, Trump tariffs
text: The United States announces plans to impose additional tariffs on certain products from France and Germany, particularly aircraft parts, in retaliation to tariffs imposed by the European Union on similar U.S. products this year.

context: Abortion in Argentina > Voluntary Interruption of Pregnancy Bill
text: Argentina legalizes abortion by a Senate vote of 38 to 29, with one abstention. President Alberto Fernández has indicated that he will sign the bill into law.

Indonesia bans any activities held by the Islamic Defenders Front, a hardline Islamic group led by the controversial cleric Muhammad Rizieq Shihab. The Coordinating Political, Legal, and Security Minister Mahfud MD says the ban is necessary because the group no longer has any legal standing as a mass organisation.

context: Trade negotiation between the UK and the EU
text: The United Kingdom's House of Commons approves the EU–UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement with the European Union by 521 votes to 73.

context: Trade negotiation between the UK and the EU
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson formally signs the agreement into law.

Bobi Wine, challenger to the incumbent President Yoweri Museveni who has been in office since 1986, is arrested along with his entire campaign team in the town of Kalangala. No information about the arrest has been made available.

Scientists at the Russian Academy of Sciences announce the discovery of a "well-preserved" woolly rhinoceros carcass in Abyysky District, Sakha, Russia, which was revealed by melting permafrost in August. The Russian Academy of Sciences says that the woolly rhinoceros was likely 3 or 4 years old when it died by drowning in the river, and could be anywhere from 20,000 to 50,000 years old.

context: 2020–21 Premier League, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: A proposed match between Tottenham Hotspur and Fulham F.C. at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium that would have taken place in the evening is postponed due to a significant rise of COVID-19 cases in the clubs across the league.

Allied Democratic Forces militants kill at least 25 people in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Local officials say most of the victims were farmers working in the fields, and that some victims were decapitated.

Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison announces a change, effective January 1, to the wording of the country's national anthem, in which the word "young" in the second line "For we are young and free" is changed to "one", in an effort to reflect the country's long indigenous history.
Two people are confirmed dead and 15 others are feared dead after a landslide at an informal alluvial mining camp in Goilala District, Central Province, Papua New Guinea.

The Algerian Civil Defence says that 20 people were killed and 11 others injured when a vehicle carrying illegal migrants overturned in Tamanrasset. Tamanrasset is a crossing point for illegal migrants from neighboring countries, specifically Mali and Niger.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: A further 20 million people in England are placed into Tier 4, the level with the strictest COVID-19 restrictions. All secondary schools in England are to remain closed for an additional two weeks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 55,892 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,488,780.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium
text: Health officials report that at least 26 residents of a retirement home in Mol have died from complications related to COVID-19 since a volunteer dressed as Sinterklaas, who later tested positive for the virus, visited the home on December 5. Officials, however, have not confirmed that the volunteer was the source of the outbreak at the home, where 85 others have also tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic reports a record 16,939 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 718,661 as the positivity rate reaches 52%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports their first case of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a man who travelled from South Africa to the Haut-Rhin region and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 7,627 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 413,678.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China, COVID-19 vaccine
text: China approves BBIBP-CorV made by Sinopharm for general use, after the vaccine was considered to be 79.34% effective.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China, COVID-19 vaccine
text: The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2. The patient is a 23-year-old woman who travelled from the United Kingdom to Shanghai on December 14 and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia receives their second shipment of 1.8 million doses of CoronaVac from Sinovac.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia also reports a record 7,356 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 611,097.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Tokyo reports a record 1,337 new cases in the past 24 hours. It is the first prefecture to surpass 1,000 daily cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Nationwide, a record 4,520 new cases are reported in Japan in the past 24 hours. It is the first time that the country has reported more than 4,000 daily cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea imposes the highest level of social distancing measures at prison facilities nationwide. These restrictions will remain in effect until January 13.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Florida, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Florida confirms its first new case of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the United Kingdom. The individual is a Martin County man with no history of travel.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victoria tightens their restrictions as three new cases are reported, bringing the total number of cases in the state to six. Under the new restrictions, in-home gatherings will be limited to 15 people, masks must be worn indoors, and people are advised to stay out of the Melbourne city centre on New Year's Eve.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil detects their first two cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the United Kingdom.
The World Health Organization lists the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine for emergency use.

context: Post-Brexit United Kingdom relations with the European Union, Trade negotiation between the UK and the EU
text: The EU–UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement enters into force at 23:00 GMT, formally ending the Brexit transition period.

context: Spain–United Kingdom relations, Effect of Brexit on Gibraltar
text: Spain and the United Kingdom reach an agreement to keep Gibraltar in the European Union's Schengen Area as freedom of movement between the EU and UK is due to end.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin, Grafton vaccine incident
text: A Wisconsin pharmacist is arrested after destroying 500 doses of Moderna's vaccine.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest, Dolal Idd protests
text: The authorities arrested dozens of protesters in Minneapolis as they demanded answers into the fatal police shooting of 23-year-old Dolal Bayle Idd on December 30. The protests came after the body camera footage from a deadly traffic stop was released. At least 15 people were detained for allegedly rioting and 21 people were cited and released.

The Court of Final Appeal of Hong Kong orders pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai to return to prison on national security law grounds, after a ruling by a lower court released him on bail. Chinese state media had labeled Lai's release as "unbelievable".
Authorities in Mali charge six people, including former prime minister Boubou Cissé, with an "attempted coup".

context: COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia, 2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia
text: U.S. Senator David Perdue and his wife test negative for COVID-19, but will quarantine ahead of his upcoming runoff matchup against Jon Ossoff after coming into contact with a person in his campaign who later tested positive for the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Ontario Finance Minister Rod Phillips resigns following his trip to Saint Barthélemy while the province was in a lockdown.
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko suggests that the country would hold a referendum on constitutional reforms.
Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton is knighted by Queen Elizabeth II.
A roadside bomb kills two members of the Egyptian Armed Forces and injures five others near Bir al-Abd in the North Sinai Governorate.
Six militia members are killed during clashes between the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated and Mai-Mai Kabido in Bukumbirwa.

On New Year's Day, Pope Francis livestreams his message from the library of the Apostolic Palace. He states "the Virgin Mary’s motherly care encourages us to use our God-given time for building up the world and peace, not destroying it." In the Catholic Church, January 1 is the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God.

Eight people aged 19 die from carbon monoxide poisoning in a cottage in Tribistovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, during a New Year's celebration, after carbon monoxide leaks from a generator used to power a heater.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England > COVID-19 pandemic in London
text: The United Kingdom Secretary of State for Education Gavin Williamson announces that all primary schools in London will remain closed for at least two weeks at the start of the new term on January 4. It was previously announced that only schools in 23 of the 32 boroughs would be closed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in the Isle of Man, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The Isle of Man reports two cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Turkey reports its first 15 cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in people who traveled from the United Kingdom and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Turkey bans all travelers from the United Kingdom due to the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France announces it will tighten curfews in 15 departments beginning tomorrow at 6:00 p.m. local time in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway
text: Norway will lift its ban on flights from the United Kingdom beginning tomorrow at 4:00 p.m. GMT.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: India approves the emergency use of the vaccine developed by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca, becoming the third country in the world to do so after the United Kingdom and Argentina.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Israel becomes the first country to vaccinate at least 10% of its population against COVID-19, with around 950,000 doses already administered.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia extends the recovery phase of the Movement Control Order (MCO) nationwide except for Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Sabah as well as other locations under a conditional and enhanced MCO until March 31 due to a substantial increase in the number of new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines includes the United States in its travel ban of countries and territories reported to have new variants of SARS-CoV-2, which comes into effect on January 3. The move comes after the United States reported its first case of a new variant from the United Kingdom on December 30.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore, 501.V2 Variant
text: The Singaporean Ministry of Health announces that long-term pass holders and short-term visitors who had travel history to South Africa over the past 14 days will be not allowed to enter Singapore starting January 4, due to reports of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 circulating in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Bangkok will close all schools, daycare centers for both children and seniors, preschools and tutoring centers from January 4 to 17. Other public facilities will be closed beginning January 2. This comes as the authorities tighten measures to reduce the spread of a new wave of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports a record 585 new deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 20 million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Chad
text: Chadian President Idriss Déby signs a decree that imposes a lockdown in the country's capital N'Djamena for the first time since the pandemic began and also declares a dusk-to-dawn curfew due to a rise in the number of cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay
text: Uruguay reports a record of 12 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 193.
Taiwanese President Tsai Ing-wen says that she is ready to have talks with China and urges the country to have dialogues with Taiwan.

context: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, Nuclear program of Iran
text: The International Atomic Energy Agency says Iran has notified it of its intention to enrich uranium to 20% purity, in accordance with a law recently passed by the Islamic Consultative Assembly. Iran did not specify when this enrichment would begin. The December 2020 bill, adopted after the assassination of Iranian nuclear scientist Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, instructs the government to increase uranium enrichment if sanctions against Iran are not eased within two months.
The African Continental Free Trade Area, the largest free-trade area since the formation of the World Trade Organization in 1995, commences.
Initiative 190 comes into effect in Montana, making it the 13th state to legalize recreational cannabis.

context: George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon, 2020–2021 United States racial unrest
text: On December 31 and into the early hours of January 1, protesters and police clashed in a New Year's Eve protest which police declared a riot shortly before midnight, alleging the demonstrators' use of violence. Within 30 minutes, police advanced on the demonstration, protesters used fireworks while officers shot pepper balls, rubber bullets, and other "less-lethal munitions". In the wake of the protests, the Portland Police Bureau order all people in the area to leave immediately. Authorities have not stated the number of protesters arrested.

The United States Senate votes 81–13 to override President Donald Trump's veto of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021. This is the first successful veto override of the Trump presidency.

context: War on terror > Insurgency in the Maghreb > 2021 Tillabéri attacks
text: At least 79 civilians are killed and 20 others are injured when Islamist militants attack two villages simultaneously in Tillabéri, Niger, near the border with Mali.

context: War on terror > Insurgency in the Maghreb
text: Two Algerian People's National Army personnel and four militants are killed during a gunfight in Messelmoun, Algeria.

context: War on terror > Mali War > Operation Barkhane
text: Two French Army personnel are killed when their armoured personnel carrier hit a roadside bomb in Ménaka, Mali. It is the second attack in the past few days that targeted French military personnel, the first being the December 28 JNIM-claimed bombing that killed three French military personnel.

context: War on terror > Somali Civil War
text: Five people are killed, including two Turkish nationals, after an al-Shabaab suicide bomber blew himself up near the Mogadishu-Afgooye road construction work. Fourteen people are injured, including four other Turkish citizens.
Eleven Hazara coal miners are kidnapped near their mine and then killed nearby by Khorasan Daesh militants in Machh, Pakistan.

Pope Francis accepts the resignation of Auxiliary Bishop Richard Brendan Higgins, the episcopal vicar for veterans affairs of the Archdiocese for the Military Services. During his career, Bishop Higgins’ is vicar for veterans affairs and responsible for more than 200 chaplains serving at over 150 veterans' affairs hospitals in the United States, Puerto Rico and Guam. His retirement at age 75 is announced in Washington, D.C. by Archbishop Christophe Pierre, the apostolic nuncio to the United States.
Rescue workers find the bodies of four people who went missing during a landslide in Gjerdrum, Viken, Norway, on December 30. Six people are still missing.
Three people are killed when a small plane crashes into a house in Lyon Township, Michigan, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 57,725 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the highest daily total since the beginning of the pandemic. Another 445 deaths are also reported, bringing the country's death toll to 74,570.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reactivates emergency critical-care COVID-19 hospitals amid a surge in both cases and hospitalizations.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Over 800,000 people in Russia have received the Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Gibraltar
text: Gibraltar imposes a second lockdown for the next 14 days beginning at 10:00 p.m. local time (21:00 GMT) today, in order to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: The Government of Greece announces a one-week closure of all shops that were allowed to reopen during the holiday season, as well as all places of worship beginning tomorrow in order to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases ahead of the reopening of schools on January 11. A curfew from 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time will also be imposed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 7,582 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 625,518.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: East Java Governor Khofifah Indar Parawansa tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 3,321 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 94,492.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea, 501.V2 variant
text: South Korea reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 when a person who traveled from South Africa on December 26 later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Vietnam reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 when a 44-year-old woman who traveled from the United Kingdom later tested positive for COVID-19 while in quarantine on December 24.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victoria closes its land border with New South Wales due to an increase in COVID-19 cases, after several months of open borders. Meanwhile, New South Wales makes wearing masks in public mandatory, while also easing restrictions for southern suburbs of the Northern Beaches as the number of cases in those areas decrease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Palau, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Palau receives 2,800 doses of the Moderna vaccine in a special contribution from the United States. The government announced that it will vaccinate healthcare workers first and then vaccinate seniors and people with medical conditions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York surpasses one million cases of COVID-19, becoming the fourth state to do so after Texas, California and Florida.
Kazakhstan formally abolishes the death penalty, making a two-decade freeze on executions permanent, according to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.
The Hennepin County Sheriff's Office releases footage of deputies executing a search warrant on the last known address of Dolal Idd, as well as a raid on his family's house.
Authorities in Pakistan arrest Zakiur Rehman Lakhvi, alleged leader of the Lashker-e-Taiba group, which is blamed for the 2008 Mumbai attacks that killed 166 people.

The homes of United States Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell and House Speaker Nancy Pelosi are vandalized after the government failed to pass the CASH Act, a bill that would increase direct payments from $600 to $2,000.

Saïd Bouteflika, the brother and special advisor of former Algerian president Abdelaziz Bouteflika, is cleared of conspiracy charges following a retrial. Saïd Bouteflika had been sentenced to 15 years in prison in 2019 for "undermining the authority of the armed forces" and "conspiring against the authority of the state" following his brother's resignation in the context of the 2019–20 Algerian protests.

The electoral commission of Niger declares that a second round of the presidential election will take place on February 21 after no candidate received a majority of the vote. The two candidates will be former minister Mohamed Bazoum, the leader of the ruling Nigerien Party for Democracy and Socialism, who won the first round with 39.33% of the votes; and former president Mahamane Ousmane, who won 16.99% of votes.

context: War on terror > Insurgency in the Maghreb > 2021 Tillabéri attacks
text: Twenty-one more people are found dead and others die of their injuries a day after the attacks in Tchombangou and Zaroumdareye, in Tillabéri, Niger, bringing the death toll to 100. More than 75 others are wounded.

context: War on terror > Mali War > Mali wedding airstrike
text: A group of Islamist insurgents take hostages in Mopti. While separating the victims by gender, an airstrike killed at least 20 people.
Rebel forces seize the city of Bangassou in southeastern Central African Republic after storming the city in a pre-dawn raid, according to MINUSCA officials.
Islamic State insurgents kill nine people and wound 16 others in an ambush targeting buses traveling down a highway in central Syria.
A relief worker is killed and three others wounded after Islamic State-linked militants opens fire on their vehicle in Maguindanao, Philippines.
Rescue workers find the bodies of three people who went missing during a landslide in Gjerdrum, Viken, Norway, on December 30, bringing the death toll to seven. Three people are still missing.

At least 18 people are killed during a funeral in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, India, when the roof they were sheltering under during heavy rainfall collapses. Police dispatch rescue workers and sniffer dogs, and they say that the rescue operation has been completed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Cyprus reports its first cases of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in 12 people who traveled from the United Kingdom and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports its first cases of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in four people who traveled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19 after a record 4,962 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway
text: Prime Minister Erna Solberg announces a series of new nationwide restrictions including a ban on alcohol being served in restaurants and bars and an advisory against having any guests in private residences in order to reduce the spread of a third wave of cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom begins distribution of the AstraZeneca and University of Oxford vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: India officially approves the emergency use of AstraZeneca and University of Oxford's AZD1222 vaccine, which is to be manufactured locally by the Serum Institute of India, as well as Bharat Biotech's BBV152 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait; Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Kuwait announces the suspension of direct commercial passenger flights to and from the United Kingdom beginning January 6 at 4:00 a.m. in order to reduce the spread of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Saudi Arabia reopens its air, sea, and land borders, and resumes international passenger flights as well, after borders were closed in December to prevent the spread of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the UK. People arriving from South Africa, the United Kingdom, and other countries where the new variant is spreading are required to spend 14 days in another country and present a negative test result prior to entering Saudi Arabia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Thailand reports its first case of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a British national who traveled from the United Kingdom and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Thailand announces it will get two million doses of CoronaVac starting in February.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Egypt approves the use of Sinopharm's BBIBP-CorV vaccine, with the vaccination campaign expected to start later this month. Egypt plans to buy 40 million doses of this vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya
text: President Uhuru Kenyatta signs an executive order that bans all gatherings except funerals and weddings of up to 150 people. He also extends the nationwide night curfew until March 12.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: New Zealand reports six cases of new variants of SARS-CoV-2 in five people who traveled from the United Kingdom and another who traveled from South Africa, all between December 13 and 25, and who later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil > COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil
text: The Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency announces that the country will receive 2 million doses of AstraZeneca's vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses 600,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: Assassination of Qasem Soleimani, American intervention in Iraq
text: Thousands of Iraqis demand American forces withdraw from the country during protests in Liberation Square, Baghdad, a year after an American drone strike killed Iran's general Qasem Soleimani and Iraq's militia commander, Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. The anniversary of their deaths in Baghdad was also marked in Iran as well as by supporters in Syria, Lebanon, Yemen and other Middle East countries.

context: Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election > Trump–Raffensperger phone call
text: The Washington Post releases the recording of a telephone conversation where United States President Donald Trump calls Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger to pressure him to "find 11,780 votes" in his favor.

context: 2021 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
text: The 117th United States Congress begins. Nancy Pelosi is re-elected as Speaker of the House with a narrow seven-vote majority (216–209).

context: Kivu conflict > Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
text: Twenty-two people are killed during an Allied Democratic Forces mass stabbing at a village in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports three new cases of the new Alpha variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan surpasses 500,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Officials in Mississippi announce a plan to distribute vaccines for people over 65 years of age.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico, COVID-19 vaccine
text: According to the New Mexico Department of Health, over 230,000 people in the state have signed up to receive vaccinations.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: New York reports its first case of the new SARS-CoV-2 Alpha variant in a man in his 60s from Saratoga County who tested positive for COVID-19 despite having no travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria abandons a plan to allow anyone with a negative test result to exit the lockdown a week early, instead extending strict measures and keeping restaurants and non-essential shops closed until January 24.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Contrary to the strategy adopted by the United Kingdom, Spain is expected to maintain its plan to administer two doses per person of the COVID-19 vaccine tozinameran, which is the recommendation of the manufacturer Pfizer-BioNTech. Germany is also considering the single-dose strategy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: British Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces a third nationwide lockdown in England beginning at midnight. All schools and universities will be closed until mid-February and people will only be allowed to leave their homes for essential reasons like shopping and exercise.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon announces that a lockdown in level four areas such as mainland Scotland will begin at midnight, and that there will be a legal requirement to stay at home for the remainder of the month. Schools will also remain closed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 58,784 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,713,563.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: The Lebanese Government announces a 25-day nationwide lockdown in the country beginning January 7 in order to reduce the increase in COVID-19 cases that occurred during the holiday season. A curfew from 6:00 p.m. until 5:00 a.m. local time will also be in effect until February 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia surpasses 500 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reports a record 745 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4,639.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Vietnam agrees to buy 30 million doses of AstraZeneca's vaccine.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard seizes a South Korean-flagged ship in the Persian Gulf over alleged oil pollution and environmental hazards. The ship was travelling from Saudi Arabia to the port of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates.

context: United States and the International Criminal Court
text: United States District Judge Katherine Polk Failla blocks the Trump administration from imposing sanctions on the International Criminal Court.

United States Representatives Ted Lieu and Kathleen Rice urge Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Christopher A. Wray to open a criminal investigation into President Donald Trump's phone call with Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger for violating state and federal laws. Additionally, Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis announces that her office is ready to investigate Trump after his call with Raffensperger.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: British Member of Parliament Margaret Ferrier is arrested after breaching COVID-19 restrictions.
Proud Boys chairperson Enrique Tarrio is arrested for destroying a Black Lives Matter sign at the Asbury United Methodist Church during a protest in Washington, D.C., last month.

A Malaysian coroner concludes that 15-year-old French-Irish tourist Nora Quoirin, who disappeared in August 2019 while vacationing at a resort in Seremban and whose body was found in a nearby jungle ten days later, had died by misadventure. Quoirin's family questions the verdict, saying that evidence suggests that her death was caused by abduction, homicide, or sexual assault.

A judge in the United Kingdom blocks the extradition of WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to the United States, citing that it would be "oppressive" to his mental health and also cites the likelihood of Assange committing suicide if he is sent to the United States. If convicted in the United States, Assange could face up to 175 years in prison. Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador says that his country is willing to provide political asylum to Assange.

Kidnapped Auxiliary Bishop Moses Chikwe, of the Owerri Archdiocese in Nigeria, is freed by his captors. Kidnapped last Sunday, police allege that no ransom is paid. International condemnation includes Pope Francis, during his new year message calling for Bishop Chikwe's release. While in Imo state, a Catholic women's organization, stage a peaceful protest at the Imo state government house, calling on Governor Hope Uzodinma, to quicken action for the release of the Auxiliary Bishop.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen announces the increase of the COVID-19 risk level from level 4 to 5, indicating "widespread infection in society", as well as "a risk that treatment capacity at hospitals will be exceeded". In addition, public and private gatherings will be limited to five people. The rules will be in effect until January 17.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Chancellor Angela Merkel and leaders of 16 states agree to extend the country's lockdown until January 31.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy's Council of Ministers approves a decree that prohibits travel between the country's regions except for health or work reasons, with people in "red zone" areas only allowed to move once per day. They also extend most lockdown restrictions until January 15. The country will be in a "yellow zone" on January 7 and 8, with eased restrictions and allowing restaurants, bars, shops and malls to open, while on January 9 and 10 the country will be in an "orange zone", with malls closed and restaurants and bars open for takeaway and delivery only.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: Maltese president George Vella receives his first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland
text: The Northern Ireland Executive issues a stay-at-home order in Northern Ireland, which is currently in the second week of a six-week lockdown, legally enforceable from January 8, in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 60,916 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,774,479.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin announces that a nationwide mass vaccination program against COVID-19 will begin on January 13. President Joko Widodo will become the first person in the country to receive a vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Iran reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in an Iranian who travelled from the United Kingdom and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: The Israeli Cabinet agrees to tighten the nationwide lockdown by closing schools and non-essential shops for 14 days. The measures will come into force at midnight between Thursday and Friday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 4,915 new cases in the past 24 hours. In addition, a record 76 deaths are also reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Oman reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a resident who travelled from the United Kingdom and tested positive while in quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea surpasses 1,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda bans public and private transport in and out of Kigali and between districts and extends a curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time for another 15 days amid a deadly second wave of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe reports 1,365 new confirmed cases and 34 deaths in the past 24 hours, its largest daily increase for both cases and deaths since the pandemic began as the country begins a month-long lockdown to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Georgia reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in an 18-year-old male with no travel history, and who is currently in isolation at home.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. surpasses 21 million cases of COVID-19, just four days after surpassing 20 million cases.

Saudi Arabia reopens its border with Qatar, ending the three-year diplomatic crisis. The resolution was brokered by Kuwait and the United States. ([https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/saudi-arabia-lifts-blockade-qatar-breakthrough-agreement-eases-gulf-crisis-n1250102 NBC News])
Kosovo's parliament unanimously approves deploying the Kosovo Security Force on international peacekeeping missions, following a formal request by the United States Central Command.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest > Shooting of Jacob Blake, Kenosha unrest > Kenosha unrest shooting
text: Kyle Rittenhouse, the 17-year-old boy accused of shooting three people (including two killed) during a protest in Kenosha, Wisconsin, will plead not guilty.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest > Shooting of Jacob Blake, Kenosha unrest
text: Kenosha County District Attorney Michael Graveley announces that no charges will be made against Rusten Sheskey, the Kenosha police officer accused of shooting Jacob Blake.
Washington, D.C. mayor Muriel Bowser activates the District of Columbia National Guard due to an organized protest of pro-Trump supporters.
A federal judge bans Proud Boys chairman Enrique Tarrio from entering Washington, D.C.

Iran requests that Interpol issue a red notice for the arrest of U.S. President Donald Trump and 47 other U.S. officials for their role in the assassination of Qasem Soleimani in January 2020. A similar request was previously rejected by Interpol.

A court in Vietnam sentences three freelance journalists to between 11 and 15 years in prison for anti-state propaganda, criticising the government and "infringing the interests of the Communist Party", among other convictions.
Cleta Mitchell resigns from her law firm after participating in President Trump's phone call with Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger.

context: 2020 United States Senate elections > 2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia, 2020–21 United States Senate special election in Georgia
text: Voters in Georgia head to the polls to cast their votes to determine who will control the United States Senate. Republican Senator David Perdue will face Democrat Jon Ossoff, and incumbent Republican Kelly Loeffler will face Democrat Raphael Warnock.
Alabama wide receiver DeVonta Smith wins the Heisman Trophy, making him the first receiver to do so since Desmond Howard in 1991.

Team USA defeats Team Canada 2–0 in the gold medal game to win the 2021 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships, while Team Finland defeats Team Russia 4–1 in the bronze medal game. Team USA's Trevor Zegras is named MVP of the tournament.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: Thousands of pro-Trump protesters storm the United States Capitol, causing it to be evacuated. Washington, D.C. mayor Muriel Bowser proclaimed a citywide nighttime curfew. Shots were fired, and at least six people were injured. A woman died from gunshot wounds by Police, according to police. Multiple members of Congress called this an attempted coup d'état. The FBI, police, and National Guard from Maryland, Virginia, and D.C. itself were deployed to stop the riot. Smoke bombs and pepper spray were also used. Multiple suspected pipe bombs were reported, including at the Republican Party headquarters.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: U.S President pro tempore Chuck Grassley announces that the United States Senate has entered recess as Senator James Lankford (R-OK) was given out a speech, with an aide informing Lankford that pro-Trump protesters were entering the building. Additionally, the U.S. House enters a recess.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: The United States Senate chamber and House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's office are also breached by pro-Trump protesters.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: President-elect Joe Biden says "It's not a protest, it's an insurrection", and calls on President Donald Trump to "demand an end to this siege" by his followers. In response, President Trump released a video saying, "These are the things and events that happen when a sacred landslide election victory is so unceremoniously & viciously stripped away from great patriots who have been badly & unfairly treated for so long. Go home with love & in peace. Remember this day forever!"

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: At least seven Democratic members of Congress, including Ilhan Omar, Ayanna Pressley and Seth Moulton, and Republican Vermont Governor Phil Scott, call for Trump's immediate resignation or impeachment and removal by Congress, when it can reconvene, for insurrection against the United States.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: The United States Capitol Police says that the Capitol was secured by 6 p.m. The Electoral College certificates were also secured.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: Three more people die during the United States Capitol riots during "separate medical emergencies", bringing the total death toll to four.

context: 2020–21 United States election protests > January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: Stephanie Grisham resigns as the Chief of Staff to the First Lady as a result of the riots. Matt Pottinger resigns as deputy national security adviser; Mick Mulvaney, former chief of staff, resigns from his remaining duties as special envoy to Northern Ireland and Anna Cristina Niceta resigns as White House social secretary.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel's role in the Syrian Civil War
text: Israel launches airstrikes against IRGC and Hezbollah bases near Damascus, Syria.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in China
text: Members of the World Health Organization investigating the origins of the pandemic are denied entry into China.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 8,854 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 788,402.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto announces two-week restrictions in parts of the islands of Java and Bali beginning January 11.
