text: China reports 138 new cases in the past 24 hours, the biggest single-day increase in more than 10 months, bringing the total number of cases since the beginning of the outbreak to 87,844. In addition, the country also reports its first death from COVID-19 since April, bringing the nationwide death toll to 4,635.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 11,557 new cases, bringing the nationwide total to 869,600 confirmed cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 3,337 new cases, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 147,855.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, COVID-19 vaccine
text: The Food and Drug Administration approves the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine for emergency use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in the Gambia
text: The Gambia reports their first two cases of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a 34-year-old man who travelled to the United Kingdom and an 82-year-old woman who also tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria
text: The Federal Ministry of Education announces that schools in Nigeria will reopen on January 18. Parents have appealed to the ministry to rescind the decision following a recent spike in COVID-19 cases.

context: Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Lineage B.1.1.248
text: British Transport Secretary Grant Shapps announces a ban on all travellers from South American countries, as well as Portugal, Panama and Cape Verde due to a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that was identified in Brazil. The ban will come into effect tomorrow at 4:00 a.m. GMT.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) says that Iran has informed them that it has begun installing equipment for the production of uranium metal, another violation in kind in response to Western violations of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. The IAEA says that Iran now has enough enriched uranium to make a nuclear weapon, but still possesses less than it had before the deal was signed.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia announces the arrest of Kevin Seefried, a Delaware man who was seen carrying the Confederate flag during the storming of the United States Capitol. His son, Hunter Seefried, is also arrested.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The Department of Justice announces that Robert Sanford, a retired firefighter from Boothwyn, Pennsylvania, has been arrested for allegedly throwing a fire extinguisher at Capitol Police officers during the storming of the Capitol.

context: Crime in Australia > Domestic violence in Australia
text: A mother and three children are found dead in a suspected murder–suicide in Tullamarine, Victoria, in the second case of suspected familicide in Victoria in the past week.
The Supreme Court upholds former President Park Geun-hye's 22-year prison sentence for corruption.

Eight more Michigan officials are charged along with former Governor Rick Snyder for their roles in the Flint water crisis. Former health director Nick Lyon and former state medical executive Eden Wells are also charged with involuntary manslaughter in the deaths of nine people who contracted Legionnaires' disease during the crisis.

Voters head to the polls to elect their next president and parliament. The two main presidential candidates are incumbent President Yoweri Museveni and opposition activist and musician Bobi Wine. The election has been widely criticized as being unfair, with both the United States and European Union cancelling their observations of the election.

context: War in Afghanistan > Taliban insurgency, 2021 Afghanistan attacks
text: At least nine security personnel are killed in Kunduz, near the border with Tajikistan, when Taliban insurgents simultaneously attack two checkpoints.
An Egyptian UN peacekeeper is killed and another injured after a bomb planted by jihadists detonates under a truck that was part of a UN logistics convoy.
A Burundian UN peacekeeper is killed in a rebel ambush near Grimari in Ouaka, Central African Republic, acccording to MINUSCA. Two Bangladeshi peacekeepers are also wounded in the attack.

Canadian convenience store chain Alimentation Couche-Tard withdraws its bid to take over the French retailer Carrefour, after the French government expressed its intent to veto the €16 billion (US$19.5 billion) deal.

A magnitude 6.2 earthquake strikes the Majene Regency in West Sulawesi, Indonesia, killing at least 42 people and wounding more than 820 others. It was preceded by a foreshock measuring 5.7 a few hours before.
The number of COVID-19 deaths worldwide surpasses two million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine
text: Governor Janet Mills receives her first dose of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: President-elect Joe Biden is expected to deploy the United States National Guard and FEMA resources to distribute vaccines across the United States when he takes office. He also says that he will invoke the Defense Production Act to produce vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Illinois reports their first case of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who traveled to the United Kingdom and the Middle East and was later diagnosed with COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Oregon, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Oregon reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated from the United Kingdom in a man from Multnomah County with no travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Utah, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Utah reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated from the United Kingdom in a man from Salt Lake County with no travel history who tested positive last month.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Governor Tony Evers announces that the state will extend its mask mandate for 60 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico reports a record 21,366 new confirmed cases, bringing the total of confirmed cases to 1.61 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in China > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China reports 144 new cases, the majority in Hebei and Heilongjiang provinces. This is the highest number of daily cases in the past 10 months and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 87,988.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Uttarakhand, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Uttarakhand reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a 44-year old man who was in close contact with people who travelled to the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 12,818 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, including 3,095 in West Java, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 882,418.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia extends their movement control order to Kelantan beginning at midnight as COVID-19 cases continue to rise.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines extends until January 31 its travel ban on more than 30 countries and territories where cases of SARS-CoV-2 variants have been reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany surpasses two million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 159 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 8,543.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports a record 40,197 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 2,252,164.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden > COVID-19 vaccination in Sweden
text: King of Sweden Carl XVI Gustaf receives his first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces the closure of all travel corridors beginning January 18 at 4:00 a.m. GMT. He also announces that all travellers must have proof of a negative COVID-19 test from the previous 72 hours and quarantine for 10 days upon arrival, unless they test negative after five days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile
text: The Chilean government reports 4,471 new cases, the highest daily total since June. A potential new lockdown in the Santiago Metropolitan Region is under evaluation according to the Ministry of Health.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Paraguay, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Paraguay approves the emergency use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, becoming the fourth South American country to approve the use of the vaccine against COVID-19, after Argentina, Bolivia and Venezuela. Supply of the vaccine will be facilitated by the Russian Direct Investment Fund.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia reports a record 4,170 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours as the country enters a four-day lockdown and also closes all schools until January 24 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.
Authorities in Namibia suspend the importation and transit of poultry from European countries where an outbreak of the Avian influenza subtype H5N8 has been reported.

Russia says that it will withdraw from the Treaty on Open Skies, following the U.S. withdrawal from the treaty last year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says that the U.S. withdrawal has "significantly upended the balance of interests of signatory states".

context: Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack
text: The Federal Bureau of Investigation announces that far-right activist Tim Gionet, commonly known as "Baked Alaska", has been arrested in Houston for participating in the attack on the United States Capitol.

The family of Abdelbaset al-Megrahi, the Lockerbie bomber, loses a posthumous appeal at a top Scottish court against his conviction. Al-Megrahi was the only person convicted for the terrorist attack, whereas his family say that he was the victim of a "miscarriage of justice".
Opposition activist Bobi Wine claims victory in the presidential election, despite early results giving incumbent President Yoweri Museveni a wide lead, and calls the results "a joke".
Bobi Wine tweets that the military has "taken control" of his home and placed him under house arrest, just hours after claiming victory in the disputed election.
Outgoing United States Vice President Mike Pence congratulates incoming Vice President Kamala Harris, 73 days after the presidential election.
The third Rutte cabinet of the Netherlands falls after negotiations regarding the childcare allowance scandal.

President Mahmoud Abbas announces that the legislative elections will be held on May 22, while the presidential elections will be held on July 31. These are the first elections in the State of Palestine since 2006.

The Lao People's Revolutionary Party elects Prime Minister Thongloun Sisoulith as its new General Secretary, replacing retiring chief Bounnhang Vorachit. Sisoulith was elected for a five-year term as leader of the Central Committee of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party, the top post in the country, and part of the country's Politburo.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on association football, COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: FC Barcelona postpones its presidential election originally scheduled for January 24, following an increase in COVID-19 cases in Catalonia.

Hundreds of residents flee and government forces withdraw after the town of Marte in Borno State, Nigeria, is captured by Islamic State – West Africa Province militants. The military says it "tactically withdrew" troops, while confirming the town is under insurgent control.
Automotive manufacturers Fiat Chrysler and PSA finalize their 50–50 merger agreement, founding Stellantis. The new corporation becomes the world's fourth largest automobile manufacturer by volume.
Five people die of carbon monoxide poisoning at a nursing home in Lanuvio, Lazio, Italy. Seven other people are hospitalized in critical condition.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses 700,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Los Angeles County surpasses one million cases of COVID-19, becoming the first county in the United States to do so.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Los Angeles County reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a man who traveled to the United Kingdom and is currently in quarantine in Oregon.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Michigan reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a woman from Washtenaw County who traveled to the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Louisiana, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Louisiana reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in the Greater New Orleans area.
sources: Office of the Governor of Louisiana

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wyoming, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Wyoming reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a man from Teton County with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launches the world's largest vaccination programme against COVID-19 in India, which plans to vaccinate more than 1.3 billion people. A sanitation worker is the first person to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 14,224 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 896,642.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 4,029 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 155,095.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan approves the AstraZeneca vaccine for emergency use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark, 501.V2 variant
text: Denmark reports their first case of the South African variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who travelled to Dubai.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports records for both daily counts of new cases and deaths, with 10,947 new cases and 166 deaths, bringing the nationwide cumulative totals to 539,416 confirmed cases and 8,709 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia
text: Serbia receives one million doses of Sinopharm's BBIBP-CorV vaccine. They are the first European country to receive a Chinese-made vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Vice President Fuat Oktay receives the first dose of the CoronaVac vaccine at a hospital in Ankara.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina > COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina
text: Argentina receives their second batch of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina
text: Argentina also reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a man who travelled from the United Kingdom in late December and later tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil > COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil
text: The Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency announces that the country has returned documents from União Química seeking approval for Russia's Sputnik V vaccine as it didn't meet the criteria.

context: Qatar–Saudi Arabia relations, Qatar diplomatic crisis
text: Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud announces that Saudi Arabia will re-open its embassy in Qatar in the coming days, after a diplomatic crisis that saw the nations severing ties for three years.

context: Capital punishment in the United States
text: The federal government carries out its final execution under the Trump administration, executing convicted murderer Dustin Higgs by lethal injection at USP Terre Haute in Indiana.

context: 2021 Christian Democratic Union of Germany leadership election
text: North Rhine-Westphalia minister-president Armin Laschet is elected leader of the Christian Democratic Union, one of the ruling parties in the Bundestag and the party of incumbent Chancellor Angela Merkel. Laschet's election makes him a front-runner to be the party's candidate in the federal election in September.

The Electoral Commission of Uganda declares incumbent President Yoweri Museveni the winner of the presidential election, winning about 59% of the vote, while opposition leader Bobi Wine received only 35% of the vote, according to the commission.

context: War in Afghanistan > 2021 Afghanistan attacks; Taliban insurgency
text: Two judges, both female, are shot dead in an ambush while en-route to their offices at the Supreme Court in Kabul; their driver is wounded. Afghan officials claim the Taliban is responsible, however no one has claimed responsibility for the attack and a spokesman for the Taliban, Zabihullah Mujahid, says that the group was not responsible.
Eighty-three people are killed during clashes between different ethnic groups in El Geneina, West Darfur, Sudan. They started after a row in which a man was stabbed to death.
More bodies are found under debris in Sulawesi, Indonesia, after a magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck the island two days ago, bringing the death toll to 78.
A Bell UH-1 Iroquois helicopter of the Philippine Air Force crashes in the Pantaron Mountain Range in Bukidnon, Philippines, killing all seven personnel onboard.
Six people have been killed by floods and landslides that affected nine subdistricts and 33 neighborhoods in Manado, North Sulawesi, Indonesia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 9,102 recoveries, bringing the total number of recoveries to 736,460.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: Lebanon signs a deal to receive two million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman
text: Oman announces the closure of all land borders for at least one week, beginning tomorrow at 6:00 p.m., as part of measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates reports a record 3,453 new confirmed cases in a single-day, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 253,261.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Guinea
text: Guinean President Alpha Condé receives the first dose of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa, 501.V2 variant
text: South Africa delays the reopening of schools due to the rapid increase in cases of the 501.V2 variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: American music producer Phil Spector, who was convicted for the 2003 murder of American actress Lana Clarkson, dies from COVID-19 at a hospital in Northern California.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Massachusetts reports their first case of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a woman in her 20s from Boston who traveled to the United Kingdom and began experiencing symptoms the day after she returned.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, COVID-19 vaccine
text: The Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (Anvisa) grants emergency use authorization requests for the vaccines developed by Sinovac and Oxford-AstraZeneca.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Minutes after Anvisa's announcement, a nurse from São Paulo becomes the first person in Brazil to receive a COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria extends their nationwide lockdown until February 7 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19 amid fears about new SARS-CoV-2 variants. People will also be required to wear full protective masks beginning January 25.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Otero County Commissioner Couy Griffin, the founder of "Cowboys for Trump", is arrested for his involvement during the storming of the United States Capitol, in which he allegedly entered restricted area during the riot. He claimed to be planning to drive to Washington, D.C. with a rifle and revolver.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Gracyn Courtright, a West Virginia student who is a senior at the University of Kentucky, is charged for entering the United States Capitol during the riot.

context: Aftermath of the poisoning of Alexei Navalny
text: Opposition politician and anti-corruption activist Alexei Navalny is arrested upon landing in Moscow, according to a statement from the prison service. The prominent Putin critic was arrested on charges of parole violations and terms of a suspended prison sentence and will be held in custody until a court makes a decision in his case.

A caravan of at least 6,000 Honduran migrants bound for the United States prompts the deployment of Guatemalan police and military troops to the Guatemala–Honduras border, where security forces fire tear gas and assault migrants attempting to cross the border. Health officials report several casualties.

context: War in Afghanistan > 2021 Afghanistan attacks; Taliban insurgency
text: Over 40 security force members have been killed in fighting with the Taliban in Kunduz, Baghlan and Nimroz provinces, Afghanistan.
Two United Nation peacekeepers, from Gabon and Morocco, are killed in an ambush by anti-balaka insurgents near Bangassou, Central African Republic, according to MINUSCA.

Houthi forces and pro-government troops clash in the port city of Al Hudaydah, leaving at least 23 people dead. The fighting centered around the government-controlled Ad Durayhimi District in the south of the city. Houthi-run Almasirah network claims "dozens" of government fighters have been killed.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin announces a new RM15 billion economic assistance package, the Malaysian Economic and Rakyat Protection Assistance Package, which is expected to reduce the impact of COVID-19 on the Malaysian economy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in China > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports 107 new confirmed cases, which is the first time in nearly a month that more than 100 cases are reported and brings the total number of confirmed cases in the city to 9,664. This sudden rise in cases is partially due to an outbreak among ethnic minorities.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Lakshadweep
text: The Indian union territory of Lakshadweep reports their first case of COVID-19 in a man who left for Kavaratti by ship from Kochi, making it the last territory to report their first case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 9,475 recoveries, including 2,802 from Jakarta, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 745,935.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan detects possible community spread of the B.1.1.7 variant in three people from Shizuoka with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Nepal reports their first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in three people who travelled to the United Kingdom three weeks ago and later tested positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkmenistan
text: Turkmenistan registers the Sputnik V vaccine despite having no confirmed cases in the country, according to the Russian Direct Investment Fund. It becomes the first country in Central Asia to approve a Russian-made vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic confirms the detection of the B.1.1.7 variant that originated in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Bavaria detects a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in 35 newly-infected patients in Garmisch-Partenkirchen, which is different from the strain originating from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Hair salons, health centers, car inspection stations, and non-essential shops in Greece reopen for the first time since November after the government eased a nationwide lockdown in order to revitalize the retail sectors.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 167 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,028.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The Spanish Health Ministry reports a record 84,287 new cases in the country over the weekend, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,336,451.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Outgoing U.S. President Donald Trump signs an executive order that allows travel restrictions on Brazil, the United Kingdom, and Europe to be lifted after January 26. However, incoming Press Secretary Jen Psaki says that the restrictions are expected to remain in place.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California becomes the first U.S. state to surpass three million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Maryland Governor Larry Hogan receives the Moderna vaccine at the State House in Annapolis.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania
text: Thirty-nine residents are confirmed to have died from COVID-19 at a single nursing home in Denver, Pennsylvania.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Morocco reports its first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in the Port of Tangier Med.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the environment
text: The International Energy Agency reports that global methane emissions in 2020 amounted to about 70 million metric tons, which is 10 percent lower than the estimated amount of methane emissions in 2019. The agency cites the decline in industrial activities, as a result of the pandemic, and the introduction of new emission regulations for the reduction in emissions.

Germany condemns the arrest of opposition politician and activist Alexei Navalny upon his return to Russia yesterday. German Foreign Minister Heiko Maas calls the arrest "utterly incomprehensible" and calls for Navalny's immediate release. Likewise, British, Danish, and other European diplomats also condemn the arrest.

South Korean President Moon Jae-in urges incoming U.S. President Joe Biden to learn from the policies, both positive and negative, of Donald Trump towards North Korea and says that the North has a "clear willingness to denuclearize if Washington and Pyongyang could find mutually agreeable steps to decrease the nuclear threat and ensure the North's security".

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Fashion Institute of Technology student Nicholas Moncada is arrested for allegedly storming the United States Capitol, after posting "Outside Pelosi's office" on Instagram and livestreaming the event.

The COO of Samsung, Lee Jae-yong, is sentenced to two and a half years in prison on charges of bribery. Lee was convicted of bribing former South Korean President Park Geun-hye and was arrested in the courtroom following the verdict.

Guatemalan police report that around 4,000 United States-bound Honduran migrants held up at the Guatemala–Honduras border since January 16 have been dispersed. Police have used various riot control methods to disperse migrants.

The Tunisian interior ministry deploys the national guard in several cities across the country and reports that a total of 632 people have been arrested following a series of riots that first occurred January 15, a day after the government imposed a nationwide lockdown in response to an increase in COVID-19 cases.

The constitutional court of the Central African Republic confirms the re-election of President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, despite a voter turnout of only 35.25 percent. The low turnout was attributed to the hindrance of polling stations from operating and voters unable to cast their ballots as various armed groups currently control roughly two-thirds of the country, thus prompting most opposition candidates and activists to call the election farce and fraudulent.

context: Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan cancels the upcoming Taiwan Lantern Festival for the first time since 1990, due to an increase in COVID-19 cases on the island.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration of the United States orders Ford Motor Company to recall about three million of its vehicles containing airbags manufactured by Takata, citing "potential future rupture risks".
Fifteen people are killed by a truck in Surat, India while they were sleeping by a road.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: Andrew Yang, a candidate for Mayor of New York City in the upcoming mayoral election, will quarantine after one of his staffers tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Vermont
text: Vermont Governor Phil Scott, Health Commissioner Mark Levine, and other officials quarantine after a contractor that Levine was in contact with tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: A memorial at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is held, honoring the 400,000 Americans who have died as a result of COVID-19. Additionally, bells are rung at the Washington National Cathedral and a moment of silence is held.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 400,000 deaths from COVID-19, just five weeks after passing 300,000 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico reports a record 1,584 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to nearly 143,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a new record for the second consecutive day, of 218 deaths, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,246. At the same time, the nationwide number of ICU patients reaches a record 670, just below the maximum allocation capacity of 672 ICU beds set the day before.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portuguese Economy Minister Pedro Siza Vieira tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: The first 30,000 doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine are sent from Spain to Andorra after both governments reached an agreement earlier today.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Chancellor Angela Merkel and the leaders of all 16 states agree to extend the nationwide lockdown until February 14, due to the threat of new variants of SARS-CoV-2. They also agree to mandate medical masks for all passengers on public transport.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland reports a record 93 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,708.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 1,610 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 91,470.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong extends their work from home arrangements for civil servants until January 27, as the city attempts to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel extends their third nationwide lockdown until January 31 as the country reports its highest number of cases since the pandemic began. They will also require all travelers to present a negative COVID-19 test result within 72 hours of arrival or face a fine of NIS 2,500 ($772).

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The Shizuoka prefectural government issues an emergency alert after three cases of the more contagious variant from the UK are reported in people with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Kuwait reports their first cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in two women who travelled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia's Senior Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob announces the extension of the second movement control order to six states from January 22 at 12:01 a.m. local time until February 4. This means that all states and federal territories except Sarawak will be placed under tighter restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The New Zealand government imposes a mandatory requirement for all travellers to present a negative COVID-19 test result before departing for New Zealand, beginning January 25. This requirement does not include residents of Australia, Antarctica and most Pacific Island countries.

A Ugandan government spokesman accuses the U.S. government of "subversion" after ambassador Natalie E. Brown tried to visit opposition leader Bobi Wine at his home, where he is under house arrest. Brown said that she wanted to check on the "health and safety" of Wine.
The outgoing Trump administration declares that China has committed genocide against Uyghur Muslims and other ethnic minority groups.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Grafton vaccine incident, COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin pharmacist Steven Brandenburg is charged with attempted misdemeanor property damage for deliberately trying to defrost doses of Moderna's vaccine.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Three members of the Oath Keepers far-right militia group are arrested by federal prosecutors for conspiring to breach the United States Capitol.
The United States Department of Justice closes an insider trading probe into U.S. Senator Richard Burr of North Carolina without making him face any criminal charges.

The Philippine Department of National Defense terminates a 32-year-old accord with the University of the Philippines, the country's national university, that limits the access of police and military personnel into the university's campuses. Faculty members, students, and activists protest the move, calling it "a violation of academic freedom" and claiming that it would aid the government's attempts at red-tagging people.

A 65-year-old Thai woman is sentenced to 43 years in prison for insulting the Thai monarchy in online posts in 2014. Her sentence, initially for 87 years, was reduced after she pleaded guilty to the charges. It is the longest punishment for lèse-majesté handed down in Thai history.

Bishop Daniel Thomas of the Diocese of Toledo issues statements on the deaths of a suspect and police officer, and the vandalism and arson at Our Lady, Queen of the Most Holy Rosary Cathedral in Toledo, Ohio.

Turkey's Information and Communication Technologies Authority bans advertisements on Twitter, Periscope and Pinterest after these companies failed to appoint local representatives under a new social media law.
Scientists discover that WASP-107b is a super-puff. WASP-107b is an exoplanet the same size as Jupiter but with one tenth the mass, located 212 light years away from Earth.
Three Afghan soldiers are killed and four others are wounded in an attack on their vehicle by unidentified gunmen in Herat Province.

context: Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Dublin cancels their annual Saint Patrick's Day festival for the second year due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The event will instead be held virtually on a special online TV channel.

context: Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Cork, Limerick, and Ennis have all cancelled their respective Saint Patrick's Day parades for the second year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
An explosion caused by a gas leak at a residence for priests in Madrid, Spain results in four fatalities and injures ten others. It also partially destroys the residence.
A boat carrying migrants from West Africa capsizes in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya, resulting in 43 fatalities.
An explosion caused by coal dust and air in a thermal power plant in Angren, Uzbekistan kills three workers and leaves three others injured.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: The Netherlands bans all flights from the United Kingdom, South Africa and all South American countries beginning January 23 in order to reduce the spread of more contagious variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: Prime Minister Mark Rutte issues a statement that would ask the parliament to vote regarding a weekend curfew from 8.30 p.m. to 4.30 a.m. in a parliamentary debate that will begin tomorrow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: Andorra begins its vaccination campaign against COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 14,647 new confirmed cases and 219 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 581,605 confirmed cases and 9,465 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: The Russian Direct Investment Fund files the registration of the Sputnik V vaccine with the European Medicines Agency with the first review expected in February.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports a record 41,576 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,412,318.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 1,820 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 93,290.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: India begins exporting the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine to Bhutan and Maldives.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 9,755 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 763,703.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: Lebanon reports a record 61 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,084.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The government reaches an agreement with Pfizer for an additional 12 million doses of their vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Beijing impose a partial lockdown in five neighbourhoods after two cases in Daxing were linked to B.1.1.7 variant found in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines surpasses 10,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya, 501.V2 variant
text: Acting Health Director-General Patrick Amoth confirms the first cases of the variant found in South Africa. The patients are two people who had traveled to that country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe's International Trade and Foreign Minister Sibusiso Moyo dies due to complications from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: President Joe Biden signs an executive order mandating face masks on federal property and during interstate travel.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States reports a record 4,409 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile
text: Chile approves the CoronaVac vaccine developed by Sinovac for emergency use in the country.
Iraq reports an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N8 bird flu in the city of Samarra.

The Chinese foreign ministry places sanctions on 28 members of the outgoing Trump administration, including former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former National Security Advisor John Bolton, and former White House Chief Strategist Steve Bannon. The sanctions are believed to be in response to Pompeo's announcement on Tuesday that the internment of Muslim Uyghurs constitutes genocide.

context: Presidency of Joe Biden > Inauguration of Joe Biden
text: Joe Biden is sworn in as the 46th President of the United States.

context: Presidency of Joe Biden > Inauguration of Joe Biden
text: Kamala Harris is sworn in as the 49th Vice President of the United States, making her the first woman, first Indian American in United States history to hold the office.

context: Presidency of Joe Biden > Inauguration of Joe Biden
text: Donald Trump becomes the first outgoing president to refuse to attend his successor's inauguration since Andrew Johnson, who did not attend Ulysses S. Grant's inauguration in 1869.

context: Presidency of Joe Biden > Cabinet of Joe Biden
text: The Senate votes to confirm Avril Haines, Biden's nominee for United States Director of National Intelligence (DNI), 84-10. Haines is the first Biden appointee to be confirmed by the Senate, and the first woman to serve in the DNI.

Biden signs his first executive orders reversing several Trump administration decisions, including rejoining the Paris Agreement and the World Health Organization, repealing 2017 travel bans, ending funding for the United States–Mexico border wall, and revoking the permit for the Keystone XL pipeline.

context: 117th United States Congress > 2020 United States Senate election in Georgia, 2020 United States Senate special election in Georgia
text: Jon Ossoff and Raphael Warnock of Georgia are officially sworn in as Senators of the United States Senate.
Alex Padilla of California is officially sworn in as Senator of the United States Senate, as an appointee replacing Kamala Harris.

context: Syrian civil war > American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War
text: A United States convoy consisting of 40 trucks and armored vehicles enters northeastern Syria from Iraq via the Al Waleed crossing.

context: ISIL insurgency in Iraq > 2021 Baghdad bombings
text: A suicide attack at an open market in Baghdad, Iraq, kills at least 32 people and injures 110 others. Attacks have been rare in the country since the 2017 military defeat of ISIL, making this incident one of the deadliest since then.

The Central African Republic government declares a 15-day state of emergency after rebels attempt to surround and blockade the capital Bangui. Pro-François Bozizé loyalists and anti-balaka militias now control around two-thirds of the war torn nation.

context: Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: Organisers announce that the Glastonbury Festival has been cancelled for the second consecutive year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on entertainment, COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: Dubai suspends all entertainment permits issued by the emirate for establishments due to an increase in violations of COVID-19 health protocols.

Indonesian authorities, led by Transportation Minister Budi Karya Sumadi, officially end the search for remaining victims and debris from Sriwijaya Air Flight 182, which crashed into the Java Sea on January 9, killing all 62 people on board.
Fifteen people are killed and eleven others injured in a fire at a nursing home in Kharkiv, Ukraine.
Five people are killed in a fire at a Serum Institute of India facility in Pune, Maharashtra, India.
A truck carrying sticks of gelatin explodes at a boulder-crushing facility in Abbalagere in Shivamogga district, Karnataka, India, killing eight workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama
text: Alabama Governor Kay Ivey extends the statewide mask mandate to March 5.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Tennessee reports their first two cases of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 that was first identified in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: President Joe Biden signs an executive order requiring usage of masks in airports and on airplanes, trains and buses.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico reports a record 22,339 newly confirmed cases and 1,809 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Trinidad and Tobago, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Trinidad and Tobago reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a person returning from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record of 221 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,686.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: The government announces the closure of all schools, kindergartens and universities for two weeks beginning tomorrow due to an increase in COVID-19 cases, as well as the emergence of the Variant of Concern 202012/01.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Hungary approves the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine and Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, becoming the first European Union member state to approve the Russian vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: The Dutch House of Representatives votes to impose a curfew from 9.00 p.m. to 4.30 a.m. beginning January 23.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin announces that as part of an easing of COVID-19 restrictions, museums and libraries will reopen beginning tomorrow, while theatres and cinemas will be allowed to accommodate more patrons. In addition, colleges, sports schools and children's clubs will resume in-person attendance, but university students will continue studying remotely.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports a record 44,357 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,456,675.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 346 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 27,203.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka reopens to foreign tourists after a nearly 10-month pandemic closure, however tourists are required to receive multiple testings and follow quarantine measures that have been put in place.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand's Food and Drug Administration approves the emergency use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. 50,000 doses of the vaccine are expected to arrive in February.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina > COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina
text: President Alberto Fernández receives a dose of the Russian-made Sputnik V vaccine, a day after the usage of vaccines for people over the age of 60 was approved by the country's health regulator.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South African Minister in the Presidency Jackson Mthembu dies due to COVID-19.
The European Court of Human Rights rules that Russia was responsible for a series of human rights violations during its 2008 war with Georgia.

Bashar al-Jaafari, Permanent Representative of Syria to the United Nations, called on Biden to change US foreign policy in Syria, which is nearing 10 years of civil war. During a session of the UN Security Council, Jaafari accused the United States of using the multi-sided war to steal the country's oil reserves and other natural resources.
The Tokyo District Court upholds a ban on dual citizenship of Japan and another country, rejecting appeals for damages claiming that the law was unconstitutional.

A Vatican tribunal convicts two former executives of the Institute for Religious Works (the IOR, commonly known as the Vatican bank) on embezzlement and money-laundering charges. Angelo Caloia, who was president of the IOR from 1999 to 2009; and two lawyers who had acted as IOR consultants, were found guilty of arranging to profit from the sale of Vatican properties.

context: Presidency of Joe Biden, Efforts to impeach Joe Biden
text: Georgia Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene introduces six articles of impeachment against newly-inaugurated President of the United States Joe Biden, alleging an "abuse of power" when Biden served as Barack Obama's Vice President.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics, COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolian Prime Minister Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh resigns a day after thousands in Ulaanbaatar protested against the way authorities behaved with a COVID-19-infected mother and her newborn baby.

Julie Payette resigns as Governor General of Canada following a review that cites allegations of a toxic work environment at Rideau Hall. Chief Justice of Canada Richard Wagner will carry out the duties of that office as Administrator of Canada until the Crown appoints a new Governor General.
Surangel Whipps Jr. assumes the office of President of Palau succeeding Thomas Remengesau Jr..

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: United States district judge for the Western District of Washington Barbara Jacobs Rothstein rejects a lawsuit filed by Parler requesting reinstatement on Amazon.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: House Oversight Committee chairwoman Carolyn Maloney calls for the FBI to investigate Parler for their role in the storming of the United States Capitol.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2020 Summer Olympics, COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: International Olympic Committee President Thomas Bach says that the Summer Olympics will be held in July, despite a state of emergency currently being declared in Tokyo.
FIFA warns top-division European football clubs and their players against participating in the proposed European Super League, threatening them with a ban from all FIFA-sanctioned competitions.

context: Syrian civil war, Israel's role in the Syrian Civil War > Syria missile strikes (January 2021)
text: An Israeli airstrike in the city of Hama, Syria, destroys five Syrian military sites. According to SANA, four people from the same family, including two children, are killed in the strikes.
The World Trade Organization rules that the United States violated the organization's rules when it significantly raised the tariff on some South Korean goods, from 9.49% to 59.72%, in May 2016.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reports a record 764 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Florida
text: Florida reports 277 deaths in the past 24 hours, tying their previous state record set in August of last year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: New Jersey reports their first two cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2. Neither had travelled.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 25 million cases of COVID-19, with about one in every 13 Americans testing positive for the virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Belize
text: The number of recoveries in Belize surpasses 11,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba, 501.V2 variant
text: Cuba reports their first case of a variant from South Africa in an asymptomatic person who travelled from the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Panama, 501.V2 variant
text: Panama reports their first case of a variant from South Africa in a 40-year-old Zimbabwe native who entered the country from there.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany surpasses 50,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany reports their first case of the more contagious B.1.1.248 variant in a person who travelled from Brazil to Hesse.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record of 234 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,920.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal also reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in South Africa. They do not indicate whether the individual travelled.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Belgium declares a ban on non-essential travel in and out of the country from January 27 through March 1 in order to curb the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: A panel of scientists that advises the British government announces that a variant first discovered in the United Kingdom is 30% more deadly than the original SARS-CoV-2 virus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: For the first time since the beginning of the pandemic, Hong Kong will impose a lockdown in the Yau Tsim Mong District beginning this weekend. Negative COVID-19 testing results will be required in order to leave one's residence.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 108 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record of 18 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 660.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar
text: Myanmar receives its first 1.5 million doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Botswana
text: Botswana surpasses 100 deaths from COVID-19.
Pfizer says that they will supply 40 million doses of their vaccine to lower- and middle-income countries.

The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons enters into force, banning the development, testing, production, stockpiling, stationing, transfer, use and threat of use of nuclear weapons in 51 countries. However, the world's major nuclear powers have not endorsed this international agreement.

context: Cannabis in the United States > Cannabis in Arizona, 2020 Arizona Proposition 207
text: Arizona begins legal sales of recreational cannabis, making it the 15th state to do so.

context: Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: In Bnei Brak, an ultra-Orthodox town near Tel Aviv, ultra-Orthodox Jews attack an unmarked police vehicle while officers were inside it, causing a riot in which at least six people were arrested. Israel is currently in a lockdown.
Farmer leaders allege a conspiracy to kill four of them and create disturbance during their proposed tractor rally on Republic Day in Delhi.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack
text: A magistrate judge orders Oath Keepers member Donovan Crowl to be detained on charges for his role during the attack on the United States Capitol.

Seven culprits involved in the deaths of 39 Vietnamese unlawful immigrants smuggled in a refrigerator lorry in Grays, Essex in 2019 have been sentenced on multiple counts of manslaughter. Five people received sentences of between 3 to 18 years in prison, while the two main leaders of the smuggling operation received 20 and 27 years respectively.

context: Corruption in the mining industry of Guinea
text: Israeli businessman Beny Steinmetz is sentenced by a Geneva court to five years in prison for corruption in obtaining mining rights to an iron ore deposit in Guinea, and is ordered to pay a fine of CHF 50 million (US$56 million) to the canton of Geneva.

Former Bosnian Army general and deputy Minister of Defense Sakib Mahmuljin is sentenced to ten years in prison for failing to prevent or punish foreign Islamist fighters who murdered and tortured Serbian prisoners during the Bosnian War.
Police in Russia arrest five aides of Alexei Navalny ahead of planned protests. Navalny has been under arrest since returning to Russia on January 17.

Sam Gor drug lord Tse Chi Lop is arrested by police at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol in Amsterdam. The Australian Federal Police are seeking to extradite him to face trial. Twenty law enforcement agencies assisted the operation, known as "Operation Kungur".
The U.S. Senate votes 93–2 to confirm Lloyd Austin as Secretary of Defense, making him the first African-American to lead the The Pentagon.

In response to a bill proposed by parliament to require dot-com companies to compensate local news outlets for hosting their content, Google threatens to block Australians from using its web search engine should the current draft of the bill become law.

Twitter suspends an account linked to Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei after Khamenei threatened to assassinate former U.S. President Donald Trump in revenge for the assassination of Qasem Soleimani in 2020.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: TikTok announces that they have banned Baked Alaska, the far-right activist who was arrested by the FBI for participating in the attack on the United States Capitol.
Alphabet Inc. announces that it will shut down its subsidiary Loon, which provides an aerial wireless network through high-altitude balloons, saying that it is not "commercially viable".

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: British Athletics cancels its annual indoor championships that were set to begin in Glasgow in February due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: Organisers of the Tour de Normandie cancel the annual seven-day bicycle race that was scheduled for May due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. This is the second year that it has been cancelled.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: Real Madrid announces that their coach Zinedine Zidane has tested positive for COVID-19.
Eleven Popular Mobilization Forces members are killed, including a brigade commander, and ten others wounded in an ambush by suspected Islamic State militants east of Tikrit.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The University of Michigan shuts down all sports activities for two weeks after the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 is discovered in five people with ties to the school.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: North Carolina reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person in Mecklenburg County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: Federal officials announce that all indoor portions of the National Mall and memorial parks will be closed to the public to combat the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state), Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Washington reports their first cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in two people residing in Snohomish County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick
text: New Brunswick's Edmundston region begins a 14-day lockdown. Non-essential travel is prohibited in and out of the area. In addition, all non-essential businesses, schools and public spaces are closed, and all indoor and outdoor gatherings among people of different households are prohibited.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: A teen in London, Ontario, dies from COVID-19, making him the youngest person in the area to die from the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 9,912 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 791,059.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesian COVID-19 Task Force chairman and Chairman of the National Disaster Management Agency Doni Monardo announces that he has tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan surpasses 5,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 4,275 new confirmed cases and 4,313 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 180,455 confirmed cases and 137,019 recoveries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Health Minister Pavithra Wanniarachchi tests positive for COVID-19 after previously endorsing sorcery and magic potions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Health authorities impose tougher lockdowns in Oslo and nine neighbouring municipalities due to an increase in cases of a more contagious variant from the UK that also caused two deaths in care home residents yesterday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 15,333 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 624,469. The country also reports a record 274 deaths in the past 24 hours, surpassing 10,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the military
text: Chief of the Defence Staff Miguel Ángel Villarroya resigns after he admitted to receiving a dose of the COVID-19 vaccine while not being on the priority list.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey signs a deal with the Russian Direct Investment Fund for the production of its Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt, COVID-19 vaccine
text: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi announces that the country will begin vaccinations tomorrow. Medical staff will be the first to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia bans gatherings including demonstrations and extends their curfew to between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. local time until February 14 in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil > COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil
text: Brazil begins distribution of the AstraZeneca-Oxford University vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Amazonas Governor Wilson Lima announces new, tougher restrictions to curb the spread of COVID-19, beginning January 25. People will only be allowed to leave their homes for essential purposes such grocery shopping.

context: 2021 Russian protests, aftermath of the poisoning of Alexei Navalny
text: Over 3,500 people are detained in Russia amid nationwide protests in support of jailed opposition leader Alexei Navalny. Moscow officials say 29 people have received medical assistance in hospitals, while a female protester in Saint Petersburg is currently in intensive care after being kicked by a riot police officer.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Garret Miller, a Texas man who participated in the storming of the United States Capitol, is charged for threatening to assassinate U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

context: Police brutality in the United States
text: A Tacoma, Washington police officer drove through a downtown crowd, running over at least one person and sending them to the hospital. The officer was responding to calls that a group of people were blocking a downtown intersection when the crowd surrounded on the police car, Tacoma Police Department said.

Brazilian indigenous leaders Raoni Metuktire of the Kayapo tribe and Almir Narayamoga Surui of the Paiter Surui tribe call for the International Criminal Court to investigate President Jair Bolsonaro for "crimes against humanity" such as environmental damage to the Amazon rainforest.
Six Malian troops are killed and 18 others are injured in simultaneous jihadist attacks in the central Mopti Region. The military also stated that around 30 militants were also killed in the clashes.
A plane crashes in Palmas, Tocantins, Brazil, killing four Palmas Futebol e Regatas footballers, their team's president, and the pilot.

Eleven of the miners who went missing two weeks ago in Qixia, Shandong, China, after the gold mine where they worked collapsed, are rescued alive. Another miner is found dead, while ten others are still missing.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Israeli cabinet agrees to close Ben Gurion International Airport and ban all incoming and outgoing international passengers from the airport, beginning at midnight tomorrow. Cargo flights, medical evacuations and firefighting flights are exempted from this rule.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel > Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Clashes broke out in three cities across Israel as police attempted to enforce coronavirus lockdown restrictions in a number of ultra-Orthodox communities. Israel is currently in a COVID-19 pandemic lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel reports several cases of a faster-spreading variant of SARS-CoV-2, which was recently discovered in the United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: The Union Health Ministry announces that India has become the fastest nation to reach 1 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 4,427 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 141,446.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C., Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Around 38 United States Capitol Police officers have tested positive for COVID-19 since the storming of the United States Capitol.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois
text: The Chicago Teachers Union votes to defy an order by the public schools to return to in-person instructions over COVID-19 concerns.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador announces that he has tested positive for COVID-19 and is receiving medical treatment.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Netherlands, Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Rioting youths torched a COVID-19 testing center and threw fireworks at police in the fishing village of Urk overnight into Sunday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Netherlands, Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Rioters set fires in the center of Eindhoven and pelted police with rocks at a banned demonstration against coronavirus lockdown measures. Police also faced off with curfew-defying crowds in The Hague, Amsterdam, Enschede, Venlo, Stein, Roermond, Oosterhout, Breda and elsewhere across the Netherlands. More than 100 people have been arrested. It was the worst violence to hit the Netherlands since the pandemic began and the second straight Sunday that police clashed with protesters in Amsterdam. The country has been under a lockdown since December.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: France imposes new border restrictions that require travellers from other European Union countries arriving by air or sea to present negative PCR test results obtained in the previous 72 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 275 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 10,469.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia
text: Serbia reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a person who travelled from London and later began experiencing mild symptoms.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt
text: Egypt launches a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 with the first doses of Sinopharm's vaccine given to healthcare workers in Ismailia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand health officials report the first community case of COVID-19 in more than two months in a person who travelled from Europe.

The Russian government accuses the United States of "interfering in Russian domestic affairs" after some U.S. officials criticized the police crackdown on protests backing jailed opposition leader Alexei Navalny.

For the second consecutive day, Taiwan reports an incursion of its air defense identification zone by China's People's Liberation Army Air Force. The incursion involved 12 fighter jets, two anti-submarine aircraft and a reconnaissance plane. Taiwan deployed air defence missile systems in response, according to a statement from the Ministry of National Defense.

context: Israel–United Arab Emirates relations, Israel–United Arab Emirates normalization agreement
text: Israel opens an embassy in Abu Dhabi, four months after the signing of the agreement, while the United Arab Emirates approves the establishment of an embassy in Tel Aviv.
Protesters gather in the Sudanese cities of Khartoum and Omdurman over rising inflation, food shortages, and power cuts in the country.
Sudanese police fire tear gas at demonstrators in Khartoum, Sudan, over the country's economic woes.
The Central African government renders custody of an alleged Séléka commander to the International Criminal Court, where he is expected to face charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

context: List of mass shootings in the United States in 2021
text: A mass shooting in Indianapolis, Indiana, leaves six dead and one injured.

American manufacturer Tesla files a lawsuit against one of its former software engineers for allegedly copying confidential computer scripts onto a personal file hosting service. The former employee denies the company's allegation, claiming he transferred the files by mistake.

The two major political parties Reform Party and Centre Party agree to form a government, whose Prime Minister will be Kaja Kallas, who will become the first female to take the office. She is succeeding Jüri Ratas, who resigned following a corruption scandal that involves his party.
Portuguese President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa is reelected with 60.7% of the vote in Sunday's election.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon says she intends to hold a "legal referendum" on independence since Brexit removed Scotland from the European Union against its will. Another referendum would require the approval of the United Kingdom's government, which Prime Minister Boris Johnson opposes.

SpaceX successfully launches a record 143 satellites into orbit on a single rocket in its Transporter-1 mission. The payload consisted of 120 CubeSats, 12 microsatellites, 10 Starlink satellites, and 1 transfer stage. It is also the maiden flight of the SHERPA-FX satellite dispenser.

context: 2020 NFL season, 2020–21 NFL playoffs, Super Bowl LV
text: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Green Bay Packers, 31-26, winning the 2020 NFC Championship and advancing to the Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl being held at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, this will be the first time an NFL team will play the championship game on their home field. They will play the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat the Buffalo Bills 38-24 in the 2020 AFC Championship.
Two senior leaders of the Tehrik-i-Taliban and three other militants are killed during two separate security operations in North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
