context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on retail
text: British multinational retailer Debenhams announces that it will permanently close all of its brick and mortar stores in the United Kingdom, with the loss of 12,000 jobs, after being bought by online fashion retailer Boohoo.com.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea, COVID-19 recession, Economy of South Korea
text: South Korea records its worst annual economic growth since 1998 following the Asian financial crisis. Its gross domestic product contracted 1.0 percent in 2020 from 2019.

Cyclone Eloise leaves at least thirteen people dead and more than 8,000 people homeless after making landfall in central Mozambique. Major flooding is also reported in Eswatini, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

Nine of the miners who went missing during a mine collapse in Qixia, Shandong, China, are found dead by rescue workers. Yesterday another miner was found dead, bringing the death toll to 10, while eleven others were rescued alive. Another miner is still missing.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic, 501.V2 variant
text: President Joe Biden signs an order banning travel from South Africa due to fears of the 501.V2 variant; the ban is expected to take effect on January 30. Additionally, Biden also extends travel restrictions to Brazil, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Ireland, and other European countries, which were expected to expire tomorrow under an executive order signed by former President Donald Trump.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California Governor Gavin Newsom lifts the regional stay-at-home order in all areas statewide, including three areas where ICU capacity remains under 15%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota, Lineage B.1.1.248
text: Minnesota reports the first U.S. case of the new variant of SARS-CoV-2 found in Brazil. The patient is a Twin Cities resident who traveled to Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Nevada reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 strain of SARS-CoV-2 in a person with no recent travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Virginia reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person from Northern Virginia with no recent travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario Premier Doug Ford announces that the second state of emergency in the province will be extended to February 8.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico's richest person and billionaire Carlos Slim tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports a record 93,822 new confirmed cases over the weekend, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,593,582.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The Prime Minister's Chief of Staff Iván Redondo tests positive for the COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria, Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Austria begins to require people aged 14 or older to wear FFP2 masks in shops, pharmacies and hospitals, as well as on public transport.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Netherlands, 2021 Dutch curfew riots, social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: More than 180 people were arrested in 10 Dutch cities as protesters against the curfew and lockdown clashed with riot law enforcement overnight for a third night in a row.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reopens schools, restaurants, and gyms as a tough lockdown aimed to prevent a new wave of COVID-19 was ended.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain
text: Bahrain approves the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine for emergency use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong approves the BioNTech vaccine for emergency use in the city.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports 9,994 new cases and 10,678 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 809,488.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey receives 6.5 million doses of the Sinovac Biotech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 vaccine
text: The Therapeutic Goods Administration approves the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine for use in Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, 501.V2 variant
text: Australia suspends their travel bubble with New Zealand for the next 72 hours after New Zealand's first community case in months was confirmed to be of the 501.V2 variant from South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe surpasses 1,000 deaths from COVID-19.
Moderna says that their vaccine would work against the new variants found in South Africa and the United Kingdom.

context: Greek–Turkish relations, Aegean dispute, 2020–2021 East Mediterranean crisis
text: The Greek and Turkish governments conduct the two countries' first direct dialogue regarding the dispute since 2016.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion, COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada
text: The United States Supreme Court declines to hear a case from the Calvary Chapel Dayton Valley, a church in Dayton, Nevada, that faces restrictions from Governor Steve Sisolak, to consider how far the state should go when imposing restrictions on places of worship.

context: Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump
text: The article of impeachment for former U.S. President Donald Trump is brought to the United States Senate, officially triggering the trial, which is scheduled to begin on February 8.

context: Transgender personnel in the United States military
text: President Joe Biden repeals the Trump administration's decision to ban transgender people from serving in the United States military.
Nineteen people are found dead in two vehicles in Camargo, Tamaulipas, near the Mexico–United States border. The victims, who were likely undocumented migrants, were shot and then set on fire.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Brandon Straka, the WalkAway movement founder and "Stop the Steal" activist who spoke at a rally held by pro-Trump supporters, is arrested on a felony charge of interfering with police during the storming of the United States Capitol.

context: Adass Israel School sex abuse scandal
text: Malka Leifer, the former school principal facing 74 charges of child sexual abuse, is extradited to Melbourne, Australia following a six-year delay of the case that allowed for her to be a fugitive in Israel.
A driver rams pedestrians with his vehicle during a series of hit-and-runs attack in Portland, Oregon, killing a person and injuring five others.
Two Swedish filmmakers, who filmed the wreck of the MS Estonia that sank in 1994 for a documentary, face trial for violating a treaty that prohibits visiting the site.
The Canada House of Commons votes to call on Prime Minister Justin Trudeau to label the Proud Boys as a terrorist organization.
Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte is set to hand in his resignation tomorrow, due to an ongoing political crisis which began on January 13.
Kaja Kallas wins the support of the Riigikogu to become the new Prime Minister, the first woman to do so.
The United States Senate votes 84–15 to confirm Janet Yellen as Treasury Secretary, making her the first woman to serve as head of the Treasury Department.
A Palestinian man, attempting to stab two soldiers at a road junction near Nablus in the West Bank, is shot and killed by an Israeli commander.

context: Tornadoes of 2021 > List of United States tornadoes in January 2021
text: An EF3 tornado hits Fultondale, Alabama, killing one person and injuring 30 others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: President Joe Biden orders an additional 200 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine to be distributed by the end of August.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: Vice President Kamala Harris and Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff receive their second doses of Moderna's vaccine at the National Institutes of Health center in Bethesda.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alaska, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Alaska reports its first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Kentucky, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Kentucky reports its first two cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin, face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The Wisconsin State Senate votes to repeal the statewide mask mandate imposed by Governor Tony Evers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Barbados
text: The Caribbean Public Health Agency reports the presence of B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in Barbados.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia surpasses one million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: A record 10,868 recoveries are reported in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran approves the Sputnik V vaccine for use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reports a record of 959 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, including 914 cases in Samut Sakhon reported yesterday evening, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 14,646.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates reports a record 3,601 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 285,147.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan lifts its restrictions aimed to combat the spread of COVID-19 and announces that concert halls will be allowed to reopen at 50% capacity.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: The government extends the Level 5 lockdown restrictions until March 5. They also agree to impose a 14-day mandatory hotel quarantine for all travelers without negative COVID-19 test results as well as all travelers from Brazil and South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 291 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 11,012.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19, becoming the fifth country to do so after the United States, Brazil, India, and Mexico.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru
text: President Francisco Sagasti announces a total lockdown in the capital Lima and nine other regions following a significant increase in COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru
text: The Cayetano Heredia University says that a volunteer in the local trial of a coronavirus vaccine produced by China's Sinopharm Group has died from COVID-19-related pneumonia. The university said that the volunteer had received the placebo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia
text: The Minister of National Defense of Colombia, Carlos Holmes Trujillo, dies after contracting COVID-19.
The number of worldwide confirmed COVID-19 cases surpasses 100 million.
The highly pathogenic H5N8 avian influenza is reported in two backyard hobby grey crowned cranes in Central Italy, who are killed along with ten healthy birds to prevent spread.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Acting U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Michael R. Sherwin announces that 400 suspects have been identified and 135 people have been charged in connection to the storming of the United States Capitol.

Samyukt Kisan Morcha protestors storm the Red Fort in Delhi, clashing with police. One protestor is killed and more than 80 police officers are injured. Protest leaders blame the violence on "rogue elements", and say they will continue to dispute the government's agriculture acts.

Acting United States Attorney General Monty Wilkinson announces that President Biden has rescinded the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy, which led to the separation of over 3,000 migrant families on the Mexico–United States border.
Colombian businessman Alex Saab, an affiliate of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro who is charged in the United States for alleged money laundering, is placed under house arrest in Cape Verde.

context: 2021 Italian government crisis, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics
text: Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte resigns amid a political crisis over the government's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The United States Senate votes 78–22 to confirm Antony Blinken as the 71st Secretary of State.

Sixteen people are dead and eight injured after three bombs explode in Balad, Mogadishu and Dinsoor. The attacks are claimed by Al-Shabaab. The deadliest attack is in Balad, which result in 14 soldiers killed.
The European Aviation Safety Agency clears the Boeing 737 MAX passenger airliner to return to service in European Union airspace.
A short squeeze causes GameStop stock to increase tremendously after Reddit users predicted a hedge fund closure over the last week.
A collision between a bus and a truck in Dschang, West, Cameroon, kills 53 people and leaves 29 others injured with severe burns.
Mount Merapi on Java, Indonesia, erupts. No casualties have been reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: New Jersey confirms their first death from the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who had "significant underlying conditions."

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Alabama confirms their first three cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in two children and an adult from Montgomery and Jefferson counties.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico reports a record 27,944 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to over 1.8 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: President Joko Widodo receives his second dose of the Sinovac Biotech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 387 deaths and 10,974 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 28,855 deaths and 831,330 recoveries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh
text: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina launches a vaccination programme in Bangladesh using the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar
text: Myanmar begins a vaccination programme using the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Healthcare workers are the first people to be vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal
text: Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli launches a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 in Nepal beginning with 430,000 frontline and healthcare workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: Cyprus announces a cautious easing of the second nationwide lockdown beginning February 1 following a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases that peaked after Christmas.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: North Macedonia reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person with no known travel history who recovered on January 22.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway
text: Prime Minister Erna Solberg announces the closure of all borders for non-essential travel beginning January 29 in an attempt to reduce the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants into Norway.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: Prime Minister Robert Abela announces the imposition of new measures to stop the curve: restaurants, kiosks, and snack bars must remain closed for the entire month of February from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., bars are completely closed, recommends that schools postpone the two days of school holidays for Carnival.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces the introduction of 10-day hotel quarantine for travellers from 30 high-risk countries, including Brazil, Portugal, South Africa, and all South American nations due to spread of variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco receives half a million doses of the Sinopharm vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa approves a vaccine developed by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for emergency use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile
text: Chile's health regulator approves a vaccine developed by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for emergency use in the country.

One of the fourteen men accused of conspiring to kidnap Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer pleads guilty in a federal court and agrees to testify against his co-defendants. His sentencing is scheduled for July 8.
a 16-year-old far-right extremist boy is arrested in Singapore for plotting attacks against two mosques on the anniversary of the deadly 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings.
In the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, 100 Hindu activists attack a prayer gathering in the Catholic media center.

context: Statehood movement in the District of Columbia
text: Democrats in the United States Senate introduce a bill that would make Washington, D.C. the 51st state.
In accordance with decommunization laws, the last statue of Vladimir Lenin in the country (excluding territories currently annexed by Russia or occupied by separatists) is demolished in Odesa Oblast.

Sandro Botticelli's Portrait of a Young Man Holding a Roundel is sold at auction for $92.2 million at Sotheby's in New York City, making it the second most expensive painting by an old master ever sold at public auction.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, COVID-19 recession
text: The Philippines' GDP contracts 9.5% in 2020, its first annual contraction since 1998 following the 1997 Asian financial crisis and the country's worst economic performance since records began in 1947.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 recession
text: The United States's GDP contracts 3.5% in 2020, its first annual contraction since 2009 following the financial crisis of 2007–2008 and the country's worst economic performance since 1946.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism
text: The World Tourism Organization reports that the global tourism sector lost $1.3 trillion in revenue in 2020, calling it "the worst year in tourism history". The organization attributes the loss to COVID-19.
GameStop stock briefly tops US$500 before dropping 36% from Wednesday's closing. Trading was halted multiple times due to the climb and the crash.
Robinhood, TD Ameritrade, and Webull restrict the trade of heavily shorted stocks such as GameStop, AMC, BlackBerry, Nokia, and Koss on their platforms.

A class action lawsuit was filed against Robinhood in response to shutting down the buying of stocks at the center of the short squeeze. US Representative Rashida Tlaib (D-MI) has called for an investigation into the ban on stock sales.
Six people are killed and nine others hospitalized due to a leak of liquid nitrogen at a poultry plant in Gainesville, Georgia, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona > COVID-19 pandemic in the Navajo Nation
text: The Navajo Nation surpasses 1,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in South Carolina, 501.V2 variant
text: South Carolina reports the United States' first two cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in people with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico surpasses India to have the third-highest death toll in the world.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports new daily records for both cases and deaths, with 16,432 new cases and 303 deaths, bringing the nationwide cumulative totals to 685,383 confirmed cases and 11,608 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: The government announces the closure of its border with Spain for two weeks beginning January 31.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: The number of deaths from COVID-19 in Andorra reaches 100.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, 501.V2 variant
text: Spain reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a 30-year-old man who travelled from South Africa to Vigo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: The Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople Bartholomew I receives the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 476 deaths in the past 24 hours, 200 of which are from West Java, bringing the nationwide death toll to 29,331.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 113 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Food and Drug Administration approves the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine for emergency use in the Philippines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam reports their first two locally transmitted COVID-19 cases in 55 days in Hải Dương and Quảng Ninh provinces, with one of them linked to the B.1.1.7 variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco begins its COVID-19 vaccination campaign with King Mohammed VI receiving the first dose.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Senegal reports their first case of a more contagious variant of SARS-CoV-2 that originated in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa
text: Africa secures another 400 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Australia extends the suspension of their travel bubble with New Zealand for another 72 hours due to concerns about new variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil surpasses nine million cases of COVID-19, becoming the third country to do so after India and the United States.

Vaccine developer Novavax announces that their vaccine candidate is 89% effective in preventing severe COVID-19, based on trial data from the United Kingdom; their vaccine was less effective against new variants of the virus, based on data from South Africa.

context: Decolonisation of Africa > Chagos Archipelago sovereignty dispute
text: The United Nations' International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea rules that the United Kingdom has no legal sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago, and must return control of the islands back to Mauritius. The British Foreign Office rejects the ruling, saying that "Mauritius has never held sovereignty over the British Indian Ocean Territory and the UK does not recognise its claim".

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on long-term care facilities, COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York Attorney General Letitia James releases a report accusing the state of undercounting the number of COVID-19 deaths in nursing homes.

context: Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: One protester is shot dead and many more are wounded after attempting to storm a government building during an anti-lockdown riot in Tripoli, Lebanon. The municipality building was set on fire before protesters pulled back to the city's main square.
Sadyr Japarov is sworn in as President of Kyrgyzstan.
Google removes major Australian news sites from some of its search results in an "experiment" in reaction to the Australian government's calls for Google to pay these sites for their content.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission releases a report accusing Google of misusing its advertisement system to promote Alphabet Inc.'s own financial interests.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > Super Bowl LV, COVID-19 pandemic in Florida
text: Tampa Mayor Jane Castor issues an outdoor mask mandate for the city during Super Bowl LV.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 recession
text: France's GDP contracts 8.3% in 2020, the country's worst economic performance since World War II.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, COVID-19 recession
text: Spain's GDP contracts 11% in 2020, the country's worst economic performance since the Spanish Civil War.
A winter storm causes mudslides in southern California, resulting in over 50 car accidents.
The National Weather Service issued a Winter Storm Warning for all areas above 6,500 feet (1,981 meters) in Nevada.
Fifteen people are killed in a COVID-19 facility due to a fire at the Matei Balș Hospital in Bucharest, Romania.
A helicopter crashes against a hill in eastern Cuba, killing all five people onboard.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Arizona reports the first three cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Delaware, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Delaware reports the first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in three people from New Castle County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The CDC issues a rule requiring all travelers using public transportation to wear a mask while boarding, during the trip, and while disembarking. The rule also states face shields, bandanas, and scarves are not permissible forms of face covering.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and major Canadian airlines agree to suspend all flights to "sun destinations" such as the Caribbean and Mexico until April 30.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Trudeau announces new measures to take effect "in the coming weeks" that will require incoming travelers to undergo mandatory PCR testing upon arrival and quarantine in a hotel for a maximum of three days at their own expense.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: Prime Minister Jean Castex announces the closure of borders to all travelers outside the European Union beginning January 31 in order to reduce the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants and avoid a third lockdown. In addition, travel between the overseas territories will be limited and all large shopping centres will be closed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany, travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The German Ministry of Interior bans entry to all travellers from the United Kingdom, Ireland, Brazil, Portugal, and South Africa from tomorrow until February 17 in order to reduce the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants. In addition, travellers from Lesotho and Eswatini will also be banned beginning January 31.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece delays the reopening of high schools, which was scheduled to begin on February 1, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases, particularly in red zone areas.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary approves the Chinese-made Sinopharm vaccine for use in the country, becoming the first EU member state to do so.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: The Verkhovna Rada passes a law banning registration of the Sputnik V vaccine developed by Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: The European Medicines Agency approves the Oxford-AstraZeneca Vaccine for use within the EU and recommends that the European Commission grant it 'limited marketing authorization' within the union.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 5,725 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 203,933.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Presidential Spokesperson Harry Roque announces that the General Community Quarantine (GCQ) in Metro Manila will be extended until February 28 and also places the Cordillera Administrative Region under GCQ status because most of the cases of the B.1.1.7 variant have been reported in the region.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: The government announces that COVID-19 restrictions will be eased in most areas of the country beginning February 1, allowing some businesses to reopen and restaurants to extend their operating hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkmenistan
text: Turkmenistan approves the EpiVacCorona vaccine, becoming the first country outside of Russia to do so.
Pharmaceutical company Johnson & Johnson announces their single-dose COVID-19 vaccine is 66% effective in preventing moderate disease and 85% in preventing severe disease during a global trial.
Novartis signs an agreement with Pfizer and BioNTech to help produce their vaccine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin signs a bill extending the New START nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States until 2026, ahead of its expiration date next week, following talks with U.S. President Joe Biden.
A Vanuatu patrol boat detains two Chinese fishing vessels near the Torres Islands in the Coral Sea for suspected illegal fishing.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol > Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Two members of the Proud Boys are charged with conspiracy to breach the United States Capitol, including one of the members seen smashing a window with a police shield.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol > Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The FBI announces that two women are arrested in Pennsylvania for their roles in the January 6 riot. One of the women, Dawn Bancroft, made threats to shoot House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.

context: Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, crime in the United Kingdom
text: Migrants set fire to the Napier Barracks at Shorncliffe Army Camp in Kent after "reports of a disturbance". The Home Office says people "set about destroying the barracks", after being told that they were being moved due to a COVID-19 outbreak at the camp. Kent Police say that the fire caused "a significant amount of damage" and is investigating it as a suspected arson attack.
The parliament of Portugal passes legislation to legalize euthanasia.

A man is arrested after being linked to the murders of three women and the wounding of a man in the past three days in and around Valence, France. The victims, who were shot in four separate locations, were HR managers; the attacker's motives are suspected to be linked to his earlier employment.

context: Death of Brian Sicknick, aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer announce that Brian Sicknick, the United States Capitol Police officer who died from injuries sustained during the storming of the United States Capitol, will lie in honor at the Rotunda.

A car bombing kills at least five people and injures 22 others in the Turkish-occupied town of Afrin in northern Syria. Turkey's Ministry of National Defense accuses the Kurdish-led YPG of being behind the attack.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland, 501.V2 variant
text: Maryland confirms its first case of the 501.V2 variant from South Africa, becoming the second U.S. state to do so after South Carolina.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in South Carolina, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: South Carolina reports its first case of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom. The patient is a person from the Pee Dee region who previously travelled internationally.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba
text: Cuban authorities announce that the country will tighten its measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19 and require all tourists to isolate after visiting the island until they test negative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 14,518 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, 4,601 of which are from West Java, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,066,313.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran imposes a 14-day quarantine upon arrival for all travelers from Europe.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 5,728 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 209,661.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports its first death from COVID-19 since May 2020 in a woman in her 80s.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan reports its first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a 10-year-old child who travelled with her family to the United Arab Emirates last week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam approves the use of the AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Algeria begins its vaccination program using Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Tunisia becomes the third country in Africa to register the Russian-made Sputnik V vaccine after the country approves the vaccine for one year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The Italian Medicines Agency approves the use of the AstraZeneca vaccine in Italy for all adults but recommends that other vaccines be given to people aged over 55.

The United Kingdom announces that it will apply to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, which forms a trade bloc of 11 Asia-Pacific nations. The UK will be the first non-founding country to apply to join the bloc.
Iran hangs Javid Dehghan, the former leader of the Salafi jihadist group Jaish ul-Adl, for the murder of two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps members in Sistan and Baluchestan Province.

Former Tigray Region president and fugitive Debretsion Gebremichael speaks out for the first time since going into hiding following the fall of Mekelle to federal forces in November 2020, saying "They [the federal government] have temporary military dominance", and "we are engaged in extended resistance". His current whereabouts are unknown.

A suicide bomber blows himself up outside the Afrik Hotel in Mogadishu, Somalia, while gunmen storm the hotel and open fire. Five people are killed in the al-Shabaab attack, including a former military general; ten civilians are wounded. The three other attackers are shot dead during a gun battle with security forces.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, 501.V2 variant
text: Israel reports its first reinfection case of the 501.V2 variant in a 57-year-old man who recently travelled to Turkey and who previously recovered from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: Lebanon surpasses 300,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine, COVID-19 vaccination in Israel
text: Israel agrees to transfer 5,000 doses of COVID-19 vaccine to the Palestinians to immunize frontline medical workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea extends its social distancing restrictions for another two weeks amid concern around the upcoming Lunar New Year holidays and an increase in the number of cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam, 501.V2 variant
text: Vietnam reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a 25-year-old man from South Africa who travelled to Hanoi on December 19 and tested positive for COVID-19 four days later while in quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The number of hospitalized COVID-19 patients in France reaches 27,613, the most since December 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: Minister for Primary Education Arie Slob announces that primary schools and daycare centres will reopen on February 8, but secondary schools and after-school clubs will remain closed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Captain Tom, a British Army World War II veteran who raised millions of pounds for charity during the pandemic, is hospitalized after testing positive for COVID-19. He has not yet received a COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Western Australia Premier Mark McGowan announces a five-day lockdown in the Perth metropolitan, Peel, and South West regions, beginning at 6:00 p.m. AWST, after a quarantine hotel security guard tests positive for COVID-19, possibly of the B.1.1.7 variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba
text: Cuba reports a record 1,012 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 26,686.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt
text: Egypt receives its first shipment of 50,000 doses of the AstraZeneca vaccine from India.

context: Russia–United States relations > 2021 Russian protests, aftermath of the poisoning of Alexei Navalny
text: United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken condemns Russian authorities for using "harsh tactics" in protests that broke out following the arrest of Alexei Navalny.

context: Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations, immigration to the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom formally launches a visa scheme allowing all Hong Kong residents with British National (Overseas) passports (BNO), and their "immediate dependents", to fast-track their UK citizenship. At least 300,000 people are expected to apply. In response, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China says that it will "no longer recognise" BNO passports as legal travel documents.

context: Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Police in Brussels, Belgium announce that they have arrested more than 400 people in order to prevent a banned demonstration against anti-COVID-19 measures.
More than 5,000 people are detained by police at nationwide protests calling for the release of jailed opposition leader Alexei Navalny.
Nguyễn Phú Trọng is re-elected as General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam for a third five-year term as top leader in Vietnam.

Shirlene Ostrov resigns as chairwoman of the Hawaii Republican Party following a series of tweets posted by vice chairman Edwin Boyette on the party's Twitter account defending people who supported the QAnon conspiracy theory. Additionally, Boyette resigned on January 24th after the tweets were posted the day before.
The military hands over power to Min Aung Hlaing and announces a state of emergency for a year, after detaining Aung San Suu Kyi and other leaders of the National League for Democracy party.
Twelve people are killed when two vessels sink close to a port on Colombia's Pacific coast, in Tumaco.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia confirms 18 cases of the new variants of SARS-CoV-2 from the United Kingdom and South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario, 501.V2 variant
text: Ontario reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from the Peel Region with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 26 million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Tokyo surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan receives 500,000 doses of Sinopharm's COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam closes schools in 22 provinces ahead of the Tết holiday and ends a Communist Party congress early following the detection of a new cluster of COVID-19 cases in northern areas.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: Dubai closes all bars and pubs for the entire month of February and limit other activities due to rise of COVID-19 cases across the United Arab Emirates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Armenia
text: Armenia approves the use of the Sputnik V vaccine developed by Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria announces the easing of its lockdown from February 8, allowing non-essential shops and schools to reopen while toughening border restrictions and implementing a curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. local time.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Isle of Man
text: The Isle of Man lifts its second "circuit-breaker" lockdown after 20 days without a community case.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy eases its national restrictions by allowing the reopening of bars, restaurants and museums in 16 "Yellow-zone" regions. However, a curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. will remain in place.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Lithuania reports its first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a woman from Vilnius who tested positive for COVID-19 in early January.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa receives one million doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine produced by the Serum Institute of India.

context: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état > Myanmar–United Kingdom relations
text: The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office summons the ambassador of Myanmar to the United Kingdom in response to the coup.

context: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état > Myanmar–United States relations
text: U.S. President Joe Biden threatens to re-impose sanctions on Myanmar's military leaders and calls for them to relinquish the power that they seized in the coup.
Andorra stops recognizing Juan Guaidó as the interim President of Venezuela.

Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican Secretary of State, visits Cameroon this week. He hopes peace and reconciliation can be found in the country, which is struggling amid an armed separatist movement in the Southwest and Northwest regions.

Internet access remained blocked following violent clashes between police and farmers protesting controversial agricultural reforms. Online access was suspended in at least 14 of 22 districts in Haryana near New Delhi. That order was first imposed on Republic Day in Haryana districts for 24 hours, but has been extended every day since.
A total of 159 people are detained at the protests over the appointment of Melih Bulu as the rector of Boğaziçi University in Istanbul, Turkey.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Over 228 people have been charged or arrested for participating in the storming of the United States Capitol.

Protesters marched in Rochester, New York, after a nine-year-old girl was handcuffed and pepper-sprayed by police. Protesters ripped away barricades protecting a Rochester police precinct as hundreds took to the streets in outrage.
Ballot Measure 110 goes into effect in Oregon, making it the first state to decriminalize possession of small amounts of specified Schedule I and Schedule II drugs.

context: 2021 President of the Chamber of Deputies of Brazil election, 2021 President of the Federal Senate of Brazil election
text: The National Congress of Brazil elects new leaders for the 56th Legislature. Arthur Lira and Rodrigo Pacheco, candidates supported by President Jair Bolsonaro, are elected President of the Chamber of Deputies and President of the Federal Senate respectively.
Burmese State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi is placed under house arrest in the capital Naypyidaw after the military coup that overthrew her government.
Three Ethiopian opposition parties say that at least 52,000 civilians have died in Tigray.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan
text: The United States Senate votes 50–49 to pass a budget resolution that would allow Democrats to pass President Joe Biden's $1.9 trillion relief package without support from Republicans.
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos announces that he will step down as CEO during the third quarter. Current Amazon Web Services CEO Andy Jassy is expected to replace him.
Fourteen people are killed and twelve others are injured after a coach overturned at a sharp turn near Uthal, Pakistan.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: Captain Tom, a British Army veteran who served in World War II and who donated to charities during the lockdown, dies from COVID-19 at the age of 100.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon announces a phased return to school for Scotland's youngest children, with nurseries and all primary pupils from P1 to P3 planned to be back in the classroom beginning on February 22.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain will restrict travel to South Africa and Brazil due to concerns about new variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports 724 deaths in the past 24 hours, the most since April.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: Andorra surpasses the 10.000 COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The French National Authority for Health approves the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine for people aged under 65.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland reports a record 101 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 3,418.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands, COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns
text: Prime Minister Mark Rutte extends all of the country's tough lockdown measures for at least a month due to the spread of more transmissible variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino
text: Former Captain Regent Fausta Morganti dies from COVID-19 at the age of 76.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: New Brunswick reports its first two cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Saskatchewan reports its first two cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in the Regina area.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico approves the use of Sputnik V vaccine in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 21 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 791.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia extends its movement control order in all states and territories except Sarawak until February 18.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 12,848 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 896,530.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The Japanese government extends an ongoing state of emergency in 10 prefectures, including Tokyo, which surpassed 100,000 cases yesterday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan, COVID-19 vaccine
text: Kyrgyzstan is expected to receive 504,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine in March.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Prime Minister Imran Khan launches the vaccination campaign against COVID-19 in Pakistan, with the first dose of Sinopharm's vaccine administered to a doctor in Islamabad.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestinian Authority begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 starting with healthcare workers in the occupied West Bank.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The Ministry of Health confirms that 276 people in 10 provinces and cities are currently infected with the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 vaccine > Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine
text: A peer-reviewed result published in the journal The Lancet finds Russia's Sputnik V vaccine to be 91.6% effective against symptomatic COVID-19 infection. It is the third major vaccine candidate to exceed 90% efficacy, along with the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines.
China blocks a United Nations Security Council statement formally condemning the military coup in Myanmar.

Two FBI agents are killed and three others are wounded during a shootout in Sunrise, Florida, while serving an arrest warrant. The gunman is later found dead. This is the deadliest incident involving FBI agents since 1986.

Five children and one adult are killed, and another person wounded, during a mass shooting at a home in Muskogee, Oklahoma. A 25-year-old male suspect who had been living with the victims is taken into custody.
The United States Senate votes to confirm Pete Buttigieg as Transportation Secretary, making him the first openly gay person to be confirmed to a Cabinet post.
The Senate also confirms Alejandro Mayorkas as Secretary of Homeland Security, making him the first Jewish person, first Latino person and first immigrant to head the Department of Homeland Security.
President Sergio Mattarella invites former President of the European Central Bank Mario Draghi to form a new government following the resignation of Giuseppe Conte as Prime Minister.

context: 2020–21 Premier League, Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.
text: Manchester United defeats Southampton 9–0 to equal the record for the largest winning margin in a Premier League match, equalling that of Leicester City's 0–9 victory against the same team in the previous season and their own 9–0 win against Ipswich Town in 1995.

context: Syrian civil war > Syria missile strikes (February 2021)
text: Israel launches airstrikes in Syria, Syrian forces responded late on Wednesday to "Israeli aggression" in the south of the country, according to state news agency SANA.
Nine soldiers are killed and six others are wounded during an ambush near the village of Boni, Mopti, Mali. Twenty attackers are also killed.
Four Tunisian soldiers are killed by a land mine during a counter-terrorism operation in Mount Mghila, central Tunisia.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, Shortages related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: General Motors announces the suspension of operations at its Fairfax, Ingersoll, and San Luis Potosí assembly plants due to a global shortage of semiconductors.
Over 70 homes are destroyed by a large wildfire in Western Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in Catalonia. Experts believe that it has no relation to South Africa, the variant's country of origin, and that it originated in Europe.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain surpasses 60,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Czech Republic surpasses one million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: The Swedish government announces that all travellers will be required to show a negative COVID-19 testing result within 48 hours of arrival beginning February 6 in order to prevent the spread of variants of SARS-CoV-2. Swedish citizens as well as foreign residents living in Sweden will be exempt from this rule.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom
text: The number of people who have been vaccinated against COVID-19 in the United Kingdom surpasses 10 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The Japanese House of Councillors passes a law that will introduce fines for people and businesses that do not comply with restrictions imposed to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait
text: Kuwait will suspend entry for non-citizens for two weeks beginning February 7, due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: The Health Sciences Authority approves the use of the Moderna vaccine for people aged above 18 in Singapore, becoming the first country in Asia to do so.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates reports a record of 3,977 new confirmed cases and 12 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 313,626 and the nationwide death toll to 878.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Kansas
text: Kansas reports its first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in Ellis County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Medsafe provisionally approves the use of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine in New Zealand with certain conditions.

GlaxoSmithKline and the German biotech firm CureVac sign an agreement worth 150 million euros ($180.7 million) to develop a vaccine to counter many variants of SARS-CoV-2. The vaccine, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to be introduced in 2022.
Preliminary tests indicate that the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine may reduce transmission of COVID-19 and not simply prevent symptomatic infections.
sources: U.S. News & World Report via MSN

text: Authorities in Brandenburg, Germany, cull 14,000 turkeys due to an outbreak of H5N8 bird flu on a farm in the Uckermark area.
The Venezuelan government releases the crew of two Guyana-flagged fishing vessels detained by the Venezuelan military in January for alleged illegal fishing in the disputed Guayana Esequiba region.
The police file criminal charges against overthrown de facto leader Aung San Suu Kyi for illegally importing communications equipment and seek her custody until February 15 as part of investigations.

Public Safety Minister Bill Blair announces the designation of 13 groups as terrorist organizations, including the American far-right group Proud Boys and white supremacist organizations such as the Russian Imperial Movement, Atomwaffen Division, and The Base. In the process, Canada has become the first country to designate the Proud Boys as a terrorist organization.

Fifteen people are arrested in Ethiopia over a plot to attack the United Arab Emirates' embassy in the capital Addis Ababa. Several other suspects, who were planning attacks against the UAE's diplomatic mission in Sudan, are also arrested.
Mario Draghi accepts the order from President Sergio Mattarella to form an "emergency government" after Giuseppe Conte's resignation.

context: Yemeni Civil War, Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen
text: U.S. President Joe Biden announces that the United States will end their support for Saudi Arabia in their intervention in Yemen. However, he also said the United States will continue targeting al-Qaeda operations in the country.

Lebanese political activist and Hezbollah critic Lokman Slim is assassinated, with his body being found inside his car with multiple gunshot wounds in Sidon District. Prime Minister Hassan Diab says "this heinous crime shall not pass without accountability".
New Zealand announces a new floating public holiday to commence in 2022 based on the Māori celebration of Matariki.
The number of homes destroyed rises to 81, as a new bushfire to the north threatens the Bullsbrook township.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin
text: Governor Tony Evers issues a new mask mandate after the Legislature voted to repeal the original mandate.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: President of the 75th session of the United Nations General Assembly Volkan Bozkır receives his first dose of COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Johnson & Johnson requests emergency approval for its vaccine from the Food and Drug Administration.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: President Andrés Manuel López Obrador says he is in "good health and recovering" after testing positive for COVID-19 in late January.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: The Ministry of Health grants emergency use authorization for China's Sinopharm vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran receives its first shipment of 500,000 doses of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestine receives 10,000 doses of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Taiwan reports its first death of a foreigner from COVID-19. The patient was a British national in his 70s. It is also the first death from the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 reported in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, Lineage P.1
text: France reports four cases of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy surpasses 90,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The government confirms that British nationals and non-residents returning from 30 "red list" high-risk countries will need to quarantine in hotels or government-approved accommodation beginning February 15, two weeks after it was announced by Prime Minister Boris Johnson.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Private gatherings in Victoria are limited to 15 people after a worker at a quarantine site for tennis players competing in the Australian Open tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru
text: Peru signs a deal with Pfizer to purchase 20 million doses of its vaccine.
Somalia declares a state of emergency due to swarms of desert locusts.

The Biden administration calls for India to resolve the farmers' protests via dialogue. However, the Ministry of External Affairs compared reactions to the January 26th incident at Red Fort to the January 6 riot that occurred at the Capitol.

A probe by the Modi government to the source of a protest toolkit Greta Thunberg posted suggested it was put together by a Canadian pro-Khalistan organization and that the toolkit had a plan to carry forward the "malign Indian campaign" even if the government repealed the laws.

context: Foreign relations of Guyana, Foreign relations of Taiwan
text: Taiwan announces that it will establish a Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Guyana. The United States welcomes the "milestone".

context: Foreign relations of Guyana, Foreign relations of Taiwan
text: After criticism from China, Guyana terminates the above agreement and says it will continue to follow the One-China policy.

British broadcasting regulator Ofcom revokes the license of China Global Television Network (CGTN), an English-language Chinese news network, after concluding the network was "ultimately controlled" by the Chinese Communist Party. China responds to the move by accusing BBC News of spreading "fake news" about COVID-19.

Turkish Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu accuses the United States of being behind the coup d'état attempt in 2016, which killed more than 250 people. The U.S. State Department says the accusation was "wholly false", and "inconsistent with Turkey's status as a NATO ally".
Henry Puna becomes the new Secretary-General of the Pacific Islands Forum replacing Meg Taylor.
A woman is stabbed to death outside a hospital, and another killed at a nearby street, in Ayrshire, Scotland. The perpetrator dies during a car crash while escaping from the scene.
The United States House of Representatives votes 230–199 to remove Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA) from her assignments on the Education and Labor and Budget committees.

context: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état, Censorship in Myanmar, Censorship of Facebook
text: American technology company Facebook, Inc. reports that multiple Internet service providers in Myanmar have restricted access to its social networking services, including Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. The company has urged authorities to restore connectivity.
The International Criminal Court announces that it will pave the way for investigations into alleged war crimes in Palestinian territories. Israel and groups like Hamas could be investigated.
Swedish troops are deployed to Mali to join French-led counter-insurgency operations against jihadist groups. The Riksdag approved the deployment of up to 150 soldiers in June 2020.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan
text: The United States Senate votes 51–50 to pass a budget resolution as a step to pass the $1.9 trillion stimulus package without Republican support, with Kamala Harris casting her first tiebreaking vote as Vice President.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan
text: The United States House of Representatives votes 219–209 to approve the Senate's budget resolution, with all Republicans and one Democrat voting against the resolution.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economy of Indonesia, COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia's GDP contracts 2.07% in 2020, the first economic contraction since the aftermath of the 1997 Asian financial crisis in 1998.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain > COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid, Lineage P.1
text: Spain reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant in a 44-year-old man who travelled from Brazil to Madrid on January 29 and later tested positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain approves the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine in people aged 18 to 55.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece imposes a ten-day curfew in Attica, Thessaloniki, and Halkidiki, and also closes high schools in these areas beginning tomorrow in an attempt to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki announces that hotels, theatres, swimming pools and other indoor facilities will be allowed to reopen at 50 percent capacity on February 12, but that restaurants and fitness centres will continue to remain closed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine secures 12 million doses of the vaccine developed by AstraZeneca and Novavax.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: India reaches past 5 million vaccinations.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain
text: Bahrain announces that all indoor gyms, indoor exercise classes, sports halls, and swimming pools will be closed from February 7 to February 21 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. The country also announces that government entities and institutions can allow up to 70 percent of their employees to work from home.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel announces that it will ease its lockdown measures beginning February 7. People will no longer be restricted to within one kilometer of their homes, many services will be allowed to operate, and all national parks will reopen. However, international borders will remain closed until February 20.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea surpasses 80,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Western Australia lifts a five-day lockdown in Perth and surrounding areas after it reports no community cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Immigration and government officials announce that New Zealand will restart its Refugee Quota Programme this month, nearly a year after closing its border due to the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Iowa
text: Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds announces that the state will lift its mask mandate and gathering restrictions, which will take effect on Sunday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Oklahoma, Lineage P.1
text: Oklahoma reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant originated from Brazil in a woman who had a travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia, 501.V2 variant
text: Virginia reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from eastern Virginia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 vaccine > Variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: AstraZeneca-Oxford developers say that their vaccine candidate is effective against the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.
Palau announces its intention to withdraw from the Pacific Islands Forum after claiming fraudulence in the recent election for the organization's Secretary General.
A man is killed and 10 others are injured in stabbing attacks in Croydon, London, England.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: Prominent National League for Democracy official Win Htein is arrested for sedition and taken from his house in Yangon by members of the military and police.

context: Second Libyan Civil War, Libyan peace process
text: Delegates of the United Nations-supported Libyan Political Dialogue Forum vote in Geneva to elect Mohammad Younes Menfi as President of the Presidency Council and businessman Mohammed Dbaiba as Prime Minister, defeating President of the House of Representatives Aguila Saleh, and Interior Minister Fathi Bashagha.
The military junta in Myanmar orders internet service providers to block Twitter and Instagram "until further notice".

Scientists belonging to a German–Malagasy expedition announce the discovery of Brookesia nana, a lizard found in Madagascar. The male's body spanning only , is potentially the smallest reptile on Earth.
An ambush on a convoy by suspected MNDAA insurgents in Shan State, Myanmar, kills nine civilians and three policemen, and injures 13 others.
The United Nations says that the Ethiopian government is blocking aid from going to 2.3 million people in non-government-controlled rural areas in Tigray who are in dire need of assistance.
A bombing targeting a Hindu shop in Kabul, Afghanistan, kills three people. Attacks against Hindu and Sikh minorities increased in the country in the last years, mainly by Islamic State militants.
The Cuban Council of Ministers approves a measure authorizing private activity in most sectors.
Eleven people are dead and three others have been rescued after their wooden boat overturns in a lake in Susong County, in east China's Anhui province.
Four skiers are killed and four others are injured in an avalanche in Millcreek Canyon, Utah, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri
text: Missouri reports its first case of B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in an adult from Marion County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China's National Medical Products Administration gives a conditional approval to Sinovac's Coronavac vaccine for general use.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports a record 61 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,989.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar
text: Myanmar approves the use of the Sputnik V vaccine developed by Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The government eases the restrictions on business operating hours outside of the Seoul Capital Area, allowing those businesses to operate until 10 p.m. local time amid a backlash over prolonged restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy signs a decree authorizing the emergency use of monoclonal antibodies to treat COVID-19 patients.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: The Netherlands surpasses one million cases of COVID-19.

context: Immigration policy of the Joe Biden administration
text: U.S. President Joe Biden suspends and initiates the process to terminate the Trump-era "Asylum Cooperative" agreements with El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras.

The leaders of Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, Nauru, Kiribati, and the Marshall Islands will meet on Monday to discuss leaving the Pacific Islands Forum after Marshallese candidate Gerald Zackios was not chosen as Secretary-General. Palau had earlier announced that it was leaving the forum.
Moussa Faki is re-elected as Chairperson of the African Union Commission.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Governor Gavin Newsom issues revised COVID-19 mitigation guidelines for churches after the U.S. Supreme Court lifts the state's ban on indoor worship in areas hardest hit by the pandemic. The new guidelines limit indoor services to 25 percent of the church's capacity in hard-hit areas and restricts indoor singing and chanting.
An Australian economic advisor to Aung San Suu Kyi reveals that he has been detained by the Tatmadaw. He is the first foreign national confirmed to be in the custody of Myanmar's military.
After a juggler is shot dead by a Carabinero, several protests are held in Panguipulli, southern Chile. The protests escalate into riots and several buildings, including the city hall, are burned.
Egypt frees Al Jazeera journalist Mahmoud Hussein after four years in detention. He had been held on charges of spreading false news, joining a banned group and receiving foreign funds.

French religious sister Nathalie Becquart is named by Pope Francis one of the Undersecretaries of the Synod of Bishops, becoming the first woman to reach that office and having a right to vote in the Synod.

context: Censorship in Myanmar, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: The military junta shuts down the country's internet with a near-total blackout in effect amid growing protests against the coup.

In American football, Green Bay Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers wins his third MVP award, making him the sixth player to do so after Jim Brown, Brett Favre, Johnny Unitas, Peyton Manning, and Tom Brady.
A roadside bomb explodes in Dusmareb, Somalia, killing twelve agents of the National Intelligence and Security Agency, including its local head.

Finnish Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto arrives in Khartoum to help reduce tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia. He will also visit a refugee camp containing refugees fleeing the Tigray War and visit Ethiopia after spending time in Sudan.
