A glacier breaks off in Joshimath, India, in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district resulting in flash floods along the Alaknanda River and Dhauliganga River. Eighteen people are found dead and 200 more are feared dead.
An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 occurs in the southern province of Davao del Sur, Philippines, with damage and aftershocks expected. No casualties have been reported.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: U.S. Rep. Ron Wright (R-TX) dies from COVID-19 at the age of 67, thus making him the first member of Congress to die from the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 27 million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario, Lineage P.1
text: Ontario reports Canada's first case of the Lineage P.1 variant in a person who travelled from Brazil to Toronto.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Beatriz Yamamoto Cázarez becomes the fifth incumbent member of the Congress of the Union to die from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan
text: Afghanistan receives 500,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine from India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh
text: Bangladesh begins a nationwide vaccination programme against COVID-19 in Dhaka.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia receives its first 600,000 doses of the Sinopharm vaccine from China.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam surpasses 2,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria tightens its border controls with all neighbouring countries in order to avoid non-essential travel due to the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary approves the use of the Sputnik V vaccine in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa suspends its rollout of the Oxford-AstraZenenca vaccine after research finds that the vaccine is less effective against the 501.V2 variant discovered in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 vaccine > Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, 501.V2 variant
text: A limited-size clinical trial in Johannesburg suggests that the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine is weak against the 501.V2 variant of SARS-CoV-2.

The health ministry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo announces a "resurgence" of the Ebola virus in the country's eastern side, after it was reported that a woman there died from the disease four days prior. The announcement comes three months after the World Health Organization declared an end to the Kivu Ebola outbreak in the country's Équateur province.

Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei says that the United States should "lift all sanctions" if it wants to reverse its nuclear steps, saying that Iran complied with all obligations of the 2015 deal and accuses the United States and European countries of not doing so.

The Haitian government says that it has thwarted an attempted coup d'état against President Jovenel Moïse, with at least 23 people arrested. Protesters assert that Moïse's term expires today, however, he claims that his term ends on February 7, 2022; in accordance with the constitution.

General elections occur in Ecuador to elect the successor of President Lenín Moreno. Socialist and former aide of President Rafael Correa, Andrés Arauz, is expected to finish in first place, but may face a run-off.
General elections occur in Liechtenstein to elect the 25 members of the Landtag.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: Tens of thousands of people protest against the military coup in Myanmar's largest city Yangon, calling for the release of jailed leader Aung San Suu Kyi. The protests are the largest to occur in the country's history since the 2007 Saffron Revolution.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers win the Super Bowl following a 31–9 victory against the Kansas City Chiefs, making them the first wildcard team to win the Super Bowl since the 2010 Green Bay Packers and the first to win it in their home stadium. Quarterback Tom Brady is named Super Bowl MVP.
Sarah Thomas becomes the first female NFL official to officiate a Super Bowl.
Tigres UANL defeats Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras 1–0 in the semi-finals, to become the first CONCACAF team to reach the final of the FIFA Club World Cup.

Houthi forces resume an offensive against Maʼrib, the last stronghold of the internationally-recognized Yemeni government in northern Yemen. A government source says that 20 pro-government fighters have been killed and 28 others have been injured repelling five attacks in the past 24 hours.

Twenty-four workers die in a flooded illegally-run textile workshop in a private house in Tangier, Morocco, which occurred as a result of intense rains that hit the region. Ten others were rescued and hospitalized.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo announces that restaurants can bring back their indoor dining from February 12, three days ahead of originally schedule on Valentine's Day Sunday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas, 501.V2 variant
text: The Houston Methodist Hospital reports Texas' first case of the 501.V2 variant in a man from Fort Bend County who recovered several weeks ago. This makes it the fourth state known to have this variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg quarantines for 14 days after a member of his security detail tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: President Andrés Manuel López Obrador resumes morning news conferences two weeks after testing positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 13,038 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 963,028.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Laos
text: Laos receives 300,000 doses of China's Sinopharm vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 24 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 896.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: Seoul metropolitan government launches COVID-19 test for pet cats and dogs, which comes after South Korea reported its first case of COVID-19 infection in an animal (kitten) on January 24.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education
text: France introduces new measures to ban homemade masks in educational institutions, requiring school children over the age of six to only wear category 1 masks in schools.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: The Netherlands extends its nationwide curfew until March 3 in order to prevent the spread of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Cyprus, Variant of Concern 202012/01
text: Northern Cyprus reports its first case of B.1.1.7 variant in 16 samples that contracted SARS-CoV-2 variant first detected in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: The European Commission finalizes a deal to secure 300 million additional doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina, Lineage P.1
text: Argentina reports its first cases of two different Brazilian SARS-CoV-2 variants in two people infected with the P.1 variant and two others infected with the P.2 variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda eases its lockdown in the capital Kigali and allows businesses to resume operations with up to 30% of essential staff.
The government of Vietnam reports that it has culled more than 100,000 poultry in 14 provinces so far this year in a bid to contain the spread of highly pathogenic H5N1 and H5N6 bird flu strains.

context: Greece–Israel relations, COVID-19 pandemic in Greece, COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sign an accord that would allow vaccinated travellers to visit freely between the two countries without any restrictions in order to revive their battered tourism sector.
The governments of Germany, Poland, and Sweden each expel a Russian diplomat to reciprocate the Russian government's expulsion of three European Union diplomats on February 6.

context: Trial of Benjamin Netanyahu, corruption in Israel
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads not guilty to charges of bribery, breach of trust and fraud at the Jerusalem District Court.
The government of Colombia announces the legalization of undocumented Venezuelan migrants currently in the country, making them eligible to receive 10-year residency permits.

context: Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election, Trump–Raffensperger phone call
text: Georgia officials launch an investigation into former U.S. President Donald Trump for several phone calls made urging officials such as Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger to overturn Joe Biden's win in the state.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: A nationwide general strike takes place in Myanmar in response to the military coup with thousands marching in the capital Naypyidaw, where they clashed with riot police. Several injuries have been reported.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: The military junta declares martial law in the country's second largest city Mandalay amid protests against the coup. Public gatherings of more than five people are banned, and a curfew from 8 p.m. until 4 a.m. has been imposed.

An alliance of opposition parties ceases recognising Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed as the President of Somalia, and propose the creation of a "national council of lawmakers, opposition leaders and civil society" to govern the country as the President's term expires with no clear plan for succession.

Haitian opposition names judge Joseph Mécène Jean-Louis from the Supreme Court the new interim President of Haiti to lead a "transitional government" after arguing that incumbent Jovenel Moïse's term has expired and calling on him to step down. The Organization of American States considers that Moïse's five-year term ends in 2022 as he took office in 2017.

The Palau National Congress passes a joint resolution supporting the decision made by President Surangel Whipps Jr. to leave the Pacific Islands Forum. The National Congress says that the "gentleman's agreement was not honored".

context: 2021 Australian Open, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: The Grand Slam of the Australian Open begins in Melbourne Park, three weeks later than originally scheduled due to the pandemic, with daily attendance capped at 30,000 people per day.
Five people are killed in two separate attacks targeting government employees in Kabul, including the head of the provincial department of the Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development.
Tatmadaw raids the headquarters of ousted de facto leader Aung San Suu Kyi's party National League for Democracy in Yangon, according to a party statement posted on Facebook.

The National Transportation Safety Board concludes their investigation of the crash that killed former professional basketball player Kobe Bryant and eight others nearly a year prior, citing pilot error and spatial disorientation as the cause of the crash.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba
text: Manitoba reports its first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec
text: Quebec reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in Abitibi-Témiscamingue.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Food and Drug Administration grants emergency use authorization for Eli Lilly and Company's combination antibody therapy bamlanivimab/etesevimab for use in COVID-19 positive adults and children aged 12 and older who are at high risk of severe disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: Health Secretary Matt Hancock announces that all British and Irish residents returning from 33 "high-risk" countries will be charged £1,750 to stay in quarantine hotels in England for 10 days and that those who fail to do so or who violate COVID rules face fines of up to £10,000 or up to 10 years in jail.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scottish Transport secretary Michael Matheson announces that all people who arrive from outside the UK and Ireland will be charged £1,750 for “managed quarantine” at one of six hotels at Aberdeen, Edinburgh and Glasgow airports.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Chancellor Sebastian Kurz announces a statewide isolation order in Tyrol beginning February 12 in order to prevent the spread of the 501.V2 variant. Residents will have to present a negative COVID-19 test result from the last 48 hours in order to leave the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus
text: Belarus surpasses 260,000 cases of COVID-19 after reporting 561 new cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announces a near-full lockdown in the Attica region, which includes the capital Athens, from February 11 until February 28. All schools, churches, hair salons, and retail stores, with the exception of supermarkets and pharmacies, are ordered to close; and restaurants are only allowed to offer delivery services.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain surpasses three million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland
text: Switzerland reports its first case of the Brazilian P.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 among healthcare workers using the Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia approves the emergency use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: The government allows more businesses in retail sector and Mosques in most of Malaysia to reopen beginning tomorrow and allows restaurants to resume dine-in service with two people seat on the table despite COVID-19 cases in the country remains high.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan approves the emergency use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, becoming the third vaccine to be approved in the country after the Sinopharm and Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Equatorial Guinea
text: Equatorial Guinea imposes a curfew from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. local time for the first since the beginning of the pandemic and prohibits many leisure activities. The country also reduces domestic flights to once per day, and international flights to twice per week for domestic airlines and once per week for foreign airlines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru
text: Peru launches a vaccination program against COVID-19 two days after it received 300,000 doses of Sinopharm's BBIBP-CorV vaccine. President Francisco Sagasti becomes the first person to get vaccinated.

Five countries: Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, Kiribati and Nauru, officially withdraw from the Pacific Islands Forum over a disagreement regarding the choice of the forum's new Secretary-General.
Indian actor and activist Deep Sidhu is arrested by the Delhi Police's special cell unit for his role in inciting the January 26 riot at the Red Fort.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest > George Floyd protests, George Floyd protests in Richmond, Virginia
text: A Ku Klux Klan member is sentenced to three years and eight months in prison for driving his pickup truck into Black Lives Matter protesters in Richmond, Virginia, during the summer.

context: Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump
text: Former United States president Donald Trump's second impeachment trial begins.

context: Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump
text: The United States Senate votes 56–44 to proceed with the impeachment trial, rejecting claims by Trump's attorneys that the proceeding is unconstitutional.

A court in Baden-Württemberg overturns the nighttime curfew imposed since mid-December to stop the spread of COVID-19 following an emergency application. It means that the 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew will be scrapped on February 11.

A court in Budapest rejects an appeal by independent radio station Klubrádió to have its broadcast license renewed by the government's media regulator, which says that the station had infringed rules. Klubrádió owner András Arató says that the station will appeal the decision at the Supreme Court.

One person is killed and four others injured in a mass shooting at an Allina Health clinic in Buffalo, Minnesota. A 67-year-old man is arrested, and the clinic is believed to have been intentionally targeted.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: Demonstrations in Myanmar's capital Naypyidaw, continue in response to the military coup. Riot police fire rubber bullets and use water cannons to disperse protesters.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: 90 townships in 30 cities, including Naypyidaw and all 44 townships in Yangon, are placed under curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time and all gatherings of more than five people are banned.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics
text: Parliament suspends their sittings for the next three weeks after 17 MPs and 151 staff tested positive for COVID-19.
United Arab Emirates Space Agency spacecraft Hope enters orbit around Mars. The space probe will study the climate of Mars, and meteorological phenomena such as dust storms.
Four bombings in the Afghan capital Kabul kill at least four people, including a district police chief and his bodyguard. Three others are reportedly wounded.

Red Cross officials report that 80% of Tigray's 6 million people are unreachable. In the regional capital of Mekelle, which is now home to 250,000 displaced people, vaccines have expired and there are no longer any HIV or tuberculosis drugs.

Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) forces ambush Ethiopian and Eritrean troops in May Keyah, 50–60 kilometers south of Mekelle. Fighting between the TPLF and Ethiopia is also reported in Guya, Kola Tembien.

The Houthis carry out a drone strike on Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia, damaging a civilian aircraft. A Houthi spokesman says that the attack is in response to coalition airstrikes and other actions in Yemen.

Indonesia's National Transportation Safety Committee issues a preliminary report into the crash of Sriwijaya Air Flight 182, which reveals that a malfunctioning cockpit throttle caused the left engine of the aircraft to lose power before it plunged into the Java Sea.

A magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off the Loyalty Islands Province, New Caledonia. It is the strongest recorded earthquake of the year so far. A tsunami warning was issued with the Australian Bureau of Meteorology confirming that a tsunami was generated by the earthquake.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California > COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area, 501.V2 variant
text: California reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant in people from Alameda County and Santa Clara County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Florida, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Florida surpasses 300 cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Maine reports its first two cases of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom in a person from Franklin County who previously travelled internationally.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico approves the use of China's Sinovac and CanSino vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain
text: Bahrain approves the emergency use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, becoming the fourth vaccine to be approved in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia launches a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using 600,000 doses of Sinopharm's BBIBP-CorV vaccine. The son of Prime Minister Hun Sen, Hun Manet, and several cabinet ministers are among the first people to get vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong will reopen theme parks and sports and entertainment facilities, as well as extend dining hours in restaurants to 10:00 p.m. local time beginning February 18 as the number of cases continues to decline.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: A pet dog owned by a COVID-19 patient in South Korea tests positive for COVID-19 after it showed symptoms.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Croatia detects the first case of UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a samples from three people including a three-year-old children.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The federal government and leaders of 16 German states agree to extend the nationwide lockdown until March 7 due to concerns about variants of SARS-CoV-2 despite a decline in the number of new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal, Lineage P.1
text: Portugal reports its first two identified cases of COVID-19 infection with the Lineage P.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2, both of which were detected in the Lisbon metropolitan area.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia surpasses four million cases of COVID-19, becoming the fourth country to do so after the United States, India, and Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom
text: Charles, Prince of Wales and Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall receive their first doses of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: The New Zealand Government grants a formal approval of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine and announces that high-risk groups such as quarantine personnel, frontline health workers and airline staff will be the first to receive the vaccine.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends the use of Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine by all adults worldwide, including people over age of 65 and recommends an interval of 8 to 12 weeks between the doses.

context: Myanmar–United States relations, 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: U.S. President Joe Biden announces sanctions on the military leaders who directed the coup in Myanmar.

The International Atomic Energy Agency confirms that Iran has carried out its plan to produce uranium metal at a nuclear facility in Isfahan, a major breach of the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. Uranium metal is essential to making the core of a nuclear weapon.

The Supreme Court of Pakistan commutes the death sentences of two schizophrenic prisoners after considering that if their illness makes them unable to comprehend the rationale of their crimes, the death sentence will not meet the ends of justice. The ruling is celebrated by human rights groups.

A court in Russia orders the arrest of Alexei Navalny's ally Leonid Volkov for "appealing to minors to join illegal protests". Volkov, who lives in the European Union and who will not be extradited, said on Facebook that he will "ignore the charges".

context: Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election, Trump–Raffensperger phone call
text: Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis opens a criminal investigation into former U.S. President Donald Trump for attempting to overturn Joe Biden's victory in Georgia, including conducting a phone call with Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger where he pressured Raffensperger to "find enough votes" for him.
British sex offender David Wilson is sentenced to 25 years imprisonment for 96 offences against 51 boys aged 4 to 14.

The Saudi government releases women's rights activist Loujain al-Hathloul from prison, after being held in custody for almost three years. She will still be banned from traveling for the next five years, and has been placed on a three-year probation.

context: Twitter suspensions > Donald Trump on social media, 2024 United States presidential election
text: Twitter confirms that the ban on Donald Trump's account will remain permanent, even if he were to run for president in 2024.

The China National Space Administration space probe Tianwen-1 enters into planetary orbit around Mars. It is the first Chinese spacecraft to reach Mars. A rover will be deployed to explore the Martian surface sometime in May.

Following their 3–1 win against Swansea City in the fifth round of the FA Cup, Manchester City sets a record for the most consecutive wins in all competitions by a top-flight English football club, with 15 consecutive wins.

China and India will withdraw troops around Pangong Lake in a disputed area of eastern Kashmir following sustained talks between the two countries. Tensions have been high since border clashes last year killed dozens.
Three Turkish soldiers are killed by PKK separatists in Iraqi Kurdistan.
Four Pakistani soldiers and four militants are killed in an attack on a security outpost in South Waziristan, according to the Inter Services Public Relations.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in France, impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation
text: France's government cancels a plan by international airport operator Groupe ADP to expand Charles de Gaulle Airport, the country's largest airport, citing reduced traffic due to the pandemic and inconsistency with environmental policies.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia, COVID-19 recession
text: Malaysia's GDP contracts 5.6% in 2020, its worst annual contraction since 1998 following the 1997 Asian financial crisis.
Six people are killed and at least 65 others are injured during a 133-vehicle accident following freezing rain near Fort Worth, Texas, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia
text: Prime Minister Andrej Plenković announces a slight easing of restrictions beginning on February 16, citing the stable number of new cases in the past few weeks. Foreign language schools, casinos, gyms and betting shops can reopen and restaurants and bars can also sell coffee to go.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic
text: The Chamber of Deputies votes down an appeal by Prime Minister Andrej Babiš to extend the state of emergency beyond February 14.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany will close its border with the Czech Republic and Austria's Tyrol region beginning on the evening of February 14 because of a high risk of variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro
text: Montenegro's Institute for Medicines and Medical Devices approves the purchases of Russia’s Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: The Assembly of the Republic votes to extend its state of emergency, allowing the government to extend its second lockdown until March 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia
text: The government announces that starting from February 15, all retail stores will be allowed to reopen and customers will no longer need to present a negative COVID-19 testing result to enter. Schools and universities will also be allowed to resume their classes. Also, skiers will now be allowed to present negative test results from the past seven days instead of just the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and health workers across the country receive their second doses of COVID-19 vaccine as the country begins to administer second doses of Sinovac's CoronaVac vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco receives their second shipment of four million doses of AstraZeneca's vaccine from India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: President Cyril Ramaphosa announces that the country has secured nine million doses of Johnson & Johnson's vaccine, with the first shipment of 80,000 doses arriving next week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe purchases 600,000 doses of Sinopharm vaccine, in addition to 200,000 doses donated by China. These vaccines are expected to arrive at the beginning of March.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California surpasses New York as the U.S. state with the highest number of COVID-19 deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois, 501.V2 variant
text: Illinois reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from Rock Island.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina, 501.V2 variant
text: North Carolina reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant an adult in the central part of the state who had no travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio
text: Ohio Governor Mike DeWine lifts a statewide curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. EST, citing drop of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C., Variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: Washington, D.C. confirms its first cases of the 501.V2 variant from South Africa and the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. President Joe Biden announces that his administration has finalized a deal purchasing a total of 200 million vaccine doses from Moderna and Pfizer.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: South Australia tightens its border restrictions with Victoria due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in Victoria. Travelers from Melbourne will be banned from entering South Australia, though people living in other parts of the state will still be permitted to cross the border.
The Democratic Republic of Congo reports its second death of the Ebola virus outbreak in North Kivu province.

Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko expresses his support for Russian President Vladimir Putin as both men face protests. He also criticized the protests in his own country as a "rebellion" during the All Belarusian People's Assembly.

context: China–United Kingdom relations, Censorship in China
text: China's National Radio and Television Administration bans BBC World News, in response to British telecommunications regulator Ofcom revoking the television license for the state-run China Global Television Network last week.
The Greek parliament approves legislation to create a special police force in universities. The measure faces opposition from various student groups, who describe it as "anti-democratic".

context: National Emergency Concerning the Southern Border of the United States
text: U.S. President Joe Biden ends former President Donald Trump's nearly two-year emergency declaration on the Mexico–United States border.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports, COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The German Badminton Association (DBV) cancels the upcoming 2021 German Open in Mülheim an der Ruhr scheduled for March 9 to 14 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Bayern Munich defeats Tigres UANL 1–0 in the final to win the FIFA Club World Cup. Robert Lewandowski is awarded the Golden Ball of the tournament.

A French presidency official and a senior Chadian official announce that Chad will reinforce their troops by 1,000 in order to fight jihadists in the border regions of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso. It will be formally announced in a summit on February 15–16.

A Togolese peacekeeper has died after being wounded yesterday in an attack on a MINUSMA base near Douentza in Mopti, central Mali, which wounded 28 peacekeepers, according to United Nations spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The United States Senate votes by unanimous consent to award United States Capitol Police officer Eugene Goodman the Congressional Gold Medal for keeping rioters away from the Senate chamber during the storming of the United States Capitol.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway
text: The Norwegian economy contracts by 2.5% in 2020 due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, even as their Q4 GDP grew faster than expected by 1.9%.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The Office for National Statistics says that the economy of the United Kingdom has contracted by a record 9.9% since the pandemic began, but has narrowly avoided a double-dip recession. This is nonetheless estimated to be the largest annual contraction since 1709.
An earthquake of magnitude 5.9 strikes 35 kilometres west of Murghob, Tajikistan. The tremors are felt as far away as northern India and Pakistan.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York
text: New York governor Andrew Cuomo announces to extend the operating hours of indoor dining in restaurants in New York City to 11:00 p.m. EST beginning from Valentine's Day as it expands their curfew on restaurants and bars statewide.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: New Hampshire reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a person from Hillsborough County who had close contact with someone who travelled internationally.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia reports Canada's first case of the Nigerian variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a young person from the Interior Health region who is currently self-isolating.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexican authorities lower the pandemic alert level in Mexico City and the State of Mexico to orange status due to a decrease in the number of COVID-19 hospitalizations.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia approves the emergency use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca and Sinovac Biotech vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: The number of recovered COVID-19 patients in Indonesia surpasses one million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan receives their first shipment of 400,000 doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine from Belgium.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan approves the emergency use of China's CanSinoBio vaccine, becoming the fourth vaccine to be approved in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece extends their full lockdown to Achaia and the island of Euboea beginning February 13 in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia, COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia
text: Russia gives a preliminary approval for its Sputnik V vaccine to be manufactured in Serbia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom surpasses four million cases of COVID-19, becoming the fifth country to do so after the United States, India, Brazil, and Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Chile
text: President Sebastián Piñera receives the first dose of the Sinovac's CoronaVac vaccine.

context: Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations, Censorship in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong's public broadcaster Radio Television Hong Kong joins mainland China in blocking BBC World News and BBC World Service.

context: 2020–2021 United States racial unrest, Black Lives Matter protests in New York City
text: A Black Lives Matter protest turned violent in New York City, resulting in nearly a dozen arrests and injuries among police officers. The New York Police Department said two officers were injured during the march in midtown Manhattan.

Prime Minister-designate Mario Draghi meets with President Sergio Mattarella and presents the list of proposed ministers for his cabinet. Draghi's oath of office is scheduled for tomorrow at 12:00 p.m. local time.
President Alexander Lukashenko says that the country will hold a referendum that would change their constitution before January 18, 2022.

North Korean Supreme Leader Kim Jong-un fires Economic Affairs Minister Kim Tu-il less than a month after appointing him to his cabinet for "lack of innovation". He is replaced by O Su-yong, according to state media.
A study by University College London suggests that the bluestones that form Stonehenge in Wiltshire, England, likely originated from another stone circle in Pembrokeshire, Wales, called Waun Mawn.
Facebook restricts the content posted by the Myanmar's Tatmadaw in order to stop the spread of "misinformation" in a wake of military coup.
The Chairman of Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games Yoshiro Mori resigns due to a scandal over sexist remarks he made about women.

At least four security forces personnel, including a commander, are killed in eastern and southern Afghanistan as clashes with an unidentified terrorist group intensify. Separately, in Kandahar, a Humvee containing explosives detonates, injuring seven police officers.

Egyptian and American archaeologists discover an ancient mass-production brewery in the ancient Egyptian city of Abydos, likely dating back to the Early Dynastic Period. Mostafa Waziri, the secretary-general of the Egyptian Supreme Council of Antiquities, believes it to be "the oldest high-production brewery in the world".
A 7.3 magnitude earthquake strikes off the Tōhoku coast of Japan, injuring at least 110 people.
A series of severe weather-related incidents in Northern Italy leaves four people dead and 25 others injured.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: Lebanon receives its first shipment of 28,500 doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine from Belgium.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Two 11-week-old white tiger cubs that died in Lahore Zoo on January 30 are believed to have died of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The government decides to lower social distancing levels to level 2 in the Seoul Capital Area and level 1.5 in other regions beginning February 15, allowing nightclubs to reopen and extending the operating hours of restaurants, coffee shops and gyms in the Seoul Capital Area until 10:00 p.m. local time. However, gatherings of more than five people continue to be prohibited, but theatres, libraries, and other types of businesses will no longer be subject to operating hours restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates surpasses 1,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Prince Edward Island, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Prince Edward Island reports its first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a man in his 20s who had travelled internationally.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Victoria returns to Stage 4 restrictions in a five-day "circuit breaker" lockdown due to an ongoing outbreak of the B.1.1.7 variant at the Melbourne Airport Holiday Inn. All non-essential businesses are closed, masks are mandatory in all public places, and people are only permitted to leave their homes for essential work, education or care-giving, or for up to two hours a day for essential shopping and outdoor exercise within a radius of of their homes. All international flights to Melbourne have also been cancelled for the duration of the lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Cyprus
text: Northern Cyprus extends its full-scale curfew until February 22 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: The cabinet announces that 20 of South Africa's land borders with Botswana, Lesotho, Eswatini, Namibia, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe will reopen on February 15.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: Venezuela receives its first shipment of 100,000 doses of the Sputnik V vaccine.
Guinea's health ministry reports the country's first deaths from the Ebola virus disease since the 2013–2016 epidemic.

context: Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump
text: The United States Senate votes to acquit former President Donald Trump for the second time when the 57–43 vote in favor of conviction fails to reach the necessary two-thirds majority. Seven Republicans join the entire Democratic caucus in voting for conviction, making it the closest trial vote since the Andrew Johnson impeachment trial of 1868.
Prime Minister Mario Draghi and the ministers of his cabinet are officially sworn in at the Quirinal Palace in Rome, ending the government crisis.
White House Deputy Press Secretary TJ Ducklo resigns after making threats towards Politico journalist Tara Palmeri.

context: 2021 Australian Open, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports
text: Spectators at a late-running tennis match are ordered to leave as Victoria's 5-day "circuit breaker" lockdown comes into effect. Matches at the Melbourne tournament will continue without any spectators for the duration of the lockdown.

According to Turkish authorities, a Turkish military operation against Kurdish PKK fighters in Duhok, Iraq, ends with the death of 48 PKK fighters, three Turkish soldiers, and 13 Turks who had been kidnapped by the PKK.

context: Kivu conflict > Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
text: Militants of the Islamic State's Central Africa Province raid the town of Ndalya in the Ituri Province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing 11 civilians and three members of the armed forces.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra
text: The Indian state of Maharashtra records 4,097 fresh infections after 39 days of no infections

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan's Ministry of Health officially approves the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine, three days after a government panel recommends its approval. This is the first government-approved vaccine in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon
text: Lebanon begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19, a day after the first 28,500 doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine arrived in the country. A doctor at Rafik Hariri University Hospital in Beirut is the first person to be vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: The number of recovered COVID-19 patients in Pakistan surpasses 500,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia extends precautionary measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19, which restricts social gatherings to 20 people and suspends all events and parties, for another 20 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand, 501.V2 variant
text: Thailand reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person who travelled from Tanzania and undergoes mandatory quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: In defiance to the Chamber of Deputies, the Czech government re-declares a state of emergency for the next two weeks in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19, especially because of the emergence of the more contagious B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The French Direction générale de la Santé asks regional health agencies and hospitals to go into "crisis mode" beginning on February 18 in order to prepare for a possible increase in COVID-19 cases as a result of highly contagious variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Health Minister Roberto Speranza signs a provision that extends the ban on recreational skiing at resorts until March 5, effectively preventing ski resorts from opening tomorrow for the first time this season due to the spread of the UK variant and other variants of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia surpasses 80,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico receives a shipment of 870,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine from India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand reports their first community cases of COVID-19 since January 24. The patients are a family from Auckland.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda begins a COVID-19 vaccination programme with limited supplies of WHO-approved vaccines acquired through unnamed international partners, making it the first country in East Africa to begin its campaign. Healthcare workers and other high-risk groups will be the first to receive a vaccine.
Guinea declares a new Ebola epidemic after three people died and four others became ill in the country’s southeast.

context: Cyprus-Israel relations, COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus, COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Cypriot President Nicos Anastasiades and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announce an agreement to allow vaccinated travelers to travel between the countries without the need to quarantine in order to restore their countries' tourism industries.
The leaders of the junta issue warnings to the public against harboring fugitives at the same time that arrest warrants are issued. Among the fugitives is democracy activist Min Ko Naing.
Catalans head to the polls to elect the new Parliament of Catalonia.

Pro-independence parties gain a majority of the votes for the first time, though voter participation was the lowest in history. The anti-independence Socialists' Party of Catalonia, led by former national Health Minister Salvador Illa, wins the most seats for a single party. The far-right Vox places fourth and enters Parliament for the first time, winning 11 seats. Citizens, who placed first in the previous election, falls to seventh and loses 30 seats.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in Peru, impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics
text: Peru's Foreign Minister Elizabeth Astete resigns amid an uproar over secret vaccination before the country receives one million doses for health workers.
Kosovans head to the polls to elect the new Assembly of Kosovo. The Vetëvendosje party is expected to gain most seats as it shows on exit polling data.

context: Yemeni Civil War > Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict
text: The Houthis say that they have struck Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport and King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah with drones. A Houthi spokesman said on Twitter that the attacks halted operations in the airports for two hours. The Saudi-led coalition says that it intercepted drones heading towards the kingdom but did not confirm the attacks.

context: Syrian civil war > Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War
text: Israeli airstrikes on Iranian weapons and missile depots near Damascus, Syria, kill six foreign nationals, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. The headquarters of the Syrian Army's 4th Armoured Division is also hit.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Operation Barkhane
text: Chadian President Idriss Déby announces that his government will deploy 1,200 troops to the tripoint of the Burkina Faso–Mali and Burkina Faso–Niger borders.

context: 2021 Myanmar protests, aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: Myanmar's military junta deploys Tatmadaw troops and cuts Internet services in many parts of the country hours after security forces fired live rounds to disperse a demonstration in the northern state of Kachin.
Multiple rockets strike near Erbil International Airport in Kurdistan Region, Iraq, killing a foreign civilian contractor and wounding nine others, including a U.S. service member.

Bishop David Zubik of the Pittsburgh Diocese announces that four Catholic elementary schools are merging to form two schools for the school year beginning in fall 2021. The decision comes after more than a year's deliberation and hours of study.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark, Economy of Denmark
text: Denmark's GDP contracts 3.7% in 2020, which is the first annual economic contraction since 2009 due to the impact of the pandemic.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 recession > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan, economy of Japan
text: Japan's GDP contracts 4.8% in 2020, which is the first annual economic contraction since 2009 due to the impact of the pandemic.
The World Trade Organization formally appoints former Finance Minister of Nigeria Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala as its first African and first female Director-General.

A passenger barge crashes and capsizes on the Congo River in Mai-Ndombe Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing at least 60 people, while 240 others are reported missing. At least 300 people have been rescued from the river.
At least 37 people are killed by a bus falling off a bridge into a canal in Madhya Pradesh, India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico begins the second phase of its vaccination programme for people over the age of 60 against COVID-19 in more than 300 municipalities.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut, 501.V2 variant
text: Connecticut reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from Fairfield County with no known international travel history, which was notified by health officials in New York.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Mississippi reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Australia suspends its quarantine-free travel bubble arrangement with New Zealand after the discovery of three new community cases in Auckland.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Australia receives 142,000 doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand receives 60,000 doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Auckland enters level three restrictions for the next three days in response to an ongoing COVID-19 outbreak, closing all non-essential businesses and suspending all in-person education. The rest of the country will enter level 2 restrictions, which will limit public gatherings.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern confirms that three members of a family in Auckland who tested positive for COVID-19 are infected with the UK variant and that this is not connected to any managed isolation or quarantine facilities.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Cambodia reports their first three cases of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom in 28-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman from India and a 23-year-old woman who travelled from China.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Iraq announces that they will re-impose a partial lockdown from February 18 until March 8 after reporting their first cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan surpasses 7,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency scales back Q1 vaccination targets to 750,000 people due to delayed shipments from COVAX and the decision not to use the AstraZeneca vaccine on people aged 65 or older until more efficacy data becomes available.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnamese authorities order two million people in Hải Dương province to stay at home for 15 days beginning tomorrow due to a growing COVID-19 outbreak in the province. Gatherings with more than two people are banned, and when leaving their homes, residents must stay from others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: The United Kingdom begins a mandatory hotel quarantine for all British and Irish citizens and all permanent residents arriving in England from 33 "high risk" countries, requiring them to stay for 10 days at government-designated accommodations.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scotland begins a mandatory hotel quarantine for all international arrivals, requiring them to self-isolate for 10 days in one of six government-designated hotels.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia
text: Colombia receives their first shipment of 50,000 doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe receives their first shipment of 200,000 doses of the Sinopharm vaccine.
The World Health Organization announces the approval of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine.
An Ebola vaccination campaign begins in the city of Butembo, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Health workers are the first to be vaccinated.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan accuses the United States of supporting "the PKK terrorists", following the killing of 13 Turkish hostages held captive in Kurdistan Region. Turkey also summons the U.S. ambassador David M. Satterfield in response to the killings.

Iran says that it has informed the International Atomic Energy Agency that it will no longer allow snap inspections of its nuclear facilities as of February 21. The snap inspections were a condition of the 2015 Iranian nuclear deal.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol, January 6 commission
text: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi announces that Congress will establish a 9/11-style commission to investigate the January 6 riot at the United States Capitol.

Turkish authorities announce the detention of 718 people they accuse of having links to Kurdish militant groups. Among those arrested include pro-Kurdish Peoples' Democratic Party officials. The mass arrests are seen as a direct response to the murder of 13 Turkish hostages in Iraq. The Kurdistan Workers' Party blamed Turkish airstrikes on their bases for the deaths of the hostages.
President Francisco Sagasti appoints Allan Wagner Tizón as new foreign minister, a day after Elizabeth Astete resigned over secretly receiving a vaccination against COVID-19.
Michael McDowell wins the 63rd running of the Daytona 500. It is McDowell's first career victory in the Cup Series.

Houthi forces continue to advance on the city of Maʼrib, capturing the village of al-Zor and reaching the Marib Dam. Yemeni government officials say that dozens of people have been killed in the past 24 hours as government forces counter the Houthi offensive. UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Mark Lowcock condemns the Houthi assault, warning of "unimaginable humanitarian consequences".

A spokesperson for the rebel group Tigray People's Liberation Front claims that an estimated 100,000 troops (both Tigrayan and Ethiopian) have been killed during the conflict. Three Ethiopian opposition parties previously claimed that an estimated 52,000 civilians have also died.

Rwandan President Paul Kagame says the reported deaths in Tigray were too high to let Ethiopia and the African Union handle the situation alone. He adds that the UN should intervene in the Tigray War, explaining that when a state is not able to stop atrocities on its territory, such as genocide, the UN has a duty to intervene.

context: War in Afghanistan, Afghan peace process
text: New Zealand announces that it will withdraw its forces from Afghanistan by May.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The White House announces that President Joe Biden will extend the foreclosure ban and mortgage forbearance through the end of June as an effort to address the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
A tornado in Brunswick County, North Carolina, kills three people and injures ten others.

context: 2020–21 North American winter, February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm
text: A winter storm kills at least 23 people and causes power outages for millions of people across the United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon confirms that a phased return to school will begin on February 22, which will include pre-school children, pupils in primaries 1, 2 and 3, and secondary students who need to carry out practical assignments.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary > COVID-19 vaccination in Hungary
text: Hungary receives 550,000 doses of the Sinopharm vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy's first case of B.1525 variant found in Naples in a person who had recently travelled from a country in Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta, 501.V2 variant
text: Malta reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts, 501.V2 variant
text: Massachusetts reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in a woman in her 20s from Middlesex County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Republic begins to inoculate medical workers as part of a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 following the arrival of the first 20,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico
text: Mexico surpasses two million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea > COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea
text: South Korea signs an agreement with Novavax and Pfizer to secure additional doses of the COVID-19 vaccine for 23 million people in the second quarter of this year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Palestine reports their first cases of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom in 139 people from the West Bank.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: Health Minister Mai al-Kaila accuses Israel of blocking the delivery of 2,000 doses of the Sputnik V vaccine to the Gaza Strip, intended for ICU and emergency staff.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India, Variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: India reports their first four cases of the 501.V2 variant from South Africa and one case of the Lineage P.1 variant from Brazil in people who traveled internationally.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia extends their movement control order in Selangor, Johor and Penang as well as the federal territory of Kuala Lumpur until March 4 but eases restrictions in other parts of the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: Morocco receives its second shipment of 500,000 doses of China's Sinopharm vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: The first batch consisting 80,000 doses of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine arrives at OR Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg, which is unapproved for general use in South Africa and worldwide.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The Therapeutic Goods Administration approves the emergency use of the vaccine developed by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca for people over 18 years of age in Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazilian Environment Minister Ricardo Salles tests positive for COVID-19.

The World Health Organization asks six African countries (Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Ivory Coast, Sierra Leone, and Liberia) to be on the alert for possible Ebola outbreaks after Guinea and the Democratic Republic of Congo reported new cases that signaled a resurgence of the outbreak.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état, COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar
text: The Myanmar Police Force files new charges against ousted State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi for violating COVID-19 regulations, which may allow her to be held indefinitely without trial.

A lower court in The Hague orders the government to scrap its 9:00 p.m. to 4:30 a.m. curfew, citing violations of freedom of movement and assembly. Prime Minister Mark Rutte's government appealed the court decision, which was overturned by a high court.

A court in Bangladesh sentences five men to death for murdering Avijit Roy, an American-Bangladeshi blogger critical of religious extremism, six years ago. The men belong to the al-Qaeda-inspired group Ansarullah Bangla Team. Another man was sentenced to life in prison.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The NAACP and U.S. Representative Bennie Thompson file a lawsuit accusing former President Donald Trump, Trump lawyer and former New York City mayor Rudy Giuliani, and far-right groups such as the Proud Boys and Oath Keepers of conspiring to incite the January 6 riot at the United States Capitol. The lawsuit, citing the Ku Klux Klan Act of 1871, also accuses the defendants of disrupting the certification of Biden's victory by Congress.
Belarus authorities raid the offices of the Association of Journalists and Viasna Human Rights Centre as part of the latest move to end protests against President Alexander Lukashenko.
Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison announces that there will be a probe following accusations of rape against his government in Parliament.

Two men accused of leading a Christian-majority Anti-balaka group in the Central African Republic that targeted Muslims plead not guilty at the start of their trial at the International Criminal Court.

Footage obtained by the BBC programme Panorama reveals that Dubai sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed Al Maktoum has been held in a private villa for at least a year after she attempted to escape from her family in February 2018. Latifa's close associates are calling for international intervention after they stopped receiving messages from her, fearing for her safety.
The Electoral Tribunal unanimously dismisses the electoral protest of former Senator Bongbong Marcos against Vice President Leni Robredo.

Thousands of protestors defy COVID-19 restrictions and take to the streets in Kherrata to both commemorate the second anniversary of the protests and to repeat their demands for the ruling government to step down.

A school pupil is killed and 27 others are kidnapped from their school in the early hours in Kagara, Niger State, Nigeria. Three staff members and 12 of their relatives are also abducted. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India
text: The Indian government issues new Standard Operational Procedure (SOP) guidelines that would be mandatory for travelers from the United Kingdom, Europe, Brazil, and South Africa to conduct self-paid molecular COVID-19 testing, beginning from February 22 at 23:59 p.m. IST.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 vaccine > COVID-19 vaccination in Israel
text: The Israeli Maccabi Healthcare Services confirm that, in a trial of 602,000 people who received the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, the vaccine's effectiveness was 95%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 beginning with 40,000 health workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: The first shipment of the Sputnik V vaccine donated by Russia arrives in Gaza after Israel allows the shipment of 1,000 vaccines, which was previously blocked.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan approves and certifies the use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine for mass vaccination.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark, 501.V2 variant
text: Denmark reports their first community transmission of the 501.V2 variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The Spanish Health Ministry introduces a ten-day quarantine for all travelers arriving from Brazil and South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announces that the country will gradually lift COVID-19 restrictions, including curfews and weekend lockdowns beginning in March on a provincial basis, which will divide the country into four categories based on infection and vaccination rates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The British clinical trials ethics body approves the world's first COVID-19 human challenge study, which will begin in the next few weeks. Volunteers aged 18 to 30 will be exposed to the virus in the trial.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: The European Commission signs a deal with Moderna to secure additional 300 million doses of the vaccine in the European Union.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia
text: Somalia orders all government employees in ministries and departments except directors and senior staff to work from home following an increase in COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa begins its vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using a vaccine from Johnson & Johnson, which has not yet been authorized worldwide. President Cyril Ramaphosa, government officials, and health workers are among the first to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tanzania
text: Zanzibar's first Vice President, Seif Sharif Hamad, dies from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland, Lineage P.1
text: Maryland reports their first case of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil in a deceased adult aged older than 65 living in Washington metropolitan area, who had international travel.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: North Dakota reports their first case of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2.

Protesters in the capital Naypyidaw, Mandalay, and the country's largest city Yangon stage a record number of demonstrations against military junta since February 1 coup. Many of public and private employees and civil servant join demonstrations despite military's warning.
Astronomers announce the discovery of HD 110082 b, a sub-Neptune exoplanet that is three times larger than Earth and which orbits a relatively young star.

Houthi forces take control of the Marib Dam, al-Balaq, Dahwan, and Athaf mountains, and the Kholan area, among others, as coalition forces retreat. This is the first time since 2015 that the Houthis control Marib Dam, which gives the Houthis fire control of the southern road to Marib.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb, Mali War
text: Jihadist insurgents kill nine people in an ambush in Burkina Faso, while another jihadist attack near Bandiagara, Mopti Region, Mali, kills nine people and leaves others missing, according to local government officials.

Secretary General of NATO Jens Stoltenberg announces an increase in NATO personnel in Iraq from 500 to around 4,000 amid a surge in ISIL activity in the country. The training mission will also be expanded to more areas beyond Baghdad and include more Iraqi security institutions, according to Stoltenberg.

Facebook bans Australian news publishers from posting and Australian users from viewing and sharing news content in a preemptive retaliation move against the Australian Competition & Consumer Commission's (ACCC) proposed News Media Bargaining Code, which would require Facebook to pay to host Australian news content. A number of key government and charity organisations were also blocked for several hours.
Alphabet Inc. agrees to begin paying News Corp for news content. News Corp CEO Robert Thomson credits the ACCC's proposed legislation with making the deal possible.

context: 2020–21 North American winter > February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm, 2021 Texas power crisis
text: In Texas, power is restored to millions of homes, but millions of people lack safe drinking water and 325,000 homes and businesses remain without power.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Lockdown restrictions are eased in Victoria as contact tracers are confident that all cases linked to a recent outbreak are self-isolating. People are permitted to leave their homes for non-essential reasons but are required to wear a mask when they are indoors. Private gatherings of up to five people and public gatherings of up to 20 people are once again permitted. Non-essential businesses and on-campus learning have been reopened, and businesses that were working from home can have up to 50% of their employees return to the office.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: South Australia reopens its land border with Victoria to the state's regional population, while still restricting travelers from Melbourne, the location of the recent outbreak. Similar restrictions are also in place at the New South Wales and Tasmanian borders.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Restrictions are eased in New Zealand, with Auckland downgraded to alert level 2 and the rest of the country to alert level 1. Most Auckland schools are reopened and masks are made mandatory on public transportation.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong grants emergency use authorization to the Sinovac CoronaVac vaccine, making it the second vaccine to be approved in the city.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 25 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby surpassing 1,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal
text: Nepal approves the emergency use of the Sinopharm vaccine, which is the second vaccine to be approved in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia's Food and Drug Authority approves the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria
text: Nigeria approves the emergency use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine produced by the Serum Institute of India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe begins its vaccination programme against COVID-19 using China's Sinopharm vaccine. Health minister and Vice President Constantino Chiwenga is the first person to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil surpasses 10 million cases of COVID-19, being the second country to do so after the United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: Venezuela launches a vaccination program against COVID-19 using Sputnik V vaccine starting with frontline health workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada, 501.V2 variant
text: Nevada reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person who travelled from South Africa to Reno and who later began showing symptoms of COVID-19.

Lab studies suggest that the Pfizer–BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines are significantly less effective in providing antibody protection against the 501.V2 variant of the disease, which is most prevalent in South Africa.

context: Iran–United States relations, United States sanctions against Iran
text: The Biden administration rescinds the UN sanctions placed on Iran by his predecessor Donald Trump, seen as a potential step towards rejoining the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. The "snapback" of sanctions had been ignored by the rest of the world.

Israel and Syria carry out a Russian-mediated prisoner exchange. An Israeli woman who crossed the border into Syria's Quneitra Governorate and was detained by the Syrian military, is returned in exchange for two Syrian shepherds held by the Israel Defense Forces.
Canada and the United Kingdom announce sanctions on the military junta generals in response to the coup and the arbitrary detention of Aung San Suu Kyi and other political figures.

context: 2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest, Internet Censorship in India
text: A New Delhi court sends climate activist Disha Ravi to jail for allegedly sharing a "toolkit" on social media in connection with the ongoing farmers' protest against three farm bills as it investigates further. Ms. Ravi, a resident of Bangalore, was arrested on February 4 and flown overnight to New Delhi.
