Following pressure from the international community, Ethiopia releases three reporters working for the BBC, AFP, and Financial Times, alongside two local news reporters and two translators, without charge. No reason was given for their arrest, and it is still unclear if four other journalists have been released.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, Economy of Australia
text: The Australian GDP contracted 1.1% in 2020 amid restrictions related to the pandemic.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economy of Brazil
text: The Brazilian GDP contracts 4.1% in 2020 amid disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. It is the country's third worst economic performance after 1981 (-4.25%) and 1990 (-4.35%).

Chancellor of the Exchequer Rishi Sunak delivers the 2021 Spring budget to the House of Commons, announcing the government's tax and spending plans for the year ahead, as well as further COVID-19 support measures, including extending the furlough until the end of September and increasing the minimum wage beginning in April.
Ten people are killed in a plane crash in Jonglei State, South Sudan.
A 6.3 magnitude earthquake strikes central Greece and is felt in neighbouring countries. Most of the damage is reported in the Greek region of Thessaly.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: President Ram Nath Kovind receives his first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan receives their first shipment of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan
text: Uzbekistan surpasses 80,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: The government announces that they will receive 3,000 doses of the AstraZeneca vaccine from France.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark, Lineage P.1
text: Denmark reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil in a person from the Capital Region.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro
text: Montenegro receives 30,000 doses of the Sinopharm BBIBP-CorV vaccine donated by China.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Polish biotechnology company Mabion S.A. signs an agreement with Novavax to begin commercial-scale production trials for Novavax's future vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia
text: Slovakia imposes an overnight curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time, in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. The curfew will last until at least March 19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: The Government of Catalonia announces that 79,000 vaccinated persons were mistakenly recorded as COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda receives its first shipment of 240,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal
text: Senegal receives 324,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Sudan
text: Sudan receives over 800,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine at the Khartoum International Airport through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative, becoming the first country in the Middle East and North Africa to receive it.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey, variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: New Jersey reports its first two cases of the Lineage P.1 variant in Hudson County and 34 cases of a New York variant of SARS-CoV-2 in the northeastern part of the state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: São Paulo governor João Doria announces that the entire state will revert to "red phase" restrictions, which means that all malls and non-essential businesses will be closed for two weeks beginning March 6 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.
China confirms an outbreak of African swine fever in domestic pigs being illegally transported through Funing County in Yunnan province.

Attorney-General, House Leader, and Industrial Relations Minister Christian Porter comes forward as the minister accused of raping a woman in 1988, who has since committed suicide, in an anonymous letter sent to Prime Minister Scott Morrison last week. Porter denies the allegations and announces that he will be taking a mental health leave.
Alek Minassian is found guilty of murdering 10 people, and attempting to kill 16 more, in a vehicle-ramming attack.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The United States Capitol Police announces that it has obtained intelligence on a "possible plot" by an identified militia group to breach the United States Capitol building on the following day, March 4, which has recently been the subject of QAnon conspiracy theories. In response to the intelligence, the United States House of Representatives announces that it has ended its work for the week.
A pipe bomb explodes outside a COVID-19 test centre in Bovenkarspel, Netherlands, causing minor damage. No one is wounded in the explosion.
France bans far-right Identitarian nationalist group Génération Identitaire. Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin says the movement incites "discrimination, hatred and violence".

German intelligence agency Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution formally places far-right oppositional party Alternative for Germany under surveillance, accusing it of aiming to subvert the constitution. It is the first time that a major political party has been placed under surveillance since the end of World War II.

Freedom House, in its annual Freedom in the World report, downgrades India from "free" to "partially free". The report cites the rise in mob violence against Muslims, increased government interference in the judiciary, increased intimidation against journalists and activists, and the government's heavy-handed approach to COVID-19 lockdowns that left millions of migrants stranded as the main reasons for the downgrade.

Hungary's ruling party Fidesz withdraws from the conservative European Parliament bloc European People's Party (EPP), after the EPP changed its rules to allow it to expel a party's entire delegation. Fidesz's membership had been suspended since 2019 after it accused then-European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker and philanthropist George Soros of conspiring to "flood" Europe with migrants during a national campaign.
The United Nations calls on Ethiopia to grant them access to the Tigray region to investigate reports of mass murders and sexual violence that may amount to war crimes.
Archbishop Cesare Nosiglia of Turin, Italy announces that for the second time, the Shroud of Turin will be exposed for veneration on social media and websites on Holy Saturday, April 3.
An army helicopter crashes in Bitlis, Turkey, killing 11 military personnel and injuring two others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: The Robert Koch Institute's Standing Committee on Vaccination officially approves the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine for people aged over 65.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: The government orders all schools and non-essential shops in Hungary to close from March 8 until March 22 (for non-essential shops) and April 7 (for schools) due to a third wave of COVID-19 infections.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: Prime Minister Robert Abela announces that the government will limit indoor gatherings to four households and will ban mass gatherings other than weddings and religious activities beginning tomorrow due to a record increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. The government will also restrict the operation of restaurants and snack bars to only offer takeaway services.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Ukraine reports its first cases of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the United Kingdom in two people from Ivano-Frankivsk.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > European Commission–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine dispute, COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy invokes the European Union powers to block shipment of 250,700 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine to Australia amid escalations between the bloc and AstraZeneca. The European Commission endorses the move.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Prime Minister Hun Sen receives a dose of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied by the COVAX initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait
text: Kuwait's Cabinet decides to impose a curfew from 5:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time for the next month but will allow salons, gyms, and other commercial activities to reopen on March 7 subject to operating restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines
text: The Philippines receives its first shipment of 487,200 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied by the COVAX initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka's National Medicines Regulatory Authority approves the use of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, becoming the second vaccine to be made available for the general public.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Lesotho
text: Lesotho receives its first shipment of 36,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe becomes the first country in Africa to approve India's Covaxin vaccine manufactured by Bharat Biotech.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Nine great apes in San Diego Zoo becomes the first non-human primates to receive an experimental COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine, 501.V2 variant
text: Maine reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil reports a record 1,910 deaths from COVID-19 in the last 24 hours, bringing the national death toll to 259,271.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: The United States Capitol Police requests that the National Guard remain at the Capitol for 60 days in response to a possible second attack on the building.
Police in Bignona, Senegal, open fire against a group of people demonstrating against the arrest of opposition leader Ousmane Sonko, killing a protester.
Twenty people are killed and others are feared dead after smugglers intentionally throw 80 migrants overboard during a voyage from Djibouti to Yemen.

context: The Troubles, Brexit and the Irish border
text: The Loyalist Communities Council and other loyalist groups in Northern Ireland inform Prime Minister Boris Johnson that they are withdrawing support for the Good Friday Agreement in opposition to the Northern Ireland Protocol.

The Indian government's Income Tax Department raids the residences of the founders of Phantom Films due to allegations of tax evasion. Those being interrogated include Anurag Kashyap, Taapsee Pannu, Vikas Bahl, Vikramaditya Motwane, and Madhu Mantena. The incident prompts the Maha Vikas Aghadi alliance and Rahul Gandhi to support the film stars who are being interrogated, saying the Bharatiya Janata Party is using all the arms of the government to stifle the voices of those who support the Indian farmers' protest.
Italian Democratic Party secretary Nicola Zingaretti resigns, citing infighting over government posts.

The North Dakota House of Representatives votes to expel State Representative Luke Simons (R) following allegations that he threatened and sexually harassed women going back to 2017, when he first took office. This is the first time that either chamber of the North Dakota Legislative Assembly has passed such a vote.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports, COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan, 2021 Pakistan Super League
text: Pakistan suspends its Twenty20 cricket competition in the Pakistan Super League after seven players tested positive for COVID-19.

context: Somali Civil War > 2021 Mogadishu suicide car bombing
text: At least 20 people are killed and 30 others are wounded by a suicide car bombing outside a restaurant near the port in Mogadishu.

At least seven soldiers are killed after al-Shabaab militants storm a jail in Bosaso, Puntland, Somalia. More than 400 prisoners are freed during the assault, the majority of whom are Al-Shabaab fighters.

A female doctor is killed and a child is wounded in Jalalabad, Nangarhar, when a bomb attached to the doctor's rickshaw explodes, while seven workers at a Hazara plaster factory are shot dead in Surkh-Rōd District, Nangarhar. ISIL is suspected to be behind the attacks.

context: Aftermath of the assassination of Luca Attanasio
text: Mwilanya Asani William, the attorney investigating the murder of Italian ambassador Luca Attanasio and two other people in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, is murdered by unknown gunmen during an ambush.
One person is killed and 11 others are wounded when rockets strike oil refineries near al-Bab and Jarablus, Syria.
The number of farmers who died during the protests, which began in August 2020, increases to 248.
A man is killed after police open fire on a group of protesters in Mandalay.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company, COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California health officials say that stadiums, Disneyland, and other theme parks can reopen beginning on April 1 with limited capacity.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
text: The United States Senate, in a 58–42 vote, rejects an amendment introduced by Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders that would raise the minimum wage to $15 after he made efforts to include it in President Joe Biden's $1.9 trillion relief package.
The German government reaches an agreement with energy providers to compensate them up to €2.4 billion for loss in income attributed to the phase-out of nuclear power, ending years of litigation.

An 8.1 magnitude earthquake strikes off the coast of New Zealand's North Island, initially prompting a tsunami warning. The earthquake was preceded by a 7.4 magnitude foreshock and followed by a 6.1 magnitude aftershock.
A minibus and a trailer-truck collide on a highway near Atfih, Middle Egypt, killing 18 people and injuring five others. The truck driver has since been arrested.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois, Lineage P.1
text: Illinois reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil in a person from Chicago.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee, 501.V2 variant
text: Tennessee reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin, 501.V2 variant
text: Wisconsin reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, 501.V2 variant
text: Manitoba reports its first confirmed case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in a person from Winnipeg.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Health Canada approves the single-dose Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: India administers 1.4 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine in the last 24 hours, which is the highest number of daily vaccinations since the program began on January 16.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: The government extends the COVID-19 state of emergency in the Greater Tokyo Area, which includes the capital Tokyo and surrounding prefectures, for the next two weeks until March 21 as the number of new cases have not fallen sufficiently in order to lift the emergency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports their first two cases of the B.1.525 variant in two people who travelled from Dubai.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan grants emergency use authorisation of the Sinopharm BBIBP-CorV vaccine for people over 60 years of age.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety approves the use of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine following separate evaluations of the vaccine's safety and efficacy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy surpasses three million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova
text: Moldova becomes the first country in Europe to receive a COVAX initiative shipment of 14,400 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania, 501.V2 variant
text: Romania reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in people from Bucharest and Pitești.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: The fatality count from COVID-19 surpasses 200,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria
text: Nigeria officially launches a vaccination campaign against COVID-19, with a doctor who has spent the past year treating COVID-19 patients becoming the first person to be vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using 392,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca and Pfizer–BioNTech vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda
text: Uganda receives their first shipment of 864,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied through the COVAX initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announces that Auckland will move to alert level 2 and rest of the country to alert level one beginning March 7 at 6:00 p.m. NZT after no new community cases have been reported.

Australia's Special Broadcasting Service suspends China Global Television Network and China Central Television from broadcasting in the country following a human rights complaint from pan-Asian human rights organization Safeguard Defenders.

context: Myanmar–United States relations, 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: The Biden administration sanctions Myanmar's Ministry of Defence and Ministry of Home Affairs in response to the coup and the military junta's crackdown on protesters.
Pope Francis arrives in Baghdad in the first ever Papal visit to Iraq.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol > Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: A former U.S. State Department official during the Trump administration is arrested and charged for assault and other crimes in relation to the storming of the United States Capitol, thereby making him the first known Trump administration official to be tried in relation to the events of January 6.
Protests continue in Senegal against the arrest of opposition leader Ousmane Sonko, with three more people confirmed dead, bringing the death toll to 4.
A call for a specific law against honour killings begins in India, after a father in Uttar Pradesh beheaded his daughter two days ago, after opposing her relationship with a man.

The Cologne administrative court temporarily bars the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) from placing the far-right party Alternative for Germany (AfD) under surveillance, ruling that BfV's announcement two days ago that it was surveying the party violated an agreement to keep the surveillance classified. The court said that the BfV will have to wait until a lawsuit brought by the AfD on the matter is settled before it can proceed.
YouTube suspends channels run by Myanmar's military and removes junta propaganda videos for "violating its community guidelines and terms of service".
Fighting between Houthi forces and pro-government troops in Maʼrib Governorate, Yemen, kills 58 and 32, respectively, in the past 24 hours, according to unnamed military sources.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
text: The United States Senate votes 50–49 to pass President Joe Biden's $1.9 trillion relief package after 24 hours of debate and vote-a-rama sessions on the bill. The amended legislation will head back to the United States House of Representatives for a final vote.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, receives a dose of the COVID-19 vaccine in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines > COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines
text: Moderna signs a supply deal with the government to supply 13 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine from mid-2021.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei
text: The government announces that it will ease their social distancing measures when Brunei enters a "New Normal" phase on March 8 as the country has reported no community cases in the last 300 days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia confirms that it will ease COVID-19-related restrictions in entertainment and events and will reopen cinemas, gyms, and sport centres beginning on March 7.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland > COVID-19 vaccination in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland reaches a milestone of 500,000 doses of the COVID-19 vaccine administered.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: French authorities extend their weekend lockdown to the northern region of Pas-de-Calais, prompting hundreds of thousands of people to stay at home on Saturdays and Sundays due to the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi
text: Malawi receives its first shipment of 360,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria
text: President Muhammadu Buhari and Vice President Yemi Osinbajo receive their first doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji
text: Fiji receives its first shipment of 12,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores receive their first doses of the Russian Sputnik V vaccine.
China confirms an outbreak of the African swine fever in the key pork-producing provinces of Hubei and Sichuan.
Prime Minister Imran Khan wins a vote of confidence in the National Assembly of Pakistan amid boycotts from the opposition Pakistan Democratic Movement.
Three Palestinian fishermen are killed in an explosion off the coast of Gaza. The blast is caused by an unknown weapon, suspected to be a rocket.
Khin Maung Latt, a campaign manager from Aung San Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy, dies in police custody after being arrested yesterday.

In retaliation for yesterday's drone attacks against the kingdom, the Saudi-led coalition conducts airstrikes against the Houthis in the Yemeni capital Sanaa. There have been no reports of any immediate casualties.

U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin says that the United States will continue to defend troops and interests. He also says that those who carried out the rocket attack in Iraq will be held accountable.
Nine activists are killed in police raids in the northern Philippines two days after President Rodrigo Duterte ordered government forces to kill communists in the country.

A series of explosions kill 20 people and injure more than 600 others in Bata, Equatorial Guinea. The cause is suspected to be negligence related to use of dynamite at a local military base. Almost all buildings in the city are heavily damaged.
A fire occurs at a detention center for migrants in Sanaa, Yemen, killing at least eight people and injuring more than 170 others.
At least one person is killed and 40 others are injured when a train derails in Sindh, Pakistan.
A Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil crashes in Normandy, France, killing National Assembly member and businessman Olivier Dassault and the aircraft's pilot.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 vaccination in Australia
text: Former Prime Minister Julia Gillard and current Health Minister Greg Hunt receive their first doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Caledonia
text: New Caledonia orders a strict lockdown for two weeks beginning at midnight tomorrow following the detection of nine COVID-19 cases among non-quarantined travellers arriving from Wallis and Futuna.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Auckland is downgraded to alert level 2 while the rest of New Zealand moves to alert level 1 following confirmation that there are no more community cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel reopens restaurants, bars, and other entertainment venues for those who have been vaccinated against COVID-19. Middle-school students return to school in some areas and university classes also resume for those who have been vaccinated. Israeli citizens are also allowed to return to Israel without any special permissions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: At age 95, former Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad becomes the oldest person in Malaysia to receive a dose of the COVID-19 vaccine in Langkawi, Kedah.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal
text: Nepal receives 348,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka receives its first shipment of 264,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria suspends vaccinations using the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution while investigating the death of a person who received it.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia
text: North Macedonia grants emergency use authorization for Russia's Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia, 501.V2 variant
text: Slovakia reports its first seven cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio, Lineage P.1
text: Ohio reports its first cases of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia receives its first shipment of 2.2 million doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

Swiss voters approve a ban on full-facial coverings in public, known popularly as a so-called "burqa ban", and a free trade agreement with Indonesia, while rejecting a government proposal to introduce nationwide electronic IDs, which would be required to open a bank account or request official documents.

Rangers wins the Scottish Premiership, the top-flight league in Scottish football, for the first time since 2011 after their rivals Celtic failed to win against Dundee United. It is Rangers manager and former England captain Steven Gerrard's first trophy as a manager, and the win also denies Celtic a record 10th consecutive Premiership title.
Former FC Barcelona president Joan Laporta wins the club's 14th presidential election with 54.2% of the votes.
Two people are killed and three others injured in Myitkyina after being shot in the head, as security forces open fire on people protesting against the coup d'état in Myanmar.
Multiple people are injured by a homemade bomb accidentally detonating in a classroom at Newaygo High School in Newaygo, Michigan, United States.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
text: Myanmar's State Administration Council revokes the licence of five media companies, namely Myanmar Now, Khit Thit Media, Democratic Voice of Burma (DVB), Mizzima, and 7Day, amidst the crackdown on press outlets covering anti-coup protests.

Cyprus, Greece, and Israel sign an agreement to build the world's largest and deepest submarine power cable that will connect the three Mediterranean countries' power grids at a cost of about $900 million. The project is expected to be completed by 2024.
The death toll from yesterday's explosions in Bata, Equatorial Guinea, rises to 98 people. More than 615 others are wounded.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England, impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education
text: Millions of students across England return to primary and secondary schools after two months studying at home during the third lockdown as a first step towards a return to normality.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19, becoming the second country in Europe to reach the milestone after the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The region of Campania enters a lockdown which is expected to end on March 21.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria reports its first case of the Lineage P.2 variant first detected in Brazil in a person from Salzburg state.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports its youngest death from COVID-19. The patient was a 37-day-old infant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: Prime Minister Mark Rutte extends the country's strict lockdown until the end of the month and advises against foreign travel until April 15. The curfew from 9 p.m. to 4:30 a.m. will remain in place through the election on March 17, but those working or visiting a voting booth will not be fined for breaching it.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in East Timor
text: East Timor imposes a "sanitary fence and mandatory confinement" in the capital Dili for the next seven days beginning at midnight. This is the country's first lockdown since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia receives its first shipment of 1.1 million doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine supplied through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports a record 108 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,336.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Syria
text: President Bashar al-Assad and his wife Asma al-Assad both test positive for COVID-19, according to a statement from the presidential office. They are both reported to be in good health with "minor symptoms".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam begins a vaccination programme against COVID-19 starting with health workers in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Hai Duong Province using the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Hawaii, 501.V2 variant
text: Hawaii reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in South Africa in a person from Oahu with no known travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan, 501.V2 variant
text: Michigan reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in South Africa in a child from Jackson County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. surpasses 29 million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: The government announces a deal with Pfizer to receive 14 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine by June, and a total of 99 million doses by the end of the year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announces that the New Zealand Government has secured 8.5 million doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine, and that they have now secured enough vaccines to vaccinate the entire population of New Zealand.

The trial of former Minneapolis Police Department officer Derek Chauvin begins in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Chauvin's trial is the first time that a judge in Minnesota has authorized cameras to show a full criminal trial.

Brazilian Supreme Federal Court Justice Edson Fachin rules that all convictions of former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva must be nullified. This ruling restores Lula's political rights and thus clears the way for his presidential candidacy in 2022.
A judge in Senegal releases opposition leader Ousmane Sonko on bail, after days of protests as a result of his arrest. Eight people died during the protests.

Protesters block all major roads leading to the capital Beirut amid continued unrest over the crash of the pound, increase in consumer goods prices, mass unemployment and delay of the formation of a new government.
Parliament meets in the central city of Sirte to vote on the approval of the interim Government of National Unity, led by Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh. Voting is expected to take place tomorrow.
At least 39 people are dead while 165 others are rescued when two boats sink off the coast of Tunisia while trying to reach Lampedusa, Italy.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Alaska
text: Governor Mike Dunleavy announces that Alaska will drop its eligibility requirements for the COVID-19 vaccine and allow all residents over the age of 16 to receive it, thereby becoming the first state to do so. The state has also led other states in the percentage of its population to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota
text: North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum receives the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia, Lineage P.1
text: British Columbia reports its first three cases of Lineage P.1 variant first detected in Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon announces that four people from two households will be able to meet outdoors from March 12, three days sooner than expected, as part of easing of their national lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia, variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: The Estonian government approves new measures to lockdown the entire country from March 11 until April 11 due to the spread of variants of SARS-CoV-2, which means that non-essential shops will be closed, primary schools will shift to remote learning, and groups of more than two people will be banned.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italian President Sergio Mattarella receives the first dose of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia
text: Prime Minister Zoran Zaev confirms that the government will impose a nationwide curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time from tomorrow until March 22, as well as a mandatory 14-day quarantine for all travelers from Africa, in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine grants approval for the Sinovac CoronaVac vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Sudan
text: Sudan begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 beginning with medical workers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia receives its first major shipment of 30,000 doses of the Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe
text: Zimbabwe grants emergency use authorization for four COVID-19 vaccines, including China's CoronaVac and BBIBP-CorV, Russia's Sputnik V, and India's Covaxin.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Prime Minister Hun Sen orders a temporary closure of the country's civil institutions and reduces their on-site employees by 90% for at least a week, with the exception of military and health workers due to an increase in COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: The Indonesian Food and Drug Authority approves the emergency use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines surpasses 600,000 total COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil reports a record 1,972 new deaths in the past 24 hours amid slow vaccination rollout and overwhelmed hospitals, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 268,370.

context: United States–Venezuela relations, Immigration policy of the Joe Biden administration
text: The Biden administration grants temporary protected status to Venezuelans living in the United States. The decision will allow thousands of Venezuelan migrants to stay and work legally in the U.S., and it will remain in effect for 18 months.

context: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état, Myanmar–United Kingdom relations
text: Myanmar recalls its Ambassador to the United Kingdom Kyaw Zwar Minn after he publicly called for the release of jailed State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi.

The European Parliament votes to strip Carles Puigdemont, Toni Comín, and Clara Ponsatí of their parliamentary immunity, allowing Spanish prosecutors to extradite them to Spain and prosecute them for sedition and embezzlement.
Núria Calduch becomes the first female Secretary of the Pontifical Biblical Commission named by Pope Francis.

The China National Space Administration and Roscosmos sign a memorandum of understanding to establish a joint lunar space station. Roscosmos Director General Dmitry Rogozin says that the space station will be a "complex of experimental research facilities created on the surface or in the orbit of the Moon", and will be available for use by "international partners".

The Victoria State Government announces the establishment of a truth commission into genocidal violence against the state's Indigenous population from the late 18th century to the early 20th century, as part of a process towards developing a treaty.

The armed forces kill twelve people in an operation in the Guaviare Department against a group run by a former FARC leader. Defense Minister Diego Molano Aponte says that there were child soldiers present at the camp but declines to say if they were killed or state their ages.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States House of Representatives votes 220–211 to pass the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, which extends weekly jobless benefit payments of $300 until September, sends $1,400 checks to individuals, and funds other coronavirus relief programs for states and businesses. The stimulus bill will be sent to President Joe Biden for his signature.

An overnight fire at an OVHcloud server farm in Strasbourg destroys a data center and damages another, taking millions of .fr websites offline in France, including government websites, banks, online shops, and news websites.
A bus carrying dozens of pilgrims plunges into a ravine in Indonesia's Java island, killing at least 27 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan
text: Michigan surpasses 600,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey, 501.V2 variant
text: New Jersey reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan
text: Saskatchewan surpasses 30,000 cases of COVID-19, and 400 related deaths.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Karnataka, 501.V2 variant
text: Karnataka reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan approves the emergency use of the Russian Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports a record 109 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,481.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan begins COVID-19 vaccination rollout for those aged 60 years or older as part of the second phase of their vaccination programme.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya
text: Kenya approves the emergency use of the Russian Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Mauritius
text: Mauritius imposes a two-week nationwide lockdown for the second time since the pandemic began, with only essential services able to continue to operate, after the discovery of 14 local COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tanzania
text: The President of Tanzania John Magufuli has not been seen in public since February 27. Opposition leaders call for the release of information as rumors grow that he is on a ventilator at a hospital in Nairobi, Kenya.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Togo
text: Togo begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine. Prime Minister Victoire Tomegah Dogbé is the first person to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria
text: Bulgaria reports 3,502 new cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total since December 11, and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 266,805.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: The Government of Malta announces that, due to record numbers of new cases, all theatres, museums, and gyms will be closed, all organised sports and religious activities will be banned, and gatherings will be limited to four people. The government also announces that all educational institutions will be closed as of March 15 and travel to Gozo will be restricted to residents and essential activities.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports 17,260 new cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total since November, and it subsequently brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,828,313.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji
text: Fiji begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine donated by the COVAX initiative. Ten frontline workers are the first to receive doses of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea
text: The government of Papua New Guinea approves the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine. Prime Minister James Marape says that vaccination will not be compulsory and will initially be directed at health workers, people over 50 years of age and people with underlying health conditions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil reports a record 2,286 new deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours as intensive care units in 25 of 27 regional capitals reach near-full capacity, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 270,656.

At an extraordinary session in Sirte, the Libyan parliament votes 121 to 11 to approve a new Government of National Unity led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh. The new interim unity government will govern Libya until a general election is held in December.

The government says a decree by Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan dismissing the Chief of the General Staff Onik Gasparyan is now legally effective despite President Armen Sarksyan refusing to sign the decree into force.
Ivorian Prime Minister Hamed Bakayoko dies of cancer at a private hospital in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany.

U.S. and Arab officials disclose a clandestine Israeli naval operation against vessels in the Persian Gulf, Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea carrying Iranian oil and weaponry to Syria since 2019. At least twelve Iranian vessels have been bombed with limpet mines, according to U.S. officials.
Twelve protesters are killed as security forces open fire on anti-coup protests.

Militants raid a school in Zamfara, killing a student during an attempted mass kidnapping. As the kidnap fails, the attackers fled and started shooting in the streets, killing twelve more people. It is the second school attack in Zamfara in two weeks.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
text: U.S. President Joe Biden signs the $1.9 trillion relief package into law.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economy of Brazil, COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: The National Congress of Brazil approves an $8 billion spending package to help deal with the second wave of the pandemic in the country.
At least 20 people are killed and 24 others injured in a fire at a clothing factory in Cairo, Egypt.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 vaccination in Italy
text: The Italian Medicines Agency bans a batch of Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccines as a precautionary measure following the death of three military officers in Sicily who had been vaccinated.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: Belarus reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2, which originated in the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark, COVID-19 pandemic in Norway, COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland
text: The Danish Health Authority temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine for two weeks as a "precaution" following reports that some vaccinated people had experienced blood clots, causing one person to die after receiving the vaccine. It has not been determined whether there is a link between the vaccine and the clots. Norway and Iceland have also suspended their use of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary reports a record 8,312 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 489,172.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Costa announces that kindergartens, hair salons, bookshops, libraries, pre-schools and primary schools will be allowed to reopen March 15, as a part of the country's gradual easing of its two-month lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden and Prince Daniel, Duke of Västergötland, test positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: The European Commission grants the approval of single-dose Johnson & Johnson vaccine for general use. It comes after the European Medicines Agency recommends the conditional marketing authorisation for the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia reports its first death from COVID-19. The patient is a 50-year-old man from Phnom Penh.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran receives a shipment of 150,000 doses of the Indian Covaxin vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: The Gaza Strip receives 40,000 doses of the Sputnik V vaccine from the United Arab Emirates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority announces a uniform curfew in Metro Manila for two weeks beginning on March 15 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency extends the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine to people aged 65 and older as overseas trials show its effectiveness.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Benin
text: Benin receives a shipment of 144,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine from India through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Eswatini
text: Eswatini receives a shipment of 20,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwandan President Paul Kagame becomes the first head of state in East Africa to receive a dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota, 501.V2 variant
text: Minnesota reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant of SARS-CoV-2, which originated in South Africa. The patient is a person from the Twin Cities area who became ill on January 24 and tested positive on January 29.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state), Lineage P.1
text: Washington (state) reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2, which originated in Brazil. The patient is a person from the King County.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in South Dakota, Lineage B.1.1.7
text: South Dakota reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant of SARS-CoV-2, which originated in the United Kingdom.

Catalan politician Meritxell Serret surrenders to the Supreme Court after three years in self-imposed exile in Belgium following the declaration of independence in 2017 and her imputation of a crime of disobedience.

context: Andrew Cuomo sexual harassment allegations, New York COVID-19 nursing home scandal
text: The New York State Assembly's judiciary committee is authorized to initiate an impeachment investigation into sexual misconduct allegations against Governor Andrew Cuomo. Earlier that day, more than 50 state lawmakers had called for Cuomo's resignation in the wake of the allegations and his handling of deaths at nursing homes due to COVID-19.

The Kyrgyzstan Parliament approves a new referendum on a draft constitution that would expand the powers of President Sadyr Japarov and allow him to run for office again after his term ends. The referendum will be held on April 11.

China's National People's Congress passes the "decision on improving the electoral system of Hong Kong", which will rewrite the election rules in Hong Kong to ensure a system of "patriots governing Hong Kong". This is seen by many Western countries as further eroding the freedoms of the Hong Kong people.
Pope Francis appoints Archbishop Leo Boccardi, until now apostolic nuncio in Iran, as apostolic nuncio in Japan.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports, COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil > COVID-19 pandemic in São Paulo (state)
text: Governor of São Paulo João Doria announces the suspension of all professional sports from March 15 until March 30 amid a rise of the number of COVID-19 cases.
Thirty students and several staff members are kidnapped from a school in Kaduna State, Nigeria, by a group of gunmen.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria > COVID-19 vaccination in Bulgaria
text: Prime Minister Boyko Borisov announces the suspension of the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine following the death of a 57-year-old woman from Plovdiv after she received her dose.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The French Haute Autorité de Santé approves the use of the single-dose Johnson & Johnson vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France surpasses four million cases and 90,000 deaths of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: A lockdown will start on March 15 and last until April 6 for the Italian regions of Lombardy, Apulia, Friuli Venezia Giulia, Piedmont, Lazio, Veneto, Emilia Romagna, and Marche, thereby bringing the total number of regions under lockdown in the country to 11. The Autonomous Province of Trento is also placed under a lockdown, while strict measures are imposed for eight more regions. Between April 3–5, the entire country will be placed under a lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The Italian Medicines Agency approves the use of the single-dose Johnson & Johnson vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus
text: Belarus reports 1,186 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases to 300,146 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports 14,941 new cases of COVID-19 in the last 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total this year, and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,850,930.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Azerbaijan
text: Azerbaijan approves general use of the Russian Sputnik V vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan, Variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: Japanese health authorities reports its first case of a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a traveler aged 60s from the Philippines. The variant is different from the Brazil, South African, and UK variants.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia receives 14,400 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine through COVAX initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan surpasses 600,000 cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka, 501.V2 variant
text: Sri Lanka reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant, which originated in South Africa, in a person who travelled from Tanzania and is currently staying at a quarantine centre.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand postpones the public vaccination of Prime Minister Prayut Chan-o-cha and his cabinet using the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine following reports of side-effects in some vaccinated people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona, Lineage P.1
text: Arizona reports its first three case of the Lineage P.1 variant, which originated in Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York Lieutenant Governor Kathy Hochul receives a dose of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine at Catholic Health in Buffalo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 100 million COVID-19 vaccine doses that have been administered.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil reports 85,663 new confirmed cases and 2,216 more deaths from COVID-19, surpassing India as the country with the second-highest number of cases in the world, and also bringing Brazil's total cases to 11,363,380.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Auckland returns to alert level 1 and lifts all COVID-19-related restrictions aside from their face mask requirement on public transport after no community cases were found.
The World Health Organization grants emergency use approval for the single-dose Johnson & Johnson vaccine, becoming the third vaccine to be approved after the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines.

In an interview with Greek newspaper Ta Nea, UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson says Britain is the legitimate and legal owner of the historic 2,500-year-old Elgin Marbles amid growing calls to return the marbles to Greece.

context: Hong Kong national security law, 2021 arrests of Hong Kong pro-democracy primaries participants
text: An upper court in Hong Kong denies bail for a second time to 11 of the 47 defendants in the case, citing national security risks. Among those who were again denied bail are prominent activists and politicians such as Leung Kwok-hung, Claudia Mo, Jimmy Sham, Lester Shum, and Fergus Leung. The remaining defendants either withdrew their bail application or remain in custody under other circumstances.

context: Aftermath of the killing of George Floyd
text: The family of George Floyd, the man killed while in police custody last May, settles their lawsuit against the city of Minneapolis for $27 million.
A Metropolitan Police officer is charged with kidnapping and murder.

The Bolivian office of the Prosecutor General issues an arrest order for former interim President Jeanine Áñez, five former members of the national cabinet and the former leadership of the Armed Forces, accusing them of the crimes of sedition and terrorism.
A car bombing near a police station in Herat Province kills at least eight people and wounds more than 50 others.
Twelve people are killed after soldiers open fire on protesters in Mandalay, Yangon, and Pyay. A 13-year-old child is among those killed, the youngest victim of the unrest to date.
Avatar retakes its place as the world's highest-grossing film of all time from Avengers: Endgame following a domestic release in China.
A Kazakh Air Force Antonov An-26 crashes in Almaty, killing four crew members on board and wounding two others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reaches a milestone of five million people having received their first vaccination shot.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (country)
text: Georgia receives 43,200 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine distributed through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
text: Hungary reports a record 9,444 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 507,627.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Wales
text: Wales begins to ease their first step of lockdown restrictions, with "stay-at-home" replaced by "stay local". According to new rules, four people from two households can meet outside and outdoor sports can be resumed.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan's health minister resigns after six COVID-19 patients die due to a lack of supplemental oxygen at a hospital ward in Al-Salt.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan receives 144,000 doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine distributed through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports a record 169 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,833.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, Lineage P.1
text: The Philippines reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a person who travelled from Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 in order to reduce the number of COVID-19 infections, a week after the country received 2.2 million doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using the Sputnik V vaccine. Health workers, soldiers, people over age 65, and people with underlying conditions are the first to receive the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: PlainSite public data reveal 450 workers at the Tesla Factory in Fremont have tested positive for COVID-19 since Tesla CEO Elon Musk reopened the building last May.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Australia reports its first local COVID-19 cases in two weeks, when a doctor in Brisbane tests positive.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives his first dose of the CoronaVac vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Legislative Assembly of Mato Grosso member Silvio Favero, known for introducing a bill against mandatory COVID-19 vaccinations, dies from COVID-19 in Cuiabá, Brazil.

context: China–United Kingdom relations, Hong Kong protests
text: The United Kingdom formally declares China to be in breach of the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, saying that China is now in "a state of ongoing non-compliance" of the treaty. Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab says that the UK will "continue to stand up for the people of Hong Kong".
A Metropolitan Police officer is remanded in custody and will appear at the Old Bailey in London on March 16.

At a candlelight vigil in Clapham, mourners defying COVID-19 gathering restrictions clash with police officers attempting to disperse them, resulting in four arrests. The actions of the police draw condemnation from several officials, including London Mayor Sadiq Khan and Home Secretary Priti Patel.

context: 2020–21 United States racial unrest, Shooting of Breonna Taylor
text: People rally in Louisville, Kentucky, on the first anniversary of the death of Breonna Taylor, who was shot by officers who forced entry to her home using a no-knock warrant. Surrounding roads are closed off, but many felt the security measures were excessive.

Former interim President Jeanine Áñez is arrested by police and is accused of participating in an alleged coup d'état against ousted President Evo Morales in November 2019. Before being arrested, Áñez denounced the arrest and stated that the "persecution had begun".
The Labor Party wins the state election in Western Australia, in one of the biggest landslide victories in the country's history.

Security forces kill at least 54 anti-coup protesters in several cities, thirty-seven of whom were in Yangon. A policeman is also killed. It is the protests' deadliest day. The civilian Vice President, Mahn Win Khaing Than, says that they will pass legislation to "give people the right to defend themselves against the military" and calls for a "revolution" to overthrow the junta. Meanwhile, a junta spokesman labels the protesters as "criminals" but refuses to elaborate.

People armed with axes and crowbars attack and set ablaze ten Chinese factories and a hotel in Yangon, resulting in injuries to several Chinese nationals. Some protesters have accused the Chinese government of supporting the Burmese military.
The 63rd Grammy Awards is held in Los Angeles.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: Labour minister Élisabeth Borne tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: The Government of Ireland temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine following reports from the Norwegian Medicines Agency regarding serious blood clots developing in four people who received the vaccine, one of whom later died.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 vaccination in Italy
text: Piedmont temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine after a teacher in the town of Biella reportedly died after receiving the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: The Netherlands suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine until March 29 following reports of Denmark and Norway regarding possible serious side effects.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta, Lineage P.1
text: Alberta reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant, which was originally detected in Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain
text: Bahrain eases some of its COVID-19-related restrictions, allowing restaurants, cafés, swimming pools, and sport facilities to reopen, but restricts gatherings to no more than 30 people.

AstraZeneca provides an update that from more than 17 million people given a vaccination dose in the UK and EU, there is no evidence of an increased risk of pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or thrombocytopenia, in any defined age group, gender, batch, or in any particular country.
Twenty anti-coup protesters are gunned down by soldiers.
The military junta expands the provisions of Myanmar's martial law, which is perceived as an attempt to legitimize their violent pushback against anti-coup protesters.

context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency, 2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: At least 15 civilians are killed during a mass stabbing in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The ADF is suspected to be behind the attack.

The Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, the Vatican body responsible for promulgating Catholic doctrine, rules that priests cannot bless same-sex unions or marriages, calling any such blessing "not licit".

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: British chocolate maker Thorntons announces it will be permanently closing down all of its stores, with the loss of about 600 jobs, thereby ending its 110-year presence on the high street. The company says it has been massively hit by the pandemic lockdowns and adds that high street conditions are too severe to continue. The company will continue sales online and through supermarkets.
Three people are killed and one injured when a small plane crashes in Pembroke Pines, Florida, U.S.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: The Andorran government announces the suspension of the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as of March 16.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: Cyprus suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine until March 18 pending review from the European Medicines Agency following reports of possible serious side effects among vaccinated people in other EU countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia
text: Prime Minister Kaja Kallas tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: The Ministry of Health detects a new variant of SARS-CoV-2 in a cluster of eight cases in a hospital in Lannion, Brittany. Many of these cases can't be detected by PCR tests.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Nine of the 20 regions, as well as the autonomous province of Trentino, enter a strict state of lockdown, in the government's latest attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Two other regions are also currently in lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia
text: Latvian health authorities temporarily suspend the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of blood clot issues among vaccinated people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: The Directorate-General of Health temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of "rare, but severe" suspected side-effects among vaccinated people in other countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia
text: Slovenia suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of cases of blood clots in vaccinated people in other countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey reports 15,503 new cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total this year, and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,894,893.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City
text: The Vatican Museums and the Palace of Castel Gandolfo's gardens closes for third time for the duration of the last lockdown decree of the Italian Government.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe
text: Germany, Italy, France, and Spain suspend the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine following reports of blood clots.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: The Ministry of Health temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine while awaiting a WHO review amidst reports of cases of blood clots in vaccinated people from several European countries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordan reports a record 9,417 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 486,470.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Maldives
text: The Maldives Food and Drug Authority approves the emergency use of the Pfizer–BioNTech and the Sinopharm BBIBP-CorV vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: President Arif Alvi and First Lady Samina Alvi receive their first doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: Brazil signs a deal with Pfizer to purchase 100 million doses of the Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia
text: Somalia receives their first shipment of 300,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine from the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative.

The European Union notifies the United Kingdom of its intent to start an infringement procedure. According to the EU, the UK breached the Northern Ireland Protocol by unilaterally extending the grace period related to trade on the island of Ireland beyond April 1.

context: Death of Brian Sicknick, aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol
text: Two men are arrested and charged by the United States Department of Justice for assaulting police officer Brian Sicknick during the storming of the United States Capitol.
Portugal's Constitutional Court rejects a bill legalizing assisted suicide for terminally ill patients as unconstitutional.

The United States Senate votes 51–40 to confirm U.S. Rep. Deb Haaland as Secretary of the Interior, thereby making her the first Native American to head the department and the first to be confirmed to a Cabinet post. Haaland is an enrolled member of the Laguna Pueblo.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > 2021 Tillabéri attacks
text: Gunmen in Niger kill at least 58 people after ambushing a convoy returning from a market and then attacking a nearby village.
Protesters storm the Presidential Palace in Aden, Yemen, amidst anger over the lack of services and poor living conditions.
Thousands of residents flee Hlaingthaya Township in western Yangon amidst fears of a massacre by the military after martial law was declared in the industrial suburb.

The Israel Antiquities Authority finds fragments of the Dead Sea Scrolls in the Cave of Horror, believed to be hidden during a Jewish revolt against Rome 1,900 years ago. In addition, a 10,500-year-old weaving basket made of woven flowers is also found.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England, Variants of SARS-CoV-2
text: England reports their first two cases of the new P.3. variant, which was originally detected in the Philippines and has been designated as a "variant of investigation".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania
text: Lithuania suspends the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following three reports of suspected serious adverse thromboembolic reactions among vaccinated people in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia, 501.V2 variant
text: Russia reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant, which was originally detected in South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino
text: San Marino surpasses 5,000 people vaccinated and becomes the fifth country in the world in terms of vaccine administrations in proportion to its population.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia
text: Serbian prime minister Ana Brnabić announces a five-day nationwide lockdown from tomorrow until March 21, which will close all non-essential shops. Students in the lower grades of primary schools will most likely switch to online classes from March 22 for at least one week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Emeritus queen consort Sofía receives the first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: The Public Health Agency of Sweden temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine pending a review from the European Medicines Agency following reports on abnormal blood clotting in vaccinated people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia reports a record 105 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,430.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Gujarat
text: The Gujarat state government decides to extend the curfew timing by two hours to 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. IST in Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot until March 31.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi, 501.V2 variant
text: Delhi reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant, which was originally detected in South Africa. The patient is a 33-year old man from Kerala.
