text: China reports its first confirmed case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a person who travelled to Tianjin from overseas on December 9.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan
text: Pakistan reports its first confirmed case of the Omicron variant in a 57-year-old unvaccinated woman from Karachi.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The Australian state of Queensland reopens its land borders with New South Wales and Victoria to vaccinated domestic travellers.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania > COVID-19 pandemic in Philadelphia
text: Philadelphia imposes a vaccine mandate for indoor activities such as dining, cinemas, and at the Wells Fargo Center for a 76ers or Flyers game.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York state reimposes a mandatory indoor mask mandate for businesses that haven't implemented a vaccination requirement amid threats of the COVID-19 surge and the Omicron variant in winter.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 50 million cases of COVID-19.

Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan of the United Arab Emirates discuss strengthening bilateral trade and cooperation in multiple areas, at the first meeting of the leaders of the two countries.
South Africa cancels a plan to forcibly deport 200,000 Zimbabweans from the country amid an outcry and concerns over perceived xenophobia and human rights abuses.

Eight people are injured as a teenager detonates an improvised explosive device, in an attempt to blow himself up, at a Russian Orthodox school near a convent in Serpukhov, Russia. The perpetrator is identified as a student at the school, and is currently hospitalised in critical condition.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2021 NFL season
text: The National Football League reports their first case of the Omicron variant in a Washington Football Team staffer. Additionally, 36 players tested positive for COVID-19 throughout the NFL.
Two explosions at Camilo Daza International Airport in Cúcuta kill two law enforcement officials and one of the perpetrators.
At least 62 people are killed and more than 100 others injured when a fuel tanker explodes in Cap-Haïtien, Haiti.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia, COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia
text: Indonesia begins administering the COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 6 and 11 years, with 100 children receiving the Sinovac Coronavac vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 94 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 4,387.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The Italian Council of Ministers approves the extension of the COVID-19 state of emergency until March 31 and also rules that travellers from other EU countries must present a negative swab test prior to departure due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: Caretaker Prime Minister Mark Rutte announces that primary schools will be closed on December 20 and that existing restrictions requiring bars, restaurants, and non-essential shops to close at 5 p.m. have been extended until January 14 due to concerns over the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States surpasses 800,000 deaths from COVID-19, remaining the highest death toll in the world.
The final results of a trial of Paxlovid conducted by Pfizer shows 89% cut of risk of hospitalization and death in high-risk patients and is likely to work against the Omicron variant.
A United Nations investigation into the 2021 Colombian protests found that the National Police of Colombia resorted to acts of police brutality that resulted in the massacre of 11 civilians.

context: COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The House of Commons votes to approve "Plan B" measures that include the extension of the indoor mask mandate, vaccine passports, and mandating COVID-19 vaccines for NHS workers in England, despite large opposition from Boris Johnson's own Conservative Party.

context: Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange
text: Australian Deputy Prime Minister and National Party Leader Barnaby Joyce and a small group of Liberal Party backbenchers join the Labor Party in criticising the Liberal-National Coalition Morrison Government's inaction on the United Kingdom's imminent extradition of Australian publisher Julian Assange to the United States, arguing that Assange has not broken any Australian laws.

A court in Minsk, Belarus, sentences opposition activist Sergei Tikhanovsky to 18 years in prison for several charges, including organising riots, following what was widely described as a "sham trial". Tikhanovsky's wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, left Belarus amid the protests that occurred in the country in 2020.
Ugandan politician Bobi Wine is placed under house arrest in Magere, Wakiso District.
Scientists announce that NASA's Parker Solar Probe became the first ever spacecraft to enter the stellar corona of the Sun during a flyby in April.
The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they are in "full control" of the disputed Al Fushqa District after clashing with Ethiopian forces in the border region.
A boat carrying Indonesian migrants capsizes off the southern coast of Malaysia, killing 11 people and leaving 25 others missing.
A privately-owned Gulfstream GIVSP jet crashes near Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic, killing all nine people onboard, including Puerto Rican music producer Flow La Movie.
A fire occurs at the World Trade Centre Hong Kong, injuring 13 people and leaving 300 others trapped within the building.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Mary, Crown Princess of Denmark tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 vaccination in France
text: France begins to require people aged above 65 years to receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster dose or lose their Health Pass validity status unless they show proof of a negative test in the previous 24 hours. The requirement will be extended to all age groups from January 15.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary, COVID-19 vaccination in Hungary
text: Hungary begins administering the COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years using the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia
text: Slovenia reports its first cases of the Omicron variant in four samples from people in the Ljubljana region who tested positive between November 29 and December 6.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England, COVID passports in the United Kingdom
text: The NHS COVID pass begins to be implemented in England as a precondition in order to enter nightclubs, indoor events with more than 500 people, outdoor events with more than 4,000 people, and all events with more than 10,000 people as part of "Plan B" measures that are intended to reduce the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 78,610 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The European Medicines Agency recommends that adults over the age of 18 years who received the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine should get a booster dose two months after receiving their first dose of the vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a 22-year-old woman who travelled from Ghana.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Philippines reports its first two imported cases of the Omicron variant in an overseas Filipino who travelled from Japan on December 1 and a Nigerian national who arrived in the country on November 30.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 7,850 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 536,495.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand > COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand
text: The number of people who are fully vaccinated against COVID-19 in New Zealand surpasses 90%.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Auckland reopens its domestic borders to travellers who are vaccinated or who have tested negative in the previous 72 hours after closing its borders for four months due to an outbreak of the Delta variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Australia reopens its borders to vaccinated skilled migrants and foreign students without an exemption, after a closure of more than 18 months due to the pandemic, despite the worldwide spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya
text: Kenya reports its first three cases of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda
text: Rwanda reports its first six cases of the Omicron variant in a group of travellers and their contacts, prompting the government to close all nightclubs and extend the quarantine for international travellers to three days.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California reimposes its indoor mask mandate due to fears of the spread of the Omicron variant. The mandate will last until at least January 15.
Malta legalizes the personal use and limited cultivation of cannabis, becoming the first country in the European Union to do so.
One person is killed, eleven others are injured and more people are unaccounted for after an arson attack at a four-storey block of flats in Reading, England. A suspect has been arrested.

A court in Hanoi, Vietnam, sentences two Facebook users to lengthy jail sentences for "conducting propaganda against the state". One man was sentenced to 10 years in prison and five years of house arrest while another man was given a six-year prison term and three years of house arrest.
David Fuller, a double murderer who sexually abused the corpses of more than 100 women, is sentenced to a whole life tariff.
Siaosi Sovaleni becomes prime minister-designate of Tonga.

context: Syrian civil war > Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war, Israel's role in the Syrian civil war
text: Israeli warplanes launch overnight airstrikes in southern Syria, with missiles originating from the Golan Heights, killing a soldier and causing some material damage, according to a Syrian military official. Syrian air defences engaged the Israeli missiles, with most missiles reportedly intercepted.

The United Kingdom's Ministry of Defence says a Royal Air Force Typhoon has shot down a "small hostile drone" over Syria. It is the first enemy aircraft shot down by an RAF pilot since the Falklands War.
Gunmen open fire on a car carrying settlers near the outpost of Homesh, in the occupied West Bank, killing one person and wounding two more.

Thousands of people are evacuated from their homes in central and southern Philippines as Typhoon Rai, described as one of the strongest storms of the year, begins to make landfall in mid-eastern parts of the country, with warnings of very destructive typhoon-force winds.
Five children are killed and four others are injured after falling from an inflatable castle that was blown into the air in Devonport, Tasmania, Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in an hospital cleaning employee at the Kemayoran Athletes Village in Jakarta with no overseas travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan, COVID-19 vaccination in Japan
text: Japan officially approves the usage of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine as a booster dose for people over the age of 18 years. This comes after health ministry experts recommended the vaccine yesterday.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: The Malaysian government announces that due to the threat of the Omicron variant, there will be a ban on all large-scale Christmas and New Year's Eve celebrations. The government will also require people over the age of 60 as well as adults who received the Sinovac Coronavac vaccine to receive a booster dose before February in order to maintain their full vaccination status.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: The Palestinian Authority reports its first cases of the Omicron variant in three people from different cities in the West Bank who travelled abroad.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark > COVID-19 drug development
text: The Danish Health Authority approves the usage of the Molnupiravir antiviral pill developed by Merck & Co. for at-risk patients with symptoms, becoming the first EU country to authorize the usage of this drug.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Denmark reports a record 9,999 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany, COVID-19 vaccination in Germany
text: Germany administers a record 1.5 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Italy imposes mandatory COVID-19 testing for all travellers from European Union countries and mandates a five-day quarantine on arrival for those who are unvaccinated due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases and the spread of the Omicron variant in Europe.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
text: Poland reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a 30-year-old Mosotho woman who is currently in isolation in a hospital in the city of Katowice.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record for the second consecutive day of 88,376 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi
text: Malawi announces that public service workers, healthcare workers and journalists will be required to be vaccinated against COVID-19 beginning on December 20 amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 infections.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a fully vaccinated person who travelled from Germany and is currently isolated at a managed isolation quarantine facility in Christchurch.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > History of COVID-19 vaccine development
text: The WHO issues interim recommendations for mixing and matching COVID-19 vaccine for second and booster shot, where mRNA-based vaccines can be used as subsequent doses after initial doses of the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine and vice versa, while these vaccines can be used after initial doses of Sinopharm's inactived vaccine.
Caretaker Prime Minister of the Netherlands Mark Rutte is appointed as formateur and tasked with forming a new coalition government following the conclusion of the 2021 cabinet formation.
Rioters burn down the office of the Kurdish National Council in Dirbêsiyê, Syria, injuring four people.
Israeli settlers burst into several villages in the occupied West Bank, beating and injuring at least two people.
Around 2,500 Karen refugees cross the Myanmar–Thailand border into Thailand.
A Ukrainian soldier is killed and another is injured after pro-Russian separatist forces targeted Ukrainian positions near Mariupol with rocket-propelled grenades and mortars.

The Turkish lira plunges to an all-time low of 17.0705 to the U.S. dollar, triggering a direct central bank intervention in the stock market. The lira has lost 55% of its value this year, including 37% in just the last 30 days. President Recep Erdoğan announces a 50% rise in the minimum wage from next year.
Twelve people are killed as Typhoon Rai impacts the Philippines, causing severe damage.
Eight people are killed and many more are injured by floods in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia
text: Cambodia surpasses 3,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia
text: Mongolia reports no COVID-19 deaths in the past 24 hours for the first time since April 4.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Qatar
text: Qatar reports its first four cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in three fully vaccinated people and an unvaccinated person who all travelled abroad.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Finland
text: The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare reissues a nationwide face mask mandate recommendation in public space and public transport for adults aged 12 years and older due to the rising number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 vaccination in France
text: The French National Consultation Ethical Committee approves the administration of the COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: President of Asturias Adrián Barbón is admitted to hospital when his health condition worsens after testing positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record for the third consecutive day of 93,045 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Australia reports a record 3,837 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, including a record 2,213 cases in New South Wales.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada ends a travel ban on many African nations, including Nigeria and South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt
text: Egypt reports its first three cases of the Omicron variant.

Russia demands that NATO end all military activity in Eastern Europe and never admit Ukraine as a member of the military alliance, saying that it wants a legally binding guarantee to end further eastward NATO expansion. Other demands include a Russian veto on Ukrainian membership in NATO, the removal of U.S. nuclear weapons from Europe, and the withdrawal of multinational NATO battalions from Poland and the Baltics.

A senior Biden regime official says that the U.S. is "prepared to discuss Russia's proposals" with its NATO allies, but says that "there are some things in those documents that the Russians know will be unacceptable."
Twenty-four people are killed and four more are injured during an arson attack at a medical clinic in Osaka, Japan.
Facebook exposes a group of spy firms that could affect the private security of over 50,000 people.

context: Elections in the United Kingdom > 2021 North Shropshire by-election
text: Helen Morgan of the Liberal Democrats wins North Shropshire, a seat in the British House of Commons which the Conservative Party has held since the constituency's creation.
Brazil, Denmark, Latvia, Poland, Slovakia, the United Kingdom and the United States issue a joint condemnation of the worldwide persecution of Jehovah's Witnesses.

EastEnders actress Rose Ayling-Ellis becomes the first deaf person to win the BBC show after she and her professional partner Giovanni Pernice beat the show's first male same-sex couple containing TV chef John Whaite and his professional partner Johannes Radebe in the final.
Fourteen people are killed and several others are injured by a gas explosion in a sewage system in Karachi, Pakistan.
Three workers are killed and three other people are injured when two cranes collapse on a street in Turin, Piedmont, Italy. A residential building is also damaged.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: France imposes a ban on British citizens from entering the country without compelling reasons due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in the United Kingdom. French and EU citizens returning from the UK must self-isolate for seven days unless they show a negative COVID-19 test result on arrival, which will reduce the self-isolation to 48 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal, COVID-19 vaccination in Portugal
text: Portugal begins administering COVID-19 vaccines for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine
text: Ukraine reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a person who travelled from the United Arab Emirates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: The Mayor of London Sadiq Khan declares a "major incident" in effort to ease pressure of hospitals amid a record-breaking COVID-19 cases in the UK caused by the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)
text: New York state reports a record for the second consecutive day of 21,908 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina, COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
text: At midnight, Argentina and Brazil reopen their borders for tourists with a mandatory proof of vaccination or a negative COVID-19 test.
Ukrainian ambassador to Israel Yevhen Korniychuk says that Ukraine might recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.
An armed land dispute between the residents of the Nahualá and Santa Catarina Ixtahuacán municipalities, in Guatemala, results in the death of 12 people.

Former Ukrainian President and oligarch Petro Poroshenko leaves Ukraine on a "pre-planned diplomatic tour" of Turkey and Poland after the National Bureau of Investigation attempts to issue a summons regarding charges of abetting terrorism. The National Bureau of Investigation claims that Poroshenko was involved in looting national resources from the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine.
The death toll in the Philippines from Typhoon Rai increases to 375. At least 500 more people are injured.
The Semeru volcano in Java, Indonesia, erupts for the second time this month, spewing a two-kilometre-high ash column. The first eruption killed at least 46 people on December 4.
A light plane crashes off Australia's east coast of Queensland, killing all four people on board, including two children.

A "tornado-like" severe weather event impacts Sydney's Northern Beaches on Australia's east coast, downing trees and cutting power to thousands of residents. One woman is killed and two women are in a critical condition in Sydney's Royal North Shore Hospital after a "large" pine tree fell in Narrabeen.
A child dies in hospital three days after an inflatable castle was lifted into the air in Devonport, Tasmania, Australia, bringing the death toll from the accident to six.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran
text: Iran reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a person who travelled from the United Arab Emirates.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lanka announces that it will require a proof of COVID-19 vaccination certificate for entry into public places beginning on January 1 in an attempt to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
text: The Netherlands imposes strict lockdown measures that restrict visitors to two people, closes all non-essential shops, bars, and restaurants until January 14, and closes schools until January 9, due to an increase in COVID-19 cases caused by the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland introduces an 8:00 p.m. closure time for bars and restaurants, restricts the capacity of most indoor and outdoor events to 50%, and allows a maximum of 100 guests for weddings in order to reduce the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru
text: Peru reports its first four cases of the Omicron variant in one person who travelled from South Africa and another three who had no travel history.
Chileans go to the polls to elect their president in a run-off between leftist Gabriel Boric and right-wing candidate José Antonio Kast.
With over 50% of votes counted, Boric is declared the winner as Kast publishes a tweet conceding defeat.

Tens of thousands of protesters demonstrate against the October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état, leading to government forces spraying protesters with tear gas in an attempt to halt the demonstrations, one of the largest in Sudan's history.
A man in India is beaten to death by guards at the Golden Temple, the holiest place in the world according to the Sikh religion. Authorities allege he may have tried to harm the Guru Granth Sahib.

context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency > 2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks, 2021 Uganda bombings
text: The governments of Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo reveal that they have captured 35 rebels and destroyed numerous enemy strongholds within the past week.
The Israeli Defense Forces report that they have arrested more than 100 members of the Palestinian Islamist organization Hamas, amid a recent increase in tensions.
Three members of the Islamic State are killed in Faqeerabad, Peshawar, during an operation by the Pakistani police.
An investigation by the BBC discovers that a massacre of 40 civilians took place in July, in Kani Township, a People's Defence Force stronghold in Sagaing Region.
The death toll from the fuel tank truck explosion in Cap-Haïtien, Haiti, six days ago rises to 90.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand > COVID-19 vaccination in Thailand
text: Thailand's Food and Drug Administration approves the usage of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reports its first locally transmitted case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a 49-year-old woman.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India, COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: It is announced that more than 85% of eligible Indians have been partially vaccinated, and that over 55% have received both doses.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel's government agrees to ban all travel to Germany, Italy, Belgium, Hungary, Morocco, Portugal, Canada, Switzerland, Turkey, and the U.S. without special permission beginning on December 22 due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait
text: Kuwait will require incoming travellers who fully vaccinated against COVID-19 more than nine months ago to receive booster dose beginning from January 2 and also requires them to self-isolate for 10 days unless they received a negative PCR test within 72 hours of their arrival beginning from December 26.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 vaccination in France
text: The French approves the usage of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Germany bans all travel from the United Kingdom and imposes a mandatory 14-day quarantine and proof of a negative PCR test from the previous 48 hours for German residents and citizens returning from the UK, amid the spread of the Omicron variant in Britain.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom ends its travel ban on Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The European Commission authorizes the use of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine after the European Medicines Agency recommended the use of the vaccine, becoming the fifth vaccine to be approved for use by the European Union.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec
text: Quebec closes all bars, gyms, spas, cinemas, and concert halls as well as suspends in-person learning and mandates remote working after the province reported a record 4,857 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Texas
text: The United States reports its first confirmed death related to the Omicron variant in an unvaccinated man in his 50s in Harris County, Texas who had underlying health issues.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Costa Rica
text: Costa Rica reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in an eight-year-old boy who recently travelled from the United States along with his family.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Panama
text: Panama reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a 50-year-old person who recently travelled from South Africa.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina, COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia
text: Argentina donates 1 million doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine to Bolivia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia
text: Colombia reports its first case of the Omicron variant in two Colombia people who travelled from the United States and a U.S. citizen who travelled from Spain.

Poland and Lithuania join Ukraine in calling for stronger Western sanctions on Russia, with Polish President Andrzej Duda saying that "everything must be done" to prevent a potential Russian invasion of Ukraine, and that he was "absolutely against any policy of concessions to Russia".
Pentagon Press Secretary John Kirby says a small Department of Defense team has returned from Ukraine after assessing the country's air defences.
The trial of Aung San Suu Kyi is delayed by Burmese courts until December 27.
Egyptian blogger and activist Alaa Abdel Fattah is sentenced to five years in prison by Egyptian authorities for spreading fake news. His family continues to protest the verdict.

The Nagaland Legislative Assembly publicly demands that the Government of India repeal the Armed Forces Special Powers Act, which has been in effect since 1958. This comes after a massacre occurred in Mon district, Nagaland on December 4.

context: Yemeni Civil War > Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen
text: The Saudi-led coalition launches airstrikes on Sanaa International Airport in the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The air raid targeted six sites, including places used for "launching drone attacks", according to a statement from the coalition.

The French Army announces that they have killed Soumana Boura, a leading member of the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara, the previous day. Boura was involved in the killings of six French aid workers and their two Nigerien guides in a mass shooting in August 2020 in Kouré, Niger.
The Tigray Defense Forces withdraws all its troops from the Afar and Amhara regions of Ethiopia.
Heavy floods continue to affect eight Malaysian states for the third day, killing 14 people and partially submerging several towns and villages.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany > COVID-19 vaccination in Germany
text: The Standing Committee on Vaccination recommends the shortening of the interval between the second dose and booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine to three months and urges all citizens over the age of 18 to receive a booster dose of an mRNA-based vaccine after receiving their first two doses in order to reduce the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: German Chancellor Olaf Scholz and 16 state premiers agree to tighten the restrictions beginning on December 28, including limiting the number of people in private gatherings to 10 and banning spectators at large-scale musical, sporting and cultural events due to concerns related to the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain > COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid
text: The Community of Madrid reports a record 11,221 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Prime Minister António Costa announces that nightclubs and bars will be closed and all people will work from home for at least two weeks beginning on December 25 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. There will also be capacity restrictions at shops and people will require a negative COVID-19 test in order to enter events.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden
text: The Swedish government announces that several new measures will begin on December 23, including limiting the number of people at private gatherings to 50, requiring the use of a vaccination pass for public events with a capacity of more than 500 people, and recommending work from home where possible, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The European Commission announces a binding proposal that will make the EU Digital COVID Certificate only valid for travel within the European Union for nine months without a booster dose after a person's primary vaccination schedule in order to standardize different travel requirements in the member states. The new rules will be mandatory for all 27 EU member states beginning on February 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel > COVID-19 vaccination in Israel
text: The Health ministry recommends that Israelis over the age of 60 years and healthcare workers should receive a fourth dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, becoming the world's first country to administer a fourth dose of the vaccine. The move is welcomed by Prime Minister Naftali Bennett.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: Israel reports its first confirmed death related to the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a man in his 60s with pre-existing health conditions who died at the Soroka Medical Center in Beersheba. The hospital later states that the death was actually because of the Delta variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines
text: The Philippine Food and Drug Administration reduces the interval of the COVID-19 vaccine booster dose to three months for people who received a two-dose vaccine and two months for people who received a single-dose vaccine in order to reduce the effects of variants.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reinstates its mandatory hotel quarantine for all incoming foreign travellers and suspends the "sandbox" program for places other than Phuket after the country reported its first locally transmitted case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina > COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina
text: The provinces of Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Santa Fe, Río Negro and Santiago del Estero begin implementing the usage of a "sanitary pass" for large events.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina
text: Argentina reports 9,336 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the highest daily total in 4 months, thereby bringing the nationwide total of cases to 5.4 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand postpones a phased reopening of the border for quarantine-free travel to the end of February in order to strengthen the country's defence against the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 vaccination in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California Governor Gavin Newsom announces that healthcare workers will be required to receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster dose in order to keep their "fully vaccinated" status, becoming the second state to impose such mandate.

context: Lithuania–United States relations, Second Cold War
text: The U.S. State Department approves the sale of 341 FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank guided missiles and 30 command launch units to NATO ally Lithuania amid rising tensions with Russia.

Three inmates in Japan are executed by hanging, marking the first executions in the country in nearly two years. One inmate was the perpetrator of a 2004 mass stabbing in which he killed seven of his relatives.
Two soldiers and four civilians are killed in clashes between the Kurdish SDF and the Turkish-backed SNA in Tell Tamer.
The University of Hong Kong removes the Pillar of Shame overnight, a monument dedicated to the victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre in China.

context: Jade trade in Myanmar > 2021 Hpakant jade mine disaster
text: Dozens of people are missing following a landslide at a jade mine in Hpakant, Kachin State.
At least 64 people are confirmed dead following a boat accident off the coast of Antseraka, Analanjirofo, Madagascar, on Monday, with 24 others still missing.

Madagascar's police minister Serge Gellé is rescued after swimming for 12 hours to shore after his helicopter crashed off the country's northern coast during the boat accident rescue operation. President Andry Rajoelina hails Gellé's survival.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland
text: Northern Ireland reports a record 3,231 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Wales
text: First minister Mark Drakeford announces new restrictions, including limiting the number of people in events to 50 people outdoors and 30 people indoors, no more than six people in a group at bars, restaurants, and cinemas, and imposing a face mask mandate due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. These measures will be in effect beginning on December 26.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 106,122 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the first time that the country has reported more than 100,000 new cases in a single day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: The government announces a series of new restrictions, including closing restaurants at 10 p.m. beginning on December 27, discourage large-scale New Year's Eve celebrations, capacity restrictions of indoor and outdoor events, and imposing strict entry requirements for travellers from the UK, Denmark, Norway, and the Netherlands where the Omicron variant is already dominant in an effort to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and its variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium
text: Prime Minister Alexander De Croo announces that, due to the spread of the Omicron variant, water parks, cinemas, theatres and concert halls will be closed, and all indoor events and outdoor events using a tent will be banned. Additionally, shopping will only be allowed in pairs and professional and amateur sport events will be held without spectators. These measures will begin on December 26.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey, COVID-19 vaccination in Turkey
text: The Health ministry approves the emergency use of the country's first homegrown COVID-19 vaccine named Turkovac.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia closes all bars, nightclubs, gyms, fitness centres, and dance studios, and bans all indoor gatherings due to the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Jamaica
text: Jamaica reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a person who travelled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Food and Drug Administration grants emergency use authorization for Pfizer's antiviral COVID-19 oral pill named Paxlovid for at-risk people over the age of 12 years, becoming the first at-home oral treatment to be approved by the FDA.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria
text: Nigeria destroys 1,066,214 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine with short shelf lives that expired in November.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Africa > COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia
text: Tunisia begins to implement the usage of a mandatory COVID-19 vaccination pass in order to enter cafés, state institutions, banks, and shopping centres despite popular opposition and criticism from Amnesty International.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel
text: The Soroka Medical Center in Beersheba clarifies that the man thought to be Israel's first Omicron death had actually had the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant, following the final laboratory results regarding his condition.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports its first locally transmitted cases of the Omicron variant in three people from Osaka Prefecture with no international travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia, COVID-19 vaccination in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in Western Australia
text: Western Australia will become the first state and territory to mandate a booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine for essential, mining, and healthcare workers, due to the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: Venezuela reports its first seven cases of the Omicron variant in a group of people who had travelled from another country, such as Spain, Dominican Republic, Panama, and Turkey.

context: Animal welfare and rights in Australia
text: A landowner and an earthmoving business each face 126 charges for the deaths of 70 koalas last year at a partially cleared tree plantation in Cape Bridgewater, Victoria, Australia.

context: Animal welfare and rights in Italy
text: Italy bans fur farming and orders all remaining mink farms to shut down by June 2022, while a ban on breeding animals for their fur becomes effective immediately.
Gunmen ambush a column of a civilian militia in Loroum, Burkina Faso, killing 41 people. It is one of the deadliest single-day attack against the militia.
Twenty-four more people are found dead after the boat accident off the coast of Analanjirofo, Madagascar, three days ago, bringing the total death toll to 85.
Eleven people are dead as a boat carrying migrants sinks in the Aegean Sea. Around 90 other people are rescued.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei
text: Brunei reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a person who travelled from the United Kingdom.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait
text: The Kuwaiti Directorate General of Civil Aviation announces that all citizens who wish to travel, but who were fully vaccinated more than nine months ago, must receive a booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine beginning on January 2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, COVID-19 drug development, COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines
text: The Philippine Food and Drug Administration approves the emergency use of the Molnupiravir drug made by Merck & Co. for high-risk adult patients and also approves the use of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Singapore suspends new ticket sales for the quarantine-free Vaccinated Travel Lane until January 20 in an attempt to reduce the number of imported cases of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 109 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 5,015.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra
text: Prime Minister Xavier Espot tests positive for COVID-19 with mild symptoms.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a record 91,608 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set in November 2020.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Germany reports its first confirmed death related to the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: The Italian government announces a ban of New Year's Eve celebrations as well as all mass gatherings and closes nightclubs and bars until the end of January. The government also agree to reintroduce mandatory mask wearing outdoors and will reduce the validity of vaccine certificate to six months beginning from February 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: Malta reports its first two cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant, prompting the health ministry to ban all standing events except for weddings and funerals beginning on December 17 and restrict entry to the hospitality sector and sporting events to only those with a valid vaccine certificate. A 1 a.m. curfew will also be imposed for all businesses beginning on January 17.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: Russia surpasses 600,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record for the second consecutive day of 119,789 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Preliminary data from the United Kingdom suggests the hospitalization rate of the COVID-19 Omicron variant is between 50% to 70% lower than the Delta variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras
text: Honduras begins administering a booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine for all adults aged above 18 years using the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Food and Drug Administration grants emergency use authorization for Merck & Co.'s antiviral COVID-19 oral pill named Molnupiravir for at-risk individuuals.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina, COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina
text: Argentina receives more than 2.6 million doses of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine for use as booster doses.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South America > COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador, COVID-19 vaccination in Ecuador
text: Ecuador's Minister of Public Health announces that the COVID-19 vaccination will be mandatory for all citizens over the age of 5 years unless they have a medical exemption due to the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants and an increase in the number of new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: New South Wales reports a record 5,715 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant becoming the dominant strain in the state. The NSW Government reintroduces mask-wearing in indoor settings, despite the state having a 93.5% vaccination rate.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: Australia reports a record 8,697 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set on December 22.

President Joe Biden signs the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act into law banning imports from China's Xinjiang region citing concerns about the use of forced labour. China denies human rights abuses in Xinjiang.

context: Japan–United States relations, Taiwan–United States relations
text: The United States and Japan approve a plan for a joint military operation in response to a possible "Taiwan emergency". The operation would consist of deploying U.S. Marines on the Ryukyu Islands near Taiwan, while the Japan Self-Defense Forces would provide logistical support such as ammunition and fuel supplies.

context: 14-Year-Old Valentina Orellana-Peralta killed in LAPD response
text: While responding to multiple reports of a violent assault suspect at a Los Angeles clothing store, LAPD officers fired upon one male subject. Valentina Orellana-Peralta was sheltering with her mother and other patrons and was killed by an errant shot. Valentina and the suspect both succumbed to their injuries in the store. Several patrons were injured by the suspect prior to officers' arrival.
Former Minneapolis police officer Kim Potter is found guilty on both counts in the killing of Daunte Wright. She is scheduled to be sentenced on February 18, 2022.

context: Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania
text: The Seimas votes 89–17 with 19 abstentions to approve a law that would require MPs to have a health pass, which shows proof of vaccination, a negative test result from the previous 72 hours, or that a person has recovered from COVID-19, in order to attend hearings beginning in January.

The Australian Government pays a A$2,000,000 settlement to the Shire of Ngaanyatjarraku to end a class action lawsuit in the Federal Court over the controversial Community Development Program, which saw unemployed Ngaanyatjarra and other Indigenous Australian people in remote communities working up to 25 hours a week otherwise unpaid in order to receive the JobSeeker payment, which is generally considered to be less than the cost of living and which is provided to other Australians in exchange for completing a fortnightly quota of job applications. The Ngaanyatjarra accused the program of being racist and a form of modern slavery.

context: Yemeni Civil War > Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
text: The Houthis launch a missile strike on the Saudi Arabian city of Jizan, killing two people and injuring seven more.

context: Yemeni Civil War > Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
text: Three people are killed and six others are injured during coalition air raids in Ajama, Yemen.

Russian president Vladimir Putin demands that NATO guarantee that it will not move its forces into Ukraine, accusing NATO and the U.S. of "trying to send Ukraine and Russia into direct armed conflict."

After five days of military training, Iran fires sixteen ballistic missiles at a target in a show of force against Israel. The incident is part of a wider increase in tensions between the two countries.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb; 2021 Niger attacks
text: Jihadists kill six soldiers in Niger, resulting in the ensuing deaths of twenty-two of the attackers.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Africa
text: The United Nations Economic Commission for Africa warns that the effects of the pandemic on Africa's economy could push the number of "extremely poor" Africans to 514 million people. The World Bank also announced a recession as the economies of African countries continue to shrink.
At least 39 people are killed and 100 others are injured after a ferry catches fire in Jhalakathi.
Sixteen people are dead as a boat carrying migrants overturn and sink near the island of Paros, Greece. Sixty-three more people are rescued.
A surfer is killed an apparent shark attack in Morro Bay, off the coast of California, United States. It is the first fatal shark attack in the area since 2003.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France > COVID-19 vaccination in France
text: The French recommends that booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine can be administered as soon as three months after the primary vaccination schedule due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a record for the second consecutive day of 94,122 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece cancels all public Christmas and New Year's Eve celebrations, as well as mandates mask wearing outdoors and requiring people to wear two masks or a high-protection mask in order to use public transport and enter supermarkets due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports a record for the second consecutive day of 50,599 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5.57 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Catalonia reimposes a curfew between 1 a.m. and 6 a.m. in municipalities where the infection rate surpasses 250 cases per 100,000 inhabitants, limits the number of people in social gatherings to 10, closes nightclubs, and restricts the capacity of the hospitality sector due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. These measures will be in effect until at least January 7.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record for the third consecutive day of 122,186 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bhutan, COVID-19 vaccination in Bhutan
text: Bhutan begins administering booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine for people over the age of 65 years, overseas travellers, healthcare workers, people with underlying health conditions, and adults living in high risk areas.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: Singapore reports no deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours for the first time since September 19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reports its first domestic cluster of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in 21 people from Kalasin province. The outbreak originated in a couple who travelled from Belgium earlier this month.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Ecumenical Patriarch of the Eastern Orthodox Church Bartholomew I of Constantinople tests positive for COVID-19 and is showing mild symptoms.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: The South African Health Department suspends COVID-19 contact tracing and quarantine for people with asymptomatic cases due to 80% of the population being vaccinated or recovered from COVID-19.
Former South Korean president Park Geun-hye is pardoned by the South Korean Justice Ministry.
Former Gambian President Yahya Jammeh is accused of numerous different crimes, including rape, torture, mass murder, and killing journalists by the Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission.
Hong Kong authorities remove the Hong Kong Goddess of Democracy from the Chinese University of Hong Kong campus and a memorial to the Tiananmen Square massacre from Lingnan University campus.
Japan decides not to send government delegates to the 2022 Winter Olympics, although the Japanese team will still be present.

context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency; 2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: A suicide bomber blows himself up at a restaurant during Christmas celebrations in Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing five people and injuring 13 others.
Human rights groups and media outlets uncover a massacre of 30 civilians in Hpruso, Kayah State, that occurred the day before. Two Save the Children staff are also reported missing.
The global version of video game digital distribution service Steam is reportedly blocked in China. The China-only version of the service, launched in February of this year, remains accessible.

The scientific committee (Pevolca) of the Canary Islands government declares that the Cumbre Vieja volcano's eruptions on La Palma island stopped after 10 days of inactivity. However, the authorities do not consider the emergency situation to be over.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia > COVID-19 pandemic in Sarawak
text: Malaysia reports its first locally transmitted case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a fully vaccinated 38-year-old Chinese woman from Sarawak with no international travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India, COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: The Drug Controller General of India approves the emergency use of the Covaxin vaccine manufactured by Bharat Biotech for children between the ages of 12 and 18 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Israeli government finalizes an agreement with Pfizer to purchase 100,000 courses of the anti-viral drug Paxlovid for high-risk patients over the age of 12 years, with delivery expected to begin in one week.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkmenistan
text: Turkmenistan becomes one of the first countries to approve the usage of the single-dose Sputnik Light COVID-19 vaccine. The health ministry also purchases 600,000 doses of the two-dose Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a record for the third consecutive day of 104,611 new cases of COVID-19, which is also the first time that the country has reported more than 100,000 new cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports a record for the third consecutive day of 54,762 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5.62 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: Ireland reports a record for the second consecutive day of 13,765 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: New South Wales reports a record 6,288 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Republic reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: James Webb Space Telescope, Ariane flight VA256
text: The James Webb Space Telescope is successfully launched using the Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, French Guiana.
Asa Coast Railway announces a dual-mode vehicle that can operate on roads and railways.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps releases a video on social media threatening to destroy the Israeli city of Dimona and a nearby nuclear facility in the Negev desert.

A massive Roman castrum dated to the reign of Caligula is discovered in Velsen, Netherlands. The site is the most northern fort found by archaeologists, and believed to be a stationing port of Caligula’s failed invasion of Britain.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China reports 206 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases in 21 months, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 101,077.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Iran, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Iran bans all travellers from the United Kingdom, France, Denmark and Norway for 15 days and indefinitely suspends all land travel to Turkey due to the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Oman, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Oman's Supreme Committee announces that all incoming expatriates over the age of 18 years who want to enter the country must show proof of at least two doses of the COVID-19 vaccine as well as a negative PCR test from the previous 72 hours. They also announce that the ban on travelers from South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, and Mozambique will be lifted.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine
text: The Gaza Strip reports its first locally transmitted case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland
text: Northern Ireland imposes tightened COVID-19-related restrictions, which include closing nightclubs and banning indoor seating at events, restricting socialization to three households, and reintroducing the rule of six at bars, restaurants, and pubs that only offer table service.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo
text: Kosovo reports its first cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in two people who travelled from the United States, a person who travelled from France, two people who travelled from the United Kingdom, and four people with no international travel history.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: New South Wales reports a record for the second consecutive day of 6,394 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Australia
text: South Australia reports a record 744 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the statewide total of confirmed cases to 4,324.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria
text: Algeria begins to implement vaccine passports as a precondition for people to enter or leave the country and also for people to enter a wide range of public venues such as sports facilities, theatres and museums as part of an attempt to increase the country's low COVID-19 vaccination rate.

Kodiak, Alaska sets the highest temperature ever recorded in December in the state of Alaska, reaching . The Aleutian Islands and island communities in West Alaska have seen abnormally high temperatures since mid-December, including eight straight days of over in Unalaska, including on Christmas Day, the warmest Christmas temperature on record for the state. Temperature anomalies for late December reach in some areas. The state also lately experiences unusually wet spells of weather.
The Taliban regime dissolves Afghanistan's Independent Election Commission, saying that "there is no need for these commissions to exist and operate".
Flooding in the Bahia state of Northeast Brazil kills 18 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Kerala
text: The Indian state of Kerala imposes a nighttime curfew from December 30 to January 2 in order to reduce the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 vaccination in Israel
text: The Sheba Medical Center near Tel Aviv, Israel, begins the world's first clinical trial of fourth doses of the COVID-19 vaccine, involving 150 medical personnel, in order to determine if a fourth dose can provide extra immunity against COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, COVID-19 vaccination in Israel
text: The health ministry reduces the interval between the second dose and booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine to three months, citing concerns about the spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea, COVID-19 drug development
text: South Korea authorizes the emergency use of the anti-viral oral drug Paxlovid manufactured by Pfizer for high-risk patients over the age of 12 years, becoming the first drug to be approved for use in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates
text: The Ministry of Health and Prevention approves the emergency use of Sinopharm's new recombinant protein vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland > COVID-19 drug development
text: Swissmedic approves the use of the monoclonal antibody cocktail Ronapreve developed by Roche and Regeneron to treat severe COVID-19 patients.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland > COVID-19 vaccination in Switzerland
text: Swissmedic approves the use of the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine as a booster dose for people over the age of 18 years, which can be administered two months after the first dose, or six months after a person receives mixed vaccinations with mRNA-based vaccines.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: French prime minister Jean Castex announces that, for the next three weeks, all public gatherings will be limited to 2,000 people indoors and 5,000 people outdoors. Work from home will be mandated where possible, and outdoor mask wearing will be mandatory in city centres. The interval between the second dose and the booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine will also be reduced to three months in response to the rapid spread of the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: The Greek government announces new restrictions that will be in effect from January 3 until at least January 16, which include mandatory high-protection or double mask wearing in supermarkets and on public transport, closure of entertainment and hospitality venues at midnight, reinstating work from home policies for up to 50% of employees, and reducing the capacity of sports stadiums to 10%. This comes after the country reported a record 9,284 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland
text: Iceland reports a record 672 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: New South Wales reports Australia's first confirmed death from the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a fully vaccinated man in his 80s who had experienced breakthrough infections and also had underlying health conditions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales
text: Sydney's St. Vincent's Hospital incorrectly issues premature negative COVID-19 test results to 1,395 people who had actually tested positive in the past 48 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Australia
text: South Australia reports a record 842 new cases in the past 24 hours. The state also reports their first death from COVID-19 since April 2020 in a 92-year-old woman.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Canada surpasses two million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Paraguay
text: Paraguay reports its first cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in three people who travelled outside the country earlier this month.

A bird flu outbreak in northern Israel kills at least 5,200 migratory cranes and forces farmers to slaughter hundreds of thousands of chickens in what authorities say is the deadliest wildlife disaster in the nation's history.

context: Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Syrian state media reports that Israel has bombed the Port of Latakia. If this is confirmed by the IDF, it would be the second airstrike on the facility this month. Secondary explosions are believed to be from Iranian munitions stored at the facility.

context: Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Massive damage at the port is reported from the air raid with most of the port on fire, although there are no immediate reports of casualties from the attack. Videos on social media show multiple large explosions and anti-aircraft fire over the city. A hospital, shops, and some residential buildings were also badly damaged.
At least 38 people are killed in the collapse of a private gold mine in En Nahud, Sudan.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi enters Level 1 "Yellow alert" which closes cinemas, schools, colleges, and gyms, imposes a nighttime curfew from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., and restricts the capacity of public transport, restaurants, funerals and weddings, due to an increase in the number of Omicron variant cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare issues emergency use authorizations for the Covovax vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India and the Corbevax vaccine. The ministry also issues an emergency use authorization for Merck & Co.'s anti-viral drug Molnupiravir.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh, COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh
text: Bangladesh begins administering booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine for people over the age of 60 and frontline workers who have been fully vaccinated more than six months ago as the country attempts to reduce the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China issues stay-at home orders for hundreds of thousands of people in Yan'an due to the spread of COVID-19 cases, which also resulted in a lockdown in Xi'an, the country's largest lockdown since last year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a person who travelled from the United Kingdom on December 19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus
text: Cyprus reports a record for the second consecutive day of 2,241 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 154,926.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a record 179,807 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports a record for the second consecutive day of 21,657 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,105,885.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy reports a record 78,313 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal
text: Portugal reports a record 17,172 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,303,291.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record 138,831 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario
text: Ontario reports 8,825 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases since March 2020 to 715,405.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: California becomes the first U.S. state and the world's first subnational entity to surpass five million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The United States reports a record 512,553 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The seven day average of child hospitalizations reaches a record level, with 378 children under 18 admitted each day. ([https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/us-children-hospitalized-covid-record-numbers-82004052 ABC)]

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa
text: South Africa postpones a plan to end COVID-19 contact tracing and suspend some quarantine measures in order to consider additional comments about the policy after the government received many inquiries about the plan.

Russian police arrest two allies of opposition politician and activist Alexei Navalny, Kseniya Fadeyeva and Zakhar Sarapulov, under extremism charges. Leonid Volkov, another ally of Navalny, had tried to persuade Fadeyeva and Sarapulov to leave Russia as he and others have done, but they refused.
The Supreme Court of Russia orders the liquidation of human rights group Memorial for violating the Russian foreign agent law.
Social Democratic Union of Macedonia leader Dimitar Kovačevski is confirmed as North Macedonia's Prime Minister-designate following the resignation of Zoran Zaev.

Troops loyal to Prime Minister Mohamed Hussein Roble gather outside the presidential palace in the capital Mogadishu after President Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed tried to suspend the Prime Minister in what has been described as an attempted self-coup.

A night curfew is imposed in North Darfur, Sudan, after armed groups looted and burned a United Nations World Food Programme warehouse and UNAMID facilities in Al-Fashir, stealing around 1,900 tonnes of food.
Three people are killed and four others are injured in a fire at a candlelit vigil in Kosiv, Ukraine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France
text: France reports a record for the second consecutive day of 208,099 new cases of COVID-19, which is also the highest daily total recorded in any European nation since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: Greece reports a record for the third consecutive day of 28,828 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,134,713.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Despite the number of new cases caused by the Omicron variant reaching a record 98,030 cases, Italy completely lifts the mandatory quarantine for those who received COVID-19 vaccine booster shot and reduces it to five days for the vaccinated people whose most recent dose was more than 120 days before exposure.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Malta
text: Malta reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,337 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 49,625.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Despite the number of cases caused by the Omicron variant reaching a record high, Spain reduces the isolation period for people who test positive for COVID-19 and the mandatory quarantine for people who had close contact with someone who tested positive to seven days due to staffing shortages and disruptions in some industries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain reports for the first time more than 100,000 cases of COVID-19 in one day.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports a record for the second consecutive day of 183,037 new cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
