text: Kuwait lifts many of its COVID-19-related restrictions, including allowing foreign travel for unvaccinated and vaccinated citizens and allowing the entry of unvaccinated people into shopping malls as long as they show a negative PCR COVID-19 test from the previous 72 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore, COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore
text: The Singaporean Health Sciences Authority grants interim authorisation for the use of the protein-based Novavax COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden, COVID-19 vaccination in Sweden
text: The Public Health Agency of Sweden recommends that people over the age of 80 years, residents of nursing homes, and people receiving at-home care should receive a fourth dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall, tests positive for COVID-19.
The United States suspends all imports of Mexican avocados after threats are made against an American plant safety inspector in Uruapan, Michoacán.

The flag of Mauritius is raised on the British-controlled Chagos Archipelago in the Indian Ocean for the first time in history. Mauritian Prime Minister Pravind Jugnauth describes the event as a "historic moment", saying that it was time for the United Kingdom to cede control of the archipelago.

The government of Canada invokes the Emergencies Act for the first time since the law was passed in 1988, thereby giving the federal government temporary powers to deal with ongoing blockades associated with the protests.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Chrystia Freeland announces that, as part of the invoking of the Act, crowdfunding platforms such as GoFundMe and GiveSendGo must immediately register with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and authorizes banks to freeze accounts suspected to be involved in the blockades.
The United States Department of Justice asks Honduras for the arrest and extradition of former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández, who left office less than a month ago.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Vladimir Putin claims that a "genocide" is occurring in Eastern Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The State Duma of Russia passes a bill to officially recognise the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic in Eastern Ukraine as independent states. The bill has been sent to President Vladimir Putin for final approval.
Russian President Vladimir Putin says that diplomatic talks will continue. Russia also announces that troops will be partially pulled out from the border but that exercises will continue.
Several Ukrainian websites, including the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine, Privatbank, and Oschadbank are affected by cyberattacks.
The U.S. and its NATO allies in Europe say that they are ready to retaliate against Russian cyberwarfare on Ukraine depending on the severity of the attacks.
The Luhansk People's Republic says that a service member has been killed on the frontline by a Ukrainian military sniper, according to its office at the Joint Centre of Control and Coordination.

An attempted terrorist attack on a memorial rally in the city of Luhansk is reportedly stopped. Russian media blames the Ukrainian Defence Ministry and "special services" of being involved in the attack. A video shows an improvised explosive device being discovered inside a garbage can.

context: Capsizing of the Villa de Pitanxo
text: A Spanish-owned fishing trawler, Villa de Pitanxo, sinks off the coast of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, killing 10 crew members and leaving 11 others missing. A search and rescue operation is underway.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 57,049 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4.9 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 236 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, the number of cumulative COVID-19 cases surpasses four million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 57,177 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.46 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam
text: Vietnam lifts its COVID-19-related curbs on international passenger flights with no limitation on the number of flights in order to restore the travel to pre-pandemic level.

context: Canada convoy protest > 2022 alleged plot to kill Coutts RCMP officers
text: Four men are arrested on suspicion of plotting to murder officers with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. The arrests occurred during a protest blockading the Canada–U.S. border near Coutts, Alberta.

A number of protestors at Coutts have dispersed after an RCMP raid on a "smaller group within the larger protest" resulted in the seizure of weapons, ammunition, and body armour and the arrests of 13 people on Monday.
Chief of police of the Ottawa Police Service Peter Sloly resigns amid criticism of his handling of the protests.
Families of nine victims of the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting reach a $73 million settlement with Remington Arms, according to their attorney, Josh Koskoff.
Former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández is arrested in Tegucigalpa after the U.S. requested his extradition on charges of drug trafficking.

context: 2022 United States elections > 2022 Louisville mayoral election
text: In Louisville, Kentucky, council candidate Quintez Brown is charged with attempted murder, a day after he allegedly opened fire on mayoral candidate Craig Greenberg in his campaign office, narrowly missing him.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli–Syrian ceasefire line incidents during the Syrian civil war
text: Syrian state media agency SANA reports that Israel has fired missiles at the Syrian town of Zakiyah, with no recorded casualties.
Cristina Calderón, the last full-blooded Yahgan and last native speaker of the Yahgan language, dies in Chile.

context: 2022 Brazil floods and landslides > 2022 Petrópolis floods
text: At least 117 people are killed by mudslides and flooding in Petrópolis, Rio de Janeiro. It is the heaviest rainfall registered in the city since 1932.

context: List of fatal shark attacks in Australia
text: A man is killed in a shark attack off Little Bay, Sydney, Australia. It is the first fatal shark attack in Sydney since 1963. A witness estimated that the shark was about in length.
At least 13 people are killed after wedding guests fall into a well in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record for the second consecutive day of 64,718 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4.96 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 27,831 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.11 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 90,443 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.55 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland
text: Switzerland lifts almost all of its COVID-19-related restrictions, with people no longer needing to show COVID-19 vaccine certificates to enter public venues, due to confidence that infection rates had been uncoupled from hospitalization.

The European Court of Justice dismisses Poland and Hungary's challenges against the regulation and confirms that the regulation is in compliance with the treaties of the European Union. This will allow the European Commission to suspend funds from the EU budget to member states that have rule of law issues which are likely to affect the management of EU funds.

The Alaska Aces, the second most successful team in the history of the league with 14 championship titles in 35 years, announced that it will cease to exist after the conclusion of the ongoing 2021 PBA Governors' Cup.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The Ukrainian government accuses Russian separatists of shelling a kindergarten in Stanytsia Luhanska, Luhansk Oblast using artillery, injuring three civilians. The Luhansk People's Republic says that its forces were attacked by the Ukrainian military with mortars, grenade launchers and machine gun fire. At least 32 shells hit the city, causing power outages and damaging multiple structures.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The United Nations Security Council convenes in order to discuss Russia's military buildup on the Ukrainian border.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The U.S. State Department confirms that the U.S. deputy ambassador to Russia was expelled from the country. White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Karine Jean-Pierre calls the expulsion "unprovoked".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Josep Borrell says that shelling has begun in eastern Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Senior British officials say that Russian President Vladimir Putin has now decided to invade Ukraine following "changes in the last 24 hours".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Germany deploys 130 troops and 60 armoured personnel carriers to Lithuania. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda says that the German forces are authorized to defend the country from threats. More troops are expected to arrive later this week.

France and the EU-wide Takuba Task Force announce that they will begin withdrawing from Mali, stating that the military government in place since last year's coup has placed "multiple obstructions" to their counter-terrorism operations.

Panama-flagged car carrier MV Felicity Ace is abandoned approximately 90 nautical miles southwest of the Azores following a severe fire onboard. The ship's entire 22-man crew safely evacuates using lifeboats.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia
text: British Columbia lifts most of its COVID-19 restrictions, allowing all businesses to reopen and operate at full capacity. Indoor gatherings and organized events are also permitted to operate without occupancy limits. However, provincial mandates requiring the use of vaccine cards for entry into businesses and the use of masks in indoor settings remain in effect.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California
text: Governor Gavin Newsom announces that California will become the first U.S. state to approach COVID-19 as an endemic rather than a pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic
text: The Dominican Republic ends all COVID-19-related public health measures, including mask wearing mandates and use of vaccine passes in order to enter public places, despite not reaching 70% of its vaccination target.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia surpasses 5 million cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Japan reports a record 269 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand reports a record 1,929 new community transmitted COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland
text: Swiss President Ignazio Cassis tests positive for COVID-19.
Tamara Lich and Chris Barber, two organizers of the protest in Ottawa, are arrested by police.

Australia designates the entirety of Hamas, including its political wing, as a terrorist organisation, and also designates Atomwaffen Division, Tahrir al-Sham and the Guardians of Religion Organization as terrorist organisations.

The Kuwaiti Ministers of Defense and the Interior, both members of the ruling Al-Sabah family, resign. The resignations are accepted by the Emir, who appoints a different member of the Al-Sabah family and Mohammad al-Fares, the current Oil Minister, to their respective posts.

The British government ends its immigrant investor programs, known as a Tier 1 (Investor) visa, with "immediate effect". The scheme was introduced in 2008 in order to encourage wealthy people from outside the European Union to invest in the United Kingdom.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic order mandatory mass evacuations of civilians from their respective capital cities, Donetsk and Luhansk. Around 700,000 people are expected to be evacuated to Russia with the first buses carrying civilians to the Russian border already travelling to Rostov Oblast. Russian President Vladimir Putin orders lump-sum allowances of 10,000 rubles (130 US dollars) to be paid to refugees from Donbas.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: A UAZ-469 jeep is blown up outside of a building of the Donetsk People's Republic government in Donetsk city. No injuries are reported.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: Russia confirms that the Druzhba pipeline is on fire in rebel-held Luhansk Oblast after a massive explosion cut off gas to almost a hundred households. Transit supplies to Europe were not affected and continue as usual.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: Additional explosions are reported in Luhansk. The Luhansk People's Republic authorities state that a gas station has been blown up.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The British government relocates its embassy from Kyiv to the western Ukrainian city of Lviv, and again urges its citizens to leave the country while they still can.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Estonia delivers a shipment of U.S.-made FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank missiles to Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: U.S. President Joe Biden says that Vladimir Putin will launch a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in the "coming days" and that Russian troops will try to capture the capital Kyiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Anti-war protesters gather in Burlington, Vermont to call for a peaceful solution to the ongoing conflict amidst fears of a war with Ukraine.
Eight Malian soldiers and 57 Islamist militants are killed during a gunfight in the Archam region, after 40 civilians were killed there during terrorist attacks last week.

Mali's ruling military junta demands that French forces leave the country "without delay" after French President Emmanuel Macron announced a withdrawal of troops in an "orderly fashion" in the coming months.

context: Piracy in the Gulf of Guinea
text: Denmark recalls its frigate HDMS Esbern Snare from the Gulf of Guinea following a request from NATO to increase readiness and contribute to deterrence in Europe. The warship has been conducting anti-piracy measures in the Gulf since October.

Israel's Iron Dome fails to intercept a Hezbollah-operated military drone from Lebanon that penetrated seventy kilometers into Israeli airspace. The drone flew for forty minutes before returning to Lebanon. Israeli jets fly at very low altitude over Beirut in response to the incident.
At least seventeen people are killed in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Poland and the United Kingdom as Storm Eunice impacts northwestern Europe. Millions are also left without power.
England records a record wind gust of 122 mph (196 kmh) on the Isle of Wight in the English Channel.
The Grain Power Station in Kent, England, goes offline following the collapse of one of its towers and the roof of The O2 Arena in London is severely damaged due to high winds.
The roof of the ADO Den Haag Stadium, in The Hague, the Netherlands, is severely damaged.
Eleven people are missing after a ferry travelling between Greece and Italy catches fire.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 109,831 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.75 million.

India and the United Arab Emirates sign a free trade agreement over digital goods, raw materials, and apparels. It is the first major trade deal signed by India since Prime Minister Narendra Modi came into power in 2014.

U.S. Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin announces the sale of 250 M1 Abrams main battle tanks to Poland amid tensions with Russia. The Polish Land Forces will become the first European military to operate the American M1 Abrams.

The Ottawa Police Service makes over 100 arrests, including the arrest of protest organizer Pat King. Police accuse protestors of assaulting officers with one person being arrested after allegedly throwing a bicycle at a horse with a mounted officer on it.
Former Minneapolis police officer Kim Potter is sentenced to 2 years in prison for the killing of Daunte Wright in April 2021. During the sentencing, Potter expressed condolences to Wright's family.

context: 2022 Winter Olympics > LGBT athletes in the Olympic and Paralympic Games
text: Timothy LeDuc becomes the first openly non-binary athlete to compete at a Winter Olympics. They competed in figure skating with their skating partner Ashley Cain-Gribble for the United States.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: The Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic declare a full military mobilisation, a day after beginning to evacuate civilians to Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: Two Ukrainian troops are killed and four others are injured by shelling from separatist forces. Separatists have opened fire on more than 30 settlements with artillery, according to the Ukrainian military.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > War in Donbas
text: Russia launches an investigation following reports that shells landed inside Rostov Oblast, 2 km from the Russia–Ukraine border. At least one structure on a farm is reportedly destroyed.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: British Prime Minister Boris Johnson says that Vladimir Putin is planning "the biggest war in Europe since 1945" and that Russia intends to launch an invasion that will encircle the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
Fourteen people are killed by an al-Shabaab suicide bomber at a restaurant in Beledweyne, Somalia.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United States relations
text: U.S. Vice President Kamala Harris warns that the United States will impose sanctions on Russia if it invades Ukraine.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urges sanctions on Russia before a potential invasion occurs.
Ottawa police continue clearing protesters on Parliament Hill. Over 170 people have been arrested since Thursday as part of an effort to end the protests.
Freedom Convoy demonstrators admit that the protests are near the end.

Jeffrey Epstein associate Jean-Luc Brunel is found dead inside his cell at La Santé Prison in Paris. Brunel faced allegations of sexual assault spanning three decades and of participating in the sex trafficking ring run by Epstein.

context: 2022 Winter Olympics > Slovakia at the 2022 Winter Olympics, Ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics
text: The Slovakia men's hockey team wins their first medal at the Winter Olympics after defeating Sweden in the men's tournament.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Belarus–Russia relations
text: Military exercises between Belarusian and Russian forces in Belarus are extended amid tensions with Ukraine. Around 30,000 Russian troops are currently stationed in Belarus, according to NATO.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Belarus–Russia relations
text: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken says a decision by Russia and Belarus to extend military drills is Moscow following its "playbook" for an invasion of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > France–Russia relations
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin and French President Emmanuel Macron announce that they will work toward a ceasefire agreement in order to avert war with Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–United States relations
text: Biden has agreed "in principle" to meet with Putin in French-brokered summit talks as long as Russia does not invade Ukraine, the White House says.
The United States says it has intelligence indicating orders have been sent to Russian military commanders to proceed with an incursion on Ukraine.
U.S. President Joe Biden holds a National Security Council meeting on the ongoing crisis.

Following the meeting, Biden abruptly cancels plans to go to his home in Delaware for the Presidents' Day holiday. It is a rare occurrence for a U.S. president's travel plans to change in this manner, especially when the plans involve the president leaving Washington, D.C.
Biden speaks with Macron on diplomacy with and deterrence efforts against Russia, after Macron and Putin agreed to work towards a ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine.

Satellite imagery shows a shift in Russia's military deployment around Ukraine, with several units or troops deployed outside of bases or training grounds and some positioned along tree lines, according to an analysis by Maxar Technologies, who released the imagery.

The Luhansk People's Republic says that two civilians have been killed by Ukrainian military shelling in the village of Pionerskoye, near the Russia–Ukraine border. Five buildings were also destroyed.

Australian Defence Minister Peter Dutton reveals that a Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy destroyer fired at a Royal Australian Air Force Boeing P-8 Poseidon over the exclusive economic zone of Australia with a military-grade laser weapon as the ship transited through the Arafura Sea last week.

Seven children are killed and five more are injured during a Nigerian Air Force airstrike in the Maradi region of Niger. The army reported that the airstrike was the result of "a mistake on the border".

Leaked data from Credit Suisse exposes the identities of over 30,000 of the bank's clients whose anonymous numbered Swiss bank accounts, which collectively held over $100 billion, had allowed them to keep their identities secret. Its clients included heads of state (such as king Abdullah II of Jordan), human rights abusers, drug traffickers, intelligence officials, and individuals under sanctions or involved in financial crimes such as tax evasion or corruption, among others. The secret data from Switzerland's second largest bank was leaked about 1 year ago to the German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung and was analyzed by the non-profit Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) and 46 other news organizations, including The New York Times, Le Monde and The Guardian.
sources: Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project

text: The controversial Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam begins producing electricity, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed attending the inauguration of the dam.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy > COVID-19 vaccination in Italy
text: The Italian Health ministry recommends that severely immunocompromised people should receive a fourth dose of the mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine at least 120 days after receiving their previous booster.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Queen Elizabeth II tests positive for COVID-19 with "mild cold-like symptoms".

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in California > COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area
text: The Point Bonita Lighthouse, a lighthouse located at the Marin Headlands near Sausalito, reopens to visitors for the first time after two years of closure due to the pandemic.

Taiwan announces that its army will conduct live military drills next month which will simulate an invasion attempt of its islets of Dongyin and Kinmen, and its coast guard will conduct similar drills near Pratas Island, amid rising tensions between Taiwan and China.

context: Nepal–United States relations, Millennium Challenge Corporation's Nepal Compact
text: Hundreds of protestors gather outside the Nepalese parliament in Kathmandu in order to protest a United States grant from the Millennium Challenge Corporation for infrastructure projects, stating the deal undermines Nepal's sovereignty. Several protesters are injured following clashes with police.
The closing ceremony for the Winter Olympics is held in Beijing.
Rookie Austin Cindric wins the 64th running of the Daytona 500, becoming the ninth driver to score his first career Cup Series victory in the event.

Juwan Howard, head coach of the Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team, strikes Joe Krabbenhoft, assistant coach of the Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team, in an altercation following a 76–61 loss to the Badgers. Howard says Greg Gard, the Badgers' head coach, touched him in the handshake line, and that he was also upset that Gard had called a timeout with 20 seconds left in the game, which Gard had done to avoid a 10-second violation.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic
text: The European Union says it is prepared to issue sanctions against Russia if the country recognizes the Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic, breakaway regions of Ukraine that declared independence in 2014. Ukraine considers the quasi-states terrorist organizations.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin signs decrees recognising the independence of the Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic with immediate effect. He also asks the parliament to ratify the treaties on friendship and mutual aid with the breakaway territories.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic
text: President Putin addresses the nation and declares that Ukraine is a country with "no tradition of independent statehood and an artificial creation of Soviet Union founder Vladimir Lenin", and that the country has become a "U.S. puppet regime rife with corruption". He also reiterates his claim that Ukraine joining NATO would be a security risk to Russia.
Russian Armed Forces are deployed to the separatist republics of Donetsk and Luhansk for a "peacekeeping mission", shortly after Russia recognized the independence of the republics.
A senior U.S. official says Russian troops could move into the separatist regions of Ukraine by the end of the day.
A large column of military vehicles, including tanks, is reported on the outskirts of Donetsk city hours after Russia formally recognised the self-proclaimed republic as an independent state.
Russia says that it has killed five Ukrainian soldiers who tried to infiltrate its territory. Ukraine disputes the claim as "fake news".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The U.S. State Department evacuates its remaining diplomats in Ukraine to Poland.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan states that the United States will rally the international community to hold Russia accountable should it invade Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The U.S. says it will impose sanctions on the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic in response to Putin recognizing their independence and sovereignty.
Separatist forces shell the village of Zaitseve, Donetsk Oblast, killing two Ukrainian soldiers and a civilian.

In response to yesterday's leak of client data from Credit Suisse, Switzerland's second largest bank, the EU's European Commission is asked to "re-evaluate Switzerland as a high-risk money-laundering country" by the European People's Party, which is the group with the largest number of seats in the European Parliament.
At least 63 people are killed and 40 others injured by an explosion at a gold mine in Gbomblora, Poni, Burkina Faso.
An Iranian F-5 jet crashes into a school in Tabriz, East Azerbaijan Province, killing both pilots as well as a person on the ground.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record 7,533 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the territory to 60,383.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan
text: Jordanian Prime Minister Bisher Al-Khasawneh tested positive for COVID-19 while leading his country delegation in Cairo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea surpasses 2 million COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in England
text: British Prime Minister Boris Johnson says that he is lifting domestic coronavirus restrictions in England, including the legal requirement for people with COVID-19 to self-isolate, from February 24. As part of the plan, free self-testing will end by April 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa, COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa
text: South Africa changes its COVID-19 vaccination rules to allow mixing of vaccines between the Pfizer–BioNTech and Janssen COVID-19 vaccines for second and third doses and also reduces the interval between the second and third doses of the Pfizer vaccine in order to increase the country's vaccination rate.
Morocco's trade minister, Ryad Mezzour, and Israel's economy minister, Orna Barbivai, sign a trade deal in Rabat.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Wang Wenbin announces that China will sanction American defense contractors Lockheed Martin and Raytheon after the United States approved a US$100 million missile defense repair deal between the two companies and Taiwan.
The Constitutional Court decriminalizes abortion in all cases for up to six months of gestation, and removes time limits in cases of rape, fetal defects, or if the mother's life is in danger.

context: Aftermath of the 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état
text: Burkinabé President Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba orders an inquiry into the deaths of two civilians during last month's coup d'état.

context: Social media use by Donald Trump
text: Former U.S. President Donald Trump's Truth Social app launches in the Apple Store.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic
text: Syria voices support for Russia's recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic as independent states.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Anti-war protesters gather at the Russian Embassy in Berlin, Germany, to oppose President Vladimir Putin's decision to send soldiers to separatist regions in Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Protesters also gather at the Russian Embassy in Kyiv to protest ongoing tensions between Russia and Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The United States calls the Russian troop deployments in eastern Ukraine "an invasion".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The Russian parliament ratifies the friendship and cooperation treaties with the DPR and LPR, following Putin's request made the previous day.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: The foreign ministers of European Union member states agree on a package of new sanctions against Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Germany suspends the Nord Stream 2 project in response to Russia's recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic as independent states.

The U.N. Security Council unanimously passes a resolution declaring that Iraq is no longer required to pay out to victims of its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Iraq had paid out US$50 billion to 1.4 million claimants, including one claim to the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation that totaled US$14.7 billion, by the time of the resolution's passage.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong Chief Executive Carrie Lam announces a citywide testing campaign due to surge of the cases caused by the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. It is planned to test each citizen three times during the campaign.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: Singapore reports a record 26,032 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 622,293.

context: Aftermath of the 2020 Nova Scotia attacks
text: A public inquiry into the 2020 shootings in Nova Scotia, Canada, that killed 22 people is opened.

context: Persecution of Christians in North Korea, Religion in North Korea
text: A South Korean state commission confirms that retreating North Korean soldiers murdered over 1,150 South Korean Christian civilians in the early stages of the Korean War due to a state anti-religion campaign.

context: 20th National Congress of the People's Party (Spain)
text: The secretary general of the People's Party, Teodoro García Egea, resigns after a scandal over alleged spying on the President of the Community of Madrid Isabel Díaz Ayuso.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Ukraine announces the mobilization of its military reserves with a maximum service length of one year for reservists between the ages of 18 and 60 years.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Ukraine urges all citizens to leave Russia immediately, following an increase in tensions in the region.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Ukraine closes its civilian airspace nationwide due to potential hazards.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Russia closes its airspace in a region to the east of its border with Ukraine.
Tunisia announces that they will remove Death on the Nile from theaters over Gal Gadot’s role in the film and her normalization of Israel.
Brent Crude oil reaches its highest price since its 2014 peak, at $99 per barrel, amid rising tensions between Russia and Ukraine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea > COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea
text: South Korea approves the use of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 171,452 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,329,182.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia, COVID-19 vaccination in Cambodia
text: Cambodia begins its COVID-19 vaccination rollout for children over the age of three years, becoming the world's first country to administer vaccines for children under the age of five years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record 8,674 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the territory-wide total of confirmed cases to 75,248.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada, COVID-19 drug development
text: The Canadian government signs an agreement with AstraZeneca to procure 100,000 doses of the Evushield COVID-19 antibody therapy for use in high-risk patients.
Prime Minister of Canada Justin Trudeau revokes the state of emergency that was declared under the Emergencies Act on February 14.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Chernobyl
text: Russian troops enter the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone. Ukraine says that Russian forces have captured the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy calls the attack on Chernobyl a "declaration of war on all of Europe".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Snake Island campaign
text: Ukraine reports that Russian Navy warships have attacked Snake Island near the Danube Delta.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sumy
text: Russian troops enter Sumy and take control of the road leading from Kyiv to Moscow. Battles for strategic cities on the railway to Sumy are also underway.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Antonov Airport
text: Russian gunships bombard Antonov Airport near Kyiv. Ukraine says that three helicopters were shot down in defence. Russian Airborne Forces seized control of the airport, but the Ukrainian Ground Forces have recaptured the airport.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Antonov Airport
text: An-225 Mriya, the largest aircraft in the world by weight and by wingspan, is destroyed during a Russian air strike on the suburb of Kyiv. The plane did not manage to leave Hostomel before hostilities began.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv, Kyiv Offensive
text: The Mayor of Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko, announces a curfew in the capital from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin orders a military operation to "demilitarise and denazify" Ukraine. Putin also warns of "consequences you have never seen in history" for anyone who tries to interfere or "create threats for our country".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine confirms that Russian Ground Forces have entered Luhansk, Sumy, Kharkiv, Kherson, Chernihiv, and Zhytomyr Oblasts and have also crossed the border from occupied Crimea. Russian troops also attack the port cities of Odesa and Mariupol in amphibious landings.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia announces that they have taken control of the North Crimean Canal in the Kherson Oblast and have restored the supply of water to Crimea.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian ballistic and cruise missiles strike multiple Ukrainian cities and airfields, with eighteen people being killed in Odesa. A missile also strikes the Ministry of Defence intelligence headquarters in Kyiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Ukrainian Air Force Antonov An-26 is shot down and crashes in Obukhiv, killing five crew members, according to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: An attack on a military unit in Podilsk kills six civilians and injures seven others.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine's military reports that at least 137 of its soldiers have been killed in Eastern Ukraine, with a senior Ukrainian government official estimating that hundreds of Ukrainian troops have been killed by airstrikes. Ukraine's military also says that 50 Russian soldiers have been killed in action.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declares martial law across the country in response to the invasion. Zelenskyy also orders a general military mobilization of fit-to-serve Ukrainian citizens, with men between the ages of 18 and 60 years prohibited from leaving the country.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Armed Forces says that its "lightning offensive" has crippled the Ukrainian military and suppressed its air defense systems. However, the Ukrainian Air Force says that it is repelling Russian invaders.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Defence Ministry says that it has destroyed 83 Ukrainian "above-ground military facilities", including 11 aerodromes.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine says that it has shot down six Russian warplanes and two helicopters, and destroyed dozens of enemy armored vehicles, according to its Joint Centre of Control and Coordination. However, Russian military representatives deny the claims.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that two Russian civilian ships have been hit by anti-ship missiles in the Sea of Azov, causing multiple deaths. Russia subsequently restricts access for civilian vessels on the Sea of Azov.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Turkish-owned vessel is bombed off the coast of Odesa, according to Turkey's Directorate General of Coastal Safety. No casualties are reported.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–NATO relations
text: Romania, Poland, and the Baltic states agree to trigger article 4 of NATO's North Atlantic Treaty in response to Russian aggression.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–NATO relations
text: German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock states that Germany will "launch the full package with the most massive sanctions against Russia."

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukraine suspends diplomatic relations with Russia in response to the invasion.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Lithuanian president Gitanas Nausėda announces that he will sign a decree declaring a state of emergency and asks Seimas to ratify it in an extraordinary session.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Moldova declares a state of emergency in response to the invasion. Hundreds of Ukrainians are crossing the border, according to President Maia Sandu.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine, Belarus and Moldova close their airspaces to commercial aircraft.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: U.S. President Joe Biden orders Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin to send 7,000 troops to Germany in order to assist NATO allies.

Eight polio vaccination workers are killed by unknown gunmen in Kunduz and Takhar, leading to the suspension of the vaccination campaign in the two provinces. The campaign was launched nationwide in November 2021.

context: Israel's role in the Syrian Civil War
text: Israel fires several missiles towards Damascus, Syria, killing three Syrian soldiers.
It is announced that Russia will participate in the upcoming Eurovision Song Contest in Turin, Italy despite invading Ukraine.
Iraq unveils three monumental structures in Hatra in an effort to restore the city after it was destroyed by the Islamic State in 2015.

A massive selloff occurs on the Moscow Stock Exchange, which prompts its operator to trigger circuit breakers twice in three hours. The Russian ruble's exchange rate falls to a record low of ₽89.98 per US dollar.

The National Bank of Ukraine pegs the official hryvnia rate to the US dollar at ₴29.25, bans foreign currency purchases on the interbank market and introduces cash withdrawal limits. The central bank also orders a suspension of all transactions with Russian accounts and introduces unlimited short-term liquidity loans for banks.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong begins rolling out COVID-19 vaccine passports for people over the age of 12 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record 31,199 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.3 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: Singapore suspends a plan to ease and simplify COVID-19-related rules, including home gatherings, which was expected to begin tomorrow due to an increase in new COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Thailand reports a record 23,557 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.79 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 vaccination in Canada
text: Health Canada approves Medicago's CoVLP COVID-19 vaccine for use in adults, making it the first domestic vaccine to be approved for use in Canada.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maine
text: Maine surpasses 2,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The European Medicines Agency recommends the usage of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine as a booster dose for teenagers over the age of 12 years and also approves the use of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine for children between the ages of 6 and 11 years.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–European Union relations
text: The European Union says that it will introduce the "strongest, harshest package" of sanctions on the Russian economy in response to the invasion.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–New Zealand relations
text: The New Zealand government is expected to introduce a package of sanctions against Russia that includes a ban on the entry into and transit through the country of Russian government officials and other people connected to the invasion, as well as a ban on the export of goods to Russian military and security forces.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–South Korea relations
text: South Korean president Moon Jae-in announces that the country will impose economic sanctions against Russia.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson announces that the United Kingdom will impose sanctions on Russian banks and oligarchs. Russian airline Aeroflot will also be banned from operating flights to the UK due to the invasion.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Canada–Russia relations
text: Canada terminates all export permits with Russia in response to the invasion of Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United States relations
text: U.S. President Joe Biden announces sanctions against Russia and vows that additional sanctions could be coming. He also reaffirms that the U.S. will not directly intervene in Ukraine but will continue to defend NATO.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > India–Russia relations
text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold a telephone meeting. During the meeting, Modi called for Russia and Ukraine to "end the violence".

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Latvia and the Czech Republic suspend issuing visas to Russian citizens.

context: Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Anti-war protests in Russia
text: Protesters in Russia are detained as people gather in cities across the country in order to protest Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

context: Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Anti-war protests in Russia
text: Russian activist Marina Litvinovich is detained by Moscow police after calling for anti-war demonstrations across Russia.

context: Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Anti-war protesters gather at Russian embassies in many countries to oppose President Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

context: Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Protesters gather at 10 Downing Street to denounce Russia's invasion of Ukraine and to call for Prime Minister Boris Johnson and the United Kingdom to support Ukraine.
Three former Minneapolis police officers, J. Alexander Kueng, Thomas K. Lane and Tou Thao, are found guilty of violating the civil rights of George Floyd under government authority.
Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov signs a decree that bans the slaughtering of cattle during funerals in the country.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: UEFA announces that the 2022 UEFA Champions League Final will be moved from Saint Petersburg, Russia, in response to the invasion of Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Formula 1 driver Sebastian Vettel says that he will not participate in the 2022 Russian Grand Prix, which is expected to be held on September 24 in Sochi.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: The Ukrainian military says that it has blown up a bridge in order to prevent Russian forces from advancing to Kyiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: Ukraine says that Russian troops have entered Kyiv and heavy fighting is underway. Videos on social media show tanks advancing through the city's Obolon neighbourhood. Gunfire and explosions are also reported in the city's Podilskyi District.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: The US Department of Defense says that Russia is losing momentum in its attack on Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Millerovo air base attack
text: Ukrainian OTR-21 Tochka missiles attack the Millerovo air base in Rostov oblast, Russia, destroying two Russian Air Force warplanes according to Ukrainian officials. Images appear to show the airbase on fire.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Starobilsk
text: A column of Russian soldiers is defeated by the Ukrainian army in Starobilsk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Ivankiv
text: Ukrainian airborne assault troops engage Russian soldiers at Ivankiv and Dymer.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Chernihiv
text: A captain and corporal from the Russian 11th Guards Air Assault Brigade surrender to the Armed Forces of Ukraine near Chernihiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sumy
text: Russian forces reportedly retreat from Sumy.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Chernobyl
text: The Ukrainian government's State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate says that higher than usual gamma radiation levels have been detected in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone after the power plant was captured by Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Antonov Airport
text: The Russian Defence Ministry says that Russian Airborne Forces have recaptured the strategic Hostomel Airport near Kyiv, after assaulting the airbase with 200 helicopters.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukraine–NATO relations, 2022 NATO virtual summit
text: During an emergency NATO summit, Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg announces that NATO will provide weapons to Ukraine. He also announces that the NATO Response Force will be activated for the first time in history.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kazakhstan–Russia relations
text: Kazakhstan will deny Russia’s request for troops to join the war. It will also not join Putin’s recognition of Donetsk People's Republic or Luhansk People's Republic.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses European leadership of "inaction" in face of the Russian invasion, saying "Like World War II, you said never again, but here it is again and you're not doing enough to respond". Zelenskyy also calls on citizens across the European Union to protest and force their governments to take more decisive action.
A Moldovan-flagged chemical tanker is hit by a missile near the Port of Odesa, seriously injuring two crew members, according to Moldova's naval agency. It is unclear who launched the missile.

Russian President Vladimir Putin urges the Armed Forces of Ukraine to "take power in your own hands" and overthrow the Ukrainian government, which he referred to as a "gang of drug addicts and neo-Nazis".
Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova warns both Finland and Sweden that they could face "detrimental military and political consequences" if they attempt to join NATO.
At least 23 FARC dissidents are killed by the Colombian Army during an operation in Arauca Department.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eurovision Song Contest 2022
text: Russia is disqualified from competing in the Eurovision Song Contest 2022 due to its invasion of Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Expo 2020
text: The Dubai expo will be open to all nations despite Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
At least seven people are killed and 85 others are injured by an earthquake in Sumatra, Indonesia. The 6.2 magnitude earthquake is felt as far away as Malaysia and Singapore.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record 10,010 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, which is the first time that the territory has reported more than 10,000 cases since the beginning of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia
text: Indonesia reports a record 61,631 new COVID-19 recoveries in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 4.73 million.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan
text: The Kyrgyzstan Health Ministry announces that the country plans to purchase doses of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine, as well as around 100,800 doses of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record for the second consecutive day of 32,070 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.33 million.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–Taiwan relations
text: Taiwanese Premier Su Tseng-chang announces that Taiwan will impose sanctions on Russia following the invasion of Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: Russia bans all British airlines from its airspace and airports in response to the UK's ban on its flag carrier Aeroflot.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–European Union relations
text: The European Union freezes all assets held by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in the EU.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United States relations
text: The Biden administration announces that the U.S. will join the European Union in imposing sanctions on Putin.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Council of Europe announces the suspension of Russia's membership.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Council of the OECD formally terminates the accession process of Russia to the organisation.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin tells Chinese President Xi Jinping that Russia is willing to hold talks with Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urges Vladimir Putin to engage in talks in order to end the conflict.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Kremlin Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov says that Russia has agreed to hold talks and will send a delegation to Minsk, Belarus.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian presidential advisor Mykhailo Podolyak says that the country is ready to hold talks with Russia on neutral status in order to implement a ceasefire. A time and place is expected to be announced.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: President Zelenskyy calls for Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett to serve as a mediator in talks between Ukraine and Russia.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Foreign relations of the Federated States of Micronesia
text: The Federated States of Micronesia suspends diplomatic ties with Russia.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > China–Russia relations
text: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urges Russia to respect the "territorial sovereignty" of Ukraine and to "put an end to civilian casualties by resuming negotiations."

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Belarus–Ukraine relations
text: Secretary of the Belarus Foreign Ministry Anatoly Glaz says that Belarus is ready to help bring peace to Ukraine amid reports of possible peace talks in Minsk.

context: Nuclear program of Iran > Russia–United States relations
text: U.S. State Department spokesperson Ned Price says that the U.S. will still engage with Russia in efforts to revive the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action and prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons despite Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

context: Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela
text: Brazil and Venezuela will reopen their border after a two year closure due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainians, Norwegians, and Russians hold a joint anti-war protest in Kirkenes, Norway, calling for Vladimir Putin to be tried at the International Criminal Court at The Hague, Netherlands.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Protesters gather in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, to stand in solidarity with Ukraine.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Protesters gather at the Russian consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland, for a second consecutive day to express outrage over the war.
Russia announces that it has partially restricted access to Facebook.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > 2021–22 UEFA Champions League
text: UEFA announces the relocation of this year's Champions League final from the Krestovsky Stadium in Saint Petersburg to the Stade de France near Paris, in response to the crisis.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > 2022 Formula One World Championship
text: The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile cancels this year's edition of the Russian Grand Prix in Sochi initially scheduled for September 25, stating that "it is impossible to hold the Russian Grand Prix in the current circumstances".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: Russian Ground Forces attempt to attack an army base near Kyiv on Victory Avenue as well as an electricity generating station in the city. The Ukrainian military says that they repelled both attacks.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: A residential tower block near Kyiv International Airport is hit by a missile.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive, Battle of Kyiv
text: Ukraine's army claims that its air defences shot down two Russian Ilyushin Il-76 transport planes carrying paratroopers near the cities of Vasylkiv and Bila Tserkva in Kyiv Oblast, but did not provide any video evidence or details on crash sites. Ukraine also claims that a Sukhoi Su-25 attack jet was shot down.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Melitopol
text: The Russian Armed Forces report that they have captured the city of Melitopol in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. However, this claim is disputed. Russian state media says that Russian troops entered the city after facing "no resistance".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy posts a video of himself in the capital Kyiv amid rumors that he left the country.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Navy warns that all civilian ships and vessels attempting to approach the Ukrainian Black Sea coast will be destroyed as "terrorist threats".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Poland says that around 100,000 Ukrainians have crossed the border since the invasion began.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin issues orders to expand the offensive, after declaring peace talks "dead".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian military destroys rails at all railway junctions leading to Russia as part of an attempt to prevent Russian military supplies from being delivered by freight trains.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Sergey Aksyonov, the head of the Republic of Crimea, says that supplies of water via the North Crimean Canal returned after Russians destroyed the dam that prevented the flow of water from the Dnieper river.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces shell the city of Sartana, Ukraine, and the nearby village of Buhas, killing ten Greek nationals.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: In an official joint statement, the European Commission, France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States, agree to remove some Russian banks from SWIFT. The group also commits to "imposing restrictive measures that will prevent the Russian Central Bank from deploying its international reserves in ways that undermine the impact of our sanctions."

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Several computer chip manufacturers, including TSMC and Intel, halt supplies of their products as a result of sanctions against Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports 112 deaths from COVID-19, a new single-day record.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates, Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The United Arab Emirates removes the mandatory face masks mandate in outdoor spaces, making the use of them optional.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Estonia–Russia relations
text: Estonia announces that it will close its airspace to all Russian airlines.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Turkey–Ukraine relations
text: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan says that Turkey is making efforts for an immediate ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: In a phone call, French President Emmanuel Macron calls for Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko to demand the withdrawal of Russian troops from Ukraine. During the phone call, Lukashenko also called reports of Belarus potentially having nuclear weapons "fake news".
Iran Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian announces that Iran will be studying a rough draft aimed at reviving the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia
text: Around 3,000 anti-war protesters across Russia have been detained since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched an invasion of Ukraine.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Protesters gather at the Russian embassy in London. During the protest, demonstrators are seen throwing eggs at the embassy, and call for Vladimir Putin to withdraw troops from Ukraine.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Around 200 demonstrators in Taipei, Taiwan call for the war to end.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Iranian police disperse protesters chanting "Death to Putin" outside the Ukrainian embassy in Tehran.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Protesters gather in Kansas City, Salt Lake City, the Space Needle in Seattle, and other cities across the U.S. to stand in solitary with Ukraine and call for peace.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Several Freedom Convoy truckers gather at the Grant Park in Chicago to protest in solitary with Ukraine.
Universities reopen in Afghanistan to male and female students for the first time since the Taliban took power 6 months ago.
Russia blocks access to social media platform Twitter.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv, Battle of Kyiv
text: Russian Ground Forces begin targeting gas and oil pipelines outside Kharkiv and Kyiv in an attempt to incapacitate their defenses, with multiple explosions being reported at an oil depot near Vasylkiv, Kyiv Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv, Battle of Kyiv
text: The Ukrainian Army announces that they remain in control of Kyiv. Additionally, regional governor Oleh Synyehubov announces that Ukraine remains in control of Kharkiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv, Battle of Kyiv
text: Ukraine's military says that it has destroyed a convoy of 56 tanks near the capital Kyiv and killed Chechen General Magomed Tushayev.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive
text: Russian troops enter the port city of Berdiansk and seize all administrative buildings, according to the city's mayor.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: 368,000 refugees have fled Ukraine since the invasion started, according to an estimate by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin orders Russia's nuclear forces placed on high alert, in response to what he considered "aggressive statements" by NATO members.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine says that they have used Baykar Bayraktar TB2 drones against Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The European Union says that it will provide fighter aircraft and finance €500 million in procurement and delivery of weapons to Ukraine, the first time that the EU has done so. The EU will also provide €50 million in medical supplies.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen allows volunteers to join Ukrainian soldiers to fight against Russia.

context: Syrian civil war > Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war
text: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that a Turkish drone has targeted Tell Rifaat near the Aleppo Governorate. No casualties are reported.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, the United States and Japan freeze all assets of the Russian Central Bank and the Russian National Wealth Fund under their jurisdiction, preventing the usage of more than a third of Russia's $630 billion of foreign exchange reserves.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: British Petroleum liquidates its 19.75% stake in Russian state-owned oil company Rosneft. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2022/02/27/bp-abandons-stake-russian-oil-giant-rosneft/ (The Daily Telegraph)]

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Norway's sovereign fund will divest its Russian holdings.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Russian ruble experiences extreme buy–sell spreads. While the currency exchanges in banks offer a range of 70–90 rubles per US dollar and 80–100 rubles per euro, sell quotes vary from 100 rubles to over 150 rubles for 1 US dollar. Panic selling is suspected as a reason for the fluctuations.
Six people are killed and another is missing during heavy floods in Queensland.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record 26,062 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the territory to 138,955.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: The Thailand Public Health Ministry calls for hospitals in Thailand to treat COVID-19 like an endemic instead of a pandemic beginning on March 1.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: New York City Mayor Eric Adams announces that the city will lift their vaccine mandate for indoor businesses and dining on March 7.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Peru, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Peruvian Ministry of Transport and Communications announces that they have extended the suspension of passenger flights from South Africa until March 31.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Kremlin Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov says that a Russian delegation has arrived in Gomel, Belarus, to hold talks as part of an effort to end the war. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Belarus as the country is a non-neutral party in the conflict. Ukraine and Russia eventually agree to hold negotiations on the Belarus–Ukraine border near the Pripyat river tomorrow as the Ukrainian delegation is travelling to the location via Poland for safety reasons.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukraine sues Russia in the International Court of Justice, seeking an injunction ordering an immediate end to Russian military activities.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: During a meeting intended to approve a report by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, Russian delegate Oleg Anisimov apologizes to Ukraine and says that there was "no justification" for invading Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–European Union relations, Canada–Russia relations
text: The European Union and Canada close their airspaces to Russian aircraft.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits
text: Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu, the foreign minister of Turkey, triggers the wartime clause of the Montreux Convention and limits movements of military vessels whose bases are not on the Black Sea coast.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarus–European Union relations
text: The European Union imposes sanctions on Belarus, forbidding the import of some commodities, including timber, steel, oil-derived fuels and cement.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Israel–Russia relations, Israel–Ukraine relations
text: Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett offers to mediate a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Germany–Ukraine relations
text: Germany announces it will send weapons to Ukraine.
North Korea says that it has tested a ballistic missile that entered the sea.

China and the European Union will host a virtual summit on April 1 as part of an effort to deescalate the economic and geopolitical tensions between the two governments, particularly with respect to Lithuania.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Anti-war demonstrators gather in Minsk, Belarus, to protest Russia's invasion of Ukraine despite Belarus's involvement in the invasion. Around 440 people are detained in the protests.
Belarus holds a constitutional referendum.
The ruling military junta of Burkina Faso, the Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration, says that it is considering beginning a thirty-month transition to democracy.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Censorship in the European Union
text: The European Union bans the Sputnik news agency and RT, both state-sponsored news outlets which are widely considered to be promoting Russian propaganda.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: FIFA prohibits Russia from playing under its own flag, but will allow the country to compete under a neutral banner of "Football Union of Russia", which is similar to how the International Olympic Committee requires Russian athletes to compete at the Olympics under the name of the Russian Olympic Committee. International football matches that would have taken place in Russia may only be played without spectators in other, neutral countries. However, several teams, including all possible playoff opponents for the 2022 FIFA World Cup, refuse to compete against the Russian team.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
