text: The International Judo Federation suspends Russian president Vladimir Putin's titles as the honorary president and ambassador of the federation, "in light of the ongoing war... in Ukraine".

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: Latvian ice hockey club Dinamo Riga withdraws from the Kontinental Hockey League in protest of the invasion, joining Finland club Jokerit.

The Associated Press reveals that Qatar, the host of the World Cup, paid more than $10 million for "Project Riverbed", a covert influence campaign run between 2012 and 2014 by a former CIA operative's company, which was aimed at neutralising Theo Zwanziger's criticism of FIFA's decision making process for Qatar's host bid, which Zwanziger accused of being corrupt.
Liverpool beat Chelsea 11–10 in a penalty shoot-out at Wembley Stadium to win the 2021–22 EFL Cup and claim a record ninth cup title.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Dozens of people are killed and hundreds more are injured in a massive MLRS attack on Kharkiv, according to the Ukrainian Interior Ministry. Videos appear to show cluster munitions being used in the rocket attack.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Hennadiy Matsehora, the mayor of Kupiansk who surrendered the city to the Russians in exchange for peace the previous day, is now indicted for treason by Ukrainian officials.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive
text: A long convoy of Russian Ground Forces armoured vehicles, tanks and artillery continues to advance towards Kyiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Okhtyrka
text: Ukrainian Ambassador to the U.S. Oksana Markarova confirms that Russian forces attacked Okhtyrka with a vacuum bomb.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zhytomyr Airport attack
text: Russia attacks the Zhytomyr Airport using Iskander ballistic missiles launched from Belarus.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive
text: The Russian Defence Ministry says Russian Ground Forces have captured the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and that the plant's operations have continued normally under the guard of soldiers. However, Ukraine denies that the power plant has been seized by Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Ukraine–NATO relations
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy calls for U.S. President Joe Biden and NATO to impose a no-fly zone over Ukraine. However, White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki, British Defense Secretary Ben Wallace, and NATO Secretary-General Jens Stoltenberg state that NATO and the U.S. have ruled out imposing a no-fly zone.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Kremlin Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov accuses the European Union of "hostile behaviour" towards Russia, and says that the arming of Ukraine was an "extremely dangerous and destabilising factor". Peskov says that Western arms supplies to Kyiv shows that Moscow was justified in demilitarising Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Dmitry Peskov says that Vladimir Putin's nuclear deterrent order remarks were in response to comments made by British Foreign Secretary Liz Truss.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Latvia allows volunteers to participate in the Russo-Ukrainian war.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarus–Ukraine relations
text: Belarus is expected to directly deploy its armed forces in Ukraine, thereby aiding Russia in its invasion. However, a senior U.S. defense official says that there are no indications that Belarusian troops have been deployed yet.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > France–Russia relations
text: The office of French President Emmanuel Macron states that during a phone call with the Russian President, "Putin confirmed his willingness to make commitments" to stop attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure and secure major roadways.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The United Nations reports at least 406 civilian casualties in Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian engineer of the Russian yacht Princess Anastasia attempts to scuttle the vessel in the port of Mallorca, Spain, damaging the yacht's engine room.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Two ethnic Greeks are killed after the city of Sartana is bombarded by the Russian Air Force.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian Air Force pilots begin arriving in Poland to begin taking control of fighter aircraft donated by European Union countries. The Ukrainian government says that the EU is handing over 70 fighter jets to its air force including 28 MiG-29s from Poland, 12 from Slovakia, 16 from Bulgaria, and 14 Sukhoi Su-25s from Bulgaria. Bulgarian Prime Minister Kiril Petkov said he had rejected the request. European Union security chief Josep Borrell later clarified that the donations were done "bilaterally" by individual EU member states and not from the EU itself.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: The Central Bank of Russia (CBR) raises the interest rate from 9.5% to 20%, the highest rate since 2003. The Russian ruble also loses more than a quarter of its value at the beginning of trading, with ranges of 100–120 rubles to the US dollar.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: The CBR orders all companies receiving foreign currency to exchange 80% of the revenue into rubles, in an attempt to stabilise the market.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: Russia institutes capital controls, banning all trading of Russian securities by foreign legal entities.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: The Moscow Stock Exchange, which did not open for trade on Monday, will remain closed until Saturday, as Russian regulators attempt to contain the selloff of Russian assets and rubles.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: President Vladimir Putin ordered a ban on transferring hard currency, such as U.S. dollars and euros, abroad, including by servicing foreign debt. Whether this constitutes a debt default is unclear.
Petrol prices in the United Kingdom reach an all-time high, according to the RAC.
An EU subsidiary of Sberbank is declared to be "failing or likely to be failing" by European banking regulators. The bank's assets amount to €13.64 billion.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Gujarat
text: Gujarat will lift their COVID-19 restrictions on March 2.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: A third team of medical health experts arrive in Hong Kong amid an increase in the number of new COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > History of COVID-19 vaccine development
text: Novavax says that it will pursue full approval for its COVID-19 vaccine during the second half of this year.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: A Ukrainian government delegation arrives in Belarus for peace talks with the Russian delegation in an attempt to end the war.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian presidential advisor Mykhailo Podolyak announces that peace talks have begun as part of an effort to end the war. During the talks, Ukraine calls for a ceasefire to end the war.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky says that Russia and Ukraine are interested in reaching an agreement aimed at ending the war.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: The first round of peace talks conclude. Both delegations will return to their respective capitals for consultations prior to a second round of talks, which will be held at the Belarus–Poland border.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–European Union relations, Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: In retaliation of the Russian aircraft ban, Russian authorities prohibit EU and UK airlines from landing in or crossing Russian airspace.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Monaco relations
text: Monaco, a city favoured by Russian oligarchs, adopts sanctions against Russia in line with current EU sanctions.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Switzerland relations
text: Breaking from a historic tradition of Swiss neutrality, Switzerland says it will adopt all EU sanctions on Russia effective immediately in response to the invasion. Swiss banks are believed to hold billions of dollars in Russian funds.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: The United Kingdom bans Russian ships from docking at its ports.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Canada–Russia relations
text: Canada bans the importation of Russian crude oil, becoming the first G7 member to ban the importation of Russian oil. Canada also approves the delivery of 100 Carl Gustaf 8.4cm recoilless rifles and 2,000 anti-tank rockets to Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarus–United States relations, Russia–United States relations
text: The United States closes its embassy in Minsk, Belarus, and allows "non-essential staff" at its embassy in Moscow to leave the country amid war in neighbouring Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarus–United States relations, Russia–United States relations
text: The United States announces it is expelling 12 Russian people in New York who are a part of Russia's delegation to the United Nations, saying they are "intelligence operatives" who have "abused their privileges of residency" by engaging in "espionage activities."

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukraine–United States relations
text: The United States says it will continue to provide arms to Ukraine to aid that country in its defense against Russian aggression.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Sweden–Ukraine relations
text: Swedish Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson announces that the country will send military equipment, including anti-tank launchers, to Ukraine, breaking with a doctrine of not sending arms to countries that are engaged in active conflict.
Diplomats from the U.S., United Kingdom, France, Germany, Russia, China, and Iran gather in Vienna, Austria to seek a deal to revive the 2015 Iran deal.

An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson says that efforts to revive the 2015 Iran deal could succeed if the U.S. and other Western powers take steps to solve three issues. These three issues include the extent to which sanctions would be rolled back, providing guarantees that the U.S. will not withdraw from the deal again, and resolving questions over uranium traces found at several old but undeclared sites in Iran.
France calls for the talks to end this week and for Iran and the Western countries to reach an agreement to revive the deal.
U.S. President Joe Biden announces that the U.S. will send a delegation to Taiwan in order to reaffirm its commitment to the country.
The KCNA says that the missile test that North Korea conducted on Sunday was to develop a "reconnaissance" satellite system.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan announces that the International Criminal Court will conduct a criminal investigation into war crimes and crimes against humanity in Ukraine.
The U.S. House of Representatives votes 422–3 to pass the Emmett Till Antilynching Act, a bill that would make lynching a federal crime in the U.S.

Belarus approves the adoption of the changes to the Constitution of Belarus according to President Alexander Lukashenko's proposal, with just over 65% support, according to Belarusian electoral officials.

Belarus confirms that it has revoked its status as a non-nuclear state, thus allowing the country to host and develop its own nuclear weapons. President Lukashenko says that he could ask Russia to return nuclear missiles to his country if any nuclear weapons are transferred to Poland or Lithuania.

context: Potential enlargement of the European Union > Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signs an application for the country to join the European Union.
The United Nations Security Council votes in favour of a British-drafted resolution to place an arms embargo on the Houthis.
A report from the second IPCC working group is published, focusing on adaptation to climate change and population vulnerability.
In new research published by the Nature journal, it is revealed that the Hot Jupiter exoplanet WASP-121b has clouds of metal and rains gems.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: FIFA and UEFA suspend all Russian football clubs from international competitions and also ban the Russian national football team from competing at the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. UEFA also ends its sponsorship with Russian energy firm Gazprom.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The International Ice Hockey Federation suspends all Russian and Belarusian clubs, as well as the respective national teams of the two countries, from its competitions. It also withdraws Russia's hosting rights of the 2023 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv > Kyiv offensive
text: A Russian military convoy that is about 64 kilometers (40 miles) long continues to advance toward Kyiv, as the invasion enters its sixth day.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv > Kyiv offensive
text: A senior U.S. defense official asserts that the convoy has "stalled" amid the Ukrainian military response and fuel and food shortages, but also warns that the Russian troops are "certain to regroup".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv
text: Russian forces strike the Kyiv TV Tower with a missile, causing a temporary disruption of TV and radio broadcasting. Five people are killed in the bombing, according to Ukrainian emergency services. A Russian missile also strikes the Babi Yar Holocaust Memorial Center.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv
text: The Russian Armed Forces warn Kyiv residents to leave the city as its armoured convoy approaches the city's outskirts. The Russians also warn people living around the headquarters of the Security Service of Ukraine to evacuate, with the stated purpose of "thwarting informational attacks against Russia".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kyiv
text: The Ukrainian Armed Forces foil an assassination plot against President Volodymyr Zelenskyy by killing a group of Chechen paramilitaries known as Kadyrovtsy, who were attempting to enter Kyiv on February 26, according to Ukrainian intelligence information.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarusian involvement in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Belarusian Ground Forces units enter northern Chernihiv Oblast, according to a senior Ukrainian territorial defence forces official. However, the Ukrainian presidential office says that there is no evidence that this has happened. Belarus previously said that it would not send its armed forces to Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Okhtyrka
text: Ukraine confirms that more than 70 troops were killed in a Russian ballistic missile strike on a base in Okhtyrka, Sumy Oblast, yesterday. It is the largest loss of life for Ukrainian forces in a single attack since the invasion began.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: A Russian missile strikes the Kharkiv Oblast state administration building on Freedom Square at 8 a.m. local time. Six people are injured in the strike, with the building being severely damaged. The Slovenian honorary consulate is also destroyed by a Russian missile.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: The head of the Donetsk People's Republic, Denis Pushilin, says that separatist forces are being assembled to encircle the port city of Mariupol.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The European Court of Human Rights orders an immediate cessation of bombarding and targeting of civilian targets in Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A senior U.S. defense official says that some Russian troop units have surrendered to Ukrainian forces "without a fight".
A battle between the Syrian Democratic Forces and Syrian soldiers kills two SDF fighters and two government soldiers.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Foreign relations of Andorra
text: Prime Minister Xavier Espot announces that he will enter urgently to parliamentary procedure on Wednesday so that the General Council can approve the normative framework to apply economic sanctions to Russia. This law will aim to freeze the bank assets of 700 people and 50 companies that the European Union considers to be linked to the invasion of Ukraine. It is the first time in the history of Andorra that sanctions have been applied to a foreign country.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Foreign relations of San Marino
text: The Grand and General Council of San Marino authorizes the country's government to enact sanctions against Russia, although the council rejects that the measures have a military content.

Nord Stream 2 AG, a subsidiary wholly owned by Gazprom that was supposed to operate the controversial gas pipeline in Europe, files for bankruptcy with the canton of Zug authorities after a range of sanctions was imposed on its parent company.
Russian President Vladimir Putin bans exporting currency abroad in excess of US$10,000.
The cargo ship Felicity Ace, which was carrying cars from Germany to the United States, sinks in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, after catching fire and being evacuated on February 16.
Eleven people die after a fire breaks out in a mall in Damascus, Syria.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand, COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand
text: New Zealand approves the usage of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine for people over the age of 18 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain
text: Bahrain issues an emergency approval for the vaccine candidate developed by Valneva, becoming the first country to approve the usage of the vaccine candidate.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea
text: North Korea informs the World Health Organization that it still has not reported any cases of COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
text: Queen Elizabeth II holds a virtual audience for the first time since testing positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: American health officials report that the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine protects children over the age of 5 years from hospitalizations and deaths due to the Omicron variant.
Researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology report that smoke from the 2019–20 Australian bushfire season has damaged the ozone layer, delaying its recovery by about a decade.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: A second round of peace talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations will be held tomorrow in an effort to pursue a ceasefire.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > China–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba asks China to help mediate a ceasefire. In response, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi says that China is ready to help Russia and Ukraine reach an agreement and mediate a ceasefire. China has also expressed regret for the conflict.
The European Parliament formally accepts Ukraine's application for EU membership.
The Israeli Supreme Court rules that four Palestinian families in East Jerusalem's Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood that were expected to be evicted can remain in their homes for the time being.
Former UFC Heavyweight Champion Cain Velasquez is charged with attempted murder and held in Santa Clara County Jail following a shooting yesterday.

context: Aftermath of the 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état
text: Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba, the ruling junta leader of Burkina Faso, signs a plan to begin a three-year transition to democracy.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, Media freedom in Russia
text: Russian authorities take down liberal Echo of Moscow radio station as well as an independent TV channel, Dozhd, both often critical of the government, for alleged deliberate falsehoods against the Russian military and incitement to extremism.

context: 2022 Major League Baseball season > 2021–22 Major League Baseball lockout
text: The MLBPA rejects an offer and final proposal by the Major League Baseball, thereby postponing spring training to March 12 and opening day to April 7.

context: 2022 Winter Paralympics > Ukraine at the 2022 Winter Paralympics
text: The International Paralympic Committee announces that Ukraine will send a delegation of 20 athletes to the upcoming Winter Paralympics in Beijing.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Fédération Internationale de Volleyball withdraws Russia's hosting rights of the 2022 FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship scheduled for August and September in response to the invasion.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive > Battle of Kyiv
text: The Ukrainian Air Force says that it has destroyed two Russian warplanes in a dogfight over Kyiv. A Ukrainian MiG-29 is also shot down during the air battle.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive > Battle of Kherson
text: Russian Ground Forces say that they have captured the Black Sea port of Kherson. The Ukrainian Ministry of Defense denies this claim, stating that the battle is ongoing.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive > Battle of Kherson
text: The mayor of Kherson says that the city has fallen to the invading Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: The mayor of Mariupol reports mass casualties and a water outage from "non-stop" Russian bombardments.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Horlivka offensive
text: Ukrainian forces begin an offensive towards Horlivka.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Chernihiv
text: Two Kalibr cruise missiles strike a hospital in Chernihiv after Russian troops were forced to retreat.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Russian forces launch airstrikes on Kharkiv National University and a local police department.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Enerhodar
text: Russia says that its troops have captured the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, the largest nuclear power plant in Europe. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirms that Russia had communicated that the plant was under their control and that personnel at the plant were continuing to perform their normal duties.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A missile strikes the Bangladeshi-flagged cargo ship Banglar Samriddhi docked at the Port of Olvia in Mykolaiv Oblast, killing a Bangladeshi engineer.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: An emergency special session of the UN General Assembly adopts a resolution calling for Russia to end the invasion.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: In an unprecedented move, the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) suspends all judicial proceedings against Ukraine pending before the ECHR.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian Armed Forces say that Ukraine has retaken the city of Makariv from Russia.
Members of the Free Papua Movement gun down eight people at a Telkomsel telecommunications tower in Puncak Regency, West Papua.
Anglophone rebels bomb a car in the Ekondo-Titi commune of Southwest Cameroon, killing seven people, including the mayor and a lieutenant.
The European Union removes seven Russian banks from the SWIFT financial messaging system, including VTB Bank, Novikombank, Promsvyazbank, Rossiya Bank, Sovcombank and VEB.RF.

Russian stocks endure a total wipeout in value on the London stock exchange, losing $570 billion in two weeks, with many Russian companies' stocks worth pennies. Entities such as Gazprom and Lukoil have lost almost all of their value. Sberbank, the largest bank in Russia, had a market cap of $102 billion six months ago but the value of outstanding shares is currently less than $190 million.
The World Bank suspends all programs in Russia and Belarus in response to the invasion of Ukraine.
Four people are suffocated to death in Pune district, India, after being given the task to clean out a septic tank.

A Romanian Air Force MiG-21 from the 86th Air Base, which was carrying out an air patrol mission over Dobruja, vanishes from radar, and an IAR 330 rescue helicopter sent on a search and rescue mission also disappears. A Defence Ministry spokesman later confirms that the helicopter crashed near Gura Dobrogei, killing all seven crew members on board. The fate of the MiG-21 and its pilot is still unknown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record 55,353 new COVID-19 cases and 160 deaths in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea surpasses 200,000 daily cases from COVID-19 for the first time after reporting a record 219,241 new cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korean Prime Minister Kim Boo-kyum tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Spain surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey
text: Turkey eases the majority of its COVID-19-related restrictions including easing of mask mandate indoors and outdoors and no longer asking contact tracing when entering public places two years after the first COVID-19 cases in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 vaccination in Australia
text: The Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation recommends the usage of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine as a booster dose.
A study published by the New England Journal of Medicine shows that the booster shot of the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine restores protection against the Omicron variant.
A World Health Organization (WHO) panel of International experts recommends the use of Merck & Co.'s COVID-19 antiviral pill Molnupiravir for high-risk patients.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ceasefire talks between Russia and Ukraine, scheduled to take place today, are postponed.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: The Russian delegation arrives in Belarus for a second round of talks expected to occur on Thursday morning.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Turkey relations
text: Turkey says that the Russian Navy has cancelled the transit of four of its warships through the Bosporus strait upon request after Turkey triggered the wartime clause of the Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits, which allows Turkey to close the Bosporus strait and the Dardanelles to foreign warships.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–European Union relations
text: The European Union will suspend deliveries of euro banknotes to Russia beginning on March 12, with exemptions for private persons and their family members in Russia as well as diplomatic missions with legal immunity.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United States relations
text: Pentagon Press Secretary John Kirby announces that the U.S. will postpone a Minuteman III ICBM missile test in an effort to de-escalate tensions between Russia and Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Germany–Russia relations
text: Germany seizes Alisher Usmanov's superyacht Dilbar in Hamburg after the Russian oligarch was sanctioned by the EU on Monday.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > China–Russia relations
text: A Western intelligence report indicates that China had some level of knowledge about the Russian invasion of Ukraine as it requested Russian officials not to invade during the 2022 Olympic Games. China disputes the accuracy of the reports, saying they are a way to shift blame on the country and smear it.

During a meeting in Israel, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz says that a new agreement to revive the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action "cannot be postponed any longer". However, Prime Minister Naftali Bennett calls the agreement "unacceptable" as he indicated that Iran would be allowed to install centrifuges on a large scale.

context: Protests against responses to the COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 anti-lockdown protests in New Zealand
text: Anti-lockdown rioters clash with police at the New Zealand Parliament Buildings in Wellington. A fire breaks out, destroying a children's playground. Several police officers are injured and 38 protesters are arrested.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian Opposition Leader Alexei Navalny calls for more anti-war protests in Russia and across the world, as well as protests against President Vladimir Putin.
The International Criminal Court announces that they have opened a criminal investigation into war crimes that have been committed in Ukraine since 2013, including during the invasion.
The Myanmar military junta pardons several celebrities who spoke out against the military coup including Lu Min, Wyne, Pyay Ti Oo, Eaindra Kyaw Zin and Paing Takhon.

Hundreds of women protest in the Nigerian capital of Abuja after the National Assembly rejected a series of amendments to the Constitution that would have expanded women's rights and autonomy. The proposed amendments included reserving 35% of all legislative seats and political party leadership positions for women, conferred citizenship to foreign husbands of Nigerian women, and allowing women to inherit the ancestry of their husband after five years of marriage.

context: Censorship of Wikipedia, Media freedom in Russia
text: Russia's communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, threatens to block the Russian Wikipedia for hosting an article on the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which the regulator alleges to be factually inaccurate. The same concerns the Russian edition of US-sponsored Voice of America (VOA); Current Time TV (a joint publication of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty and VOA) is already reported to be blocked in the country.

Russian space agency Roscosmos says that it will not launch 36 OneWeb satellites from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on Friday, unless OneWeb provides "legally binding guarantees" that the satellites will not be used for military purposes by the United Kingdom.

The International Paralympic Committee bans Russia and Belarus from competing in the upcoming Winter Paralympics in Beijing after initially announcing they would compete despite the invasion of Ukraine, taking part as "neutral countries".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Chernihiv
text: Vyacheslav Chaus, the governor of Chernihiv Oblast, says that at least 33 people have been killed and at least 18 others injured in Russian airstrikes on residential areas in Chernihiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Thirteen students are killed at the National University of Kharkiv after a Russian shell struck a dormitory at the university's Academy of Culture. Five foreign students are among the dead, including four Chinese and one Indian student.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kherson
text: The Ukrainian Navy patrol vessel Sloviansk is destroyed in a Russian anti-ship missile strike off the Port of Odesa, resulting in the disappearance of all its crew.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees says that over one million Ukrainians have fled the country since the invasion began.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United States relations
text: Russia and the U.S. establish a hotline in an effort to prevent escalation between the two nuclear powers.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov says that the war on Ukraine will continue "until the end", and accuses Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of allowing "a society where Nazism is flourishing". Lavrov also says that Russia is not planning a nuclear war.
Standard & Poor's downgrades Russia's debt from BB+ to CCC-, signalling that it believes that Russia is prone to defaulting on its obligations.

The Estonian cargo ship MV Helt sinks near the Port of Odesa in the Black Sea following an explosion. All six crew members on board were rescued, according to authorities. Estonian Foreign Minister Eva-Maria Liimets says that an investigation into the incident will occur.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in France > COVID-19 vaccination in France
text: French Prime Minister Jean Castex announces that France will lift their requirements for COVID-19 vaccine passports in access venues beginning on March 14.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia
text: Estonian President Alar Karis tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong
text: Hong Kong reports a record for the second consecutive day of 56,827 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the total of confirmed cases in the territory to 350,557. The territory also reporting a record 144 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the death toll in territory to 1,366.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan
text: COVID-19 vaccination in Kazakhstan

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan
text: Kazakhstan begins its production of the Sputnik Light COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Indiana
text: Indiana Governor Eric Holcomb signs an executive order ending the state’s COVID-19 emergency.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand reports a record 23,183 new community transmitted COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that the second round of talks between Ukraine and Russia have begun.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian presidential adviser Mykhailo Podolyak says that Ukraine and Russia have not "achieved the desired results they wanted", but that Russia has agreed to a temporary ceasefire in humanitarian corridors, thereby allowing more time for civilian evacuations. Both sides are expected to hold a third round of talks beginning next week.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: President Zelenskyy calls for a personal meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in an effort to end the war.

context: Nuclear program of Iran > Iran–Saudi Arabia relations
text: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman says that his country will continue talks with regional rival Iran in order to reach an agreement between the two countries. Bin Salman also reaffirms his support for a "strong" nuclear deal that would prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

context: Nuclear program of Iran > Iran–United States relations
text: U.S. State Department principal deputy spokesperson Jalina Porter says that efforts to revive the 2015 Iran nuclear deal have made "significant progress" but urges Iran not to wait any longer.

context: Potential enlargement of the European Union
text: Prime Minister of Georgia Irakli Garibashvili signs a letter to formally apply for membership in the European Union.

context: Potential enlargement of the European Union
text: Moldovan President Maia Sandu announces that Moldova is formally applying for EU membership.
The Assembly of the Republic of Kosovo approves a resolution urgently requesting the government to begin negotiations for the country's entry into NATO.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: French authorities seize the yacht of Russian oligarch Igor Sechin in La Ciotat after the European Union blacklisted Sechin and froze his assets.
The Armenian National Assembly elects Vahagn Khachaturyan in a second round as the new country's President.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Media freedom in the European Union, Censorship in the United Kingdom
text: Russian television network RT is taken off-air in the EU and the United Kingdom due to its coverage of the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: RT America ceases production and fires most of its employees. It expects the layoff to be permanent.

A new research published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology shows that the stegosaur Bashanosaurus, also known as the Bashanosaurus primitivus, is the oldest dinosaur species to be discovered in Asia.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > 2022 NFL season
text: The National Football League and National Football League Players Association announce that they will eliminate COVID-19 testing and other protocols for the 2022 season following a revision to U.S. CDC guidelines and a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases.
UEFA announces that they have banned Belarus from hosting international games due to its role in the invasion of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kherson > Battle of Mykolaiv
text: Ukrainian forces say that they have recaptured the Mykolaiv Airport.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kherson > Battle of Mykolaiv
text: Russia renews its assault on Mykolaiv with naval gunfire support.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kherson > Battle of Mykolaiv
text: The Ukrainian Navy scuttles its flagship frigate Hetman Sahaidachny at the port of Mykolaiv to prevent its capture by Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Enerhodar
text: The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Enerhodar catches fire following shelling by Russian troops. The fire is later extinguished.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Enerhodar
text: Ukrainian officials confirm that the power plant has been captured by Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Ukrainian air defences shoot down a Russian Sukhoi Su-25 jet over the city of Volnovakha in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive
text: Sky News chief correspondent Stuart Ramsay is shot and wounded by Russian troops near Kyiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: The Czech Republic introduces a state of emergency for 30 days as thousands of Ukrainian refugees arrive in the country.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Ukraine–NATO relations
text: NATO announces that they will not declare a no-fly zone over Ukrainian airspace, as such a declaration could create an avenue for further escalation by enabling NATO nations to potentially fire upon Russian aircraft in the area.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis > Ukraine–NATO relations
text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemns NATO for rejecting his appeal for a no-fly zone over his country, saying "All the people who die starting today will also die because of you. Because of your weakness, because of your disconnection".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis
text: Head of the Chechen Republic Ramzan Kadyrov calls on President Vladimir Putin to let his forces seize Ukraine's major cities, saying that it is the "only way to save the Russian people and our state".
By a unanimous vote, Ukraine becomes a contributor to NATO's Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence.

context: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Terrorism in Pakistan > 2022 Peshawar mosque attack
text: Islamic State gunmen and a suicide bomber kill at least 61 people and injure 196 others during Friday prayers at a Shia mosque in Peshawar, Pakistan.

context: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic > Economy of Brazil
text: The government announces that Brazil's economy has grown by 4.6%, the largest increase since 2011, after suffering a slump in 2020 due to the COVID-19 recession.
The Moscow Stock Exchange will extend its closure until at least March 8.
JPMorgan Chase warns that the current financial crisis in Russia might be similar or even greater in consequences than the 1998 crisis, when Russia defaulted on its obligations.
Yandex, the Russian equivalent of Google, announces that it might be heading for default.

Alphabet Inc., the parent company of Google, stops all sales of advertisements in Russia, following similar actions by Twitter and Snap Inc., as Russian regulators demand that the company stop showing "false political information" about Ukraine that they claim is misinforming the Russian public.
A wildfire occurs near the Hanul Nuclear Power Plant in Uljin County, South Korea, prompting authorities to issue a national emergency alert and evacuate residents from the area.
South Korean President Moon Jae-in orders an effort to protect the power plant amid wildfire concerns.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan > COVID-19 vaccination in Japan
text: Japan reaches 1 million booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 266,853 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland
text: President Michael D. Higgins and his wife Sabina test positive for COVID-19.
A red-breasted goose in the Jersey Zoo, Channel Islands, tests positive for H5N8 avian influenza.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin says that Russia is open to peace talks with Ukraine. However, he also urged Ukraine to meet Russian demands.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Media freedom in Russia
text: President Vladimir Putin signs amendments to the Criminal Code of Russia criminalising the spreading of falsehoods about Russian soldiers and the Russian Armed Forces, as well as calling for anti-Russian sanctions. According to the changes to the Criminal Code, spreading falsehoods about the Russian army will be punishable by 10–15 years of imprisonment, with the possibility of an additional fine of 700,000 to 1.5 million rubles (US$6,400–13,700) and up to three years of forced labour. The other two activities will carry a lesser punishment but all include possible imprisonment. The bill was previously accepted unanimously by the State Duma.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addresses anti-war protesters in cities across Europe.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Italian police seize the yacht of Russian oligarch Alexei Mordashov at the port of Imperia. Another yacht owned by Putin associate Gennady Timchenko is blocked at the port and is expected to be seized shortly. Both men have been sanctioned by the European Union.
A Turkish citizen wanted for the assassination of journalist Hrant Dink is detained in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.

context: 2021 Australian Parliament House sexual misconduct allegations
text: Minister for Education and Youth Alan Tudge, who temporarily stood down from his position last year after domestic abuse allegations were leveled against him by his former staffer and mistress, announces that he will be permanently resigning from the frontbench as a result of these allegations.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Arianespace and OneWeb suspend all future rocket launches from Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, and the use of Russian Soyuz rockets for their spacecraft.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian space agency Roscosmos ceases all joint scientific experiments on the International Space Station.

Russia blocks access to the websites of foreign government-sponsored corporations BBC News, Voice of America, Deutsche Welle and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty for spreading so-called "false information" about the "special military operation" in Ukraine. Russia also blocks access to Facebook and Twitter for the same reason.
The opening ceremony of the Winter Paralympics is held in Beijing.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: Russian and Ukrainian forces agree to open a humanitarian corridor for five hours for people who want to leave Mariupol and Volnovakha, expecting 200,000 people from Mariupol and 15,000 people from Volnovakha to use the corridor. However, the implementation of the corridor is postponed as the two parties accused each other of violating cease-fire agreement.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Head of the Donetsk People's Republic Denis Pushilin announces that Sparta Battalion Commander Volodymyr Zhoha has been killed in Volnovakha.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Chernihiv
text: A Russian Air Force warplane is shot down on the outskirts of Chernihiv, crashing into a residential area, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Chernihiv
text: A Russian Sukhoi Su-34 is shot down in Chernihiv Oblast and one of its pilots is taken prisoner by Ukrainian forces. The other pilot died.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive
text: Russian troops seize control of Borodianka in Kyiv Oblast after days of heavy shelling and airstrikes. Ukrainian authorities say that they were unable to evacuate a psychiatric hospital in the town which holds 670 patients. The hospital is now under Russian control.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv offensive
text: The Ukrainian military begins a mass evacuation of civilians from Irpin after the city was bombarded by Russian jets and artillery. Much of the city has now been destroyed.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Mykolaiv
text: Ukrainian Ground Forces retake control of Mykolaiv and seize Russian military equipment.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: The International Organization for Migration says that the refugee crisis has now become the largest and fastest exodus of people in Europe since World War II.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin says that Western sanctions on Russia are akin to a "declaration of war", and warns that any attempt to impose a no-fly zone over Ukraine could lead to "catastrophic consequences" for the world.
Russian President Putin says that around 13,000 to 14,000 people have been killed in Donbas since 2014.

context: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa > 2022 Peshawar mosque attack
text: The Islamic State claims responsibility for yesterday's massacre, which killed at least 61 people.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: South Korean electronics giant Samsung Electronics suspends all shipments to Russia due "to current geopolitical developments". Samsung is the largest supplier of smartphones in Russia with a 30% market share.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: PayPal suspends its services in Russia, citing "violent military aggression in Ukraine". Inditex also announces that it is closing all of its 502 stores in Russia, which employ about 9,000 people.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: Visa and Mastercard suspend operations in Russia following "Russia's unprovoked invasion of Ukraine". Visa says that it would cut off transactions "over the coming days", and that once a full ban is in place, bank cards issued in Russia will no longer work abroad.

context: Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian financial crisis
text: President Putin signs a decree authorising settlement of sovereign and corporate debts whose creditors come from "unfriendly countries" (whose list is to be determined within two days' time) to be made in rubles instead of foreign currencies, according to the exchange rate set by the Central Bank of Russia (CBR).
Aeroflot, Russia's flag carrier airline, announces that all flights to foreign destinations will be suspended as of March 8.

A tornado outbreak across the Midwestern United States kills six people from at least ten tornadoes, with the National Weather Service issuing multiple particularly dangerous situation (PDS) tornado warnings.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia
text: Malaysia reports a record for the second consecutive day of 33,406 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,595,172.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia will lift its COVID-19 restrictions, including PCR COVID-19 testing requirements, along with requirements for travelers to quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 216 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 8,796. The country also surpasses 4 million cases of COVID-19.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: The United Kingdom's Foreign Office advises British citizens to leave Russia immediately if their presence is "not essential", citing the "lack of available flight options to return to the UK", and the "increased volatility in the Russian economy".

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: Russian Foreign Affairs Spokesperson Maria Zakharova says that Russia will "not forget" British support for "Ukrainian ultra-nationalists", as well as the supply of British weapons to Kyiv, which are being used against Russian forces.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian negotiator Davyd Arakhamia announces that peace talks between Russia and Ukraine will resume on March 7.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Israel–Russia relations
text: Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss the invasion as well as a potential ceasefire with Ukraine. Bennett is the first world leader to meet with Putin in person since the invasion began.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyrgyzstan–Russia relations
text: Kyrgyzstan Foreign Minister Ruslan Kazakbayev expresses his support for any efforts to mediate a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.

context: Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis, International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Cyprus–Russia relations
text: Cyprus denies access for five Russian military vessels to enter its port in Limassol. Whether the military ships could enter Cypriot ports in the first place is controversial, as the international law background is unclear.
North Korea tests a ballistic missile in the Sea of Japan four days before the upcoming South Korean election. This is the ninth test conducted by North Korea this year.
Chinese Premier Li Keqiang reaffirms China's support for peaceful relations and reunification with Taiwan. However, he also calls for other countries to not engage in foreign interference.
Iranian officials reach an agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency to answer questions about their nuclear weapons program.
Baku, Azerbaijan, and Dushanbe, Tajikistan, become sister cities.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 anti-war protests in Russian-occupied Ukraine
text: Anti-war protesters gather in Kherson to protest Russia's occupation of the city.

context: International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Italian police seize luxury villas and yachts worth 143 million euros from five Russian oligarchs who have been sanctioned by the European Union.
During a Liga MX football match between Querétaro F.C. and Atlas F.C., a riot between fans breaks out.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > France–Russia relations
text: In a phone call with French president Emmanuel Macron, Russian president Vladimir Putin says that Russia will no longer attack nuclear power plants and is open to holding a trilateral meeting between Russia, Ukraine, and the International Atomic Energy Agency.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Havryshivka Vinnytsia International Airport in Vinnytsia Oblast has been "completely destroyed" after being hit with eight Russian ballistic missiles.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian military says that it has killed over 11,000 Russian troops since the invasion began, while Russian Defence Ministry spokesman Maj. Gen. Igor Konashenkov said on Wednesday that 498 Russian troops had been killed.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: U.S. officials claim that Russia has started recruiting Syrian mercenaries experienced in urban combat.
A militant attacks a marketplace in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, with a grenade, killing a man and injuring 24 others.
A 19-year-old Palestinian stabs an Israeli police officer in the Old City of Jerusalem. Police open fire on the attacker, killing him. One of the police is injured by friendly fire.
The Nigerien government confirms reports that five soldiers were killed on Friday by an improvised explosive device bombing in Torodi, Tillabéri Region.
Ukraine suspends all exports of rye, oat, buckwheat, millet, sugar, salt, and most meat and meat products that are fit for human consumption, as the country expects poor harvests and food shortages.

context: United States–Venezuela relations, 2021–2022 global energy crisis
text: The United States start talks with Venezuela about supplies of its oil, currently under sanctions, in an attempt to substitute the Russian crude. So far the talks yielded few results.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: The Chatham Islands near New Zealand reports its first case of COVID-19.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Enlargement of NATO > Ukraine–NATO relations
text: Ukrainian negotiator Davyd Arakhamia says that Ukraine is open to having non-NATO discussions in the future.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Turkey relations
text: Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan calls for Russian president Vladimir Putin to declare a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. Putin tells Erdoğan that he is ready for dialogue in an effort to end the war but also warns that any attempt to draw out negotiations could fail. He also calls for Ukraine to cease fighting in order for the military campaign to end.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Israel–Russia relations
text: Israeli prime minister Naftali Bennett says that his country will try to mediate a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia even if attempts are not successful.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia
text: Around 4,000 anti-war demonstrators are arrested during protests in cities across Russia that are aimed at opposing the invasion.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Kazakhstan will allow anti-war protests in the country amidst fears that the country could be sanctioned. Protesters gather in Almaty to protest Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

context: Protests against responses to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: A convoy of truckers inspired by the Canadian convoy protesters gather at the Capital Beltway in Washington, D.C. to call for all COVID-19 restrictions and mandates to be lifted.
North Korea says that it performed data transmission and other key tests to make a reconnaissance spy satellite. This comes a day after the country conducted a missile test.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: A Russian government directive is published ordering moving all government institutions and Internet service providers servicing them to switch to Russian DNS servers and (whenever possible and applicable) to the .ru domain zone as well as substitute all foreign-hosted Javascript code with equivalent code hosted onshore by March 11. Russian authorities, however, do not plan to cut off from the global Internet network themselves.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: The International Atomic Energy Agency confirms that the Kharkiv Institute of Physics and Technology in Kharkiv, which holds a neutron generator, has been destroyed by Russian shelling. The IAEA says that no radiation release has been detected from the facility, which housed a "small inventory of radioactive material".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Ukraine says that it has killed 41st Combined Arms Army general Vitaly Gerasimov, who allegedly took part in the annexation of Crimea, Russia's intervention in Syria, and the Second Chechen War, in the Kharkiv Oblast. He is the second general to be killed by Ukrainian forces after Andrey Sukhovetsky.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kherson offensive
text: Ukrainian Navy forces strike Russian Navy patrol boat Vasily Bykov with missiles in the Black Sea.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Russia and Ukraine set up another ceasefire in order to allow humanitarian evacuations in some cities.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Kremlin Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov says that Russia will end its military campaign if Ukraine ends its fighting campaign, does not join NATO, recognizes Crimea as Russian territory, and recognizes Donetsk and Luhansk as independent states.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Mali War
text: Two United Nations peacekeepers are killed in a bomb attack north of Mopti. Shortly before that, militants kill two Malian soldiers in Gao Region.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Mali War
text: French forces confirm reports that they killed Algerian-born senior al-Qaeda official Yahia Djouadi in a drone strike in February.
In cooperation with military officials, the Sudanese Rapid Support Forces raid an office investigating a commission that was set up to investigate the Khartoum massacre.
The price of Brent crude oil increases to $139.13 per barrel, the highest value since July 2008, amid supply disruptions and the threat of a Russian oil ban.

Metal markets register new highs. Aluminium and nickel register a record price on the London stock exchange, at about $4,000 and $55,000 per tonne, respectively; nickel prices rose 90% on intraday trading. Copper also recorded new highs, at $10,845 per tonne, while palladium reached $3,440 per ounce. Russia is a substantial producer of all of these metals, and the market expects shortages of these commodities as the country is hit by further sanctions.
One person dies and seven crew members are rescued after a fishing trawler capsizes in the North Sea while travelling to Norway, according to the Norwegian Coast Guard.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: New York City formally ends its mask mandate for its school district as well as its indoor vaccine mandate for restaurants, bars and theaters.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut
text: Connecticut reports 145 hospitalizations from COVID-19, its lowest since July 30 of last year.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium
text: Belgium removes most of its COVID-19-related restrictions, including lifting most of mask mandate and no longer requiring COVID Safe Tickets to enter most public places, after the country lowered its COVID-19 barometer from code orange to yellow.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China reports 526 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total in the country in two years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya
text: It is announced that Moderna will build a vaccine manufacturing facility in Kenya to produce mRNA vaccines, including its COVID-19 vaccine.
The number of deaths due to COVID-19 worldwide surpasses six million.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: The Russian and Ukrainian delegations hold a third round of talks at the Belarus–Poland border. During the talks, both countries say that they made limited progress on humanitarian corridors. However, no ceasefire was agreed to. A fourth round of talks will be held in the future.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: It is announced that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba will hold a tripartite meeting with Turkish Foreign Minister Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu in Ankara on Thursday. This will be the first Cabinet-level meeting between Russia and Ukraine since the invasion began.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–NATO relations
text: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán signs a decree allowing the deployment of NATO troops in western Hungary, and the transfer of lethal weapons across its territory to other NATO member states. However, the decree does not allow weapons shipments across its territory to Ukraine.

The United States Senate votes unanimously to pass the Emmett Till Antilynching Act, a bill that would make lynching a federal crime in the United States. The bill will head to President Joe Biden for his signature.
President of the Philippines Rodrigo Duterte approves a bill raising the age of consent in the Philippines from 12 to 16.
Belarus launched a widespread phishing attack against Polish and Ukrainian government and military officials. The attack has since been contained.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: The Albanian consulate in Kharkiv is destroyed during Russian shelling. No casualties are reported.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki reaffirms that the U.S. will not impose a no-fly zone over Ukraine.

A report from the Irish Times said that the United Nations told its employees in a communications guidance to refer to the war in Ukraine as a "conflict" or "military offensive" rather than as a "war" or an "invasion", and also ordered employees to not put the Ukrainian flag on any of their social media accounts to "avoid reputational risk", in an attempt to avoid upsetting Russia. However, Stéphane Dujarric, spokesman for the secretary-general of the United Nations, wrote in an email to The Guardian that no such recommendation was ever issued.

Bandits in Kebbi State attack a military convoy carrying the state's deputy governor, Dabai Yombe. He survives but 19 soldiers are killed. The convoy was making its way to Wasagu/Danko when the attack occurred.
Gunmen ambush a team of vigilantes in Kebbi State, killing a reported 62 people.

An Islamic State – Khorasan Province militant blows himself up in the city of Sibi, Balochistan, Pakistan. The attack kills five people and injures thirty. It may have been an assassination attempt on President Arif Alvi.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Biden administration bans imports of Russian oil, gas and coal to the United States. The United Kingdom also announces that it would phase out Russian oil by the end of the year.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Chinese officials indicate that they are interested in buying shares in recently-distressed Russian energy and minerals companies, seeking supply security. The negotiations, however, are still at an early stage.

Due to the panic buying of nickel futures, whose prices have increased above the $100,000 per tonne mark for the first time, and which doubled for the second consecutive day, the London Metal Exchange suspends all trading of nickel.
The death toll from the floods in Queensland and New South Wales increases to 20.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: New Zealand reports a record 23,894 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: In an interview with ABC News, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine is open to holding discussions about the Russia-recognized Donetsk and Luhansk separatist regions in eastern Ukraine. He also concedes that his country may no longer be prepared to be accepted into NATO.
U.S. President Joe Biden announces that Venezuela has freed two Americans, Gustavo Cardenas and Jorge Fernandez, after being detained in the country.

context: Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack > Criminal charges in the 2021 United States Capitol attack
text: Proud Boys leader Enrique Tarrio is indicted on conspiracy charges of obstructing the U.S. Congress during the January 6 attack at the United States Capitol.

The New York Times removes all its journalists from Russia, fearing arrests due to the recent changes to the Criminal Code of Russia penalizing "falsehoods" about the Russian Armed Forces or the country's invasion of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: A Russian airstrike destroys a maternity ward and a children's hospital in Mariupol, Ukraine, killing three people and injuring at least 17 people. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that many people are unaccounted for.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Ukrainian forces announce that they have regained control of Derhachi, a city located in the Kharkiv Raion district of the Kharkiv Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees says over two million Ukrainians have now fled the country since the invasion began. Most have gone to neighbouring Poland, with Hungary, Romania and Slovakia also taking in several hundred thousand refugees each.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Poland–United States relations
text: The Pentagon rejects an offer from Poland's foreign ministry to "deploy – immediately and free of charge – all their MIG-29 jets" to the Ramstein Air Base and place them at the disposal of the Government of the United States of America" for transfer to the Ukrainian Air Force.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The British Army confirms that a number of active-duty soldiers have disobeyed orders and gone AWOL, and have likely gone to Ukraine to fight against the Russian military. Defence Minister Ben Wallace says that the serving members are "breaking the law and will be prosecuted" when they return to the United Kingdom.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The United Kingdom's Defence Ministry says that it is sending another 1,615 MBT LAWs, and a small number of FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank missiles to the Ukrainian army. More small arms, body armour and medical supplies have also been sent.

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Fitch Ratings downgrades Russia from "B" to "C", one grade above default, and warns that Russian default on its obligations is "imminent".

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The Russian Ministry of Economic Development proposes a draft nationalisation bill that will impose receivership for up to 3 months on assets of companies that boycotted the Russian market due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine if the ownership share by legal entities from "unfriendly countries" exceeds 25%. If the companies still do not resume their business in the country, their assets will be auctioned. More than 300 companies that left Russia or suspended operations in Russia could be targeted.

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy signs a legislation banning the state from doing business dealings with Belarus and Russia.

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: John Deere announces that it will suspend shipments to Russia and Belarus following the invasion.

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Boycott of Russia and Belarus
text: American industrial conglomerate 3M suspends all business operations in Russia.

context: Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Chinese Foreign Ministry announces that China will provide 5 million yuan ($790,000) in humanitarian aid to Ukraine.

The Ukrainian state grid operator warns that Russian forces, which are in control of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, have disconnected the plant from the electricity grid, which the operator says will impact nuclear fuel cooling, and which also caused a blackout in the nearby city of Slavutych. The nuclear plant previously suspended all communications with the IAEA, the United Nations-based organisation specialising in nuclear energy production.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba says that reserve diesel generators that cool spent nuclear fuel can only last for another 48 hours and that a radiation leak from Chernobyl is "imminent" if power is not restored immediately. Kuleba also says that "Putin's barbaric war" puts all of Europe in danger. However, the International Atomic Energy Agency says there is "no critical impact on security" imminent.
Prime Minister Scott Morrison declares a national emergency in Australia in response to the ongoing floods in Australia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Austria
text: Austria suspends its universal COVID-19 vaccine mandate one week before fines of up to €3,600 were scheduled to take effect for those who did not comply with the mandate. The suspension of the mandate will be reviewed in three months.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania
text: Romania lifts all COVID-19-related restrictions including requiring a digital COVID pass to access institutions and the obligation to wear protective masks both indoors and outdoors.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea reports a record 342,446 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 Hours.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United States relations
text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov tells the United States to "await its response" to the "economic war" being waged against Russia.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: The UK bans all Russian aircraft from landing in its territory and travelling in its airspace, impounding a Russian oligarch-owned private jet at Farnborough Airport. The UK also bans all exports of aviation and space industry-related goods and services.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrives in Ankara, Turkey, for upcoming talks with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba.

context: Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–Ukraine relations
text: Ukrainian foreign policy aide Ihor Zhovkva says that Ukraine is open to holding talks discussing Russia's demand of Ukraine's neutrality as long as Ukraine is given security guarantees. However, Zhovkva warned that Ukraine will not give up any of its territories.
Preliminary results of the presidential election show a narrow victory for the conservative candidate Yoon Suk-yeol.
The wreck of Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance, which sank in 1915, has been located beneath the Weddell Sea.

context: 2022 Major League Baseball season > 2021–22 Major League Baseball lockout
text: Major League Baseball postpones opening day to April 14 after failing to reach a deal with the Major League Baseball Players Association.
