One person is killed and six others injured after an oil tanker explodes east of Hong Kong.
Russia's foreign ministry bans Prime Minister Boris Johnson, Foreign Secretary Liz Truss, and 11 other British senior politicians from entering Russia.

Japan's Ministry of Defense reports that it scrambled fighters to intercept foreign military aircraft 1,004 times in 2021, in 722 of these cases the foreign aircraft were from the People's Republic of China.
President of El Salvador Nayib Bukele announces that 12,169 gang members have been arrested since the state of emergency began on March 27.
A mass shooting at a shopping mall near Columbia, South Carolina, United States, injures 12 people.
Riots between Hindus and Muslims during a Hanuman Jayanti ceremony in Delhi, India, leave several people injured.
Rioting in Sweden continues for a second day after the far-right Hard Line party led by Rasmus Paludan organized a Quran burning event in Landskrona.

Chinese astronauts Ye Guangfu, Wang Yaping and Zhai Zhigang of the Shenzhou 13 spacecraft land successfully in Inner Mongolia after spending 183 days in space. During the spaceflight, Wang Yaping became the first Chinese woman to perform a spacewalk.

In American football, the United States Football League kicks off their inaugural season with the Birmingham Stallions defeating the New Jersey Generals 28–24, marking the return of the USFL for the first time since the 1985 season.
South Korean professional golfer Kim Hyo-joo wins the 2022 LPGA Lotte Championship.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: The Russian Armed Forces give an ultimatum to the last remaining holdout of Ukrainian troops and "foreign fighters" at the Azovstal iron and steel works plant in Mariupol to surrender. Defenders of the Azov Sea port ignore the ultimatum.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: For the first time since the invasion began, more Ukrainians entered Ukraine from Poland than left, according to the Polish Border Guard.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Six people are killed by Russian missile strikes on Lviv.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Jihadist insurgency in Niger
text: More than 70 Islamic State – West Africa Province militants are killed during airstrikes by Niger and Nigeria at the border between the two countries.

American conspiracy theorist website InfoWars files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy due to mounting legal fees from lawsuits over its spread of conspiracy theories about the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The government withdraws its ban on foreign cruise ships.

context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
text: North Korea says that it tested a new weapon to boost their tactical nuclear capabilities.
Two people are killed and 13 more injured in a mass shooting at a party in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.
Myanmar's military junta pardons 1,619 prisoners in an annual tradition. However, no political prisoners were pardoned.

Around 70 Extinction Rebellion members, including canoeist Etienne Stott and sailor Laura Baldwin, are detained after gluing themselves to a Shell oil tanker truck near the Marble Arch at Hyde Park in London, UK.
Citizen Lab's research reveals at least 65 pro-independence Catalan figures - including Pere Aragonès and Carles Puigdemont - have been targeted using NSO Group’s Pegasus spyware.

context: 2022 Nippon Professional Baseball season, Rōki Sasaki's perfect game
text: Chiba Lotte Marines pitcher Rōki Sasaki is taken out after throwing 102 pitches and eight perfect innings to end his attempt for a second consecutive perfect game, one week after completing his first one.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Russian troops capture the city of Kreminna in Luhansk Oblast. Local authorities say that four refugees have been shot dead trying to escape the city.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian defence ministry says that its forces have destroyed 16 Ukrainian military facilities, including five command posts, a fuel depot and three ammunition warehouses in "mass strikes" overnight. Russia also says that it shot down two Ukrainian MiG-29s and one Su-25.
Turkey launches a series of airstrikes on PKK targets in Duhok Governorate in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.
Two Palestinians are seriously injured after being shot by Israeli security forces in the West Bank. The Israel Defense Forces say that the Palestinians were attacking Israeli troops.
A jeep returning from a wedding crashes into another vehicle in Amethi district in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, killing six people and injuring four more.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Prime Minister Mario Draghi tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland
text: Scotland lifts their law mandating face coverings in shops, restaurants and public transport.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation
text: U.S. District Judge Kathryn Kimball Mizelle of the Middle District of Florida voids the Biden administration's mask mandate on airplanes and public transportation. Most U.S. airlines including Alaska Airlines and United Airlines subsequently end their mask mandates due to the ruling.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea ends their COVID-19 restrictions two years after they were imposed. However, the mask mandate will remain in place.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson
text: Igor Kastyukevich is appointed the de facto mayor of Kherson, the only Ukrainian Oblast capital captured during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

United States officials plan to travel to Solomon Islands due to concerns that the country is making a security pact with China. The U.S. fears the proposed agreement could lead to Chinese troops being deployed to Solomon Islands.
The Houthi movement signs an agreement to stop using child soldiers.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, Battle of Donbas > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Ukraine says that Russian forces have begun an anticipated military offensive in the Donbas with explosions reported in multiple cities.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, Battle of Donbas > War in Donbas
text: A civilian is killed and several others are injured by an explosion in Kramatorsk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, Battle of Donbas > Nuclear threats during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Amidst American allegations that Russia may use nuclear weapons, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov says that the country will not use them and will continue using conventional weapons.
The Iron Dome intercepts a Hamas missile fired into Israel's Southern District from the Gaza Strip.
Israel fires missiles at a Hamas weapon depot in Gaza in response to the Hamas attack. No injuries are reported.
At least 40 Palestinians are injured after the IDF fires tear gas and rubber bullets at Palestinians protesting a march held by right-wing settlers near the former settlement of Homesh.
At least six people are killed and many others are injured by a school bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan.
One person is killed and 14 others injured after police fire live bullets at protesters in Rambukkana.
A tractor collides with a military vehicle in South Darfur, Sudan, killing five people.

context: International reactions to the Russo-Ukrainian War > International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian foreign ministry expels 21 Belgian diplomats, 15 Dutch diplomats and 4 Austrian diplomats as a reciprocal measure.

context: International reactions to the Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Greece seizes Russian-flagged oil tanker Pegas/Lana off the island of Euboea as part of European Union economic sanctions on Russia. The ship had 19 crew members on board, according to the Ministry of Shipping.
Iranian president Ebrahim Raisi warns Israel that Iran will respond to any hostile action taken against it.
The foreign ministers of the People's Republic of China and Solomon Islands sign a security pact.
Jeune Afrique reports that on 12 April the defence ministers of Russia and Cameroon signed a new military cooperation agreement, renewing a similar agreement signed in 2015.
The East Timorese people head to the polls for the second round of the presidential election between José Ramos-Horta and incumbent Francisco Guterres.
The United States says it will ban anti-satellite missile tests.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: Ukrainian negotiator Mykhailo Podolyak says in a tweet that Ukraine is ready to hold a special round of negotiations in Mariupol in an effort "To save our guys, Azov (battalion), military, civilians, children, the living and the wounded".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: A 91-year-old Holocaust survivor is confirmed to have died on April 4, making her the second Holocaust survivor to be killed during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Presidential advisor Oleksiy Arestovych claims that Ukraine is blocking an attempted Russian advance on Sloviansk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Pentagon announces that Ukraine has received fighter aircraft and aircraft parts to bolster the Ukrainian Air Force. However, the number of aircraft sent or their origin are not disclosed.

context: Kashmir conflict > Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
text: A Railway Protection Force officer is killed and another is injured in an attack in Kakapora, Jammu and Kashmir, India.
The Israel Defence Forces launches airstrikes on targets in the Gaza Strip in retaliation for a previous rocket attack launched from Gaza.
Marches organized by ultranationalist Itamar Ben-Gvir in the Arab neighbourhood in the old city of Jerusalem are interrupted by Israeli police, leading to skirmishes between protesters and police.
Six soldiers are killed and five others are injured in a bombing in north-western Antioquia Department, Colombia. The Clan del Golfo is suspected to be behind the attack.
At least 20 people are killed and another 50 injured in clashes in the Amhara Region, Ethiopia.
Six people are killed and 19 others are injured by a bombing at a cattle market in Taraba State, eastern Nigeria. The attacker also died in the explosion. The Islamic State claims responsibility.
One person is killed and four others are injured when an IED blast hits a bus in Bursa, Marmara, Turkey.
Five people are killed and seven others remain trapped after a coal mine explosion in the Pniówek Coal Mine in Poland.
Twenty people are killed and at least one other is injured when a minibus collides with a vehicle in Bauchi State, Nigeria.
A small plane crashes into a street in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, killing six people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: New Delhi reinstates mandatory face mask wearing due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in the Indian capital.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Israel, Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's office announces that mandatory indoor mask-wearing will be lifted for the second time on April 23 at 8 p.m., pending approval from the Knesset Health Committee. However, mask wearing will still be mandatory in high-risk locations and by those who are in quarantine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports a record 2,386 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, all locally transmitted, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 40,186.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Norway > COVID-19 vaccination in Norway
text: The Norwegian Institute of Public Health announces that it has begun giving people over the age of 80 a second booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine.
The United States signs an agreement with Panama to help stop undocumented immigration.

Judge Paul Golspring of the Westminster Magistrates' Court refers to UK Home Secretary Priti Patel to sign an extradition order to the United States for Julian Assange in relation to WikiLeaks concerning human rights abuses in the Guantanamo detention camp and the Iraq war and the war in Afghanistan.
Two people are killed and three others are seriously injured after being hit in a hit and run incident in Cachar district, Assam, India.
An Iraqi Shia hacker group named the Altahrea Team launches major cyberattacks against numerous Israeli websites in retaliation for the assassination of Qasem Soleimani.

528 Rohingya refugees flee an immigration detention centre in Penang State, Malaysia, following a riot inside the building. Six people are killed after colliding with motorcyclists while crossing a road.
Former president José Ramos-Horta defeats incumbent president Francisco Guterres to become the next President of East Timor.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: Vladimir Putin tells his troops not to storm the Azovstal iron and steel works building in Mariupol, Donetsk Oblast, calling that plan "impractical" and instead ordering a blockade of the area.

context: Afghanistan conflict > Islamic State–Taliban conflict > 2022 Mazar-i-Sharif mosque bombing
text: Thirty-one people are killed and 87 others are injured in a bombing at a Shia mosque in Mazar-i-Sharif, Balkh Province. The Islamic State claims responsibility for the bombing.
Four people are killed and 18 others are injured during a bombing in Kunduz targeting the 217 Omari Corps.
Four Taliban members are killed and another is injured when their vehicle is hit by a roadside bomb in Nangarhar Province.
Boko Haram raid the town of Geidam, Yobe State, Nigeria, killing 12 people. Several buildings are destroyed, including a school.

The legislature for the U.S. state of Florida votes to strip Walt Disney World of its ability to self-govern by dissolving the Reedy Creek Improvement District, in apparent retaliation for Disney's actions during and following the passage of HB 1557, also known as the "Don't Say Gay" bill.
Six people are killed after a fire occurs at a defence research institute in Tver, Russia.
Iran arrests three alleged Israeli Mossad spies in Sistan and Baluchestan province, claiming that the spies are part of recent sensitive data leaks.

Maldivian President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih issues a presidential decree outlawing protests against India, claiming it is causing national instability and putting the security of Indian diplomats at risk.
Former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández is extradited to the United States on drug trafficking charges.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine offensive, Russian occupation of Kherson
text: Russian Major general Rustam Minnekayev says that the goal of the military operation is now to seize territory in Southern Ukraine in order to create a land corridor from Crimea to Ukraine's border with Transnistria, a pro-Russian unrecognized breakaway state that is internationally recognized as part of Moldova.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian refugee crisis
text: Ukraine says that it will not allow residents to evacuate Mariupol today over concerns that the route is too dangerous.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The mayor of Balakliia in Kharkiv Oblast is charged with treason by Ukrainian authorities for accepting aid from Russian occupation forces. The mayor is believed to have fled to Russia with his family.
At least 33 people are killed and 43 others are injured by a bombing at a Sufi mosque in Kunduz, Afghanistan.

At least 57 Palestinians are injured after Israeli police fire stun grenades and rubber bullets at a crowd of worshipers within the Al-Aqsa mosque compound in East Jerusalem, in response to stones and fireworks being thrown at Jewish worshipers.
Two rockets are launched into Israel from the Gaza Strip. One rocket lands in Sha'ar HaNegev and the other falls into the Beit Hanoun area, injuring one person.
A soldier and six rebels are killed in fighting in Jammu and Kashmir, India. Four members of the security forces are injured.

context: Somali Civil War > Pescatore Seafood Restaurant bombing
text: Six people are killed and seven others injured by an al-Shabaab suicide bomber at a restaurant on Lido Beach, Mogadishu.
The East African Community agree to set up a regional military force in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo in an attempt to end the conflicts there.
The Iranian Ministry of Industry, Mine and Trade bans the import of iPhones.
One person is killed and 14 others are injured after a magnitude 5.7 earthquake strikes Bosnia and Herzegovina.
One person is killed and two others are injured after a transport plane crashes in Zaporizhzhia (region), Ukraine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania > COVID-19 pandemic in Philadelphia
text: Philadelphia lifts their mask mandate days after reinstating it.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia > COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales, COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria
text: Public health restrictions are eased in New South Wales and Victoria.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China > COVID-19 pandemic in Shanghai
text: Authorities in Shanghai announce that they will tighten the enforcement of lockdown measures, as COVID-19 cases continue to increase in the city.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Samoa
text: Samoa reports five community spread COVID-19 cases on Manono Island, which had been free of the virus until now.

Japan and Russia sign an agreement on fishing quotas after a month of negotiations. The two countries agree on Japan's quota of 2,050 tons of salmon and trout within Russia's exclusive economic zone, which is the same level as last year, while Japan agrees to pay fees of between 200–300 million yen to Russia.
German authorities formally identify a suspect in the 2007 disappearance of a British three-year-old girl in Portugal.
France issues an international arrest warrant for former Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 bombing of Odesa
text: Infrastructure in the Southern Ukrainian city of Odesa is hit by airstrikes, killing at least five people, including a baby, and injuring 18 others, according to the local authorities.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Investigative Committee of Russia announces that they are investigating allegations by RIA Novosti that troops from the British SAS have been deployed to Western Ukraine.
Human rights groups say that eight people were killed during clashes followed by a Janjaweed raid on Thursday and Friday in Kreinik, West Darfur.

context: 2021–2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks, Ituri conflict, Kivu conflict
text: Kenya says that the East African Community plans to deploy a peacekeeping force in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Unknown gunmen from Afghanistan storm a Pakistani military outpost near the border in Pakistan’s North Waziristan District, killing three soldiers.
Over 100 people are killed after an illegal oil refining depot explodes in Ohaji/Egbema, Imo State, Nigeria.
At least 17 migrants are killed after four boats sink off the coast of Sfax, Tunisia.
Three people are killed and 98 more are rescued after an explosion at the Gaisky ore mine in Orenburg, Russia.
Ten people are dead and 16 more are missing as a sightseeing boat sinks off Japan's northern island of Hokkaido.
Four people are dead and six more are missing after an accident in a coal mine in Jastrzębie-Zdrój, Poland.
One person dies and 40 people are rescued after a boat sinks in Tripoli, Lebanon.
Turkey closes its airspace to Russian Armed Forces flights to Syria, as well as civilian aircraft that are suspected of carrying Russian troops.

Thousands of Argentinian farmers protest against President Alberto Fernández's new export taxes on farm goods, which protesters say is a "rope that is being used to choke us". The farmers used tractors to block the road leading to the Casa Rosada in Buenos Aires.
In baseball, the Chicago Cubs defeat the Pittsburgh Pirates, 21–0, the largest defeat in Pirates history and the largest victory in Cubs history since 1901.

Tyson Fury retains the WBC world heavyweight title after defeating Dillian Whyte via technical knockout in round 6 in front of 94,000 spectators at Wembley Stadium, London, a post-war British record. Post-match, Fury suggests that he may now retire from professional boxing.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian authorities claim that a person has been killed by overnight shelling in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian state media reports that Ukraine has launched rockets into a village in Belgorod Oblast, Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Swiss Federal Department of Economic Affairs vetoes Germany's request to re-export Swiss ammunition to Ukraine on the basis of Switzerland's neutrality.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken and Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin arrive in Ukraine and meet with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. In the highest-level American visit in Kyiv since the beginning of the Russian invasion, Zelenskyy is informed of the approved new military assistance for Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian embassy in Tehran denies that Iran is a secret armament supplier for the Russian war effort.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Mali War
text: Six soldiers are killed and twenty others are injured after attacks on three military bases in Mopti and Ségou regions, Mali.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso
text: Jihadist attacks on military posts in Soum Province, Burkina Faso, kill nine soldiers and six civilians, and injure around 30 others.

context: Internal conflict in Myanmar > 2021–2022 Myanmar insurgency
text: It is reported that family members of the ruling military junta in the city of Yangon are seeking refuge in the country's capital Naypyidaw as urban fighting intensifies between soldiers and insurgents.
At least 168 people are killed and 98 others injured during a three-day clash between Arabs and non-Arabs in West Darfur, Sudan.

Honduran President Xiomara Castro declares a state of emergency in the Colón Department following the death of three policemen in an ambush in Trujillo. The announced objective is to apprehend the perpetrators.
The second round of the French presidential election between Emmanuel Macron and Marine Le Pen takes place.

Exit polls show Emmanuel Macron winning the French presidential election with a majority of 58% of votes. Macron becomes the first incumbent President to win re-election since Jacques Chirac's victory in the 2002 French presidential election against Jean-Marie Le Pen, Marine Le Pen's father.

Le Pen concedes defeat to Macron, ensuring him a second term. However, she says that the results are nonetheless a significant improvement from the previous election and therefore a victory for her party.
Slovenes head to the polls to elect members of their Parliament.
Exit polls show Robert Golob's green Freedom Movement winning 35.8% of the vote over incumbent Prime Minister Janez Janša's right-wing populist Slovenian Democratic Party.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > April 2022 Belgorod and Bryansk attacks
text: Two large fires occur at an oil refinery and a military depot in Bryansk, Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: Kherson mayor Ihor Kolykhaiev announces that Russian forces have taken control of the Kherson City Council.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: According to Ukraine, Russian missile strikes hit numerous train stations across Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A person is killed after Russia bombs the Kremenchuk Oil Refinery in Kremenchuk, Poltava Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Regional authorities say that five people have been killed by airstrikes on Zhmerynka and Koziatyn, Vinnytsia Oblast.
The office of the Transnistrian Ministry of State Security in Tiraspol is attacked with grenade launchers. There is damage reported to the building, but there are no reports of casualties.

context: List of rocket attacks from Lebanon on Israel
text: A rocket is fired from Lebanon into Matzuva, Israel. Israel responds by firing at targets in Lebanon.
A limestone statue of the Canaanite goddess Anat from 2,500 BC is found in the Gaza Strip.

context: Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk
text: Elon Musk reaches an agreement to buy Twitter for $44 billion.
A landslide has left at least 2 dead and 9 injured in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China > COVID-19 pandemic in Beijing
text: Authorities in Beijing begin COVID-19 testing for millions of residents after a recent increase in COVID-19 cases.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 drug development
text: The U.S. FDA formally approves the Gilead Sciences drug Remdesivir, commonly known as Veklury, for young children with COVID-19.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Germany–Russia relations
text: Russia's foreign ministry expels 40 German diplomatic staff in a retaliatory move after Germany expelled the same number of Russian diplomats.
Former Iranian MP Ali Motahari says the Iranian nuclear program initially aimed for a secret nuclear weapon and nuclear deterrence.
Four people are killed during a mass stabbing at a house in Bermondsey, London, United Kingdom.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United Kingdom's Armed Forces Secretary James Heappey says that Ukraine can strike targets inside Russia with British weapons, saying that it is "completely legitimate" in order to disrupt attacks on Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Russian Defence Ministry accuses the UK of "provoking Ukraine" into attacking Russian territory, and warns of a "proportional response" should any attacks occur.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Germany announces the delivery of 50 ex-Bundeswehr Gepard anti-air tanks to Ukraine, the first heavy weaponry supplied by Germany since the start of the invasion.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres visits Moscow in order to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Before the meeting, Guterres calls for a ceasefire to end the war.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: President Putin says that Russia and Ukraine are continuing ceasefire talks online.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Russian missile strike destroys a strategic bridge across the Dniester Estuary in Odesa Oblast, according to Ukrainian authorities.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov says that weapons supplied to Ukraine "will be a legitimate target for Russia's military" and further stating "storage facilities in western Ukraine have been targeted". Lavrov also stated that "NATO, in essence, is engaged in a war with Russia through a proxy and is arming that proxy. War means war."

Moldova's Supreme Security Council convenes an emergency meeting after yesterday's attacks in the breakaway Transnistria. President Maia Sandu says that the attacks were aimed at "destabilising the situation in the region", and also says that the military will improve combat readiness and increase patrols on the border with Transnistria.

context: Insurgency in Balochistan > 2022 University of Karachi bombing
text: Three Chinese citizens and their Pakistani driver are killed and four others are injured when a Balochistan Liberation Army suicide bomber blows herself up near their van in Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan.
Gunmen open fire at a police station in Karimama, Benin, killing one officer and wounding several more.

context: Russia in the European energy sector > 2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute
text: Gazprom announces that it will stop delivering natural gas to Poland via the Yamal–Europe pipeline and to Bulgaria as both countries rejected Russia's demand to pay for the fossil fuel supply in Russian rubles. Poland does not expect to experience disruptions from the suspension of natural gas deliveries. However, the suspension of Russian gas deliveries to Bulgaria "poses a serious challenge to the security of supply to the country" as Bulgaria is almost completely dependent on Russian gas.
A person is killed and 24 are missing after a migrant vessel crashes off the coast of Spain's Canary Islands.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.
text: Vice President Kamala Harris tests positive for COVID-19.
A staff member and two children are killed, and another staff member is injured in a shooting at a kindergarten in Veshkayma, Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia. The gunman later kills himself.
Twenty Islamic worshippers are killed during riots in Gondar, Amhara Region, Ethiopia.
In the morning, the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are seen aligning with each other.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: In a statement, Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova says that "Russia can strike military targets on the territory of those NATO countries that supply arms to the Kiev regime" and "As far as I understand, Britain is one of those countries."

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: British Deputy Prime Minister Dominic Raab says that Russian threats to target Britain are "unlawful" and are only adding to the "pariah status" of Vladimir Putin's regime.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: UK Foreign Secretary Liz Truss states that Russian forces must be pushed out of "the whole of Ukraine" including territory Russia captured eight years ago, in what the BBC describes as "the clearest statement yet of Britain's war aims".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine offensive, Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: The Ukrainian Air Force strikes the Kherson TV Tower with a missile temporarily forcing Russian television off-air in the occupied Kherson Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that it has struck 59 Ukrainian weapon facilities during the night, including a depot in Zaporizhzhia Oblast which is being used to store weapons from the United States and Europe.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that its air defences have shot down a Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicle over the Kursk Oblast, while several explosions and a fire at an ammunition depot are reported in Belgorod Oblast. Ukraine describes the explosions in Russia as "payback" and "karma" for Moscow's invasion.

context: Transnistria conflict > 2022 Transnistria attacks, 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Transnistrian authorities say that several UAVs originating from the direction of Ukraine have been spotted near the Cobasna ammunition depot. However, this claim cannot be independently verified.

context: Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Four Syrian soldiers are killed during airstrikes in Damascus launched by Israel at an Iranian-linked ammunition depot.

An armed Palestinian teenager is killed and three more are injured as Israeli soldiers raid a refugee camp in Jenin in an operation to arrest suspects involved in prior terror attacks in Israel. Fifteen others are arrested during raids in other parts of the West Bank.
The 27-foot Soviet-era bronze statue under the People's Friendship Arch in Kyiv, representing Russian–Ukrainian friendship, is removed by order of Mayor of Kyiv Vitali Klitschko.

Prince Andrew, Duke of York is stripped of his Freedom of the City of York following an unanimous vote by city councillors. The council also calls on the Prince to relinquish his title as Duke of York.

context: Russia in the European energy sector > 2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute
text: Gazprom announces that it has "completely suspended gas supplies" to the gas companies of Poland and Bulgaria "due to [the] absence of payments in roubles". Bulgaria, Poland, and the European Union condemn the suspension.

context: Russia in the European energy sector > 2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute
text: The suspension of gas to Poland and Bulgaria causes natural gas prices to increase and also causes the Russian ruble to reach a 2 year high against the Euro in Moscow trade.

The European Commission proposes lifting all tariffs for Ukrainian produce not covered by the European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement for one year, while easing trade conditions for other goods. The temporary suspension will need to be approved by the European Parliament and the member states.
The Central African Republic adopts bitcoin as legal tender, after its legislature unanimously approved the law.

The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, servicing most of Greater Los Angeles, declares a water shortage emergency and requires agencies to enforce restrictions on non-essential water usage as of June 1. This comes amid a drought which worsened as the 2021–22 California winter season was the driest on record.

A chariot in a Hindu religious procession strikes an overhead power line leading to several electrocutions and a fire resulting in eleven deaths and over a dozen injuries in Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, India.
Five people are killed in a traffic collision in Armstrong County, Texas.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Russia–United Kingdom relations
text: Russia imposes sanctions on 287 members of the House of Commons of the United Kingdom in response to sanctions on members of its State Duma. Senior cabinet ministers and House Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle are among those sanctioned.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia announces its withdrawal from the World Tourism Organization ahead of a vote on its suspension from the UN specialized agency.
American Marine Trevor Reed and Russian pilot Konstantin Yaroshenko are freed in a prisoner exchange between Russia and the United States.
Three people are killed in a mass shooting in Biloxi, Mississippi. The shooter is later killed in a standoff with police.

The Peruvian government declares a state of emergency at Las Bambas copper mine after a week of camping by indigenous people. The government suspends civil liberties, including the right of assembly and protest.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: Oleksandr Kobets is appointed as the de facto mayor of the city of Kherson, which has been occupied by Russian forces since March 2.

The World Meteorological Organization announces that Hurricane Ida will be retired from the list of Atlantic hurricane names after causing $75 billion in damage in the U.S. and killing 55 people in Louisiana, making Ida the 12th hurricane beginning with the letter I to do so. Ida will be replaced by Imani for the 2027 season.
Bulgaria calls on its citizens to leave Moldova immediately by "any available means of transport" due to the "complicating situation" in the country, and warns against any travel there.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Two major explosions hit Kyiv after Russia conducts missile strikes during a high-level visit to the city by UN Secretary-General António Guterres. At least ten civilians are injured and a Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty journalist is killed.

context: Syrian civil war > Abu Khashab shooting
text: Seven people are killed and four more are injured inside the home of a former Syrian Democratic Forces official in Abu Khashab, Deir ez-Zor Governorate, during the Ramadan iftar. The Islamic State is suspected to be behind the attack.
Nine people are killed and 13 others are injured after two bombs explode on a pair of Shia-majority buses in Mazar-i-Sharif, Balkh Province.
Twelve trucks are set on fire in the Araucanía Region of Chile, most likely by Mapuche protesters.
A bridge collapses in Loay, Bohol, Philippines, killing four people and injuring 23 others.
Two possibly intentional explosions are heard in southern Belgorod, Russia.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: Moderna requests emergency use authorization for its COVID-19 vaccine in babies, toddlers, and young children.
Joshua Jacques, who is suspected of committing a mass stabbing in Bermondsey, London, United Kingdom, on Monday, is charged with four counts of murder.
Georgia becomes the ninth U.S. state to ban the teaching of critical race theory in schools.
Dritan Abazović is elected by the Parliament of Montenegro as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Zdravko Krivokapić, who was ousted by a motion of censure on 4 February.
A small meteor travelling at an estimated 55,000 mph (88,514 km/h) explodes above western Mississippi, United States, causing several sonic booms.
In American football, the NFL Draft is held in Las Vegas, with the Jacksonville Jaguars selecting former Georgia Bulldogs defensive end Travon Walker with the first overall-pick.

Forty-two Palestinians are injured as the Israeli police storm the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem in response to crowds within the mosque throwing rocks and fireworks in the direction of Jewish worshippers at the Western Wall.
An Israeli security guard in the Ariel settlement is shot dead in what is suspected to be a militant attack.

context: Afghanistan conflict > April 2022 Kabul mosque bombing
text: Ten people are killed and 15 others are injured when a mosque is bombed in Kabul, Afghanistan.
Six soldiers and four Coalition of Patriots for Change rebels are killed during a shootout at a military outpost in Bakouma, Central African Republic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Russia
text: The number of COVID-19-related deaths in Russia surpasses 800,000.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: The South Korean government announces that it will lift outdoor mask mandate from May 2 due to decrease of the number of COVID-19 cases, despite criticism from the incoming Yoon Suk-yeol administration regarding the mandate.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports a record for the second consecutive day of 11,517 new COVID-19 cases.
India's weather department issues a severe heat wave warning as temperatures rapidly increase across the country.

Russian President Vladimir Putin accepts an invitation to the upcoming G20 summit in Bali, Indonesia, despite Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is also invited to the summit.
The premier of the British Virgin Islands, Andrew Fahie, is arrested for alleged drug smuggling and money laundering in the United States.
British MP Neil Parish is being investigated by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards after two MPs allegedly claimed that Parish was watching pornography in the House of Commons.

A high court in Malawi convicts five people of killing an albino man and seven more people of selling the man's body parts. The body parts are desired by some local residents, who believe that they can bring luck and wealth.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian War > April 2022 Belgorod and Bryansk attacks
text: Governor of Kursk Oblast Roman Starovoyt says that shells have been launched at a border checkpoint from the direction of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Around 20 civilians have left the steel plant, a deputy commander of the Azov Battalion says.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov says that sanctions must be lifted as part of the peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia.
At least one person is killed and three others injured when a van explodes in Kabul, Afghanistan.
A natural gas pipeline is blown up in Bir al-Abd, North Sinai, Egypt, by suspected jihadist militants.
A plane carrying four people crashes in Sioux Lookout, Ontario, Canada, killing everyone on board.
A tornado strikes Andover, Kansas, United States, inflicting heavy damage. As part of the same weather system, three storm chasers are killed in a car accident due to aquaplaning.
Five people are rescued and dozens of others remain trapped after a building collapses in Changsha, China.
A tricycle falls into a man-made channel in Itay El Barud, Egypt. Eight children die and four people are rescued.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: It is announced that Beijing residents must show proof of a negative COVID-19 test in order to enter public spaces as part of a major tightening of restrictions in the Chinese capital.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports a record for the third consecutive day of 15,419 new COVID-19 cases.
Hamas warns that, if another attempt to storm the al-Aqsa Mosque is made by Israel, war could break out.

In association football, Real Madrid wins a record 35th La Liga title, following a 4–0 victory over Espanyol. Manager Carlo Ancelotti becomes the first manager to win titles in all of Europe's top five leagues.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: Some civilian evacuations begin from the Azovstal iron and steel works in Mariupol. Officials believe that up to 1,000 people have sought refuge at the plant, which has been the target of Russian airstrikes for days. However, evacuations are suspended until 8 a.m. tomorrow due to "security concerns".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Five people are killed by Russian shelling in the town of Lyman.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > April 2022 Belgorod and Bryansk attacks
text: A fire reportedly occurs at a military facility in Belgorod Oblast, Russia, slightly injuring one person and damaging seven houses.
Ukrainian intelligence officials report that Russia is poised to launch a second front from the breakaway area of Transnistria in order to take over the rest of Moldova.
The Islamic State claims via the Al-Naba newspaper that Israel killed a senior jihadist commander in the Egyptian Sinai Peninsula.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Germany–Russia relations
text: German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock says that Germany may lift sanctions against Russia if they completely withdraw their troops from Ukraine.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Hungary, a member of the European Union, says that it will veto any sanctions that would restrict energy imports from Russia. Unanimity among the 27 EU members is required to introduce sanctions.
Two people are killed and another person is missing after heavy flooding in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
text: The Greek Civil Aviation announces that Greece has lifted their COVID-19 restrictions for domestic and foreign flights. Passengers will still be required to wear a mask.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Europe > COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
text: Italy removes their Green Pass for all indoor places except hospitals and nursing homes and lifts their COVID-19 vaccination and mask mandate for museums, bars, hotels, and restaurants. However, masks will still be required for public transport until June 15.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: May Day anti-war rallies are held across the world to call for peace in Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine offensive > 2022 bombing of Odesa
text: A Russian missile hits a dormitory in Odesa, killing a 14-year-old boy and wounding a 17-year-old girl, according to Ukrainian officials. An Orthodox Church was also damaged in the missile strike.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: The resumption of civilian evacuations from the Azovstal steel mill which was expected to begin at 8 a.m. local time does not occur, as Russia begins a non-stop barrage of airstrikes and bombings following the departure of Red Cross personnel, who had left the previous day after the evacuations were suspended.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: Five Russian troops are allegedly killed during a supposed incursion into the steel plant.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belgorod and Bryansk attacks
text: Explosions are reported in the city of Belgorod, Belgorod Oblast, Russia. Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov states that "there were no casualties or damage".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Ukrainian Air Force Bayraktar TB2 drone destroys two Russian Raptor-class patrol boats near Snake Island in the Black Sea.
Residents of Las Vegas, New Mexico, and surrounding communities evacuate as the Calf Canyon/Hermits Peak Fire continues to spread.
Eight people are killed by a building collapse in Lagos, Nigeria.
Eight people are killed after a fire engulfed a residential area on the state university campus in Metro Manila, Philippines.

Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council Secretary Oleksiy Danilov accuses Hungary of having advance knowledge of the Russian invasion, saying that Hungary was warned by Russian President Vladimir Putin, and that Hungary had plans to annex parts of Western Ukraine.

context: Abortion in the United States > Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
text: A draft opinion leaked to Politico indicates that the U.S. Supreme Court is set to overturn Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey.
Spanish authorities announce that Pegasus spyware was found on the cell phones of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Minister of Defense Margarita Robles.
It is announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin will reportedly undergo cancer surgery and temporarily hand power to Russian Security Council Secretary Nikolai Patrushev.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Governor of Donetsk Oblast Pavlo Kyrylenko says that nine people have been killed by Russian shelling in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Ten people are killed after projectiles hit a coking plant in Avdiivka, Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: The United Nations says that 127 people have been evacuated from the besieged Azovstal plant and nearby areas.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin tells French President Emmanuel Macron that his country is ready to continue peace negotiations with Ukraine amidst fears that talks between the two countries have stalled.
At least 30 Burundian peacekeepers are killed and 20 more injured during an al-Shabaab attack at an African Union military base in Lower Shabelle, Somalia.
Seven people are killed as Islamist insurgents attack a village in Chibok, Borno State, Nigeria.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian debt default
text: Russia avoids default on the dollar-denominated bonds that were due in April by sending dollars to foreign investors just before the grace period expired.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > International sanctions during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: President Vladimir Putin signs a decree that will allow the Russian government to terminate any business and exports with entities and people that it deems "unfriendly".

Based on its preliminary findings, the European Commission accuses Apple of violating the EU's competition law by blocking its competitors from accessing the technology used for the Apple Pay service, and threatens to fine the company up to 10% of its global revenue.
American bank Citigroup says that the flash crash that affected several European stock markets yesterday was caused by an error from one of its traders.
Two people are confirmed to have been killed when a building in Changsha, China, collapsed on April 29.

context: Abortion in the United States > Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization > 2022 abortion protests in the United States
text: Demonstrations are held outside the U.S. Supreme Court Building in response to last night's leak of the draft opinion.

context: Abortion in the United States > Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization > 2022 abortion protests in the United States
text: In California, an anti-abortion activist is detained by the San Francisco Police Department after climbing to the top of the 61-story Salesforce Tower.

context: Abortion in the United States > Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
text: The U.S. Supreme Court confirms the authenticity of the draft opinion indicating that the court would overturn Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey. Chief Justice John Roberts condemns the leak and says that an investigation into the leak will be launched.

context: Abortion in the United States > Abortion in Oklahoma
text: Governor Kevin Stitt signs a heartbeat bill, i.e. a bill banning abortion after a heartbeat in a fetus is detected, which is at the age of about 6 weeks (except in cases of medical emergencies) and also adopts Texas-style enforcement to pursue offenders. The bill takes effect immediately.
Carlos Guillén Tatis, the agriculture counselor at the Dominican Republic's embassy in Haiti, is kidnapped in Croix-des-Bouquets, Haiti.

The European Parliament votes in favour of an election law overhaul, to be confirmed and possibly amended by the European Council, that will create a 28-seat pan-EU constituency and introduce elections of the President of the European Commission by popular vote. The reform will also create the European Electoral Authority, introduce postal voting for all EU residents, lower the minimum age of candidates to 18 and fix elections on Europe Day, May 9.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: The Associated Press confirms that approximately 600 people died in the Mariupol theatre airstrike.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: Russian forces bombard the Azovstal steel works plant in Mariupol with thermobaric missiles. Mariupol mayor Vadym Boychenko confirms that contact has been lost with Ukrainian soldiers trapped inside the plant.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: Ukraine confirms that Russian troops have entered the steel works plant after launching "an all-out assault".

Finland says that a Russian Air Force Mi-17 violated its airspace this morning, flying "four to five kilometres" inside Finnish airspace. The incursion comes ahead of an expected Finnish application to join NATO.

context: International sanctions during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The European Union proposes to ban all oil imports from Russia by the end of the year, and also remove Russia's biggest bank, Sberbank, from SWIFT.
The United States Federal Reserve announces that it is raising interest rates by 0.5%, which is the largest interest rate hike since 2000, in order to combat growing inflation.
Twenty-six people are killed when a minibus, a bus and a fuel truck collide with each other in Rivne Oblast, Ukraine.
Twenty people are killed when a bus crashes into a tea estate in Fort Portal, Uganda.
South Korea and the Japan Coast Guard both accuse North Korea of firing a ballistic missile from Sunan-guyok into the Sea of Japan.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive > Siege of Mariupol
text: Ukrainian forces say they have repelled a Russian military thrust onto the Azovstal iron and steel works in Mariupol, Ukraine.
Three people are killed and four others injured by two Palestinians in a mass stabbing in El'ad, Central Israel.
The death toll from the building collapse in Changsha, China, six days ago, increases to 53, with ten people rescued.
Floods in twelve provinces of Afghanistan destroy 500 homes, kill 22 people and injure 40 others.
WHO puts estimate of deaths due to COVID-19, including incidentals due to impacted health systems, at approximately 15 million worldwide.
Seattle Sounders FC becomes the first US Major League Soccer team to win the CONCACAF Champions League, defeating UNAM 5–2 on aggregate in the final.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine is open to continue peace talks with Russia if they guarantee the restoration of preinvasion borders, return the Ukrainians who were forcefully evacuated to Russia, and if Russian troops withdraw from the country.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian MP Oleksiy Goncharenko claims that the Russian frigate Admiral Makarov was struck with Neptune anti-ship missiles off of Snake Island. Russia denies having any information of the strike.
Eleven people are killed and nine others are injured in Islamist attacks in Loroum and Sanmatenga provinces, Burkina Faso. Twenty attackers are also killed.

context: Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk
text: The Orlando Police Pension Fund files a class-action lawsuit in the Delaware Chancery Court against Twitter Inc and Elon Musk, seeking to delay the acquisition of Twitter to 2025.
At least 26 people are killed and at least 74 others are injured by an explosion caused by a suspected gas leak at the Hotel Saratoga in Havana, Cuba.
Two people die and over 100 more are rescued as a boat carrying migrants runs aground in southern Italy.
Two people are killed and eighteen others are injured when an explosion occurs in a residential building in Madrid, Spain.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia
text: COVID-19 vaccination in Colombia

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia
text: Colombia announces that it will offer a second COVID-19 vaccine boosters for people aged above 50 years. It comes after the country reached its target for fully vaccinate 70% of population.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China decides to making regular COVID-19 testing mandatory for its citizens with setting up thousands of permanent PCR testing stations, with 9,000 already completed in Shanghai alone, as authorities aim to "normalise" tough pandemic controls even after the current round of lockdowns end.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports a record 30,035 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, which is the first time the country has reported more than 30,000 cases since the pandemic began.

Iran detains a Swedish man who was travelling as a tourist, allegedly in response to Sweden prosecuting Hamid Nouri, an Iranian official considered to be responsible for the mass killings of political prisoners in 1988.
The U.S. Senate passes 62–33 a non-binding resolution barring the Biden administration from removing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from its list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations.

Two people are killed and three others are injured during a mass shooting at a care home in Molensingel, Alblasserdam, Netherlands. The perpetrator was already wanted for murdering a man at a shop yesterday.

Sofia Sapega, the girlfriend of Belarusian activist Roman Protasevich, with whom she was detained when their flight was diverted by the Belarusian Air Force last year, is sentenced to six years in prison for "inciting social hatred". The exiled Belarusian opposition condemns the verdict.
The Sri Lankan government declares a state of emergency in response to massive anti-government protests.
NHL commissioner Gary Bettman says that Russian players will remain eligible for the upcoming NHL Draft despite other clubs banning Russian athletes.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 bombing of Odesa
text: Four Russian missiles strike the Ukrainian port city of Odesa.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Siege of Mariupol
text: Ukraine says that all women, children, and elderly have been evacuated from the besieged Azovstal steel plant.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Bilohorivka school bombing
text: Russian forces bomb a school in Bilohorivka, Sievierodonetsk Raion, Luhansk Oblast. Only two deaths are confirmed but sixty people are believed to have been killed.
Two colonels, two soldiers and four al-Qaeda insurgents are killed during clashes in Dhale Governorate, Yemen.
Ten soldiers and one officer are killed during an attack at a checkpoint at a water pumping station in the Suez Canal, Egypt.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Airline Operators of Nigeria announces that all of their airlines will suspend their domestic flights beginning on Monday, in protest of rising fuel prices caused by the war in Ukraine.

Eight people are killed and 17 others injured during wildfires in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Siberia, Russia, that destroy hundreds of buildings in 16 settlements. The Federal Agency for Forestry blames high winds for worsening the fires and impacting firefighting efforts.
Three people are injured in an explosion at a steel coke plant in Jharkhand, India.
Four Vietnamese nationals are killed when a fire breaks out at Bismark House Mill in Oldham

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports a record 46,536 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, which is the first time the country has reported more than 40,000 cases since the beginning of the pandemic.
The monkeypox virus is detected in a person who recently travelled to England from Nigeria.

context: Treatment of women by the Taliban
text: The Taliban passes a law ordering all women in Afghanistan to cover their faces in public with a burqa.
Iran preemptively shuts down the internet in Khuzestan province amid protests against a 200% increase in bread prices.
One person is killed and six others injured in a mass shooting in Cancún, Quintana Roo, Mexico.

Irish republican party Sinn Féin win the most seats in the Northern Ireland Assembly with 29% of the first-preference vote, marking the first time that a unionist party did not win the most seats since Northern Ireland's establishment in 1921.

Former president of Brazil Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announces his candidacy for the upcoming Brazilian presidential election in October, launching his candidacy with a message of "hope" and stating that he is ready to make "the greatest peaceful revolution" in the history of Brazil.

The 148th Kentucky Derby is held in Louisville, Kentucky with a full capacity for the first time since 2019 after two years of COVID-19 capacity restrictions. American thoroughbred Rich Strike wins the Derby in one of the largest upsets in history with an 80–1 odds to win.

Two Palestinians are killed by Israeli soldiers during confrontations in the West Bank, while an Israeli policeman is stabbed and wounded in Jerusalem, hours after the perpetrators of the El'ad stabbing are arrested.

context: Ituri conflict, 2021–2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: Thirty-five civilians are killed during an attack on a gold mine by CODECO rebels in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

context: Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Canada–Ukraine relations
text: Prime Minister of Canada Justin Trudeau, Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland and Minister of Foreign Affairs Mélanie Joly make an unannounced visit to Kyiv to meet with President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy amid the ongoing Russian invasion.

context: Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Canada–Ukraine relations
text: Trudeau announces the reopening of the Canadian Embassy in Kyiv.

context: Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukraine–United States relations
text: U.S. First Lady Jill Biden makes an unannounced visit to Uzhhorod, Ukraine, and holds a Mother’s Day meeting with Ukrainian First Lady Olena Zelenska.

context: European Union–United States relations, Iran–United States relations
text: The European Union recommends that the United States remove the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps from their terrorist organization blacklist.

context: 2022 abortion rights protests in the United States
text: The office of Wisconsin Family Action, an anti-abortion group in Madison, Wisconsin, catches fire and is looted. Police discover a molotov cocktail and begin an arson investigation.
John Lee is elected as the 5th Chief Executive of Hong Kong.
Carlos Alcaraz defeats defending champion Alexander Zverev to win the men's singles tennis title at the 2022 Mutua Madrid Open.
Prime Minister of Sri Lanka Mahinda Rajapaksa resigns amid mass protests over the government's handling of the economic crisis.
Pro-government supporters storm a major protest site in Colombo, clashing with police and protesters. A total of 78 people are injured.
Two people are killed and eight more are injured as police open fire against a group of protestors who were trying to set fire to the Pradeshiya Sabha chairman’s residence in Weeraketiya.

MP Amarakeerthi Athukorala opens fire against protestors who were blocking his vehicle in Nittambuwa, killing one man and injuring another. Athukorala then escaped into a nearby building, before being found dead alongside his security officer.
Gunmen open fire at two polling stations in Buluan and Lanao del Sur, Philippines, killing three guards and a voter and injuring another guard and two voters, amid the presidential elections.

The Washington Post wins the Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for its coverage of the 2021 United States Capitol attack. The New York Times wins the Pulitzer Prize for International Reporting on the war on terror's failed bombing campaigns and the most awards overall.
Nigeria's airlines say that they have cancelled a plan to suspend domestic flights, a decision they had previously made due to an increase in the cost of aviation fuel.

The Royal Thai Army announces it will ban all army personnel from using the Singaporean e-commerce site Lazada for allegedly insulting the royal family in a Facebook video ad. Digital Economy Minister Chaiwut Thanakamanusorn in a separate statement said the government is considering legal action against both Lazada and the advertising agency responsible for the ad.
One person dies and eleven others are missing after a fishing boat sinks off the coast of Ghana.
Four people are killed and fifty others are injured after a tear gas grenade is set off causing a human stampede at a public university in Potosí, Bolivia.

The Swedish Social Democratic Party announces that it will decide on May 15 whether to pursue a course of action to join NATO. Finnish President Sauli Niinistö is expected to also announce Finland's intention to join NATO on May 12.

context: Foreign relations of Iran, Foreign relations of Transnistria
text: Iranians in Moldova are urged to leave the country due to rising tensions in pro-Russian Transnistria and spillover effects from the war in Ukraine.
A prison riot in Santo Domingo, Ecuador, kills 44 inmates.
Filipinos head to the polls to elect officials in the Presidential, Senate, House of Representatives, Gubernatorial, and other local elections.
Bongbong Marcos, the son of late Philippine dictator Ferdinand Marcos, is leading in the preliminary and unofficial results to become the next President.

context: Ituri conflict, 2021–2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: Fourteen people are killed during an attack by suspected CODECO militants at a refugee camp in Fataki, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Sri Lankan Defense Ministry authorizes the Army and police force to shoot looters and assailants and to arrest protesters without warrants in response to yesterday's violence.
Apple announces it will discontinue sales of the iPod Touch, officially ending the iPod line of portable media players after more than 20 years.
The operator of Ukraine's natural gas system GTSOU announces that it will stop shipments of Russian gas through the Sokhranivka route on Wednesday.

context: Lithuania–Russia relations, Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Seimas of Lithuania unanimously votes to designate Russia as a terrorist state and to classify Russia's actions in Ukraine as genocide.

In a rare public rebuke, World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus criticizes China's "Zero-COVID" policy as "unsustainable", advising the Chinese government to change its strategy.

Former Senator of the Philippines Bongbong Marcos, son of dictator Ferdinand Marcos, is expected to become the next President of the Philippines, based on partial and unofficial counts. Marcos has more than twice as many votes as the next closest candidate Leni Robredo, the current Vice President of the Philippines. The victory will be officially ratified by the Congress of the Philippines in late May.

Crown Prince of Kuwait Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah accepts the resignation of the Government of Kuwait, after the request had been submitted more than a month ago. No timeline is given for when the next election will occur.
Yoon Suk-yeol is sworn in as the 13th President of South Korea.
Katalin Novák takes office as the first female President of Hungary.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 bombing of Odesa
text: Russian forces continue to fire missiles at the Ukrainian port city of Odesa in an apparent attempt to cut supplies to the city.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Kharkiv
text: Ukrainian military forces recapture several settlements north of Kharkiv, driving Russian troops to less than a dozen miles from the Russian border.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Killing of Shireen Abu Akleh
text: Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh is killed while covering a raid in Jenin. Palestinian sources say that Abu Akleh was shot by Israeli soldiers, while Israeli sources say that she was likely killed by indiscriminate fire by Palestinian militants. Israel eventually admitted and apologized for the murder after initial denials. Another journalist and two other Palestinians are injured in the shooting.
A Palestinian is shot dead after charging at police officers in Jerusalem.

Eight soldiers are killed and 13 others are injured during an ambush by Al-Qaeda-linked militants in Kpendjal Prefecture, Togo. The attack is believed to be connected to the current insurgency in Burkina Faso, making it the first Islamic extremist attack in Togo.
Four people are killed by a suicide bomber at a checkpoint in Mogadishu, Somalia. Al-Shabaab claims responsibility for the attack.
Seven soldiers are killed and two others are missing after gunmen ambush them in Taraba State, Nigeria.
Five soldiers are killed and four others are injured during a shooting at a security post in North Sinai, Egypt.
A small plane crashes in Cameroon with eleven people on board. It is unknown if any casualties occurred.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand
text: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announces that New Zealand will fully reopen its borders on July 31, two months before the government lifts all remaining pandemic restrictions.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) announce in a joint statement that, starting next week, masks are no longer required for flights or in airports. However, the EASA asks passengers to "behave responsibly and respect the choices of others around them," while the ECDC recommends that passengers continue to practice social distancing if it can be done in a non-disruptive manner.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: COVID-19 passes a threshold of 1 million confirmed deaths in the United States, according to a Reuters tally. Some news outlets declared that the 1 million mark was reached a week earlier.

context: Finland–United Kingdom relations, Sweden–United Kingdom relations
text: British Prime Minister Boris Johnson signs security agreements with Finland and Sweden, pledging British military assistance to both Nordic countries should they come under attack.

A report by the US Department of the Interior identifies 53 burial sites of Native American children near boarding schools, where children were forcibly sent to according to the 19th and 20th century federal government's policy of assimilation. Preliminary results suggest that more than 500 children were found to have died while in school custody.

A tentative settlement of $997 million is reached with the families of victims and survivors of the condo collapse in Surfside, Florida, United States. However, the settlement is still subject to final approval.
Greece bans the practice of conversion therapy for minors as well as all advertisements promoting it.

Hong Kong's national security police arrest four people, including Cardinal Joseph Zen, Cantopop singer Denise Ho, and former legislative councilwoman Margaret Ng, in connection with a fund that provided aid to protesters.
The Iranian Ministry of Intelligence says that it has arrested two European nationals for allegedly attempting to destabilize the nation in connection with foreign intelligence services.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Ukrainian forces repel an attempted Russian military crossing of the Donets river, west of Sievierodonetsk, in Luhansk Oblast. At least one Russian battalion tactical group is reportedly destroyed, as well as the pontoon bridge deployed in the crossing.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Air Force launches around a dozen missiles at the city of Kremenchuk, including four at the Kremenchuk Oil Refinery, in Poltava Oblast.
Turkey says that five people were injured by Kurdish nationalists launching a missile attack into the country from Syria.
One person is killed and thirteen others injured by a roadside bombing targeting a van in Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan.
The cryptocurrency market loses US$200 billion following stablecoin TerraUSD's collapse in value. Bitcoin and Ether fall to their lowest value in 16 and 11 months, respectively.

An A319-100 aircraft operated by Tibet Airlines veers off the runway and catches fire at Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport in Yubei District, Chongqing, China, injuring forty people, with some being hospitalized.
Five people are feared dead and twenty others are injured in a chemical plant explosion and fire in Kočevje, Slovenia.
Eleven people die and thirty-one others are rescued after a boat capsizes off the coast of Puerto Rico near Desecheo Island.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea
text: North Korea announces its first COVID-19 outbreak.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea
text: Supreme Leader Kim Jong-un orders a national lockdown.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Romania
text: Romania announces that starting on May 16, the fourth dose of Comirnaty – the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine – can be administered in vaccination centers and in family medicine offices for all adults.
Finland's leaders declare that the country should apply for membership of NATO "without delay," with the Parliament set to vote next week on whether to apply.
sources: President of the Republic of Finland

text: The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs threatens to take retaliatory steps against Finland, including of a "military-technical" nature, if the country joins NATO.
France summons the Iranian ambassador in response to the detainment of two French nationals.
A team of scientists at the Event Horizon Telescope release the first ever image of Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
Researchers from the University of Florida announce that plants have been grown on lunar soil, collected by Apollo missions, for the first time ever.

context: Boycott of Russia and Belarus, 2022 French Open
text: Tennis players from Russia and Belarus will be allowed to compete at the upcoming French Open as neutral athletes. However, players who speak in support for Russian President Vladimir Putin will face sanctions.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli involvement in the Syrian Civil War
text: Syrian state media says that a missile attack from Israel hit Masyaf, Hama Governorate, killing five people and injuring seven others.
Ten Syrian Army soldiers are killed and nine others are injured by a rocket attack that hit a bus in Aleppo, Syria.
Israeli police commando Noam Raz is killed in a shootout with Palestinian Islamic Jihad gunmen in Jenin, West Bank.

Israeli riot police beat pallbearers and mourners at the funeral of journalist Shireen Abu Akleh, which was attended by thousands of Palestinians in East Jerusalem. White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki and the deputy speaker for UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the images of the attacks "deeply disturbing".
Six people are injured in a mass stabbing on a train near Aachen, NRW, Germany. Police arrested an Iraqi man and are investigating whether it was a terrorist attack.

context: Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk
text: Elon Musk temporarily suspends his $44 billion takeover deal of Twitter as he seeks to confirm the company's calculations that spam bots and fake accounts constitute less than 5% of the user base.
The Croatian Parliament votes 117–13 to officially replace the kuna with the euro on 1 January.
The Sky Bridge 721 opens in Dolni Morava, Czech Republic. Spanning , it is longest simple suspension bridge in the world.
At least 27 people are killed and more than 40 others are injured in a fire at a commercial building in Mundka, Delhi, India.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea
text: North Korea says that six people have died and 187,800 others have been quarantined due to the latest COVID-19 outbreak.
The total number of people who have received a dose of the Malaria vaccine surpasses 1 million.

RAO Nordic, a subsidiary of Russian energy company Inter RAO, announces it will suspend deliveries of electricity to Finland, saying it has not been paid for prior deliveries. The suspension comes as Russia threatens retaliation if Finland joins NATO.

context: Enlargement of NATO > Finland–Turkey relations, Sweden–Turkey relations
text: Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan says that Turkey will oppose Sweden and Finland's applications to join NATO, asserting that the countries are "guesthouses for terrorist organisations", without giving details. Turkey has repeatedly criticized Sweden and other Western European countries for its handling of organisations labeled terrorist by the Turkish government, including the Kurdish militant groups PKK and YPG, and the followers of U.S.-based Islamic cleric Fethullah Gülen.

context: Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–United States relations
text: U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin holds talks with Russian Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu in the first meeting between the two since the start of the invasion.

context: War crimes during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine holds its first trial for war crimes committed during the Russian invasion, against a Russian soldier accused of shooting an unarmed civilian in March.
Anti-government demonstrations occur in multiple cities in Iran that are experiencing Internet shutdowns.
President of the United Arab Emirates and ruler of Abu Dhabi Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan dies at the age of 73.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso
text: Fifteen civilians and three VPD volunteers are killed during a shooting attack against their convoy in Kompienga.

context: Insurgency in the Maghreb > Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso
