context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland
text: Governor Larry Hogan outlines a long-term preparedness plan on how Maryland will deal with COVID-19 including a focus on treatments that would keep people out of hospitals as well as on how the state would respond to future variants.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Spain
text: Spain will begin vaccinations of close contacts of monkeypox using the Imvanex vaccine after 242 cases were reported in the country.
Poland decides to lift its state of emergency over attempts by migrants to cross the Belarus–Poland border, saying that the border barrier it has been building is mostly complete.

A 2-seater Beechcraft plane violates the airspace of seven countries in Eastern Europe, and is intercepted by two Hungarian Air Force Gripen jets, two USAF F-16s and two Romanian Air Force F-16s before being abandoned at an airfield near Targovishte, Bulgaria.
Seven people are killed and 46 others are injured by a fire, suspected to be an arson attack, that spread through an office building in Daegu, South Korea. The suspect is killed in the fire.

Thailand removes cannabis and hemp plants from its list of illegal narcotics, and will allow people to grow an unlimited number of these plants in farms and gardens for medicinal purposes as long as they inform the authorities. However, public consumption of these plants is discouraged by official authorities.
Three people are killed and another is injured in a mass shooting in Smithsburg, Maryland, United States.

The Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) sentences to death two Britons and a Moroccan who had joined Ukrainian forces on charges of terrorism, mercenary activities, and attempting to overthrow the DPR's government.

The European Parliament adopts a resolution urging to amend the treaties of the European Union in order to abolish the unanimity principle in decisionmaking with respect to sanctions and foreign policy and to grant the Parliament the right to legislative initiative.
NASA announces that the James Webb Space Telescope collided with a micrometeoroid last month, but continues to function normally.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine states that the country has "installed naval mines in the exercise of our right to self-defence".

context: 2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions
text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo accuses Rwanda of killing two Congolese children in a rocket attack. Rwanda also accuses the DRC of firing rockets into the country from Bunagana.
So called Whisky War, a pseudo confrontation between Canada and Denmark ends with the Hans Island divided.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average falls 880 points and the S&P 500 falls 117 points following the release of an inflation report that showed a faster-than-expected rise in prices and consumer sentiment reaching a record low.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: The Biden administration announces that the U.S. has lifted COVID-19 testing restrictions for international travel.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The U.S. purchases 300,000 more doses of vaccines from Bavarian Nordic, including the Jynneos vaccine, as part of an effort to combat the monkeypox outbreak.
Poland reports its first case of monkeypox.

Russia and China open the new Blagoveshchensk–Heihe Bridge. The 1 km long bridge spans across the Amur river to connect Heihe in Northeastern China's Heilongjiang province with Blagoveshchensk in Far Eastern Russia's Amur Oblast. It will shorten the travel distance of freight between China and western Russia by 1,500 km.
Russia withdraws from the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) after having been suspended by that organization due to the country's war in Ukraine.
Malaysian law minister Wan Junaidi announces that mandatory capital punishment will be abolished in the country.

FIFA dismisses a petition by the Football Federation of Chile against the Ecuadorian Football Federation to disqualify the Ecuador national football team from participating in the 2022 World Cup, claiming that one of its players, Byron Castillo, is ineligible on the grounds of his nationality.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas, Eastern Ukraine offensive > Battle of Sievierodonetsk
text: Russian forces shell the Azot chemical plant in Sievierodonetsk, Luhansk Oblast. Governor Serhiy Haidai says that the attack has caused a massive fire at the plant.

context: Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso > 2022 Seytenga massacre
text: Suspected jihadists massacre over 100 men in Seytenga Department, Séno Province, Burkina Faso.
A helicopter missing since 9 June is found crashed near Modena, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. All seven people on board were killed in the crash.
Top oil and petrochemicals producers Iran and Venezuela sign a 20-year economic cooperation agreement.

The former president of Bolivia Jeanine Áñez is sentenced to ten years in prison for the crimes of breach of duty and resolutions contrary to the Constitution and laws of Bolivia during the 2019 Bolivian political crisis.
North Korea appoints Choe Son-hui as its next foreign minister.
Demonstrators participate in more than 450 rallies nationwide to push for gun law changes after mass shootings in United States.
At this year's Tony Awards, A Strange Loop wins Best Musical while The Lehman Trilogy wins Best Play.
Three months after McDonald's suspended its operations in Russia and sold its 850 restaurants to Alexander Govor, the rebranded restaurants are reopened as Vkusno i tochka.
The Celsius Network cryptocurrency lending platform announced it was "pausing all withdrawals, swap, and transfers between accounts" amidst a large pullback in the cryptocurrency market.
Authorities in Argentina seize an Iranian Boeing 747 which was transferred to Venezuela last year. It is unclear if the impound is related to sanctions that have been imposed on both countries.
At least 30 members of the American neo-fascist group Patriot Front are arrested for conspiracy to riot at a pride event in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, United States.
Voters in France go to the polls to elect the first round of the 577 members of the 16th National Assembly.

Exit polls show the coalition of left-wing parties headed by far-left deputy Jean-Luc Mélenchon barely edging out President Emmanuel Macron's coalition Ensemble Citoyens for the most votes in the first round, winning 25.6% and 25.2% of the votes respectively. Overall turnout is projected to be 47%, the lowest recorded for a French election.
The referendum for the reform of the judicial system is invalidated as it did not reach the required 50% threshold.

In golf, Linn Grant of Sweden becomes the first female winner on the PGA European Tour following her win in the Scandinavian Mixed. The tournament was co-sanctioned with the Ladies European Tour in 2020.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sievierodonetsk
text: Russian forces destroy the last remaining bridge leading to Sievierodonetsk in Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine, trapping all remaining Ukrainian civilians in the city, according to regional governor Serhiy Haidai.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: The Donetsk People's Republic says that five people have been killed and 22 others injured in an artillery attack on a marketplace in central Donetsk. Pro-Russian media accuses NATO of supplying the munitions used in the attack.

context: Kivu conflict > 2022 M23 offensive, 2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions
text: M23 rebels capture the town of Bunagana. The Congolese military accuses Rwanda of assisting the rebels in the capture of the town.

Global stocks and government bonds plunge with the MSCI World Index dropping by 2.95%, the DOW by 4.68%, the S&P 500 by 3.88%, STOXX Europe 600 by 2.41%, Japan's Nikkei 225 by 3.01%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng by 3.99%, and South Korea's KOSPI by 3.52%. Bitcoin drops by 12.1% and Ethereum by 13.6%.
The S&P 500 closes more than 20% below its January 3 record closing high, confirming that the index is in a bear market.
A passenger train and a locomotive collide in the town of Vila-seca, Catalonia, Spain, injuring 22 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
text: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau tests positive for COVID-19 for a second time.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: Secretary of Health and Human Services Xavier Becerra tests positive for COVID-19.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan reports their first cases of the Omicron BA.4 and BA.5 subvariants in five Taiwanese citizens who arrived from overseas.

The Wikimedia Foundation files an appeal against a Russian court order demanding the removal of certain Russo-Ukrainian War-related information from the Russian-language Wikipedia, which is one of the few remaining fact-checked sources still available to the general Russian public.

The British government confirms that it will go ahead with plans to terminate the Northern Ireland Protocol in order to make it easier for goods to flow between Great Britain and Northern Ireland. The European Union accuses the UK of breaking international law by reneging on the agreement made during Brexit negotiations.
Pope Francis appoints John T. Dunlap as the new Lieutenant of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.
Indigenous peoples in Ecuador block highways leading to the capital Quito, to protest president Guillermo Lasso's policies and to call for economic reforms.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Six people are reported injured in an alleged shelling attack on Klintsy, Bryansk Oblast, Russia.

In a joint operation, the Oromo Liberation Army and the Gambela Liberation Front launch an attack on the regional capital of Gambela city. The fighting lasted for several hours before security forces were able to recapture the city from the rebels, with heavy casualties reported on both sides.
Ten people are killed and three others are injured in a shootout between security forces and suspected criminals in Texcaltitlán, State of Mexico.
A Tajik border guard is killed and three others are injured in a clash with Kyrgyzstan border troops.

Finnish authorities remove the country's last remaining monument of Soviet Union founder and leader Vladimir Lenin in Kotka, Kymenlaakso, relocating the 1979 gift from the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic to a museum.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The European Union removes Russia's largest bank Sberbank, the Russian Agricultural Bank and the Credit Bank of Moscow from the SWIFT international payments system as part of another round of economic sanctions on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine.
The government of Kiribati declares a state of disaster due to severe drought in the country.
An explosion at a chemical factory in Firouzabad, Fars, Iran, injures 103 people.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Spain removes all COVID-19 entry requirements for anyone arriving into the country from the European Union or the Schengen Area. However, travellers from outside the EU will still need to be fully vaccinated or provide proof of a negative PCR test within 72 hours before departure in order to enter Spain.
The World Health Organization announces plans to officially rename the monkeypox virus in order to combat stigma and racism surrounding the disease.
Pakistan reports its 10th case of polio this year after two more cases of the virus are reported in North Waziristan District.
The Danish Foreign Ministry announces that it has reached a deal with Canada to divide the long-disputed Hans Island in the Arctic in half between Canada's Nunavut territory and Greenland.

The Federal Ministry of Health says that it will hold consultations with over 200 representatives from medical, legal and other fields on legalizing the sale of cannabis in licensed shops for recreational purposes.
A Cambodian court convicts 60 members of the former Cambodia National Rescue Party of treason, including Cambodian-American lawyer Theary Seng.
Police in Ecuador arrest an indigenous leader after incidents that occurred during recent protests against the economic policies of president Guillermo Lasso.

The United States Tennis Association says that tennis players from Russia and Belarus will be allowed to compete at the upcoming US Open tournament despite the ongoing invasion of Ukraine, which is expected to be held in New York after Wimbledon banned them from doing so.

context: Kashmir conflict > Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
text: Indian security forces kill two suspected militants in Jammu and Kashmir, India.
Two people are killed and seven others are injured in a Turkish military action against the Sinjar Resistance Units in Sinjar District, Iraq. A 12-year-old child is reported to be among the deceased.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > List of foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States announces a new $1 billion military aid package to Ukraine that includes 18 howitzers, artillery rockets, night vision devices, and for the first time, two Harpoon anti-ship missile units.
A Yemeni journalist is assassinated after a bomb explodes inside his car in Aden.
Mohammad El Halabi, a Palestinian aid worker at the center of an international controversy over his six-year detention in Israel, was convicted on the basis of 'secret evidence'.

The Federal Reserve raises its benchmark interest rate by 0.75% to a target range of between 1.5% and 1.75% amid surging inflation. It is the largest interest rate increase in the United States since 1994.
The European Union launches legal action against the United Kingdom, alleging a breach of post-Brexit agreements regarding the Northern Ireland Protocol.

Opposition parties in Thailand file a no-confidence motion in prime minister Prayut Chan-o-cha and 10 of his ministers, accusing them of "graft, economic mismanagement and of undermining democracy and clinging to power".
FIFA announces the names of the cities in Canada, Mexico and the United States that will host the FIFA World Cup in 2026.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian officials say that four people have been killed and six others have been injured in a rocket attack in Sumy overnight.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The mayor of Melitopol claims that Ukrainian farmers caused "mass illness" in Russian troops by poisoning cherries.
The United States announces the capture of a senior ISIL leader in Syria.
One Sudanese protester is shot dead after a flare up of anti-military protests in Khartoum and Omdurman.

European benchmark natural gas prices increase by around 30% after Russia's Gazprom reduced Nord Stream 1's gas supply to Germany to 40% of the pipeline's capacity. Russia blames maintenance problems resulting from Canada's refusal to return equipment that was sent for repair and warns that usage of the pipeline could be completely suspended.

Oil prices increase in the United States following the Biden administration's announcement of new sanctions against Iran's petrochemicals industry. The sanctions are an effort to force Iran to comply with the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, from which the United States unilaterally withdrew in 2018.
Four people are killed and five others are injured in a building fire in the town of Handlova, Slovakia.
Firefighters fight wildfires across Catalonia and Navarre, Spain, as temperatures reach , complicating the efforts of the firefighters.

Sergey Cherkasov, a Russian military intelligence official, is expelled from the Netherlands for attempting to begin an internship at the International Criminal Court in The Hague using a fake Brazilian identity. Cherkasov will now face a criminal trial in Brazil.
Three people are killed in a shooting at an Episcopal Church in Vestavia Hills, Alabama, United States.
In basketball, the Golden State Warriors defeat the Boston Celtics in six games to win their fourth NBA championship in eight years. Stephen Curry is named NBA Finals MVP.

context: Kivu conflict > 2022 M23 offensive > 2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions
text: A Congolese soldier crosses the border into Western Province, Rwanda, and is shot dead by a Rwandan Police officer. Rwandan officials say that the soldier had been attacking people and had injured two officers before he was killed.

context: Kivu conflict > 2022 M23 offensive > 2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions
text: The DRC closes its border with Rwanda in response to the killing of its soldier.
M23 movement militants seize the town of Tshengerero, North Kivu.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Nuclear threats during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin says that Russia would only use nuclear weapons if the sovereignty of the country is threatened.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian authorities say that its forces hit the Russian tugboat Vasiliy Bekh transporting soldiers, weapons, and ammunition to Snake Island with Harpoon missiles.
Turkey says that four Kurdish militants have been killed during airstrikes in Kalar, Iraq.
Israel intercepts a rocket fired by suspected Hamas militants over Ashkelon. The Israel Defense Forces respond by launching airstrikes on military targets in Gaza.
Three Palestinian militants, including an Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades commander, are killed by Israeli soldiers during a raid in Jenin, West Bank.
Security forces and armed locals kill 70 al-Shabaab members in Bahdo, Somalia. Two local children and a cleric are also killed in the fighting.
One person is killed and seven others injured by an explosion at a mosque in Imam Sahib, Kunduz Province.
Three people are killed when militants attack a labor camp in Balochistan, Pakistan.
The United Kingdom is asked to host next year's Eurovision Song Contest after its organisers concluded that Ukraine is not capable of hosting the competition.

WWE Chairman and CEO Vince McMahon voluntarily steps down from his executive roles while WWE's Board of Directors investigates alleged misconduct over a $3 million "hush pact" with a former employee. McMahon's daughter Stephanie is appointed to serve as interim CEO and Chairwoman, with Vince retaining his roles related to WWE creative content.
In Spain, over 650 people in eight villages are evacuated after wildfires originating in the Sierra de Culebra mountain range grew to 9,000 hectares amidst a heat wave in Europe.
At least six people are killed by a building collapse in Cairo, Egypt.
Nine people are killed and 40 are injured after a bus crashes in Tila, Chiapas, Mexico.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Estonia removes all of its COVID-19 entry restrictions for non-EU travellers after the Estonian Health Board concluded that the situation is under control and that third-country nationals are unlikely to affect the epidemiological situation in the country.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco
text: King Mohammed VI of Morocco tests positive for COVID-19 with no symptoms.
Georgia, Iceland, Luxembourg, Serbia, and Chile report their first confirmed cases of monkeypox.
Nepal reports its first suspected case of monkeypox.

context: Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
text: The European Commission recommends that the European Council grant Ukraine candidate status for accession to the European Union.
The Japanese Supreme Court acquits the state of any responsibility to compensate around 3,700 people affected by the nuclear disaster.

context: Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange
text: The UK's Home Office approves the extradition of WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to the United States. Assange's lawyers announce that they will appeal the decision.

China launches its third aircraft carrier, the Fujian, during a ceremony in Shanghai, further enhancing the country's ability to project its military abroad. China now has the second most aircraft carriers of any country, behind only the United States, which has eleven aircraft carriers.
The English men's cricket team achieve the highest ever One Day International score of 498 against The Netherlands, beating their previous world record of 481 against Australia in 2018.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Donetsk People's Republic authorities accuse Ukrainian forces of shelling the Zasyadko coal mine and trapping 77 miners.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukrainian delegate Davyd Arakhamia says that Ukraine is planning to resume ceasefire negotiations with Russia this August.

context: Kashmir conflict > Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
text: The dead body of an Indian police official is found in a paddy field in Pampore, Jammu and Kashmir. Islamist militants are suspected to be responsible for the attack.
Islamic State kill a Sikh and a Taliban member in an attack on a gurdwara in Kabul.
At least 20 people die in an attack in Anchawadi commune, Mali.
Two people are killed and six are injured after suspected militants attacked a bus in southwestern Rwanda.
At least two people are killed by flooding in Guangxi, China.
One person is killed in a fire at a petrochemical plant in Shanghai, China.
Wildfires spread across northeastern Spain amid a heatwave, with the highest temperatures expected to be between in the region of Zaragoza.
An Iranian F-14 crashes near Isfahan, with both pilots successfully ejecting from the aircraft.
A firefighter is killed and five other people are injured after a building collapses in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: The U.S. CDC unanimously votes to approve COVID-19 vaccines for children under the age of five, including babies.
President of Ecuador Guillermo Lasso declares a state of exception in Quito and other parts of the country amid ongoing protests.

context: 2022 European heat waves > Climate change in France
text: France sees several June all-time temperature records beaten by over in an exceptionally strong heat wave. Biarritz's temperature rises to , the absolute record for the seaside resort and above the previous all-time record set in August.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kharkiv Oblast
text: Ukraine says that Russian forces are advancing on the city of Kharkiv.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sievierodonetsk
text: Russia says that its forces captured a district in the outskirts of Sieverodonetsk and that it launched Kalibr cruise missiles against a command centre in Dnipro, killing several Ukrainian generals and officers.
Two people are killed when a car hits a roadside bomb in Kabul.
A Palestinian man is shot and killed by Israeli forces while attempting to cross the separation barrier.

Militants attack two churches, one of them Baptist and the other Catholic, in Kajuru LGA of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Three members of the Catholic Church are killed and several more, mostly from the Baptist one, are kidnapped.
Eighteen people are killed after a bus collided with a truck in Niger State, Nigeria.
The Czech Republic records its highest temperature for the month of June, , in Řež. Parts of Austria, Germany and Poland also report record high temperatures.

context: Lithuania–Russia relations > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Lithuania bans the transit of goods that are under EU sanctions through their territory to the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.
The European Union condemns the "structurally deficient" justice system in Bolivia and lack of "due process" in the trial of Jeanine Áñez and asks for her release.
Citizens go to the polls to vote in the second round of the Colombian presidential election.
Left-wing candidate Gustavo Petro wins the presidential election with 50.44% of the vote, beating his opponent Rodolfo Hernández who received 47.31% of the vote, according to preliminary results.

context: 2022 Nigerian elections > 2022 Nigerian gubernatorial elections > 2022 Ekiti State gubernatorial election
text: Former state commissioner Abiodun Oyebanji of the All Progressives Congress defeats former Governor Olusegun Oni of the Social Democratic Party in the gubernatorial election. Oyebanji's win means that the APC has become the first party ever to win consecutive Ekiti gubernatorial elections.

context: Elections in Spain > 2022 Andalusian regional election
text: Ruling People's Party of Andalusia wins a historic absolute majority, the first for a conservative party in Andalusia. Citizens, whose leader was the vice-president of the region, loses all the 21 deputies it had.
French voters head to the polls to vote in the second round of the latest legislative election.
It is announced that French President Emmanuel Macron's party Renaissance and its allies will not repeat an absolute majority in the National Assembly.

context: 2022 Sri Lankan protests, 2022 Sri Lankan political crisis
text: Four civilians and three soldiers were wounded in protest over gasoline shortage when the army opened fire for the first time to quell unrest, as Sri Lanka is suffering its worst economic crisis since independence.

Russian tennis player Natela Dzalamidze changes her nationality to Georgian and will participate in the upcoming Wimbledon tournament after Wimbledon banned Russian and Belarusian players from participating in the tournament.

FINA, during its general congress, votes to disallow trans women swimmers from competing in high-level competitions. However, the body will convene a working group to develop a separate "open" category for them in select competitions.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Pro-Russian forces of the Luhansk People's Republic claim to have taken the key town of Toshkivka, 25 km south of Sieverodonetsk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian forces fire missiles at a Chornomornaftogaz drilling oil facility in the Black Sea, off Crimea, injuring three workers, with seven others missing. Russia launches missile strikes on Odesa in retaliation for the attack.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A second American volunteer fighter dies in Ukraine, after triggering a landmine.
Islamist insurgents kill 132 civilians over the weekend in a series of attacks on three villages in the Bankass Cercle of Mali's Mopti Region, including Segue.

A bazaar in Nangarhar Province is bombed, which the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan says has killed and injured "scores of people." The ruling Taliban confirm that at least ten people have been injured but cannot yet confirm if anyone has been killed.
Two Jesuit priests are murdered by gunmen in a church in Cerocahui, Chihuahua.
Eleven soldiers and two civilians are killed in an attack on a bus travelling from Raqqa to Homs. The Islamic State claims responsibility for the attack.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Panic buying is reported in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad after Lithuania banned the transit of some goods through its territory by rail. Kaliningrad Governor Anton Alikhanov calls for calm, while Russia condemns the ban.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Russian Foreign Affairs Ministry demands that Lithuania "immediately reverse" new restrictions on shipments of Russian goods to Kaliningrad, saying that the restrictions were "unprecedented" and "illegal", while also suggesting that Moscow could "take actions to protect its national interests".
Canadian defense minister Anita Anand announces an increase in defense spending to $5 billion in order to upgrade continental defense.

It is announced that Cape Verde will allocate a budget of $85 million to combat the effects of the war in Ukraine, which has caused an increase in the prices of gasoline and food, as 9% of Cape Verdeans are currently facing a food crisis.
A helicopter crashes near Burton, North Yorkshire, England, killing two people onboard.

Dutch climate and energy minister Rob Jetten announces that the Netherlands will remove all restrictions on the operation of coal-fired power stations until at least 2024, in response to Russia's refusal to export natural gas to the country. Operations were previously limited to less than a third of the total production.

Canadian Environmental Minister Steven Guilbeault announces that Canada will ban the sale of single-use plastics by December 2023, and will ban the export of these plastics by the end of 2025, with the first regulations to come into effect in December.
A study published in Nature Food finds that the impact of food transportation on climate change is three times greater than was previously believed, making up 6% of global carbon emissions.

context: Belgium–Democratic Republic of the Congo relations
text: The Belgian government repatriates Congolese independence leader and former prime minister Patrice Lumumba's remains, consisting of a tooth, through an official ceremony attended by his family at the Egmont Palace in Brussels.
Ukraine ratifies the Istanbul Convention.

context: Recognition of same-sex unions in Japan
text: The Osaka District Court rules that Japan's ban on same-sex marriage is not "unconstitutional" in a ruling on a lawsuit filed by two male couples and one female couple.
Violent protests occur across India, including the burning of trains in Hyderabad, in response to proposed recruitment reforms in the military.

President Emmanuel Macron's party Renaissance is confirmed to lose its majority in the National Assembly after yesterday's second round of legislative elections. Both the left-wing alliance NUPES and the right-wing party National Rally achieve significant electoral gains, forcing the government to seek compromises with other parties during the upcoming legislative period for the first time since the 1988 legislative election.

Leading members of the thirty-sixth government of Israel Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid agree to dissolve the Knesset, triggering a fifth snap election in just over three years. Lapid will serve as acting Prime Minister until the election is held.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of the Luhansk Oblast
text: Luhansk Governor Serhiy Haidai says that Russian forces captured the towns of Pidlisne and Myrna Dolyna, south of Lysychansk, and also confirms reports that separatist forces captured Toshkivka yesterday.
The Governor of Kharkiv Oblast, Oleh Synyehubov, reports that Russian shelling killed 15 civilians in and near Kharkiv.
A Palestinian man is stabbed and killed by an Israeli settler in the occupied West Bank.

context: 2021–2022 inflation surge > 2022 United Kingdom national rail strike
text: Railway transport workers go on a nationwide general strike in the United Kingdom after talks on a 7% pay increase for workers collapses. The RMT says that industry executives have only offered a 2% increase in pay, which is well below rising inflation levels.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia becomes China's biggest supplier of oil, surpassing Saudi Arabia and making up over half of China's oil imports.
The Edgewood Fire breaks out near San Mateo County, California, prompting evacuations and power outages. A firefighter is injured while fighting the fires.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Macau
text: Authorities in Macau place a casino and hotel with more than 700 people inside under lockdown due to an outbreak of COVID-19 in the territory.

context: International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War > Lithuania–Russia relations
text: Russian Security Council Secretary Nikolai Patrushev warns Lithuania that its citizens will "feel pain" over the ban on the transit of Russian goods to Kaliningrad through Lithuania, saying that Russia's response in the near future could have "a serious negative impact on the population of Lithuania".
Estonia reports that a Russian Border Service Mi-8 helicopter violated its airspace over the weekend. The Russian ambassador to Estonia was summoned in response to the incident.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on international relations
text: The United Nations announces that the conference of the parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity initially scheduled to take place in Kunming, China, later this year will be moved to Montreal, Canada, due to logistical complications caused by China's Zero-COVID policy.

Lebanon, Egypt and Syria sign an agreement to supply Egyptian gas to a power plant in northern Lebanon through Syria. However, the World Bank, which is financing the deal, must validate the agreement before it can take effect.
Twenty-nine Chinese military aircraft enter the Taiwanese air defence zone, prompting the Taiwanese Air Force to send their own aircraft in response.
Two people are injured, including one in critical condition, after a stabbing attack in Västerås, Sweden.
Rioters attack an International Day of Yoga celebration in Malé, the Maldives, proclaiming that yoga is against the tenets of Islam.

The South Dakota Senate, in the United States, votes to convict Attorney General Jason Ravnsborg over his role in a 2020 car accident in which his car struck 55-year old Joseph Boever, removing him from office immediately.

Egypt rejects two World Trade Organization (WTO) agreements which would have forced it to export domestically needed food to alleviate the global food crisis, citing proposals that it considers harmful to developing countries and also noting that 30 other WTO member states restrict food exports.

The armed forces of Ecuador say that they will "not allow ongoing protests" to "damage the country's democracy", as road blockades and demonstrations against the economic policies of president Guillermo Lasso continue.
Russia blocks access to The Daily Telegraph's website on the orders of the Prosecutor-General, after accusing the newspaper of "disseminating false information" about the Russian war in Ukraine.

Nuri, South Korea's first locally-developed orbital launch vehicle, launches for a second time from the Naro Space Center in Goheung County, South Jeolla, with a satellite payload of . The launch was successful, with all of the satellites being put onto the Sun-synchronous orbit.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: The Ukrainian Air Force launches drone strikes on an oil refinery in Novoshakhtinsk, Rostov Oblast, Russia, causing a large explosion and fire. Operations at the refinery have been suspended. Footage on social media appears to show at least one armed drone striking the facility.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Reporters Without Borders releases a report claiming that a Ukrainian photojournalist was summarily executed while injured on the ground by Russian soldiers during the early stages of the conflict.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine offensive
text: Seven Russian missiles strike the city of Mykolaiv, killing at least one person and damaging a number of residential and commercial buildings, according to Mykolaiv governor Vitaliy Kim.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian military says that it has inflicted "significant losses" on Russian forces after launching airstrikes on Snake Island in the Black Sea, destroying a Pantsir missile system, a radar station and numerous vehicles on the occupied island.

context: Yemeni Civil War > Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen
text: Five Southern Transitional Council soldiers and three Al-Qaeda militants are killed during a shootout in Ataq, Shabwah Governorate.

Ecuadorian indigenous groups attack a police station in Puyo, Pastaza, amid ongoing protests in the country. One protestor is shot dead by police. Eighteen police officers are missing, while another six are injured.
Anglophone Ambazonia rebels kill between 26 and 32 civilians in Akwaya, Cameroon.
Inflation in the United Kingdom reaches 9.1%, a 40-year record, as food and fuel prices continue to increase.
A magnitude 6.1 earthquake strikes Khost, Afghanistan, killing at least 1,000 people and injuring at least 1,500 others.
A McDonnell Douglas MD-82 catches fire after landing at Miami International Airport in Florida, United States.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen says that Denmark will begin administering fourth doses of the COVID-19 vaccine for people over the age of 50 years.

The UK Health Security Agency declares a national incident after traces of poliovirus were detected during routine sewage inspections in London. However, the risk to the public is currently believed to be "extremely low".

context: Africa–Canada relations, Foreign relations of Rwanda
text: Canada announces its intention to open an embassy in Rwanda. The announcement comes a few days before the 2022 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting will be held in Kigali.

The military junta of Myanmar orders all legal proceedings against deposed leader Aung San Suu Kyi to be moved from courtrooms to prison venues without explanation. Aung San Suu Kyi has been under detainment since the February 2021 coup.
The government of Bulgarian prime minister Kiril Petkov loses a motion of no confidence vote in the National Assembly.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Governor of Luhansk Oblast, Serhiy Haidai, says that Russia is "just destroying" everything in Lysychansk as pro-Russian separatists say they are close to capturing both that city and Sieverodonetsk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > War crimes in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The first trial for rape during the war in Ukraine is set to begin in absentia against a 32-year-old Russian soldier accused of murdering a civilian and repeatedly raping his wife during the offensive in Kyiv.
A third protester is killed in Quito during clashes with police as around 10,000 people continue to protest in the city.
Turkey arrests ten alleged Iranian intelligence agents and charges them with plotting to murder Israeli tourists in hotels.
U.S. sportswear retailer Nike and networking firm Cisco announce that they are permanently ending their operations in Russia and Belarus.
Five people are killed and 25 others injured by a fire at an apartment building in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

context: 2022–2023 mpox outbreak > 2022–2023 mpox outbreak in the United States
text: New York City becomes the first jurisdiction in the United States to distribute smallpox vaccines to people who are at risk of contracting the monkeypox virus.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration orders electronic cigarette company Juul to pull all of its products from the market, blaming the company for causing an increase in youth vaping.

context: Enlargement of the European Union > Accession of Ukraine to the European Union, Accession of Moldova to the European Union
text: The European Union formally awards official candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova.

context: Gun politics in the United States
text: In a 65–33 vote, the U.S. Senate passes gun control legislation for the first time in decades. The bill calls for tougher background checks on gun purchasers younger than 21, blocks gun sales to individuals with a history of domestic abuse against unmarried partners, and provides funding to encourage the adoption of a red flag law, among others. It is sent to the U.S. House of Representatives for a vote.
Citizens of Grenada head to the polls to vote in a general election.
Scientists discover the largest known bacterium, Thiomargarita magnifica, in the mangroves of the Guadeloupe archipelago in Lesser Antilles. It is up to 2 cm (3/4 inch) long.

In basketball, the 76th NBA draft is held at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, U.S., with the Orlando Magic selecting former Duke University player Paolo Banchero with the first overall pick.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sievierodonetsk
text: Governor of Luhansk Oblast Serhiy Haidai announces that Ukrainian forces will withdraw from Sievierodonetsk amid the advance of Russian and pro-Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Russian-appointed senior official for the Kherson youth department is killed by a car bombing in Kherson in an apparent assassination.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian authorities say that Russian forces have captured the city of Hirske, south of Lysychansk, in Luhansk Oblast. Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov says that his forces also captured the town of Zolote.
Two Tunisian police officers are injured in a stabbing and suspected terrorist attack in the Grand Synagogue of Tunis.
Eighteen migrants are killed and hundreds of people injured, mostly Spanish and Moroccan security forces, as around 2,000 migrants attempt to illegally enter Melilla, Spain, from Morocco.

Five people are killed and eleven others are injured in Gayan District, Paktika Province, Afghanistan, by an aftershock from the recent earthquake that killed at least 1,100 people in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
An Ilyushin Il-76 military cargo plane carrying nine people crashes near Ryazan, Russia, killing five passengers.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Taiwan, Lebanon, Singapore and South Korea report their first cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Bulgaria and Croatia report their first cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Canada
text: British Columbia reports its second case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Kentucky, North Carolina and Texas report their first cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: New York City opens the first monkeypox clinic in the United States.
South Africa and Colombia report their first cases of monkeypox.
Zambia, Libya and Fiji report their first suspected cases of monkeypox.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia
text: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud tests positive for COVID-19.
The Sanofi–GSK COVID-19 vaccine is found to be effective against the Omicron variant.

context: Accession of North Macedonia to the European Union, Bulgaria–North Macedonia relations
text: Bulgaria lifts its veto against North Macedonia's bid to join the European Union.

context: Abortion in the United States > Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
text: The United States Supreme Court overturns Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey, ending protection of the right to abortion on the federal level and returning regulation to the states. Twenty-two states enact trigger laws or reinstitute existing laws banning abortion.
A court in Norway finds the attacker not criminally responsible due to paranoid schizophrenia and sentences him to compulsory mental treatment.
A court in Cuba sentences two protesters to between five and nine years in prison for desecrating the Cuban flag and resisting authority during last year's protests.
The oppositional National Democratic Congress wins the majority of seats in Grenada's latest general election. NDC's party leader Dickon Mitchell is expected to become Grenada's next Prime Minister.

The Conservative Party is defeated in both the Tiverton and Honiton by-election and the Wakefield by-election by the Liberal Democrats and the Labour Party, respectively. Conservative chairman Oliver Dowden resigns in the aftermath of the defeats.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports > Canada at the 2022 World Aquatics Championships
text: The Canada men's national water polo team withdraws from the remainder of the 2022 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest, Hungary, due to COVID-19 cases within the team.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Sievierodonetsk
text: The mayor of Sieverodonetsk announces that Russian forces have "fully occupied" the city.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine offensive
text: Pro-Russian forces say that they have entered the city of Lysychansk, the last major city still held by Ukrainian forces in Luhansk Oblast, and that street-to-street fighting is underway.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia launches dozens of cruise missiles at targets in multiple Ukrainian cities, including Yavoriv, Zhytomyr, and Desna. At least 20 missiles were fired from Belarusian airspace.

Two people are killed and 21 others injured during mass shootings at three separate sites in central Oslo, Norway, including a gay nightclub. An Iranian-Norwegian man is arrested and charged with murder, attempted murder, and terrorism. The motive is suspected to be Islamic extremism.
A 16-year-old Palestinian teenager dies in Israeli custody after being shot yesterday by soldiers in Silwad, West Bank.
Twenty-six people are killed in an attack in Akwaya district, Southwest region, Cameroon.
Fuschia Anne Ravena of the Philippines is crowned Miss International Queen, widely regarded as the world's largest beauty pageant for trans women, in Pattaya, Thailand.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake strikes near Kish Island, Iran, killing one person and injuring 31 others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: Shanghai declares "victory" over COVID-19 and Beijing announces the reopening of primary and secondary schools following a decrease in the number of cases.
The World Health Organization declares that monkeypox is not yet a public health emergency of international concern.
Japan reports a record high temperature for the month of June of in Isesaki, Gunma Prefecture.

context: Member states of the Commonwealth of Nations
text: Togo and Gabon officially become members of the Commonwealth of Nations.
The National Assembly convenes to debate the possible removal of president Guillermo Lasso amidst ongoing protests.

context: Gun politics in the United States
text: U.S. President Joe Biden signs the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act into law.
The 19th Mediterranean Games opens in Oran, Algeria.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Several Russian cruise missiles strike Kyiv, killing one civilian and injuring four others, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General. Some of the missiles were launched from Tupolev Tu-95 strategic bombers over the Caspian Sea.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A missile strike kills a civilian and destroys a strategic bridge connecting western Ukraine with eastern battlefields in Cherkasy Oblast.
Two police officers are killed and another is injured in Dassari, Benin, by militants suspected to be from Niger or Burkina Faso.
A shootout occurs between the Mexican federal police and drug cartels in Nuevo León, close to the Mexico–United States border. Six officers are killed and four others injured.
Two soldiers and seven militants are killed in a shootout in Ghulam Khan, North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Seven Sudanese soldiers and a civilian are summarily executed after being held captive in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Twenty-one people are found dead at a tavern in East London, Eastern Cape, South Africa. The cause of their deaths is unclear.
One person is killed and another is reported missing after a fire on an inter-island ferry in Manila, Philippines.
Two people are killed and nine others are injured in a fire at a market in Bangkok, Thailand.
Four people are killed and 322 are injured when a stand in a bullring collapses in El Espinal, Colombia.
Three people are killed in Brentwood, California, U.S., when their car collides with an Amtrak train.
Two people are killed and more are missing after heavy flooding in Krasnodar region and annexed Crimea, Russia.
Russian President Vladimir Putin embarks on a foreign trip to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, his first since the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

The G7 summit kicks off in Schloss Elmau, Krün, Bavarian Alps, Germany, and will last until June 28. Prime Minister Fumio Kishida and German Chancellor Olaf Scholz makes their first appearance at the summit.
Riot police disperse hundreds of people in Istanbul after the government banned the Pride Parade, alleging that the parade could cause "public unrest due to society's sensitivities".
Nigeria's Zamfara State begins issuing firearms licenses to citizens so that they can defend themselves from bandit gangs.

The Knesset advances a bill, for a possible vote on Wednesday, which would ban indicted politicians from becoming Prime Minister of Israel. If passed, it would prevent Benjamin Netanyahu from returning to that post.
In ice hockey, the Colorado Avalanche defeat the Tampa Bay Lightning in six games to win their first Stanley Cup since the 2001 season, thereby dethroning the Lightning in their quest to three-peat.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kremenchuk shopping mall attack
text: Two missiles strike a crowded mall in the city of Kremenchuk, killing at least 13 people and injuring at least 50 others. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that more than a thousand people were in the mall at time of the attack.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Governor of Luhansk Oblast claims that a Russian strike in Lysychansk killed eight civilians who were collecting water and injured 21 others.

Russia defaults on two Taiwanese-owned Eurobonds worth US$100 million after Western sanctions on Russia led Euroclear to block Russian attempts to service the debt before yesterday's deadline. Russia describes the default as artificially manufactured and "a farce". The default will have few immediate consequences for Russia since the country is currently unable to borrow internationally due to the SWIFT ban against Russian banks.
Twelve people are killed and 251 others injured by a toxic gas leak in the port of Aqaba, Jordan.

An Amtrak Southwest Chief passenger train carrying 243 passengers collides with a dump truck near Mendon, Missouri, United States. Eight cars and two locomotives are subsequently derailed, killing three people and injuring at least 50 others.
At least 51 people are found dead inside a tractor-trailer in San Antonio, Texas, United States. Sixteen others are transported to hospitals.
The Japanese government asks the public to conserve energy and to prepare for power outages as the country faces a heat wave.
One person is killed and five others injured after a bullet train collides with an engine in Bohumin, Czech Republic.
Four people are injured when an apartment roof collapses in Budapest, Hungary.
One person is killed and ten others injured after a tornado hits Zierikzee, Netherlands.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Germany
text: Germany reports almost one hundred new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the Netherlands
text: The Netherlands reports more than forty new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Minnesota reports its first case of monkeypox.
Peru reports its first case of monkeypox.
The World Health Organization confirms the first death caused by the 2022 monkeypox outbreak.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Nauru
text: Nauru surpasses 2,000 COVID-19 cases amid an outbreak and emergency declared by President Lionel Aingimea.

World leaders at the G7 summit in Germany issue a statement pledging more financial, humanitarian, military and diplomatic support to Ukraine. This comes after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a video calling for more heavy weapons from allies.

context: Abortion in the United States > Abortion in Louisiana, Abortion in Utah
text: State judges in New Orleans and in Utah temporarily block the abortion bans for all stages of pregnancy that state officials announced after the Supreme Court's ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.

context: Abortion in the United States > Abortion in South Carolina
text: A federal judge in South Carolina lifts an injunction on the so-called heartbeat bill, effectively limiting abortion to about six weeks into pregnancy.
One person is killed and five others injured in a mass stabbing at a shelter for asylum-seekers in Kressbronn, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

World Rugby rejects the Spanish Rugby Federation's appeal against their national team's disqualification in the 2023 Rugby World Cup for fielding an ineligible player during the qualifying tournament, thus confirming Romania's qualification to the World Cup by taking Spain's berth as Europe 2.
The United Nations estimates that more than 300,000 people have been killed since the start of the civil war in 2011, which is 1.5% of Syria's pre-war population.
Two policemen and a polio vaccinator are shot dead by gunmen on motorcycles in North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

context: 2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis, 2021–2022 global energy crisis
text: Sri Lanka's power and energy minister Kanchana Wijesekera announces that the government will lift restrictions on fuel imports in response to the country's energy crisis, ending a fuel duopoly between the state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and the Indian government-owned Lanka IOC.

context: 2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis, 2021–2022 global energy crisis
text: Sri Lanka suspends sales of fuel for non-essential vehicles. For the next two weeks, only buses, trains and vehicles used for medical services and transporting food will be allowed to refuel.
A fire occurs during a prison riot in Tuluá, Colombia, killing 51 inmates and injuring 24 others.
The United States government provides US$55 million in immediate humanitarian funding following the devastating earthquake in southern Afghanistan that killed at least 1,000 people.
Nineteen people are killed when a building collapses in Mumbai, India.
Tokyo records the city's highest temperature since 1875 as a heat wave continues. Several people are hospitalized due to heatstroke.
Four people are killed when a helicopter crashes into the Arabian Sea near India.
Authorities in Argentina issue a blizzard warning for Neuquén Province as roads remain blocked by snow.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Germany
text: Germany reports nearly 70 new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Portugal
text: Portugal reports more than ten new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Spain
text: Spain reports nearly 200 new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom reports nearly 200 cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: France reports more than 100 new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Italy reports two new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Romania reports three new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Switzerland reports four new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Israel reports five new cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Nebraska reports its first case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Ohio reports its second case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The CDC announces that they will activate an emergency operations center for monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The Biden administration announces that over 296,000 doses of the monkeypox vaccine will be distributed to combat the spread of monkeypox, including 56,000 doses of the Jynneos vaccine.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The total number of monkeypox cases in the United States reaches 300.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Canada
text: Canada reports more than 40 new cases of monkeypox.
Peru reports two new cases of monkeypox.
South Africa reports its second case of monkeypox.
Benin reports their first three cases of monkeypox.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi
text: Delhi reports their first case of the Omicron BA.5 variant.

context: 2022 NATO Madrid summit, Enlargement of NATO
text: Turkey, Finland, and Sweden sign a joint memorandum on security, clearing the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO accession bids.
Iranian nuclear talks are moved to Qatar in a new bid to revive the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

context: Freedom of the press in India
text: Police in India arrest Mohammed Zubair, co-founder of fact-checking website Alt News who has been a vocal critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

Six police officers are injured and two bank robbers killed in a shootout at a bank in Saanich, British Columbia, Canada. Nearby homes and businesses are later evacuated due to a potential explosive device in the area.
Russian opposition politician Ilya Yashin is sentenced to two weeks in prison after being arrested yesterday for "disobeying police".

Protesting against the government's nitrogen policy, a group of Dutch farmers gathered at Minister for Nature and Nitrogen Policy Christianne van der Wal's home and rioted, forcing some police officers on the scene to flee for their own safety.

context: Scottish independence > Proposed second Scottish independence referendum
text: Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, announces during a parliamentary debate session that an independence referendum bill will be tabled in the Scottish Parliament. The bill sets the date for the break-up vote at October 19, 2023. Sturgeon will try to bypass Prime Minister Boris Johnson's unlikely permission to conduct the referendum by referring the bill to the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom.
In motorsport, Red Bull terminates Estonian driver Jüri Vips's contract with its junior team following an incident where Vips was heard using the word "nigga" on a Twitch livestream.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: De jure mayor of Kherson Ihor Kolykhaiev is detained by Russian security forces after Russian-installed officials say that he refused to follow orders.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: The Russian-appointed military-civilian authorities in Kherson announce a referendum on whether to join Russia.

context: 2022 Muhammad remarks controversy > Murder of Kanhaiya Lal
text: Protests and arson incidents occur in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India, after a Hindu man is murdered and beheaded in his shop by two Islamic extremists for supporting controversial remarks by a politician about the prophet Muhammad.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Timeline of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict in 2022
text: A Palestinian Islamic Jihad member is killed during clashes with Israeli soldiers in Jenin, in the occupied West Bank.

The Sudanese Armed Forces fire heavy artillery during clashes in the disputed eastern region of Al Fushqa District bordering Ethiopia, after Ethiopia was accused by Sudan of murdering seven soldiers and a civilian. Ethiopia denies responsibility for the killings and instead blames a local armed group.

A journalist for the Expreso newspaper is killed and his daughter is critically wounded by gunmen in Ciudad Victoria, Tamaulipas, Mexico. The victim is the 12th journalist murdered in Mexico this year.
Several miners including four Chinese nationals are kidnapped by terrorists in Shiroro, Niger State, Nigeria.
Six people are killed and several others are injured when a car bomb targeting the convoy of a military official explodes in Aden, Yemen.
Twenty people are found dead in the Libyan Desert, after they went missing fourteen days ago. The group, mainly composed by migrants from Chad, died of thirst.
A state of emergency is declared on Tinian, Northern Mariana Islands due to a toxic fire.
The Pino Hachado Pass between Argentina and Chile is closed as blizzards and heavy snowfall block the passage between the two countries.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Estonia reports its first case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Michigan and New Hampshire report their first cases of monkeypox.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea > COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea
text: South Korea approves the SKYCovione vaccine, their first domestically produced COVID-19 vaccine, for use in people over the age of 18 years.

The European Council broadly agrees on several measures to combat climate change. Among them is a ban on combustion engines for new cars beginning in 2035, setting aside €59 billion for a special fund to reduce the cost of transition for the poorest populations, to be paid out from 2027 to 2032, reduction of carbon dioxide emissions by 55% from the 1990 reference level, and a carbon market reform. Negotiations on the final version of these reforms is underway.
Officials from the United States and the Taliban are expected to meet in Doha, Qatar, to discuss the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan, worsened by the earthquake.

At the NATO summit, U.S. President Joe Biden announces that a new permanent U.S. military base will be established in Poland - the 5th Army's Headquarters - which has had a forward command post in the city of Poznań since last year. Poland's government has long requested such a base.
Syria officially confirms its recognition of the Luhansk People's Republic and Donetsk People's Republic, two breakaway states in southern Ukraine.

The Securities and Exchange Commission of the Philippines upholds a previous appeal to invalidate online news website Rappler's operating license for violating constitutional foreign equity restrictions on mass media ownership, thus ordering the website's termination. Rappler co-founder and 2021 Nobel Peace Prize recipient Maria Ressa says that her company will contest the ruling in court.
American singer R. Kelly is sentenced to 30 years in prison for racketeering and sex trafficking.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Snake Island during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, List of military occupations
text: Russia announces that it has withdrawn from Snake Island, in the Black Sea, as a "gesture of goodwill", ending the occupation of the island that began in February. However, Ukraine says that it drove out Russian forces from the island after a massive artillery assault.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Timeline of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict in 2022
text: Two Israeli civilians and a soldier are injured after Palestinian militants open fire inside Joseph's Tomb in Nablus.
Eight protesters are killed by Sudanese security forces in Omdurman.
For the first time since Russia began occupying the Ukrainian city of Berdiansk, a cargo ship departs from the city's port.
Hurricane watches are issued for Nicaragua and Costa Rica as Potential Tropical Cyclone Two is expected to form into Tropical Storm Bonnie in the coming hours.
Nineteen people are killed, and 48 others are feared dead, after a massive landslide in Manipur, India.
Four people are killed and three others injured after a jeep carrying migrants crashes into a trailer in Encinal, Texas, United States.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: New York Governor Kathy Hochul announces that the state will distribute more than 8,000 doses of the smallpox vaccine to help combat the spread of monkeypox.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio > COVID-19 pandemic and animals, COVID-19 pandemic in Columbus, Ohio
text: An Amur tiger at the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium in Columbus, Ohio, U.S., dies from COVID-19, making it the first animal at the zoo to die from the disease.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Nauru
text: Nauru surpasses 3,000 cases of COVID-19, about a third of the country's population.

context: Climate change in the United States > Climate change policy of the United States > West Virginia v. EPA
text: In a 6–3 decision, the Supreme Court rules that the Environmental Protection Agency has not received legislative authorization under the Clean Air Act to introduce regulations on carbon dioxide emissions from power plants by compelling them to change the resources from which they generate the power. This will likely reduce the United States' ability to address its environmental goals.

context: 2022 European heat waves > June 2022 European heat wave
text: Slovakia measures the highest ever temperature in June in Somotor near Košice, reaching .
The European Union signs a free trade agreement with New Zealand.
The Supreme Administrative Court of Poland upholds lower court rulings that annulled anti-LGBT resolutions, known as "LGBT-free zones", that had been adopted by some local authorities.
The International Criminal Court asks for the arrest of three South Ossetian servicemen for alleged war crimes during the 2008 conflict.

Two police officers and a police dog are killed, and six other people are injured, in a mass shooting in Allen, Kentucky, United States. The suspect, on whom the officers were attempting to serve a warrant, is later taken into custody.
New Zealand designates American far-right groups Proud Boys and The Base as terrorist organizations.

context: Presidency of Bongbong Marcos > Inauguration of Bongbong Marcos
text: Bongbong Marcos is sworn in as the 17th President of the Philippines.
Three new provinces are created in West Papua, Indonesia.

context: 2019–2022 Israeli political crisis > 2022 Israeli legislative election
text: The Knesset votes to disband itself and sets November 1 as the date for the new elections. Foreign Minister and Alternate Prime Minister Yair Lapid will succeed Naftali Bennett as Prime Minister until a new government is formed.
The Kiribati High Court is left judgeless as the government of the country fires the only judge sitting on the bench at the time. The other judge had also been ordered to step down.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Serhiivka missile strike
text: At least 21 civilians are killed and 38 others injured when two Russian missiles strike a multi-story building and a recreation centre in Serhiivka, Odesa Oblast.
The Bulgarian Navy destroys a naval mine that had drifted close to the country's Black Sea coast in a controlled explosion. A team of divers stated that the mine was of Soviet origin.

context: Ukrainian cultural heritage during the 2022 Russian invasion
text: UNESCO inscribes Ukraine's borscht culture into its list of endangered intangible cultural heritage.
Sri Lanka's inflation rate reaches a record 54.6% amid a steep economic crisis and a default of the country's debt.
Five people are killed and 49 are injured after a magnitude 6.1 earthquake hits Hormozgan province, Iran.
Argentina issues a notice of polar wave temperatures. The meteorological authorities also report that the country experienced one of the coldest autumns in more than 60 years.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Turkey reports its first case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Germany
text: Germany surpasses 1,000 cases of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Wisconsin reports its first case of monkeypox.
Puerto Rico, Saint Lucia and the Bahamas report their first cases of monkeypox.

Authorities in the Donetsk People's Republic announce that they will begin carrying out capital punishment in 2025, after three foreign fighters, two of them British and the third Moroccan, who were arrested in the republic after joining the Ukrainian Army amidst the ongoing Russian invasion, are sentenced to death by the court.
A third police officer dies from injuries sustained in yesterday's shootout in Floyd County, Kentucky, United States.

The trial of American basketball player Brittney Griner begins in Moscow, Russia. Griner was detained at a Moscow airport in February and could face up to ten years in prison if she is convicted on drug charges.
Philadelphia Flyers prospect and former CSKA Moscow goaltender Ivan Fedotov is arrested in Saint Petersburg for allegedly evading military service.
John Lee is sworn in as the fifth Chief Executive of Hong Kong.
Protests occur in the autonomous Uzbekistani region of Karakalpakstan against a proposed constitutional change that would strip the region of its autonomy.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Mariupol City Council claims that over 10,000 of the city's residents are being held prisoner by the separatist Donetsk People's Republic.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko claims that his country intercepted Ukrainian missiles directed at Belarus three days ago and says that Belarus "does not want war with Ukraine".
At least 30 people are killed in an ambush in Shiroro, Niger State, Nigeria.
The Israeli Navy intercepts three Hezbollah drones from Lebanon in Israeli airspace.

context: 2022 Atlantic hurricane season > Tropical Storm Bonnie
text: Tropical Storm Bonnie makes landfall near the Costa Rica–Nicaragua border. The storm subsequently crosses over from the Atlantic basin to the Pacific basin, becoming the first storm to do so since Hurricane Otto in 2016. One person is reported missing in Trinidad and Tobago.
Tropical Storm Colin makes landfall in South Carolina, United States.
Typhoon Chaba, also known as Typhoon Caloy, makes landfall in Guangdong, China, as a category one typhoon.
More than two dozen people are missing after an engineering vessel sinks off the coast of Hong Kong during the storm.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: The World Health Organization announces that European cases of monkeypox have tripled in the past two weeks.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe
text: Andorra reports its first case of monkeypox.
Two people are killed and four others injured in a mass shooting in Haltom City, Texas, United States.
The government of Uzbekistan drops plans to strip Karakalpakstan of its autonomy amid widespread protests in the region.
Internet access is restricted in Uzbekistan as regional protests continue for a second day, with the government accusing a "criminal gang" of trying to seize government buildings in Karakalpakstan.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Three people are killed by explosions at residential buildings in Belgorod, Russia, near the border with Ukraine. Fifty buildings are partially destroyed by the explosions.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Armed forces of Russia and the separatist Luhansk People's Republic capture the entire Luhansk Oblast after seizing Lysychansk. Ukrainian forces confirm that they were forced to retreat.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Six people are killed and many others are injured as heavy shelling from rocket launchers hit the city of Sloviansk, in Donetsk Oblast, according to a report from the city's mayor.
Five people are killed and thousands are injured after mass protests in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan. President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev accuses "rioters" of violence.
Seven people are killed, eight are injured, and 13 others are reported missing after a serac collapses in Marmolada, Italy.
Twenty people are killed and 13 others are injured when a bus plunges into a deep ravine in Sherani District, Balochistan, Pakistan.
Two people are killed in a shark attack off the coast of Sahl Hasheesh, Egypt, on the Red Sea.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Nauru
text: Nauru reports its first death from COVID-19.
Three people are killed and four more are injured during a mass shooting at the Field's shopping centre in Amager, Copenhagen, Denmark. A suspect has been arrested.
Fifty-one people are arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy while trying to emigrate to Australia by sea. Police said that undocumented immigration has increased because of Sri Lanka's economic crisis.

context: 2022 Formula One World Championship > 2022 British Grand Prix
text: Spanish racing driver Carlos Sainz Jr. of Scuderia Ferrari wins the first Formula One race of his career.
Ian Nepomniachtchi wins the tournament with only one round remaining and qualifies for the World Chess Championship 2023 against current World Chess Champion Magnus Carlsen.

Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy Ahmed says that "citizens in the Oromia region’s Qellen Wellega area have come under a massacre" by the Oromo Liberation Army. Lobbyists say that 150–160 Amhara civilians have been killed.
Twenty-two people are killed and many others injured during a raid by insurgents in Kossi Province, Burkina Faso.
The government of Uzbekistan says 18 people have been killed and 243 others injured as protests appear to stabilise in Karakalpakstan, though concerns over the possibility of ethnic conflict remain.
Sri Lanka announces a week-long holiday amid fuel and food shortages caused by a worsening economic crisis.
Turkey records its highest inflation in 24 years, which is currently near 80%.
El Salvador suspends classes as Hurricane Bonnie passes through Central America. Deaths have been reported in Nicaragua and El Salvador.
Sixteen people are killed when a bus plunges into a deep gorge in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, India.
At least 300 people are injured by a chlorine gas leak in Qalat Sukkar, Iraq.
Italian prime minister Mario Draghi declares a state of emergency in five regions of Northern Italy due to a severe drought in the Po Valley.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Nauru
text: Weightlifter Reanna Solomon dies from COVID-19, becoming Nauru's first recorded fatality of the pandemic.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore
text: President of Singapore Halimah Yacob tests positive for COVID-19.

context: Mass shootings in the United States > Highland Park parade shooting
text: Six people are killed and more than two dozen others injured in a mass shooting in Highland Park, Illinois, United States, during an Independence Day parade. The suspected gunman is later taken into custody in nearby Lake Forest.

context: Mass shootings in the United States
text: One person is killed and four others injured in a mass shooting outside a nightclub in Sacramento, California, United States.
Papua New Guineans go to the polls to elect their new government in a heavily guarded election.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: According to Ukraine, two civilians are killed in a Russian missile attack on Sloviansk in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: The Governor of Donetsk Oblast urges civilians to evacuate as Russia advances. Around 350,000 civilians have already evacuated.
An Israeli man is seriously injured in a stabbing and suspected terror attack on the road between Bnei Brak and Giv'at Shmuel.
Six people are killed and 32 others injured in an explosion at an arms depot in Abyan Governorate.
Seven soldiers are injured when suspected communist guerrillas detonate a land mine in Mapanas, Northern Samar, Philippines.
Two Egyptian UN peacekeepers are killed and five others are injured when their vehicle hits a mine in northern Mali.
Five rockets are fired into Uzbekistan from Afghanistan, landing in the city of Termez. Government officials report that none of the missiles exploded and that minor damage occurred to four homes.
Sri Lanka's inflation continues to increase and reaches nearly 60% as the country's economic crisis worsens.
South Korea's inflation reaches a 24-year record, as the country struggles with increasing energy and food prices.
Chinese company BYD Auto becomes the world’s largest electric vehicle producer by number of vehicles sold after overtaking Tesla, Inc. in the first half of 2022.
At least nine people are killed by flash floods caused by the monsoon in Balochistan, Pakistan.
Three people are killed by flooding in Kuala Pegang, Malaysia.

Twenty-two Malian migrants are found dead on an inflatable boat on the Mediterranean Sea off the Libyan coast, after they left Zuwarah nine days ago. The International Organization for Migration reports that the migrants died from dehydration and drowning.
Panama confirms its first case of monkeypox.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Queen Consort Letizia of Spain tests positive for COVID-19.

context: Enlargement of NATO > Finland–NATO relations, Sweden–NATO relations
text: All 30 members of NATO have signed off on the accession protocols for the membership bids of Finland and Sweden, which is subject to unanimous approval by the current members' legislative bodies.
