context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A drone strikes Russia's Black Sea Fleet headquarters, injuring five people, according to the mayor of Sevastopol.

Kosovo Police close two border crossings in North Kosovo after local Serbs blocked roads and fired shots at police to protest an order to switch Serbian car license plates to Kosovan ones within two months.
A member of the Taliban is killed during clashes with Iranian border guards on the Afghanistan–Iran border.
The death toll from the ongoing flash floods in Kentucky, United States, increases to 28.
Heavy rainfall warnings are issued for the affected areas of Kentucky as Governor Andy Beshear says that at least 37 people remain unaccounted for.
Malagasy President Andry Rajoelina mobilizes and deploys the army after 32 people were killed in Ankazobe on July 29 by cattle thieves.

context: 2022 Republic of the Congo parliamentary election
text: The second round of the parliamenentary election takes place.
England defeats Germany 2–1 in the final of the UEFA Women's Euro 2022 to give the England women's team its first major football championship.

context: War on terror > Afghanistan conflict > Drone strikes in Afghanistan > Killing of Ayman al-Zawahiri
text: A U.S. drone strike in Kabul kills Ayman al-Zawahiri, al-Qaeda's leader since the death of Osama bin Laden in 2011. The airstrike is also the first U.S. military action in Afghanistan following the Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan last year.
Shelling and heavy gunfire is reported near two villages by Artsakh authorities in Nagorno-Karabakh. The reports are denied by Azerbaijan and Russian forces in the region.
The first ship with Ukrainian grain leaves the port of Odesa for Lebanon after an agreement was signed with Russia.
The death toll from the ongoing flash floods in Kentucky and Virginia, United States, increases to 35 with 37 people missing.
Twenty-four people are killed by heavy flooding in eastern Uganda.
Nine people are killed and 76 others are injured after a fuel tanker explodes in Bent Bayya, Wadi al Hayaa District, Libya.
More than two million people are under red flag warnings in the United States as wildfires continue to spread in Northern California, Oregon, Washington, Montana, South Dakota, and Nebraska.
A Pakistan Army Aviation Corps helicopter carrying several senior Pakistan Army officials crashes in Balochistan. Rescuers have not yet reached the crash site due to ongoing floods in the region.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in India
text: India reports its first confirmed monkeypox related death in Kerala.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Peru
text: Peru reports its first confirmed death from monkeypox in a 45-year-old male with underlying health conditions.
Ghana reports its first confirmed death from monkeypox.
New Zealand has fully reopened its international borders after two years, becoming the last country in the western world to open for tourists.

A post made by the VK social media account of Dmitry Medvedev, the incumbent Deputy Chairman of the Security Council of Russia and former President of Russia, refers to Georgia and Kazakhstan as "artificial" creations and advocates the return of the two countries to Russian sovereignty. The post is quickly taken down and attributed to hackers.
Iran announces the arrest of several members of the Baháʼí Faith on charges of spying.
Citizens of the Cook Islands head to the polls to vote in a general election.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Three people evacuating in a minibus are killed by Russian shelling near Kherson Oblast, according to Ukraine's Operational Command South.
Fifty-three people are injured after a suspected gas leak in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: California declares a state of emergency due to the ongoing monkeypox outbreak.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines
text: The Department of Health announces that the Philippines have reported their first two cases of the Omicron BA.2.75 variant in two individuals from Western Visayas.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea
text: South Korea surpasses 20 million cases of COVID-19, becoming the eighth country to do so.

context: Taiwan–United States relations > Nancy Pelosi's Taiwan visit
text: U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi arrives in Taiwan despite Chinese threats of military action in response to her visit. Pelosi is the most senior U.S. official to visit the self-governing island since Newt Gingrich in 1997.

context: Taiwan–United States relations > Nancy Pelosi's Taiwan visit
text: The People's Liberation Army is placed on high alert and says that it will launch "targeted military operations" in response to Pelosi's visit to Taiwan.

context: Abortion in the United States > Abortion in Kansas > 2022 Kansas Value Them Both Amendment
text: In the first referendum since the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, Kansas voters reject an amendment in the state constitution that would grant state lawmakers the ability to apply anti-abortion restrictions.

In the first legal challenge to a state's abortion law since the Supreme Court's June decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, the Department of Justice (DOJ) files a lawsuit in a federal court against the state of Idaho to block a state law that the DOJ says imposes a "near-absolute ban" on abortion in Idaho.
The Russian Supreme Court declares the Azov Regiment a terrorist organization.
Two Taliban policemen and three Islamic State gunmen are killed during a gunbattle at a hideout in Kabul. Four other officers are wounded.
Reignited clashes in the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region between Armenia and Azerbaijan kill three soldiers and injure fourteen others.
Seventeen people are killed and four others are injured after a minibus collides with a truck in Juhaynah, Sohag Governorate, Egypt.
Two people are killed after heavy flooding in The Gambia.
Eight people are injured after an explosion at a factory in Bergerac, France.

context: Cross-Strait relations > 2022 United States congressional delegation visit to Taiwan
text: China warns airlines to avoid areas near Taiwan as it conducts military exercises in response to U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's visit to the island.
Three people are killed and six others are injured in a mass stabbing attack at a kindergarten in Anfu County, Jiangxi, China.

Belarusian journalist Iryna Slaunikava is sentenced to five years in prison amidst a government crackdown on the media following protests that occurred after the 2020 Belarusian presidential election.
American basketball player Brittney Griner is sentenced to nine years in prison by a Russian court after being found guilty of bringing cannabis-infused vape cartridges into Russia.
Prime Minister of Peru Aníbal Torres resigns citing "personal reasons", amid multiple criminal investigations focusing on president Pedro Castillo.
The former chairman of the Union of Values and federal presidential candidate for the AfD, Max Otte, is legally expelled from the CDU.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: A Russian strike kills eight civilians and injures four others, at a bus stop in Toretsk, according to regional governor Pavlo Kyrylenko.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Amnesty International releases a report alleging Ukrainian forces have endangered civilians by establishing bases and operating weapons systems in residential areas, schools, hospitals, violating international humanitarian law as they turn civilian objects into military targets.
Thirteen people, including nine civilians, are killed in a militant attack in Bam, Burkina Faso; thirty-four insurgents are also killed.
The Bank of England raises its benchmark interest rate from 1.25% to 1.75% in its largest single rate hike since 1995.
Twelve people are killed when a truck collides with a commuter bus in Central Region, Ghana.
Three people are killed and a fourth person is seriously injured by a lightning strike at Lafayette Square in Washington, D.C., United States.
Six people are killed and eight others are injured when nurse Nicole Linton drove into multiple cars at over 130MPH in Windsor Hills, California.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The Biden administration declares the ongoing monkeypox outbreak to be a public health emergency.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: The United States Food and Drug Administration announces that it will permit the use of Bavarian Nordic's Jynneos vaccine in children on a case by case basis.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa > COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa
text: South Africa reports its first death linked to the COVID-19 vaccine in a person who received the Johnson & Johnson vaccine.

context: Cross-Strait relations > 2022 United States congressional delegation visit to Taiwan
text: China launches missiles off the coast of Taiwan as part of military exercises conducted following the visit from U.S. Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: Ukraine's nuclear agency Energoatom says that Russian rockets have caused damage to the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, including a nitrogen-oxygen unit and a high-voltage power line.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
text: Volodymyr Saldo, the head of the Russian occupational administration in Kherson Oblast, is hospitalized, with former FSB officer Sergei Eliseev taking over his post temporarily.

Israel launches a series of airstrikes in the Gaza Strip, including a number against Palestinian Islamic Jihad's facilities. Ten people are killed and 55 others are wounded, including PIJ military leader Tayseer Jabari.

context: Afghanistan conflict > Islamic State–Taliban conflict > 5 August 2022 Kabul bombing
text: Eight people are killed and 18 others are injured when a bomb hidden in a cart explodes near a Shiite mosque in Kabul. The Islamic State claims responsibility for the attack.
The Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance signs a peace deal with the government of Senegal, pledging to lay down its arms in order to work towards a permanent solution.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin signs a decree banning investors from "unfriendly countries" from selling their assets in Russian banks, strategic entities, and energy and commodity projects until December 31.
Fourteen people are killed and over 40 others injured in a fire at a nightclub in Sattahip district, Chonburi province, Thailand.
The death toll from the flash floods in Pakistan increases to 550.
Five people are killed and 44 others injured in a fire at a hospital in Icheon, South Korea.
Ten people are killed in a house fire in Nescopeck, Pennsylvania, United States.
One person is killed and another is injured after heavy flooding in Dakar, Senegal.
Fifteen people are injured when an SUV crashes into a Native American parade in Gallup, New Mexico, United States.

A Texas jury reaches a verdict against Alex Jones and orders that he pay $45.2 million in punitive damages to the parents of a 6-year-old boy killed in the 2012 Sandy Hook massacre for falsely claiming the shooting was a hoax.

Provisional results show that the Benno Bokk Yakaar coalition wins 82 seats, falling 1 seat short of an absolute majority, while 80 seats were won by the opposition coalitions Yewwi Askan Wi and Wallu Sénégal.

context: 2022 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
text: The opposition Saint Kitts and Nevis Labour Party, led by Terrance Drew, wins the snap general election to the National Assembly. Drew becomes the prime minister-elect.
Israel launches airstrikes for the second day in the Gaza Strip, killing 14 people and injuring several others. Nineteen Palestinian Islamic Jihad members are also arrested in the West Bank.
Twelve people are killed and 32 others are injured when a bus carrying pilgrims from Poland to Medjugorje, Bosnia and Herzegovina, crashes in Podvorec, Croatia.
One person is killed and at least 121 others are injured after a lightning strike causes a fire near the supertanker port in Matanzas, Cuba.
Four people are killed and eight others are injured when a bus travelling from Istanbul, Turkey, to Bucharest, Romania, crashes near Veliko Tarnovo, Bulgaria.

context: 2022 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
text: Terrance Drew is sworn in as prime minister of Saint Kitts and Nevis.
sources: The St Kitts and Nevis Observer

text: Israel and the Islamic Jihad agree to a ceasefire agreement for the Gaza Strip.

context: Islamist insurgency in the Sahel > Mali War
text: Forty-two soldiers and four civilians are killed during an attack near the town of Tessit by Islamic State in the Greater Sahara gunmen. Twenty-two other soldiers are wounded, and 37 of the attackers are also killed.

context: Ituri conflict, 2021–2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: Twenty people are killed when suspected Islamists attack two villages in Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Senior Pakistani Taliban militant Omar Khalid Khorasani and three other militants are killed as their vehicle hit a roadside bomb in Paktika Province, Afghanistan.
Gustavo Petro is inaugurated as the first left-wing president of Colombia.

The government of Chad and more than 30 rebel and opposition factions sign a peace agreement at talks in Doha, Qatar. However, the main rebel group Front for Change and Concord in Chad rejects the agreement, saying that negotiators had not listened to their demands, which included the release of political prisoners.

context: Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Pentagon announces that it will send Ukraine an additional $1 billion in military assistance, including tens of thousands more munitions and explosives, the largest such aid package to the country since the start of the invasion.
Russia suspends New START arms inspections of its nuclear weapons in response to travel restrictions imposed by the United States and its allies.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation executes a search warrant at Mar-a-Lago, the primary residence of former U.S. president Donald Trump, as part of a Justice Department investigation into Trump.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian summer counteroffensive
text: Multiple explosions are reported at a Russian military air base near Novofedorivka in western Crimea. At least one person is killed and six others are injured, according to Crimean authorities.
Ibrahim al-Nabulsi, local head of the al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades, and two other people are killed during a raid by Israeli soldiers in Nablus. At least 40 others are injured.
Four Pakistani soldiers are killed in a suicide bombing in Mir Ali, North Waziristan, Pakistan.
Fifteen troops are killed when their vehicle hits a roadside bomb in Bam Province, Burkina Faso.
Four civilians and a soldier are killed, and another civilian is wounded, during three separate attacks by Boko Haram gunmen in the Far North Region, Cameroon.

Russia's Transneft says that Ukraine has suspended Russian oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline to the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia after it was unable to pay transit fees to Ukraine's pipeline operator UkrTransNafta. The Czech Republic's pipeline company says it expects supplies through the pipeline to restart within several days.
Nine people are killed by flooding caused by record-breaking rainfall in Seoul, South Korea.

Firefighters in Cuba bring a catastrophic fire at an oil terminal in Matanzas under control after it burned out of control for five consecutive days, destroying 40% of the country's main fuel storage facility and causing widespread blackouts.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands
text: The Marshall Islands confirm their first community transmission cases of COVID-19 in the capital Majuro. The government subsequently announces that the start of the school year will be delayed and suspends flights and boat travel to the country's outer islands.
Russia bans the import of agricultural products from Moldova from August 15 due to "repeated detection of dangerous quarantine objects in Moldovan products entering Russia".

A man is arrested for the killings of three Pakistani men last month and for the murder of an Afghan man in November 2021 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States. The alleged killer targeted the victims "because he was angry over his daughter marrying a Shiite Muslim"; all the victims were Shiite.
The driver of a pickup truck that collided with a motorcycle procession and killed seven people in Randolph, New Hampshire, United States in 2019 is acquitted on all charges.
Kenyans vote in a general election.
Radio astronomers have discovered a newborn, Jupiter-size exoplanet orbiting the star AS 209, using the Atacama Large Millimeter Array telescope in Chile.
Roscosmos launches the Iranian Space Agency's Earth observation satellite Khayyam from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The Chess Olympiad in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, concludes, with Uzbek chess grandmaster Nodirbek Abdusattorov winning the open event.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast
text: Russian forces install air defence systems at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, according to the head of Moscow-appointed administration of Zaporizhzhia Oblast Yevhen Balytskyi.
A Russian missile strike in Nikopol Raion, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, kills at least 13 civilians and injures 11 others.
Cartel gunmen in Mexico burn down dozens of stores and block streets with burning cars in the states of Jalisco and Guanajuato in response to arrests of cartel figures by the National Guard.

context: COVID-19 recession > Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Domino's Pizza closes all of its stores in Italy after its franchise holder ePizza SpA files for bankruptcy. The American restaurant chain says that it was severely impacted by COVID-19 restrictions in the country.
A house explodes in Evansville, Indiana, United States, killing at least three people, injuring one and damaging at least 39 nearby houses.
Anti-government protests occur in Sierra Leone, calling for the removal of President Julius Maada Bio. Both protestors and policemen are killed during clashes.
Uzbekistan's embassy in Russia warns its citizens not to join Russian forces invading Ukraine, saying that those who do so will be criminally liable for mercenaryism upon returning to Uzbekistan.
James Marape is re-elected unopposed as Prime Minister by the Parliament after his party Pangu Pati won the general election in July.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast
text: At least ten shells hit the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant with both Russia and Ukraine blaming each other for the attack, which damaged an office building and the plant's fire station.
Three soldiers are killed in an attack at a military base in Rajouri, Jammu and Kashmir, India. Two of the attackers are killed in the ensuing shootout.
Cleric Rahimullah Haqqani is killed by a suicide bomber at a seminary in Kabul, Afghanistan. IS-KP claims responsibility for the killing.
Five people are killed and 100 others injured as security forces clashes with protesters demanding presidential election be held in November in Somaliland.
Thirty-four people are injured after two rollercoaster trains collided at the Legoland Deutschland amusement park in Günzburg, Bavaria, Germany.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands
text: The Marshall Islands confirms its first death from COVID-19 in a person from Majuro.
The Latvian Parliament declares Russia a state sponsor of terrorism over its invasion of Ukraine.

Estonia and Latvia formally withdraw from the Cooperation between China and Central and Eastern European Countries group amid tensions with China over its human rights record and its support of Russia's war on Ukraine.
Sierra Leone declares a nationwide curfew amid anti-government protests that have killed two policemen and one civilian. The West African country is currently experiencing record inflation.

A gunman wearing body armor attempts to storm the offices of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States. Following a subsequent police pursuit, he is killed in a standoff with police.

A man takes several employees hostage at a bank in Beirut, Lebanon, demanding his bank savings and threatening to set himself on fire. Police officers, soldiers, and intelligence agents surround the building.
At least eight people are killed in police raids in Curitiba, Brazil.

context: Occupied territories of Ukraine > 2022 Russian-occupied Ukraine annexation referendums
text: The Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast begins preparations for a referendum on the region's accession to Russia, which will be held on September 11.

context: Islamist insurgency in the Sahel > Mali War
text: The German defence ministry suspends its military's aerial reconnaissance and transport operations in Mali after the government of Mali denied the departure of one of their flights.
Eight people are killed and five others injured in a prison riot and shootings at a food shop and a pizzeria in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua. Two other premises are set on fire.

At least a dozen vehicles are burned and several streets are blocked in the state of Baja California, mainly in the cities of Tijuana, Mexicali and Ensenada. This is the fourth major incident in the last week where arson and blocked streets have been reported.

Anglo-Indian writer Salman Rushdie is attacked at a public event in Chautauqua, New York, United States, sustaining multiple stab wounds to the neck and abdomen. The suspect is arrested by New York State Police.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Belize-flagged ship departs Chornomorsk for Turkey, becoming the first wheat export from Ukraine under a United Nations-brokered deal.
The Environment Agency of England declares a drought across eight of its fourteen areas amid an ongoing heat wave.

A mass die-off of fish occurs in the Oder river in Poland. Polish officials call it an "ecological catastrophe" with Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki vowing to "punish" those responsible. The public has been warned not to enter the water amid fears of possible contamination.
Three people are killed and 17 are missing after an overloaded boat capsizes in Uttar Pradesh, India.
Nine people are killed and 18 others injured after a microbus overturn in Minya, Egypt.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Micronesia
text: Incumbent Vice President Yosiwo George dies from COVID-19 at the age of 81.
A High Court Judge is detained following a failed deportation attempt by the Kiribati government.

A man kills a woman and two children at their home in Cetinje, Montenegro, before opening fire in the streets against random civilians, killing seven people and wounding six others. The perpetrator is later killed by an armed citizen.
South Korean president Yoon Suk-yeol pardons former Samsung executive Lee Jae-yeong, who was on parole for bribery.
Vice President of Paraguay Hugo Velázquez Moreno announces his resignation after being accused of corruption by the United States, which he denies being guilty of.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that it has captured the village of Pisky, in Donetsk Oblast, while Ukrainian forces say that they have destroyed a bridge in Russian-occupied Kherson Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian occupation of Mykolaiv Oblast
text: Establishment of pro-Russian Mykolaiv military–civilian administration with seat in Snihurivka is announced, becomes its head. It probably began functioning some days earlier.
Tropical Storm Meari makes landfall in central Japan, causing heavy rain and high winds. 72,000 people are evacuated from the city of Shizuoka.

The German environment ministry says that an unknown, highly toxic substance is responsible for the mass die-off of wildlife in the Oder river. High levels of mercury have also been found in the river. Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki says that the river will take years to "return to normal".
One person is killed and 40 others are injured when a stage at a music festival in Cullera, Valencia, Spain, collapses due to high winds caused by a nearby heat burst.
Flooding in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, kills two people and also damages The Linq hotel.

context: Treatment of women by the Taliban
text: The Taliban violently disperse a demonstration by women's rights activists who were marching to the education ministry in Kabul to demand broader rights, by chasing and beating women and firing gunshots into the air.

One person is killed and 17 others are injured after a driver plows his car into a fundraiser for victims of a house fire that killed ten people earlier in Nescopeck, Pennsylvania, United States. The perpetrator then kills his mother in a nearby town before being arrested.
Romanian swimmer David Popovici breaks the 13-year-old world record for the 100m freestyle with a time of 46.86.

A Palestinian gunman opens fire inside a bus in Jerusalem's Old City, injuring eight people, two of them critically. Israeli police later raid the Silwan neighborhood, where the suspect lived, and arrest him.
Five people are killed and 26 others are injured by an explosion in Guayaquil, Ecuador. The government blames organized crime groups.
At least 41 people are killed and 45 others are injured in a fire at the Saint Mercurius Coptic Orthodox church in Giza, Egypt.
More than 1,500 people are evacuated from Zaragoza, Spain, due to wildfires.

Six people are killed, 60 others injured and 18 more are missing in an explosion at a fireworks storage area of a mall in Yerevan, Armenia. The city's mayor stated that there were people trapped under rubble.
Seven people are killed by flooding caused by heavy rainfall in Pengzhou, Sichuan, China.

France formally ends its military intervention in Mali after withdrawing its last remaining troops from a military base in Gao. The base was handed over to Malian Armed Forces before the French forces crossed into neighbouring Niger.
Four Russian Wagner Group paramilitaries are killed during an ambush by Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants in Bandiagara.

context: War in Afghanistan > Fall of Kabul
text: The Taliban stages a Victory Day parade on the first anniversary of the capture of Kabul.

context: Israeli–Syrian ceasefire line incidents during the Syrian civil war
text: Israel launches a series of airstrikes on Damascus and Tartus, Syria, killing three soldiers and injuring three others.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom > COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom approves a Moderna COVID-19 vaccine aimed at targeting the Omicron variant and other variants of SARS-CoV-2, becoming the first country to do so.
The United States imposes sanctions on three senior members of the cabinet of Liberian president George Weah, accusing them of corruption.
Prime minister of New Zealand Jacinda Ardern announces the deployment of 120 New Zealand troops to the United Kingdom to train Ukrainian forces.
The military junta court sentences former state counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi to six years in prison for corruption.
A lawsuit is filed against the Central Intelligence Agency and its former director Mike Pompeo, accusing the agency of spying on lawyers and journalists who met with Julian Assange.
The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission declares William Ruto as the winner of the election.

FIFA suspends the All India Football Federation for violating its statutes on third-party interference. India is stripped of its hosting rights for international football tournaments, including the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup scheduled for October 2022.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: An explosion occurs at an ammunition depot in northern Crimea, forcing the evacuation of civilians. Observers suggest that the depot may have been hit by Ukrainian forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war > 2022 Jarqli airstrikes
text: Turkish airstrikes on a military base in Aleppo Governorate kill at least 16 Syrian soldiers.

Hamza Adel Al-Zamili, a leader of the Islamic State – Sinai Province and mastermind of the 2017 Sinai mosque attack, is killed by Egyptian soldiers during an operation. Nine other militants are also killed and three arrested.
A ranger is killed while seven policemen and two civilians are injured as two bombs explode at a rubber plantation in Narathiwat, Thailand.
Two policemen are killed when gunmen open fire on them as they are escorting polio workers in Gomal, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Twenty people are killed and six others are injured when a passenger bus collides with a tanker truck in Jalalpur Pirwala, Punjab, Pakistan.
Six people are killed and several others are injured when a bus falls into a gorge in Jammu and Kashmir, India.
One person is killed and nine others are injured when a test car crashes into traffic in Reutlingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
A Sudanese official reports that 66 people have been killed and 24,000 homes and buildings have been damaged since flooding began in June.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: U.S. First Lady Jill Biden tests positive for COVID-19.
A Saudi Arabian woman is sentenced to 34 years in prison for following and retweeting dissidents on Twitter.
The prime minister of Vanuatu Bob Loughman asks for the dissolution of parliament as he faces a vote of no-confidence.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Northeastern Ukraine campaign > Battle of Kharkiv
text: A Russian missile hits a dormitory in Kharkiv, killing seven civilians and injuring 16 others, according to the city's mayor and top military administrator.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia launches missile strikes on Odesa and Mykolaiv in Southern Ukraine in response to sabotage bombings of military facilities in Crimea.

context: Afghanistan conflict > August 2022 Kabul mosque bombing
text: Twenty-one people are killed and 33 others are injured by a mosque bombing in Kabul.
Inflation in the United Kingdom increases to 10.1%, the highest level since February 1982, due to increasing fuel and food prices.
The death toll from the August 6 fire at a supertanker port in Matanzas, Cuba, rises to 16. All the deceased were firefighters who were battling the blaze.
Twenty-six people are killed by wildfires in Algeria, mostly in the city of El Taref. .
Israel and Turkey restore full diplomatic relations for the first time since 2018.
Police in Tokyo, Japan, arrest a former member of the 2020 Summer Olympics organising committee after prosecutors accused him of graft and bribery.
The High Court of Australia rules that Google is not liable for defamatory material within hyperlinks that it serves as part of its search results.
Archaeologists discover one of the largest megalithic sites in Europe on a farm in southern Spain. The site dates back 7,000 years and contains more than 500 standing stones.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign, 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Explosions are reported at military facilities in Crimea and Belgorod Oblast, Russia, and are believed to have been launched by Ukraine. An explosion and large fire occur at an arms depot near Timonovo. Explosions are also reported at Stary Oskol Airport and in Russian-occupied Nova Kakhovka, Kherson Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign, 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Explosions are reported at Sevastopol International Airport. The Governor of Sevastopol Mikhail Razvozhayev says that Russian air defences have shot down a Ukrainian Air Force drone near the airport.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign, 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Residents of Kerch and nearby villages in eastern Crimea report multiple explosions. Crimean officials say that air defences were activated near the city but that "there is no danger to the town or the Crimean Bridge".

Mali accuses its former ally France of arming jihadist terrorist groups in order to destabilize the country. Malian Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop tells the United Nations that French aircraft are violating the country's airspace and dropping "arms and ammunition" to terrorist groups on the ground. France denies the accusations.

Timane Erdimi, leader of the Chadian rebel group Rally of Forces for Change and nephew of slain Chadian president Idriss Déby, returns to the country from his 17-year exile in Qatar to participate in a peace process between the government and numerous rebel groups.
The European Union statistics office reports that inflation in the Eurozone increased to a record 8.9% in July.
Six people are killed and 12 others are injured by strong winds on the island of Corsica, France.
Two people are killed and 20 others are injured by flooding in the region of Tuscany, Italy.
Five people are killed by storms in Austria.

The death toll from wildfires in Algeria increases to 38 with 200 others suffering from burns and respiratory problems. Firefighters are still trying to contain 39 forest fires in the north of the country, according to officials.
Sixteen people are killed and 36 others are reported missing after heavy rain causes flooding in Datong Hui and Tu Autonomous County, Qinghai, China.

Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Sarah Bianchi and Taiwanese minister John Deng announce that Taiwan and the United States will seek formal trade relations with each other, including cooperation on agricultural and digital trade, harmonizing anti-corruption standards, and addressing "significant distortions" caused by state-owned enterprises.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Wang Wenbin says that China will oppose any trade deals with the Taiwanese government and also told the U.S. government to "stop making misjudgements". Commerce Ministry spokesperson Shu Jueting also says that China will take steps to safeguard its interests.

context: 2021 Hong Kong democrats mass arrests, Hong Kong national security law
text: As the trial against 47 pro-democracy activists begins in Hong Kong, it is announced that 29 activists, including Joshua Wong and Benny Tai, will plead guilty and 18 activists, including Leung Kwok-hung, will plead not guilty.
A political organization in Guinea accuses military president Mamady Doumbouya of being behind the killings of two youths during anti-government protests yesterday.
President of Vanuatu Nikenike Vurobaravu dissolves the Parliament to prevent a no-confidence motion being debated against Prime Minister Bob Loughman. A snap election is expected to be called.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Explosions are reported overnight at Russian military bases in Crimea and Belgorod Oblast, Russia. Two villages have been evacuated.

context: Somali Civil War > 2022 Mogadishu hotel attack
text: At least 10 people are killed as al-Shabaab gunmen storm a hotel in Mogadishu, following two car bomb blasts and gunfire.
Fifteen people are killed and at least 28 others are injured in a rocket attack on a market in rebel-controlled Al-Bab, Aleppo Governorate, Syria.
A roadside bombing kills two Pakistani security forces in Bajaur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Russia's Gazprom announces that the Nord Stream 1 natural gas pipeline will be shut down for 3 days of unscheduled maintenance between August 31 and September 2.

The Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries says that a large overgrowth of toxic Prymnesium parvum algae linked to industrial pollution was likely the cause of the mass mortality event of fish in the Oder river.
Temperatures in Chongqing, China, reach during a historic drought. It is the highest temperature ever recorded in China outside of Xinjiang.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: The FDA announces that it has approved the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine for youths between the ages of 12 and 17.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand
text: Prime Minister Prayut Chan-o-cha announces that Thailand will lift its COVID-19 emergency decree and dissolve the Centre for COVID-19 Situation Administration (CCSA). Additionally, CCSA spokesman Thavisin Visanuyothin announces that the country will shift to an endemic phase of the disease beginning in October.

A Mexican court issues the arrest warrants for 83 suspects, consisting of military personnel, police officers, administrative and judicial authorities, and members of the Guerreros Unidos syndicate, in connection with the abduction and disappearance of 43 students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College in Iguala, Guerrero, on September 26, 2014.
Police in Nicaragua confirm that they have arrested an anti-Ortega Roman Catholic bishop in Managua and warned against further "provocative and destabilizing" activities amongst the clergy.

Islamic State and "Beatles" cell member El Shafee Elsheikh is sentenced to eight life sentences by a United States district court for his role in the kidnapping and deaths of hostages James Foley, Steven Sotloff, Peter Kassig, and Kayla Mueller.
A man is killed and a woman is injured in a shooting at the Emporia shopping centre in Malmö, Sweden.
Russia appoints former Krasnodar mayor Andrei Alekseyenko as the head of its Kharkiv military–civilian administration.

Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau nominates judge Michelle O'Bonsawin to the Supreme Court of Canada. An Abenaki member, O'Bonsawin would be the first Indigenous Canadian to sit on the country's highest court.

The government of Prime Minister of Montenegro Dritan Abazović collapses after the Parliament passes a vote of no-confidence following dispute within the coalition over an agreement the government signed with the Serbian Orthodox Church.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign, War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Nine civilians, including four children, are injured by Russian shelling on a residential building in Voznesensk, Mykolaiv Oblast, according to regional governor Vitaliy Kim.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign, War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that a number of its soldiers in Zaporizhzhia have been poisoned by Ukraine, with tests showing Botulinum toxin type B present in their bodies.
Sixteen people are killed and 21 others are injured when a bus crashes into the scene of an earlier road accident in Gaziantep Province, Turkey.
Twenty people are killed and 29 others are injured when a truck crashes into the scene of an earlier road accident involving three vehicles in Mardin Province, Turkey.
Four people are killed and others are reportedly trapped after a Shiite mosque collapsed during a landslide in Karbala, Iraq.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Indonesia confirms its first case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in North America
text: Cuba confirms its first case of monkeypox.
Darya Dugina, the daughter of far-right political philosopher Aleksandr Dugin, is killed by a car bomb in Moscow Oblast, Russia.

context: Somali Civil War > 2022 Mogadishu hotel attack
text: The siege at a hotel seized by al-Shabaab fighters in Mogadishu ends with the deaths of all of the attackers. Twenty-one other people were killed, and 117 others were injured.
Nine people are killed by heavy flooding in Khoshi District, Logar, Afghanistan.
Sixteen people are killed and three others are injured when a truck collides with a minibus in Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia.
At least 50 people are killed by flooding caused by heavy rains in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, India.
Nine soldiers are killed and four others are injured when their truck plunges into a ravine in Azad Kashmir, Pakistan.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Japan
text: Prime Minister Fumio Kishida tests positive for COVID-19.

The United Arab Emirates announces the reinstallation of its ambassador to Iran, which will take effect "in the coming days", more than six years after it cut off diplomatic relations with the Islamic republic.

Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says that Singapore will decriminalize sex between men, which is illegal under a colonial-era law, while also amending the Constitution to define marriage as a heterosexual union.
Oleksandr Nakonechny, regional head of the Security Service of Ukraine in Kirovohrad Oblast, is found dead in his apartment in an apparent suicide.

In tennis, world number 156 Borna Ćorić of Croatia becomes the lowest-ranked champion in the ATP Tour Masters 1000 after defeating Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece in the men's singles final of the 2022 Cincinnati Masters.

World number 17 Caroline Garcia of France becomes the first qualifier to win a WTA 1000 tournament after defeating Petra Kvitová of the Czech Republic in the women's singles final of the 2022 Cincinnati Masters.

context: Communist armed conflicts in the Philippines > 2022 Samar boat explosion
text: Ten communist rebels, including CPP–NPA leaders Wilma and Benito Tiamzon, are killed in a boat explosion off the coast of Catbalogan, Samar, Philippines.
The exchange rate between the euro and the United States dollar drops to 0.9928, the lowest in 20 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada > COVID-19 vaccination in Canada
text: Moderna announces that it will supply 12 million doses of its bivalent COVID-19 vaccine aimed at targeting the Omicron variant.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North America > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 vaccination in the United States
text: The U.S. CDC announces that it has recommended the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine for use in children between the ages of 12 and 17 years.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education
text: Schools in the Philippines reopen for in-person classes after a two year closure due to the pandemic.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Monkeypox cases have been reported in all 50 U.S. states after Wyoming reports its first case of the disease in a person from Laramie County.
Indiana Governor Eric Holcomb visits Taiwan and meets with Taiwanese President Tsai Ing-wen.
The cabinet of Pakistan approves the deployment of Pakistan Army troops to Qatar to provide security for the upcoming 2022 FIFA World Cup.
A record 1,295 illegal migrants cross the English Channel to the United Kingdom on "small boats", according to the Ministry of Defence.
The Pakistani police file terrorism charges against former Prime Minister Imran Khan.
A federal prosecutor requests a 12-year sentence for former president and current vice president of Argentina Cristina Fernández de Kirchner on corruption-related charges.
A nine-year-old girl is shot dead and two others are wounded in a shooting inside a house in Liverpool, England, according to Merseyside Police.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: Ukrainian forces reportedly shell the administration headquarters of the Donetsk People's Republic in separatist-held Donetsk, killing three people, according to pro-Russian officials.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Slovakia announces that it will send an additional 30 BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicles and ammunition to Ukraine.
According to the Libyan National Army, a United States-manufactured MQ-9 Reaper drone was shot down with a surface-to-air missile, crashing near Benina International Airport in Benghazi, Libya.

The dugong is declared extinct in China after scientists report no verified sightings of the large marine mammal since 2000. However, dugongs still exist in the wild in parts of Southeast Asia and Australasia.
South Korea registers a population decrease for the second consecutive year, due to having the world's lowest birth rate.

The Federal Court of Malaysia upholds the corruption conviction and 12-year prison term of former prime minister Najib Razak in connection with the embezzlement of sovereign wealth funds from 1Malaysia Development Berhad. Najib is the first former Malaysian prime minister to be imprisoned.

Two men are found guilty of conspiring to obtain a weapon of mass destruction for use in the foiled plot to kidnap Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer. One of the men is also convicted of an explosives charge.

Brazilian police conduct eight raids on pro-Bolsonaro businessmen accused of discussing the possibility of a coup d'état if incumbent President Jair Bolsonaro loses the upcoming presidential election.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announces an official inquiry into his predecessor Scott Morrison's secret swearing of himself into various ministerial positions during his second ministry.

context: 2022 Samoan o le Ao o le Malo election
text: Tuimalealiʻifano Vaʻaletoʻa Sualauvi II is re-elected by the Parliament for a second term as O le Ao o le Malo, the Samoan head of state.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast
text: The Russian-appointed head of Mykhailivka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ivan Sushko, is assassinated in a car bombing.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Chaplyne railway station attack
text: At least 25 people are killed and more than 50 others are injured in a Russian rocket attack on a passenger train in Chaplyne, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States announces a security package of nearly billion from the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative.

context: American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war, Russia–United States relations
text: U.S. President Joe Biden orders airstrikes against claimed Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Russia-linked groups in Syria in response to a August 15 rocket attack near the U.S. military base in al-Tanf, Syria, which houses the Maghaweir al-Thowra rebel group, and an airstrike by the Russian military in an area held by the Syrian opposition. The U.S. strikes targeted eleven bunkers in Deir ez-Zor used to store weapons, according to the United States Central Command.

context: American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war, Russia–United States relations
text: A spokesperson for the Iranian foreign ministry denies that Iran has any link to targets hit by U.S. in Syria and condemns the strike as "a violation of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity".
Eight people are killed in a shooting between two criminal groups in Tuzantla, Michoacán, Mexico.
Fighting resumes between the Ethiopian military and the Tigray Defense Forces in the Tigray Region. Both sides blame each other for breaking the ceasefire.

Germany and French rail transport manufacturer Alstom inaugurate the world's first fleet of hydrogen fuel-powered trains in Lower Saxony. The 14 hydrogen trains will replace a fleet of diesel locomotives on of track in the German state.
Tuvalu declares a drought and a shortage of drinking water on the islands of Nanumea, Nui, and Niutao.
Police arrest Kremlin critic Yevgeny Roizman, the former mayor of Yekaterinburg, for "discrediting the Russian army" by criticizing the invasion of Ukraine.

context: Aftermath of the 2020 Calabasas helicopter crash
text: A United States grand jury awards former professional basketball player Kobe Bryant's widow, Vanessa Bryant, $16 million against the Los Angeles County sheriff's and fire departments for releasing graphic photographs of the former player, their 13-year-old daughter, and the other victims of the helicopter crash. Another victim's widow receives $15 million.
Angolans vote to elect their president in a tight race between incumbent leftist candidate João Lourenço and center-right candidate Adalberto Costa Júnior.

The Constitutional Court of Thailand temporarily suspends Prayut Chan-o-cha's premiership due to a case filed by Pheu Thai Party lawmakers over whether the eight-year term limit for premiership should also include Prayut's time as the leader of National Council for Peace and Order. Deputy Prime Minister Prawit Wongsuwan will take over the premiership while the case is being heard.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: Ukraine says that the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant has been completely disconnected from its power grid after shelling near the Russian-occupied plant caused several fires. Security systems at the plant were activated shortly after the power failure, according to a local official.

context: American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: The United States conducts airstrikes against Iranian-backed militia groups in Syria for a second day.
Flooding in Afghanistan this month has killed 182 people and wounded 250 more as torrential rains wrought widespread devastation in central and eastern provinces.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea
text: North Korea reports four new "fever" cases in Ryanggang Province and places the province under lockdown.

Itaru Nakamura, chief of the Japanese national police agency, resigns, taking responsibility for the failures in former prime minister Shinzo Abe's security that resulted in his assassination in Nara on July 8.
Four people, including a police constable, are killed in a mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona, United States.
The electoral commission announces that President João Lourenço's MPLA has won the general election.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: Ukraine's state nuclear company, Energoatom, says that the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant has resumed supplying electricity to Ukraine's power grid after being disconnected yesterday from it for the first time in history.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: A traffic police deputy chief is killed by a bombing in the Russian-occupied city of Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Russian authorities accuse the Ukrainian forces of the attack.
Ethiopian forces reportedly airstrike a kindergarten playground in Mekelle, Tigray Region, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 13 others.
Russian peacekeepers withdraw from the city of Lachin and the villages of Zabukh and Sus, thereby returning the Lachin corridor to Azerbaijan.
Police arrest over 40 protestors for vandalism during a Just Stop Oil protest and blockade in London, United Kingdom.

A vehicle rams into a crowd of people in central Brussels, Belgium, injuring six people. The driver flees the scene but is subsequently arrested in Antwerp. A motive is still unclear, but terrorism is not being ruled out.

context: Libyan crisis, aftermath of the Second Libyan Civil War > 2022 Tripoli clashes
text: Fighting breaks out between two militias in Tripoli, Libya. At least 23 people are killed and over 140 others are injured.
Six people are killed and two others are injured when militants attack a gold mine in Boungou, Bilanga Department, Gnagna Province, Burkina Faso.

context: Hungary–Russia relations, Nuclear power in Hungary
text: Minister of Foreign Affairs Péter Szijjártó announces Russian nuclear energy provider Rosatom will begin construction of two new nuclear reactors to expand the Paks Nuclear Power Plant.
Six people are killed and seven others are injured after a truck crashes into a community barbecue in Nieuw-Beijerland, South Holland, The Netherlands.
Kosovan prime minister Albin Kurti and Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić agree on a freedom of movement arrangement between Kosovo and Serbia.

context: Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange, Censorship in the United States
text: Lawyers for WikiLeaks publisher Julian Assange file an appeal against his extradition to the U.S., after UK Home Secretary Priti Patel approved his extradition from the United Kingdom.

context: Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange, Censorship in the United States
text: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet meets with Assange’s lawyers and his wife in Geneva, Switzerland.

context: Hunter Biden laptop controversy, Censorship in the United States
text: In an interview on The Joe Rogan Experience, Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg reveals that Facebook restricted posts about the Hunter Biden laptop controversy during the 2020 United States presidential election after receiving misinformation warnings from the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
English football club Liverpool defeats Bournemouth 9–0 at Anfield, Liverpool, to equal the joint-largest winning margin in Premier League history.

A concert organized by the Bogotá Philharmonic Orchestra involving 16,000 musicians and choirs at the Simón Bolívar Park in Bogotá, Colombia, commemorating the progress in the country's peace process, sets a world record for the largest concert ever performed.
In Mongolia, the National Emergency Management Agency says that wildfires have burnt more than 1 million hectares of land so far this year, mainly due to negligence.
Colombia and Venezuela restore diplomatic relations after three years.

context: Mass shootings in the United States > 2022 Bend, Oregon shooting
text: Three people are killed, including the gunman, and two others injured in a mass shooting at a Safeway store in Bend, Oregon, United States.

context: Mass shootings in the United States
text: Three people are killed, including the gunman, and five others injured, including two police officers, in a mass shooting outside a Days Inn motel in Phoenix, Arizona, United States.
Two journalists are killed and another person is injured after two motorcycle-riding assailants shot them in Fundación, Magdalena, Colombia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukraine says it has begun a ground offensive in the Kherson Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Russian-occupation officials say that the Ukrainian military launched a barrage of missiles at the town of Nova Kakhovka, leaving the town without water or power.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern Ukraine campaign
text: Two people are killed and five others are injured after Russian forces shelled the city of Mykolaiv, according to regional governor Vitaliy Kim.

Supporters of Iraqi Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr storm the Republican Palace in Baghdad. The Iraqi Army declares a total curfew in the capital beginning at 3:30 p.m. and the Iraqi government declares a nationwide curfew beginning at 7:00 p.m.. At least twelve people are killed and 270 others are injured in clashes between protesters and Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces in the Green Zone.
Pro-Sadrist protesters blockade roads and government buildings in Basra.
Iran closes its border with Iraq until "further notice" amid the ongoing civil unrest, while Kuwait urges its citizens to leave Iraq.
At least 42 ethnic Oromo civilians are killed during a massacre in Horo Guduru Welega Zone, Ethiopia. Witnesses blame members of the Amhara Fano militia of responsibility.
Ten soldiers are killed and many more wounded during an attack aimed at cutting off a key route to the city of Taiz.
A dinghy carrying 27 Egyptians en route to Italy capsizes off the coast of Libya, killing at least two people and leaving nineteen others missing in the Mediterranean Sea.
Recent flash floods caused by heavy rainfall in northern Laos have caused at least 5.6 billion Lao kips in damage.

context: Genocide of indigenous peoples in Brazil
text: The Man of the Hole, the last member of his tribe who lived in total isolation for 26 years, is found dead in the Amazon rainforest.
In Ikongo, Madagascar, 18 people are killed and 34 are wounded when police open fire on a group protesting the kidnapping of a child with albinism.

The death toll from the clashes in Baghdad between Iraqi Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr's supporters and security forces increases to 23, with all of those killed being supporters of Sadr. 380 others are injured.
Iran captures an American unmanned ship before releasing it.
Allied Democratic Forces militants kill at least 40 people in a series of raids on several villages in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. At least 76 others are kidnapped by the group.
The Taiwanese military fire warning shots at a Chinese drone flying over islands in the Kinmen region.
A police chief is killed by suspected members of the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters in Maguindanao, the Philippines.
Sixteen people are killed and eight others are injured in a traffic collision between a truck and a minibus in Khuzestan province, Iran.
A South African Police Service plane crashes at Rand Airport in Johannesburg, killing all five passengers and critically injuring the pilot.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China
text: China announces new lockdowns in several cities following a series of COVID-19 outbreaks across the country.
The United States Embassy in Canberra says that the government of Solomon Islands will place a moratorium on US Navy ships entering its ports amid deteriorating relations between the two countries.
Six Indonesian soldiers are arrested for killing four indigenous Papuan people and mutilating their bodies in Timika eight days ago.
Portugal's health minister Marta Temido resigns after emergency services closures.

The Government of Ethiopia says that the Tigray People's Liberation Front has begun an offensive into the Wag and Welkait regions and is also pushing forward towards the Sudanese border. Tigrayan authorities say that three airstrikes have hit the Tigrayan capital of Mekelle, nearly striking a hospital.
Fourteen people are killed and several others are kidnapped as Allied Democratic Forces militants attack a village in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Five attackers are also killed.
Russia's Gazprom announces the complete shutdown of the Nord Stream 1 natural gas pipeline for three days for unscheduled maintenance.
Ten people are killed and several others are injured after a semi truck crashes near a school in Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia.
One person is killed and 50 others are injured by a hailstorm in Catalonia, Spain. This is the first direct hail-related death in Europe since 1997.
The Suez Canal was temporarily blocked after a ship ran aground on Wednesday evening. Tug boats were used to unblock the canal.
One person is killed and six others are injured after a building collapse in Kano, Kano State, Nigeria.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: The National Cabinet agrees to lower the mandatory isolation period for people infected with COVID-19 to 5 days if an individual is asymptomatic at that time. However workers in high-risk settings are still required to isolate for 7 days.
Sweden reports its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a porpoise.
Life expectancy in the United States decreases for the second consecutive year, falling by nearly a year from 2020 values.

context: International sanctions during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–European Union relations
text: European Union foreign ministers agree to suspend a visa facilitation agreement with Russia, making it more difficult and more expensive for Russian tourists to enter the EU.

context: Syrian civil war > Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Israeli Air Force jets fire four missiles at Aleppo International Airport, hitting the runway and several warehouses allegedly containing Iranian rockets, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. No casualties have been reported.
Four people are killed during clashes between rival Shia Muslim fighters in Basra, Iraq, three days after 30 supporters of Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr were killed during clashes in Baghdad.
Two Palestinian men are killed in clashes with Israeli soldiers in the occupied West Bank. One of the men was killed by Palestinian gunfire, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.

Taiwanese forces shoot down an unidentified civilian drone which entered its airspace near the Shi Islet in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense says that the drone ignored several warning shots before being shot down.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front claims that Eritrea and Ethiopia have launched a joint offensive in the Tigray Region.
The International Monetary Fund provisionally approves a US$2.9 billion bailout for Sri Lanka.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Australia
text: Victoria removes its directive to work remotely where possible.

A third person dies from an unidentified virus in Tucumán Province, Argentina. Authorities have ruled out COVID-19, influenza, and hantavirus, but continue to investigate the cluster of infections. The European Centre for Disease Control and the World Health Organization have also been notified.
A temperature of is recorded in Furnace Creek, California, United States, breaking the record for the highest September temperature ever recorded in the world.

context: Attempted assassination of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner
text: A Brazilian man, identified as 35-year-old Fernando Montiel, is arrested by the Argentine Federal Police shortly after attempting to shoot Vice President Cristina Kirchner. Montiel pointed a loaded pistol at Kirchner's head and apparently pulled the trigger, but the weapon did not fire.
Four people are killed and several others are injured after a mass shooting at a soccer field in Yecapixtla, Morelos, Mexico.
The High Court of Malaysia finds Rosmah Mansor, wife of former Prime Minister Najib Razak, guilty of corruption.

context: Afghanistan conflict > Islamic State–Taliban conflict > 2022 Herat mosque bombing
text: Eighteen people are killed and 23 others are injured by a suicide bombing at a Sunni mosque in Herat, Afghanistan. The mosque's pro-Taliban imam, who is suspected to be the target of the attack, is among the dead.
Seven policemen are killed and one is injured during an ambush in Huila Department, Colombia. Their vehicle hit a roadside bomb before being shot dead by gunmen.
A Palestinian man stabs and injures an Israeli soldier near Kiryat Arba in the West Bank. The attacker is shot dead by security forces.
The Iranian Navy captures and later releases two American sea drones in the Red Sea.
The G7 group of nations announce plans for a price cap on Russian oil. Russia vows to halt sales to countries imposing it.

Following the G7's announcement, Russia's Gazprom announces that flows through the Nord Stream 1 natural gas pipeline to Europe will not resume tomorrow because of a reported "oil leak" in a turbine. It did not give a new time frame.
Hurricane Danielle becomes the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
A double–decker bus overturned on the Gala road between Cairo, Egypt and Suez Governorate, killing eight and injuring 38.
A Toyota Innova rams into a group of pedestrian devotees in Aravalli Range, India, killing seven and critically injuring five others.
Three people were killed and 11 others were injured when a train crashed into a microbus in Northern Egypt.

Deposed leader of Myanmar Aung San Suu Kyi is sentenced to three years in prison after being found guilty of election fraud. She will now serve an overall sentence of 20 years in prison for different charges.
Former president Gotabaya Rajapaksa returns to Colombo, Sri Lanka, after seven weeks of exile.

FINA permits the use of special swim caps specifically designed for dreadlocks, hair weaves or extensions, and voluminous hair, branded as the Soul Cap, in all water sports competitions. It had been banned at the 2020 Summer Olympics.
Twenty people are killed in a mass shooting by al-Shabaab insurgents against vehicles transporting food supplies from Beledweyne to Mahas in the Hiran region.

Twenty-seven ancient artifacts housed in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City, United States, are seized by federal investigators under the suspicion that they were looted. The artifacts will be repatriated to Italy and Egypt next week.

context: Illegal immigration to the United States
text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection agents and Mexican police find nine migrants dead in the Rio Grande after dozens of migrants attempt to cross into Eagle Pass, Texas, United States. At least 70 other migrants are rescued.

President of Turkey Recep Tayyip Erdoğan accuses Greece of "arming" and "occupying" the demilitarized Aegean islands, with Minister of Foreign Affairs Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu threatening to revoke recognition of Greek sovereignty over the islands if the alleged militarization is not halted.

context: Death and funeral of Mikhail Gorbachev
text: The funeral of former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev is held in Moscow.

An estimated 70,000 people march in the Czech Republic's capital city Prague demanding that the government do more to control soaring energy prices in the country and voicing opposition to the country's involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian War. The demonstration was organized by political groups including the Communist Party.
NASA suspends the inaugural launch of the Artemis 1 rocket for a second time, after a fuel leak causes a delay of more than two hours.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian forces recapture the town of Vysokopillia in Kherson Oblast, which has been under Russian occupation since March, and raise the Ukrainian flag over the town's hospital.
Six Israeli soldiers and a civilian driver are injured when three gunmen open fire on a bus in Nablus, in the occupied West Bank. Two of the attackers are later arrested.
A Syrian Air Force helicopter crashes in Hama, Syria, killing all of the people on board.
A private Cessna 551 crashes into the Baltic Sea, off the coast of Latvia.
Ten people are killed and fifteen others injured in a mass stabbing at the James Smith Cree Nation and the nearby village of Weldon in Saskatchewan, Canada. The two suspects remain at large.
Hamas authorities execute five Palestinians in the first executions in Palestinian territories since 2017. Two of those executed were accused of espionage.
By a margin of 62% to 38%, Chileans vote to reject the new proposed constitution drafted by the Constitutional Convention.

context: Islamist insurgency in the Sahel > Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso
text: Thirty-five civilians are killed and 37 others injured as a convoy of vehicles carrying supplies strike a roadside bomb along the road from Bourzanga to Djibo, Soum Province, Burkina Faso.

context: Afghanistan conflict > Islamic State–Taliban conflict > Bombing of the Russian embassy in Kabul
text: Eight people are killed when an Islamic State suicide bomber detonates his explosives near the entrance of the Russian embassy in Kabul. Two of the victims were Russian staff members.
Five Pakistani soldiers and four Pakistani Taliban militants are killed during a gunfight in North Waziristan.
Russia's Gazprom announces that gas flows through the Nord Stream 1 natural gas pipeline to Europe will not resume until sanctions against Russia are lifted.
A magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes Luding County, Sichuan, China, killing at least 66 people and injuring at least 250 others.
Ten people are killed and nine more injured during an earthquake in eastern Afghanistan.
Three people are killed after Tropical Storm Kay strengthens into a hurricane in Mexico.
A vehicle and train collision in Kunfehértó, Hungary, kills seven people and injures the train's driver.
One person is killed and nine others are missing after a floatplane crashes in the Puget Sound near Seattle, Washington, United States.
Six people are killed after a building collapses in Lagos, Nigeria.
One of the suspects in yesterday's mass stabbing that killed ten people in Saskatchewan is found dead. The other suspect remains at large.

Ivan Safronov, a former Russian journalist, is sentenced to 22 years in prison on treason charges after being found guilty of disclosing "state secrets", which he alleged were open source. Safronov had been under detention since July 2020.
Liz Truss is elected Leader of the Conservative Party and will succeed Boris Johnson as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 6 September.
The Supreme Court of Kenya rules that William Ruto is the winner of the presidential election after facing court challenges over the results.
Six people are killed and three others are kidnapped as Islamists insurgents raid the districts of Erati and Memba, Mozambique, torching dozens of houses. Six attackers are arrested.

Gunmen storm the Comboni Missionary Sisters' church in Chipene, Mozambique, killing an Italian nun and setting ablaze the church, the nuns' homes and the hospital. Two other nuns and two priests escaped.

Fights erupt in the village of Talataye between the Islamic State, Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin and the National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad, with the Malian Armed Forces launching airstrikes amid the fighting. At least 30 people are killed.
Twenty Southern Transitional Council separatist fighters are killed by al-Qaeda gunmen in Abyan Governorate. All of the six attackers are also killed in the gunfight.
Six people are killed and eight others are injured when separatists open fire on a public bus in South West, Cameroon.
Ten people are killed in South Korea by Typhoon Hinnamnor. Seven of the victims died in a flooded underground car park. In addition, 2,900 people are evacuated and 66,000 homes are damaged.
Six people are killed when two earthquakes strike northern Afghanistan.
At least 32 people are killed in a karaoke bar fire in Binh Duong, Vietnam.

Thousands of people evacuate in N'Djamena, Chad, due to extensive flooding caused by the country's heaviest rains in 30 years. An estimated 442,000 Chadians have been impacted by the floods since the end of August.
A car crash in south Sydney, Australia kills 5 children and leaves an 18-year-old driver with minor injuries.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in India > COVID-19 vaccination in India
text: India approves a nasal COVID-19 vaccine to combat COVID-19, becoming the second country to do so after China.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Hong Kong confirms its first case of monkeypox.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States
text: Wisconsin and North Carolina expand their eligibility for the monkeypox vaccine in at-risk communities.
Kiribati suspends three retired New Zealand judges from the Kiribati Court of Appeal as the constitutional crisis worsens.

Couy Griffin, a commissioner of Otero County, New Mexico, United States, is barred from public office by a state judge due to his involvement in the January 6 attack, which was determined to be an insurrection. This is the first time that the Fourteenth Amendment has been used in more than a century to ban a person who participated in an insurrection from serving in the government.
Liz Truss succeeds Boris Johnson to become Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
One person is killed during anti-U.N. protests in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

context: An AI Artist is open sourced
text: Artificial intelligence art meets Open Source. A model that cost $600000 to train, is released for use by anyone, stirring controversy about creativity and the future of art, artists and digital illustrators.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Amid a renewed counter-offensive in the region, Ukrainian forces reportedly break through Russian defenses and advance more than 30 kilometers into Russian held territory in the Kharkiv Oblast, capturing many towns and cities including Balakliia.
Fifteen people are killed by landslides caused by heavy rain in Kasese District, Uganda.
Hurricane Kay strengthens into a Category 2 hurricane south of Baja California Sur, Mexico.
Eleven people are killed and two others are injured by a building collapse in Aleppo, Syria.
Egypt confirms its first case of monkeypox.
The remaining suspect in Sunday's stabbing spree is arrested outside Wakaw, Saskatchewan. He later dies in custody.
Three people are killed and three others injured after a gunman goes on a livestreamed shooting spree in Memphis, Tennessee, United States. A 19-year-old suspect is arrested.
The government of Albania suspends diplomatic relations with Iran after a major cyberattack allegedly occurs. Iranian diplomats and embassy staff are told to leave Albania within 24 hours.
Gervais Ndirakobuca becomes the new prime minister of Burundi, following unanimous approval by the National Assembly.
Seven people are killed and 12 others are injured by airstrikes in Idlib Governorate, Syria.
Eleven people are killed and 12 others are missing after a boat sinks off the coast of Tunisia.
Nine people are killed and two others are injured by a lightning strike in Sirajganj, Bangladesh.
Fourteen people are killed when a boat capsizes in Pará, Brazil.

context: International sanctions during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Poland–Russia relations, Estonia–Russia relations, Latvia–Russia relations, Lithuania–Russia relations
text: Poland and the Baltic states announce a ban on Russian tourists entering their countries beginning on September 19.

Former White House Chief Strategist and Senior Counselor to the President of the United States Steve Bannon pleads not guilty to state charges in New York for allegedly defrauding donors to build a wall on the U.S. southern border.

context: Death of Elizabeth II, Operation London Bridge
text: Buckingham Palace announces that Queen Elizabeth II has died at the age of 96 at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. She is succeeded as monarch by her son King Charles III.
The parliament of Solomon Islands votes to delay the next general election amid objections by opposition parties, who accuse Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare of a "power grab".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Northeastern Ukraine campaign
text: Governor of Sumy Oblast Dmytro Zhyvytskyi says that Russian forces have shelled a hospital in Velyka Pysarivka, causing an unspecified number of casualties.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Ukraine claims to have retaken more than 1,000 square kilometers of territory previously occupied by Russia, within the last week.
Three people are killed and 11 others are injured when a freight train and a passenger train collide in Novska, Croatia.
The United States Department of the Treasury sanctions the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Intelligence Minister Esmaeil Khatib in response to a cyberattack against Albania.

context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
text: North Korea passes a new law formally declaring itself a "nuclear state". The law includes the right of North Korea to use "preemptive" nuclear strikes as Kim Jong-un promises to "never give up" the country's nuclear weapons.
Mexico transfers control over its National Guard to the Mexican Army.
A new lunar mineral is discovered by the Beijing Research Institute of Uranium Geology, which is named Changesite–(Y).

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian troops retake the cities of Balakliia, Kupiansk, and Izium from Russian occupation. The Russian Defence Ministry confirms the withdrawal of troops from several towns in Kharkiv Oblast in order to allow its forces "to regroup" and reinforce the Donbas.
Five people are killed when their boat is hit by a whale and capsizes near Kaikōura, New Zealand.
Three people are killed and five others are injured when a Black Hawk helicopter crashes during a Taliban training exercise in Kabul, Afghanistan.
Eighteen people are killed when a bus and a tanker truck collide and cause an explosion in Tamaulipas, Mexico.

The Kurdish administration in Syria, the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, requests help from the World Health Organization to contain a cholera outbreak which has killed three people in the region.

context: Proclamation of accession of Charles III
text: Charles Philip Arthur George is proclaimed King of the United Kingdom as Charles III by the Accession Council at St James's Palace.

context: Proclamation of accession of Charles III
text: Charles Philip Arthur George is proclaimed King of Canada as Charles III by the Chief Herald of Canada at Rideau Hall.

context: Proclamation of accession of Charles III
text: Charles Philip Arthur George is proclaimed King of Australia as Charles III by the Governor-General of Australia David Hurley at Government House in Canberra.

context: Proclamation of accession of Charles III
text: Charles Philip Arthur George is proclaimed King of New Zealand as Charles III by the Herald of Arms at the New Zealand Parliament Buildings.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Russian forces withdraw from most of the Kharkiv Oblast as the Russian occupation of Kharkiv Oblast collapses. Ukrainian soldiers retake Chkalovske and Velykyi Burluk. Governor of Belgorod Oblast Vyacheslav Gladkov says that "thousands" of civilians are fleeing across the border into the region.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Russia launches missile strikes with Kalibr cruise missiles on critical infrastructure objects, including Kharkiv TEC-5, causing a total blackout and water shutdown in Northeastern Ukraine and the Kharkiv and Donetsk Oblasts.
