Ukrainian officials confirm at least 40 electrical substations have been destroyed in the wave of missile strikes.
At least eight people are killed and 24 others are injured after a magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea.
One person is killed and 40 others are injured after flooding causes a wall dam to collapse in Free State, South Africa.
Three people are reported missing after a small plane fails to reach its destination in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
One person is killed and 39 others are injured after a firework explodes at a festival in Santiago Tianguistenco, Mexico.
Swedes head to the polls to elect members of the Riksdag.

context: Proclamation of accession of Charles III
text: Charles III is proclaimed Lord of Mann by Lieutenant Governor Sir John Lorimer at Government House, Isle of Man.

context: Reactions to the death of Elizabeth II
text: Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda Gaston Browne announces his intention to hold a referendum on transitioning the country into a republic.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian forces continue to recapture Russian-occupied territory in Kharkiv Oblast, saying that they have seized 20 more settlements in the last 24 hours, including Dvorichna, and also claim to have captured many Russian prisoners of war.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: The Ukrainian general staff reports that Russian troops abandoned the city of Svatove in Luhansk Oblast as Ukrainian forces advanced.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Western Russia attacks
text: Multiple explosions are reported near the city of Taganrog in Rostov Oblast, Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: More than 30 municipal deputies of Russian cities sign a petition calling for Russian President Vladimir Putin's resignation amid substantial Ukrainian advances in the war.
Four Turkish soldiers are killed in clashes with PKK insurgents in Iraqi Kurdistan, according to the Turkish Defense Ministry.
Azerbaijan shells Armenian villages in the eastern region of the country.
Five people are killed during an attack on a senator's convoy in Anambra, Nigeria.
A 1500 year old ancient Mayan settlement is uncovered in central Belize by archaeologists from the Belize Archaeological Institute and UIUC, dating from between 250 to 600 AD.
A gunman kills two people, including a Toronto Police constable, and injures three others in Mississauga and Milton, Ontario, Canada, before police shoot him dead in Hamilton Cemetery.
The James Webb Space Telescope reveals its first photos of the Orion Nebula, which is located in the Orion constellation.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive
text: The Ukrainian military says that it has shot down an Iranian HESA Shahed 136 combat drone operated by Russia near Kupiansk, Kharkiv Oblast. An inscription on the drone identified it as an "M214 Geran-2", which did not immediately correspond to known Russian weaponry.

context: Afghanistan conflict > Republican insurgency in Afghanistan
text: Taliban authorities say that they have killed 40 National Resistance Front fighters in the Panjshir Province of Afghanistan, including four commanders.
Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan says that 49 soldiers were killed during overnight clashes with Azerbaijan after it shelled villages yesterday and that fighting was ongoing.
A roadside bombing in Swat District, Pakistan, kills eight people, including a local tribal leader known for his opposition to the Pakistani Taliban.
Ethiopian airstrikes hit Mekelle University's business campus and a Dimtsi Weyane radio station.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front says that Eritrea has taken the town of Sheraro.

Following the release of the Bureau of Labor Statistics consumer price index for the month of August, all 30 stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average decrease in value, resulting in a 3.9% drop in the index.
Six people are killed and five people are missing after a boat carrying migrants sinks off the coast of Turkey.
Five people are killed and 14 others are injured after a building collapsed in Amman, Jordan, 10 people are reported missing.
Seventeen people are injured after a fuel tanker explodes in Sabha, Libya.
A possible improvised explosive device explodes at Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts, United States, injuring one person.

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev agrees to change the name of Kazakhstan's capital from "Nur-Sultan" back to "Astana". He had previously changed the capital's name in 2019 to honor his predecessor Nursultan Nazarbayev.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces launch eight cruise missiles at the dam of the Karachunivske reservoir causing extensive flooding in Kryvyi Rih and a increase of water level in the Inhulets River.

Armenia formally triggers article 4 of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) after accusing Azerbaijan of launching an invasion. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan says that "we asked support from CSTO, including military support to restore Armenia's territorial integrity and ensure the withdrawal of the Azerbaijani Armed Forces from the territory of Armenia".
Two al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigade member and an Israeli soldier are killed during a shootout at a checkpoint in Jenin, in the occupied West Bank.
Two Tajik border guards are killed and two others are injured during clashes with Kyrgyz guards, who accuse Tajikistan of taking positions at a demarcated area.
Ten people are killed when Ethiopian airstrikes hit a residential area in Mekelle, Tigray Region.
Typhoon Muifa makes landfall in eastern China with the maximum wind speed near its centre reaching 42 metres per second ().
Fourteen people are killed and 25 others are injured in a three vehicle collision in Kyaukpadaung, Myanmar.
Eleven people are killed and 29 others are injured when a bus falls into a gorge in Poonch district, Jammu and Kashmir, India.
The British supermarket chain Iceland launches an appeal to the EUIPO against the country of Iceland in a 20-year-long legal process over the use and trademark of the name "Iceland".
Two Thai military personnel are killed and another is injured after a gunman opens fire at a military facility in Bangkok. The gunman is later arrested.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian Kharkiv counteroffensive > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Izium mass graves
text: Ukrainian police say that a mass grave containing more than 440 bodies has been discovered in the recently recaptured city of Izium.
Nine people are killed and 20 others are injured during a stampede at a concert in Quetzaltenango, Guatemala.
Authorities in Mexico confirm the arrest of a retired military general for his alleged role in the kidnapping of 43 students in the state of Guerrero in 2014.
U.S. House speaker Nancy Pelosi announces a visit to the Armenian capital Yerevan as a show of support for Armenia amid renewed clashes between Armenia and Azerbaijan over the past week.
Ethereum, the second largest cryptocurrency, changes its consensus mechanism from proof of work to proof of stake, ceasing all mining and reducing its energy consumption by over 99.9%
A civilian is killed and two others are injured by Ukrainian shelling on Valuyki, Belgorod Oblast, according to Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov.

context: Internal conflict in Myanmar > 2021–2022 Myanmar insurgency
text: Myanmar Army helicopters attack a school in Sagaing Region, Myanmar, killing six children and injuring 17 people. Military officials say that the school was being used as a base by anti-coup insurgents.

According to Kyrgyzstan, Tajik forces again open fire on its outposts and clashes occur along the border with Tajik forces using armored vehicles and mortars. Tajikistan accuses Kyrgyz forces of shelling one of its outposts and several villages.

context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the performing arts
text: The Phantom of the Opera, currently the longest-running show in Broadway history, announces that it will end production in February 2023, stating that a decline in attendance caused by the COVID-19 pandemic has made it unable to recoup the weekly costs of running the show.

American computer hardware company EVGA terminates its partnership with fellow hardware manufacturer Nvidia and withdraws completely from the graphics card market, alleging that the latter forced them to sell their cards at a loss and would refuse to disclose important information, such as sales numbers.
Ten people are killed, 50 others are injured, and three people are reported missing as floods hit Ancona, Marche, Italy.
Twelve people are killed by heavy rains in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, with nine of the people killed when a wall collapsed.

context: 2022 monkeypox outbreak > 2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia
text: Bahrain confirms its first case of monkeypox.
Widespread protests occur in Iran after a woman is detained and allegedly beaten to death in Tehran by officers from Iran's religious police system for not properly wearing her hijab.

Incumbent President Nayib Bukele announces that he will run for re-election in 2024, one year after the Supreme Court ruled that he was eligible to do so despite a constitutional ban on presidential re-election.
Five Syrian soldiers are killed in missile strikes launched by the Israeli Air Force near Damascus.

context: COVID-19 pandemic, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism, Tourism in Germany
text: The annual Oktoberfest in Munich, Germany, opens after not being held for two years due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Poland opens the Vistula Spit canal connecting the Vistula Lagoon and Gdańsk Bay after three years of construction.

The Japan Meteorological Agency urges residents to evacuate southern parts of the island of Kyushu as super Typhoon Nanmadol approaches. An official for the agency warns that Nanmadol can bring "unprecedented" storms and rain to the area.
Twenty-two people are killed and 10 others are injured by a landslide in Achham, Nepal.
Nine people are killed and 55 others are rescued after a bus crashes in Alajuela Province, Costa Rica, during heavy rains.
Vic Rodriguez steps down as Executive Secretary and will continue to be Bongbong Marcos chief of staff.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces shell a psychiatric hospital in Strelechya, Kharkiv Oblast, killing four medics and injuring two patients.

The death toll from the fighting between Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, which began four days ago, increases to 94. Fifty-nine of the people were killed in Kyrgyzstan, and the 35 others were killed in Tajikistan. Another 139 people are injured.

Ukraine withdraws its 250 troops from the United Nations peacekeeping force MONUSCO in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. A Ukrainian Air Force aviation unit also withdraws its eight helicopters from the mission, which made up a third of the UN's fleet.
Five gunmen storm a rehab center in the early morning in Cortazar, Guanajuato, Mexico, and open fire, killing three people and injuring two others.
A second earthquake in less than 24 hours strikes southeast Taiwan, killing one person and wounding 146 other people. The 6.9 magnitude earthquake is felt in Taipei and tsunami warnings are issued.
Twenty-seven people are killed and 20 others are injured when a bus carrying people to a COVID-19 quarantine facility crashes on a highway in Sandu County, Guizhou Province, China.

Hurricane Fiona makes landfall in Puerto Rico causing the entire island to lose power. The U.S. National Hurricane Center warns of "life-threatening flash flooding" on the island amid "historic" rainfall.
Thousands of people march in Istanbul, Turkey, to demand legislation against LGBT organizations and their activities.
Spain defeats France 88–76 in the final to win their fourth EuroBasket title.
The Las Vegas Aces win their first WNBA Championship in a series against the Connecticut Sun.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: Thirteen people are killed and many others are injured in explosions in the Donetsk People's Republic-held city of Donetsk. DPR leader Denis Pushilin accuses Ukraine of being behind the attacks.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: The Ukrainian Ground Forces recapture the village of Bilohorivka in Luhansk Oblast as it advances on Lysychansk.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: Luhansk People's Republic authorities say that a Ukrainian shelling attack has killed seven civilians including three children in the town of Krasnorichenske.
Four people are killed and more than 30 injured as police open fire on people protesting in Saqqez, Kurdistan province, Iran, over the death of a woman under police custody in Tehran.

context: Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II
text: The state funeral of Elizabeth II is held in London, United Kingdom.
Hurricane Fiona makes landfall in the Dominican Republic after causing massive devastation in Puerto Rico, killing three people.
A magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes Michoacán, Mexico, killing two people and wounding 12 others.
Mongolia places Khovd Province under quarantine after confirming a case of bubonic plague in Möst district.
Afghanistan releases American engineer Mark Frerichs in exchange for Afghan drug lord Bashir Noorzai, who has been held by the United States on drug charges since April 2005.
Equatorial Guinea abolishes the death penalty after its president Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo signs a new penal code into law.
Irish judge Síofra O'Leary is elected the new president of European Court of Human Rights, becoming the first woman to hold that position.
The State Duma of Russia reports that a referendum on the accession of the Luhansk People's Republic to Russia will be held in the near future.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Russian State Duma deputies approve the introduction of the concepts of mobilization, martial law, wartime and armed conflict, as well as punishment for desertion, into the Criminal Code.

A civilian is killed and another is critically injured during clashes between Al-Qassam Brigades' supporters and Palestinian authorities outside a police station in Nablus, in the occupied West Bank, following the arrest of two militants.
An 84-year-old woman is murdered in Holon, Israel in a suspected terror attack. The Qalqilya-born suspect is found dead, presumably by suicide, inside an abandoned building in Tel Aviv.
Tigray People's Liberation Front authorities say that Eritrea has launched a full-scale intervention into the Tigray Region of Ethiopia.
The National Bank of Georgia formally applies to join the European Union's Single Euro Payments Area.
Four people are killed and 114 others are injured as Typhoon Nanmadol makes landfall on the island of Kyushu, Japan.

Nine people have died of diarrhea, malaria and gastroenteritis during the last 24 hours in Sindh Province, Pakistan, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll from flooding to more than 1,600 people.
Eight people are injured after an explosion tore through a building in Austin, Chicago, Illinois, United States.
Nine people are killed and 31 others are injured after a concrete slab collapsed on top of the auditorium bleachers during a political event in Itapecerica da Serra, São Paulo, Brazil.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States > COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state) > COVID-19 pandemic in New York City
text: New York City Mayor Eric Adams announces that the city will end its COVID-19 vaccine mandate for private businesses on November 1.
Uganda reports an outbreak of Ebola after a rare case of the Sudan ebolavirus strain was confirmed in a 24-year-old man who later died, becoming the first known fatality from the strain since 2011.

It is announced that the referendums on the entry of the Luhansk People's Republic, the Donetsk People's Republic, and the occupied parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts into Russia as federal subjects will be held from September 23 to 27.
Protests continue for the fourth consecutive day across Iran in response to the death of Mahsa Amini while in the custody of the morality police. Two people are killed during protests in Kermanshah.

UEFA announces that Russia will continue to be suspended meaning their team is barred from the UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying draw. ([https://www.uefa.com/insideuefa/news/0279-1628176b348f-4ef8c4c59e6b-1000--uefa-euro-2024-qualifying-draw-procedure-approved/ UEFA])

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: In a major address to the nation, Russian president Vladimir Putin announces a partial mobilization, with the exceptions of students and conscripts.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Lithuania places its rapid reaction force on high alert in response to Russia's mobilization, according to Defence Minister Arvydas Anušauskas.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg says that Russia's military mobilization is "dangerous and reckless", and condemns Putin's use of "nuclear rhetoric".
Three people are killed and 13 others are injured in an explosion at a restaurant in Deh Mazang, Kabul, Afghanistan.
Fulani herdsmen shoot and kill 14 civilians in Logo, Benue State, Nigeria.
Hurricane Fiona reaches Category 4 as it moves from the Turks and Caicos Islands toward Bermuda.
Two people are killed and 5 others are injured after a helicopter crashes while travelling to a wildfire in Marmaris, Muğla Province, Turkey.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark
text: Queen Margrethe II tests positive for COVID-19 for the second time.

Two Ukrainian staffers of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe are sentenced to 13 years of prison by a court in the separatist Luhansk People's Republic for "alleged high treason and espionage for the United States".

Letitia James, the New York Attorney General, files a civil lawsuit in state court against Donald Trump, his three children as well as companies in The Trump Organization. The lawsuit alleges that Donald Trump committed fraud by artificially inflating his net worth in order to gain prestige and thus increase his property's value.

context: Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia
text: Anti-mobilization and anti-war protests occur across Russia, with many arrests also occurring.
World Taekwondo denies giving bribes in order to become an Olympic sport after allegations emerge from a former employee turned whistleblower.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Large numbers of fighting-age men leave Russia after the announcement of the mobilization. Long traffic jams occur at international border crossings and the price of tickets for international flights sharply increases.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: At least 1,300 protesters rallying against the mobilization are arrested throughout Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Donetsk People's Republic authorities accuse Ukraine of shelling a market in Donetsk, killing six civilians.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine and Russia release 55 Russian prisoners of war and 215 fighters from the Siege of Mariupol as part of a prisoner exchange mediated by Turkey and Saudi Arabia. Among those released are pro-Russian Ukrainian politician Viktor Medvedchuk, Azov Regiment commander Denys Prokopenko, British volunteers Aiden Aslin and Shaun Pinner, and Moroccan volunteer Saadun Brahim. ,
At least 71 people are killed when a boat carrying migrants from Lebanon capsizes off Syria's coast.
Two people are killed by a magnitude 6.9 earthquake in Mexico City. The earthquake was an aftershock of the magnitude 7.6 earthquake that occurred three days ago in Michoacán, Mexico.
At least three people are killed by an explosion at an oil refinery in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
Seven people are killed by landslides in El Salvador.
Amid protests after the death of Mahsa Amini, Iran restricts access to several websites, including Instagram and WhatsApp.

China's former justice minister Fu Zhenghua is sentenced to death with reprieve, which means his sentence will be life in prison without the possibility of parole, after pleading guilty to accepting bribes.

context: Afghanistan conflict > September 2022 Kabul mosque bombing
text: Seven people are killed and 41 others are injured when a car bomb explodes at a mosque in Kabul, Afghanistan.
A 60-year-old man is killed by an Ethiopian airstrike on Mekelle, in the rebel-controlled Tigray Region.
Gunmen kill ten people in a mass shooting at a pool hall in Tarimoro, Guanajuato, Mexico.

context: COVID-19 pandemic, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism, Tourism in Bhutan
text: Bhutan reopens its borders for international tourists following a two-year closure due to the pandemic.

context: Mahsa Amini protests, Iran–United States relations
text: Sanctions are imposed on seven Iranian government officials and one group by the United States Department of the Treasury, which blames the Guidance Patrol for the death of Mahsa Amini.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 annexation referendums in Russian-occupied Ukraine
text: Referendums begin in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian oblasts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia and the separatist republics of Donetsk and Luhansk on whether to join Russia, in what Ukraine and other countries consider to be "sham" referendums.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Thousands of fighting-age men continue to leave Russia due to the mobilization. Massive lines are reported at the country's borders with Georgia and Finland.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia
text: At least 700 people are detained during anti-war protests across Russia.
The Iranian Revolutionary Guards shell the "[h]eadquarters of anti-Iranian terrorists" in Iraqi Kurdistan.
Fifteen people are killed and many others are injured after armed bandits attacked a mosque in Zamfara, Nigeria.
Hurricane Fiona leaves more than 500,000 people without power in Atlantic Canada.
Two people are killed and 120,000 people experience a power outage after Tropical Storm Talas hits central Japan.
Ukraine announces a reduction of Iranian diplomatic mission staff in response to the delivery of drones to Russia as part of the Russo-Ukrainian War.
The death toll from the protests in Iran increases to 50.
The Iranian Army announces that it will "confront the enemies" in response to the ongoing protests.
Reports emerge that protestors have allegedly "taken control" of the city of Oshnavieh after security forces withdraw.
Three people are injured after a shooting occurred at an amusement park in West Mifflin, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, United States.
Voters in Nauru head to the polls to elect members of parliament.
Thousands of people protest in Luanda, Angola, accusing incumbent president João Lourenço of electoral fraud in the latest election.

Elon Musk says that Starlink will be enabled inside Iranian cities after the United States State and Treasury Departments announce measures to increase internet freedom and access to information in the country.
The planned launch of Artemis 1 is newly delayed due to a storm.
In Australian rules football, the AFL season concludes with Geelong defeating the Sydney Swans in the Grand Final by 81 points.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia, 2022 North Caucasian protests
text: Mass protests against mobilization take place in Dagestan with protesters clashing with police. ,

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia, 2022 North Caucasian protests
text: The number of people detained in anti-war protests across Russia increases to more than 2,000.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirms that Ukraine has received NASAMS air defence systems from the United States.
One soldier is killed and six others are injured in a suicide bombing in Mogadishu, Somalia.

context: Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Uzbekistan suspends the use of Russia's card payment system Mir. The move was supposedly warranted by the need "to carry out the necessary technical procedures" and was not related to sanctions.
A ferry carrying Hindu pilgrims capsizes and sinks in Panchagarh District, Bangladesh, killing 66 people and leaving dozens of others missing.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Spain
text: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez tests positive for COVID-19.
The Iranian government announces that security forces have regained control of Oshnavieh, a day after protestors allegedly "took control" of the city.
Eleven people are killed during an ambush by cattle rustlers in Turkana County, Kenya.
Italians head to the polls to elect members of the Parliament.
Exit polls show that the centre-right coalition led by Brothers of Italy leader Giorgia Meloni has won the election with a majority of seats in the Italian Parliament.
Cubans vote on legalizing same-sex marriage and same-sex adoption. The government urges people to vote in favour of legalization while the Catholic Church urges people to vote against legalization.

The Swiss go to the polls to decide four ballot questions. The voters agree to raise the retirement age for women to 65 and to increase the value added tax rates from 7.7% to 8.1%. However, voters rejected the proposal to exempt domestic bonds from taxation and to ban intensive animal farming.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization > 2022 anti-war protests in Russia, 2022 North Caucasian protests
text: Spontaneous protests against the mobilization continue in Dagestan and Kabardino-Balkaria.
A police officer is killed and another injured during a shooting and bomb attack near a police station in Mersin, Turkey. Both the attackers are killed.
Eleven soldiers are killed as a 150-vehicle convoy carrying supplies to Djibo is ambushed by Islamist militants in Gaskindé (Pobé-Mengao), Soum Province.

Russian oligarch Yevgeny Prigozhin, a close ally of Vladimir Putin, publicly admits for the first time that he founded the Wagner Group, a private military company accused of war crimes in places where they had been deployed. Prigozhin had previously denied any involvement with the organization.
The pound sterling falls to its record lowest level against the U.S. dollar.

Inter-American Development Bank chief Mauricio Claver-Carone is fired by the bank's board of governors after an external investigation, started because of a whistleblower complaint, found that Claver-Carone had an undisclosed intimate relationship with his subordinate and committed several ethics violations in connection with her.
Six people are killed as Typhoon Noru makes landfall on the island of Luzon, Philippines.
Six Pakistani military personnel are killed in a helicopter crash in Balochistan, Pakistan.
Seven people are killed in a fire in a shopping mall in Daejeon, South Korea.
Three people are killed in a building collapse in Nairobi, Kenya.
Four people are killed after a boat sinks in the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
text: Chancellor Olaf Scholz tests positive for COVID-19.
The death toll from an Ebola virus outbreak in Mubende District, Uganda, increases to 23, with a total of 36 confirmed and suspected cases.
The death toll from the cholera outbreak in Syria increases to 29, with a total of 338 cases reported, the majority of whom are in Aleppo Governorate.
The Colombia–Venezuela border reopens for commerce and trade after a seven-year closure.
Kazakhstan says that it will not recognize the results of the ongoing annexation referendums in Russian-occupied Ukraine.
A man kills 17 people and injures 24 others in a mass shooting at a school in Izhevsk, Russia, before killing himself.
The United States Forest Service seizes equipment owned by the Pacific Gas and Electric Company, as part of a criminal investigation into the company's role in the Mosquito Fire.
President Vladimir Putin signs a decree granting Russian citizenship to American whistleblower Edward Snowden.
A referendum is approved in Cuba, granting, among other things, broader rights for the LGBT community, including marriage.
NASA's DART spacecraft successfully impacts Dimorphos at 23:16 UTC, becoming the first spacecraft to impact an asteroid.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Kazakhstan says that around 98,000 Russian civilians have entered the country by land and air since Russian president Vladimir Putin ordered a military mobilization.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Latvia announces a state of emergency over the influx of Russian citizens fleeing mobilization. Special measures are taken in the border regions of the country and at all ports of entry.
Three separate spills are detected in the Baltic Sea following explosions in the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines in what appear to be acts of sabotage.

Norway raises its "emergency preparedness" in response to sightings of "unidentified drones" near its offshore oil and gas facilities in the North Sea, and is coordinating with its armed forces, police, and oil and gas industry operators, according to energy minister Terje Aasland.
Leaders from Poland, Norway and Denmark hold a ceremony to open the Baltic Pipe natural gas pipeline that will transport natural gas from the Norwegian shelf via Denmark to Poland.
Hurricane Ian makes landfall in Western Cuba as a Category 3 hurricane. Residents of the Tampa Bay area of Florida, United States, are ordered to evacuate.
Two people are killed in a fire at a PKN Orlen plant in Płock, Poland.
The Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo formally declares an end to the country's latest outbreak of Ebola.
Russia and the Taliban sign a provisional deal for Russia to supply Afghanistan with gasoline, diesel, gas and wheat.

According to the results released by Russian occupation authorities in Ukraine, the Donetsk People's Republic, the Luhansk People's Republic, as well as occupied parts of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson Oblasts overwhelmingly vote in favor of annexation, with 99.23%, 98.42%, 93.11% and 87.05% of support, respectively. Turnout exceeded 75% in each region and exceeded 97% in Donetsk Oblast. However, the voting has been widely dismissed as a sham referendum.
Valentina Matviyenko, Speaker of the Federation Council, the upper chamber of the Russian parliament, expects the annexation to be formalised by October 4.
The state funeral of assassinated former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe is held at the Budokan in Tokyo.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian emigration following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine
text: North Ossetia–Alania which contains the only border crossing between Russia and Georgia-controlled territory, bans all Russian cars that do not have the licence plate of the republic, with the exception of tourists travelling to the region. This comes as those fleeing the draft overwhelm the border.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian emigration following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine
text: A mobile draft centre is built at the Torfyanovka checkpoint, the busiest checkpoint on the Finland–Russia border, in order to prevent people who are fit to serve from fleeing the country. However, as of midday, the centre is not yet open.

Thirteen people are killed and 58 others are injured as Iran launches missiles and drones upon the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan's offices in Koye, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. Iran accused the group of being involved in the ongoing protests in the country.
An Iranian drone is claimed as shot down by US forces in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq.
Four Palestinians are killed and 44 others are injured when Israeli soldiers storm a refugee camp in Jenin, West Bank. The brother of the 2022 Tel Aviv shooting's perpetrator is among those killed.

One person is killed and two others are injured when a gunman opens fire against Chinese-Pakistani nationals at a dental clinic in Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan. All of the victims were in their 70s and had worked for the clinic for more than 40 years.

Authorities in Cameroon ban "undeclared meetings and manifestations" in Bamenda, the capital of the Northwest Region, after separatists announced a manifestation to commemorate the declaration of independence of Ambazonia, a breakaway state consisting of the English-speaking regions of Cameroon.
The Bank of England buys 65 billion pounds of bonds in a bid to stabilise the UK economy.
Two people are confirmed dead in Cuba because of the hurricane, and the island temporarily loses electricity from the damage caused.
Hurricane Ian makes landfall near Englewood, Florida, United States, as a high-end Category 4 hurricane.
Over 200,000 customers are left without power throughout Florida, U.S, due to Hurricane Ian.
A restaurant fire kills 17 people and injures three others in Changchun, Jilin, China.
Three people are killed and 15 others are reported missing after a bridge collapses in Careiro, Amazonas, Brazil.
Two people are killed and 10 others are injured after a three-way car crash in Uvalde, Uvalde County, Texas, United States.
Six people are shot and injured near several high schools and alternative schools in Oakland, California, United States.
Former Guinean military leader Moussa Dadis Camara and ten others go on trial for their alleged involvement in a massacre of anti-government demonstrators in 2009.
Jonathan Dowdall and his father Patrick plead guilty to facilitating the Killing of David Byrne in 2016.

The Russian-installed heads of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson Oblasts' occupation administrations, as well as Leonid Pasechnik, leader of the breakaway Luhansk People's Republic, officially request that they be annexed to Russia, following a referendum, widely seen as fraudulent, conducted in those regions of Ukraine. Donetsk People's Republic's leader Denis Pushilin has not yet submitted such a request but has gone with Pasechnik to Moscow for talks about the annexation, and is expected to send a request shortly.
Russ Kun becomes the President of Nauru, succeeding Lionel Aingimea.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces strike a residential neighborhood in Dnipro with a cruise missile, killing a family of four, including two children, and injuring 18 other civilians, according to local authorities.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Three people are killed and 12 others are injured by a Russian cluster munition attack on a bus stop in Mykolaiv, according to mayor Oleksandr Sienkievych.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian emigration following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine
text: Finland announces that it will deny entry to Russian tourists beginning on Thursday night, thereby cutting off the last direct link between Russia and the European Union.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launches ballistic missiles at Erbil, the capital of Iraq's Kurdistan Region, killing nine civilians and injuring 32 others. The Iraqi Foreign Ministry says that it will summon the Iranian ambassador in response to the attacks.
A section of the Sanibel Causeway in Florida, United States, collapses following damage from Ian, blocking access to the islands of Sanibel and Captiva.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis announces that the state has launched efforts to rescue people stranded from their homes by flooding from Ian. Additionally, President Joe Biden declares Ian a major disaster.
The death toll from the hurricane increases to at least 17.
Swedish authorities report a fourth gas leak from the Nord Stream pipelines.
Russian President Vladimir Putin calls the Nord Stream gas leaks "an unprecedented act of international terrorism".
One person is dead after a fire breaks out at an election agency in Asunción, Paraguay.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia > COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia
text: Indonesia grants approval for the first Chinese mRNA vaccine against COVID-19, the Walvax COVID-19 vaccine.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Asia > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan
text: Taiwan announces that it will end the mandatory quarantine of visitors on October 13 and will also restore temporarily suspended visa-free travel for countries that had a relevant agreement with the island.
Bettina Muscheidt, the European Union ambassador to Nicaragua, is declared persona non grata, presumably due to her criticism of undemocratic policies of President Daniel Ortega.

Montenegro expels six Russian diplomats, whom the country accuses of spying. In response, the Russian embassy in Montenegro announces that its consular section will suspend its services beginning on Friday and "until further notice".

The Supreme Court of India strikes down a portion of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act that forbade unmarried women from having an abortion, thus legalising the procedure for all women until the 24th week of pregnancy. The ruling also notes that forcing a woman to carry the child could constitute marital rape, which is not, however, recognised as an offence in India.
Aung San Suu Kyi, the ousted leader of Myanmar, is sentenced to a further three years' imprisonment for "violating the state's secrets act". She is already serving 20 years on other charges.

The Catholic Church reveals that it disciplined Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, an East Timorese minister and former bishop who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1996, over allegations of sexual abuse of teenage boys committed in the early 1990s.

The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda begins the trial of Félicien Kabuga, one of the richest Rwandan businessmen in the 1990s who is implicated in the Rwandan genocide. Kabuga pleads not guilty and does not appear on the first day of the proceedings.

The European Commission sues Malta in the European Court of Justice, seeking to end the country's "golden passport" scheme, which is the only such scheme still active in the EU. This scheme allows large investors to be granted Maltese citizenship, and by extension, citizenship of the European Union.

context: Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: Press Secretary of the President of Russia Dmitry Peskov says that the Kremlin is scheduled to sign agreements on the annexation of the occupied territories of Ukraine by Russia on September 30.

context: Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy announces that he will convene an urgent meeting of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine on September 30.

context: Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin signs a decree recognizing the "independence" of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts, which were proclaimed yesterday.
Russ Kun is inaugurated as President of Nauru following the general election on 24 September.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian attack on civilian convoy in Zaporizhzhia
text: Russian forces launch 16 missiles at areas near the city of Zaporizhzhia, including a gathering point for civilians preparing to cross into Russian-occupied territory, where at least 25 people are killed and 50 others are injured.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Ukraine–NATO relations
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy requests fast-track NATO membership following the Russian annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Russian mobilization
text: Uzbekistan says that it will not deport Russians fleeing conscription.

context: Afghanistan conflict > September 2022 Kabul school bombing
text: Twenty-six people are killed and 56 others are injured by a suicide bomber at a school in Dashte Barchi, Kabul, Afghanistan.
Four people are killed when armed rebels open fire on civilians in West Papua, Indonesia.

Junta leader Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba is removed from office in a coup d'état after gunfire in the Burkinabé capital of Ouagadougou. Coup leader Ibrahim Traoré imposes a curfew, suspends all political civil society activities as well as the Constitution, and closes all land and air borders.
Nineteen people are killed and 32 more injured when three gunmen attack a police station and open fire in a mass shooting in Zahedan, Iran.

context: 2021–2022 inflation surge, Economy of the Netherlands
text: Inflation in the Netherlands increases to 17% amid a substantial increase in energy and fuel prices.
Hurricane Ian makes its fourth landfall in South Carolina, after devastating portions of Florida and Cuba.
Two people are killed and 25 others are injured by a 5.9 magnitude earthquake in Northern Sumatra, Indonesia.
Eight people are killed and three others are missing after flooding in Táchira, Venezuela.
The Nicaraguan government announced that it had severed diplomatic relations with the Netherlands.

context: Russian annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: Russian president Vladimir Putin signs accession treaties to annex the occupied Ukrainian territories to Russia. However, the accession treaties must be ratified by both houses of the Russian parliament before becoming effective under Russian law.

Mexican president Andrés Manuel López Obrador confirms that the Mexican Secretariat of National Defense was hacked and that leaked data included information about the president's health issues and other national security issues.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas > Second Battle of Lyman
text: Ukrainian troops recapture Lyman after weeks of fighting for the city and one day after the annexation of the Donetsk People's Republic to Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas > Second Battle of Lyman
text: The Ministry of Defence of Russia says that it has withdrawn troops from the town of Lyman due to "a threat of encirclement".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas > Second Battle of Lyman
text: After the defeat in Lyman, the head of Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov, calls on the Russian government to introduce martial law and use low-yield nuclear weapons in Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A civilian convoy of seven cars attacked by Russian forces is discovered in Kupiansk Raion in Kharkiv Oblast with 24 people being killed, including a pregnant woman and 13 children, according to local governor Oleh Synyehubov.

An 18-year-old man is killed by Israeli soldiers in East Jerusalem, making him the 100th Palestinian killed in the West Bank this year. It is the deadliest toll of Palestinians killed there by Israeli raids since 2015.
The death toll from Hurricane Ian increases to 84.
Three people are killed and two others are injured after a helicopter crashes in Frontera, Tabasco, Mexico.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Canada, Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic
text: Canada formally ends all COVID-19 border measures, including vaccination requirements, pre-arrival testing, and quarantine, allowing all travellers to enter the country unrestricted without needing to submit public health information through the ArriveCAN government mobile app.

Venezuela releases seven Americans from its custody, including five Citgo executives, in exchange for two nephews of Venezuelan First Lady Cilia Flores who had previously been convicted of drug smuggling in the United States.
Togolese Gilbert Houngbo becomes the new Director-General of the International Labour Organization, succeeding British Guy Ryder.

At least 125 people are killed in a human crush following the dispersal of riotors by tear gas. The riot occurred between supporters of Indonesian football teams Arema F.C. and Persebaya Surabaya at the Kanjuruhan Stadium in Malang Regency, East Java, Indonesia.

context: Kurdish separatism in Iran, Iran–Iraq relations
text: Protests break out in Baghdad against Iranian involvement in the country following a series of missile and artillery strikes by the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that killed dozens of civilians in Iraqi Kurdistan.
Protests enter a fifteenth day as large crowds and strikes are held at Iran's universities.
Iranians around the world hold rallies in more than 160 cities in solidarity with protesters.
Latvians head to the polls to elect members of the Saeima.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian troops recapture Khreshchenivka as they continue to advance southwards in the Russian-occupied Kherson Oblast, with Russia's 49th Combined Arms Army reportedly withdrawing some troops from the frontline to Beryslav.

A taxi driver is shot and wounded by Palestinian militants near Elon Moreh in the West Bank. A demonstration by local Israeli settlers to protest the incident is attacked with gunfire, wounding a soldier. Palestinian militant group Lion's Den claims responsibility for the incident.
A video emerges showing Azerbaijani soldiers executing unarmed Armenian prisoners of war during clashes between Azerbaijan and Armenia last month.
A mass grave of 42 people is found in Sirte, Libya, after arrested Islamic State militants tip off authorities.
The death from Hurricane Ian rises to 87.
Twenty-six people are killed and ten others are injured when a tractor pulling a wagon with around 40 people on board overturns into a pond in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India.
Haitian authorities announce an unexpected resurgence of cholera in the country and report that at least seven people have died from the disease.

A stand-off ensues between students, protesters, and Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces in and around the Sharif University of Tehran, as gunfire is reported amid an apparent siege of the building.

context: 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: The Constitutional Court of Russia says that the annexation is constitutional, citing the need to correct the "arbitrary decisions of the Soviet government" and to prevent the claimed widespread repression of the Russians in Ukraine. It was later also clarified that the borders of the annexed subjects are intended to be those at the time of annexation.
Brazilians head to the polls to elect their president, vice president, and National Congress.
Incumbent president Jair Bolsonaro and former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will face off in a runoff election on October 30. Lula obtained 48.3% of the vote, Bolsonaro 43.3%.
Bulgarians head to the polls for the fourth time in 18 months to elect members of the National Assembly.
Bosnians head to the polls to elect the three members of their ethnically shared government.
Sergio Pérez wins the F1 Singapore GP as his teammate Max Verstappen missed the chance to win the championship.
Yalemzerf Yehualaw of Ethiopia becomes the youngest woman to win the London Marathon while Amos Kipruto of Kenya wins the men's race.
In horse racing, Alpinista wins the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe in Paris, France.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian forces advance more than along the Dnieper towards Dudchany, Kherson Oblast, in what is being called a "major breakthrough".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Defence Ministry dismisses Colonel General Alexander Zhuravlyov in response to a series of military defeats in Ukraine. He is replaced as commander of the Western Military District by Major General Roman Berdnikov.

context: Somali Civil War > October 2022 Beledweyne bombings
text: Twenty people are killed and 36 others are injured by two al-Shabaab suicide bombers when fifty-six gunmen and drug gangs open fire in a mass shooting at the local government headquarters in Beledweyne. The health minister of Hirshabelle and Hiran's deputy governor for finance and security are among the dead.
Two Palestinians are killed and another is wounded as Israeli soldiers open fire against a vehicle in the Jalazone refugee camp, Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate, in the occupied West Bank.

North Korea launches a suspected ballistic missile towards Japan with the Japanese government warning residents in Hokkaido and Aomori prefectures to immediately seek shelter. It later landed in the Pacific. The launch comes after a series of balloon launches and placard protests from South Korea and various military exercises involving the US.
Ten people are injured when a homemade explosive device explodes in Butembo, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
American wiki hosting service Fandom purchases numerous entertainment and review sites, such as TV Guide, Metacritic, and GameSpot, for US$50 million.
The U.S. death toll from Hurricane Ian increases to 87, with around 10,000 people remaining unaccounted for.
Hurricane Orlene makes landfall in the Mexican state of Sinaloa as a Category 1 hurricane.
North Korea restricts movement due to COVID-19. The announcement was made minutes after it launched a missile over Japan.
Fifteen people are killed and 21 others injured when a prison riot open fire in a mass shooting in Latacunga, Cotopaxi Province, Ecuador.
The Cabinet of Kenya votes to overturn a law prohibiting the open cultivation of genetically modified crops, and William Ruto officially authorizes the use of genetically modified maize.

context: 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
text: Swedish geneticist Svante Pääbo is awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine for "his discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution".
The Government of Colombia and the National Liberation Army (ELN) announce the resumption of peace talks in Caracas, Venezuela.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: The Federation Council of Russia unanimously approves the annexation of Ukraine's Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia regions. The annexation documents will now receive final signing by President Vladimir Putin.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukraine's 35th Marine Brigade recaptures the village of Davydiv Brid in Beryslav Raion, Kherson Oblast, as it continues its ground offensive. The Ukrainian Interior Ministry says that around 3,500 citizens have been freed from Russian occupation in recent days.
The European Union adds The Bahamas and the Turks and Caicos Islands to its tax haven blacklist, while Bermuda is removed from the list and Anguilla is named a "non-cooperative jurisdiction".
The U.S. death toll from Hurricane Ian increases to 109, including 105 in Florida.
Bangladesh suffers a severe power grid failure, leaving 80 percent of the country without electricity, according to the Bangladesh Power Development Board.
Two people are killed and 10 others injured after a plane crashes in Gao, Gao Region, Mali.
Ten people are killed and 11 others are reported missing after an avalanche in Draupadi ka Danda, Uttarakhand, India.
The Slovenian National Assembly codifies the legalization of same-sex marriage and adoption for same-sex couples.

Alain Aspect of France, John Clauser of the U.S., and Anton Zeilinger of Austria are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for "experiments with entangled photons, establishing the validity of Bell inequalities and pioneering quantum information science".
Rwanda is added to Google Street View.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Ukrainian troops recapture the strategic village of Dudchany on the west bank of the Dnieper following the withdrawal of Russian forces.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Annexation of Southern and Eastern Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin signs a law formally annexing the Donetsk People's Republic, Luhansk People's Republic, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia into Russia.

context: Tigray War > Adi Daero school airstrike
text: More than 50 people are killed in an Ethiopian Air Force airstrike on a school being used as an IDP camp in La'ilay Adiyabo, Tigray Region, Ethiopia.
Israeli soldiers surround a house in the village of Deir al-Hatab, killing a man and wounding four residents and two Palestinian Satellite Channel journalists who were covering the operation.

Eighteen people are killed, including the town's mayor, and three others injured, when a Los Tequileros drug gang open fire in a mass shooting at the town hall in San Miguel Totolapan, Guerrero, Mexico.
Four people are killed and 25 others are injured by a suicide bomber at a government ministry's mosque in Kabul.
The Nigerian military says it has secured the release of the last 23 passengers taken hostage in late March.
Three United Nations peacekeepers from Bangladesh are killed in a bombing while on patrol in the Central African Republic on Monday.
Unemployment reaches a record low in Slovenia, the lowest since the country's independence in 1991, despite a slowed economic growth.
The bridge connecting Pine Island in Lee County, Florida, reopens to the public after undergoing repairs from damage caused by Hurricane Ian.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake strikes Khowy, West Azerbaijan, Iran, wounding more than 1,000 people.
One person is killed and two others are injured by a magnitude 5.8 earthquake in Piura, Peru.
Twenty-five people are killed and over a dozen others are injured when a bus falls from a mountainous road into a gorge in Uttarakhand, India.

Lawyers for Maasai herders, who say that the Tanzanian government is trying to violently evict them from their ancestral land in order to make way for a luxury game reserve, have filed an appeal against a court ruling that dismissed their case.
The chief justice of the Supreme Court of Ukraine fires his deputy Bohdan Lvov for having dual Russian and Ukrainian citizenship.
Prime minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen calls a general election for 1 November, thereby avoiding a vote of no confidence.

Ugandan president Yoweri Museveni fires his son Lt. Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba as commander of the national infantry forces after Kainerugaba made a series of tweets threatening to capture Nairobi, the capital of neighbouring Kenya.

Americans Carolyn R. Bertozzi and Karl Barry Sharpless, and Dane Morten P. Meldal are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for "the development of click chemistry and bioorthogonal chemistry".
A Chess.com investigation finds that Hans Niemann probably cheated in more than 100 chess games.
The IOC states that they were not consulted over Saudi Arabian plans for the $500 billion desert Asian Winter Games and that this was in clear conflict with their policy of using existing arenas.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces shell residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, killing at least three people, injuring twelve others, and causing widespread fires.

context: War against the Islamic State > American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: A United States Air Force airstrike and helicopter raid kill two senior Islamic State leaders in Qamishli, Syria, including the Islamic State's deputy leader in Syria. CENTCOM says that no civilians nor any U.S. military personnel were killed or injured in the operation.
An airstrike kills at least five people and injures 37 others in Tigray Region, Ethiopia.

French author Annie Ernaux is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for "the courage and clinical acuity with which she uncovers the roots, estrangements and collective restraints of personal memory".
The Irish Dancing Commission, Ireland's governing body for Irish dancing, appoints a former judge to investigate claims of prominent dance schools and teachers fixing competitions.
Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko bans price increases as part of an effort to reduce inflation in the country.
Hurricane Ian's death toll increases to 130, with 125 deaths in the United States and five in Cuba, making it the 24th deadliest hurricane in US history.
At least 15 people are killed and 20 others are missing after a boat carrying migrants sinks off the eastern coast of the Greek island of Lesbos. Five others have been rescued.
Sixteen people are killed and 20 others are injured when a bus overturns in Bara District, Nepal.
Mozambique reports its first case of monkeypox.
U.S. President Joe Biden announces that he will pardon anyone who was convicted on prior federal charges, or who was convicted in the District of Columbia, for marijuana possession.

At least 36 people, including 24 children, are killed and 10 others injured when a dismissed policeman open fire in a mass shooting, which started at a daycare centre in Na Klang district, Thailand. The perpetrator later commits suicide after killing his family at his home.
Two people are killed and six others are injured, three of them critically, in a mass stabbing on the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise, Nevada, United States.

Iran's IRIB broadcasts purported confessions from two French citizens accused of espionage. This broadcast comes in the context of the Mahsa Amini protests which began in September as well as the claim by the Iranian government that the protests are an attempt by France and other countries such as the United States and Israel to overthrow the current Iranian Islamic government.

During three separate attacks, a 14-year-old Palestinian boy is killed by Israeli soldiers in a village near Ramallah, in the West Bank, while a 17-year-old Palestinian boy is killed and his mother wounded when Israeli soldiers open fire at residents during confrontations with Israeli settlers.In al-Mazra’a al-Gharbiyah, witnesses said Israeli soldiers opened fire at the residents during confrontations with Israeli settlers, killing a 17-year-old Palestinian and wounding another.

Two soldiers are killed and three civilians are injured when five drug gangs open fire during a attack on a senator's convoy in clashes with airstrikes, prison riots, mass shooting, and mass stabbing between the military and the New People's Army in Eastern Samar, Philippines.
The Somali Armed Forces kill 19 al-Shabaab militants in Bal'ad, Middle Shabelle, in a repelled attack amid ongoing operations against the jihadist group.
Seven soldiers are killed and four injured during an attack at an army base in Garabtisan, Djibouti, by Armed FRUD gunmen. Both the attackers are killed.
Belarusian activist Ales Bialiatski, the Russian human rights society Memorial and the Ukrainian human rights organization The Center for Civil Liberties are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
Liverpool is selected as the host city of next year's Eurovision Song Contest.
Ten people are killed, eight others are injured, and others remain trapped under rubble after an explosion at an Applegreen petrol station in the village of Creeslough, County Donegal, Ireland.
The Canadian government permanently bans 10,000 IRGC members from Canada.

An armed intruder damages several vehicles in the parking lot of the Iranian embassy in Copenhagen, Denmark. Iranian Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian criticizes the Danish police for not providing adequate protection for the embassy.
Citizens in Lesotho head to the polls to elect the 120 members of the National Assembly.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimean Bridge explosion
text: The Kerch Strait Bridge is hit by an explosion, resulting in a fire and the partial collapse of a road section. Three people are killed. The cause is currently unknown, with a Russian investigative committee saying it was a Ukrainian truck bomb.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The death toll from last Thursday's shelling by Russian forces of a residential area in Zaporizhzhia rises to 17 civilians, including a child.
Two 17-year-old Palestinians are killed and 11 more injured during a raid when three gunmen open fire in a mass shooting at a refugee camp in Jenin, in the occupied West Bank.
A shooting attack by Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades militants kills an Israeli soldier and injures two police officers and a guard.
The Ministry of Economy of Argentina announces regulations on import authorizations in an attempt to prevent fraud and preserve the country's reserves of U.S. dollars, according to the Central Bank.
At least 12 people are killed and 30 others are injured when a bus collides with a diesel tanker and catches fire in Nashik, Maharashtra, India.
At least 76 people are killed after a boat carrying people fleeing floodwater capsizes in Anambra State, Nigeria.
Four people are killed by flash floods across Cambodia. Thousands of hectares of crops are inundated.
The Netherlands and France urge their citizens to leave Iran.
The Ukrainian immigration center denies visa extensions to Iranian students in retaliation for Russia using Iranian drones during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

All rail traffic in northern Germany is suspended for nearly three hours in the morning after vital cables for the rail were found cut. Deutsche Bahn blames sabotage for the incident and Federal Police launch an investigation into the incident.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zaporizhzhia residential building airstrike
text: A Russian missile attack kills at least 13 people and injures 89 others in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimean Bridge explosion
text: Russian president Vladimir Putin formally accuses Ukraine, and specifically the Security Service of Ukraine, of being behind the explosion on the Crimean Bridge that killed three people and partially destroyed part of the bridge, saying that the explosion was an "act of terrorism".

UN Secretary-General António Guterres proposes a "rapid action force" of several countries that could intervene in Haiti in order to help the Haitian National Police restore control of the country and remove the threat posed by "armed gangs".
Hurricane Julia makes landfall overnight in Laguna de Perlas, Nicaragua.
A landslide caused by days of torrential rain kills at least 22 people in Santos Michelena, Venezuela.
Three people are killed when a wooden tourist boat carrying 14 people capsizes in Gdańsk, Poland.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal
text: Nepalese president Bidya Devi Bhandari tests positive for COVID-19 one day after being hospitalized.
An investigation is launched in the Gambia into the deaths of 66 children during the past three months, which have been linked to four brands of imported cough syrup.
Austrians head to the polls to elect their president.
Incumbent president Alexander van der Bellen secures reelection after receiving more than 50% of the votes.
Shane van Gisbergen of New Zealand, partnered with Garth Tander of Australia, win the Bathurst 1000 in a Triple Eight Race Engineering run in a Holden Commodore ZB.
Novak Djoković wins the Astana Open in Kazakhstan with a straight sets (6-3, 6-4) victory over Stefanos Tsitsipas.
Barbora Krejčíková wins the Ostrava Open in the Czech Republic (5–7, 7–6(7–4), 6–3) against world number 1 Iga Świątek.
Max Verstappen wins the Japanese Grand Prix to take the 2022 Formula One World Championship.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 10 October 2022 missile strikes on Ukraine
text: The Russian Armed Forces launch missile strikes on the Ukrainian cities and towns of Kyiv, Kharkiv, Khmelnytskyi, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Ivano-Frankivsk, Sumy, Dnipro, Lviv, Ternopil and Poltava, killing at least nineteen people and injuring hundreds more.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Moldova–Russia relations
text: Moldova confirms that Russian Navy warships in the Black Sea fired cruise missiles through its airspace to strike targets inside Ukraine. The Russian ambassador is subsequently summoned by Moldovan authorities to explain the violation.
Americans Ben Bernanke, Douglas Diamond and Philip H. Dybvig are awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences "for research on banks and financial crises".
Poland advises its citizens to leave Belarus by "commercial or private means" amid deteriorating relations between the two countries.

Former Liberian rebel commander Kunti Kamara goes on trial in Paris, France for war crimes and crimes against humanity, in a precedent-setting French trial under the doctrine of universal jurisdiction.
Fernando Santos, the manager of the Portuguese national football team, is convicted of creating a fictitious company to pay less taxes from his FPF salary.
Prime Minister of Malaysia Ismail Sabri dissolves parliament, with snap elections to be held later this year.
The Revolution for Prosperity party wins the election by a small margin, but falls short of controlling the National Assembly.
Kenyans Benson Kipruto and Ruth Chepngetich win the Chicago Marathon, with Chepngetich defending her title.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarusian involvement in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Thousands of Russian troops enter Belarus by the "trainload" as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns G7 nations that Russia is planning on launching another offensive against Kyiv with direct Belarusian involvement. The troop movements come a day after Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko accused Ukraine of planning to launch an attack on the country.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Lviv experiences a major power outage after a Russian missile strike damages "critical infrastructure".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia adds Meta Platforms, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, to its list of "terrorists and extremists" for tolerating Russophobia and allowing calls to violence against Russians.
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs says that renewed fighting between tribes has displaced more than 8,000 civilians in South Sudan.
An Israeli soldier is killed by two Lions' Den gunmen near the Israeli settlement of Shavei Shomron, in the occupied West Bank.
Fourteen people in Guatemala and ten in El Salvador are killed as Hurricane Julia causes torrential rain in both countries.
Ten people are killed and 4 others are injured after a fire broke out in Esigodini, Matabeleland South Province, Zimbabwe.
At least 32 people are injured after a carbon monoxide leak is discovered in a care home in Allentown, Pennsylvania, United States.

It is announced that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a United States-brokered agreement that will allow both countries to exploit gas fields in the eastern Mediterranean Sea, thereby ending decades of maritime border disputes between the two nations.

A meeting of the Los Angeles City Council is disrupted by protesters calling for the resignations of council members after then-president Nury Martinez was heard on a leaked audio recording making racist remarks and denigrating colleagues.
Revolution for Prosperity party leader Sam Matekane announces that his party has formed a majority coalition with the Alliance of Democrats and the Movement for Economic Change.
The Federal State of Mexico legalizes same-sex marriage.
NASA says that its DART spacecraft has successfully altered the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos by around 32 minutes in a demonstration of asteroid impact avoidance.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimean Bridge explosion
text: Russia says that it has arrested eight people, five Russians and three people from Ukraine and Armenia, over the Crimea Bridge explosion.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces strike a marketplace in Avdiivka, Donetsk Oblast, killing at least seven civilians and injuring eight others.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: French President Emmanuel Macron announces that France will send radar and air defense systems to Ukraine "in the coming weeks".

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United Kingdom's Ministry of Defence announces that it will donate AMRAAM air-to-air missiles to Ukraine in the coming weeks. The missiles are capable of intercepting cruise missiles. A further 18 howitzers will also be donated to the Ukrainian military.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Canada says that it will provide 47 million in new military aid to Ukraine including artillery rounds, winter clothing, drone cameras, and satellite communications.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Annexation of southeastern Ukraine by the Russian Federation > United Nations General Assembly Resolution ES-11/4
text: The United Nations General Assembly passes a resolution condemning Russia's "attempted illegal annexation" of Ukrainian territory. Only Belarus, Nicaragua, North Korea, Russia and Syria voted against the resolution.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Moldova urges its citizens to reduce their use of electricity after Ukraine suspended exports of electricity due to Russian missile attacks damaging critical infrastructure.

context: Right-wing terrorism in Europe > 2022 Bratislava shooting
text: Two people are killed and another is injured as a gunman opens fire outside an LGBT venue in Bratislava, Slovakia. The perpetrator, who has committed suicide after the attack, is identified as a far-right extremist.
Fighting between the Eritrean Defence Forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front is reported in Adigrat, Rama, Sheraro, and Zalambessa as Eritrea intensifies military mobilisation.
An 18-year-old Palestinian is killed and another is injured near Hebron, as Israeli soldiers storm the Al-Arroub refugee camp.

context: 2021–present United Kingdom cost of living crisis
text: According to the Office of National Statistics, the economy of the United Kingdom shrank 0.3% in August, as the cost of living crisis continues to affect many industries.
At least 33 people are killed by heavy flooding in Nepal, primarily in the Karnali Province.
Eighteen people are killed and others injured after a bus carrying 47 flood survivors bursts into flames in Karachi, Pakistan.
Two people are killed and six others are injured after a bus rolls over and catches fire in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin, United States.
Lebanon reports its first death from cholera since 1993 as cases rise to 26.
Two police officers are killed and another is wounded during an ambush in Bristol, Connecticut, United States. The perpetrator is killed after the shooting.
A jury in Waterbury, Connecticut awards eight families of the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting $965 million against far-right radio host and conspiracy theorist Alex Jones.

Amid increasing pressure over an audio recording where she made racist and denigrating remarks, councilwoman Nury Martinez announces her resignation from the Los Angeles City Council, two days after stepping down from the council presidency.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2022 Ukrainian southern counteroffensive
text: Russia announces that it will evacuate civilians from Kherson to "other regions of the country" following an appeal from Kherson Military-Civilian Administration leader Volodymyr Saldo.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian forces launch eight missiles at Mykolaiv, hitting a five-story residential building. One of the victims was an 11-year-old boy, who was rescued with broken legs after spending hours under the rubble, but later died in a hospital due to heart failure.

context: Syrian civil war > October 2022 northern Aleppo clashes
text: The jihadist group Tahrir al-Sham captures the city of Afrin in Aleppo Governorate, Syria, following days of clashes with the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights.

context: Syrian civil war > October 2022 northern Aleppo clashes
text: Tahrir al-Sham forces capture the town of Jindires amid ongoing clashes in the region.

context: Syrian civil war > 2022 Al-Sabboura bus bombing
text: Eighteen soldiers are killed and 20 others are injured when a bomb explodes on a military bus near Damascus.
Eleven people are killed and 53 more injured as a bus hit a roadside bomb on a road between Bandiagara and Goundaka, in the Mopti Region.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism
text: Taiwan lifts all remaining restrictions on entering the country, which were imposed due to the pandemic.
Canada imposes sanctions on 17 Iranian entities over human rights abuses, including former Foreign Relations Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif.

Five people are killed and two others injured in a spree shooting at several locations in a suburban neighborhood of Raleigh, North Carolina, United States. The suspect, a 15-year-old boy, is later taken into custody and is in critical condition from injuries sustained during the shooting.
Nikolas Cruz, the preperator of the 2018 Stoneman Douglas High School shooting is spared the death penalty for life in prison. He is scheduled to be sentenced on November 1.

context: Aftermath of the 2022 Swedish general election, Tidö Agreement
text: Swedish right-wing parties sign an agreement to form a government led by Ulf Kristersson. The government will include the Moderate Party, the Christian Democrats, the Liberals, and will be supported by the Sweden Democrats.
Vanuatuans head to the polls in a snap election to vote for the members of parliament.
Rare anti-government protests occur in Beijing ahead of the 20th National Congress of the ruling Chinese Communist Party, protesting the government "Zero-COVID" policy.

Rival Palestinian factions sign an agreement in Algiers, Algeria, aimed at resolving over 15 years of discord. The agreement is signed by senior Fatah leader Azzam al-Ahmad, Hamas political chief Ismael Haniyeh, Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine general secretary Talal Naji, and leaders and representatives of 14 other factions, and calls for legislative and presidential elections to be held in Palestine within one year.

Two people are killed and five others are injured in an exchange of fire between Israeli soldiers and Palestinian militants in Jenin, West Bank, following a raid conducted by the former. The Israeli soldiers aimed to capture a Hamas operative suspected of involvement in recent shootings; he was subsequently detained and taken into custody.
Three people are killed and six others are injured by a roadside bomb near a convoy carrying the relatives of a man who was killed yesterday in Mastung, Balochistan, Pakistan.
Forty-one people are killed and eleven more are injured by an explosion at a coal mine in Amasra, Bartın Province, Turkey.
Aydin Coban, a 44-year old Dutch man convicted of sexually extorting British Columbian teenager Amanda Todd, is sentenced to 13 years in prison.
Kwasi Kwarteng is dismissed by Liz Truss as Chancellor of the Exchequer following the market turbulence after the announcement of his September 2022 United Kingdom mini-budget.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Soloti military training ground shooting
text: At least 11 people are killed and 15 others injured after two shooters open fire on a group of volunteers at a Russian military training ground in Belgorod Oblast, near the border with Ukraine.

context: Mahsa Amini protests > Evin Prison fire
text: Gunfire breaks out amid a fire at the Evin Prison in Tehran, Iran, resulting in the death of eight inmates and the wounding of 61 more.
Five people are killed and nine others are injured in tribal clashes in West Kordofan, Sudan.
Twelve people are killed and three are injured in a mass shooting at a bar in Irapuato, Guanajuato, Mexico.
Twenty people are killed and 14 others are injured after a bus flips over while travelling between Pasto and Popayan, Colombia.
Two people are killed by flash flooding in Agia Pelagia, Heraklion, Crete, Greece.
Namibia reports an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in the northeastern region of Zambezi.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Donbas
text: Donetsk People's Republic authorities say that a Ukrainian rocket attack hit the office of the pro-Russian mayor of Donetsk. No casualties have been reported.
The United States and Canada send military equipment to Haiti, including tactical and armoured vehicles, as violence and shortages continue to worsen in the country.

The U.S. drafts a resolution at the United Nations Security Council to approve the deployment of a "multinational rapid action force" to Haiti, citing ongoing "instability and violence" in the country.
At least seven people are injured in a suspected gas explosion at a Japanese restaurant in Tarragona, Spain.
