UNIFIL intervenes to prevent a confrontation between the Lebanese Army and the Israeli Army near the Shebaa Farms.
Tropical Storm Ophelia makes landfall near Emerald Isle, North Carolina, United States.
At least 35 people are killed and 12 are seriously injured by an explosion at an illegal fuel depot in Sèmè-Kpodji, Ouémé Department, Benin.

One Kosovo Police officer is killed and another is injured during an ambush on their patrol in North Kosovo, near the border with Serbia, after around 30 gunmen storm a village. Three of the attackers are later killed in a shootout.
French President Emmanuel Macron announces that France will end its military presence in Niger and will remove its ambassador from the country following a deterioration in relations.

context: Aftermath of the 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh
text: The government of Artsakh says that most of its population will leave following Azerbaijan's takeover of the territory with Armenia confirming that 1,050 refugees from Artsakh have arrived in the country.

context: Assassination and terrorism in Iran, War against the Islamic State
text: Authorities in Iran disarm 30 explosive devices that were set to detonate simultaneously in Tehran and arrest 28 people linked to the Islamic State.
Two Palestinians are killed when Israeli soldiers storm a refugee camp in Tulkarem, in the occupied West Bank.

context: 2023 Hollywood labor disputes > 2023 Writers Guild of America strike
text: The Writers Guild of America and Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers reach a tentative agreement to end the strike that began on May 2.
Saudi Arabia announces that its gross domestic product has surpassed $1 trillion.
Sixteen people are killed by a fire at a coal mine in Panzhou, Guizhou, China.
Six people are killed when a train collides with a car in Hillsborough County, Florida, United States.
One person is killed and ten others are injured after a tourist van fell into a gorge in Balik Pulau, Penang, Malaysia.
President of France Emmanuel Macron announces a $150 million commitment to the International Fund for Agricultural Development during the Global Citizen Festival in New York City's Central Park.

Canadian Speaker of the House Anthony Rota apologizes for inviting Yaroslav Hunka to Parliament during a visit by Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy after it was revealed that he had fought for the Galicia Division under Nazi command.
The Cuban Embassy in Washington, D.C. is attacked with a Molotov cocktail.
NASA's OSIRIS-REx capsule containing samples from the asteroid 101955 Bennu successfully lands back on Earth.
Tigist Assefa breaks the women's marathon world record.
In auto racing, Red Bull wins their sixth World Constructors' Championship after Max Verstappen wins the Japanese Grand Prix.
Kosovo Police enter the village of Banjska, North Kosovo, with armored vehicles, a day after the village was attacked by gunmen.

context: Aftermath of the 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh > Exodus of Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh
text: The number of refugees that have fled to Armenia from Artsakh increases to 6,500, while a further 700 are sheltering with Russian peacekeepers.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Ukraine receives its first shipment of M1 Abrams tanks from the United States.

context: Yemeni civil war > Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
text: An ambush by Houthi insurgents kills two Bahraini soldiers, including an officer, and injures several others.
Sixty-eight people are killed and 290 others are injured by an explosion at a fuel warehouse near Stepanakert, Artsakh.
Six people are killed and 13 others are missing following heavy rains and a landslide in Guatemala City, Guatemala.
Flooding in Autlán de Navarro, Jalisco, Mexico, kills seven people and leaves nine others missing.
Five people are killed when two private planes collide in La Galancita, Durango, Mexico.

context: Territorial disputes in the South China Sea
text: The Philippine Coast Guard removes a series of buoys installed by China in the contested Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea under orders of President Bongbong Marcos.

context: Aftermath of the Derna dam collapses
text: The mayor of Derna, Libya, Abdelmounem al-Ghaithi, and several other officials are detained over mismanagement and negligence accusations following the Derna dam collapse which killed over 5,000 people.
Burkina Faso suspends Jeune Afrique from reporting in the country after the release of a report claiming tension and discontent within the Burkinabe Armed Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Eastern Syria insurgency > Deir ez-Zor clashes
text: Twenty-one gunmen, four SDF members, and a civilian are killed following the resumption of clashes in Deir ez-Zor, Syria.
More than 100 people are killed and more than 150 others are injured in a fire at a wedding in Qaraqosh, Nineveh Governorate, Iraq.
Thai pro-democracy activist Arnon Nampa, who led protests in 2020 and 2021, is sentenced to four years in prison on a charge of royal insult.
The Federal Trade Commission and 17 U.S. states file a lawsuit against Amazon over accusations of monopoly.
President of the United States Joe Biden visits striking UAW workers near Detroit, Michigan, becoming the first sitting American president to join a union picket line.
Civilians protest in Ouagadougou, the capital of Burkina Faso, in support of junta leader Ibrahim Traoré amid rumors of a coup plot.
Daniel Andrews announces his resignation as Premier of Victoria, Australia, after nine years in office.

Anthony Rota resigns as speaker of the House of Commons of Canada amid controversy over his decision to invite Yaroslav Hunka, a Ukrainian–Canadian veteran of the Waffen-SS, to attend a speech by President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy and to introduce Hunka as a "hero" to the House of Commons.

context: 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh > Exodus of Armenians
text: The number of refugees fleeing from Artsakh to Armenia increases to 50,243, more than a third of the region's population.

context: 2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh > Exodus of Armenians
text: Former State Minister of Artsakh Ruben Vardanyan is arrested by Azerbaijan after attempting to cross the border into Armenia.
Azerbaijan reports that 192 of its troops were killed and more than 500 others were injured during last week's offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh.
Authorities in the Mexican state of Nuevo León find at least twelve bodies dumped on roads near Monterrey, likely related to a drug cartel operating in Tamaulipas.

context: 2023 Hollywood labor disputes > 2023 Writers Guild of America strike
text: The Writers Guild of America strike ends after nearly 22 weeks, following a agreement reached between union negotiators and Hollywood's studios and streaming services.
Waheeda Rehman is awarded the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for her work in Hindi cinema.

Documents posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration indicate that South Korean automakers Hyundai and Kia have recalled over 3.4 million vehicles in the United States over concerns of fire risks, and urge owners to park these vehicles outdoors.

A magnitude 4.2 earthquake strikes the Phlegraean Fields supervolcano near Naples, Italy, the strongest earthquake to strike Campi Flegrei in 40 years. Experts say that an eruption of the supervolcano is not imminent, but called for an inspection of buildings in the immediate area.
North Korea deports U.S. soldier Travis King, who crossed the DMZ into North Korea in July, back into U.S. custody.
Five people, all members of the same Arab family, are shot dead in Basmat Tab'un, Israel.
Germany bans the neo-Nazi movement Artgemeinschaft for reportedly targeting children and young people with racial propaganda.
Samvel Shahramanyan, president of the breakaway Republic of Artsakh, signs a decree to dissolve all state institutions of Artsakh in 2024.
The ruling military government of Burkina Faso arrests four officers suspected of attempting to stage a coup. Two additional officers are on the run.
More than 80 people are injured during riots that occurred during protests over the murder of two Meitei students in Manipur, India.

Jihadist insurgents kill at least ten Nigerien soldiers in Kandadji, Tillabéri Region, Niger. Seven soldiers are later killed and five others are injured in a vehicle accident while travelling to reinforce the army unit under attack.
Six teenagers who were kidnapped by a group of armed men a few days ago are found dead near Villanueva, Zacatecas, Mexico.
One person is killed and 162 others are injured in an explosion at a warehouse near the airport in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
Nearly 1,000 people have died of dengue fever in Bangladesh in recent weeks, in the country's most severe outbreak of the disease so far.
A bluetongue disease outbreak in the Netherlands has spread to 319 sheep and cattle farming companies.
Three people are killed during two shootings and an arson attack at a teaching hospital and a nearby private home in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

A woman is killed in her house in Uppsala, Sweden, during a bombing attack intended to target the neighbor next door, while two men were killed and another was injured during two shootings the day before in Stockholm and Jordbro, as deadly violence linked to a feud between criminal gangs escalates.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson summons the heads of the armed forces and police in response to the gang violence.
The historic Sycamore Gap Tree in Northumberland, England, United Kingdom, also known as the "Robin Hood"-tree, is illegally cut down. A 16-year-old boy is arrested.
The ALPHA experiment shows that antimatter falls down in gravity, just like normal matter.

context: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa > Hangu mosque bombing
text: Five people are killed and ten others are injured by two suicide bombers at a mosque in Hangu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Four soldiers and three Pakistani Taliban militants are killed during a shootout in Zhob, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
At least 50 people are killed and more than 50 others are injured in a suicide bombing at a religious gathering in Mastung, Balochistan, Pakistan.

context: Somali Civil War > Mogadishu tea shop bombing
text: At least five people are killed and 18 others are injured when an al-Shabaab suicide bomber detonates his explosive belt in a tea shop in Mogadishu, Somalia.

Toys "R" Us announces plans to open 24 new flagship stores across the United States, along with new shops in airports and on cruise ships, after the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy six years ago.
New York City declares a state of emergency due to widespread flooding caused by heavy rain.
The death toll from an explosion at a fuel warehouse in Berkadzor, Artsakh, on Monday increases to 170 people.
Two people are killed and 17 injured after a school bus crashes into a central reservation and overturns in The Wirral, England.
Nine people are killed, four others are trapped, and 21 are rescued after a mine collapses in Chegutu, Mashonaland West, Zimbabwe.
Five people are killed and five more are hospitalized as a semi truck carrying a toxic substance turns over near Teutopolis, Illinois, United States, causing evacuations.
Duane "Keefe D" Davis is arrested by police for the 1996 murder of American rapper Tupac Shakur.
A second suspect, a man in his sixties, is arrested in connection with the felling of the Sycamore Gap Tree in Northumberland, United Kingdom.

Rafael Curruchiche, a prosecutor in the Guatemalan attorney general's office, accuses the Organization of American States and the European Union of interference in the election and says that around a thousand people denounced irregularities in electoral process.
The Supreme Court of Belarus bans the activities of the Belarusian Left Party after a complaint filed by the Ministry of Justice. Only four political parties remain permitted to operate.
Five Free Papua Movement militants are killed during a shootout with Indonesian soldiers and police officers in the Papua province.
Azerbaijan accuses Armenia of using a sniper to kill one of its soldiers in the city of Kalbajar. Armenia denies involvement in the incident.
Two Morena party pollsters are killed and a third is kidnapped in Juárez, Chiapas, Mexico. A note was left on the bodies from the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, threatening the government.
Maldivians vote in a run-off election between candidates Mohamed Muizzu and Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.
Slovaks elect the 150 members of the National Council.
The U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate pass a 45-day stopgap measure bill backed by House Speaker Kevin McCarthy. President Joe Biden signs the bill, averting a government shutdown.

context: Aftermath of the 2023 Guatemalan general election
text: The office of the Attorney General of Guatemala seizes the tally sheets of votes from the general election and the runoff. The judges of the Supreme Electoral Tribunal opposed the seizure but were attacked by police and prosecutors. Electoral tribunal officials were also intimidated.
Collingwood defeats the Brisbane Lions by four points to win the 2023 AFL Grand Final.
A suicide bomber blew himself up outside the Interior Ministry in Ankara, Turkey, injuring two police officers. A second attacker is shot dead by police.
Tuareg rebels take control of the town of Bamba, Gao Region, Mali, claiming over 80 soldiers have been killed.
At least 13 people are killed and four others are injured in a fire at a nightclub in Murcia, Spain.
Ten people are killed and 60 more are injured after the roof collapses during a baptism ceremony in Ciudad Madero, Mexico.
Ten people are killed and 25 more are injured after a truck carrying mostly Cuban migrants overturned between Pijijiapan and Tonalá in Chiapas, Mexico.
North Dakota state senator Doug Larsen and his family are killed in a plane crash in Grand County, Utah, United States.
A grizzly bear attacks and kills two people and their pet dog in Banff National Park, Alberta, Canada. The bear is later euthanised.
Charles Brown succeeds Mark Milley as chairman of the United States Armed Forces Joint Chiefs of Staff.
California Governor Gavin Newsom appoints Laphonza Butler to fill the United States Senate seat vacated by the death of Dianne Feinstein. She will be California's first openly LGBT senator.
In rugby league, the Penrith Panthers defeat the Brisbane Broncos 26–24 in the 2023 NRL Grand Final, their third consecutive win.
Bartosz Zmarzlik defends his motorcycle speedway world championship title, it was his fourth world Speedway World Championship won overall.
In rallying, Toyota Gazoo win their third consecutive World Rally Championship for Manufacturers title after Kalle Rovanperä and Jonne Halttunen win the Power Stage of the 2023 Rally Chile.
The 44th Ryder Cup comes to an end with a victory of the European team.

context: Insurgency in the Sahel > Jihadist insurgency in Niger
text: At least 29 soldiers are killed during an ambush by Islamic extremists in the Tahoua Region, Niger, involving suicide car bombs and bombings. Several attackers are killed in a counter-offensive.
Turkey launches airstrikes against around 20 PKK targets in northern Iraq, in response to the PKK's bombing of Ankara, killing an unknown number of militants.
Around eighteen to thirty-seven people are killed after an explosion at an illegal oil refinery in Emohua, Rivers State, Nigeria.
Thirty-eight people are injured in a fire at a police facility in Ismailia, Egypt.
The United Nations Security Council approves a resolution establishing a Kenyan-led security force with a mandate of one year to combat gang violence in Haiti.

For the first time in the history of the European Union, representatives of all EU states, most of them foreign ministers, meet informally outside the EU. They meet with the Ukrainian government in Kyiv and assure it of their further support.
Three Filipino fishermen are killed and eleven others survive after their vessel collides with an unidentified foreign merchant ship near the Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea.
The government of Brazil begins expelling non-indigenous residents off of the Apyterewa and Trincheira/Bacajá indigenous territories in Pará state.

The European Space Agency reports that the James Webb Space Telescope has detected "Jupiter-sized objects", unconnected to any stars, which appear to be moving in pairs in the Orion constellation. Around 40 of the objects, known as Jupiter Mass Binary Objects, have been detected so far.

context: 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
text: Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman are awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing technology that resulted in mRNA vaccines for COVID-19.
Al-Ittihad refuses to play a match with Sepahan due to the placement of busts of Qasem Soleimani at the side of the football pitch.
Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov announces the construction of Ukraine's first underground school to protect students from missile strikes.
At least 21 people are killed and 15 others are injured when a bus crashes and falls from an overpass in Mestre, Veneto, Italy.
At least 18 people are killed and 25 more injured by an oil refinery explosion in Emohua, Rivers State, Nigeria.
One person is killed and 17 others are injured in a magnitude 5.7 earthquake in Dipayal Silgadhi, Nepal.
Former Rwandan army major Pierre-Claver Karangwa is arrested in the Netherlands for his role in the 1994 genocide in Mugina, Rwanda, where thousands of people were killed.
Two people are killed and six others are injured in a mass shooting at the Siam Paragon shopping mall in Bangkok, Thailand. The 14-year-old suspect is arrested.

The New Democratic Party of Manitoba wins a majority of the seats in the Legislative Assembly; the party's leader Wab Kinew is set to become Canada's first provincial premier of First Nations descent.
Following a budget dispute within the Republican Party, Kevin McCarthy becomes the first Speaker of the United States House of Representatives to be ousted.

Pierre Agostini, Ferenc Krausz, and Anne L'Huillier are awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter.
Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announces the cancellation of Phase 2 of the United Kingdom's high-speed rail project High Speed 2.
Over 75,000 workers from Kaiser Permanente, an integrated managed care consortium in the United States, go on strike.
The gap between Italy and Germany's 10 year bond yields increases by 200.2 basis points. Italy comes under intensifying pressure to sell off the public assets.
At least 14 people are killed and 100 others are missing after a cloudburst causes severe flooding in Sikkim, India.
The Lhonak Lake bursts its banks, causing major flooding and impacting 22,000 people. It its the worst such disaster in the region in over 50 years.
Large parts of the Teesta Dam have been washed away, with multiple large bridges also being destroyed.
In his exhortation Laudate Deum, Pope Francis speaks out against climate change denial and in favor of fighting the climate crisis.
The United States and Russia test their emergency population warning systems.

context: Protests against the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian journalist Marina Ovsyannikova is sentenced to eight and a half years in prison in absentia for interrupting a news broadcast with anti-war slogans.

context: Protests against the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Around 11 anti-war protesters involved with Code Pink are arrested outside the office of U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders after calling for the Biden administration to bring an end to the war.
Moungi Bawendi, Louis E. Brus, and Alexey Ekimov are awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work on quantum dots.
Lars Schaade is appointed as the new President of the Robert Koch Institute.

In association football, FIFA awards the 2030 FIFA World Cup to Spain, Portugal, and Morocco, making it the first FIFA World Cup tournament to be hosted in North Africa. The opening ceremony will take place in Montevideo, Uruguay, to mark the 100th anniversary of the competition.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Hroza missile attack
text: Ukraine says that Russia has attacked a store and cafe in Hroza, Kharkiv Oblast, with a ballistic missile, killing at least 51 civilians.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia says that a child has been killed and three others are injured while trying to dismantle cluster munitions fired from Ukrainian forces, in the occupied city of Horlivka.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States transfers 1.1 million rounds of Iranian ammunition to Ukraine after the U.S. Navy seized them from a shipment enroute to Yemen in December.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: German Chancellor Olaf Scholz pledges a second Patriot air defense system to Ukraine.
Russia announces the successful test of the Burevestnik, a nuclear-powered and nuclear-capable cruise missile with a potential range of thousands of miles.

context: Syrian civil war > 2023 Homs drone strike
text: At least 112 troops and civilians are killed and 120 others are injured in a drone attack on a Syrian military graduation ceremony in Homs, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > 2023 Turkish drone shootdown
text: A Turkish Air Force Anka-S is shot down by an international coalition F-16 Fighting Falcon in Al Hasakah, Syria, after reportedly operating too close to U.S. forces in the vicinity.

context: Syrian civil war > October 2023 Northern Syria clashes
text: Turkey launches a series of airstrikes targeting the Syrian Democratic Forces in northeastern Syria, killing at least two people and injuring three others.
At least six people are killed and 38 others are injured during a series of airstrikes by the Syrian Air Force on Idlib.
Four Palestinians are killed in separate incidents in the occupied West Bank, three by Israeli soldiers, and one by an Israeli settler.
Jon Fosse is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for his innovative plays, prose and style, which has come to be known as Fosse minimalism.
Typhoon Koinu makes landfall in Hengchun, Pingtung County, Taiwan as a category 4 typhoon, with winds of over 342 kilometers in Orchid Island, becoming the strongest on record.
Russia and Abkhazia sign an agreement to establish a permanent naval base for the Russian Navy on the Black Sea coast of Ochamchira District, Abkhazia.
Italian authorities impound the Open Arms vessel used by Spanish NGO Proactiva Open Arms to rescue migrants in the Mediterranean Sea.
The Dutch platform supply vessel VOS Pace rescues 79 migrants in the Atlantic Ocean, nine of whom mutiny. The mutineers are later arrested in Fuerteventura, Canary Islands.
An investigation into electronic surveillance by European Investigative Collaborations reveals inefficiencies in European Union regulations governing the sale of enabling software.

context: Immigration policy of the Joe Biden administration
text: The Biden administration announces that it will waive 26 federal laws in Starr County, Texas, in order to allow construction of the border wall in an attempt to help prevent illegal entry into the country.
The EU Parliament votes 279–173, with 33 abstentions, in favor of the appointment of Wopke Hoekstra as the new EU Commissioner.
Kenyan foreign minister Alfred Mutua is replaced by Musalia Mudavadi following controversy over the country's involvement in the crisis in Haiti.
The Chamber of Representatives (Belgium) of Belgium is the first parliament in the world to adopt a resolution in support of Agent Orange victims.
sources: Official website of the Belgian Parliament lachambre.be

context: Syrian civil war > Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war > October 2023 Northern Syria clashes
text: Two Turkish soldiers are killed when the Syrian Army fires on their positions with artillery in northern Syria.
A 19-year-old Palestinian man is shot and killed by Israeli settlers attacking the city of Huwara, Palestine.
Seventeen people are killed and fifteen others are injured after a bus carrying migrants from Venezuela crashes in Oaxaca, Mexico.

Floods and mudslides triggered by heavy rain occur in Sri Lanka, with five people killed and five others injured when a tree falls on a bus in Colombo. Another person is killed by a falling rock in Galle District.
Six people are killed and 38 others are injured in a fire at a six-storey residential building in Mumbai, India.
A Piper PA-34 Seneca training plane crashes in Chilliwack, British Columbia, Canada, killing all three on board.
Iranian activist Narges Mohammadi is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her support of feminism and human rights.
Charlot Salwai is elected as Prime Minister of Vanuatu following a no-confidence vote against Sato Kilman.

Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades commander Mohammed Deif announces the invasion as the start of Operation Al-Aqsa Flood. Israel declares a state of war in response and warns Palestinian civilians to leave the Gaza Strip.

Palestinian militant groups led by Hamas launch over 3,500 rockets from the Gaza Strip into Israel and execute a surprise invasion by land, sea and air, breaking through the Gaza–Israel barrier to attack at least 22 locations in Israel's Southern District.

context: Gaza–Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Targeted communities include Be'eri, Ofakim, Sderot, Kfar Aza, Kerem Shalom, Nirim, Netiv HaAsara, Nir Oz, Nahal Oz outpost, Holit, Nir Am, Nir Yitzhak, Be'er Sheva and Sde Yemen.
text: Yonatan Steinberg, commander of the 933rd "Nahal" Brigade, is killed during clashes with Hamas in Kerem Shalom.

context: Gaza–Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Targeted communities include Be'eri, Ofakim, Sderot, Kfar Aza, Kerem Shalom, Nirim, Netiv HaAsara, Nir Oz, Nahal Oz outpost, Holit, Nir Am, Nir Yitzhak, Be'er Sheva and Sde Yemen.
text: Attackers briefly seize control of the IDF's 143rd "Gaza" Division headquarters in Re'im, Eshkol Regional Council, before it is retaken. Several Israeli soldiers are captured and taken hostage to the Gaza Strip.

context: Gaza–Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Targeted communities include Be'eri, Ofakim, Sderot, Kfar Aza, Kerem Shalom, Nirim, Netiv HaAsara, Nir Oz, Nahal Oz outpost, Holit, Nir Am, Nir Yitzhak, Be'er Sheva and Sde Yemen.
text: Battle of Sderot: At least twenty Israeli police officers are killed by Hamas inside the police headquarters of Sderot after the building is seized.

context: Gaza–Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Targeted communities include Be'eri, Ofakim, Sderot, Kfar Aza, Kerem Shalom, Nirim, Netiv HaAsara, Nir Oz, Nahal Oz outpost, Holit, Nir Am, Nir Yitzhak, Be'er Sheva and Sde Yemen.
text: The Re'im music festival massacre is reported. Hundreds are injured, and some survivors are taken as hostages. Atrocities are reported in other locations: Netiv HaAsara attack, Kfar Aza massacre, Holit massacre, Nir Oz massacre and the Be'eri massacre which is discovered after 50 Israeli hostages are rescued by IDF forces.

context: Gaza–Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Targeted communities include Be'eri, Ofakim, Sderot, Kfar Aza, Kerem Shalom, Nirim, Netiv HaAsara, Nir Oz, Nahal Oz outpost, Holit, Nir Am, Nir Yitzhak, Be'er Sheva and Sde Yemen.
text: Scores of Israeli and non-Israeli civilians are taken hostage to Gaza. Hamas spokesman Abu Obaida says they are being held in "safe places and resistance tunnels".

Thousands of Israelis are injured by missile attacks and shootings, and at least 700 are killed. At least 400 Palestinians are killed and over 1,600 are injured in the Gaza Strip by airstrikes launched by the Israeli Air Force.
At least 2,445 people are killed and 9,240 others are injured when two magnitude 6.3 earthquakes strike Herat Province, Afghanistan.
The death toll from the severe flooding caused by a cloudburst in Sikkim, India, increases to 47 people.
Thirteen people are killed and seven others are injured in an explosion at a firecracker warehouse in Attibele, Karnataka, India.
Presidential candidate Marc Ravalomanana is injured by police during a demonstration prior to the election.

A seventh individual, linked to the August assassination of Ecuadorian presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio, dies in a prison in Quito, following the deaths of six others during riots at a prison in Guayaquil.
Venezuela issues an arrest warrant through Interpol for Juan Guaidó, who is currently in-exile in the United States, citing crimes of treason, usurpation of functions and money laundering.
The Chinese Communist Party expels Chinese Football Association first vice president Du Zhaocai for corruption.
Research into the White Sands fossil footprints in New Mexico reveals that human settlement in North America may have originated earlier than previously assumed.
In auto racing, Red Bull driver Max Verstappen wins his third World Drivers' Championship after his teammate Sergio Pérez fails to complete the sprint race of the 2023 Qatar Grand Prix.

section: Holidays not aligned to the Gregorian Calendar
text: Jewish holiday celebrated worldwide

section: Holidays not aligned to the Gregorian Calendar
text: Jewish holiday that coincides with Shemini Atzeret in Israel, and is celebrated the following day in the rest of the world.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Battle of Sderot
text: Hamas forces and the IDF clash for a second day in Sderot.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war, Israel–Hamas war protests
text: Pro-Israel and pro-Palestine rallies occur in several American cities, including Atlanta, Chicago and New York.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Re'im music festival massacre
text: More than 260 bodies are found in Re'im, Southern Israel, after Hamas attacked a trance music festival. Foreign nationals are among those killed in the massacre.
Israel's Security Cabinet says that it has approved a military operation against Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the Gaza Strip.
The death toll in the Gaza Strip increases to 370 with more than 2,200 injured. The death toll in Israel increases to more than 750 with over 2,000 injured. Hamas says they hold 130 Israeli captives.
Israeli ambassador to the United States Michael Herzog says that Americans have been taken hostage by Hamas in Gaza.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)
text: Hezbollah forces in southern Lebanon open fire on Israeli positions in Shebaa Farms with artillery and guided rockets. Israel responds with airstrikes on Hezbollah artillery positions.
Swaminarayan Akshardham, the world's second largest Hindu temple, is officially inaugurated and opened in Robbinsville, New Jersey.
The western area of Maui, Hawaii, U.S., located north of Kaanapali, reopens for tourism two months after wildfires damaged the area.
At least 27 people are killed and 50 more injured during landslides caused by heavy rains in Yaoundé, Cameroon.
The Ecuadorian government extends the country's state of emergency by a month.
An Egyptian policeman kills two Israeli tourists and an Egyptian tour guide and injures a third Israeli in Alexandria, Egypt. The gunman is later arrested.
The second part of the presidential debates is held.
Luxembourg goes to the polls to elect the Chamber of Deputies.
Kelvin Kiptum sets a new marathon world record at the Chicago Marathon, becoming the first runner to break 2 hours and 1 minute.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Shati refugee camp airstrike
text: Israel launches airstrikes on the Al-Shati refugee camp in the Gaza Strip, resulting in civilian casualties.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Pro-Palestine and pro-Israel protests are held in London, United Kingdom, with pro-Palestinian protesters also gathering at the Israeli Embassy.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United Nations Security Council meets in an emergency session but fails to achieve unanimity for a joint statement.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Jabalia camp market airstrike
text: Israel launches airstrikes on a market in the Jabalia Camp in the Gaza Strip, killing more than 60 civilians and injuring 120 others.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Israel announces a total blockade of the Gaza Strip, encompassing supplies of food, water, electricity, and gas.
Israeli air attacks and shelling targeting houses and apartment buildings displace over 123,000 people in Gaza, according to the UN Office for Humanitarian Affairs.

At least 22 members of a Palestinian family, including seven children, are killed in an Israeli air strike in Khan Younis, Gaza Strip. Six members of the family remain trapped under the rubble of the destroyed house.
The death toll from the Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip increases to 687 people, with more than 3,800 injured. The death toll in Israel increases to 900 with more than 2,500 injured.
In Beita, Nablus, a Palestinian is shot by Israeli soldiers. Earlier, one Palestinian was killed by Israeli forces in Hebron, West Bank, one in Jericho, and two in Ramallah.
In Duma, Nablus, a Palestinian is shot by Israeli soldiers, while Israeli settlers torch cars and attack farmers.
In Einabus, West Bank, two Palestinians are shot by Israeli soldiers. Twelve people are evacuated for tear gas inhalation, with Israeli forces attempting to stop the evacuation by emergency services.
Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirms that 18 Thais, mostly migrant workers, have been killed, while several others have been taken hostage by the militant group.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Four Hezbollah members killed in an Israeli airstrike on Marwahin and Ayta ash Shab, Lebanon

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Two IDF soldiers, Lt. Col Alim Abdallah, Deputy Commander of the IDF's 300th Brigade killed and three IDF soldiers wounded in a rocket and artillery shootout on the border with Hezbollah.
The Tatmadaw launches an artillery attack on an IDP camp near Laiza, Kachin State, killing at least 29 people and injuring 56 others.
Claudia Goldin is awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for her research into female income and employment.
Tropical Storm Max makes landfall in Guerrero, Mexico. Tropical storm warnings are issued for the states of Guerrero and Michoacán.
The death toll from the floods in Sikkim, India, increases to 74.
A court in Kenya temporarily blocks the government from deploying police personnel to Haiti until 24 October.
A car crashes into the Chinese consulate in San Francisco, California, United States, and its driver is shot dead by police.

Peruvian police liberate 44 individuals, mostly Malaysians, from a Taiwanese organized crime group's extortion scheme in La Molina, Lima. Concurrently, six Taiwanese and two Peruvians are arrested, and the victims, who were deceived with job offers and trafficked via Amsterdam, Netherlands, will be extradited to Malaysia following an investigative process.
Dozens of road blockades are reported throughout the country, mainly in Guatemala City, organized by community organizations demanding the resignation of Attorney General María Consuelo Porras.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign
text: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. withdraws from seeking the Democratic nomination and announces an independent bid for the presidency.
Former U.S. Representative (TX-23) Will Hurd suspends his campaign for the Republican nomination and endorses Nikki Haley.

context: Aftermath of the 2023 Gabonese coup d'état
text: Gabonese leader Brice Oligui Nguema appoints a new parliament with 98 members, including opposition leaders and pro-Bongo politicians.
France begins withdrawing its forces from Niger after the ruling military government ordered them to leave.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Hajji Tower airstrike
text: At least six Palestinian journalists have been killed in Israel's ongoing shelling of the Gaza Strip. Funerals for two of them are held at a hospital in Gaza City.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Israeli airstrikes hit near the Rafah crossing between Gaza and Egypt, after an Israeli official advised Palestinians to leave the Gaza Strip through the border crossing.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemns Israel's decision to order a blockade on Gaza, including a ban on food and water, saying that the action is in violation of international law.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The World Health Organization calls for a humanitarian corridor into Gaza, after thirteen health facilities are damaged by Israeli attacks.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The United Nations Agency for Palestine (UNRWA) says that 187,518 people, which is nearly a tenth of Gaza's population, have fled their homes. Nearly 137,500 internally displaced people are sheltering in 83 UNRWA schools, with bread being provided by the World Food Programme. Four schools and eight healthcare facilities in Gaza also sustained damage and the territory is experiencing a severe shortage of drinking water due to the ongoing Israeli blockade.

The death toll in the Gaza Strip has increased to 950 people, with more than 4,000 injured. At least 18 people were killed, and 100 others were injured in the West Bank. The death toll in Israel surpasses 1,000.

Israeli airstrikes on Gaza damage residential buildings and large tower blocks, as well as schools and UN buildings, killing civilians. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemns these actions, saying that they are in violation of international law.
Israeli airstrikes destroy a Palestinian Telecommunications Company building in Gaza City, causing widespread communications and internet outages.
An Israeli soldier and two Palestinian Islamic Jihad militants are killed in clashes on the border with Lebanon.
An Israeli airstrike kills Jawad Abu Shammala and Zakaria Abu Maamar, two senior officials of Hamas' political office.

Finland reports that damage to the Balticconnector submarine pipeline connecting Finland and Estonia is being investigated as either an act of sabotage or accidental damage after officials ruled out a simple malfunction.
Ten additional charges are filed against U.S. Rep. George Santos including identity theft, credit card fraud, and submitting false campaign reports.
Hurricane Lidia makes landfall in the Mexican state of Jalisco as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir–Simpson scale, killing one person.
Liberians elect their president.
In association football, UEFA announces that the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland will host UEFA Euro 2028, while Italy and Turkey will host UEFA Euro 2032.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The Palestine Liberation Organization says that Israel refused a request to bring food and medical supplies into the Gaza Strip.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Gaza's only power plant stops producing power due to a lack of fuel, thereby threatening to further impact over-capacity medical facilities. Authorities begin rationing and directing power to emergency services.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The UN Palestine Agency says that Israeli airstrikes have killed eleven of its staff in Gaza, with four Palestine Red Crescent Society paramedics and one Magen David Adom ambulance driver also being killed in clashes. The agency also says that it has less than two weeks' supply of food and water available to assist the more than 180,000 people who have sought refuge in their schools in Gaza.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: Dozens of Israeli Air Force warplanes carry out more than 200 airstrikes overnight on the Al-Furqan neighborhood in Gaza City. The Rimal and al-Karama neighbourhoods are also targeted by airstrikes, with eight 12-storey buildings destroyed. At least 30 people are killed and hundreds more are injured.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: Israeli airstrikes destroy more than 22,600 residential units and 10 health facilities and also damage 48 schools as Hamas continues to fire rockets from civilian areas in violation of international law. At least 260 children have been killed by Israeli attacks on Gaza.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: At least 16 Palestinians are killed in an Israeli air raid on the southern city of Khan Younis and at least three Palestinians are killed and nine others are injured by Israeli soldiers in the Qusra south of Nablus in the West Bank.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: At least 1,055 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli air attacks and 5,184 others have been injured, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. At least 1,300 people in Israel have been killed and 2,800 others have been injured, according to the Israeli military.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: Germany approves an Israeli request to use two of its IAI Heron combat drones in strikes on the Gaza Strip.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Three Lebanese civilians are injured in IDF and Hezbollah clashes near Tyre, Lebanon.

A magnitude 6.3 aftershock strikes near the Afghan city of Herat, killing at least one person and injuring 65 others just four days after two earthquakes of the same magnitude struck the same area, killing thousands of people.
Flights are suspended at Luton Airport in Bedfordshire, England, United Kingdom, after a fire occurs in a multistorey car park at the airport.
China deports Australian journalist Cheng Lei following over three years of detention and a conviction on espionage charges.
The Dominican Republic partially reopens its border with Haiti for some commercial activity after closing the border last month.

Police in Vienna, Austria, announce that they have banned a pro-Palestinian protest over mentions of "from the river to the sea" in invitations and the characterization of the protest as a call for violence.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Benny Gantz agree to form an emergency government during the war.

Smer leader Robert Fico agrees to form a coalition government with the left-wing Hlas and ultranationalist Slovak National Party, paving the way for Fico to become Prime Minister of Slovakia for a fourth time.

context: October 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
text: Republicans in the U.S. House nominate Steve Scalise to replace Kevin McCarthy as House Speaker.

Syria says that Israel has launched airstrikes on the international airports of Damascus and Aleppo, taking both out of service. Air defences are activated in response to the attacks, and no casualties are reported.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Three of five water plants in Gaza are inoperable due to the Israeli bombings and a lack of fuel, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres says that life-saving supplies, including food, fuel and water, must be allowed into Gaza.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Israeli Energy Minister Israel Katz says that the blockade of Gaza will not end until all Israeli hostages are released by Hamas.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Former Human Rights Watch executive director Kenneth Roth says that the ongoing attacks on Palestinian civilians, carried out by Israel, could constitute a war crime.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The Norwegian Refugee Council calls for humanitarian corridors to be established in order to allow the safe passage of personnel and relief supplies into Gaza.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: The United Nations says that nearly 339,000 people have been displaced in Gaza by ongoing Israeli bombing raids.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: At least 51 people are killed and 281 others are injured in Israeli air strikes on neighborhoods in Gaza City.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: The death toll in Gaza increases to 1,200, with nearly 5,600 others injured. The death toll in Israel surpasses 1,400.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: Israeli settlers kill a Palestinian father and son during a funeral in the West Bank.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war
text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt denies rumors that the Rafah border crossing is closed, asserting that the crossing remains operational and has not been closed since the beginning of the blockade. The ministry also calls upon the international community to send humanitarian aid to Palestine through the El Arish International Airport.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Three people are killed and two others are injured in Belgorod Oblast, Russia, after debris from a downed Ukrainian drone hit several houses.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Avdiivka
text: Ukraine says that Russia has begun an assault on the city of Avdiivka, in Donetsk Oblast, supported by tanks and armored vehicles.

International Monetary Fund managing director Kristalina Georgieva confirms that Zambia, the first African nation to default following the COVID-19 pandemic, has agreed to a debt agreement with foreign creditors concerning US$6.3 billion of its debt.
Zimbabwe bans gatherings of more than 50 people amid a cholera outbreak in the country.

U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Wally Adeyemo announces that the United States and Qatar will block Iran from receiving $6 billion transferred from South Korea to Qatar last month as part of a prisoner swap.

The United Nations Human Rights Council extends a special rapporteur's mandate to investigate human rights violations in Russia for an additional year, despite Russia's previous refusal to recognize the rapporteur's mandate or permit their entry into the country.

Multinational investment bank Goldman Sachs sues the Malaysian government for alleged violations of a 2020 settlement related to the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal, filing the case at the London Court of International Arbitration.
Former first lady Sylvia Bongo Ondimba is jailed by the ruling military junta.

An Aurora Police Department officer who was involved in the arrest of Elijah McClain is found guilty of negligent homicide and third-degree assault, while another officer is acquitted of manslaughter and assault charges.
Rallies in support of Palestine take place around the world, including in Argentina, Canada, Chile, Germany, Japan, South Africa, South Korea, and Spain.
French Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin announces that France will ban all pro-Palestinian protests in the country.
United States Senator Bob Menendez is charged with acting as a foreign agent for Egypt while serving as a member of the United States Senate.

Madagascar's constitutional court postpones the upcoming election from November 9 to November 16, amid a political crisis involving protests against the Ntsay government following President Andry Rajoelina's resignation.

context: October 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
text: Steve Scalise withdraws his candidacy for House Speaker a day after being nominated, citing a lack of sufficient support from the Republican Party in the U.S. House.

context: Islamic terrorism in Europe > Arras school stabbing
text: A teacher is killed and another teacher and a security guard are seriously injured in a stabbing attack at a high school in Arras, Hauts-de-France, France. The Chechen attacker is arrested by police.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Israeli Defense Forces notifies the United Nations that the 1.1 million Palestinians living north of Wadi Gaza in the Gaza Strip have been ordered to relocate to Southern Gaza within 24 hours ahead of an expected ground invasion.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Israeli Air Force begins dropping evacuation leaflets over Gaza City warning residents to leave the city immediately.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Hamas tells Palestinians to remain in their houses and not to relocate to Southern Gaza, despite Israeli orders to do so.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United Kingdom begins evacuating British citizens from Israel.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Israeli troops conduct "localized raids" into Gaza in an attempt to locate Hamas-held hostages.
At a press conference, Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant says that the main goal of the upcoming military operation will be to "topple Hamas rule in Gaza".
Israeli soldiers open fire against protestors in the occupied West Bank, killing eleven people and injuring 124 others.

Human Rights Watch accuses the Israeli Defense Forces of using white phosphorus munitions in its military operation in the Gaza area and Lebanon, saying that this puts civilians at risk of serious and long-term injuries.
Hamas says that 13 hostages, including foreigners, have been killed in Israeli airstrikes.
An Israeli missile strike hits a group of journalists on the Lebanese side of the border with Israel, injuring six of them, and killing a Reuters videographer, Issam Abdallah.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Reuters photojournalists Issam Abdallah killed, Christina Assi critically injured and five journalist of AFP and Al Jazeera injured by two IDF tank shells when documenting an IDF outpost in southern Lebanon.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Avdiivka
text: Heavy fighting occurs between Ukrainian and Russian forces for control of Avdiivka in Donetsk Oblast. Ukraine says that Russia has launched airstrikes and artillery attacks on the city overnight but that its troops were "holding their ground".

A diplomat at the Embassy of Israel in Beijing, China, is stabbed by an unknown foreign attacker. The diplomat was taken to a hospital for treatment and is in stable condition. The incident is being treated as a terrorist attack.
Seven people are killed and 15 are injured after a suicide bombing at a mosque in Puli Khumri, Baghlan Province, Afghanistan.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: German literary society LitProm postpones a ceremony at the Frankfurt Book Fair honoring Palestinian author Adania Shibli with the LiBeraturpreis award following the war.

context: Acquisition of Activision Blizzard by Microsoft
text: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority approves Microsoft's takeover of video game company Activision Blizzard.
Seven people are killed and 16 others are injured when a vehicle carrying illegal immigrants from the Middle East crashes in Mühldorf, Bavaria, Germany.
A military helicopter crashes in Canelas Municipality, Durango, Mexico, killing three people.
The United States' National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reports a 99% likelihood of 2023 becoming the warmest year on record.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: During a CIS Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Russian President Vladimir Putin says that Russia will offer to mediate a ceasefire.
Anti-Israel protests occur in many cities across the Middle East.
Cities across the United States tighten their security after former Hamas leader Khaled Mashal called for a Global Day of Jihad against Zionism.
Russian police detain one of the three lawyers of Alexei Navalny and raid the houses of the other two, accusing them of belonging to an extremist organization.

context: October 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
text: Jim Jordan wins the Republican nomination for House Speaker after Steve Scalise withdrew his bid.
NASA successfully launches its Psyche space probe from Kennedy Space Center. The spacecraft will explore the M-type asteroid 16 Psyche, a suspected core of a protoplanet in the asteroid belt.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)
text: Shia Islamist militant group Hezbollah fires on five Israeli outposts in the Shebaa Farms with guided missiles and mortar shells. A Hezbollah member is killed during a subsequent gunbattle with Israeli troops.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)
text: Two civilians are killed during shelling by Israeli forces in Shebaa, Lebanon.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip > 2023 attacks on Palestinians evacuating Gaza City
text: Seventy people have been killed in attacks on convoys evacuating Gaza City, according to Hamas.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 724 children are killed by Israeli shelling and airstrikes in Gaza, Defence for Children International says.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 27 Palestinians are killed by Israeli airstrikes in Jabaliya in the Gaza Strip.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: All living generations of 45 families have been wiped from the Gaza civil registry, the health ministry says.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The United Nations health organization has condemned Israel’s order to evacuate 22 hospitals treating more than 2,000 inpatients in northern Gaza, saying it "could be tantamount to a death sentence"

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Medical Aid for Palestinians says ambulances in Gaza are being targeted by Israeli air raids.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza is hit by Israeli strikes and sustained damage, says the Episcopal Diocese of Jerusalem that runs it.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs says that more than 50,000 pregnant women and newborn babies in Gaza do not have access to essential medical care.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The UN Palestine agency says that its shelters in Gaza are no longer safe and also warns that there is a shortage of water in Gaza.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October-November 2023 Jenin incursion
text: Israeli forces storm Jenin in the West Bank.
Palestine's United Nations envoy says that Palestinians are in danger of mass ethnic cleansing.
Amnesty International says that they have verified images of Israeli forces near Sderot using white phosphorus-based rounds.
Al-Dura pediatric hospital is evacuated after being hit with white phosphorus munitions from Israeli airstrikes.
At least 15 hospitals are damaged by Israeli shelling and airstrikes, with two currently inoperable. 28 medical staff are killed and 23 ambulances are damaged or destroyed by Israeli airstrikes.
At least 2,268 Palestinians have been killed and 8,700 others injured in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. At least 1,300 Israelis have been killed and at least 3,400 others are injured.

The Israel Defense Forces announce that airstrikes in the Gaza Strip have killed Murad Abu Murad, the head of Hamas's air operations and Ali Qadhi, a top Hamas commander, both of whom were involved in the 7 October invasion of Israel.

context: Islamic terrorism in Europe > Arras school stabbing
text: France raises its Vigipirate to the highest level and announces the deployment of 7,000 soldiers through Opération Sentinelle following a fatal stabbing incident at a school in Arras, Hauts-de-France, which President Emmanuel Macron describes as "Islamist terror".
More than 5,000 demonstrators march in support of Palestine to the White House in Washington, DC,.
Thousands of demonstrators march in support of Palestine in San Francisco.
Armenian President Vahagn Khachaturyan formally approves the country joining the International Criminal Court.
A majority of voters in Australia vote to reject the establishment of an Indigenous Voice to Parliament.

Prime Minister Chris Hipkins concedes defeat to the New Zealand National Party which has won the most seats, although not a majority. Opposition Leader Christopher Luxon is expected to form a coalition government with ACT New Zealand.

UNITA, Angola's main opposition party, exits a special parliamentary session in objection to the proposed public voting method for President João Lourenço's impeachment motion, which is subsequently dismissed.
An annular solar eclipse is visible in the Western Hemisphere.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)
text: One civilian is killed and three others are injured in a cross-border attack by Hezbollah in Shtula, Northern Israel. Israel retaliates with airstrikes on Hezbollah positions in Lebanon.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)
text: United Nations peacekeeping force UNIFIL says its headquarters in Naqoura, Lebanon, has been hit by a rocket.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: An estimated one million Gazans have been displaced, according to the United Nations Palestinian agency, as aid groups describe the situation in the besieged enclave as "catastrophic".

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The Palestinian Ministry of Health says that about 70 percent of people in Gaza do not have access to health services, although the World Health Organization has been able to deliver medical supplies for 2,000 patients. The ministry also says that at least 50 families in the Gaza Strip have had all of their family members killed by Israeli shelling and air strikes.
Human Rights Watch confirms that Israel has used white phosphorus in Gaza and Lebanon.
Israel conducts military operations in Ramallah in the West Bank, arresting more than 50 people.
The Israel Defense Forces kill senior Hamas commander Billal Al Kedra in an airstrike in Khan Yunis.

A man kills a 6-year-old Palestinian Muslim boy and seriously injures his mother during a stabbing attack in Plainfield Township, Illinois, United States. The perpetrator, who was the victims' landlord, states he was motivated by the ongoing Israel–Gaza war.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian attacks across Ukraine over a 24-hour period kill at least six people, including two civilians in Kherson, which was bombarded with over 100 shells by Russian forces. In a separate incident, a 14-year-old boy is killed by a land mine in Mykolaiv Oblast.

Another magnitude 6.3 earthquake strikes Herat Province, Afghanistan, killing four people and injuring more than 150 others, several days after a series of powerful earthquakes killed over 1,000 people in the province.
At least 47 people are killed and dozens more are missing after a boat capsizes in Province of Équateur, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The Taliban government confirms that it will attend the Belt and Road Initiative forum in Beijing, China, next week, as the countries form closer economic ties, including the potential construction of a large copper mine in Logar Province, Afghanistan.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The heads of the Arab League and the African Union release a joint statement stating that Israel's planned ground invasion of Gaza "could lead to a genocide of unprecedented proportions".

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi says that Israel's reaction to Hamas's attack "went beyond self-defence and amounted to collective punishment".
Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro announces the provision of 30 tonnes of humanitarian aid to Gaza.
Thousands of people attend rallies in support of Palestine in several Australian cities.
In the United Kingdom, rallies take place in Manchester in Northern England, Edinburgh and Glasgow in Scotland, and London, amid police warnings that support for Hamas could result in arrest.
Protesters in Amsterdam call on the EU to take a stand against Israel's bombardment of Gaza, condemning European leaders for their silence on the violence Israel is committing in Gaza.
Thousands of people attend rallies in support of Palestine in Istanbul, Turkey.

Lawyers and human rights organisations in Israel receive dozens of complaints from Palestinian workers and students who have been suspended from schools, universities and workplaces over social media posts or conversations with colleagues.

A man is killed and other is wounded in stabbing attacks in Hartlepool, County Durham, England. The attacks are being investigated by Counter Terrorism Policing. Police arrest a Moroccan asylum seeker nearby.
Ecuadorians vote in the second round of the presidential election between Luisa González and Daniel Noboa.
The National Electoral Council declares Noboa as president-elect with González conceding defeat. Noboa is Ecuador's youngest president-elect.
Poles elect members of the Senate and the Sejm. Votes are also cast in a referendum on migration, the removal of the border wall between Belarus and Poland, and the retirement age.

Exit polls suggest that Poland's opposition parties, led by the Civic Coalition under former prime minister Donald Tusk, are poised to secure a parliamentary majority, potentially ending the eight-year governance of the Law and Justice (PiS) party. The exit poll voter turnout reaches a record of 73%.

context: Islamic terrorism in Europe > 2023 Brussels shooting
text: Two Swedish nationals are killed and another is injured during a shooting in Brussels, Belgium. The perpetrator, Tunisian Abdesalem Lassoued, an Islamic State sympathizer, flees the scene.

context: Islamist insurgency in the Sahel > Mali War
text: The United Nations peacekeeping mission in Mali, MINUSMA, initiates a withdrawal from two camps in Aguelhok and Tessalit, Kidal Region.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Gaza war
text: The World Health Organization says that 21 hospitals in Gaza have been ordered to evacuate by Israel, warning that this "may amount to a violation of international humanitarian law".

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Gaza war
text: Israel begins evacuating 28 communities located within two kilometers of the border with Lebanon amid clashes with Hezbollah.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Evacuations during the Gaza war
text: Hundreds of Americans are evacuated by sea from Haifa, Israel, to Cyprus.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Journalists killed in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Muhammad al-Najjar, a member of the Board of Directors of the national authority for the documentation and prosecution of crimes committed by the Israeli government, is killed in an Israeli airstrike, along with 16 members of his family.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Journalists killed in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Eleven Palestinian journalists have been killed by the Israeli military and more than 20 others have been injured, according to the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis
text: Hamas releases the first video of a hostage on Telegram since the war started, a 21-year-old Israeli woman from Shoham who was kidnapped during the Re'im music festival massacre. In the video, the woman claims to be receiving medical treatment from her captors.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The World Health Organization announces that there are only 24 hours of water, electricity, and fuel remaining in Gaza.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Medical Aid for Palestinians says that hospitals in Gaza are currently facing a "catastrophic" shortage of medical supplies with the United Nations also reporting that at least four hospitals in northern Gaza are no longer operational because of Israeli bombings.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The chief of the UN agency for Palestine, UNRWA, announces it can no longer deliver assistance to the hundreds of thousands of people in need in Gaza.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Sameh Shoukry, Egypt's Minister of Foreign Affairs, announces that US-backed efforts to re-open the Rafah border crossing have failed, citing Israel's refusal to guarantee the safety of incoming aid convoys and outgoing foreign nationals.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The United Nations reports that more than 400,000 Palestinians are sheltering in UN schools and buildings in the Gaza Strip and that fourteen UNRWA personnel have been killed in Israeli airstrikes.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Palestinians protest in several cities across the West Bank calling for an end to Israeli attacks on Gaza.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The UNRWA retracts its statements concerning looting by Hamas affiliates, clarifying that they have confirmed no theft had taken place, after a prior announcement that men claiming to be from Hamas stole fuel and medicine from their offices in Gaza. Subsequently, Israeli journalist Barak Ravid claims to have received additional confirmation from sources within the United Nations that such theft did, in fact, occur.

At least six civilians are killed and eight others are injured in airstrikes near Khan Younis and at least seven people, including five emergency workers, are killed in Israeli airstrikes on two civil defense facilities in Gaza City.
At least four people, including three children, are killed as a result of an Israeli airstrike on the UN Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza.
Hamas forces launch missiles at the two largest Israeli cities, Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, saying that this was in response to Israel's "targeting of civilians".

Israeli military forces carry out raids in multiple areas in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, Nablus, Bethlehem, and Hebron, arresting around 600 people. Most are held without charges under "administrative detention", where the individuals are not told the reasons for their arrest.
Hamas Shura Council member Osama Mazini, who was in charge of negotiation affairs concerning the captured Israeli soldier Gilad Shalit, is killed in an airstrike in the Gaza Strip.

A report by a UN-mandated investigative body has found that Israeli forces used "lethal force without justification" when they shot and killed Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh in the West Bank last year.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Nine Lebanese civilians injured by IDF fired white phosphorus munitions on Dhayra.

context: China–Philippines relations > Territorial disputes in the South China Sea
text: The Philippine military demands that China stop "dangerous and offensive" actions in the South China Sea after a People's Liberation Army Navy ship performed "aggressive maneuvers" near the disputed Thitu Island last week.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > Colombia–Israel relations
text: Colombia requests the departure of the Israeli ambassador following Colombian President Gustavo Petro's remarks criticizing Israel's actions. In response, Israel suspends security exports to Colombia.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Pakistan relations
text: Pakistani Foreign Minister Jalil Abbas Jilani condemns the Israeli bombing on Gaza, equating the actions with genocide.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > Israel–United States relations
text: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken visits Israel and reaffirms American support for Israel.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Arab League Secretary-General Ahmed Aboul Gheit calls for an immediate end to military operations in Gaza and for aid to be allowed into the enclave.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The China International Development Cooperation Agency announces that they will provide emergency humanitarian aid to the UN Palestine agency and the Palestinian Authority.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Around 25,000 people demonstrate in Cotabato, Philippines, to express solidarity with Palestinians and to condemn Israel's air raids on the Gaza Strip.
Russia suspends imports of Japanese seafood due to concerns over wastewater discharges from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Plant.
Former Bank of China chair Liu Lian'ge is arrested on allegations of corruption.
Around 49 anti-war protesters calling for U.S. President Joe Biden to press for a ceasefire are arrested outside the White House by U.S. Secret Service members.
Australia's internet safety commissioner fines American technology company X Corp. for AU$610,500 (US$385,000) for inadequately addressing child sexual abuse content on Twitter.

The Constitutional Court of Indonesia rules that regional leaders under the age of 40 can run for president or vice president, thus allowing President Joko Widodo's son Gibran Rakabuming Raka to run as a Vice Presidential candidate in the next presidential election.
The Italian Olympic Committee announces that bobsleigh, luge, and skeleton events will not be held in Italy due to the high costs of rebuilding the Eugenio Monti Olympic Track in Cortina d'Ampezzo.
The International Olympic Committee approves the inclusion of cricket, flag football, lacrosse, squash, and baseball/softball at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.
Police in Brussels, Belgium, shoot and kill the Islamic State sympathizer who killed two Swedish tourists yesterday.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion
text: At least 471 people are killed and 314 others are injured by an explosion at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza City, according to the Hamas-run Gaza Ministry of Health, saying it was caused by a Israeli airstrike. The casualties are transported to Gaza City’s main hospital, al-Shifa.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion
text: The Israel Defense Forces claims to have evidence that the explosion was caused by a Palestinian Islamic Jihad rocket failure. A spokesman for Islamic Jihad calls the Israeli statement "a lie and fabrication."

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion
text: Palestine’s Permanent Observer Mission to the United Nations sends a statement to media organisations challenging the veracity of comments from Israel after the explosion.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion
text: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation releases a statement denouncing Israel for the hospital explosion and the international community for its “impunity” in the war in Gaza.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion
text: U.S. President Joe Biden postpones an upcoming visit to Jordan following the explosion.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip, Gaza Strip evacuations
text: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights says that Israel's blockade of Gaza and its evacuation order in northern Gaza may amount to a forcible transfer of civilians, which is a violation of international law.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October 2023 UNRWA school airstrike
text: An Israeli airstrike hits a United Nations school inside a refugee camp in Gaza, killing at least six of the more than 4,000 people sheltering there. Dozens more are injured, including UNRWA staff.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October 2023 UNRWA school airstrike
text: The Israeli Ministry of Health says that 4,399 people in Israel have been injured since the start of the war.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October 2023 UNRWA school airstrike
text: The World Health Organization says that 2,800 people have died and 11,000 have been injured in Gaza since Israeli air strikes began, with about half of those being women and children.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October 2023 UNRWA school airstrike
text: The World Health Organization says that there have been 51 attacks against healthcare facilities in Gaza, killing 15 health workers and injuring 27 others, and that "we have seen consistent attacks on healthcare in the occupied Palestinian territory."

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > October 2023 UNRWA school airstrike
text: Hamas announces that Ayman Nofal, a member of the general military council and commander of the central command in the Al-Qassam Brigades, was killed in an Israeli airstrike.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Five Hezbollah fighters are killed by Israeli soldiers when trying to cross a barrier at the border with Lebanon.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Lebanese state media reports that villages Dhayra and others were "continuous(ly)" bombarded by the IDF overnight, allegedly using White phosphorus munitions. In the early morning it was reported that multiple people were suffering from symptoms of suffocation after the IDF allegedly fired white phosphorus shells on the village.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza-Israel conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Three people injured from a Hezbollah missile strike on the Metula, northern Israel.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive
text: Ukraine launches ATACMS tactical ballistic missiles at Russian bases in Berdiansk and Luhansk, saying that they destroyed nine helicopters and a supply depot and killed several Russian military personnel.
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold talks at the Belt and Road Initiative forum in Beijing, China.

context: Russia and weapons of mass destruction
text: The State Duma votes unanimously to revoke Russia's ratification of the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty.
The Supreme Court of India refuses to legalize same-sex marriage, saying that this is a decision that needs to be made by parliament.

The Diocese of Joliet, Illinois, confirms that Joseph Czuba, the man charged with killing a 6-year-old Palestinian Muslim Wadea al-Fayoume and injuring the boy's mother, is a member of a local Catholic Church parish.

context: October 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
text: The Republican majority fails to deliver enough votes for Jim Jordan to become House Speaker on the first vote, with 20 members of the Republican party voting against him.
Allied Democratic Forces gunmen shoot and kill a British and South African honeymoon couple and their local tour guide at the Queen Elizabeth National Park in Western Uganda.

context: Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present) > Evacuations during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Saudi Arabia tells its citizens to immediately leave Lebanon due to the deteriorating security situation in the south of the country.

context: Gaza-Israel conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The United States vetoes a United Nations Security Council resolution that would have condemned violence against civilians while urging humanitarian aid to Palestinians in Gaza. Twelve countries vote in favour of the resolution, while Russia and the United Kingdom abstain.
