context: China–Philippines relations, Territorial disputes in the South China Sea
text: The Philippines says that it will respond to any Chinese attempts to interfere with its resupply of troops in the South China Sea.

The National Defense Ministry of Taiwan says that more than 30 Chinese PLA Air Force warplanes have entered Taiwanese airspace and that at least nine PLA Navy warships have been detected around Taiwan. The ROC Armed Forces are deployed in response to the violation.
Uganda's Constitutional Court upholds the Anti-Homosexuality Act, 2023, which prescribes the death penalty for certain homosexual acts.
Businesswoman Sam Mostyn is appointed as the next Governor General of Australia and will succeed David Hurley on 1 July.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: Russia launches multiple Shahed drone strikes on Kharkiv, Ukraine, killing at least five people, including three rescue workers, and injuring five others.

Russian appointed officials claim that Ukrainian shelling has killed two civilians and injured nine others in Donetsk. Separately, four people are killed in drone attacks in Russian-occupied Kherson Oblast.
U.S Secretary of State Antony Blinken says that Ukraine will eventually become a NATO member.
Two West Papua National Liberation Army leaders, including Abubakar Tabuni, are killed during a shootout with the Indonesian Army near the Grasberg mine in Mimika Regency, Central Papua.

Eleven security forces, including five Revolutionary Guards, are killed in Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran, during an attack against the Revolutionary Guards' headquarters by members of Jaish ul-Adl. Sixteen militants are killed in the ensuing shootout.

Former Al-Nusra Front emir Abu Maria al-Qahtani is assassinated in a suicide bombing in Sarmada, Idlib Governorate, Syria. The Islamic State are accused of being behind the attack, which also injured several others at his house.
99 Cents Only Stores announces an orderly wind-down, closing all of its 371 stores in the United States beginning April 5.
Shipping lanes and airspace in the Great Belt strait in Denmark are closed for several hours after a missile launcher malfunctions on the frigate .
Fourteen people are killed in a collision between a bus and a truck in Bolivia.
Five foreigners are killed when a fire breaks out in an apartment building in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.
Scientists from the Federation University Australia report that thousands of Adélie penguins have been found dead in Antarctica amid an increase in bird flu cases among wild bird populations.
Bird flu spreads to cattle herds in at least six U.S. states, while a dairy farm worker is infected in Texas, becoming the second person to ever become infected with the virus in the United States.
Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula, the Speaker of the National Assembly of South Africa, is arrested and charged with corruption one day after resigning from office.
A man stabs the Governor of Murmansk Oblast Andrey Chibis at a meeting in Apatity, Murmansk Oblast, Russia. The attacker is arrested by police.
Myriam Spiteri Debono is sworn in as President of Malta, succeeding George Vella and becoming the third woman to hold the office.

Researchers at the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument in Arizona, United States, release the largest 3D map of the universe featuring more than six million galaxies. Using this map, researchers are able to measure the acceleration of the expansion rate of the universe with unprecedented accuracy, detecting hints that the rate of expansion has been increasing over time.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Doctors Without Borders office in Pokrovsk is completely destroyed by a Russian missile strike. Five civilians are injured in the attack.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine's SBU claims to have destroyed six Russian military aircraft and heavily damaged eight others in a drone attack on Morozovsk Air Base in Rostov Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zaporizhzhia strikes
text: At least three people are killed and at least 13 others are injured in a Russian double-tap missile strike in Zaporizhzhia.
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe launches a new currency, Zimbabwe Gold, backed on gold reserves and foreign currencies amid depreciation of its current currency, the Zimbabwean dollar.
A magnitude 4.8 earthquake strikes northwestern New Jersey, causing tremors throughout the East Coast of the United States.

context: Ecuador–Mexico relations > 2024 raid on the Mexican embassy in Ecuador
text: After local police arrest former vice-president Jorge Glas at its embassy in Quito in violation of [https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Vienna_Convention_on_Diplomatic_Relations#Article_22 Article 22] of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, Mexico suspends diplomatic relations with Ecuador.

Armenia and the European Union agree on a landmark deal to support the Armenian economy over the next four years following high-level talks in Brussels. The €270m support package is designed to help Armenia become less dependent on Russia.
President Alexander Lukashenko announces that Belarus will suspend its participation in the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe.
The Venezuelan government announces that it will give safe passage to Argentina to six aides of opposition leader María Corina Machado who are taking refuge in the Argentine embassy in Caracas.
Prime Minister Katrín Jakobsdóttir resigns and announces that she is standing as a candidate for the presidential election on 1 June.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv kills eight civilians and injures ten others. At least nine high-rise buildings and a petrol station are badly damaged.
Eight children are killed and two more injured by a roadside bomb in Daraa Governorate, Syria.
The Karen National Union captures the town of Myawaddy in Kayin State as hundreds of junta troops surrender and hand over their weapons to rebel forces.

context: 2024 Central Asian floods > Orsk Dam collapse
text: Around 2,500 houses are flooded and at least four people are killed after the Orsk dam in Orenburg, Russia, bursts due to maintenance errors following heavy rainfall. Around 47,000 people in Russia and Kazakhstan are evacuated. Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev calls it one of the "worst natural disasters in the past 80 years".

context: 2024 raid on the Mexican embassy in Ecuador
text: Nicaragua suspends diplomatic relations with Ecuador following the raid on the Mexican embassy in Quito, Ecuador.

context: Mass shootings in the United States > 2024 Doral shooting
text: Two people, including the perpetrator, are killed and seven others are injured in a mass shooting at a bar in Doral, Florida, United States.
Slovaks vote in the second round of the presidential election between Ivan Korčok and Peter Pellegrini. Peter Pellegrini wins with over 53% of the vote.
In association football, Athletic Bilbao win their first major trophy in 40 years after defeating Mallorca in the Copa del Rey final.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Siege of Khan Yunis
text: Israel withdraws all ground forces from the southern Gaza Strip, including Khan Yunis, leaving just one IDF brigade, the 933rd Nahal Brigade, remaining in the enclave.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis
text: The IAEA reports that the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's Unit 6 was targeted by a drone strike, although nuclear safety has not been compromised, according to the statement.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: A Rapid Support Forces attack kills 28 civilians and injures 240 more in the outskirts of Khartoum, Sudan.
A ferry travelling from Lunga in Mossuril District to the Island of Mozambique sinks off the coast of Nampula Province, Mozambique, killing at least 94 people and leaving 26 others missing.
Polish opposition party Law and Justice comes first in local elections while the ruling coalition retains a majority of the votes.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Battle of Chasiv Yar
text: Heavy fighting between Russian and Ukrainian troops occurs around the city of Chasiv Yar, with Ukraine describing the situation as "difficult" and "tense".
Shelling kills three civilians in Huliaipole, Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
Ukraine claims to have damaged the Russian Navy missile ship in the Baltic Sea near Kaliningrad.

context: Sudanese civil war > Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war
text: Khartoum reports 384 cases of dengue fever which are attributed to the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Sudan.
Over 100 civilians in South Kordofan are killed after allies of the Rapid Support Forces launch attacks in villages across the state.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip, Rafah offensive
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he has ordered an invasion of Rafah in the southern Gaza Strip with a date "being set" for the ground offensive.
Hezbollah shoots down an Israeli Hermes 900 drone, for the first time in the conflict.

Protesters set fire to government buildings and dozens of vehicles in the Mexican state of Guerrero amid anger over the police killing of a college student in March and the kidnapping of 43 students in 2014. Governor Evelyn Salgado Pineda's office in Chilpancingo is ransacked.
A total solar eclipse occurs in North America for the first time since 2017. It is the last total solar eclipse to be visible in the contiguous United States until 2044.

context: 2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament
text: In college basketball, Connecticut repeats as national champions, becoming the first program to do so since the Florida Gators did so in 2006 and 2007.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The largest humanitarian aid airdrop since the war began takes place over the northern Gaza Strip, with at least 14 aircraft from nine nations taking part in the operation.
Six police officers are killed and two more injured during an ambush by Jaish ul-Adl gunmen in Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran.
Heavy fighting and clashes occur between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in areas controlled by the RSF primarily near Wad Madani in Gezira State.

context: Economic impact of the Israel–Hamas war, Israel–Turkey relations
text: The Turkish Trade Ministry announces that it will suspend the export of 54 categories of goods to Israel in response to Israel banning Turkey from participating in humanitarian air drops over the Gaza Strip.

A Federation University Australia expedition confirms that bird flu is currently spreading across Antarctica, with outbreaks confirmed in wild bird populations in Beak Island, Hope Bay, Devil Island, and Paulet Island.
Three people are killed, five are injured and four are missing in an explosion at a power plant on Lake Suviana, near Bologna, Italy.
The death toll from Sunday's ferry sinking in Mozambique increases to more than 100 people, with around 20 people still missing.
More than 100,000 people in Russia and Kazakhstan are ordered to evacuate amid catastrophic flooding along the Ural river.

The United Nations' International Organization for Migration reports that 38 people died when a boat, which has carried around 66 Ethiopian migrants, has sank off Godoria, Djibouti, a day before while on its way to Yemen. At least six more are still missing and presumed dead.
sources: AFP via South China Morning Post

text: The Arizona Supreme Court upholds a law criminalizing most types of abortions in the case Planned Parenthood Arizona v. Mayes.
Icelandic Minister of Foreign Affairs Bjarni Benediktsson is appointed Prime Minister after Katrín Jakobsdóttir's resignation on 5 April.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: Russian airstrikes in Kharkiv Oblast kill at least three people and injure four others.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Odesa strikes
text: Four people are killed and seven others are injured in a Russian missile strike in Odesa.
An Israeli attack in Gaza kills three civilians related to Ismail Haniyeh.
American video game company Epic Games announces that it will lay-off around 870 employees, roughly one-sixth of its workforce, due to slower growth than expected.
A bus carrying Eid Al-Fitr pilgrims collides and plunges into a ditch in Balochistan, Pakistan, killing seventeen people and injuring 16 others.
Five people are killed and 35 others are injured in a fire at the New Lucky House in Kowloon, Hong Kong.
A person is killed by flooding in Mississippi, United States, as severe weather hits the Southern United States.

South Koreans vote for members of the National Assembly. The opposition, primarily consisting of the Democratic Party, its alliance and the Rebuilding Korea Party, wins the election in a landslide, increasing their legislative majority but falling short of the two-thirds supermajority needed to pass constitutional amendments or override the veto of President Yoon Suk Yeol.
Cornel West names Melina Abdullah as his VP pick as part of his presidential campaign.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Mykolaiv strikes
text: At least four people are killed and five others are injured in a Russian missile strike in Mykolaiv.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, damaging power facilities and causing widespread power outages for about 200,000 people. Ukraine says that the Trypilska thermal power plant in Kyiv Oblast was destroyed in an overnight attack.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: Russia warns its citizens against travelling to the Middle East amid increasing tensions between Iran and Israel.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: U.S. President Joe Biden warns that Iran is threatening to launch a significant attack against Israel and promises "ironclad U.S. support" for Israel in the event of an attack.

The Karen National Union, local PDF groups, and other Karenni organizations seize the town of Myawaddy, Kayin State, from the Tatmadaw after three days of fighting. Junta planes subsequently bomb the town, causing more than 1,000 locals to flee into neighbouring Thailand.
Archaeologists announce the discovery of new frescos at the ancient Roman city of Pompeii, depicting mythological ancient Greek figures.

A search operation at a power plant on Lake Suviana, near Bologna, Italy, has recovered the bodies of three workers who were missing after an explosion two days ago. This brings the confirmed death toll to six. A seventh worker is still missing, while the five injured are still in critical conditions.
A Robinson R22 helicopter owned by the Philippine Air Force crashes near a public market in Cavite City, Philippines, killing both pilots.
A court in Vietnam sentences tycoon Trương Mỹ Lan to death for embezzling $12.46 billion from the Sai Gon Joint Stock Commercial Bank.
Thirty-eight prisoners escape from a prison in Moroni, Comoros.
South Korean prime minister Han Duck-soo and all senior advisers to President Yoon Suk Yeol resign en masse in response to the results of yesterday's parliamentary elections.
The Netherlands increases its military budget to 2 percent of its GDP for the first time since 1994.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches drone strikes across Ukraine. Critical infrastructure is damaged in Kherson Oblast and a fire occurs at the Dnieper Hydroelectric Station in Zaporizhzhia causing around half a tonne of oil products to leak into the Dnieper river.

context: Sudanese civil war > Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war
text: Canada pledges $132.2 million dollars to Sudan to help people affected by the country's ongoing humanitarian crisis.

context: Alliance of Sahel States > Nigerien crisis
text: Dozens of Russian military instructors arrive in Niger as part of an agreement with the ruling military junta to a install state-of-the-art air defence system.
Hezbollah forces launch dozens of rockets into northern Israel. The militant group says that the missile barrage targeted IDF artillery positions. No casualties are reported.
Two Fano militants are killed and a third is arrested during a shootout with police near the Millennium Hall in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. A civilian is also killed and two officers are wounded.

context: Economic impact of the Israel–Hamas war, Egypt–European Union relations
text: The European Union pledges €1 billion in short-term financial aid to Egypt to help stabilise the country's economy.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: It is reported that Israel is preparing for a direct retaliatory strike from Iran on southern or northern Israel as soon as the next 24 to 48 hours. A person briefed by the Iranian leadership says that while plans to strike are being discussed, no final decision has been made.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: The United States restricts travel for its embassy personnel in Israel amid fears of a retaliation by Iran.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: The British government advises against all travel to Israel and the Palestinian territories due to the imminent possibility of an Iranian strike.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: France advises its citizens against traveling to Iran, Lebanon, Israel Palestine due to the risk of military escalation.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: Germany tells its citizens to leave Iran immediately, saying that "air, land and sea transport routes" will likely be affected by military action in the region.
The military junta in Mali prohibits all forms of media from reporting on activities of political parties and associations.
Pakistan designates the Iranian Quds Force Liwa Zainebiyoun as a terrorist organization.
Russia successfully test-launches an intercontinental ballistic missile from the Kapustin Yar launch complex in Astrakhan Oblast.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > 2024 Iranian strikes in Israel
text: Iran and its proxies launch between 400 and 500 drones and cruise missiles at Israel from Iran, Iraq, Syria, southern Lebanon, and Yemen.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > 2024 Iranian strikes in Israel
text: U.S. naval ships mobilize to the Middle East to protect Israel against incoming missiles.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > Iranian seizure of the MSC Aries
text: Iran seizes the MSC Aries, a Portuguese-registered, Madeira-flagged container ship owned by Zodiac Maritime which is chaired by Israeli billionaire Eyal Ofer.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > Israeli bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus
text: The Netherlands announces that their embassy in Tehran will close on Sunday.
Israeli settlers attack Palestinians in the West Bank after missing Jewish teenager Benjamin Achimeir is found dead.
Gunmen abduct and kill nine people from a bus in Nushki District, Balochistan, Pakistan. All victims, whose bodies were found under a bridge, appear to have been shot at close range.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Russian Ministry of Defense claims that the village of Pervomaiske near Donetsk has been captured by Russian troops.
An offensive by the Rapid Support Forces begins in El Fasher in the Sudanese state of North Darfur.
Eighteen people are killed, two are injured and some are missing after landslides hit South Sulawesi, Indonesia.
Six people are killed and seven others are injured in a mass stabbing at a shopping center in Sydney, Australia. The perpetrator is shot and killed by police.
Simon Kennedy of the Liberal Party of Australia wins the by-election in the seat of Cook, succeeding former Prime Minister Scott Morrison.
At least 15 people are killed and 60 more are missing during a landslide in Idiofa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Heavy floods in Afghanistan have killed at least 33 people and injured 27 others in three days. About 600 houses were either damaged or destroyed, and around 200 livestock died. The floods also damaged around 800 hectares of agricultural land, and more than 85 kilometers (53 miles) of roads.
Cyprus suspends Syrian asylum applications as there are increasing numbers of refugees.
Three people are injured, one critically, in a shooting at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia. The perpetrator targeted his wife, who was not injured.
In association football, Bayer 04 Leverkusen win their first Bundesliga title.
American professional golfer Scottie Scheffler wins the Masters Tournament at the Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Georgia. This win is Scheffler's second win at the tournament.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict > 2024 Iranian strikes in Israel, Iran–Japan relations
text: Japan increases its four-stage danger ranking level for most of Iran, including Tehran, to Level 3, which urges Japanese citizens to avoid all travel to Iran.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher
text: At least nine civilians are killed and sixty others are injured in a renewed offensive by the Rapid Support Forces on the city of El Fasher.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher
text: The Rapid Support Forces capture Mellit, North Darfur.

context: Sudanese civil war > Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war
text: Donors pledge more than 2 billion euros for humanitarian aid in Sudan.

context: Sudanese civil war > Siege of El Obeid
text: Five civilians are killed and ten others are injured in crossfire between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces in the city of El Obeid.
The Joint Darfur Force declares war on the Rapid Support Forces and allies with the Sudanese Armed Forces.
Clashes occur in Al-Madina Arab, Gezira State, between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk announces that more than 10% of the company's global workforce will be laid off.
Lockheed Martin wins a $17 billion defense contract from the U.S. government to develop anti-ballistic missiles.

Fifty-eight people have been killed in Tanzania and 13 people have been killed in Kenya in the past two weeks by flooding caused by torrential rains, with more than 125,000 people in coastal areas of East Africa affected by the flooding. Tanzania announces plans to construct fourteen dams in an attempt to reduce the damage from future floods.
Lightning and heavy rains have killed at least 49 people across Pakistan in the past three days, mainly farmers in the eastern Punjab province.
The death toll from landslides caused by torrential rain in Tana Toraja, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, increases to 20, after the last missing people are found dead.
A magnitude 6.5 earthquake strikes West New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea. No damage or casualties are reported.

context: Sudan–United Kingdom relations, Sudanese civil war
text: The United Kingdom sanctions Alkhaleej Bank and Al-Fakher Advanced Works, two companies financing the Rapid Support Forces, and Red Rock Mining, which finances the Sudanese Armed Forces.

context: 2021 Australian Parliament House sexual misconduct allegations
text: Former Australian political staffer Bruce Lehrmann loses his defamation case against Network 10 and journalist Lisa Wilkinson for broadcasting an interview with Lehrmann's former coworker Brittany Higgins in which she claimed that Lehrmann raped her.

Four people are injured, including bishop Mar Mari Emmanuel, in a mass stabbing at a church in Sydney, Australia. The perpetrator is arrested. A mob clashes with police outside the church while trying to attack the detained suspect.

context: Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse
text: A federal court in the U.S. state of Virginia hears the first claims by survivors of the Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq. Three detainees accuse the CACI for their role in the torture at the prison.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > Tax Day protests
text: Pro-Palestinian protests in the United States stop traffic on the Golden Gate Bridge and disrupt traffic to Seattle–Tacoma International Airport.
Lee Hsien Loong announces that he will resign as Prime Minister of Singapore on May 15 and will be succeeded by Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lawrence Wong.

Thousands of people protest against a controversial foreign agent law in Tbilisi, Georgia. Georgia's Interior Ministry reports at least 14 people have been detained. Georgian Dream parliamentary leader Mamuka Mdinaradze is punched during a debate in parliament by a member of the opposition.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Ismail Yusuf Baz, commander of Hezbollah's coastal sector is assassinated with one civilian killed in Ain Ebel, Lebanon, in an Israeli airstrike.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Fourteen Israeli soldiers and four civilians were wounded in drone attacks in northern Israel. One IDF officer later succumbs. > Al-Maghazi refugee camp airstrikes
text: At least 13 people are killed in a strike on a refugee camp in the Gaza Strip.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > April 2024 Israeli settler rampages
text: A mob of Israeli settlers in Aqraba kills two Palestinians in revenge for the killing of Israeli teenager Benjamin Achimeir amid escalating ethnoreligious violence in the West Bank.
Australian police say that the stabbing attack at an Assyrian church in Sydney was an Islamic terrorist act.
Indian security forces kill at least 29 Maoist insurgents in a major counterinsurgency operation in Kanker district, Chhattisgarh. A large quantity of weapons are also seized.
Russian peacekeepers begin withdrawing from Nagorno-Karabakh, leaving the region under the full control of Azerbaijan.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signs a new army draft law.
American video game company Take-Two Interactive lays off 5% of its workforce.
Argentina and Denmark sign a 2.1 billion kroner (US$300 million) deal for the sale of 24 Royal Danish Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons to Argentina.
Heavy rains and flash floods affect parts of the Persian Gulf, killing at least 18 people in Oman and causing travel disruptions in the United Arab Emirates.
At least six people are killed and three others are reported missing after a boat capsizes along the Jhelum River in Srinagar, India.

A fire occurs in Copenhagen's 17th-century Stock Exchange Building, leading to the collapse of the building's iconic Dragespir spire. Important Danish artworks including From Copenhagen Stock Exchange are safely removed from the building.
The U.S. House of Representatives sends impeachment articles for Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas to the Senate.
Police in Brussels, Belgium, shut down the right-wing National Conservatism Conference which was expected to be hosted by Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.
European Space Agency scientists announce the discovery of Gaia BH3, the second-largest known black hole in the Milky Way.
World Athletics announces that they will investigate the results of Sunday's Beijing half marathon to determine if Chinese marathon record holder He Jie won because of match fixing.
18 people are killed and 78 others are injured in a Russian missile strike which damaged an eight-storey building in a densely populated area of Chernihiv.
Fourteen Israeli soldiers and four civilians injured in drone attacks in northern Israel. One IDF officer later succumbs.
Taqaddum leader and former Prime Minister of Sudan Abdalla Hamdok meets with French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris, France.
Vietnam announces a $24 billion rescue for the Sai Gon Joint Stock Commercial Bank, which is currently involved in a fraud case.
The United Arab Emirates records its heaviest rainfall in 75 years, with significant flooding reported in Dubai. At least 20 people are killed by flooding in Oman and Ras Al Khaimah.
Hundreds of people are evacuated after the Ruang volcano erupts in North Sulawesi, Indonesia.
The Biden administration announces that it will reimpose oil sanctions on Venezuela.
Switzerland's Federal Assembly votes to ban public displays of the Nazi swastika.
Voters in Croatia elect the members of the Sabor. The ruling Croatian Democratic Union and its coalition win the most seats, but fail to obtain a majority.
Voters in Solomon Islands elect a new National Parliament.
The United States Senate votes to dismiss both impeachment articles against Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas, by a vote of 51–48 on the first article and 51–49 on the second.
Scientists announce that they have identified fossil remains of the Ichthyotitan, the largest marine reptile currently known, in the Westbury Formation in England.

In basketball, the NBA announces that it has banned Jontay Porter, a two-way player under contract to the Toronto Raptors and their G League affiliate Raptors 905, for multiple major violations of the league's gambling policy.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Germany arrests two German-Russian nationals for an alleged military sabotage plot on behalf of Russia to undermine military support for Ukraine.

A Kenya Air Force Bell UH-1H Huey II crashes in Elgeyo-Marakwet County, Kenya, killing ten people, including Chief of Defence Forces Francis Omondi Ogolla. President William Ruto declares three days of national mourning.

context: Palestine and the United Nations, Enlargement of the United Nations
text: The United States vetoes a UN Security Council resolution supporting the State of Palestine joining the United Nations. The vote was 12 in favor, the United States opposed, and two abstentions, from the United Kingdom and Switzerland.

In ice hockey, the National Hockey League board approves the relocation of the hockey assets of the Arizona Coyotes to Salt Lake City, Utah. The currently unnamed expansion team will play their home games at the Delta Center, while the Coyotes franchise will be deactivated pending the construction of a new arena in the Phoenix metropolitan area.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict > 2024 Israeli strikes on Iran
text: Missiles are launched by the Israel Defense Forces towards Isfahan, Iran. Locations in Iraq and Syria are also attacked by Israel.
The Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade tells its citizens to leave Israel, citing a high threat of military reprisals and terrorist attacks.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russian missile strikes kill seven civilians in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, including five in Synelnykove and two in Dnipro, with several others critically injured.
A Russian Air Force Tupolev Tu-22M3 aircraft is shot down in Russian airspace over Stavropol Krai after launching missiles at targets in Ukraine.

An Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces command post at the Kalsu military base was hit by an explosion resulting from an air strike, killing one fighter and wounding six others. Security sources say it is not known who was responsible, and Israel and the United States both deny involvement.

Taylor Swift releases her new album The Tortured Poets Department as a double album. On Spotify, the album breaks the record for most-streamed album in a single day and Swift becomes the most-streamed artist in a single day.
American car manufacturer Tesla, Inc. recalls thousands of Cybertrucks due to "safety concerns" involving the truck's accelerator pedals.
The United States agrees to withdraw American troops from Niger.
A man fatally sets himself on fire near the New York City courthouse where former President Donald Trump is currently on trial.
Indians begin voting to elect members to the 18th Lok Sabha. There are 969 million people eligible to vote, and voting will continue until June in seven phases.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Israeli attacks in the West Bank during the Israel–Gaza war
text: Fourteen Palestinians are killed in an Israeli attack in the West Bank.
The Governor of Smolensk Oblast, Russia, says that a Ukrainian drone attack caused a fire at a fuel depot in Kardymovsky.
A river boat en route to a funeral capsizes in the Mpoko River in Bangui, Central African Republic, killing at least 58 people.

context: Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, United States support for Israel in the Israel–Hamas war
text: The U.S. House of Representatives passes a series of bills that would provide $95 billion in military aid to countries including Ukraine, Israel, and Taiwan.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > Israel–Hamas war protests in the United States
text: American college students plan demonstrations in solidarity with pro-Palestinian Columbia University protesters arrested in New York City earlier this week.

context: Mass shootings in the United States
text: Two people are killed and six more are injured in a shooting at a block party in Memphis, Tennessee.
Protests occur in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, against mass tourism in the Canary Islands which is allegedly increasing house prices for locals.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Bombing of the Gaza Strip
text: Twenty-two people are killed, including 18 children, in overnight Israeli strikes in Rafah in the Gaza Strip, according to local health officials.
A car veers off the track during the international Fox Hill Supercross motor race in Diyatalawa, Sri Lanka, and crashes into a group of spectators, killing seven people and injuring 21 others.
Nine people are killed after a vehicle collided with another vehicle in Jhalawar District, India.
Ecuadorians vote in a referendum on proposed constitutional changes.
Maldivians elect the members of the parliament.
A referendum on whether to remove ethnic Albanian mayors from office in Serb-majority North Kosovo is boycotted by most Serbs, who demand that the mayors resign.
Basques in Spain elect the members of the Basque Parliament.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian Ministry of Defence claims control over the village of Novomykhailivka in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United Kingdom announces its largest ever military support package for the Ukrainian military, pledging 400 vehicles, including 162 MXT-MVs, 60 boats, 1,600 air defence missiles, 4 million rounds of firearm ammunition, and an additional £500 million in funding.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia strikes the Kharkiv TV Tower with a Kh-59 cruise missile, causing the upper half of the tower to collapse and disrupting the broadcasting signal in Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Siege of Khan Yunis
text: Israeli troops and tanks raid Khan Yunis in Gaza after abruptly withdrawing from the city earlier this month.

context: Islamic State insurgency in the North Caucasus
text: Two police officers are killed and another is injured during a mass shooting of a police squad in Karachay-Cherkessia, Russia.
Twelve Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters militants are killed and seven soldiers are wounded during a shootout in Datu Saudi Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur, Philippines.
Four people are killed and ten are missing during floods caused by heavy rain in Guangdong Province, China. Around 110,000 people are evacuated.

context: China–Japan relations > Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine
text: China objects to an offering that Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida made at Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine on Sunday.

context: Israel–Hamas war > 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel
text: The head of the Military Intelligence Directorate of Israel Aharon Haliva resigns for failing to prevent the Hamas offensive on Israel on October 7, 2023.
President Mohamed Muizzu's party, the People's National Congress, is declared the winner of the election.
Vito Bardi is re-elected president of the Italian region of Basilicata.
A familicide of the Candy family in Yukon, Oklahoma, United States kills five people including the perpetrator, 42-year-old Jonathon David Candy.
NASA announces that it has received decipherable data from the Voyager 1 space probe for the first time in five months.
An Israeli Air Force airstrike kills two people and injures six others in Hanine, Lebanon.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Nasser Hospital mass graves, Nasser Hospital siege
text: United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk calls for an international investigation on Israel after hundreds of bodies are discovered in mass graves near the Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis in Gaza.

A Hezbollah militant, a Redwan Force commando and an air defense engineer killed in Israeli drone strikes in Abu al-Aswad and Tyre, Lebanon. [https://english.news.cn/20240424/16d07a6137c44122b90b4bf3ce829049/c.html [(Xinhua)]
Hezbollah launches drone strikes on two IDF bases in Acre, Israel.[https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/lebanons-hezbollah-launches-deepest-attack-into-israel-since-gaza-war-1.102296772 [(Gulf News)]
The United States Federal Trade Commission votes to ban nearly all employment agreements that prevent workers from joining competing businesses.
Two Royal Malaysian Navy helicopters collide in mid-air during a rehearsal parade in Lumut, Malaysia, killing all ten people on board.
Five migrants drown while attempting to cross the English Channel and 49 others are rescued.
At least 21 migrants die after their boat capsizes off the coast of Djibouti.
A Douglas DC-4 crashes into the Tanana River in Alaska, United States, shortly after takeoff from Fairbanks, killing two people on board.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine, International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Jamaica becomes the 140th UN member state to recognize the State of Palestine.

context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
text: North Korea claims that it tested a new command-and-control system in a simulated nuclear counterstrike.
Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Rishi Sunak announces that he plans to increase the United Kingdom's defence budget to 2.5% of its GDP by 2030, totaling around £85 billion.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States announces a $61 billion aid package for Ukraine as part of a bill that was recently approved after being stalled in the US Congress for months. The package includes ammunition for artillery and air defense systems, along with armoured fighting vehicles.
The union representing air traffic controllers in France cancels a planned 24-hour strike on Thursday, although a majority of flights have already been cancelled.
Widespread flooding occurs in Nairobi, Kenya, with tens of thousands of people affected.
Nine people are killed and five others critically injured after a truck plunged into a ditch in Rangamati, Bangladesh.

context: National Security Act, 2024 > Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act
text: US President Joe Biden signs the PAFACA Act into law. The act could result in video sharing platform TikTok being sold or banned in the United States.

Argentina issues an arrest warrant via Interpol for Iranian interior minister Ahmad Vahidi in connection with the 1994 bombing of a Jewish Community Center in Buenos Aires. Vahidi is currently believed to be in Sri Lanka.

The Government of Colombia issues a formal apology to the indigenous communities of the Amazon basin for their enslavement and mistreatment during the Amazon rubber boom in the 19th and 20th centuries.
Iranian rapper Toomaj Salehi is sentenced to death for supporting the 2022 protests.
Moldova announces that it has brought a criminal case against Gagauzia governor Evghenia Guțul for using Russian funds to finance the now-banned Șor Party.
Three people are injured in a stabbing at the Ysgol Dyffryn Aman school in Ammanford, Wales. The suspect is arrested.
Russian Deputy Defense Minister Timur Ivanov is arrested on suspicion of bribery.
The centre-right opposition candidate, Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova, wins the first round of the presidential election and will face incumbent president Stevo Pendarovski in the second round on 8 May.
Thousands of people protest in Buenos Aires, Argentina, against reductions in funding for universities made by President Javier Milei.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says that he is considering resigning from office after the launch of a judicial investigation into his wife after accusations by a right-wing legal platform.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Israel intensifies strikes on Rafah ahead of a planned ground offensive.
The city of Venice, Italy, introduces an entry fee for day-trippers, trying to limit the overcrowds of tourists.
Floods caused by weeks of heavy rains in Kenya have killed at least 38 people, according to the Red Cross.
Floods and landslides have killed at least 155 people in Tanzania, according to Prime Minister Kassim Majaliwa.
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov warns that Russia will make NATO nuclear weapons in Poland one of its primary targets if they are deployed there.

The New York Court of Appeals overturns former American film producer Harvey Weinstein's 2020 conviction in the state for rape by a vote of 4–3, and orders a new trial. However, Weinstein will still remain in prison on a 2022 conviction in California for rape.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: The University of Southern California cancels its main commencement ceremony due to safety concerns.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Arabic language spokesperson of the United States Department of State resigns in opposition to U.S. Gaza policy.

context: 2024 Scottish government crisis > Premiership of Humza Yousaf
text: The Scottish National Party's coalition in the Scottish government with the Scottish Greens collapses as the Scottish National Party withdraws, although the party announces its intention to continue as a minority government. In response, the Scottish Conservatives call a no confidence vote against First Minister Humza Yousaf.
Ariel Henry formally resigns as Prime Minister of Haiti and is replaced by the Transitional Presidential Council.
The first round of the NFL draft is held in Detroit, Michigan, U.S., with the Chicago Bears taking former USC quarterback Caleb Williams with the first overall pick.
Thirty rabbis and peace activists from the United States and Israel are arrested near the Gaza–Israel barrier while protesting to bring awareness to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.
An 18-year-old woman is stabbed in Ramla, Israel, and is reported to be in "serious" condition.

The Philippine Army announces that it has killed Nawapi Abdulsaid, an Abu Sayyaf militant, during a shootout two days ago in Hadji Mohammad Ajul, Basilan, Philippines. Abdulsaid was involved in fifteen beheadings as well as in attacks against security forces.
Four Yemeni expatriate workers are killed by a drone attack in the Khor Mor gas field in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.
A tornado outbreak in areas near Omaha, Nebraska, United States, leads to the issuance of multiple tornado emergencies across the states of Nebraska and Iowa.

A Doppler on Wheels unit records wind speeds of 224 miles / 360 kilometers per hour in a tornado near Harlan, Iowa, the strongest recorded by a mobile weather radar since the 2013 El Reno tornado, equivalent to EF-5 intensity on the Enhanced Fujita scale.
At least ten people are killed in a fire at a guesthouse in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
Chinese Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesman Wang Wenbin says that China will host unity talks between Hamas and Fatah.
A court in Ukraine orders the arrest of agriculture minister Mykola Solskyi on a charge of illegal acquisition of land worth $7 million.
Thousands of people protest in Budapest, Hungary, demanding reforms to child protection laws.
A court in Romania rules that the human trafficking trial of British businessman Andrew Tate can proceed.
Vương Đình Huệ, the Chairman of the National Assembly of Vietnam, resigns following a sweeping anti-corruption probe.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine says that it attacked two oil refineries and an airfield in Krasnodar Krai, Russia, using drones.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russian missiles strike Ukrainian power plants and natural gas storage facilities in Lviv, Ivano-Frankivsk, and Dnipropetrovsk Oblasts.
A humanitarian aid flotilla headed for Gaza was halted in Turkey after Guinea-Bissau withdrew its flag from two out of three vessels.

context: Tornadoes of 2024 > Tornado outbreak sequence of April 25–28, 2024
text: At least three fatalities are reported in Oklahoma as a tornado outbreak impacts the central United States.
At least five people are killed and at least 33 others are injured by a tornado in Guangzhou, China.

A magnitude-6.5 earthquake strikes off the southwestern coast of Java island, Indonesia. The epicenter of the earthquake was located about 150 kilometers away from Garut, West Java. At least four people are injured and some buildings are damaged.
A munitions truck explodes at a military base in Kampong Speu province, Cambodia, killing 20 soldiers and destroying multiple buildings.
At least one person is killed in a stab attack in Koszalin's Rokosowo district, Poland. Łukasz R. was charged and arrested on April 29.

Authorities in Russia arrest a fifth suspect in last month's attack on a music venue in Krasnogorsk, Moscow Oblast, Russia, a Tajik man accused of providing the attackers with financing and communication.
Iraq's parliament votes to criminalize same-sex relationships, to be punishable by a maximum of 15 years in prison.
Three police officers are killed during an ambush in Cañete, Chile, after receiving false emergency calls. They are shot dead before their vehicle is set on fire.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > 2024 Constitution Party presidential primaries
text: Randall Terry, an anti-abortion activist and candidate in the 2012 Democratic Party presidential primaries, wins the nomination for the Constitution Party.

context: Elected British politicians who have changed party affiliation
text: Conservative MP Dan Poulter defects to the Labour Party.
Several Palmeiras players are attacked and injured by Corinthians fans during a pitch invasion at a futsal final in São Paulo, Brazil.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Ukraine withdraws from the villages of Berdychi, Semenivka, and Novomykhailivka in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Islamic State insurgency in the North Caucasus
text: Two police officers are killed and four more injured during a shooting at a checkpoint in Karachay-Cherkessia, Russia. The five gunmen are also killed in the ensuing shootout. The group also attacked another checkpoint a week ago in the same region, killing two officers and wounding another.
Nicole Kidman becomes the first Australian to earn the AFI Life Achievement Award for her contribution to American cinema.
At least 25 people are killed and 13 injured when a bus plunges into a ravine in Cajamarca, Peru.
Eighteen people are killed and 32 others are injured as a bus crashes on a highway in Malinalco, Mexico.
The Philippines announces that it will close all schools on Monday and Tuesday, due to an extreme heat wave currently affecting the country.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Green Party presidential candidate Jill Stein is arrested while participating in a pro-Palestine protest at Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Hawai'i becomes the first US state to call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Cornel West 2024 presidential campaign
text: Cornel West wins the nomination of the Green Mountain Peace and Justice Party, gaining ballot access in Vermont.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present) > Red Sea crisis
text: Houthi forces strike four ships in the Red Sea and damage the Malta-flagged, Greece-owned bulk carrier Cyclades.
Israeli airstrikes in Rafah and Gaza City kill at least 40 people.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Odesa strikes
text: Four people are killed and 28 others are injured in a Russian missile strike in Odesa. Ukraine says that Russia used an Iskander-M ballistic missile with a cluster warhead in the attack.

Five Dawla Islamiya militants are killed and three soldiers are wounded during two shootouts in Munai, Lanao del Norte, Philippines. The military were hunting the group's leader, Nasser Daud, who however escaped from the scene.
Five people are killed and five more injured in a bomb attack in El Wak town in Mandera County, northern Kenya, near the border with Somalia.

At least 45 people are killed and dozens of others are missing following a dam burst in Mai Mahiu, Kenya, amid ongoing heavy rains and flash floods in the country, which have killed more than 120 people.
A Mil Mi-17 helicopter of the Colombian National Army Aviation group crashes in Santa Rosa, Bolívar, Colombia, killing nine soldiers on board.
Two people die in a heatwave in Kerala, India.

context: Ecuador–Mexico relations > 2024 raid on the Mexican embassy in Ecuador
text: Ecuador files a complaint against Mexico at the International Court of Justice over Mexico's move to grant political asylum to former Ecuadorian vice-president Jorge Glas.
Four law enforcement officers and suspect are killed and four others are injured in a shootout in Charlotte, North Carolina, United States.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign
text: Independent candidate for president Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is nominated for president by the American Independent Party, gaining him ballot access in California and Nevada.
Ahead of a planned vote of no confidence, Scottish First Minister Humza Yousaf announces that he will resign from office.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says that he will not resign, following the opening of preliminary court proceedings against his wife María Begoña Gómez for alleged corruption.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: Russian forces strike Kharkiv with guided bombs, killing at least two people and injuring six others.
An Israeli police officer is injured in a stabbing by a Turkish national in the Old City of Jerusalem. The assailant was fatally shot by other responding officers at the scene.
The death toll from ongoing flooding in Kenya increases to 169, with 91 people reported missing.
Nine people are killed and two more injured during an explosion caused by a gas leak at a restaurant in Beirut, Lebanon.
Fifty-five people are injured after a Los Angeles Metro light rail train collides with a transportation bus in downtown Los Angeles.
The Mount Ruang volcano in North Sulawesi, Indonesia, erupts for the second time this month, prompting the evacuation of more than 12,000 people.
China's coast guard expels a Philippine Coast Guard ship and another vessel from the waters near Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses > 2024 Columbia University pro-Palestinian campus occupation
text: Over 100 protestors are arrested by the NYPD after attempting to occupy Hamilton Hall.

Police in Tbilisi, Georgia, utilize a water cannon, tear gas, and stun grenades as part of a crackdown on protests against a law requiring foreign non-governmental organizations to register as foreign agents.

context: Prosecution of Donald Trump in New York
text: Judge Juan Merchan fines Donald Trump $9,000 for contempt of court, and threatens to jail Trump if he continues to violate his gag order.

A man attacks people with a sword after crashing a car into a house in Hainault, London, England, United Kingdom, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring four other people, including two police officers.
French prosecutors announce that actor Gérard Depardieu will be tried for the alleged sexual assault of two women in 2021.
The founder of the cryptocurrency exchange service Binance, Changpeng Zhao, is sentenced to four months in prison for money laundering.
The International Court of Justice rejects a request by Nicaragua asking the court to order Germany to suspend aid to Israel.
A Chinese spacecraft carrying the Shenzhou 17 crew lands back on Earth at the Dongfeng site after completing a six-month mission on the Tiangong space station.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Odesa strikes
text: Two Russian ballistic missiles strike the port city of Odesa, killing three people and injuring sixteen others.

Russia displays captured NATO military vehicles and equipment at an open-air exhibition in Victory Park on Poklonnaya Hill in Moscow. Among the captured vehicles are a German Leopard 2 tank and an American M1 Abrams tank.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of Gaza, Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Amid pressure from the United States, Israel reopens the Erez-Beit Hanoun Crossing and allows aid trucks into the northern part of the Gaza Strip.
Forty-eight people are killed and 30 more injured as twenty-three vehicles fell down during a highway collapse in Meizhou, Guangdong, China.
The death toll from ongoing flooding in Kenya increases to 181, as more homes and roads are destroyed.
Ten people are killed by heavy rain in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
At least nine people are killed in an ongoing heatwave in eastern India.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > Colombia–Israel relations
text: President Gustavo Petro announces that Colombia will suspend diplomatic relations with Israel over its actions in Gaza.
British authorities begin detaining migrants ahead of deportation flights to Rwanda.

Irish Taoiseach Simon Harris announces the deployment of 100 police officers to the border with Northern Ireland amid fears that thousands of migrants might flee the UK in order to avoid deportation to Rwanda. Ireland also declares the United Kingdom a "safe country" so that asylum seekers can be deported back to the UK.

U.S. federal judge Catherine Eagles blocks several of North Carolina's restrictions on the abortion pill mifepristone, striking down a requirement that the drug can only be prescribed by doctors in-person, as well as a requirement for patients to have an in-person follow-up appointment.
A student is fatally shot by police officers outside Mount Horeb Middle School in Mount Horeb, Wisconsin, United States, after the police received reports of someone carrying a weapon.
At least 217 people are detained by Turkish police during May Day rallies in Istanbul, after police fire tear gas and rubber bullets into the crowds.
At least 45 people are arrested and 12 police officers are injured at May Day protests in Paris. French police use tear gas and batons to disperse several protests.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses > 2024 University of California, Los Angeles pro-Palestinian campus occupation
text: Pro-Israel counter-protestors attack the pro-Palestinian encampment at the University of California, Los Angeles, throwing objects and attempting to destroy barricades.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: The administration of Shiraz University in Southern Iran offers free tuition to college students in the United States who have been expelled for participating in anti-Israel campus protests.
The Scottish National Party administration survives the vote of no confidence earlier this week, prompting the party to seek a replacement for outgoing First Minister Humza Yousaf.
The United Methodist Church votes 692–51 to repeal a longstanding ban on LGBTQ clergy while additionally prohibiting superintendents from forbidding a same-sex wedding.

context: Syrian civil war > Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Several people are injured in alleged Israeli airstrikes on Damascus, Syria, the first since the attack on the Iranian consulate in April.

context: Alliance of Sahel States > Nigerien crisis
text: Russian military personnel enter the United States–operated Niger Air Base 101 near Diori Hamani International Airport in Niger.
Russian forces take control of the village of Berdychi in Donetsk Oblast.
At least nine people, including eight children, are injured in a Russian guided airstrike in Derhachi, Kharkiv Oblast.
A Palestinian National Security Forces patrol kills a Palestinian Islamic Jihad gunman in Tulkarm in the West Bank.

context: Economic impact of the Israel–Hamas war, Israel–Turkey relations
text: Turkey suspends all trade with Israel in response to their conduct in the war in Gaza and demands that humanitarian aid be allowed to enter the Gaza Strip uninterrupted, after previously suspending some exports to Israel in April.
The death toll from ongoing flooding in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, increases to 13.
Eleven people are killed and nine others injured after lightning strikes across five districts in Bangladesh.
Five people are killed and 21 injured after a vehicle veered off the road and overturned in Samangan Province, Afghanistan.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine
text: Trinidad and Tobago formally recognizes Palestine as an independent nation.
South Korea raises its terrorism alert level to the second-highest level, citing strong chances of an attack from North Korea on its overseas diplomatic offices.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses > 2024 University of California, Los Angeles pro-Palestinian campus occupation
text: Police storm the pro-Palestinian encampment at the University of California, Los Angeles, arresting protesters and dismantling the encampment.
Protests occur in Batumi, Georgia, against a law requiring foreign non-governmental organizations to register as foreign agents.
Jeremiah Manele is elected Prime Minister of Solomon Islands.
The United Kingdom holds local elections, as well as a parliamentary by-election in the Blackpool South constituency. The Labour Party wins most councils.
The mining town of Rubaya, Democratic Republic of the Congo, is seized by the March 23 Movement.

Twelve people are killed and more than 20 others are injured during explosions caused by bombs at two camps for displaced people in Lac Vert and Mugunga, in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Two people are killed and two others are injured by Russian shelling in the city of Kurakhove in the Donetsk oblast.
British Foreign Secretary David Cameron promises £3 billion of annual military aid to Ukraine for "as long as it takes."
The United States tells Qatar to evict Hamas if the latter obstructs an Israeli hostage deal.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission gives ExxonMobil approval in the acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources for $60 billion.
Panama bans First Quantum Minerals from extracting copper following the closure of its Cobre Panamá mine last year.
The death toll from the heavy rains in southern Brazil increases to 39 people, with more than 70 others missing.
A bus plunges into a ravine in Diamer District, Pakistan, killing 20 people and seriously injuring 30 others.

Thirteen people are killed and 2,000 homes are flooded during heavy rains in Haiti, mainly in the city of Cap-Haitien. Rains occurs also in Puerto Rico, where planes are landed in San Juan to reroute.

Mexican authorities locate the bodies of three tourists, one American and two Australians, in Baja California, where they were reported missing in April. Three people have been arrested and are being questioned in relation to the case.

Three Indian men are arrested in Canada and charged with the murder of Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar last year. The Canadian government is investigating whether the men had ties to the Indian government.

context: Capital punishment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
text: A military court in the Democratic Republic of the Congo sentences eight soldiers to death for cowardice and other crimes.
U.S. Representative Henry Cuellar is indicted for accepting nearly $600,000 worth of bribes from an Azerbaijan-controlled company and a Mexican bank.
The International Criminal Court warns against outside interference, saying that efforts to undermine the court's work must "cease immediately".

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses > 2024 Sciences Po pro-Palestinian occupation protest
text: French police evacuate Sciences Po University in Paris and close the university in response to pro-Palestine protests and building occupations by students.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: The Houthis offer American students who have been suspended in pro-Palestine protests education at Sanaa University in Yemen.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Students at the National Autonomous University of Mexico hold pro-Palestine solidarity encampments and protests.

The China National Space Administration launches the Chang'e 6 spacecraft from the Wenchang Space Launch Site on a two-month mission to collect lunar rock and soil samples from the far side of the Moon.
Two people are killed and six others are injured in Russian overnight drone strikes on the Kharkiv and Dnipro regions of Ukraine.
German MEP Matthias Ecke is "seriously injured" in Dresden, Germany, in what is suspected to be a politically-motivated attack against the Social Democratic Party of Germany.

The death toll from ongoing heavy rains in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, increases to 56, with 67 people still missing and nearly 25,000 displaced. The airport in Porto Alegre, the capital of Rio Grande do Sul, suspends all flights until further notice.
At least 14 people are killed by floods and landslides in South Sulawesi, Indonesia.
Israeli police forcibly removes and arrests a guard of the Greek consulate inside the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in East Jerusalem, during Holy Saturday.
Indian Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar rejects comments made by US President Joe Biden saying that India's economic growth was being held back by "xenophobia".

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Palestinian doctor and rector at the University of Glasgow Ghassan Abu-Sittah is denied entry into France after landing at Charles de Gaulle Airport on his way to speak at the French Senate. Last month, he was denied entry into Germany.

Russian state media reports that a number of officials from Ukraine and NATO countries have been placed on Russia's wanted list, including Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, former president Petro Poroshenko, Ukrainian Ground Forces commander Oleksandr Pavlyuk, and Estonian prime minister Kaja Kallas. The Ministry of Internal Affairs neither states what crimes the wanted individuals are being charged with, nor clarifies the allegations that are being brought against them.
Sadiq Khan wins re-election as mayor of London, England, with 43.8% of the vote, becoming the first London mayor to be elected to a third term.
Real Madrid are crowned champions of La Liga after Barcelona's 4–2 defeat at Girona.
Barcelona are crowned champions of Liga F after winning 1–4 at Granada.
The 150th edition of the Kentucky Derby is held, with American thoroughbred racehorse Mystik Dan winning in a photo finish.

The International Olympics Committee (IOC) bans Kuwait's Sheikh Ahmad Al-Fahad Al-Ahmed Al-Sabah from all positions within the committee for 15 years over ethics breaches. Sheik Ahmad was previously banned by the IOC for three years in 2023 over his alleged interference in the Olympic Council of Asia elections, as well as for forgery and a fake arbitration procedure.
2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict

context: Israel–Hamas war > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Israeli air raids in Meiss Ej Jabal, Lebanon, cause "massive destruction" according to a Lebanese state-run agency, killing four civilians and injuring three others. In response, Hezbollah fires dozens of Katyusha and Falaq rockets towards Kiryat Shmona, Israel.
Three IDF soldiers are killed and ten civilians are injured when Hamas launches a rocket barrage at the Kerem Shalom border crossing.
Hamas announces the end of ceasefire talks held in Cairo, Egypt, while Israel vows to continue its military operations.
A woman is killed and 17 other people are injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv, Ukraine.

A man is injured in a stabbing at a car park in Perth, Australia. The 16-year-old perpetrator is killed by police officers and is described as a "religious radicalized individual". A possible Islamist motive is behind the attack.

With the closing performance of the Celebration Tour at Copacabana Beach, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, American singer Madonna attracts 1.6 million people in a free concert and breaks the record for the most attended stand-alone concert by any artist, and the all-time highest attended concert by a female artist.
The death toll from the ongoing flooding in Kenya increases to 228.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 78, with more than 100 people still missing.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Virginia State Police dismantle a pro-Palestine encampment on the University of Virginia campus in Charlottesville, and arrest more than 15 students.
Panamanians elect their President and members of the National Assembly.

José Raúl Mulino, the stand-in for former president Ricardo Martinelli, wins the presidential election with more than 35% of the vote, after his three nearest opponents conceded. He will assume office in July.
The ruling Union for the Republic party wins 108 out of 113 seats in the National Assembly.
The Israeli Cabinet votes to close all Al Jazeera offices in Israel, with Israeli authorities later raiding these offices.
Thousands of Hungarians protest in Debrecen, Hungary, against Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's rule and policies.

context: 2024 Formula One World Championship > 2024 Miami Grand Prix
text: In auto racing, McLaren driver Lando Norris wins his first Formula One race at the Miami Grand Prix.
Kyle Larson edges out Chris Buescher in the closest finish in NASCAR Cup Series history, winning a photo finish by one-thousandth (0.001) of a second.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Israel tells civilians to evacuate parts of eastern Rafah ahead of a planned ground invasion.

Hamas states that it has accepted a ceasefire proposal negotiated by Egypt and Qatar. Israel rejects the proposal, claiming that the deal does not meet its "core demands", but confirms that it will continue negotiations in Cairo, Egypt.

Two IDF soldiers of the 98th Paratroopers Division's 655th Battalion were killed in a Hezbollah drone strike near Metula, northern Israel, bringing the IDF death toll of the conflict start to 18. and 30 rockets are fired at Kidmat Tzvi, Golan Heights, **Three injured in IDF strikes on 15 Radwan targets including a factory in al-Lwaiza and a Hezbollah compound in Sefri, near Baalbek in southern Lebanon.[https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/explosive-laden-drone-launched-by-hezbollah-from-lebanon-hits-near-metula/ [(The Times of Israel)].

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Six people are killed and 35 others are injured in Ukrainian drone attacks in Belgorod Oblast, Russia.

context: Kurdish–Turkish conflict > Kurdistan Workers' Party insurgency
text: The Turkish Air Force carries out airstrikes on Iraqi Kurdistan, reportedly killing 16 PKK insurgents.
The 2024 Met Gala takes place at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City with the theme "The Garden of Time", celebrating the Met's exhibit Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion.
The 2024 Pulitzer Prize ceremony is held, with 16 awards in Journalism and 10 in Letters, Drama, & Music.
Steward Health Care, a for-profit hospital chain in the United States, files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 85.
An under construction apartment building collapses in George, South Africa, killing 34 people and injuring 16 others.
Five workers are killed and another is critically injured while carrying out maintenance work on a wastewater lifting tank in Palermo, Italy.
The U.S. Storm Prediction Center issues a rare high risk convective outlook ahead of an expected significant tornado outbreak in parts of Oklahoma and Kansas.
An EF4 tornado strikes the cities of Barnsdall and Bartlesville, Oklahoma, killing one and leaving one other missing.
An American soldier is arrested in Russia on charges of criminal misconduct. According to US officials, the soldier was based in South Korea and had been accused of stealing from a woman.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Japanese students at the University of Tokyo, Sophia University, Tama Art University, International Christian University, and Hiroshima University hold solidarity encampments.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Belgian and Dutch students hold solidarity encampments and occupy parts of the Ghent University, the University of Amsterdam, and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
Chad holds presidential elections under its junta, contested between incumbent Mahamat Déby and Prime Minister Succès Masra.
John Swinney is elected leader of the Scottish National Party following the resignation of First Minister Humza Yousaf.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Assassination attempts on Volodymyr Zelenskyy
text: The Security Service of Ukraine says that it detained two Ukrainian government protection unit colonels recruited by Russia's Federal Security Service who were planning an assassination of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other top Ukrainian officials.
Ukrainian forces launch a missile strike on an oil terminal in Luhansk, causing a large fire and injuring at least five workers.
Israeli forces enter Rafah in a "limited" operation, taking control of the Rafah Border Crossing on the Egypt–Gaza border.
At least 27 people are killed by Israeli airstrikes in Rafah.
The death toll from rocket strikes on an IDP camp in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo, increases to 18.
The Boy Scouts of America announces the renaming of the organization to Scouting America on February 8, 2025, in an effort to make girls feel more welcome.

context: Tornadoes of 2024 > Tornado outbreak of May 6–10, 2024
text: A FedEx warehouse in Portage, Michigan, United States, is destroyed by a tornado.
The death toll from ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 90, with more than 150,000 people left homeless.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine
text: The Bahamas formally recognizes Palestine as an independent nation.

Russia declares American nonprofit organization Freedom House an "undesirable organization", effectively outlawing the group, after accusing the group of "discrediting the Russian Army" and advocating sanctions against Russia.
Two people are killed and 21 others are injured in a mass stabbing at a hospital in Zhenxiong County, Yunnan, China. A suspect has been detained.
TikTok and its parent company ByteDance sue the United States government over the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, alleging that the law is unconstitutional.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Dutch police end a pro-Palestinian occupation at the University of Amsterdam.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is inaugurated for a fifth six-year term.
The Scottish Parliament votes to elect John Swinney as First Minister of Scotland with 64 votes in favour and seven abstentions from the Scottish Greens.
A third mass grave holding at least 49 bodies is discovered in Gaza City's al-Shifa Hospital.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Israel reopens the Kerem Shalom border crossing, allowing humanitarian aid into Gaza. However, the UN states that no aid has entered.

Israeli troops reach the outskirts of Rafah with Hamas saying that heavy fighting is underway. The Israeli military says that it has "uncovered terrorist infrastructure" and killed a number of Hamas militants as it advances.
Two Hezbollah and three PIJ killed in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, injuring three people and damaging critical infrastructure. Ukraine says that it shot down 39 of 55 missiles and 20 of 21 drones.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least seven people, including four children, are injured in a Russian airstrike on Kharkiv.
Russia occupies the villages of Novokalynove in Donetsk Oblast and Kyslivka in Kharkiv Oblast.
A motorcycle bombing kills three Taliban security personnel in Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan. The Islamic State – Khorasan Province claims responsibility for the attack.

context: Tornadoes of 2024 > Tornado outbreak of May 6–8, 2024
text: Dozens of tornadoes strike the United States over the past three days, killing five people and leaving multiple others injured.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 100, with 128 people still missing and 163,000 people displaced.
Rolling blackouts occur in several cities in Mexico amid an ongoing heatwave in the country.
A Boeing 767 operated by FedEx is forced to make an emergency landing at Istanbul Airport after the front landing gear fails to deploy.

A Republic of Singapore Air Force (RSAF) F-16C fighter jet crashed at Tengah Air Base after the pilot experienced issues during take-off. The pilot ejected successfully and is receiving medical attention. The RSAF has temporarily suspended training for the F-16 fleet until investigations show that it is safe to resume.
AstraZeneca withdraws its marketing authorizations in Europe and withdraws its COVID-19 vaccines worldwide due to low demand, after finding that the vaccines can very rarely lead to blood clots.

The Indian Central Bureau of Investigation arrests four people linked to a network of human traffickers who have been luring young men to go to Russia with the promise of jobs or university admission, then forcing them to fight in the war in Ukraine. The Ministry of External Affairs is working with Russia to secure discharges for 20 Indian nationals in the Russian Army.
Two Cambodian and Chinese people are deported from Singapore after being convicted of laundering over S$3 billion (US$2.2 billion), Singapore's largest ever money laundering case.

context: Elected British politicians who have changed party affiliation
text: British Conservative MP Natalie Elphicke defects to the opposition Labour Party, citing the Sunak government's failure to stop the English Channel migrant crisis.
The United States House of Representatives vote 359–43 to keep Mike Johnson as House Speaker, defeating an initiative by Marjorie Taylor Greene to have him removed.
Researchers at Google DeepMind announce the development of AlphaFold 3, an AI model that can predict the structures of almost all biological molecules and model the interactions between them.
The ship Belem arrives in Marseille, France, with the Olympic flame.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive
text: Israeli tanks and warplanes strike eastern Rafah. 80,000 people have fled Rafah throughout the week.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > United States support for Israel in the Israel–Hamas war
text: U.S. President Joe Biden threatens to withhold weapons from Israel if it launches a major invasion of Rafah.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present) > Red Sea crisis
text: The Houthis claim responsibility for attacks on three container ships in the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.
Israeli far-right extremists launch two arson attacks on the perimeter of the UNRWA headquarters in East Jerusalem, forcing it to temporarily close down.

context: Syrian civil war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Four Hezbollah militants killed in an Israeli airstrike in Bafliyeh, Lebanon.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Assassination attempts on Volodymyr Zelenskyy
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fires the head of the state guards Serhiy Rud after allegations that two members of the guards were involved in an assassination plot against Zelenskyy.

context: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, Iran–Israel relations
text: Iran warns that it will build a nuclear weapon if Israel continues to target its nuclear facilities.
Air India Express cancels 85 flights due to staff calling in sick at the last minute, which is related to a protest against working conditions imposed by the airline's new owner Tata Group.
Air Vanuatu cancels all of its flights as the Vanuatu Government considers putting the airline into voluntary administration.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 107, with at least 136 people still missing and 165,000 people displaced.
Nine people are killed and two injured after a truck crashed into a passenger van near Qingtongxia, Ningxia, China.
Eight people are killed after a Beechcraft King Air crashes on Lake Maracaibo, in Zulia, Venezuela.
Two Boeing 737 planes are involved in accidents involving takeoff and landing in Senegal and Turkey.
Australia and Tuvalu sign a new security agreement, whereby Australia agrees to protect Tuvalu during natural disasters, pandemics, or military aggression.
Former Fijian prime minister Frank Bainimarama is sentenced to one year in prison for perverting the course of justice.
