Thousands of pro-Palestinian protesters march in Malmö, Sweden, against Israel's participation in the Eurovision Song Contest. Among the protesters is Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg.
Trade unions in Argentina launch a general strike against President Javier Milei's planned reforms and budget cuts.
Bayer Leverkusen breaks Benfica's record of 48 undefeated games in modern European men's club association football.
A Hezbollah and PIJ militant killed in Aedsheet and Blida, Marjeyoun District, two civilian cell tower repairers killed Tayr Harfa in Israeli airstrikes.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kharkiv offensive
text: Russian forces launch an attack on Ukraine's Kharkiv Oblast, near the town of Vovchansk, opening up a new front.
A Ukrainian strike against oil infrastructure kills three in Luhansk.
The death toll from rocket strikes on an IDP camp in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo, increases to 35.
Hundreds of Islamic State-linked fighters attack the town of Macomia, Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique.
Indian security forces kill 12 Maoist rebels in Chhattisgarh.
Over 200 people are killed by floods in Baghlan Province, Afghanistan.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 126, with 141 still missing and more than 300,000 people displaced.
Seven people are killed and six others are injured when a passenger bus plunges from the Potseluev Bridge into the Moyka river in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
At least 60 people are injured when a passenger train collides with a locomotive in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Amid record low birth rates and an aging population, Pope Francis urges Italians to have more children. The Italian government also expands a campaign to encourage at least 500,000 births annually by 2033.

context: Palestine and the United Nations > United Nations General Assembly Resolution ES-10/23
text: The United Nations General Assembly votes 143–9 with 25 abstentions to approve a resolution granting Palestine new rights and privileges, and to reconsider Palestine's request to become a UN member. The nine countries that opposed the resolution were Argentina, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Israel, Micronesia, Nauru, Palau, Papua New Guinea and the United States.
A Colombian court in Bogotá grants conditional release to former paramilitary leader Salvatore Mancuso. He was held at La Picota prison while being accused of war crimes and human rights violations.

context: Arrest of Arvind Kejriwal, 2024 Indian general election
text: The Supreme Court of India grants Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal interim bail for 21 days in connection with the Delhi liquor policy money laundering case, thereby permitting Kejriwal to campaign in the ongoing general election.
A Pennsylvania jury orders ExxonMobil to pay $725.5 million to a former mechanic who claimed that the company's gasoline and solvents caused him to develop leukemia.

Peruvian authorities launch an investigation into President Dina Boluarte for disbanding a police force that was investigating her brother Nicanor Boluarte, who was arrested for alleged influence peddling.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Police dismantle encampments and arrest dozens of students protesting at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Academic staff of The New School in New York City hold the first faculty-led solidarity encampment in the United States.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign
text: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. qualifies to appear on the ballot in Oklahoma for the 2024 United States presidential election as an independent candidate.
Thousands of protesters march through Warsaw, Poland, against the European Union's environmental regulations.
Emir of Kuwait Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah dissolves the National Assembly and suspends some articles of the Constitution.
Eight hundred protesters storm the Tesla plant in Grünheide, Germany, in protest of the environmental impact of the company's expansion.
A geomagnetic storm hits Earth, reaching G5 intensity and causing widespread aurorae, with NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center issuing its first G4-level storm watch since 2005.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Three people are killed in a Ukrainian strike in Donetsk. Separately, two people are killed in Ukrainian strikes in Belgorod and Kursk.
Switzerland's entry, "The Code" by Nemo, wins this year's Eurovision contest.

Dutch musician Joost Klein is disqualified from the Eurovision final over reported verbal threats, which are under investigation by Swedish authorities. This is the first time that a performer has been disqualified during the festival.
The Norwegian announcer for Eurovision, Alessandra Mele, announces that she will withdraw from announcing votes while declaring support for Palestine in the ongoing war.
The death toll from the ongoing flooding in northern Afghanistan increases to 300, with more than 1,000 houses destroyed.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 136, with 125 still missing, and more than 300,000 people displaced.
At least 28 people are killed after heavy rains in the Agam and Tanah Datar districts in West Sumatra, Indonesia, which triggered a flash flood and cold lava flow from Mount Marapi.
Eleven people are killed and 53 others are injured when a bus crashes in West Java, Indonesia.
Fifty thousand people march in Tbilisi, in protest of the proposed Law on Transparency of Foreign Influence.
The Russian Defence Ministry states that its forces have captured several villages in Kharkiv Oblast.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > May 2024 Belgorod missile strike
text: At least 17 civilians are killed and 30 others are injured when a missile hit an apartment block in Belgorod, Russia.
President of Russia Vladimir Putin reassigns Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu to the National Security Council and replaces him with Deputy Prime Minister Andrey Belousov.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive
text: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken warns Israel lacks a credible plan to protect Rafah civilians.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of El Fasher
text: Fighting during RSF attacks on eastern El Fasher, over the weekend, kill at least 38 civilians and injure 189 others amid fears of an all out RSF assault on the city.
The death toll from the ongoing flooding in northern Afghanistan increases to 315, with more than 1,600 people injured, and more than 1,000 houses destroyed.

The death toll from the ongoing flooding in southern Brazil increases to 143, with 125 people still missing. The Brazilian government has announced R$12.1 billion in emergency spending in response to the crisis.
The Marywilska 44 shopping mall in Białołęka district, Warsaw, Poland, is destroyed in a suspected arson attack. Many of the venues were Vietnamese-owned.
Wildfires in British Columbia and Alberta, Canada, force thousands to evacuate.
Egypt announces it will intervene on South Africa's side in the South Africa v Israel case in response to Israel's growing assault on Rafah.
The Socialists' Party of Catalonia wins the regional election with its best result since 2003. Pro-independence parties lose their absolute majority in the Parliament.

context: 2024 Lithuanian presidential election, 2024 Lithuanian constitutional referendum
text: Lithuanians elect the President of Lithuania and vote on a constitutional amendment that would allow dual citizenship.
Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova is sworn in as the first female President of North Macedonia.
Forty-nine Vatican Museums employees start an unprecedented labor dispute over unfair and poor working conditions against the Vatican's Pontifical Commission.
Hundreds of protesters march in Tunis, Tunisia, to demand the release of imprisoned journalists, activists, and opposition figures.
Bayer Leverkusen extend their record unbeaten streak in European association football to fifty matches
Manchester United Women won their first ever major trophy which was the fa cup in a 4-0 victory over tottenham hotspur
The Israeli military advances into northern and southern Gaza.
A staff member of the United Nations Department of Safety and Security is killed and another is injured in Rafah.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis
text: Hamas says that it has "lost contact" with the militants holding four Israeli hostages in the Gaza Strip, including Israeli-American Hersh Goldberg-Polin.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kharkiv offensive
text: Russia claims that its troops have entered the town of Vovchansk, from Kharkiv.

Three years after the previous GameStop stock squeeze, Redditors return to artificially inflate GameStop's share price by 75%, reaching an 18-month high. The share price of AMC Theatres also increases by more than 70%.
U.S. President Joe Biden signs a bill banning imports of uranium from Russia.
The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern Brazil increases to 147 people, with 127 people still missing.
The final remains of the collapsed Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore, Maryland, United States, which killed six workers, are demolished with explosives.
The death toll from the flash flood and lahar in West Sumatra, Indonesia, increases to 43, with 15 others still missing.
At least 17 people are killed, 75 are injured, and others are trapped after a billboard collapses during heavy rains in Mumbai, India.

The Airlines for America trade association and several major American airlines file a lawsuit against the United States Department of Transportation over a rule requiring upfront disclosure of airline fees.
Indonesian police conducts a major drug raid on a lab hidden in a villa in Bali, Indonesia. They arrested one Indonesian, two Ukrainians, and one Russian.
A referendum to allow dual citizenship in Lithuania fails to pass.
Gitanas Nausėda and Ingrida Šimonytė advance to the run-off election, which will be held on 26 May.
The High Commissioner of New Caledonia imposes a curfew and mobilizes security forces after a general strike and violent protests over proposed constitutional changes in the capital city Nouméa.
An administrative court in Münster, Germany, rules that the Alternative for Germany political party could threaten democracy and can be spied on.
OpenAI announces a new model of their generative pretrained transformer (GPT) named GPT-4o, capable of visual and video speech recognition and translation.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kharkiv offensive, Kharkiv strikes
text: At least 20 people are injured when Russian airstrikes hit a residential building in Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kharkiv offensive, Kharkiv strikes
text: Ukraine pulls back from positions near Lukyantsi and Vovchansk in Kharkiv Oblast.

Israeli tanks enter residential areas of Rafah as they attempt to capture the city. Hamas' armed wing al-Qassam Brigades says that it destroyed an Israeli troop carrier with a Al-Yassin 105 anti-tank missile, killing several troops and injuring several others, while the Israel Defense Forces claim to have "eliminated" several terrorists in the city.

context: Israeli settler violence > Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Israeli protestors attack a convoy of aid trucks in the West Bank, damaging 15 trucks and causing $2 million worth of damage.
One civilian killed and five IDF personnel injured in Hezbollah shelling on Adamit kibbutz and launches 60 rockets at IDF air traffic control base in Mount Meron, Israel.
Two Hezbollah militants and Hussein Makki, a field commander killed and one injured in Israeli airstrikes on Meiss Ej Jabal and Tyre Lebanon.

Riots erupt in New Caledonia as France plans to change the constitution, allowing more recent white French settlers to vote in the island's provincial elections, which protesters claim would marginalise the Indigenous Kanak people.
Three Kanak residents are killed and many more injured during a drive-by shooting by a group of French settlers.
At least 54 officers are injured and more than 130 people are arrested. Shops and cars are looted, while a prison breakout has been prevented.
The 77th annual Cannes Film Festival opens in Cannes, France, with Meryl Streep receiving an honorary Palme d'Or award.
U.S. President Joe Biden passes tariff increases on Chinese imports, including electric vehicles and batteries, computer chips, and medical products.
Inflation in Argentina slows to a single digit number of 8.8 percent amid severe austerity plans by president Javier Milei.
The share price of GameStop increases by a further 61%.
The death toll from a building collapse in George, South Africa, last week, increases to 33.
Thirteen people, including former Congressman Édgar Alarcón, are killed in a bus crash in Vinchos, Huamanga Province, Peru.
Eight people are killed and 40 others are injured when a bus carrying farmworkers collides with a truck and overturns in Marion County, Florida, United States.
Russian police arrest former head of personnel of the Ministry of Defence for bribery of over $1 million. Kuznetsov's charges carry up to 15 years of jail time.
Two prison guards are killed and three others are critically injured in an ambush of a prison van near Rouen, Normandy, France, to free an inmate with ties to a drug dealing gang.
Tunisian police raid the headquarters of the Tunisian Order of Lawyers in Tunis and arrest Mahdi Zagrouba, who is known for his opposition to President Kais Saied.
The Supreme Court of Kazakhstan sentences former Minister of National Economy Kuandyk Bishimbayev to 24 years in prison for torturing and murdering his wife.
Russian dissident Vladimir Kara-Murza loses his appeal against a 25-year prison sentence.
A court in Germany convicts and fines Alternative for Germany member Björn Höcke €13,000 ($14,000) for using a Nazi slogan that once belonged to the Sturmabteilung.
Riot police clash with protesters on the streets of Tbilisi, Georgia, after the parliament approves a controversial "foreign agent" law that requires media organizations to declare foreign funding.
The United States warns Georgia that $390 million in planned economic support will be "under review" if the Georgian government considers the U.S. as an "adversary", and not as a strategic partner.
The sun emits the largest solar flare since 2005, days after producing auroras in the Northern and Southern Hempisheres.
Russia places its nuclear capable submarine-launched Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile into service.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Battle of Jabalia
text: Five Israeli soldiers are killed in a friendly fire incident in Jabalia after IDF tanks open fire on their position.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Syrian civil war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: A Syrian and four injured in an Israel-targeted drone misfire by Lebanon-branch Hamas in Lebanon with Hezbollah drones launched at Lower Galilee, IDF outposts in Golani Junction in Tiberias and damaging Tal Shamayim base Sky Dew aerostat.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Syrian civil war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: One Hezbollah member killed and two injured in an Israeli airstrike in Tyre, Lebanon.[https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1413838/hezbollah-fighter-killed-in-israeli-drone-strike-on-car-south-of-sour-day-222-of-the-gaza-war.html [(L'Orient le Jour)]
Three IDF soldiers injured in Hezbollah drone strike on Israeli positions in Metula.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Southern Ukraine campaign, Northern Kharkiv Oblast front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russia says its forces have captured the village of Robotyne in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and several more villages in Kharkiv Oblast. Ukraine confirms it has pulled back its troops from Vovchansk to "preserve the lives of our servicemen and avoid losses".

Prime Minister of Slovakia Robert Fico is injured in a shooting in Handlová, Slovakia, which is being treated as an assassination attempt. The shooter has been apprehended and is identified as a 71-year-old writer from Levice, Slovakia.

The Slovak government describes Prime Minister Robert Fico's condition as life-threatening. Deputy prime minister Tomáš Taraba stated that Fico underwent surgery, was stabilized, and is expected to survive.
France declares a state of emergency in New Caledonia as anti-French rioting continues, which has killed four people. Schools are closed and a curfew is announced in the capital Nouméa.
The United States issues sanctions on two commanders of the Rapid Support Forces, Ali Yagoub Gibril and Osman Mohamed Hamid, for their roles in the escalating violence in Darfur.
Authorities evacuate over 6,000 people as wildfires approach the city of Fort McMurray, Alberta, Canada.
The death toll from the flash flood and lahar in West Sumatra, Indonesia, increases to 62, with 25 others still missing.

The United States impose visa restrictions on more than 250 members of the Nicaraguan government and also sanction three Nicaraguan entities for "repressive action" and a failure to control migrant smuggling through Nicaragua.
Six people are injured during a mass stabbing at a railway station in Zofingen, Switzerland. The suspect, who has suffered self-inflicted wounds, is detained. His motives are unknown.

Federal prosecutors in New York City charge two brothers, Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, after they were arrested for exploiting the Ethereum blockchain and stealing $25 million worth of cryptocurrency.
The United States Supreme Court lets Louisiana use a new congressional map with two majority-Black congressional districts in the 2024 United States House of Representatives elections.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > 2024 United States presidential debates
text: U.S. President Joe Biden and presumptive Republican nominee Donald Trump agree to hold a presidential debate on June 27, hosted by CNN, which will be the earliest general election debate in modern history in the United States. A second debate will be held in September.
A new coalition government in the Netherlands is agreed by Geert Wilders, Dilan Yeşilgöz, Pieter Omtzigt, and Caroline van der Plas.
Lawrence Wong is sworn in as the fourth Prime Minister of Singapore, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong.
Scientists announce the discovery of SPECULOOS-3 b, an Earth-size exoplanet that orbits a red dwarf star that has a similar size as Jupiter.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Insurgency in the North Gaza Strip > Battle of Jabalia
text: Palestinian fighters, including Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad, claim dozens of attacks on Israeli troops in and around the Jabalia refugee camp.

context: Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: Global Affairs Canada announces sanctions on four "extremist" Israeli settlers in the West Bank for engaging in violence against Palestinian civilians and their property.

context: Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Arab League calls for a United Nations peacekeeping force and international protection in the occupied Palestinian territories until a two-state solution is implemented.

context: Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United States House of Representatives passes a bill which would defund certain offices if President Biden impedes any weapons shipments to Israel. The President is expected to veto the bill if it passes the Senate.
Two Hezbollah militants killed in an Israeli airstrike in Tyre, Lebanon.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken announces a $2 billion military aid package for Ukraine, aimed at investing in Ukraine's industrial base.
France deploys 1,000 police officers to New Caledonia in an attempt to control the ongoing riots.
Prime Minister of Slovakia Robert Fico is reported to be in serious but stable condition.

context: Milestones of the Dow Jones Index
text: The Dow Jones index surpasses 40,000 points for the first time.
Heavy storms kill at least four people in Houston, Texas, United States.
President of Russia Vladimir Putin meets with President of China Xi Jinping in Beijing, China.
The United States announces sanctions on two Russian individuals and three Russian companies for facilitating weapons transfers between Russia and North Korea.
Foreign minister of Kosovo Donika Gërvalla-Schwarz writes to the Council of Europe to ask for member nations to consider granting Kosovo entry into the council.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott pardons Daniel Perry, who was sentenced to 25 years in prison for killing a man at a Black Lives Matter protest in 2020.
The European Union opens a formal investigation into Meta for potential breaches in online content rules relating to child safety on Facebook and Instagram, which violate the Digital Services Act.
Permanent Member of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee's Secretariat Trương Thị Mai resigns after just over a year in office amid the Communist Party's anti-corruption campaign.
Tunisian lawyers launch a one-day strike and protest in Tunis following the recent arrest of two lawyers and repressive measures enacted by President Kais Saied.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Humanitarian aid deliveries begin arriving at the U.S.-built Gaza floating pier.
The IDF retrieves three hostages, having been found deceased. The three were abducted from the Re'im music festival massacre, including Shani Louk.
Hamas announces that an Israeli strike killed Sharhabil Sayed, a Hamas commander in Lebanon.
Israel announces that an Air Force strike killed Islaam Hamaisa, a commander of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad's Jenin Brigade.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine launches a massive drone attack across southwestern Russia, causing fires at several oil refineries, including at the port of Novorossiysk.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least three civilians are killed and 28 others are injured by Russian guided bombs in Kharkiv.
Gunmen open fire on a group of tourists in Bamyan Province, Afghanistan, killing three Spanish citizens, two Afghan civilians and a Taliban guard. Seven others are injured.

Two police officers are killed and another is injured outside the Ulu Tiram police station in Johor, Malaysia. The killer is later fatally shot. Seven suspected members of Jemaah Islamiyah are arrested in connection to the attack.
Israeli air strikes kill five people in Lebanon, including two children.
Houthi forces shoot down a United States Air Force MQ-9 Reaper drone with a surface-to-air missile over Marib Governorate, Yemen. Wreckage of the downed drone appears on social media.
A child in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, dies of measles, the province's first such death since 1989.

France accuses Azerbaijan of being behind the protests and violence in New Caledonia after Azerbaijani and Togolese flags are seen alongside indigenous Kanak symbols at the protests. Azerbaijan has previously spoken out against French colonialism and supported pro-independence participants, in response to French support for Armenia.
A man is shot dead by police after trying to set a synagogue on fire in Rouen, France.
The RCMP identifies the killer of four people in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, in 1976 and 1977 as American serial rapist Gary Allen Srery, who died in prison in 2011.
Iranian police arrest more than 260 people, including three European citizens, on suspicion of spreading Satanism and nudity in Iran.

Police in Louisville, Kentucky, United States, arrest American golfer Scottie Scheffler, who was travelling to the 2024 PGA Championship, for assault of a police officer, criminal mischief, reckless driving, and disregarding traffic signals.
A brawl breaks out in the Legislative Yuan, Taiwan's parliament, following disagreements over draft reforms between the Democratic Progressive Party and the Kuomintang.
Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope discover the earliest known merging of black holes, 740 million years after the Big Bang.
The annual FIFA Congress in Bangkok, Thailand, awards Brazil the host rights for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
Benny Gantz threatens to withdraw his party from the unity coalition if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu doesn't submit a post-war plan for Gaza by June 8.
Austria unfreezes €3.4 million (US$3.7 million) in funds to the UNRWA.
The Arakan Army seizes control of Buthidaung after the army captures Tatmadaw positions in the surrounding area. The town, which hosts a majority Rohingya population, is burned amidst the crossfire.
The death toll from the ongoing protests and riots in New Caledonia increases to six.
At least 68 people are killed by floods in Ghor and Faryab provinces, Afghanistan.
Three people are killed and five others are injured in a boat collision on Bobs Lake in Ontario, Canada.
At least 23 migrants are missing after boarding a boat travelling from Tunisia to Italy.
The Foreign Ministry of Pakistan asks that Pakistani nationals in Kyrgyzstan stay indoors after mob attacks on Pakistanis and other foreign nationals are reported.
Italian financial police seize 134 Fiat cars imported from Morocco following a dispute on stickers indicating the origin of the car.
President of Georgia Salome Zourabichvili vetoes the proposed "Law on Transparency of Foreign Influence".
Hundreds of protesters march in Lima, Peru, to demand the reversal of a new law that describes transgender people as having a mental illness.
The Communist Party of Vietnam nominates Minister of Public Security Tô Lâm as the next President after Võ Văn Thưởng resigned as President in March due to the party's anti-corruption campaign.
In association football, Bundesliga champions Bayer 04 Leverkusen become the first Bundesliga team to finish a season unbeaten after defeating FC Augsburg on the final matchday.
In association football, Chelsea F.C. Women wins their 7th Women's Super League title after defeating Manchester United W.F.C. 6–0 in the final match.
In boxing, Oleksandr Usyk defeats Tyson Fury by split decision and becomes the first undisputed four-belt heavyweight champion in history.

context: 2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo coup attempt
text: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo say that they foiled a coup by armed men in Kinshasa that killed two police officers and four attackers, including the coup's leader, Christian Malanga, a opposition leader of the United Congolese Party. Around 50 attackers, including Malanga's 20-year-old son and a US citizen from Maryland, are arrested.
France deploys law enforcement to New Caledonia to regain control of the road to La Tontouta International Airport, which is currently controlled by protesters.

At least six people are killed and 27 others are injured in a Russian double tap missile strike on a recreation area near Kharkiv. Separately, five people are killed and nine others are injured in a Russian strike using a multiple launch rocket system on two villages in Kupiansk Raion, Kharkiv Oblast.
A Bell 212 helicopter crashes in Varzaqan, East Azerbaijan province, Iran, killing all the eight people on board, including President Ebrahim Raisi and Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian.
Two people are killed and five others are missing after a boat collision on the Danube river near Verőce, Hungary.
Seven villages on the island of Halmahera, Indonesia, are forced to evacuate after the Mount Ibu volcano erupts.

Spain recalls its ambassador to Argentina after President of Argentina Javier Milei calls Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's wife Begoña Gómez corrupt during a rally in Madrid and also refuses to meet with King Felipe VI.
President Luis Abinader wins re-election with 59% of the popular vote.
A bright meteor crossed the skies of the Iberian Peninsula, producing a bluish flash of light that was widely recorded by security cameras and observers.
Manchester City win the Premier League, becoming the first team in the 136-year history of the Football League to win four consecutive top-flight titles.

context: Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war, War crimes in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Karim Khan, the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, requests arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, Hamas political leaders Ismail Haniyeh and Yahya Sinwar, and Al-Qassam Brigades leader Mohammed Al-Masri for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.

context: Haitian crisis > Gang war in Haiti
text: Toussaint Louverture International Airport in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, reopens after being closed for three months due to gang violence, as the US military flies in supplies and civilian contractors to help the police in order to pave a way for an intervention.
Red Lobster, an American restaurant chain, files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
The container ship Dali is freed from bridge debris since its initial collision on March 26 and is escorted by tugboats back to the port of Baltimore.
A court in Novosibirsk, Russia, sentences a 24-year-old man to 25 years in prison for allegedly plotting an arson attack on a military recruitment office with alleged directions from Ukraine.
Judges grant Julian Assange permission to appeal his extradition order from the United Kingdom to the United States.

The U.S. Supreme Court denies an appeal by former Guantanamo Bay detention camp detainee Omar Khadr to vacate his convictions for his role in the killing of former U.S. Army soldier Christopher Speer in Afghanistan.
Migz Zubiri resigns as President of the Senate of the Philippines and is replaced by Francis Escudero.
The Constitutional Court of South Africa rules that former President Jacob Zuma is ineligible to run in the upcoming parliamentary election due to his 2021 jail sentence.
First vice president of Iran Mohammad Mokhber becomes acting president following the death of Ebrahim Raisi.
Lai Ching-te is sworn in as President of Taiwan, with Hsiao Bi-khim as his Vice President.

context: Israel–Hamas War > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The UNRWA suspends food distribution in Rafah due to insecurity and a lack of supplies.

context: Israel–Hamas War > Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Israeli army launches a raid on the city of Jenin in the West Bank, with sources claiming that seven Palestinians were killed.

A high-ranking Lebanese army officer and three Hezbollah members assassinated in IDF airstrikes in Tyre, Lebanon, Beqaa Valley and Kfar Dajjal with three children injured in a school bus. The state department of Lebanon issues a formal complaint to the United Nations Security Council.
Gunmen kill 40 people in an attack on a village in Nigeria's Plateau State.
Jenny Erpenbeck wins the International Booker Prize for her novel Kairos, translated from the German by Michael Hofmann.
Pixar Animation Studios lays off 14% of its workforce, approximately 175 people.

A Singapore Airlines flight from London, England, to Singapore makes an emergency landing at Suvarnabhumi Airport in Bangkok, Thailand, after experiencing severe air turbulence over the Bay of Bengal, resulting in one death and 104 injuries.
Eleven workers drown after a microbus falls off a ferry into the Nile River in Giza, Egypt.

At least five people are killed and 35 are injured as a strong tornado devastates the town of Greenfield, Iowa, United States. A Doppler on Wheels unit records a wind gust of between and over Greenfield, the strongest winds recorded inside a tornado by a mobile weather radar since the 2013 El Reno tornado, equivalent to EF5 intensity on the Enhanced Fujita scale.
Spain permanently recalls its ambassador from Argentina amid a diplomatic crisis over President of Argentina Javier Milei's comments about Prime Minister of Spain Pedro Sánchez's wife, Begoña Gómez.

Moldova becomes the first non-European Union (EU) signatory country to sign a security and defense pact with the EU to receive assistance in strengthening and managing its borders, facilitating cooperation in cybersecurity, and combating disinformation.
A Swiss parliamentary committee rejects a ruling by the European Court of Human Rights that alleged the country violated its citizens' human rights by not doing enough to prevent climate change.

The Israeli Ministry of Communications seizes broadcasting equipment from the Associated Press and suspends their live feed of Gaza, accusing them of breaking the new media law by supplying images to Al Jazeera.
Canadian serial killer Robert Pickton is reported to be on life support after being physically attacked in a prison in Port-Cartier, Quebec.

The European Union passes the Artificial Intelligence Act, to be applied in 2026. The act imposes strict transparency obligations on AI systems, restricts governments from using real-time biometric surveillance in public spaces, and bans social scoring, predictive policing, and untargeted scraping of facial images.
A court in Saint Petersburg, Russia, sentences Anatoly Maslov, a 77-year-old hypersonic missiles expert, to 14 years in prison for state treason.
The Netherlands moves to ban international adoptions.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia captures the village of Klishchiivka in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: At least two people are killed and four are injured by Ukrainian shelling in Lysychansk, Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Sweden announces US$7 billion in military aid to Ukraine from 2024 to 2026.
Russia returns six Ukrainian children displaced by the war back to Ukraine, in a deal brokered by Qatar.
Australia and New Zealand begin evacuating their citizens from New Caledonia amid civil unrest.

context: San Pedro Garza García stage collapse
text: Ten people are killed, including a child, and 213 are injured after a temporary stage collapses in high winds at a campaign event for the Citizens' Movement party in San Pedro Garza Garcia, Nuevo León, Mexico. Later, the Nuevo León government pledges 400,000 pesos ($23,900) in compensation to families of the deceased.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine > Norway–Palestine relations, Ireland–Palestine relations, Palestine–Spain relations
text: The governments of Norway, Ireland, and Spain announce that they will recognise the State of Palestine as a sovereign state beginning on May 28, and also call for a two-state solution. In response, Israel recalls its ambassadors to these countries.

The Russian Ministry of Defence proposes to unilaterally adjust Russia's maritime border in the Baltic Sea, prompting comments of concern made by Baltic members of NATO, including Finland and Lithuania. The Ministry of Defense later retracts the proposal.
The Kyrgyz Ministry of Internal Affairs announces that ten people, including four foreigners, have been detained in connection with violent riots that occurred in Bishkek last week.
Prime Minister Succès Masra of the transitional government resigns after Mahamat Déby is elected President.
Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announces that the next general election will be held on 4 July.
Security Minister Tô Lâm is elected President by the National Assembly, two months after the resignation of Võ Văn Thưởng amid the ruling Communist Party's anti-corruption campaign.
President of the United States Joe Biden announces a student loan debt cancellation of $7.7 billion for 160,000 people.

German far-right party Alternative for Germany bans Maximilian Krah, its leading candidate in European elections, from further activities due to his comments defending members of the Schutzstaffel (SS).

Russia launches a Soyuz-2 rocket carrying the Kosmos 2576 satellite from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome launch site in Arkhangelsk Oblast. The United States Space Command accuses it of being an anti-satellite weapon capable of attacking other satellites, and is in the same orbit as a satellite operated by the National Reconnaissance Office.
The United Nations Security Council votes against a resolution introduced by Russia and China banning member states from placing weapons in outer space.

In association football, Atalanta win the UEFA Europa League over Bayer Leverkusen by a score of 3–0 in the final, ending Bayer Leverkusen's record of 51 unbeaten games. It is also Atalanta's first major trophy since 1963.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kharkiv offensive
text: Seven people are killed and at least 28 others are injured in Russian missile strikes in Liubotyn and Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimea attacks
text: At least two people are killed in a Ukrainian missile strike on Alushta, Crimea. Explosions are reported across the peninsula and Ukrainian media reports that multiple targets were hit.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russian forces captures the village of Andriivka in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 60 Palestinians are killed in Israeli attacks in Rafah, Deir al-Balah, and Gaza City, Gaza.
Pope Francis and the Dicastery for the Causes of Saints approves the canonization of Carlo Acutis, who will become the first millennial saint.
Romanian author Mircea Cărtărescu wins the International Dublin Literary Award for his novel Solenoid, translated by Sean Cotter.
Ten people are killed and 64 others are injured after an explosion of four boilers at a chemical factory in Dombivili, India.
Eleven people are killed and two others are injured in an explosion at a sugar factory in Morogoro, Tanzania.
Four people are killed and 16 others are injured when the second floor of a restaurant collapses in Palma de Mallorca, Spain.
China's People's Liberation Army begins two days of military drills around Taiwan. In response, Taiwan mobilizes its military.
Colombian President Gustavo Petro orders the opening of an embassy in Ramallah in the West Bank.

U.S. President Joe Biden announces during a state visit by Kenyan President William Ruto that he will designate Kenya a major non-NATO ally as it is expected to lead the international intervention in Haiti.
Russia removes the border markers signaling the border with Estonia on the Narva River, prompting a protest by the EU.

context: United States v. Live Nation Entertainment
text: The United States Department of Justice sues Ticketmaster and its parent company Live Nation, seeking the breakup of the company and accusing the company of creating a monopoly by eliminating competition and increasing prices.
Three people are killed and five others are injured in a shootout between two groups at a café in Istanbul, Turkey.

The United Nations General Assembly votes 84–19, with 68 abstentions, to establish July 11 as an annual day of remembrance for the Srebrenica genocide, despite receiving opposition from Serbia and Bosnian Serbs.
Sources claim that Russian President Vladimir Putin is interested in negotiating a ceasefire, which would freeze the conflict at the current frontlines.
The European Union makes a decision allowing Ukraine to use interest funds from frozen Russian bank accounts, totaling €2.5 billion ($2.7 billion) per year.
Two American Christian missionaries, one of them the daughter of a Missouri State Representative, and a Haitian pastor are killed in a gang ambush in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
Norah becomes the first film from Saudi Arabia to screen as part of the official calendar at the Cannes Film Festival.
Black Dog, a Chinese film directed by Guan Hu, wins the Un Certain Regard prize for international films at the Cannes Film Festival.
Four people are confirmed killed and many others are presumed dead in a landslide in Enga Province, Papua New Guinea.
Fourteen people are killed and three others are injured in a building fire in a densely populated area of Hanoi, Vietnam.
Dozens of people are killed across Mexico in a deadly heatwave, with temperatures as high as recorded.
Hundreds of international students from Pakistan and other Asian countries leave Kyrgyzstan following attacks by Kyrgyz nationalist mobs on student hostels in Bishkek earlier this month.
Russia arrests more than 20 people in connection with the Islamic State – Khorasan Province attack on the Crocus City Hall concert venue in Krasnogorsk, Moscow Oblast, in March.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: The International Court of Justice, in a 13–2 decision, orders Israel to stop their military offensive in Rafah.

context: United States v. Live Nation Entertainment
text: The first consumer class action lawsuit by ticket buyers is filed against Ticketmaster and Live Nation Entertainment, following the lawsuit filed by the United States Department of Justice.

Families in Uvalde, Texas, U.S., file a lawsuit against Daniel Defense and Activision Blizzard for creating the DDM4 V7 gun and promoting the weapon through the game Call of Duty, respectively. They also sue Meta Platforms for owning Instagram, which was used by the gunman.
A record number of Conservative MPs stand down ahead of the UK election.
Jeremy Corbyn is expelled from the Labour Party after confirming that he will stand as an independent candidate in the election.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war > Israeli allegations against UNRWA
text: Italy restores €35 million (US$38 million) of funding for UNRWA several months after it suspended the aid due to allegations linking UN staff to the October 7 attacks.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Four U.S. Army vessels connected to a floating pier off the Gaza Strip become disconnected and wash up on beaches, two in Israel and two in the Gaza Strip.

context: Syrian civil war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Two Hezbollah militants killed in an Israeli airstrike on a truck in Al-Qusayr, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: A Hezbollah-Syrian Army officer killed in a car bombing in Damascus.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia captures the village of Arkhanhelske in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least fourteen people are killed and 58 others are injured in Russian strikes on a hardware store and residential area in Kharkiv, Ukraine.
Anora, directed by Sean Baker, wins the Palme d'Or prize at the Cannes Film Festival.
At least 27 people, including many children, are killed in a building fire at a family entertainment venue in Rajkot, Gujarat, India.
At least five people are killed after a tornado strikes the cities of Pilot Point and Valley View in Texas, United States.
At least seven infants are killed in a fire in a baby care facility at a hospital in Shahdara, East Delhi, India.
Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announces plans to conscript young persons with an option for alternative civilian service if the Conservative Party wins the upcoming election.
Al Ain win their second Champions League title after beating the Yokohama F. Marinos by an aggregate score of 6–3 over a two-legged final.

Bayer Leverkusen win their second DFB-Pokal title after beating 1. FC Kaiserslautern by a score of 1–0 in the final at the Olympiastadion in Berlin, Germany, completing the first unbeaten double-winning season in German football.
Manchester United win their 13th FA Cup title after beating the defending champions, Manchester City, by a score of 2–1 in the final at Wembley Stadium in London, England.
Barcelona win their third Women's Champions League title after defeating Olympique Lyonnais 2–0 in the final.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive, Refugee camp airstrikes in the Israel–Hamas war > Tel al-Sultan massacre
text: Between 47 and 52 people are killed in an Israeli airstrike and subsequent fire in a tent camp for displaced civilians in Rafah in the Gaza Strip.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Insurgency in the North Gaza Strip
text: A spokesperson for Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades claim that they captured IDF soldiers in Jabalia yesterday. However, the IDF denies this claim.
The Al-Qassam Brigades fire rockets towards Tel Aviv, Israel, for the first time in four months.
Five Hezbollah militants, five civilians killed and two civilians injured in IDF strikes on Aitaroun, Naqoura, Ayta ash Shab, Hula and Yaroun in southern Lebanon.
More than twenty civilians are killed in an attack by unidentified gunmen in a village in Mopti region, Mali.

The Houthis, with assistance from the International Committee of the Red Cross, free more than 100 detainees in Sana'a, Yemen, in a "unilateral humanitarian initiative" to pardon prisoners and return them to their families.
At least three people have been confirmed dead in Armenia following flooding on the Armenia–Georgia border, with several bridges collapsing as a result of the flooding.
The International Organization for Migration estimates that more than 670 people were killed in the landslide in Enga Province, Papua New Guinea, on Friday.
The death toll from an overnight tornado outbreak in the U.S. states of Texas, Oklahoma, and Arkansas increases to 15.
Ten people are killed and 39 others are injured in a collision between a bus and three other vehicles on a highway near Mersin, Turkey.

context: France–Germany relations, List of international presidential trips made by Emmanuel Macron
text: Emmanuel Macron makes the first state visit by a President of France to Germany in 24 years.
Incumbent president Azali Assoumani is sworn in for his fourth term in office.
Gitanas Nausėda wins the Lithuanian presidential run-off with 75.57% of the vote.
Charles Leclerc wins the Monaco Grand Prix for the first time in his career, becoming the first Monégasque to win his home race in 93 years.
Hosts Czechia wins the title for the seventh time after beating Switzerland 2–0 in the final. Czechia ends their 14-year gold drought by winning it for the first time since 2010.
In auto racing, Josef Newgarden wins the Indianapolis 500 for the second consecutive year, becoming the first driver to do so since Hélio Castroneves in 2002.
In cricket, the Kolkata Knight Riders defeat the Sunrisers Hyderabad in the final of the Indian Premier League to win their third IPL title.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Prime Minister of Spain Pedro Sánchez signs a bilateral security pact with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and pledges €1 billion (US$1.1 billion) of military aid to Ukraine.
Russia captures the villages of Netailove in Donetsk Oblast and Ivanivka in Kharkiv Oblast.
An Egyptian border guard is killed in a shootout at the Rafah Border Crossing.

context: Israel–Hamas war, 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: A civilian and a PIJ member killed and nine injured in an IDF airstrike on the Salah Ghandour Hospital in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon.
Twenty-three gunmen and seven soldiers are killed during three shootouts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Yemen's Houthi militia says that they attacked three merchant ships and two destroyers from the United States Navy.
Papua New Guinea asks for international help following the landslide in Enga Province three days ago, and reports that more than 2,000 people were buried alive and are now presumed deceased.
The death toll from a tornado outbreak in the U.S. states of Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma, and Arkansas on Saturday and Sunday increases to 21.
A teenager is killed and six other people are injured in a shooting in downtown Lansing, Michigan, United States.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive, Refugee camp airstrikes in the Israel–Hamas war > May 2024 Al-Mawasi refugee camp attack
text: At least 21 people are killed and 64 others are injured in a Israeli attack on a tent camp in al-Mawasi, Rafah Governorate.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive, Refugee camp airstrikes in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Israeli tanks reach central Rafah for the first time with heavy clashes being reported.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The U.S. removes the Gaza floating pier from the Gaza Strip for repair after its flotilla was damaged in bad weather.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russian guided bombs hit a block of apartments in Toretsk, Donetsk Oblast, killing at least two civilians and injuring six others.
A Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier takes on water after being hit by three missiles off the coast of Yemen.
Seventeen people are killed and six others are missing after a stone quarry collapses due to strong winds in Aizawl, Mizoram, India.
One person is killed and seven others are injured in a natural gas explosion at an apartment building in Youngstown, Ohio, U.S.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine > Norway–Palestine relations, Ireland–Palestine relations, Palestine–Spain relations
text: The governments of Norway, Ireland, and Spain officially recognise the State of Palestine, after declaring their intention to do so on May 22.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine > Denmark–Palestine relations
text: The Parliament of Denmark rejects a proposal to recognise a Palestinian state.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war protests
text: Pro-Palestinian protestors in Mexico set fire to the Israeli embassy in Mexico City.
The Senate of Colombia approves a resolution banning Spanish-style bullfighting in the country.
Former FTX co-CEO Ryan Salame is sentenced to more than seven years in prison and fined more than $11 million for fraud and criminal conspiracy.
A Polish Border Guard soldier is seriously injured in an incident among a surge in migrants trying to cross the EU border from Belarus.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: Mexico announces it will intervene in support of South Africa in South Africa's genocide case against Israel.
The Georgian parliament overrides a presidential veto of the foreign agents law, thereby requiring president Salome Zourabichvili to endorse the bill within five days.

The Kuomintang and Taiwan People's Party pass amendments granting the Legislative Yuan greater powers to oversee the executive and to question officials and citizens, despite claims that these amendments violate civil liberties and could reduce the powers of president Lai Ching-te of the Democratic Progressive Party.
Garry Conille is named the new Prime Minister of Haiti by the Transitional Presidential Council.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations, Ukraine–NATO relations
text: Sweden announces a package of $1.23 billion in military aid to Ukraine, the largest given by Sweden so far.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations, Ukraine–NATO relations
text: France and Germany announce that French and German weapons sent to Ukraine, including long-range missiles, are permitted to target bases inside Russia.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations, Ukraine–NATO relations
text: The Polish Defence Ministry says it has given Ukraine permission to use Polish-supplied weapons to strike targets inside Russian territory.
Israel says that it has taken full control of the Egypt–Gaza border after capturing the Philadelphi Corridor.
Two Israeli soldiers who were seriously wounded by a vehicle-ramming attack the day before succumb to their injuries.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict, Syrian civil war
text: One civilian, three Hezbollah members and ten injured in an IDF airstrike Baniyas and Homs, Syria.
The town of Grindavík, Iceland, and the nearby Blue Lagoon are evacuated due to volcanic activity.
At least 28 people are killed when a bus falls into a ravine in Washuk District, Balochistan, Pakistan.
The India Meteorological Department records a record-high temperature of in Delhi, resulting in one death.
Brazil recalls its ambassador to Israel amid an ongoing diplomatic crisis between the two countries.

Amnesty International says that the number of executions recorded globally in 2023 was the highest since 2015 and up more than 30% from 2022, with Iran carrying out 74% of the global total. The figures exclude China, because execution numbers are considered a state secret.
Four people are injured in a mass shooting in Dalston, London, UK.
Citizens of Madagascar vote for members of the National Assembly.
South Africans vote for members of the National Assembly and provincial legislatures.
Vanuatuans hold the first national constitutional referendum to vote on amendments related to party switching.

In association football, Olympiacos win their first UEFA Europa Conference League title after defeating Fiorentina by a score of 1–0 in the final, becoming the first Greek team to win a major European club trophy.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations > 2024 Kharkiv offensive
text: The United States gives Ukraine permission to strike Russian territory near Kharkiv Oblast with U.S.-supplied weapons, but not with long-range missiles.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations > 2024 Kharkiv offensive
text: Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen says Denmark has approved Ukrainian airstrikes on Russian territory using Danish-supplied F-16 jets.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The Israeli military lifts a ban on the sale of food to the Gaza Strip from Israel and the West Bank.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive, Siege of Gaza City, Refugee camp airstrikes in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Israeli airstrikes kill twelve Palestinian civilians in Rafah and one at the al-Shati camp near Gaza City.
The United States Navy and the Royal Navy strike thirteen Houthi locations across Yemen, damaging underground facilities and vessels, killing at least two people and wounding ten.

context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
text: North Korea launches a series of short-range ballistic missiles from Pyongyang toward the Sea of Japan.
A bus falls into a gorge in Jammu division, India, killing 21 people travelling to a pilgrimage site in Reasi district.
A person is killed after falling into a running aircraft engine of a departing plane at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport in the Netherlands.
The third human case of H5N1 bird flu in the United States is found in a dairy worker in Michigan.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine
text: Slovenia's ruling cabinet approves a motion to recognize Palestine as an independent nation and sends the motion to the National Assembly for adoption.
The Spanish parliament votes to pass a bill granting amnesty to hundreds of Catalan secessionists involved in the Catalan declaration of independence from 2011 to 2017.

context: Prosecution of Donald Trump in New York
text: Former President of the United States Donald Trump is found guilty by a jury on all 34 felony counts relating to falsifying business records, becoming the first U.S. president to be convicted of a crime.
Hong Kong convicts fourteen activists and politicians guilty of subversion under its national security law.

The United States Department of Labor files a lawsuit against Hyundai Motors over illegal use of child labor at the company's automobile factory in Montgomery, Alabama, amid a nationwide increase in child labor in the U.S.
Four people, including a police officer, are killed in a mass shooting in Minneapolis, Minnesota, U.S.
Footballer Gerard Piqué is placed under official investigation for his alleged involvement in illegal payments in the relocation of the Supercopa de España from Spain to Saudi Arabia.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: Police dismantle and remove the student pro-Palestinian encampment at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan, U.S.
OpenAI removes online influence operations based in Russia, China, Iran, and Israel, due to the usage of AI by these operations to generate propaganda and fake content.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine launches missile and drone strikes across Krasnodar Krai, Russia, injuring two people and damaging several oil refineries.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least three people are killed and 16 others are injured when Russian missiles hit civilian infrastructure in Kharkiv.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Treatment of prisoners of war in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine and Russia announce their first exchange of prisoners of war in nearly four months, with 150 people freed following negotiations mediated by the United Arab Emirates.

context: Red Sea crisis > 30 May 2024 Yemen strikes
text: The death toll from yesterday's U.S. Navy and British Navy airstrikes in Yemen increases to 16 with 35 others injured.

context: Red Sea crisis > 30 May 2024 Yemen strikes
text: The Houthi Supreme Political Council states that it launched an attack on the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, although American officials deny this claim.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: Seven soldiers are killed and 28 others are injured in an offensive by the Rapid Support Forces near Khartoum, Sudan.
A man with a knife stabs several people at an anti-Muslim rally in Mannheim, Baden-Württemberg, Germany including two policemen, including one in the neck, before being injured by a bullet.
A medic is killed and another is injured in an Israeli airstrike against an ambulance in Naqoura, Lebanon.
France bans Israeli defense firms from exhibiting at the Eurosatory weapons expo convention.

At the 2024 Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, U.S. Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin meets with Chinese Minister of National Defense Dong Jun, with the two agreeing to resume military-to-military communication between the two countries.
Former First Lady of Zambia Esther Lungu is arrested on fraud charges.
Canadian serial killer Robert Pickton dies in prison after being attacked by another inmate earlier this month.
French security services arrest a Chechen teenager suspected of plotting a islamist-inspired ambush on a football game during the Summer Olympics.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > Israel–Hamas war protests in the United States
text: Pro-Palestinian protesters occupy parts of the Brooklyn Museum in New York City, New York, U.S.
Five people and a Hezbollah militant killed and five injured in IDF strikes on Aadloun and Ain Qana in southern Lebanon.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher > Kutum Hospital airstrike
text: The Sudanese Armed Forces bomb a hospital in Kutum, Sudan, injuring dozens of people.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher
text: Around eleven civilians are killed and 42 others are injured in large clashes between the Rapid Support Forces, the Sudanese Armed Forces, and various rebel militia groups in El Fasher, Sudan.
Sudan’s Ambassador to Russia confirms willingness of his country to allow construction of a Russian naval base on the Red Sea.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, injuring at least four people and damaging critical infrastructure, including energy facilities. Ukraine says that it shot down 35 of 53 missiles and 46 of 47 drones.
A boat carrying 25 people capsizes in eastern Afghanistan, killing 20 of them.
At least 33 Indian election polling staff die from heatstroke in a heatwave across the country.
A court run by the Houthis in Yemen sentences 44 people to death on charges of collaborating with the Saudi coalition.
A jury in Idaho, United States, sentences Chad Daybell to death for the murders of his ex-wife and two of his wife's children.

Ticketmaster and parent company Live Nation submit an SEC filing acknowledging a data breach of customer information potentially affecting 560 million users. Banco Santander and cloud provider Snowflake Inc. are also believed to have been affected by the same data breach.
Icelanders vote for the President of Iceland. Incumbent president Guðni Th. Jóhannesson had previously announced that he would not be seeking a third term.
Halla Tómasdóttir is elected as the President of Iceland with the plurality of the votes at 34.2%. Her opposition Katrín Jakobsdóttir concedes the election with 25.2%.
The final phase of the general election in India is held, with the ruling National Democratic Alliance projected to win a majority. Results will be announced on June 4.
In association football, Real Madrid win a record 15th Champions League title after defeating Borussia Dortmund 2–0 in the final at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher
text: The Ministry of Health of North Darfur reports that there has been 82 deaths and hundreds of injuries due to clashes in El Fasher over the last two days.

context: Sudanese civil war > Darfur campaign > Battle of El Fasher
text: UNICEF reports that more than 270,000 people, including more than 130,000 children, are at risk following fighting at the Golo Reservoir in El Fasher, North Darfur, Sudan.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russia–NATO relations, Russia–United States relations
text: Russia accuses NATO and the United States of "provoking a new level of tension" after some allies agreed to let Ukraine's military use Western-supplied weapons to strike targets inside Russia.

context: Syrian civil war > Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war
text: Israeli airstrikes in the Aleppo region kill 17 Iranian-backed militia members, including two Iranian advisors, and three Hezbollah members.
A firefighter is killed and thousands of people are evacuated after heavy rains cause flooding in southern Germany, particularly in Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war, Israel–Maldives relations
text: The Maldives announces a ban on Israeli passport holders from entering the country.
A mass shooting in Akron, Ohio, kills a 27-year-old man and wounds 24 people.
Mexicans elect a new president and legislature, eight governors, the mayor of Mexico City, and around 20,000 other positions in federal and local elections.
Claudia Sheinbaum wins the presidential election. She will begin her term as Mexico's first female president on October 1.

Former president of Iran Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announces that he intends to run again following the death of Ebrahim Raisi. Ahmadinejad has been rejected from running in the two previous presidential elections.
China's Chang'e 6 lunar exploration mission to collect moon rock successfully lands on the far side of the Moon.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict, Syrian civil war
text: Three Hezbollah members killed in Israeli airstrikes on Naqoura and Kauthariyet El Rez in southern Lebanon.[https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1415919/serial-fires-in-southern-lebanon-following-israeli-strikes-day-241-of-the-gaza-war.html [(L'Orient le Jour)]

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict, Syrian civil war
text: 16 Iranian-supported militia members killed in an IDF airstrike on a copper plant near Aleppo, Syria.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict, Syrian civil war
text: Hezbollah fires drone attacks at IDF center station in the Galilee and in Metula.
The Rapid Support Forces announce the establishment of a civil administration in the state of South Darfur, which they fully control.
A Syrian man is arrested after throwing a Molotov cocktail at the Israeli embassy in Bucharest, Romania and attempting to self-immolate.
The value of GameStop shares increases by 21% after Keith Gill posts a $116 million investment on Reddit.
More than 211 people are killed and nearly 25,000 others suffer from heatstroke amid a severe heat wave in India.
The Kīlauea volcano in Hawaii, United States, erupts for the first time in nine months.
At least 11 people are killed by two tornadoes in the South African province of KwaZulu-Natal.

context: Afghanistan–Kazakhstan relations, International relations with the Taliban
text: Kazakhstan removes the Taliban from its list of terrorist organizations.
The Islamabad High Court overturns former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan's charges of leaking national security secrets.
The Chinese Ministry of State Security arrests and charges a couple for allegedly spying for Britain's MI6 agency.
Chairperson of the Parliament of Georgia Shalva Papuashvili signs the foreign agent bill into law amid mass protests and warnings from Western countries against signing the bill.
Spanish and French farmers block roads on highways through the Pyrenees mountains in protest against trade with non-European Union member states.
Nigel Farage appoints himself leader of Reform UK and announces that he will run as a candidate for the party in the upcoming UK general election in Clacton.

Major Nigerian unions Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress begin an indefinite general strike, causing closures of schools, public offices, and airports, as well as a shutdown of the national power grid amid a cost-of-living crisis and record low minimum wages in Nigeria.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov warns that French military instructors will be "legitimate targets" if they are deployed to Ukraine.
The Kanlaon volcano in central Philippines erupts, causing evacuations and a suspension of activities in the city of Canlaon.
A controversy erupts due to the sudden declaration of the NEET-UG results 10 days earlier than the originally scheduled date amid allegations of irregularities and paper leaks..
The alliance of parties led by Narendra Modi reaches the 272 seats threshold needed to form a government, but Modi's BJP party loses its outright parliamentary majority.

The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) suspend the nationwide general strike, pending talks with the federal government of Nigeria about the raising of the country's minimum wage.

context: International recognition of the State of Palestine
text: Slovenia's parliament approves a motion to recognize a Palestinian state.

US President Joe Biden enacts an executive order to temporarily suspend asylum claims processing at the Mexico–United States border when the seven-day average of claims exceeds 2,500 per day. Amnesty International criticizes the executive order, accusing Biden of "setting a dangerous international precedent".
The State Council of South Korea suspends the 2018 Panmunjom Declaration due to border tensions over balloons sent across the border by North Korea.
A local Mannheim politician is injured by a stabbing, five days after the May 31 attack in the German city.
The China National Space Administration's Chang'e 6 spacecraft lifts off from the surface of the far side of the Moon carrying samples of lunar soil and rocks back to Earth.

The National Health Service declares a "critical incident" after several hospitals in London, including King's College Hospital, say they have cancelled appointments and turned away patients after a cyberattack on their Synnovis IT systems.
Venezuelan infielder Tucupita Marcano is permanently banned from Major League Baseball and Minor League Baseball for betting on Pittsburgh Pirates games while being a member of the team.

context: Sudanese civil war > Wad Al-Noora massacre
text: The Rapid Support Forces storm the village of Wad Al-Noora in Gezira State, Sudan, and massacre nearly 100 villagers.

context: 2021–2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: At least 16 people are killed in Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The local government believes the Allied Democratic Forces are responsible.
A Syrian man fires several shots at the U.S. Embassy in Beirut, Lebanon, and is shot by security forces.
Hezbollah strikes an Iron Dome battery in Ramot Naftali, Israel.

The United States and South Korea participate in the first precision guided bombing drill in 7 years over the Korean Peninsula, as tensions rise after North Korea sends trash-filled balloons into South Korea.
Four Slovaks and Ukrainians are killed and more than 20 others are injured when a passenger train collides with a freight train in Pardubice, Czech Republic.
A panel of the United States Food and Drug Administration rejects MDMA-assisted psychotherapy as a treatment for PTSD.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov announces that Russia will send additional military supplies and instructors to Burkina Faso to help the country increase its defense capabilities.

US President Joe Biden institutes a broad asylum ban on migrants illegally crossing the Mexico–United States border, with actions to deport or turn people back to Mexico, with exceptions for unaccompanied children, people with serious medical or safety threats, and victims of trafficking.

A court in Florence, Italy, convicts American journalist Amanda Knox and sentences her to a three-year imprisonment over her accusations related to the murder of Meredith Kercher in Perugia in 2007. The sentence will count as time already served.

context: Israel–Hamas war protests > Israel–Hamas war protests in Israel
text: Thousands of Israeli ultranationalists march through East Jerusalem on Jerusalem Day, with some chanting anti-Arab slogans.

Boeing's Starliner capsule launches its first astronaut-crewed flight into space to the International Space Station after several delays at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, United States.
Russian cosmonaut Oleg Kononenko becomes the first human to spend 1,000 days in outer space.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Attacks on schools during the Israeli invasion of Gaza
text: At least 40 Palestinians, including fourteen children, are killed and more than 70 injured after an Israeli airstrike on a United Nations school that was sheltering refugees in central Gaza.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Three Palestinians are killed and several others are injured in an Israel Defense Forces raid on Jenin in the West Bank.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: President of France Emmanuel Macron announces that the country will send Dassault Mirage 2000-5 fighter aircraft to Ukraine and train its pilots by the end of 2024.
The Houthis and the Islamic Resistance in Iraq claim to have launched two joint military attacks against ships at the Port of Haifa in Israel. However, Israel denies the claims.
A blizzard in the Himalaya mountains of Uttarakhand, India, kills nine Indian trekkers.
At least six people, including mostly children, drown after a school bus falls into the Orontes River near Darkush, Syria.
Six fishermen are killed and one is critically injured after a boat's engine exploded and caught the wooden hull on fire off the coast of Naga in the Philippines.
One person is killed and more than 100 others are injured after two trams collide in Kemerovo, Russia.
A child is killed and at least thirteen other people are injured by tornadoes in the U.S. states of Michigan, Maryland, and Ohio.
A French citizen is detained in Moscow, Russia, under suspicion of collecting military information.

The United States Department of State sanctions several Georgian Dream politicians with travel bans for passing the "Law on Transparency of Foreign Influence", threatening further penalties if Georgia continues "anti-democratic activity".
The Biden administration imposes sanctions on the Lions' Den militant group based in Nablus in the West Bank, for committing attacks in the West Bank since October 2022.
A Polish border guard soldier dies after being stabbed by a migrant trying to cross the EU border from Belarus.
Elections to the European Parliament begin and will continue until June 9, with the Netherlands and Estonia voting today.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: Spain applies to join South Africa's case at the International Court of Justice accusing Israel of genocide.

SpaceX launches Starship's Integrated Flight Test 4, successfully guiding both the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage to soft water landings in the Gulf of Mexico and the Indian Ocean, respectively.
The Oklahoma Sooners win the 2024 Women's College World Series in softball with the first-ever four-peat.

context: Israel–Hamas war > International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war
text: United Nations advisors announce that it intends to add the Israeli military, Hamas, and Palestinian Islamic Jihad to their list of countries and armed groups that harm children in their upcoming "Children and Armed Conflict" report.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United States reinstalls the temporary Gaza floating pier after weather-related damage had to be repaired.

context: Yemeni civil war > Red Sea crisis
text: The Houthis detain 11 Yemeni employees of United Nations agencies and others working for aid groups.
According to a Houthi-run television station, the United States and the United Kingdom carry out six airstrikes on Hodeida International Airport, the Port of Salif, and Al-Thawrah, Yemen.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: At least 40 people are killed and 50 others are injured in an attack by the Rapid Support Forces in Omdurman, Sudan.
A glass railing collapses outside the overcrowded RICH nightclub in Mexico, causing several concertgoers to fall three stories, killing two and injuring 15.
A boat carrying over 171 people sank in the Mediterranean Sea off Libya, killing at least 11 people. 160 others were rescued.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen is shoved by a man, who has since been arrested, in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Elections to the European Parliament continues, with Ireland and the Czech Republic voting today.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis > 2024 Nuseirat rescue operation
text: The Israel Defence Forces airstrikes and raids the Nuseirat refugee camp in Deir al-Balah Governorate in Gaza, rescuing four hostages kidnapped by Hamas during the Re'im music festival massacre on October 7, including Noa Argamani.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis > 2024 Nuseirat rescue operation
text: Many Palestinians, including women and children, are killed and injured during the raid, with Palestinian officials claiming 236 killed and 400 wounded, while Israeli sources claim under 100 casualties. It is unknown how many casualties were civilians and how many were militants.

context: Somali Civil War > Somali civil war (2009–present) > 2024 El Dher attack
text: Al-Shabaab attacked four military bases and overran the town of Dherka Derka for several hours, killing many soldiers of the Somali National Army. The militants were eventually defeated by a U.S.-assisted airstrike.

context: 2021–2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: At least 41 people are killed in an overnight attack in Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Local leaders suspect the Allied Democratic Forces are responsible for the attack.

context: Economic impact of the Israel–Hamas war, Colombia–Israel relations
text: Colombia announces the suspension of coal exports to Israel stating that it will resume exports after Israel complies with the International Court of Justice provisional measure of protection and stops its genocide in Gaza.
Doctors Without Borders recovers 11 bodies and rescues dozens of migrants off the coast of Libya.
Police in Vietnam arrest journalist Huy Đức and lawyer Tran Dinh Trien over Facebook posts.
Elections to the European Parliament continue, with Slovakia, Italy, the Czech Republic, Latvia, and Malta voting today.
In tennis, Iga Świątek wins the Women's singles title at the French Open after defeating Jasmine Paolini, becoming the third woman to win three consecutive titles in the Open Era.

context: Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir > 2024 Reasi attack
text: Nine people are killed and 41 others are injured near Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir, India, when a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims falls into a ravine after being shot at.

context: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa > 2024 Lakki Marwat bombing
text: An IED kills seven Pakistan Army personnel in Lakki Marwat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Two people are killed in Israeli airstrikes near Aitaroun, Lebanon, according to the National News Agency.

President Bernardo Arévalo announced that the remains of Guatemalan writer and 1967 Nobel Prize winner for Literature, Miguel Ángel Asturias, would be repatriated to Guatemala. Asturias is buried in the Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris, France.
At least twenty-two people are killed and 48 injured after a truck collided with a bus in Sofala, Mozambique.

South Korea announces that it will resume loudspeaker broadcasts over the Korean Demilitarized Zone for the first time since 2018 in response to North Korea sending hundreds of balloons carrying garbage across the border.
Slovenian voters approve the use of cannabis for medicinal and recreational use in adults.

War Cabinet Minister Benny Gantz resigns after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to present a post-war plan for Gaza by Gantz's previously announced June 8 deadline. Minister Gadi Eisenkot also resigns.
Belgians vote for the 150 members of the Chamber of Representatives as well as for regional representatives and members of the European Parliament.
Bulgarians vote for the sixth time in three years to elect the 240 members of the parliament.
The last day of the European Parliament elections takes place, with voting occurring in 20 countries.

Following major losses for French President Emmanuel Macron's Renaissance party in the European Parliament elections, Macron dissolves the National Assembly and calls snap elections for June 30 and July 7.
Narendra Modi is sworn in for his third term as Prime Minister of India.
