Mexico's ruling party Morena and its coalition allies win a supermajority in the Chamber of Deputies but not in the Senate, falling short of the two-thirds majority needed to change the Constitution.
Sammarinese elect the members of the Grand and General Council.
Parliamentary elections are held in the Georgian breakaway region of South Ossetia.
Voters in Switzerland reject limits on healthcare spending and an initiative against compulsory vaccination, while approving the initiative of a new law on electricity.
In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz wins the Men's singles title at the French Open after defeating Alexander Zverev in the final, earning his third Grand Slam title.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimea attacks
text: Ukraine's military says that its missile strikes near Yevpatoriya and Chornomorske in Russian-occupied Crimea damaged three Russian air defense systems.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian Defence Ministry says that its forces have recaptured the village of Staromaiorske in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States lifts a ban on sending U.S. weaponry to Ukraine's Azov Brigade.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of El Fasher
text: The last remaining operational hospital in Al-Fashir, North Darfur, closes down after being stormed and looted by the Rapid Support Forces, according to Médecins Sans Frontières.
At least 50 people are killed and an unknown number are kidnapped, including women and children, when gunmen attack the village of Yargoje in Katsina State, Nigeria.
At least 55 people are killed and 155 others are injured in fighting between the Dir and Marehan clans in central Somalia.
It is reported that wildfires have burned around of tropical wetland in Brazil's Pantanal so far this year, a 935% increase in the number of fires that occurred in the same period last year.
An aircraft carrying Malawian Vice-President Saulos Chilima and nine others is reported missing while flying from Lilongwe to Mzuzu.
Forty-nine migrants, mostly from Ethiopia and Somalia, are killed and 140 are missing after their boat capsizes off the coast of Yemen.
Three people are killed in floods and landslides in Hà Giang province, Vietnam.

Poland announces a "no-go zone" in the Białowieża Forest in order to prevent migrants from crossing the border from Belarus. In response, concerns are raised about the potential impact on tourism during the summer.

context: Doe v. Chiquita Brands International, Right-wing paramilitarism in Colombia
text: After 17 years of litigation, Chiquita Brands International is found liable by a jury in United States Federal Court of financing the far-right paramilitary death squad United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia in the Antioquia and Magdalena Departments of Colombia.

Four American instructors from Cornell College in Iowa, United States, and one Chinese passerby are wounded in a stabbing attack at a park in Jilin City, China. The perpetrator is arrested a day later.
A Spanish court sentences three men to eight months in prison for racist chants directed towards Brazilian football player Vinícius Júnior.
The United States Consulate General in Sydney, Australia, is vandalized by a pro-Palestinian activist.

context: Israel–Hamas war > United Nations Security Council Resolution 2735
text: The United Nations Security Council votes 14–0, with Russia abstaining, to back the ceasefire proposal outlined by US President Joe Biden.

context: 2024 Belgian federal election > 2024 Belgian government formation
text: Following resignation of De Croo, government formation talks begin.
The New Flemish Alliance win the highest percent of votes in the federal election, followed by Vlaams Belang and the Reformist Movement.
Belgian Prime Minister Alexander De Croo resigns after his party Open Flemish Liberals and Democrats loses to centre-right and conservative parties.
Several large protests are held in Yerevan, Armenia, calling for Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to resign due to Armenia ceding territory to Azerbaijan in the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
No party attains a majority in the Bulgarian National Assembly, with GERB attaining a plurality of seats.
Apple holds its 2024 Worldwide Developers Conference in Cupertino, California, United States, unveiling its Apple Intelligence, iOS 18, iPadOS 18, MacOS Sequoia, and more.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Ukraine–European Union relations, Ukraine–United States relations
text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announces that the European Union will give Ukraine €3.4 billion (USD$3.6 billion) throughout the summer from Russian frozen assets revenue.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Ukraine–European Union relations, Ukraine–United States relations
text: The United States approves a move to send a second Patriot missile system to Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarus–Russia relations
text: Russia and Belarus begin the second stage of their tactical nuclear weapons drills.
Russia says that it has captured the villages of Tymkivka in Kharkiv Oblast and Miasozharivka in Luhansk Oblast.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken announces more than $400 million in new humanitarian aid for Palestinians in Gaza.
Iraqi security forces in cooperation with U.S.-led coalition forces kill Abu Zainab, a senior member of Islamic State in Raqqa, Syria.
Senior Hezbollah commander Taleb Abdallah and three other militants are killed in an Israeli strike on a control center in Jwaya, southern Lebanon.

Hezbollah launches 90 rockets at IDF targets of a factory, center station in Ein Zeitim and Ami'ad and an airforce surveillance station in Meron, 70 at the Mount Meron area, ten more at Zar'it, and launching 145 more.

South Korea says that its forces fired warning shots at North Korean soldiers who briefly crossed the demarcation line in the Korean Demilitarized Zone. South Korean authorities state that they believe the intrusion, which occurred in a densely forested area, was accidental.

The International Organization for Migration says that more than 10 million people have now been internally displaced by the war in Sudan, including around a third of the population of the capital Khartoum, making it the world's worst displacement crisis.
The World Bank approves $1 billion for the construction of the Dasu Dam in northwest Pakistan.
Production begins at Senegal's first offshore oil project at the Sangomar oil fields which aims to produce 100,000 barrels of oil per day.
The wreckage of an aircraft which went missing yesterday in Malawi amid bad weather is found. All ten people on board, including the country's Vice-President Saulos Chilima, are confirmed dead.

Floods hit the Spanish island of Majorca, affecting the third busiest airport in Europe. ([https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/06/11/torrential-rain-floods-majorca-airport-spain/ The Telegraph])
A Russian Aerospace Forces Sukhoi Su-34 aircraft crashes during a routine training exercise in North Ossetia–Alania, Russia, killing both crew onboard.

context: Russia–Sri Lanka relations, Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Sri Lanka's foreign ministry says that the country has received assurances from Russia that it would stop recruiting Sri Lankan citizens to fight in Ukraine.
Hunter Biden, son of U.S. President Joe Biden, is convicted in a federal court in Delaware on three felony counts of possession of a firearm while under the influence of narcotics.
A man self-immolates at St. Mark's Square in Zagreb, Croatia, and later dies in hospital.
Riots occur in Tiaret, Algeria, in opposition to water rationing as a government response to prolonged droughts.
Eight individuals from Tajikistan with suspected ties to Islamic State are arrested across several United States cities for border immigration violations.
Austria announces that parliamentary elections will be held on September 29.
France's left-wing political parties establish an electoral alliance, the New Popular Front, ahead of the French parliamentary elections.
John Moran becomes the first directly-elected mayor in the Republic of Ireland.
Former South African president Jacob Zuma and his party uMkhonto weSizwe appeal to the Constitutional Court to block the newly elected parliament from sitting, citing electoral fraud.
Hunger strikes occur in at least 16 prisons in Venezuela to protest against poor living conditions such as overcrowding as well as delays in the reviews of the prisoners' judicial processes.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India–Russia relations
text: Two Indians recruited by the Russian army are killed in Ukraine with the Indian foreign ministry urging Moscow to quickly return all Indian nationals who are serving in the Russian army.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kryvyi Rih strikes
text: Nine people are killed and 26 others are injured in a Russian airstrike on Kryvyi Rih.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv strikes
text: Russia launches a wave of cruise missiles and drone attacks at Kyiv. Ukraine claims to have intercepted all missiles and drones, although debris did cause some damage to infrastructure.

Israel kills three Hezbollah fighters and Taleb Abdullah, a senior commander, in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah retaliates by launching over 250 rockets towards northern Israel, the most the group has sent in the war.

context: Impact of war on children, Sudanese civil war
text: The United Nations adds the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces to its list of offenders for violating children's rights.
Russian soldiers complete their withdrawal from the Nagorno-Karabakh region of Azerbaijan.
The Houthis strike and sink the Greek-owned, Liberian-flagged cargo ship Tutor with an unmanned surface vehicle.
Sixteen Syrian soldiers, including an officer, are killed in Homs Governorate in a minefield laid by Islamic State militants and in an attack by the Islamic State.
The Greek Ministry of Culture announces the discovery of a large Bronze Age-era Minoan architectural construction used between 2000–1700 BC at the construction site of the Kasteli Airport in Crete.

The Royal Canadian Geographical Society announces that a Canadian-led team has located the wreckage of Quest, the polar exploration ship of the Shackleton–Rowett Expedition off the coast of Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada.

context: International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Moscow Exchange suspends all trading in US dollars and euros in response to increased sanctions by the European Union and the United States.
50 people are killed and 56 are injured in a fire at a building housing foreign workers in Mangaf, Kuwait.
At least 86 people are killed after a boat carrying 271 passengers capsizes on a river near Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Several people are injured and 25 shops are destroyed in a fire in Manama Souq, Bahrain.
The National Weather Service issues a rare Flash Flood Emergency in southern Florida, United States, for life-threatening flooding conditions only expected once every 500 to 1,000 years.
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announces that Armenia will withdraw from the Collective Security Treaty Organization amid deteriorating relations with Russia.
The United States imposes sanctions on Evghenia Guțul, the pro-Russian governor of Moldova's Gagauzia region.
The United States expands secondary sanctions on foreign financial institutions that conducted business with more than 4,500 US-sanctioned Russian entities.

context: Killing of Peter R. de Vries
text: A court in the Netherlands sentences three men to up to 28 years in prison for the murder of reporter Peter R. de Vries in 2021, and three other men to 14 years for aiding in the murder.

The American Civil Liberties Union files a lawsuit in federal court against the Biden administration for US President Joe Biden's new presidential directive which limits migrants seeking asylum at the Mexico–United States border.
The Oklahoma Supreme Court dismisses a lawsuit by the last Tulsa race massacre survivors seeking reparations.

A man in Hudson, Florida, United States fatally shoots a family of four with a 9 mm gun before burning their bodies in a fire pit. The perpetrator was identified as 25-year-old Rory John Graeme Atwood.

context: Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines
text: The Argentine Senate passes an extensive economic reform bill package proposed by President Javier Milei, decided by a 36–36 vote, with the tie broken by Vice President Victoria Villarruel.

context: Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines > 2024 Argentina protests
text: Anti-government protestors clash with police outside the National Congress Palace in Buenos Aires, Argentina, after the reform bill's passing.
Dozens of demonstrators are injured in Yerevan, Armenia, after police fire stun grenades at an anti-government rally outside the National Assembly Building.
French president Emmanuel Macron suspends electoral reforms in New Caledonia amid riots in the territory.
South Africa's Inkatha Freedom Party says that it will join a unity government with the African National Congress and the Democratic Alliance.
U.S. attorney general Merrick Garland is found in contempt by the United States House of Representatives for refusing to comply with subpoenas.
The French Republicans party votes unanimously to remove party leader Éric Ciotti for attempting to form an electoral alliance with Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally party.
Armenia signs the Artemis Accords at a NASA Headquarters ceremony, becoming the 43rd country to join the American-led effort to explore the Moon.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Leaders at the G7 summit agree to loan Ukraine US$50 billion and use interest from Russia's frozen central bank assets as collateral for the loan.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: U.S. President Joe Biden and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sign a ten-year security agreement to strengthen Ukraine's defensive capabilities.
Hezbollah launches more than 200 rockets at northern Israel. In response, Israeli artillery strikes targets in Yaroun, Hanine, and Yater in southern Lebanon.
The Israel Defense Forces launch incendiary devices across the Lebanese border with a trebuchet in order to prevent infiltration from the border.
Suspected Islamist rebels kill more than 20 people in Mayikengo, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Six Nigerien soldiers are killed in an attack on the Niger–Benin Oil Pipeline in Dosso region, Niger.

A Russian warship and a nuclear-powered submarine conduct military drills in the Caribbean Sea simulating a missile strike on enemy ships after passing near the coast of Florida in order to reach Havana, Cuba.
The general secretary of the miners' confederation in Mali announces that at least 22 miners have died in Kalana, Mali, following the collapse of a mine tunnel five days ago.
A heatwave forces Greek authorities to close the Acropolis for visits during the afternoon.

context: Sudanese civil war > United Nations Security Council Resolution 2736
text: The United Nations Security Council votes 14–0, with Russia abstaining, to demand that the Rapid Support Forces stop their siege of Al-Fashir, Sudan, and that all parties maintain humanitarian access and protection for civilians under International Humanitarian Law.

context: FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine
text: The Supreme Court of the United States rules against efforts to restrict access to the abortion pill mifepristone, due to a lack of standing by the plaintiffs.
The European Court of Justice fines Hungary €200 million and imposes a daily €1 million penalty for failing to follow the European Union's asylum laws and for illegally deporting migrants.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United Nations suspends humanitarian aid delivery at the U.S. military-constructed Gaza floating pier pending investigations on whether the pier was used in the Israeli raid on the Nuseirat refugee camp and on the security of humanitarian workers at the pier.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United States military plans to temporarily dismantle the Gaza floating pier and move it to Israel following predictions of rough seas, suspending humanitarian aid shipments at the pier for the third time in the past month.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United States State Department officially adds the Israeli group Tsav 9 to its list of sanctioned entities for impeding the delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Germany vetoes a European Union sanction package that would prevent EU members from re-exporting Russian liquefied natural gas from EU ports and prevent EU companies from selling sanctioned products to Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin announces that he is ready for a ceasefire if Ukraine withdraws from Russian-claimed territories, including liberated areas, and stops its accession to NATO. However, Ukraine rejects the offer.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of El Fasher
text: The Sudanese Armed Forces kill Ali Yaqoub Gibril, a commander of the Rapid Support Forces in Darfur, Sudan.
The United States military launches attacks on and destroys seven Houthi radar stations in Yemen in retaliation after a merchant sailor went missing following Houthi strikes on ships in the Red Sea.
At least six people are killed and more than 1,000 tourists are stranded in heavy rains and landslides across the state of Sikkim, India.

Reuters releases a report that alleges that the United States military conducted a clandestine online campaign, ordered by the Trump administration in 2020 and ended by the Biden administration in 2021, to discredit the CoronaVac vaccine of China-based manufacturer Sinovac Biotech in the Philippines and other developing countries.
The World Health Organization officially confirms a human Influenza A virus subtype H9N2 case in a child in West Bengal state, India.

The Netherlands-flagged dredger Vox Maxima collides with the stationary bunker vessel Marine Honour in Pasir Panjang Terminal, Singapore, causing an oil spill that spreads across several Southern Islands alongside the beaches in East Coast Park. Sentosa announce a temporary suspension of any water activities while their beaches remain open.
The Niger State Security Court retracts the immunity of deposed president Mohamed Bazoum, thereby allowing Bazoum to be prosecuted for high treason and undermining national security.
Kyrgyzstan arrests 15 alleged Islamic State – Khorasan Province supporters in Bishkek.

The United States Department of State designates the far-right Nordic Resistance Movement as a terrorist organization. Three of its leaders are subsequently designated as Specially Designated Global Terrorists.
The Cambodian National Police and the National Authority to Combat Drugs seize and destroy seven tons of illicit drugs, mostly methamphetamine, worth US$70 million as part of a crackdown operation.
Cyril Ramaphosa is re-elected as President of South Africa for a second term.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Three people are killed and five others are injured in a Russian cluster munition strike on the village of Ulakly in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Humanitarian aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States announces a $1.5 billion aid package to Ukraine, focused primarily on the country's energy industry and humanitarian assistance.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > June 2024 Ukraine peace summit
text: World leaders meet at the Bürgenstock Resort in Switzerland to advance the Ukrainian peace process.
An IED kills eight IDF personnel in a Namer armoured personnel carrier in Rafah.
Twelve people are killed and a dozen injured after a bus fell into a deep gorge in Uttarakhand, India.
Two people are killed in a plane crash near Chino, California, United States.
A Dutch tourist is found dead and three other tourists are missing on different Greek islands.
Iran and Sweden complete a prisoner swap mediated by Oman, with former Iranian official Hamid Nouri being exchanged for former Swedish diplomat Johan Floderus and a Swedish-Iranian citizen.

context: Territorial disputes in the South China Sea
text: China issues new regulations allowing its national coastguard to detain foreigners accused of illegally entering China's claimed territorial waters and adjacent waters.
Over 600,000 people march in cities across France to protest against the far-right National Rally party.
Honduran President Xiomara Castro announces new measures to reduce gang activity in Honduras, including building a 20,000-capacity "megaprison" and plans to designate gang members as terrorists.
Thousands of women march in São Paulo, Brazil, in protest of a bill that would equate late abortions after 22 weeks to homicide with sentences of six to 20 years in prison.
Nine people are injured, including two young children, in a shooting at a splash pad in Rochester Hills, Michigan, United States.
Two people are killed and fourteen are injured after a shooting at a Juneteenth celebration at a park in Round Rock, Texas, United States.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine > Humanitarian aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Norway announces that it will give Ukraine 1.1 billion kroner (US$103 million) to help repair its energy infrastructure and secure the country's electricity supply before the winter.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine > Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The two-day Global Peace Summit, dedicated to the discussion of "Ukraine's Peace Formula", ends at the Bürgenstock Resort in Switzerland.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russia claims that it captured the village of in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine.

Israel's military announces that it will begin "tactical pauses" in combat along roads in Southern Gaza during the daytime in order to allow humanitarian aid trucks to travel through the Kerem Shalom crossing into Gaza with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu calling the pauses "unacceptable".

context: Rostov-on-Don pre-trial detention center hostage crisis
text: Previously-detained inmates with alleged links to the Islamic State take two employees hostage in a pre-trial detention center in Rostov-on-Don, Russia. Russian national guards storm the center, killing all six hostage takers.
At the 2024 Tony Awards, Stereophonic wins Best Play and The Outsiders wins Best Musical.
At least six people are killed in a landslide caused by heavy rainfall that struck a highway in Baños in central Ecuador, with 30 other people reported missing.
Around 1,200 people are evacuated from the Hungry Valley area near Los Angeles, California, United States, as the Post Fire spreads through the dry mountains near Interstate 5.
At least 19 Jordanian and Iranian pilgrims are killed during the hajj in Saudi Arabia, with at least 14 dying from heat stroke.
Seven people are injured and one other person is injured while running away in a shooting at a pop-up party in Methuen, Massachusetts, United States.
Liechtensteiners vote 53.7% positively on a referendum to build a new state hospital.

Hundreds of LGBTQ+ Ukrainian Armed Forces troops and supporters march in central Kyiv to demand legal reforms for more same-sex partnership rights despite opposition from the Ukrainian Orthodox Church as well as from counter-protesters.

context: 2024 FIA World Endurance Championship > 2024 24 Hours of Le Mans
text: In endurance racing, the AF Corse Ferrari team wins the 24 Hours of Le Mans for the second consecutive year with drivers Antonio Fuoco, Miguel Molina, and Nicklas Nielsen.
In American football, the Birmingham Stallions defeat the San Antonio Brahmas to win the inaugural UFL championship. Stallions quarterback Adrian Martinez is named the Most Valuable Player.

context: Israel–Hamas war > United States support for Israel in the Israel–Hamas war
text: Two congressional Democrats agree to sign a $18 billion weapon package for Israel including 50 F-15 Eagle fighter jets after initially delaying proceedings, following heavy pressure from the Biden Administration.
Eight Palestinians are killed by Israeli fire while waiting for commercial trucks in Gaza.
Hezbollah commander Muhammad Ahmed Ayoub is allegedly killed in an Israeli airstrike in Selaa, Lebanon, with further strikes occurring against Hezbollah targets across southern Lebanon.
At least 139 people suffer from botulism in Russia believed to be caused by eating ready-made salads, leading to a nationwide recall of the salads.
Eleven people are killed and sixty others are injured when a cargo train collides with a Kanchanjungha Express passenger train in Darjeeling district, West Bengal, India.
At least ten people are killed after two boats carrying migrants shipwreck off the southern coast of Italy, with 64 additional people reported missing.
Egypt's Tourism Hajj Mission announces that at least eight Egyptian pilgrims have died during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.
Seven people are killed amid heavy rains across El Salvador.
Six people, including three children, are killed in a house fire in Newnan, Georgia, United States, and five others are hospitalized.
A person is killed and eight others are injured during an ammunition explosion at a military training area in Libavá, Czech Republic.
France and Belgium announce they are strengthening their cooperation in land defence.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk orders Germany to explain a recorded incident where German police appear to desert a migrant family in Osinów Dolny, Poland, just east of the Germany–Poland border.
Russian President Vladimir Putin announces that he will visit North Korea this week, the first state visit by a Russian President in 24 years.
In the United States, Maryland Governor Wes Moore pardons more than 175,000 people with low-level marijuana convictions.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announces the dissolution of the war cabinet after Minister Benny Gantz of the Resilience Party left the cabinet.

In basketball, the Boston Celtics defeat the Dallas Mavericks in five games in the NBA Finals, winning their 18th overall NBA championship. The Celtics surpass the Los Angeles Lakers to become the team with the most NBA championships.

context: Red Sea crisis > Attacks on the MV Tutor
text: The Liberia-flagged MV Tutor sinks in the Red Sea six days after being attacked by a Houthi unmanned surface vessel and missile.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Ukraine experiences rolling blackouts due to Russian attacks on power plants across the country.
South Korean soldiers fire warning shots at North Korean soldiers who crossed the Demarcation Line, apparently in error. It is the second such incident at the demarcation line in the past month.
North Korean troop casualties are reported following landmine explosions in the Korean Demilitarized Zone.
Nvidia surpasses Microsoft as the world's most valuable publicly-traded company after its market cap exceeds US$3.34 trillion.

The United States Department of Agriculture announces a temporary suspension on imports of mangoes and avocados from Michoacán, Mexico, after an incident that reportedly caused security concerns for safety inspectors.
More than 577 pilgrims from Jordan, Egypt, Tunisia, and Indonesia are confirmed to have died of heat-related illnesses during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.

At least one person dies, over 500 structures are damaged or destroyed, and several thousand people are forced to evacuate from Ruidoso, New Mexico, United States, after the South Fork Fire burns over 15,276 acres of land.
At least nine people are killed and 15 others are missing during landslides caused by floods in Guangdong and Fujian provinces, China.
Nine people are killed in a fire caused by an electric short circuit at a hospital in Rasht, Iran.
At least four people are killed and more than 120 others are injured by a magnitude 5.0 earthquake in Kashmar, Iran.
Ecuador's foreign ministry announces that it is reinstating a visa requirement for travelers from China, citing an increase in irregular migratory flows from China.
Israel and Kosovo agree to allow their citizens reciprocal visa-free travel.

The Swedish Parliament votes 266–37 to adopt a defense agreement with the United States, giving the U.S. military access to 17 military bases and training areas in Sweden, including for weapon and military equipment storage.
Former Prime Minister of Thailand Thaksin Shinawatra is indicted on a charge of royal defamation.
A court in Iran sentences Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi to one year in prison for propaganda against the state.
Kazakh opposition activist Aydos Sadykov is shot and injured in Kyiv, Ukraine.

context: LGBT rights in Thailand, Recognition of same-sex unions in Thailand
text: The Senate of Thailand passes a marriage equality bill that will legalize same-sex marriage in the country, with the bill now awaiting royal assent.
Regan Smith breaks the 100 metres backstroke world record at the US Olympic Swimming Trials in Indianapolis, Indiana, United States.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel's role in the Syrian civil war
text: An Israeli airstrike kills a Syrian army officer in southern Syria.
Hezbollah announces that an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon killed three of its fighters.

Hezbollah secretary general Hassan Nasrallah threatens Cyprus if it allows Israel to use its airports and bases for military exercises which Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides denies as well as announcing the possibility of a ground invasion of Galilee.
The European Commission reprimands Belgium, France, Hungary, Italy, Malta, Poland, and Slovakia for breaking budget rules.
Tropical Storm Alberto forms in the Gulf of Mexico, the first storm of the 2024 Atlantic hurricane season.
At least 922 pilgrims are now confirmed to have died from heat-related causes during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.
At least nine people are killed and 46 others are injured in a series of explosions at a military ammunition depot in N'Djamena, Chad.
Landslides caused by heavy monsoon rains in Bangladesh and India kill at least 15 people, injure several others, and displace millions of people.
At least four people are killed and more than a dozen others are missing after record rains impact parts of southern China.
Canada adds Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to its list of terrorist entities.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un sign an agreement to grant mutual aid and support in case either nation faces aggression.
Sudan accuses the United Arab Emirates of arming the Rapid Support Forces.
New Caledonia police arrest independence leader Christian Tein and seven others on suspicion of being involved in the deadly violence in the territory.

context: Antisemitism during the Israel–Hamas war, Antisemitism in 21st-century France
text: Two teenagers are charged with the gang rape of a 12-year-old Jewish girl in Courbevoie, France, in an attack suspected to have been motivated by antisemitism.
Two Just Stop Oil environmental protesters are arrested after damaging three standing stones of the Stonehenge prehistoric megalithic structure with orange powder paint.
The National Assembly of Tajikistan approves a bill banning "alien garments" and children's celebrations for Eid al-Fitr and Eid Al-Adha.
South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol declares a 'demographic national emergency', citing an ultralow birth rate and a declining population.
Human Rights Watch reports that China has changed the names of hundreds of villages inhabited by Uyghurs in order to reflect the ruling Communist Party's ideology.

The Italian Parliament passes a law granting more autonomy to the country's regions following a night of debate. The opposition Democratic Party and former Prime Minister Matteo Renzi express opposition to the bill, with the latter launching a campaign to force a referendum.
The city of Brussels, Belgium, announces that it will not host a UEFA Nations League match between Belgium and Israel on September 6 due to security concerns.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine is prioritized first among the countries to receive ordered deliveries of MIM-104 Patriot missile systems from the United States.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: United States officials announce that they will allow Ukraine to use US weapons to strike Russian forces within Russia, provided they are located right across the border with Ukraine, removing the prior limit of only allowing strikes across the Kharkiv front.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Three people are killed and four others are injured in Russian cluster munitions strikes on the village of Rozkishne, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
The Rapid Support Forces captures Al-Fulah, the capital of West Kordofan, Sudan, after the Sudanese Armed Forces withdraw from the city after several hours of fighting.

The Israel Antiquities Authority announces the discovery of a 3,300-year-old ship and its cargo, one of the oldest known examples of a ship sailing far from land. The ship was discovered last year by a company drilling for natural gas off the coast of Northern Israel.
At least 1,081 pilgrims are now confirmed to have died from heat-related causes during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.
At least 36 people are killed and more than 60 others are hospitalized after consuming tainted liquor in Kallakurichi district, Tamil Nadu, India.
A cruise ship rescues 68 migrants and finds five bodies in a wooden dinghy that was drifting off the Canary Islands, Spain.
At least two people are killed and nine others are injured when a passenger train collides with a train on a test run near Santiago, Chile.
Kuwait announces temporary power cuts in parts of the country during peak consumption hours, saying that the country is struggling to meet increased demand caused by extreme summer heat.
U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal and Lindsey Graham move to designate Russia a state sponsor of terrorism after its defensive pact with North Korea.
Outgoing Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte is announced as the next Secretary General of NATO, beginning his term on October 2.

Congress of the Philippines lawmakers pursue an investigation into a U.S. military social media disinformation operation to discredit Chinese COVID-19 vaccines to Filipinos to determine the damages caused, international law infringements, and possible legal action.
The orange powder paint sprayed on Stonehenge by Just Stop Oil activists yesterday is removed with a handheld blower fan, leaving no visible damage.

Two Just Stop Oil activists film themselves cutting through a metal fence and spraying orange paint on two private jets at Stansted Airport in Essex, England, United Kingdom. Police arrest the activists for criminal damage.
A tourist accused of desecrating the Quran is removed from a police station in Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, by a mob who beat him to death before setting his corpse on fire.
The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom rules that the future impact of proposed fossil fuel projects must be assessed, when considering site proposals for drilling.
The Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs announces sanctions on firms based in China, India, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan, for their alleged support to Russia in the Russo–Ukrainian war.

One person is killed, at least 200 people are injured, and over 100 are arrested in protests across Kenya against government plans to raise $2.7 billion in additional taxes. Kenya Police fired live rounds, tear gas, and water cannons at protesters.
Researchers announce the discovery of the Lokiceratops rangiformis, a dinosaur species named after the Norse god Loki, in North America. The findings are published in the journal PeerJ.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature announces that the Iberian lynx has been upgraded from endangered to vulnerable for the first time since 1986, after a 2023 census showed a population of 2,021 animals.
Serbia threatens to withdraw from UEFA Euro 2024 if UEFA does not punish Croatia and Albania after their supporters chant "kill, kill, kill the Serb" during a match in Hamburg, Germany, on Wednesday.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Rafah offensive > June 2024 Al-Mawasi refugee camp attack
text: Twenty-five people are killed and 50 others are injured in Israeli shelling near Muwasi, Rafah. Gaza Strip.
An IED kills five Pakistan Army personnel in Kurram District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Niger's military junta revokes the operating license of French nuclear fuel producer Orano at the Imouraren uranium mine amid tensions between the two countries.
At least 1,119 pilgrims, more than half of whom are from Egypt, are now confirmed to have died from heat-related causes during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.
President of Tunisia Kais Saied dismisses the Minister of Religious Affairs after 49 Tunisians are reported to have died in this year's Hajj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia.
The death toll from the floods and landslides in Meizhou, Guangdong, China, increases to 47 people.
At least six people die due to heat-related illness in the Phoenix metropolitan area in Arizona, United States, as temperatures reach .
At least 21 people are killed by floods in Niger's Maradi region and the suburbs of Niamey after unusually heavy rainfall in the region.

Most of Montenegro and parts of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Croatia experience blackouts as a result of a heavy load on the electrical grid caused by an unexpected increase in power consumption due to high temperatures.
At least 11 people are killed in wildfires in southeast Turkey.
A worker is killed and five others are critically injured in an explosion at an aluminium processing plant in Bolzano, South Tyrol, Italy.
France reports nearly 200 cases of cholera in Mayotte.
The death toll from torrential rains in El Salvador increases to 19 people, including at least two children.

context: Enlargement of the European Union > Accession of Moldova to the European Union, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
text: European Union member states agree to begin negotiations on the accession of Moldova and Ukraine to the EU next week.

context: Enlargement of the European Union > Accession of Moldova to the European Union, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
text: Moldovan president Maia Sandu signs the decree that begins negotiations on Moldova's accession to the European Union. Sandu also announces that the first Moldova–EU intergovernmental conference will take place on 25 June.

context: Armenia–Palestine relations, International recognition of the State of Palestine
text: Armenia officially recognises the State of Palestine.
Israel and Ukraine mutually impose travel restrictions to each others' citizens, preventing reciprocal visa-free travel without an authorization permit.

Four people are killed and ten others are wounded in a shooting at the Mad Butcher supermarket in Fordyce, Arkansas, United States. The suspect, Travis Eugene Posey, is shot and arrested by Arkansas State Police.
China officially defines Taiwanese separatist behavior as a criminal act.
The High Court of Namibia rules that two colonial-era laws criminalizing sex between men are unconstitutional.
A court in Geneva, Switzerland, sentences Indian-born billionaire Prakash Hinduja and three of his family members to four years in prison for exploiting domestic workers at their villa in Cologny.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > June 2024 northern Gaza City airstrikes
text: At least 42 Palestinians are killed by Israeli airstrikes in northern Gaza.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least three people are killed and 38 others are injured when Russian guided bombs hit civilian infrastructure in Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, injuring two people and damaging energy infrastructure. Ukraine says that it shot down 12 of 16 missiles and all 13 drones.

context: 2021–2024 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks
text: At least 23 people are killed by CODECO militia groups in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
At least seven people are killed and 100 are kidnapped by unknown gunmen in Katsina State, Nigeria.
The death toll from the tainted liquor incident in Kallakurichi district, Tamil Nadu, India, increases to 54.
The death toll from the storms and heavy rains in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras increases to 30 people, including at least six children.
Three people are missing following thunderstorms and landslides in southeastern Switzerland.

A severe water crisis on the island of Capri, Italy, due to Italian mainland water system failures causes several areas in Anacapri to run dry, and forces the mayor of Capri to suspend tourist arrivals on the island.
French prosecutors charge a 19-year-old and a minor with planning and collecting arms for a violent "terrorist conspiracy" against Jewish targets.
Thousands of people march in a pride parade in Budapest, Hungary, to protest against Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's anti-LGBTQ+ policies.

A University of Illinois team lead by Joshua Wurman and Karen Kosiba confirms mobile radar measurements of between and in the tornado that struck Greenfield, Iowa, United States, on May 21. This is the first unambiguous radar confirmation of tornado winds over .

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Crimea attacks > June 2024 Sevastopol missile attack
text: Ukrainian forces launch an ATACMS missile bombardment on Sevastopol, Crimea, with missile fragments hitting a beach, killing five people and injuring at least 153 others of which 27 were children. Russia's ministry of defense says that it holds the United States responsible for the attack and vows that there will be a response.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: One person is killed and ten others are injured in Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure in Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Eight Palestinians are killed in IDF airstrikes that hit a UNRWA-run vocational college in Gaza City that was being used to distribute aid.
At least 16 people are killed and 13 others are injured in Dagestan, Russia, when gunmen open fire on a synagogue and an Orthodox church in Derbent and on a traffic police post in Makhachkala.
North Macedonia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs urges all its citizens in Lebanon to leave as soon as possible due to "deteriorating security" in the region from escalating conflicts.
The Houthis claim to have carried out a joint military operation with the Islamic Resistance in Iraq to target four vessels in the Port of Haifa, Israel.
The Saudi health minister announces that 1,301 people are now confirmed to have died during this year's Hajj pilgrimage.
One person is found dead after floods in southern Switzerland.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israel–Hamas war protests in Israel
text: More than 150,000 Israelis rally and march in Tel Aviv to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his government, calling for new elections, the return of hostages, and a ceasefire.
Independence leader Christian Tein and seven other activists are flown to France for pre-trial detention after being arrested for inciting violence and riots in New Caledonia.

On the Grand Duke's Official Birthday, Henri, Grand Duke of Luxembourg announces that his son and heir Guillaume will assume royal duties beginning in October, in preparation for Henri's eventual abdication.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Gaza humanitarian crisis
text: Eleven Palestinians, including the director of Gaza's Ambulance and Emergency Department, are killed in Israeli airstrikes on the al-Shati refugee camp, Bani Suhaila, and Gaza City.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Three-phase Israel–Hamas war ceasefire proposal
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejects the U.S.-backed ceasefire proposal for the war in Gaza, instead committing to continuing the war and "the goal of eliminating Hamas."

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: At least four people are killed and 40 others are injured when Russian Iskander-M ballistic missiles hit Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
The death toll from the attack on a synagogue and Orthodox church in Derbent and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, yesterday, increases to 20, with 46 others injured.
Twenty-three people are killed and eight others are injured in a fire at a lithium battery factory in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi, South Korea.
Eight people are killed in a fire in an office building in Fryazino, Moscow Oblast, Russia.

Officials in Blue Earth County, Minnesota, United States, issue an evacuation warning due to flooding on the Blue Earth River breaching the Rapidan Dam, pushing it into an "imminent failure condition" upstream of several cities. Flooding also collapses a railroad bridge connecting South Dakota and Iowa and kills two people.

The Royal Zoological Society of Scotland reports that Scottish wildcat kittens have been born in the Cairngorms National Park, in a "major milestone" for the conservation of the critically endangered population.

Trial courts in Metro Manila, Philippines, dismiss the remaining charges filed against former senator Leila de Lima during the presidency of Rodrigo Duterte, including the last of the three involving her alleged conspiracy in the illegal drug trade, as well as another on her disobedience to a summons for a House hearing.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange enters a plea deal with the U.S. Justice Department, in which he will be found guilty on one federal charge in exchange for his release back to Australia.
A mass shooting in two apartments in North Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, killed six people, including the 47-year-old gunman, Eric Adams. 13-year-old Olivia Munoz was wounded in the shooting.

Violence and riots resume in New Caledonia after eight pro-independence activists were flown to France for pre-trial detention yesterday. Protesters burn police vehicles, block roads, and set fire to the town hall in Koumac.

In ice hockey, the Florida Panthers defeat the Edmonton Oilers in seven games to win the 2024 Stanley Cup Final, marking their first Stanley Cup championship in franchise history. The Panthers also avoid becoming the fifth team in National Hockey League history to lose a series despite having a 3–0 series lead.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip, Bombing of the Gaza Strip
text: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 24 people in Gaza City, including ten family members of Hamas political chief Ismail Haniyeh.
The European Court of Human Rights unanimously finds Russia guilty of systematic violations of human rights in the Crimean peninsula.
Russia and Ukraine each return 90 prisoners of war in a prisoner exchange mediated by the United Arab Emirates.
Kenyan police units arrive in Haiti for a United Nations-backed security mission to restore order.

The European Commission levies an antitrust fine against Microsoft, charging it with violating European Union competition law by illegally linking its Microsoft Teams app with Microsoft Office, giving the former an unfair advantage over Slack.
Puerto Rico announces its first island-wide heat advisory to all 78 municipalities due to predicted highs of 114°F (46°C) and widespread power outages.

context: Enlargement of the European Union > Accession of Ukraine to the European Union, Accession of Moldova to the European Union
text: The European Union formally launches accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova.

The United States Department of the Treasury announces economic sanctions on 50 people and companies in Hong Kong, the United Arab Emirates, and the Marshall Islands, for allegedly funding and helping Iran's military gain access to the international financial system.
The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe elects former Swiss president Alain Berset as the Council's new Secretary General, succeeding Marija Pejčinović Burić.
Russia bans 81 media outlets from access inside the country, including Agence France-Presse and Politico, in retaliation for a European Union ban on Russian media outlets.

context: Gun violence in the United States
text: U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy declares gun violence a public health emergency.

context: Gun violence in the United States
text: A gunman kills five people and critically injures a girl in North Las Vegas, Nevada, then kills himself upon being confronted by the police the following day.

The Supreme Court of Israel rules that the Israel Defense Forces and the government are legally bound to conscript Haredi yeshiva students, overturning their prior exemption from mandatory military service.

context: Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange
text: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is freed following a plea deal with the United States, which results in Assange pleading guilty to espionage-related charges.

context: International Criminal Court investigation in Ukraine
text: The International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Russia's Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov and former defence minister Sergei Shoigu.

context: Kenya Finance Bill protests > 2024 Parliament of Kenya assault
text: Thousands of anti-tax protestors assault and set the Parliament of Kenya building in Nairobi on fire, as riots begin following the approval of a finance bill. The ceremonial mace is also stolen by protesters. Ten people are killed and more than 50 others are injured as police open fire on protestors.

context: Kenya Finance Bill protests > 2024 Parliament of Kenya assault
text: President William Ruto deploys the military to stop the protests.

context: 2024 United Kingdom general election date betting scandal
text: A fifth Conservative Party member is investigated for involvement in the ongoing election betting scandal.
The Peruvian Ministry of Health announces that it will stop labeling transgender individuals as suffering from mental disorders, but will instead use the term "gender discordance".

context: Spanish General Council of the Judiciary blockade
text: The two major political parties, Spanish Socialist Workers' Party and People's Party agree to renew the members of the General Council of the Judiciary after five years of blockade and the necessary mediation by the European Commission to reach an agreement.
The Chang'e 6 lunar exploration mission successfully returns to Earth after collecting rock and soil samples from the far side of the Moon.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip, Bombing of the Gaza Strip
text: An Israeli airstrike on a home in Beit Lahiya in North Gaza kills at least 15 Palestinians.
President Luis Arce accuses military general Juan José Zúñiga of plotting a coup, and calls for a general strike and blocking of roads to prevent the coup. The attempted coup fails.
Bolivian general Juan José Zúñiga is arrested following his failed coup attempt.

Niger's ministry of defence announces three days of national mourning following yesterday's ambush of security forces near the village of Tassia in Tillabéri Region, which killed at least 20 soldiers and a civilian and injured several others.
Two South African soldiers are killed and twenty others are injured in a mortar attack on a South African National Defence Force logistics base in Sake, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Unidentified attackers open fire on a Tunisian military patrol near the border with Libya, killing a soldier, according to the Tunisian Ministry of Defence.
Three fishermen are found dead following heavy rainfall and winds that caused coastal flooding along New Zealand's eastern coast.
Twenty people are killed following two days of heavy rains in Nepal.

context: Russia–European Union relations, Belarus–European Union relations
text: The leaders of Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia call on the European Union to construct a €2.5 billion (US$2.67 billion) defence line between them and Russia and Belarus to secure the EU from military, economic, and migrant-related threats.
Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte is formally selected as the next NATO Secretary-General.

context: International Criminal Court investigation in Mali
text: The International Criminal Court convicts Malian Islamist Al Hassan Ag Abdoul Aziz of Ansar Dine on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity.
German government ministers agree on legislation to expedite deportation for individuals who post or "like" social media content that celebrates or promotes terrorist acts.
Former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández is sentenced to 45 years in prison and fined $8 million for drug trafficking and firearms offences in a U.S. federal court.

context: 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in New York
text: Incumbent New York representative Jamaal Bowman loses a Democratic Party primary challenge against George Latimer in the 16th district, in what has become the most expensive House of Representatives primary in history by campaign spending.
President William Ruto withdraws the controversial Kenya Finance Bill 2024 following an assault on the parliament that killed multiple people.

France's government orders the dissolution of several far-right and radical Muslim groups prior to the upcoming legislative election due to their violence, discrimination, and hate speech toward different races, women, and LGBTQ+ people.

In basketball, the first day of the draft for the National Basketball Association is held at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, U.S., with the Atlanta Hawks selecting French player Zaccharie Risacher with the first overall pick.
At least 568 people have died from heat-related illnesses due to extreme temperatures and humidity in southern Pakistan.

An Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report states that over 755,000 people in Sudan face the most severe IPC level of extreme hunger as well as the worst levels of acute food insecurity ever recorded in the country.
Seven people are killed and five others are injured when a train collides with a bus near Nové Zámky, Slovakia.
Three people are killed and 40 others are injured in a train derailment amid heavy rains in Komi, Russia.
The Russian satellite Resurs-P No.1 breaks up into over 100 pieces of debris near the International Space Station.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: According to an anonymous South Korean government official, North Korea is preparing to send engineering forces to the Russian-occupied Donetsk region of Ukraine in July.

The US Supreme Court issues a ruling in Moyle v. United States, dismissing the case and reinstating the ability to perform exceptional emergency abortion care in Idaho, where a formal ban on abortion is in place.

context: Opioid epidemic in the United States
text: In Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P., the United States Supreme Court blocks a proposed Purdue Pharma bankruptcy settlement that would have shielded members of the Sackler family from civil lawsuits relating to the opioid epidemic, citing issues regarding the protection of third parties from lawsuits.
The Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party expels former defense ministers Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe from the party following charges of corruption against them.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy signs a law establishing English as an official language of international communication in Ukraine.

The U.S. Justice Department charges 193 people, including 76 medical professionals, with participating in healthcare fraud schemes totalling $2.75 billion, which include unlawful distribution of Adderall and fraudulent drug addiction treatment.
The first U.S. presidential debate for the upcoming presidential election is held between incumbent President Joe Biden and former president Donald Trump on CNN.
Thousands of people protest in cities across Kenya, calling for the removal of President William Ruto.

The leaders of the European Union member states agree to nominate Ursula von der Leyen as President of the European Commission and Estonian Prime Minister Kaja Kallas as the next High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, and elect former Portuguese Prime Minister António Costa as the next President of the European Council.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Dnipro strikes
text: At least one person is killed and 12 others are injured when a Russian missile hits a nine-storey residential building in Dnipro, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian Ministry of Defence claims that its forces have taken control of the village of Rozdolivka in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
Philippine troops claim to have killed at least ten suspected communist guerrillas, including three commanders, near a village in Pantabangan, Nueva Ecija, Philippines.

The Argentine Chamber of Deputies approves economic reform measures proposed by President Javier Milei, which include investment incentives, the privatization of numerous state-owned entities, and tax overhauls.
Four people are killed and nine others are injured when a minivan crashes into a nail salon in Deer Park, Long Island, New York, United States.
A roof at the Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi, India, collapses amid heavy rains killing one person, injuring eight others, and leading to the cancellation of some domestic flights.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake strikes off the coast of central Peru, injuring 23 people.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The U.S. military dismantles the Gaza floating pier for the third time due to bad weather.
A mass shooting in Corpus Christi, Texas, United States kills two people, an 18-year-old and a 15-year-old, and leaves three other people injured including two 19-year-olds and a 20-year-old.
British police arrest 27 Just Stop Oil activists accused of planning to disrupt airports during the upcoming summer holidays.
Maldivian Minister of the Environment Fathima Shamnaz Ali Saleem and three others are arrested for allegedly performing black magic on President Mohamed Muizzu.
Indonesian officials arrest and intend to deport 103 Taiwanese nationals suspected of running a cybercrime operation in Tabanan, Bali, Indonesia.

George Alvarez, the perpetrator of the 2023 Brownsville crash in Texas, United States, that killed eight people and injured ten others is found guilty of eight counts of intoxication manslaughter and ten counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and is sentenced to sixty years in prison.
Iranians vote in a snap presidential election following the death of president Ebrahim Raisi.

Mongolians vote for members of the State Great Khural. This is the first election since the Khural was expanded to 126 seats and the first to use parallel voting. The ruling Mongolian People's Party loses its supermajority but claims victory, maintaining a slim simple majority.
Thousands of Serbians protest in Loznica, Serbia, against the Rio Tinto mining company and its plans to develop a lithium mining project in Jadar.
Thousands of Japanese people protest at the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo over multiple alleged sexual assault cases involving U.S. service members against Japanese people on Okinawa Island.

In ice hockey, the first day of the draft for the National Hockey League is held at the Sphere in Las Vegas, Nevada, U.S., with the San Jose Sharks selecting Macklin Celebrini with the first overall pick.

M23 rebels take control of Kayna, Luofu, Kanyabayonga, and surrounding areas after heavy fighting with FARDC. Almost the entire population of Kanyabayonga, including refugees it had taken in from Rutshuru, flee the rebel advance. The town is considered a pathway to the cities of Butembo and Beni.
Thirty people are killed in Borno State, Nigeria, by bomb blasts at a hospital, wedding and funeral.
Five large bombs planted by ISIL are discovered in the walls of the Great Mosque of al-Nuri, Mosul, Iraq.
At least twelve people, including four children, are killed by Russian attacks in Ukraine.
The Rapid Support Forces launch an assault and capture the town of Singa, the probable capital of Sennar State, Sudan.
Landslides in Nepal kill nine people, including three children.
Five people are killed in a fire at a dormitory building in Balashikha, Moscow Oblast, Russia.
Five Indian soldiers are killed in Ladakh, India, after their tank sinks in abruptly increased water levels in the Shyok River during a military exercise.
Five people are killed and 38 others are injured after an explosion at an fireworks warehouse in Zamboanga City, Philippines.
Tropical Storm Beryl intensifies into Hurricane Beryl, becoming the first hurricane in the 2024 Atlantic hurricane season.
The Biden administration extends Temporary Protected Status to 309,000 Haitian refugees in the United States until February 2026, offering them deportation relief and work permits.

context: Violent incidents in reaction to the Israel–Hamas war > 2024 attack on the Israeli embassy in Belgrade
text: A man attacks a police officer guarding the Israeli embassy in Belgrade, Serbia, with a crossbow before being shot and killed. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić calls the incident a terrorist attack against Serbia.
Several hundred people march in Paris, France, to honour Nahel Merzouk and protest against police brutality and far-right parties.
Saeed Jalili and Masoud Pezeshkian advance to the Iranian presidential run-off, amid record-low voter attendance.
Mauritanians vote between incumbent Mohamed Ould Ghazouani and six other candidates for President; Ghazouani wins re-election on the first ballot.
Over 100,000 German protesters and 1,000 police officers clash at an Alternative for Germany event in Essen, Germany. Police use pepper spray and batons on protesters.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Rafah offensive
text: At least six Palestinians are killed in Rafah in the Gaza Strip, as Israeli tanks re-enter Shuja'iyya and parts of northern Gaza, displacing more than 60,000 people.
18 IDF soldiers are injured by a Hezbollah drone attack on the Golan Heights.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kharkiv strikes
text: At least one person is killed and ten others are injured when a Russian guided bomb hits a postal sorting hub in Kharkiv, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian Defence Ministry says that its forces have taken the villages of Spirne and Novooleksandrivka in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk Oblast.
M23 rebels take control of Kirumba, the largest town in Lubero Territory, Democratic Republic of the Congo, as they continue north.
The American film Inside Out 2 surpasses $1 billion in worldwide box office earnings in less than three weeks, the fastest of any animated film in history.
At least four people are killed and two others are missing after landslides and torrential floods in Ticino and Valais, Switzerland.
A Chinese Tianlong-3 rocket stage is accidentally launched during a static fire test in Gongyi, Henan, China, causing it to crash and explode. No casualties are reported.
A propane tank explosion at a restaurant in Izmir, Turkey, kills five people and injures 63 others.
Hurricane Beryl undergoes rapid intensification and strengthens into a Category 4 hurricane, becoming the earliest Category 4 Atlantic hurricane on record.

context: 2024 French legislative election > 2024 French protests against the far-right
text: Thousands of left-wing protesters gather in cities across France to protest the National Rally's lead in election polls, while showing support for the New Popular Front left-wing alliance.
French citizens vote in the first round of legislative elections for the 17th National Assembly of the Fifth French Republic.
Uruguayans vote to elect the presidential candidates for all political parties that are running in the general election on 27 October.
Thousands of Haredi Jewish men protest in Jerusalem, Israel, against a recent Supreme Court ruling that ordered the conscription of Haredi yeshiva students, clashing with Israel Police.
The Bulgarian Orthodox Church elects Metropolitan Daniel of Vidin, a member of the pro-Russian faction among the church's senior clergy, as Patriarch of All Bulgaria.
France win their second Volleyball Nations League title after defeating Japan in four sets in the final at Atlas Arena in Łódź, Poland.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Northern Aleppo clashes
text: Anti-Turkish riots occur in Turkish-occupied Northern Syria following anti-Syrian riots in Kayseri, Turkey, yesterday.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Northern Aleppo clashes
text: Four people are killed and over 20 are injured as Turkish soldiers open fire against protestors in Afrin, Syria.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Siege of Khan Yunis
text: The Israel Defense Forces order a mass evacuation of Palestinians from the entire eastern half of Khan Yunis and surrounding areas in anticipation of a new ground assault on the city.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia says that it has captured the villages of Novopokrovske in Donetsk Oblast and Stepova Novoselivka in Kharkiv Oblast.
Hurricane Beryl makes landfall on the island of Carriacou, Grenada, as a category 4 hurricane.
Hurricane Beryl intensifies to a category 5 hurricane, becoming the earliest on record in the basin, and kills at least one person on the Windward Islands.
A car driving the wrong way in central Seoul, South Korea, strikes pedestrians waiting at a traffic light, killing nine people and injuring four others.

An Air Europa Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft experiences severe turbulence while flying from Madrid, Spain, to Montevideo, Uruguay, injuring 40 people and forcing the flight to divert to Natal, Brazil.
At least 89 migrants are killed after their boat, which carried 170 migrants, capsized off the coast of Ndiago, Mauritania.
Bolivia summons its ambassador to Argentina after Argentine President Javier Milei called the recent coup attempt "fraudulent" and implied that it was staged.

context: Blasphemy in Pakistan; Jaranwala church arsons
text: A court in Sahiwal, Punjab, Pakistan sentences a Christian man to death for blasphemy against Muslims on social media after anti-Christian mobs burned down dozens of homes and churches in Jaranwala, Punjab, in August 2023.

In a landmark ruling, the Supreme Court of the United States rules 6–3 that presidents have presumed absolute immunity from criminal prosecution for official acts taken in exercising constitutional powers while serving as president, and have no immunity for "unofficial acts".
Mexican authorities discover the bodies of nineteen men who were shot dead in and near a dump truck abandoned in La Concordia, Chiapas, near the Guatemalan border.
Ukrainian officials uncover a plan to storm parliament and seize control from the current government on Constitution Day, and arrest four individuals implicated in the plot.
A mass shooting in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States, kills three people and injures two others. An adult suspect has been arrested.
A Nepali court sentences Ram Bahadur Bomjon, a man who thousands believed was a reincarnation of The Buddha, to 10 years in jail for child sexual abuse.

The Australian Government increases the visa fee for international students from A$710 (US$473) to A$1,600 (US$1,068) in an attempt to reduce record levels of migration that have increased pressure on the Australian housing market.
Sam Mostyn is sworn in as the 28th Governor-General of Australia.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa unveils his cabinet made up of seven parties.

A dozen resigned United States government officials release a joint statement denouncing President Joe Biden's administration for its "undeniable complicity" in war crimes against Palestinian civilians by violating U.S. laws to continue sending Israel weapons.

context: Israel–Hamas war > Siege of Khan Yunis
text: An Israeli airstrike kills at least nine people in Khan Yunis in the Gaza Strip, hours after Israel ordered a mass evacuation of parts of the city.
Two people are killed and nine others are injured when Russian artillery and drones hit Nikopol in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine.
Kazakh dissident Aydos Sadykov has died two weeks after being shot outside his home in Kyiv, Ukraine.
One person is killed in a landslide caused by Tropical Storm Chris in San Salvador, El Salvador.
123 people are killed in a stampede at a religious gathering in Hathras, Uttar Pradesh, India.

Seventy-six more deaths and at least 500 hospitalizations in Japan are linked to use of red yeast rice supplements distributed by Kobayashi Pharmaceutical, causing kidney disease and other severe conditions.
Floods in northern Myanmar trap thousands of people in their homes and cause power outages and disruptions to telephone services.

context: Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine > Hungary–Ukraine relations, 2024 peace missions by Viktor Orbán
text: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán visits Kyiv, Ukraine, for the first time since the start of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, proposing a ceasefire plan which is rejected by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Panama and the United States sign a deal to reduce the flow of illegal immigration to the southern United States border through the Darién Gap, with the United States covering the costs of repatriating migrants who enter Panama illegally.

context: Islamic terrorism in Europe > Terrorism in the United Kingdom
text: St James's University Hospital nursing assistant Mohammad Farooq is convicted at Sheffield Crown Court of crimes relating to plotting lone wolf attacks on RAF Menwith Hill in North Yorkshire and his Leeds workplace.

context: Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election
text: Former New York City Mayor and lawyer Rudy Giuliani is disbarred in the U.S. state of New York for his efforts in attempting to overturn the 2020 election.

Australia issues statements to several social media and search engine websites ordering the websites to draft and enforce guidelines to prevent minors from seeing inappropriate material before October 3 or face national restrictions.

The United States Department of Homeland Security deports 116 Chinese migrants back to China to deter illegal migration across the Mexico–United States border, representing the nation's first "large charter flight" deportation in the past five years.
Serial killer Lucy Letby is convicted of an attempted murder in a retrial at Manchester Crown Court in Manchester, England.
In the Netherlands, the Schoof cabinet is installed with Dick Schoof taking office as the new prime minister.
Protestors march in Tbilisi surrounding the Parliament Building in protest of the Georgian Dream party, the law on foreign agents, and in support of Georgia joining the EU.

Protests against the controversially rejected Kenyan finance bill and President William Ruto continue in major cities in the country, with the National Commission on Human Rights reporting at least 39 people killed and 361 injured in the protests.
The fifth busy beaver number is confirmed to be 47,176,870.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign > Battle of Chasiv Yar
text: Russian forces take control of the Novy district of Chasiv Yar, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: One person is killed and at least 14 others are injured in Russian guided bomb and missile attacks across Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against infrastructure > Dnipro strikes
text: At least five people are killed and 53 others are injured when Russian drones and missiles hits civilian infrastructure in Dnipro, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: NATO nations agree to grant Ukraine €40 billion (US$43 billion) in military aid in 2025.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis
text: Three kamikaze drones attack an electrical substation for the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, injuring eight workers, causing forest fires near the plant's switchyard, and leaving Enerhodar without power or water.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Karmiel mall stabbing attack
text: An Israeli soldier is killed and another is injured in a stabbing attack at a mall in Karmiel, Israel.

context: Israeli occupation of the West Bank
text: The Israeli government approves the seizure of of Palestinian land in the Jordan Valley, representing the largest land seizure in the West Bank in more than three decades.
An Israeli strike kills Mohammed Nasser, a top commander in Hezbollah, in Tyre, Lebanon. Nasser is one of the highest-ranking Hezbollah members to die in the conflict.
Hezbollah launches a barrage of at least 100 Katyusha rockets, towards northern Israel, targeting Israeli military positions, in retaliation for the killing of Nasser.
Five people, including former senator Hidayat Ullah, are killed when their vehicle en route to an election rally strikes a roadside bomb in Bajaur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

Scientists announce the discovery of the world's oldest cave painting, depicting three people gathered around a large red pig, estimated to be at least 51,200 years old, in Leang Karampurang cave in the Maros-Pangkep region, South Sulawesi, Indonesia.
The death toll from Hurricane Beryl in the eastern Caribbean increases to nine, with deaths reported in Grenada, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and Venezuela.
Four police officers are killed in floods caused by Tropical Storm Chris in Tepetlán, Mexico.
At least sixteen people are killed and more than 300,000 others are displaced by floods and landslides in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, India.
Three people are killed and three others are missing after a fishing boat sinks off the coast of Marinha Grande, Portugal.
At least 26,000 people are forced to evacuate amidst dozens of large wildfires in Northern California, United States.
Temperatures in Moscow, Russia, reach , the highest on this day since 1917.
Investigators in Germany and Sweden arrest eight suspects allied with Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government over alleged participation in crimes against humanity in Syria.
The Supreme Court of Japan rules that the country's forced sterilization law, which was in effect from 1948 to 1996, was unconstitutional.

Sierra Leone outlaws child marriage, setting the legal age of marriage to 18 years. Offenders could face up to 15 years in prison and/or a fine of around US$4,000, with witnesses to child marriages also facing possible jail or fines.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency fines General Motors $145.8 million for excess emissions found in 5.9 million GM vehicles.
Pro-Palestinian protesters climb the roof of the Australian Parliament building in Canberra, Australia.
Eighteen leaders of Jemaah Islamiyah announce the disbanding of the group, after 31 years of operation. The group committed several massacres in Indonesia, including the 2002 and 2005 Bali bombings.

Hezbollah launches at least 200 rockets and a swarm of drones at Israeli territory and threatens to expand its targeting range, in retaliation for the killing of Mohammed Nasser, a top Hezbollah commander.

context: Israeli occupation of the West Bank
text: Israel approves the construction of 5,295 settler homes in dozens of settlements in the West Bank, which are internationally recognized as violating international law.

Six Chinese gold miners and two Congolese soldiers are killed during an attack against a gold mine in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Two other workers are kidnapped. CODECO claims responsibility for the attack.
The Islamic State kills eight people, including two civilians, in an ambush on pro-government militiamen in Syria's Badiya desert.
Hudson's Bay Company, the parent company of Saks Fifth Avenue, completes a merger and purchases luxury department stores Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman for $2.65 billion.
Hurricane Beryl causes a six- to nine-feet high storm surge and fierce winds along Jamaica's southern coast, killing at least one person before tracking towards the Cayman Islands.
Twenty-five people drown in southeast Sudan while trying to flee fighting between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces.
Three people are killed and seven others are injured when a pickup truck is driven into a crowd celebrating Independence Day in the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City, United States.
Eleven people die and another 153 people are diagnosed with West Nile fever in an ongoing outbreak in Israel.

Germany summons Turkey's ambassador to Germany in a tit-for-tat move over footballer Merih Demiral's wolf salute gesture while celebrating a goal at a UEFA Euro 2024 match in Leipzig, Germany, on Tuesday.
The Shanghai Cooperation Organization officially grants membership to Belarus.

context: Violent incidents in reaction to the Israel–Hamas war > Antisemitism during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Greek anti-terrorism police arrest seven people over arson attacks against an Israeli-owned hotel and a synagogue in central Athens.

context: Mass shootings in the United States
text: Thirty-three people are killed in mass shootings at Fourth of July celebrations, with 11 people killed and 55 others injured in Chicago, Illinois, two people killed and three others injured in Huntington Beach, California, one person killed and six others injured in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and one person killed and five others injured in Boston, Massachusetts.
Oslo District Court finds Iranian-born Norwegian Zaniar Matapour guilty of a shooting during pride celebrations in the Norwegian capital in 2022 and sentences Matapour to 30 years in prison.
The Butembo military court in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, sentences 25 FARDC soldiers to death for allegedly fleeing fighting against M23 rebels.
Belarus frees ten political prisoners including former opposition leader Ryhor Kastusioŭ.
