text: Slovak deputy prime minister Tomáš Taraba announces that he will boycott the Olympics closing ceremony in response to being offended by what he called "progressive political theater" hosted by "drag queens" during the opening ceremony.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Olympic organisers cancel the second session of triathlon training due to water quality concerns in the Seine river.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > 2024 Haret Hreik airstrike
text: Israel launches a missile attack on southern Beirut, Lebanon, killing at least four civilians and injuring 80 others. Senior Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr is claimed by Israel to be the main target. He was in the area at the time of the attack, but his status is currently unknown.
An Israeli civilian is killed in the HaGoshrim kibbutz by a rocket fired from Lebanon.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian defense ministry says that its forces have taken control of the settlement of Pivdenne in Donetsk region, Ukraine.

context: Sudanese civil war > Attempted assassination of Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
text: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the military junta leader of Sudan, survives an assassination attempt carried out with a drone strike while he was visiting a military base in Gibet. Five people are killed.
Riots occur in response to a previous mass stabbing in Southport, Merseyside. The right-wing English Defence League was present in front of a mosque, despite not having existed for over a decade.

context: Attacks on U.S. bases in Iraq, Jordan, and Syria during the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United States carries out an airstrike near Hillah, Iraq, killing four members of Iraq's Popular Mobilization Units. Iraq condemns the strike, saying the US-led military coalition committed a "heinous crime" by targeting security sites and said the attacks were a serious violation of the coalition's mission and mandate.
Angolan President João Lourenço announces that the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda have agreed to a ceasefire following Angola-mediated talks.
The Turkish defense ministry says that it targeted Kurdish militants in northern Iraq with air strikes, killing 13 people.
Unidentified gunmen open fire on a bulletproof vehicle carrying local staff working for a United Nations development agency in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan. No casualties have been reported.
Tesla recalls more than 1.8 million vehicles due to a hood issue that could increase the risk of a crash. An over-the-air software update for the issue was made available in June.
Rex Airlines, Australia's third-largest airline, suspends all domestic Boeing 737 flights and enters voluntary administration.
Spain's competition watchdog fines online travel agency Booking.com with a record €413 million fine for "abusing its dominant position" in the past five years.
The death toll from torrential rains and floods caused by remnants of Typhoon Gaemi in Hunan, China, increases to 22.

The World Health Organization reports that it is now "very likely" that poliovirus has infected Gazan citizens and is spreading among the population. The statement was released shortly after the Gaza Health Ministry declared a polio epidemic in the territory.
At least 162 people are killed, 191 others are injured, and more than 89 others are missing in landslides in Wayanad district, Kerala, India.
A helicopter crashes near Killucan, County Westmeath, Ireland, killing two people.
Five people are killed and nine others are injured when a boat capsizes on the Nile River in Cairo, Egypt.

context: Algeria–France relations, Political status of Western Sahara
text: Algeria withdraws its ambassador from France after France declared its support for the Western Sahara Autonomy Proposal, which was proposed by Morocco in 2007.
Turkey and Armenia resume talks aimed at normalizing diplomatic relations and agree to simplify visa rules for some passport holders.
The Taliban suspends relations with 14 Afghan overseas diplomatic missions and announces that they will no longer accept consular documents issued by these missions.
Kyrgyzstan says that 94% of its border with Tajikistan has been agreed upon by officials from both countries.
U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken announces the allocation of $500 million to fund the Philippine military.
Freddy Superlano, a leading figure in Venezuela's opposition coalition, is arrested as the death toll from ongoing anti-Maduro protests increases to four.

A federal investigation commissioned by U.S. Interior Secretary Deb Haaland discovers that sixty-five federal American Indian boarding school sites have unmarked or marked gravesites, and confirms that "at least" 973 Native American children died at boarding schools, primarily from abuse and illness.
British Islamic preacher Anjem Choudary is sentenced to life in prison with a minimum sentence of 28 years for directing the al-Muhajiroun militant network.

Interpol announces that more than 200 people have been arrested and more than US$1.6 billion of illegal drugs and precursor chemicals seized as part of a two-month operation against narcotics trafficking conducted across Europe, North America, and Africa.
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko pardons a German citizen on death row.
Masoud Pezeshkian is inaugurated as the ninth president of Iran.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Olympic officials postpone the men's individual triathlon race due to poor water quality levels in the Seine river.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Several athletes test positive for COVID-19, including Australian swimmer Lani Pallister, forcing her to withdraw from the 1500 metre freestyle swimming event.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Brazil at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Brazil wins a bronze medal in women's artistic gymnastics team competition, their first ever medal in the event.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The United States wins a bronze medal in women's rugby, their first ever medal in the sport at the Olympics.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
text: Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh is assassinated in Tehran, Iran, after attending the inauguration ceremony of Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian. Hamas and Iran blame Israel for the assassination; however, the Israeli government officially declines to comment.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
text: Qatar and Egypt warn that peace negotiations are in jeopardy as a result of the assassination.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Killing of journalists in the Gaza war
text: Al Jazeera Arabic journalist Ismail al-Ghoul and his cameraman are killed in an Israeli airstrike while conducting a news broadcast near Ismail Haniyeh's home in the Gaza Strip.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > Killing of Fuad Shukr
text: A source close to Hezbollah tells AFP that the body of top commander Fuad Shukr has been recovered, nearly 24 hours after he was killed in an Israeli airstrike on southern Beirut, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: One Israeli civilian killed in a Hezbollah rocket strike in northern Israel and Israeli airforce planes are fired at in Lebanese airspace.
Mali announces that it carried out joint airstrikes with Burkina Faso on insurgents in and around Tinzaouaten. The CSP-PSD says that a Burkinabé drone strike killed dozens of civilians.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Siege of Mariupol, Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukraine demands that Russia explain the death of Ukrainian POW Oleksandr Ishchenko in Russian captivity, who was being tried with 21 other captured Ukrainian troops for being part of the Azov Brigade that Russian prosecutors allege is far-right affiliated.
At least 19 people are killed during a suicide bombing by Boko Haram at a market in Konduga, Borno State, Nigeria.

The Cavite provincial government in the Philippines declares a "state of calamity" after an oil spill from the sunk MT Terra Nova ship reaches the shores of eight municipalities, requiring implementation of a no-catch zone and relief aid to be given to around 25,000 fishermen.
The Mirola 1 oil tanker is discovered to have run aground near the coast of Bataan, becoming the third vessel to cause an oil spill in Manila Bay in the past week.
Strong thunderstorms and winds in eastern Nebraska cause significant destruction, causing widespread power outages in Lincoln and Omaha, the two largest cities in the state.
One person is killed and at least 40 others are injured when a tent collapses in a windstorm at a Buddhist retreat in Busby, Alberta, Canada.

Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico threatens to suspend Slovakia's diesel exports to Ukraine if the Ukrainian government continues to suspend pipeline oil transport from Russian oil company Lukoil, which Slovakia claims is causing a national energy crisis.

The United States pauses US$95 million in assistance to the country of Georgia due to its government passing a law on "foreign agents", which US officials referred to as "anti-democratic" and a "draconian measure to stifle dissent".

context: Human trafficking > Human trafficking in the United States > Human trafficking in California
text: Fourteen people are arrested in a sting operation by a joint task force at the San Diego Comic-Con in San Diego, California, United States, for participating in a sex trafficking network. Ten victims were recovered, including one teenager.

context: Human trafficking > Human trafficking in Spain
text: Twenty-six people are arrested by Spanish police in Madrid, Málaga, and Toledo for operating a sex trafficking ring that abused over 600 women. 32 women were freed during the operation.

Rioting occurs in Hartlepool, United Kingdom, reportedly in response to the Southport stabbing attack. At least eight people are arrested and a number of Cleveland Police officers are injured in the unrest.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Diving at the Summer Olympics
text: China surpasses the United States for the record of most gold medals in Olympic diving.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Guatemala at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Adriana Ruano wins the gold medal in women's trap shooting to set a new Olympic record and win the first gold medal for Guatemala in Olympic history.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > North Korea at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Kim Mi-rae and Jo Jin-mi win the silver medal in Women's synchronized diving, North Korea's first medal in the sport.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Novak Djokovic defeats Dominik Koepfer to advance to the quarterfinals of the Men's singles tournament, becoming the only player to reach the quarterfinals four times, and the oldest quarterfinalist in Olympic tennis history at the age of 37.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Siege of Gaza City
text: At least fifteen Palestinians are killed and 29 others are injured in an Israeli strike on a school in the Shuja'iyya neighborhood of Gaza City.
Israel claims to have verified that it killed Hamas military commander Mohammed Deif in an attack on al-Mawasi on July 13. Hamas denies the allegations.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Hezbollah fires dozens of Katyusha rockets at northern Israel.
Intel announces plans to lay off 15% of its workforce in order to reduce its operating costs.
South Korea reports that as many as 1,500 people may have been killed by floods in North Korea caused by the remnants of Typhoon Gaemi.
At least 12 people are killed and more than 250 people are declared missing after heavy downpours and flooding in northern India, with rainfall amounts of up to reported in some areas.
The death toll from the landslides caused by torrential rains in Kerala, India, increases to 296 people, with at least 240 others still missing.
The Global Famine Review Committee declares a famine in Darfur, Sudan, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification.

context: 2024 Russian prisoner exchange, Germany–Russia relations, Russia–United States relations
text: Russia and several Western nations, including Germany and the United States, conduct a major prisoner exchange mediated by Turkey, with ten prisoners being transferred to Russia, thirteen to Germany, and three to the United States. Journalist Evan Gershkovich, former marine Paul Whelan, and Russian opposition figure Vladimir Kara-Murza are among those freed.

China and India conduct a 30th round of talks in New Delhi, India, to resolve their ongoing border disputes, agreeing to speed up negotiations over the disputes and to maintain peace and tranquility in border regions.
The Moldovan government expels a Russian diplomat from the country over alleged espionage.

A criminal court in Guinea sentences former president and military leader Moussa Dadis Camara to 20 years in prison for crimes against humanity while suppressing an opposition rally in Conakry in 2009.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer addresses the nation following civil unrest in Southport, Hartlepool, and Whitehall, accusing the "far-right" of being behind the violence. Starmer also warns social media platforms to crackdown on misinformation.

Fourteen protestors are killed, four are injured and at least 31 are arrested, including a journalist, during nationwide protests that turned violent in Nigeria amid a cost-of-living crisis, which protestors blame on President Bola Tinubu's new reforms.
Russia withdraws from the Framework Convention for the Protection of National Minorities, originally established by the Council of Europe in 1995.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: American swimmer Katie Ledecky wins her 13th Olympic medal in swimming, becoming the first American female to do so and the second American to do so after Michael Phelps.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Novak Djokovic defeats Stefanos Tsitsipas to advance to the semifinals of the Men's singles tournament, becoming the only player to reach the semifinals four times, and the oldest semifinalist in Olympic tennis history.

context: Somali civil war > 2024 Lido Beach attack
text: Thirty-eight people are killed and 212 others are injured in a mass shooting and suicide bombing by al-Shabaab militants near the Beach View Hotel on Lido Beach in Mogadishu, Somalia.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: Five Syrian migrant workers are killed in IDF airstrikes and shelling of Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon.

context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict > Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
text: United States President Joe Biden deploys multiple U.S. military warships, troops, and other military assets to the Middle East to support Israel against potential attacks from Iran and its proxies.

Several global financial markets fall significantly, with the Dow Jones falling by 610 points after the United States Department of Labor reported that the unemployment rate increased to 4.3% in July, the highest since October 2021.
At least 11 people are killed in a fire in a residential-commercial building in Manila, Philippines.
Argentina recognizes Edmundo González as President-elect of Venezuela, becoming the third country to do so after the United States and Peru.

Rioting occurs in Sunderland, England, United Kingdom, as hundreds of far-right protesters attempt to march on a mosque and clash with riot police in the city centre. A police station and Citizens Advice bureau is set on fire by rioters.

Turkey blocks internet access to Instagram, following comments made by Turkish communications director Fahrettin Altun that condemned Meta Platforms for taking down Instagram posts offering condolences or expressing sorrow towards the assassination of Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh.

context: Mass surveillance in the United Kingdom
text: Several civil rights groups denounce proposals made by British Prime Minister Keir Starmer to grant British police nationalized live facial recognition technology and surveillance to charge people police consider significantly likely to participate in far-right riots, condemning the opportunism of the proposals, their potential racial and gender inaccuracy, and their possible use to target future legal protests.
A man is arrested by national police in Dublin, Ireland, following attacks on Government Buildings, The Custom House, and Áras an Uachtaráin.
Four men, including a police officer, are found shot to death near Cancún, Quintana Roo, Mexico.

The United States Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission file a joint lawsuit against TikTok and its parent company ByteDance for violating a law prohibiting companies to collect and use personal information of children under the age of 13.
Protests against President Bola Tinubu's economic reforms continue across Nigeria, as security forces fire tear gas at protestors and the government orders curfews across several northern states.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Novak Djokovic defeats Lorenzo Musetti to advance to the finals of the Men's singles tournament, becoming the only player to reach the finals four times, and the oldest finalist in Olympic tennis history.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Félix Auger-Aliassime to advance to the finals of the Men's singles tournament, becoming the youngest finalist in Olympic tennis history at 21 years old.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Individual Neutral Athletes at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Belarusian gymnast Ivan Litvinovich wins a gold medal in trampoline gymnastics, making him the first male neutral athlete to win a gold medal at the Summer Olympics.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: At least fifteen people are killed in an Israeli attack on a school sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood of Gaza City.
One killed and six were injured in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah launches rockets at Upper Galilee in northern Israel which are intercepted by Israel's Iron Dome and misses an Israeli airforce plane in Lebanese airspace.
The United States embassy in Beirut, Lebanon, urges its citizens to leave the country amid increasing tensions in the Middle East.
The Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin takes two Russian citizens hostage in Mbanga, Niger.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Economic impact of the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: S&P Global downgrades Ukraine's credit rating to "SD" for 'selective' default after Ukraine was unable to pay a US$34 million international bond payment, and also stating that Ukraine's credit rating could fall to "D", which would represent a complete default following restructuring of Ukraine's debt.
A record prolonged heat wave persists over Antarctica, with temperatures reaching higher than average in some areas during the middle of winter.
The Japanese Meteorological Agency issues excessive heat warnings for 37 of the 47 prefectures amid heat waves where at least 59 people have died from heat stroke since April.

context: Parole for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans
text: The Biden administration provisionally suspends all migrant permits allowing Venezuelans, Cubans, Haitians, and Nicaraguans to enter and stay in the United States for up to two years following suspicions of fraud by several migrant financial sponsors.
The Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam elects President Tô Lâm as the new General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, succeeding Nguyễn Phú Trọng, who died on July 19.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Dominica at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Thea LaFond wins the gold medal in the Women's triple jump, earning Dominica its first ever Olympic medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Philippines at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Carlos Yulo wins the gold medal in Men's floor gymnastics, the Philippines' first medal in the sport and the country's second ever gold medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Saint Lucia at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Julien Alfred wins the gold medal in the Women's 100 metres, earning Saint Lucia its first ever Olympic medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics, Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: American swimmer Katie Ledecky wins her ninth gold medal, tying with Soviet artistic gymnast Larisa Latynina's record of most gold medals by a female Olympian.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia said its armed forces captured the village of Novoselivka Persha in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy announces that the country has received its first F-16 fighter aircraft from NATO allies.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: At least 91 people are killed in violent clashes between anti-government protesters and police units across Bangladesh, as protestors call for Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to resign.
Two people are killed and two others are injured in a stabbing spree in Holon, Israel. The Palestinian perpetrator is subsequently shot and killed by Israeli police.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: At least four people are killed and 18 others are injured in an Israeli strike on the al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah in the Gaza Strip.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: An IDF officer and soldier is injured near Ayelet HaShahar in dozens of Hezbollah rocket attacks on IDF targets near Beit Hillel, Birkat Risha, Malkia and Ramya in northern Israel.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict
text: IDF strikes Hezbollah targets in Marjayoun, Hula and Zibqin, starts a fire in a power station in Taybeh and an IDF drone misses its target of a motorcyclist in Rab El Thalathine in southern Lebanon.

context: Foreign relations of Ukraine, Foreign relations of Mali
text: Mali cuts all diplomatic relations with Ukraine for providing intelligence to Tuareg rebels that enabled them to ambush and kill large numbers of Wagner Group mercenaries and Malian troops.

context: Malaysia–United Kingdom relations, 2024 United Kingdom riots
text: Malaysia issues a travel warning urging its citizens to not visit the United Kingdom due to ongoing violent riots.
More than 150 people are arrested following violent far-right riots targeting mosques and migrant infrastructure throughout the United Kingdom.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Novak Djokovic defeats Carlos Alcaraz in the Men's singles final to win the Olympic gold medal, becoming the third male player to achieve a singles Career Golden Slam.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini win the gold medal in the Women's doubles tournament, earning Italy its first gold medal in the sport and making Errani the oldest tennis player to achieve a Career Golden Slam.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Algeria at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Kaylia Nemour wins the gold medal in the Women's uneven bars, the first gold medal in gymnastics for Algeria.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Cape Verde at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Daniel Varela de Pina wins a bronze medal in Men's flyweight boxing, earning Cape Verde its first ever Olympic medal.

context: Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present) > Attacks on US bases in Iraq, Jordan, and Syria during the Gaza war > 2024 Al-Asad Airbase missile attack
text: At least five United States personnel are injured when two missiles strike the joint American–Iraqi Al Asad Airbase in al-Anbar Governorate, Iraq.

context: Gaza war > Israeli razing of cemeteries in the Gaza Strip
text: Israel returns 89 decomposed, unidentifiable Palestinian bodies to the Gaza Ministry of Health.
A Hezbollah militant and a Lebanese paramedic are killed in Israeli airstrikes on Meiss Ej Jabal, Shebaa, Rachaya Al Foukhar and an alleged Hezbollah weapons storage facility in Kafr Kila, Lebanon.
Hezbollah launches a drone to an IDF site near Malkia which was intercepted.
Ahead of expected retaliation against Israel for the assassination of Ismail Haniyeh, Iran issues a NOTAM, advising aircraft to change their routes over the country due to potential dangers en route.
Nearly 100 Congolese National Police officers flee to Uganda as fighting between M23 rebels and the Congolese military intensifies.

Separatist fighters shoot and kill a New Zealander helicopter pilot in Central Papua province, Indonesia, shortly after landing in the village of Alama. The four indigenous Papuans onboard the aircraft are later released.
The Houthis claim an attack on the Liberia-flagged container ship MV Groton in the Gulf of Aden.
Japan's Nikkei 225 stock market index falls by more than 12%, suffering its worst two-day decline ever and its largest daily percentage drop since Black Monday in October 1987.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, the S&P 500, and the Nasdaq Composite all fall by 3%, registering their biggest three-day declines since June 2022.
At least six people are killed in Florida, United States, by severe weather caused by Hurricane Debby.
At least thirteen people are killed by a rainfall-triggered landslide in Wolayita, Ethiopia.

context: 2024 Venezuelan presidential election > International reactions to the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election
text: The European Union joins the United States and several Latin American nations in refusing to accept the claimed Venezuelan presidential election victory of Incumbent President Nicolás Maduro.

Brazil becomes the representative of the interests of Argentina and Peru in Venezuela, after Venezuela expels the Argentinian and Peruvian diplomats following tensions in the aftermath of the presidential election.

context: International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war, Economic impact of the Israel–Hamas war
text: The United Kingdom provisionally suspends all arms exports to Israel, pending a policy review.
Rioting takes place in Plymouth and Birmingham, England, while police are attacked with molotov cocktails in Belfast, Northern Ireland, as the number of people arrested rises to 400.

Venezuelan Attorney General Tarek William Saab opens a criminal investigation into opposition officials Edmundo González and María Corina Machado for calling on the Armed Forces to abandon their support for President Nicolás Maduro throughout the protests and riots in the country.
District of Columbia District Judge Amit Mehta finds Google guilty of violating the Sherman Antitrust Act by illegally maintaining a monopoly over internet search.
Uganda Police arrest and charge fourteen Ugandan opposition officials and lawmakers with terrorism charges for participating in anti-government and anti-corruption protests last month.

The Hanoi People's Court in Vietnam sentences Bamboo Airways chairman and real estate business tycoon Trinh Van Quyet to 21 years in prison for defrauding investors of 3.6 trillion VNĐ (US$144 million).

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina resigns and flees to Delhi, India.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Protestors storm the prime minister's residence and the National Parliament building in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Chief of Army Staff Waker-uz-Zaman announces the formation of an interim government in Bangladesh and vows to launch an investigation into the government crackdowns.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's pole vault
text: Sweden's Armand Duplantis wins his second consecutive gold medal, breaking his own world record with a jump of .

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Colombia at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Ángel Barajas wins the silver medal in Men's horizontal bar, earning Colombia its first ever medal in gymnastics.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Belgium withdraws from the Mixed relay triathlon event after triathlete Claire Michel becomes ill days after she swam in the Seine river during the women's triathlon event.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Thailand at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Kunlavut Vitidsarn wins the silver medal in the Men's singles badminton event, earning Thailand its first medal in the sport.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukraine launches an incursion into Kursk Oblast, Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia claims that it captured the village of Tymofiivka in Donetsk Oblast.

Six IDF soldiers and 13 Israeli civilians injured in a Hezbollah drone strike and a malfunctioning of the Iron Dome on a highway in Mazra'a and Hezbollah launches rockets at IDF targets in Avivim, Birkat Rasha, Acre and the Golani Brigade of Egoz Unit in northern Israel.
Five Hezbollah militants killed in an Israeli airstrike on Mayfadoun, Lebanon.

context: Sudanese civil war > Siege of El Fasher
text: At least 53 people are killed and 60 others are injured in Rapid Support Forces raids on several neighborhoods in El Fasher and Gezira State, Sudan.
Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi accuses former President Joseph Kabila of backing the Alliance Fleuve Congo, a U.S-sanctioned coalition of rebel groups, whose main member is the M23.
Japanese whaling company Kyodo Senpaku announces the country's first fin whale kill in fifty years off the coast of Iwate Prefecture.
Japan's Nikkei 225 stock market index rises more than 10%, a day after declining by more than 12%.
At least 123 people, many of whom were elderly, are reported to have died from heat illnesses in the Greater Tokyo Area of Japan in July amid an ongoing heatwave in the country.
At least two people are killed when a hotel collapses in Kröv, Germany.

context: Foreign relations of Niger, Foreign relations of Ukraine
text: Niger suspends diplomatic relations with Ukraine over Ukraine's alleged support for rebels who ambushed and killed dozens of Malian soldiers and Russian mercenaries during the Battle of Tinzaouaten in July.

Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announces a visit to Moscow, Russia, from August 12–14 to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the peace process for the Gaza war and to "strengthen bilateral relations in all areas" between the two nations.
The European Union approves a grant of €4.2 billion (US$4.58 billion) in financial aid to Ukraine.

context: Gaza war protests > 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses
text: In the United States, Massachusetts District Judge Richard Stearns rules that Harvard University must face a lawsuit accusing the university of intentionally ignoring requests for safety from Jewish students following "severe and pervasive harassment" on campus, while also calling the university's claims that antisemitic acts are protected under the First Amendment "dubious".
Haredi Israelis storm the army base in Tel HaShomer in protest of compulsory conscription.

A court in Tunisia sentences opposition leader Abir Moussi to two years in prison for insulting the election commission. The court also sentences four potential presidential candidates, including activist Nizar Chaari, to eight months in prison and bans them from running for office on charges of vote buying.

context: Capital punishment in Iran, Mahsa Amini protests
text: The Iranian government executes a man who was convicted of killing an Islamic Revolutionary Guards officer during anti-government and mandatory hijab law protests in 2022.

context: Censorship in Germany, Israel–Hamas war protests in Germany
text: A court in Berlin, Germany, convicts a woman and fines her for "condoning a crime" by leading a chant using the phrase "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free" during a protest in October 2023.
Nigeria detains tailors who made Russian flags that were used in anti-government protests.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Bangladeshi President Mohammed Shahabuddin dissolves the national parliament in preparation for an interim government following the resignation and departure of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: President Shahabuddin names civil society leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus as the chief of the interim government.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > 2024 Democratic Party vice presidential candidate selection
text: Presumptive Democratic Party nominee Kamala Harris selects Minnesota Governor Tim Walz as her running mate.

context: Gaza war > Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
text: Yahya Sinwar is named the new leader of Hamas, following the assassination of Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Australia at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Fourteen-year-old Arisa Trew wins the gold medal in Women's park skateboarding, becoming the youngest Australian to ever win an Olympic gold medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Romanian Prime Minister Marcel Ciolacu announces he will boycott the closing ceremony of the Paris Olympics due to an initial judging error in another competitor's Women's floor gymnastics routine, which after being corrected, caused Romanian gymnast Ana Bărbosu to move from bronze medal position to 4th place.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Wrestling at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Cuban wrestler Mijaín López wins the gold medal in the Men's Greco-Roman 130 kg event, becoming the first Olympic athlete to win gold in the same event at five consecutive Olympic games and the first wrestler to win five gold medals in Olympic history.

context: Gaza war > 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel
text: The Israel Defense Forces confirms the death of Bilha Yinon, the last person missing in Israel following the attack by Hamas on October 7, 2023.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Six Palestinians are killed in an Israeli raid on the Maghazi refugee camp and in Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip.
Egypt and the United Kingdom issue NOTAM alerts and order their airlines to avoid Iranian and Lebanese airspaces.
Three killed and ten injured in Israeli airstrikes on Jwaya, Lebanon.
Hezbollah launches rockets on the Israeli-occuped Syrian Golan Heights and shelled an IDF outpost in Jal al-Allam, Israel.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russian Chief of General Staff Valery Gerasimov says that the Ukrainian advance into Kursk Oblast has been stopped as reports emerge of continued heavy fighting in the vicinity of Sudzha.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Acting Governor of Kursk Oblast Alexei Smirnov declares a state of emergency in the region.
Thirty people are killed, five are missing and hundreds are displaced after days of floods in Hodeidah and Hajjah, Yemen.
Five people, including four Chinese nationals, are killed in a helicopter crash in Nuwakot District, Bagmati Province, Nepal.
The Government of Brazil reports that deforestation in the Amazon Rainforest is at its lowest level since 2016.

context: Environmental threats to the Great Barrier Reef
text: The water temperature around the Great Barrier Reef is reported to have reached a 400-year record high, which is causing more mass bleaching events.

context: 2023 Thai general election > Lèse-majesté in Thailand
text: The Constitutional Court of Thailand orders the dissolution of the Move Forward Party, which won the most seats and votes in last year's election, but was blocked from forming a government, over the party's campaigning on Lèse-majesté decriminalization.
Nigeria arrests seven Polish nationals for raising Russian flags during anti-government protests this week.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: Turkey submits a bid to join South Africa's side in the International Court of Justice case against Israel's conduct in the Gaza Strip.
Police in Berlin, Germany, arrest a palliative care nurse for allegedly killing four elderly patients.
Russian-American Ksenia Karelina pleads guilty in a Russian court to a charge of treason.

Police in Austria arrest two men affiliated with the Islamic State for allegedly planning to commit a terrorist attack at American singer Taylor Swift's upcoming concerts at the Ernst-Happel-Stadion in Vienna, which are subsequently cancelled.

context: 2024 United States House of Representatives elections
text: Missouri Democratic congresswoman Cori Bush loses her primary election to St. Louis County prosecutor Wesley Bell, becoming the second member of the Squad to lose a primary.
Comorian president Azali Assoumani grants extensive powers to his son and alleged successor Nour El Fath, allowing El Fath to intervene in multiple stages of government decision-making.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > China at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: China wins their first gold medal in artistic swimming.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: French police detain Australian field hockey player Tom Craig for allegedly purchasing cocaine.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > India at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Indian wrestler Vinesh Phogat is disqualified from the final of the Women's freestyle 50 kg event for being above the stipulated weight during the weigh-in on the morning of the finals, eliminating her from the medal competition and relegating her to last place in the classification.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy appears to confirm ordering a major cross-border operation inside Russia, saying that "Russia brought war to our land, and it should feel what it has done".

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Large explosions are reported near the town of Rylsk in Kursk Oblast, Russia, with videos on social media appearing to show a destroyed column of military vehicles.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukraine launches twelve rockets and 14 drones into Russia, according to both acting Governor of Kursk Oblast Alexei Smirnov and the Russian Ministry of Defence.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian forces capture dozens of Russian soldiers in their offensive in Kursk Oblast. Russian authorities say that fighting is still ongoing for control of several settlements near the border.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian troops and tanks enter the town of Sudzha, forcing the local residents to flee.
One Lebanese civilian and a Hezbollah militant are killed and three Lebanese civilians are injured in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah fires 25 rockets at the Israeli-occupied Syrian Golan Heights and fifteen rockets at Shlomi and Kabri in Upper Galilee, Israel. All rockets are intercepted by the Iron Dome.
Tropical Storm Debby makes its second landfall near Bulls Bay, South Carolina, United States.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off the coast of Kyushu, Japan. A tsunami advisory is issued for parts of the islands of Kyushu and Shikoku.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Muhammad Yunus returns to Bangladesh to lead the country's interim government.

Former Catalan government president Carles Puigdemont returns to Barcelona, Spain, after seven years of "self-exile", defying an arrest warrant issued by the Supreme Court. Catalan regional police subsequently institute tight controls on traffic in and out of the city, as part of an attempt to arrest Puigdemont.
Two Mossos d'Esquadra officers are arrested for allegedly collaborating on Puigdemont's escape, following his public appearance in Barcelona.
Socialists' Party candidate Salvador Illa is elected as the new Catalan government president by the Parliament of Catalonia, becoming the first non-separatist president in more than 10 years.
YouTube is reportedly blocked and slowed down across Russia following the website's blocking of several channels that expressed support for the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Botswana at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Letsile Tebogo wins the gold medal in Men's 200 metres, earning Botswana its first ever gold medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Ecuador at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Lucía Yépez wins the silver medal in the Women's freestyle 53 kg wrestling event, the first medal in the sport for Ecuador.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Pakistan at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Arshad Nadeem wins the gold medal in Men's javelin throw, breaking the Olympic record and earning Pakistan its first ever medal in Athletics and its first ever individual gold medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Refugee Olympic Team at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Cindy Ngamba wins a bronze medal in Women's middleweight boxing, the first-ever medal won for the Refugee Olympic Team.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russia declares a "federal-level" emergency in Kursk Oblast as Ukrainian forces continue to advance.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Akhmat special forces commander Apti Alaudinov says that Ukrainian troops "simply passed-by" their positions without engaging them, with Akhmat troops choosing to retreat until more Russian reinforcements could arrive. Other reports indicate that Akhmat troops fled from Ukrainian forces.
sources: The New Voice of Ukraine via MSN

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: A Russian military convoy is destroyed on the E38 highway in Oktyabrsky District.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian troops capture the Gazprom gas facility in Sudzha. A video shows Ukrainian soldiers inside the natural gas facility, with much of the town reportedly under Ukrainian control.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukraine launches a "massive" drone attack on Lipetsk Oblast, Russia, with Lipetsk air base reportedly on fire. Several villages are evacuated, with six people reportedly injured.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign > 2024 Kostiantynivka supermarket missile attack
text: A Russian missile attack on a supermarket in Kostiantynivka, Donetsk Oblast, kills 14 people and injures 43 others.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The United States announces it will send Ukraine a $125 million military aid package, including FIM-92 Stinger missiles, artillery ammunition, and anti-armor systems.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Third Battle of Khan Yunis
text: Israeli troops launch a new assault on Khan Yunis, with airstrikes killing at least 21 Palestinians in the city and Israeli troops initiating ground operations in the city for the third time since the war's beginning.

context: Gaza war > United States support for Israel in the Gaza war
text: The United States finances Israel with $3.5 billion to spend on U.S. weapons and military equipment.
Samer al-Hajj, a Hamas security official for the Ain al-Hilweh Palestinian refugee camp, is assassinated by an Israeli drone strike in Sidon, Lebanon.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israeli occupation of the West Bank
text: The United States declares the Netzah Yehuda Battalion eligible for US military assistance. The unit is known for establishing illegal outposts on Palestinian land, and was removed from its traditional posting in the West Bank in 2022 due to human rights violations against Palestinians.
A Voepass Linhas Aéreas ATR 72-500 aircraft crashes in Vinhedo, São Paulo, Brazil, killing all 62 people on board.
Nine people are killed and 26 others injured after a bus crash in Polatlı, Turkey.
A military court in Sierra Leone sentences 24 soldiers to prison terms ranging from 50 to 120 years for their roles in a failed coup attempt in November 2023.

Prosecutors in China charge multiple funeral directors with selling more than 4,000 corpses to two major medical companies over several decades. Police seized 18 tonnes of bones and 34,000 semi-finished products, with the thieves having earned around 380 million yuan (US$53 million) before they were arrested.

context: Foreign relations of Mali, Foreign relations of Sweden, Mali–Russia relations
text: Mali orders the Swedish ambassador to leave within 72 hours, days after Sweden announced that development aid to Mali would be suspended over Mali's support for Russia.
The Biden administration partially lifts a three-year-old ban on American weapons sales to Saudi Arabia.
Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro suspends the X social network in Venezuela for 10 days, accusing X's owner Elon Musk of promoting hatred.

The Austrian interior minister announces the arrest of an Iraqi man in connection with a foiled terror attack at American singer Taylor Swift's concerts in Vienna, which were cancelled in response to the attack.
Hundreds of people protest in Dhaka, Bangladesh, against violence targeting the country's Hindu minority.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Algeria at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Imane Khelif wins the gold medal in the Women's 66 kg boxing event, after facing controversy and harassment related to a 2023 gender evaluation by the International Boxing Association, which is no longer recognized by the IOC.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: In the first-ever breakdancing event at the Olympics, Ami Yuasa of Japan wins the B-Girls gold medal, with Dominika "Nicka" Banevič of Lithuania winning the silver and Liu "671" Qingyi of China winning the bronze.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: French police arrest Egyptian wrestler Mohamed Ibrahim El-Sayed for allegedly groping a woman at a café.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russia introduces a "counter-terrorist regime" in Belgorod, Bryansk, and Kursk Oblasts in response to the ongoing incursion, resulting in travel restrictions and an increased security presence.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: The state-run Russian news agency TASS reports that over 76,000 residents have evacuated from Kursk Oblast this week.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian forces enter Belgorod Oblast for the first time during the ongoing incursion, reportedly capturing the village of Poroz.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The Ukrainian Navy strikes and heavily damages a Russian offshore natural gas platform in the Black Sea being used by the Russian Armed Forces.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarusian involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: President of Belarus Alexander Lukashenko increases Belarus's defensive presence on the Belarus–Ukraine border after accusing Ukraine of illegally sending about a dozen intercepted drones across the border into Belarusian airspace.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: One worker is killed and several others are injured in a Russian missile strike on a "critical infrastructure facility" in Kramatorsk.

Israeli rockets strike Al-Tabaeen school in Gaza City during Fajr morning prayers, killing more than 93 Palestinians and injuring 47 others, several of whom were trapped in the building as it was damaged by a fire.
Over seventy people are killed in an Arakan Army drone attack on Rohingya people fleeing Myanmar.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Religion and the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy announces governmental deliberations toward banning a traditionally Russia-linked branch of the Orthodox Church in Ukraine in order to strengthen the country's "spiritual independence".
Eighteen people are killed and fourteen others are rescued after a landslide at Kiteezi Landfill, a rubbish dump in Kampala, Uganda.

context: 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement > Non-cooperation movement
text: Chief Justice of Bangladesh Obaidul Hassan resigns following an ultimatum from protesters and is briefly succeeded by Md. Ashfaqul Islam on an acting basis. Syed Refat Ahmed is later appointed Chief Justice by President Mohammed Shahabuddin.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign
text: Officials of the Donald Trump campaign report that it was hacked by anonymous sources, with the campaign formally blaming "foreign sources", specifically claiming that Iran was behind the hacking.
Thousands of anti-racism protesters march in cities across the United Kingdom to protest against far-right riots, political figures, and the Reform UK party.
A petrol bomb is thrown towards an Islamic centre in Newtownards, County Down, Northern Ireland.

Tens of thousands of environmentalist and anti-Aleksandar Vučić protesters demonstrate in Belgrade, Serbia, to protest a European Union–backed plan to develop Europe's largest lithium mine in the Jadar valley.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Albania at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Chermen Valiev wins a bronze medal in Men's freestyle 74 kg wrestling, earning Albania its first ever Olympic medal.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: In the first-ever men's breakdancing event at the Olympics, Philip "Phil Wizard" Kim of Canada wins the B-Boys gold medal, with Danis "Dany Dann" Civil of France winning the silver and Victor Montalvo of the United States winning the bronze.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Three swimmers for Germany fall ill with vomiting and diarrhea and require outpatient treatment after swimming in the Seine as part of Olympic competitions.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Japan at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Rikuto Tamai of Japan wins a silver medal in Men's 10 metre platform diving, earning the country its first ever Olympic medal in the sport.

context: 2024 Summer Olympics > Uzbekistan at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Svetlana Osipova of Uzbekistan wins a silver medal in taekwondo the first ever Olympic medal obtained by a Uzbek female athlete in the sport.

context: Islamic State–Taliban conflict > 2024 Kabul bus bombing
text: At least one person is killed and eleven others are injured in an Islamic State minibus bombing in Dasht-e-Barchi, Kabul, Afghanistan.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Kyiv strikes
text: Two people, including a 4-year-old child, are killed and three others are injured in a Russian KN-23 ballistic missile attack in Kyiv, Ukraine.
The death toll from a landslide at the Kiteezi Rubbish Dump in Kampala, Uganda, increases to 21.
Two people are killed and twelve families are displaced in an explosion possibly attributed to a gas leak in Bel Air, Maryland, United States.

In a phone call with European Council President Charles Michel, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian accuses the European Union of facilitating Israeli crimes against humanity and terrorism in the Gaza Strip by implementing double standards that destabilize the Middle East and increase the chances of a global war.
Incumbent president Paul Kagame is sworn in for a fourth term in office.
The 2024 Summer Olympics conclude with the closing ceremony taking place at the Stade de France in Paris, France.
The United States finish atop the medal table with 40 gold medals and 126 total medals, ahead of China who finished with 40 gold medals and 91 total medals, with silver medals being the tiebreaker.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Acting Governor of Kursk Oblast Alexei Smirnov accuses the Ukrainian military of using chemical weapons that poisoned Russian civilians. Ukraine's State Security Service denies these claims and accuses Russia of falsifying war crimes.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian colonel general Oleksandr Syrskyi announces that Ukrainian forces now control over of Russia's Kursk region.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russian forces take the settlement of Lysychne in Donetsk Oblast.

context: 2024 Iran–Israel conflict, Israel–Hezbollah conflict > Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
text: United States Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin orders the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier strike group and the USS Georgia SSGN cruise-missile submarine to the Middle East to defend Israel from possible retaliation from Iran and to strengthen the U.S. military position in the region.

Hezbollah fires 30 Katyusha rockets targeting the IDF 146th Division headquarters in Ga'aton and an IDF surveillance station in Metula. An Israeli Iron Dome interceptor missile destroys an Avdon residence.

context: Gaza war > Third Battle of Khan Yunis
text: Ten Palestinians are killed in an Israeli airstrike on a residential home in Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip.

context: Damage of landmarks from climate change
text: The Double Arch, a natural arch made of 190 million-year-old rock in the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, collapses, possibly due to changing water levels and erosion.
Chevron Corporation delivers the first oil from a Gulf of Mexico oil field, drilled under extreme subsea pressure.
One person is killed and several others are injured when a helicopter stolen from Cairns Airport crashes into a hotel in Cairns, Queensland, Australia.
One person is killed and 132 others are injured after a magnitude 5.0 earthquake strikes Salamiyah, Homs Governorate, Syria.

context: United States support for Israel in the Gaza war
text: The Council on American–Islamic Relations files a lawsuit against the United States government and the FBI over alleged anti-Palestinian discrimination against two Palestinian Americans for placing them on a watch list despite having no violent crime convictions.
Pakistan Army officials arrest former Director-General of the Inter-Services Intelligence Faiz Hameed, accusing him of abusing his position of power and raiding a business last year.
A teenager stabs five people at a mosque in Eskişehir, Turkey.

context: 2024 United States presidential election, Twitter under Elon Musk
text: Former president and Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump comes back to X (formerly Twitter) for a two-hour interview with its owner Elon Musk, mainly focusing on Trump's 2024 presidential re-election campaign. .
The first Cabinet of Indonesia meeting session in Nusantara is held, marking the beginning of the transition of the official capital away from Jakarta.
Iranian Vice President Mohammad Javad Zarif resigns after 11 days in office, citing disappointment with his progress and the new Cabinet.
Liquid water is confirmed to be present at depths of below the surface of Mars, based on a new analysis of data from NASA's InSight lander.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukraine says that its troops are still advancing in Kursk Oblast and now control 74 settlements inside Russia. The Russian Defence Ministry says that its forces are fighting the Ukrainians about from the border.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Akhmat special forces commander Apti Alaudinov says that the Ukrainian advance into Kursk Oblast is currently stopped due to Russian counter-attacks.

context: Gaza war > United States support for Israel in the Gaza war
text: The United States government approves $20 billion in weapon sales to Israel, including fifty F-15 fighter jets and advanced upgrade kits for Israel's existing F-15 jets.

Two Hezbollah militants, three Lebanese civilians killed, 21 injured in Israeli airstrikes on Hezbollah targets in Baraachit, Tyre, Aabbassiyeh, Kfarkela, At Tiri and Marjayoun in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah launches rockets at Kfarchouba, Shebaa Farms, Shtula, Kiryat Shmona and Beit Hillel.

Israeli crowds led by far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir storm the Al-Aqsa Mosque and several villages in the West Bank on Tisha B'av. Israel Police officers reportedly offered protection to Israeli settlers, while the United States and the United Nations denounce the raids.
The Houthis storm the headquarters of the United Nation's Human Rights Office in Sanaa, Yemen, and detain Yemeni workers, and seize official documents.
Schools are canceled in Puerto Rico as Tropical Storm Ernesto is expected to strengthen into a hurricane overnight.
At least one person is killed and dozens of others are injured in wildfires across Greece, with evacuations ordered for residents in at least one area near Athens.
The death toll for the landslide in the Kiteezi Rubbish Dump in Kampala, Uganda, increases to 24.
At least 68 people are killed in Sudan's worst flooding since 2019, impacting several internally displaced person camps amid the ongoing Sudanese civil war.

context: Human rights in Austria, 2024 Vienna terrorism plot
text: Austrian Chancellor Karl Nehammer announces a package of new anti-terrorism measures, including granting Austrian security services the ability to monitor private communications sent on messaging and social media apps and decrypt encrypted messages, and restricting the right to assembly of groups declared "hostile to democracy".

Thousands of doctors and university students participate in walkouts and protests against sexual violence in cities across India after the alleged rape and murder of a female medical trainee in Kolkata last week.
Ford and Mazda issue warnings to owners of over 475,000 vehicles with Takata airbag inflators, cautioning them of the possibility for the inflators to explode with metal shrapnel.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukrainian forces have captured more than 100 Russian soldiers in the last 24 hours during their offensive in Kursk Oblast. Zelenskyy also says that he is open to exchanging the prisoners for Ukrainian prisoners of war.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukraine announces that it will create a strategic buffer zone on the Russia–Ukraine border that is "designed to protect our border communities from daily enemy attacks".

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russia evacuates thousands more civilians from borderlands in the Kursk Oblast amid deeper progression of the Armed Forces of Ukraine into the region.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian drones strike the Borisoglebsk air base in Voronezh Oblast, Russia, destroying several hangars.

context: Gaza war > Three-phase Israel–Hamas war ceasefire proposal
text: Top Hamas official Osama Hamdan states that the organization is "losing faith" in the United States' role as mediator in Israel–Hamas ceasefire proposals due to the U.S. not applying pressure on Israel to act in good faith, and threatens to withdraw from future U.S.-mediated negotiations.
Libya's House of Representatives vote to end the term of the Tripoli-based government led by Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh, declaring the eastern-based cabinet as the legitimate government.
Tropical Storm Ernesto strengthens into a hurricane north of Puerto Rico.

The World Health Organization officially declares a new outbreak of mpox. The strain of this outbreak is different from the primary strain of the 2022–2023 mpox outbreak, which affected thirteen countries and resulted in at least 524 reported deaths, and the new strain is more lethal.
Germany issues its first arrest warrant related to the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage for a Ukrainian man who crossed the border from Poland into Ukraine before the arrest could be carried out.

context: Illegal drug trade in the United States
text: The United States Drug Enforcement Administration announces that it seized more than of methamphetamines hidden in celery at a farmers market in Forest Park, Georgia, United States. A Mexican citizen was arrested in relation to the seizure.
Sweden, Denmark, Norway, and Finland form an international police hub in Stockholm to prevent escalating Swedish gang activity and criminal networks from spreading to other Nordic countries.
The Constitutional Court of Thailand dismisses Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin for illegally appointing a minister to his cabinet.
Former President of Argentina Alberto Fernández is indicted on charges of making threats and causing bodily harm to former first lady Fabiola Yáñez.
Kiribati citizens vote for the 45 members of the parliament.

Japan's Prime Minister and president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party Fumio Kishida announces that he will not run in the party’s presidential election scheduled for late September, effectively stepping down from the premiership.

After more than a year of high-level investigation, the Vatican expels Luis Fernando Figari, the leader of the Peruvian society of apostolic life Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, for financial corruption and for downplaying allegations of sexual and psychological abuse.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive > Ukrainian occupation of Kursk Oblast
text: Ukraine establishes a military administration in Sudzha with major general Eduard Moskalyov appointed as its senior commander. General Oleksandr Syrskyi says that the administration will "maintain law and order" in the region.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russia announces the mandatory evacuation of all civilians from Glushkovsky District in Kursk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: The Russian Defence Ministry claims that Russian forces have retaken the settlement of Krupets.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: The Security Service of Ukraine captures 102 Russian servicemen as prisoners of war, marking the largest single group of Russian soldiers to surrender during the conflict.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Ukrainian troops and military vehicles enter Russia's Belgorod Oblast with the region declaring a state of emergency. Heavy fighting is reportedly underway.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign > Pokrovsk offensive
text: Pokrovsk's military administration issues immediate evacuation orders for its citizens due to shelling from Russian troops about 10 km away from the city in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United Kingdom says that Ukraine can use British weaponry, including Challenger 2 tanks, for its military operations inside Russia.

context: Gaza war > Evacuations during the Gaza war
text: Peter Dutton, the leader of Australia’s Liberal Party, calls on the Australian government to ban the entry of Palestinian refugees fleeing from conflict in the Gaza Strip, which is met with significant condemnation from several politicians and organizations as promoting racial stereotypes.

context: Gaza war > Evacuations during the Gaza war
text: SBS World News reports that the Australian government has rejected a majority of Palestinian visa applications, accepting 2,922 applications and rejecting 7,111 applications while granting 8,746 visas to Israeli citizens and rejecting only 235 applications.

context: Gaza war > Casualties of the Gaza war
text: The Gaza Health Ministry reports that more than 40,000 Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, including more than 16,000 children, have been killed due to the ongoing Israeli invasion and blockade, and that more than 10,000 Palestinians are still missing.

Hezbollah launches four rockets at IDF targets in Shamir and Malkia in Upper Galilee which were intercepted by the Iron Dome causing a fire in Shamir and Ruwaysat al-Alam of Kfarchouba in southern Lebanon.
American video game magazine Game Informer discontinues publication after 33 years. The magazine's website is also shut down.
A Russian Air Force Tupolev Tu-22M crashes due to a "technical malfunction" in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia. The pilots safely ejected, according to Russian media.
Sweden reports the first case of the new mpox variant outside Africa in a patient in Stockholm.
Pakistan reports its first case of mpox this year.

context: Germany–United States relations, Foreign relations of NATO
text: The United States approves the sale of 600 MIM-104 Patriot air defense missiles to Germany worth US$5 billion (€4.6 billion) to improve German national defense and the overall security of NATO.

Ukraine denies its involvement in explosions that damaged the Nord Stream 2 pipeline in 2022 and accuses Russia of causing the explosions, following Germany issuing its first arrest warrant on the case towards a Ukrainian man.
New Zealand extradites German hacker and Megaupload founder Kim Dotcom to the United States to face charges for computer fraud, cyber espionage, and embezzlement.

Croatian Defence Minister Ivan Anušić announces that the country will reintroduce a compulsory 2-month military service starting from January 1, 2025, as part of it's reform of the Armed Forces of Croatia. Conscription was previously scrapped in 2008 when Croatia shifted to a volunteer-based system.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > 2024 United States presidential debates
text: The Democratic Party candidate for vice president Tim Walz and the Republican Party candidate for vice president JD Vance agree to a debate on October 1 on CBS.

context: 2024 Venezuelan presidential election > International reactions to the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election
text: Brazilian President Lula da Silva, Colombian President Gustavo Petro, and US President Joe Biden call for new elections in Venezuela.
Sri Lanka receives a record number of presidential candidates for the upcoming election with 39 applications accepted, surpassing 2019's record of 35 candidates.
The Edmonton Elks of the Canadian Football League are sold to businessman Larry Thompson, ending 75 years of community ownership.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Ukraine reports capturing 82 Russian settlements within an area of since the start of the Kursk incursion on August 6.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Over 120,000 Russian citizens have been evacuated according to Russia, and at least 100 Russian soldiers are captured according to Ukraine.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Russia accuses the United States and European nations of directly helping Ukraine in its incursion on Kursk Oblast by planning operations and providing military support, and states that their involvement "created all the prerequisites for Ukraine to lose its sovereignty and lose part of its territories".

A Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile strike on an airbase in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, destroys a MiG-29 jet that was equipped with Storm Shadow missiles. Ukraine's air force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat later confirms the loss of the aircraft on August 20. There are no casualties reported.

context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israeli occupation of the West Bank
text: One Palestinian is killed and many houses are burned down in a large organized Israeli settler raid on the village of Jit, Qalqilya Governorate, in the West Bank.
Sixteen people are killed and 20 more kidnapped during an attack by Allied Democratic Forces militants at agricultural lands in Mambasa, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Sixteen soldiers are killed and 18 more injured during a suicide car bombing in Mudiyah, Abyan Governorate, Yemen. Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula claims responsibility for the attack.
Thousands of people are ordered to evacuate in northern Japan as Typhoon Ampil approaches the country.
At least 54 people are killed in Chad after days of floods.
The first case of polio in the Gaza Strip in 25 years is confirmed, coming from an unvaccinated 10-month-old child in Deir al-Balah.
Eleven inmates are killed during shootouts with police after escaping from a jail in Saint-Marc, Haiti.

Bulgaria passes a new amendment by a large parliamentary majority that bans “propaganda, promotion, and incitement” of LGBT “ideas and views” in schools, sparking criticism from several European LGBTQ+ organizations stating that the law will marginalize LGBTQ+ children.
The Argentine Federal Police dismantle an alleged Islamist terrorist organization planning attacks against Jewish community centers in Mendoza.

context: 2024 United States presidential election > Cornel West 2024 presidential campaign
text: Independent presidential candidate Cornel West and his running mate Melina Abdullah are both disqualified from and refused entry on the 2024 Michigan presidential election ballot due to an improperly notarized form.
Luis Abinader is sworn in for a second term as President of the Dominican Republic.
The Thai House of Representatives selects Paetongtarn Shinawatra as the new Prime Minister, replacing Srettha Thavisin who was dismissed by the Constitutional Court on Wednesday.

context: Wow! signal, Search for extraterrestrial intelligence
text: The Wow! signal is found to have likely been caused by a rare astrophysical event, the sudden brightening of a cold molecular cloud triggered by a stellar emission.
sources: University of Puerto Rico at Arecibo

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > August 2024 Deir el-Balah attacks
text: Eighteen people from the same family are killed in an airstrike in the town of Az-Zawayda in the Gaza Strip.

context: Gaza war > Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war
text: Two senior Hamas militants are killed in an Israeli airstrike in Jenin in the occupied West Bank.

context: Gaza war > Three-phase Israel–Hamas war ceasefire proposal
text: Israeli officials state that they are attempting to "lower expectations" of a ceasefire deal due to significant gaps between Israel and Hamas demands, after United States president Joe Biden stated that he was "optimistic" about the progress of US-mediated negotiations in Qatar.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: Rockets launched by the Armed Forces of Ukraine destroy a Russian bridge over the Seym river in Glushkovo, Kursk Oblast. Russia's foreign ministry claims that the missiles were launched using Western-made rocket launchers and that the missiles killed volunteers who were evacuating Russian civilians.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Budget of Germany, Germany–Ukraine relations
text: Germany issues an indefinite ban on requesting or providing new military aid to Ukraine that has not already been approved in order to reduce federal budget spending. The moratorium results in a "tangible dispute" within the Scholz coalition government.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis
text: The International Atomic Energy Agency declares that the safety of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant is deteriorating, following an investigation into an explosive drone strike that targeted a perimeter access road at the power plant.
Ten Syrian citizens, including two children, are killed in an Israeli airstrike on a residential building in Nabatieh, Lebanon.
Hezbollah reportedly strikes the Ayelet HaShahar kibbutz in Upper Galilee, Israel, wounding two Israeli soldiers in retaliation.

context: Somali Civil War > 2024 Mogadishu tea shop bombing
text: At least 20 people are killed and ten others are injured in a bombing at a tea shop in Daynile District, Mogadishu, Somalia.
At least 85 people are killed in arson and looting attacks amid a rampage by Rapid Support Forces in the village of Galgani in Sennar State, Sudan.
The state electricity company of Lebanon Électricité du Liban runs out of fuel reserves and announces that it can no longer supply power to the country, leading to a complete nationwide blackout.
A 7.2-magnitude earthquake strikes off the eastern coast of Kamchatka Krai, Russia with a tsunami warning being issued.
A Fouga Magister aircraft operated by the French Air Force performing an air show crashes off the coast of Le Lavandou, France, killing the pilot.
Six people are arrested in connection to a mass shooting due to feuds that occurred last week in Clarendon Parish, Jamaica, which killed eight people and injured nine others.
Four convicts escape in a prison break at a psychiatric hospital in Straubing, Bavaria, Germany.
For the first time, the Indonesian Independence Day ceremony is held simultaneously in Jakarta and Nusantara due to the relocation of the country's capital.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine > 2024 Kursk offensive
text: The Armed Forces of Ukraine destroy a second bridge over the Seym river in Zvannoye.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarusian involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko reports that nearly one third of the Belarusian Army has been deployed along the Belarus–Ukraine border, in response to Ukraine stationing more than 120,000 troops at the border. However, Ukraine claims no movement of Belarusian troops has been observed.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: The Russian Ministry of Defence claims that Russian forces have captured the village of Svyrydonivka in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
The Central Bank of Libya suspends all operations following the kidnapping of the head of its information technology department by an unknown party.
A bomb explodes in Tel Aviv, Israel, killing one person and injuring another.

Record rainfall strikes regions of the Austrian capital of Vienna with most of the city's average total summer rainfall falling in just one hour, causing significant flooding and damage throughout the city.

Ongoing nationwide blackouts in Lebanon caused by fuel shortages provoke significant governmental conflict, with the Minister of Energy blaming the Central Bank for not paying Iraq for fuel imports and the Central Bank blaming Parliament for not authorizing emergency fund transfers for fuel payments.

More than 100 people are killed during nearly three weeks of persistent heavy rainfall and flooding across Yemen, with the country's national weather agency declaring a severe weather alert for future "very heavy thunderstorms".
At least eight family members are killed when their van collides with a delivery truck in Sariaya, Quezon, Philippines.
An oil spill originating from the El Palito refinery in Puerto Cabello, Venezuela, is reported to have contaminated more than of the Gulf of Paria as well as most of Morrocoy National Park.
Twenty medical students from the University of Jos and the University of Maiduguri are kidnapped while traveling in Benue State, Nigeria.
Venezuelan opposition officials and supporters gather in cities across the country to protest against President Nicolás Maduro and the results of the 2024 presidential election.

President of Vietnam and General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Tô Lâm arrives in China for a three-day state visit, Tô's first overseas visit since becoming president and general secretary.
In cycling, Katarzyna Niewiadoma wins the 2024 Tour de France Femmes by four seconds, her first win at the event after placing third at the 2022 and 2023 events.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign > Pokrovsk offensive
text: Ukrainian officials order the immediate evacuation of the remaining 53,000 citizens in Pokrovsk due to the advancement of the Russian Armed Forces.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Eastern Ukraine campaign
text: Russia captures the city of Zalizne and the Vyimka railway station in Donetsk Oblast.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Belarusian involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Belarus announces that it has further increased its Belarus–Ukraine border presence against Ukraine significantly, adding aircraft and air defense forces following its accusations of Ukraine's military sending 120,000 troops to its border and conducting "aggressive policies". Ukraine denies Lukashenko's claims, stating its forces have not observed unusual movements of Belarusian troops on the border.

An Israeli soldier is killed and several others are injured in Hezbollah rocket launches at IDF positions in Ya'ara and Biyadh Blida, with Burkan missiles and drone strikes in Western Galilee being intercepted by the Iron Dome. Hezbollah claims that it attacked and repelled Israeli soldiers attempting to infiltrate southern Lebanon through the Hadab Aita forest and had inflicted casualties.
