text: SDF forces clash with the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army near Tell Abyad, Raqqa Governorate and in Manbij District, Aleppo Governorate, as pro-government forces withdraw from the region, leaving a power vacuum.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives
text: Local forces in Talbiseh, northern Homs Governorate, attack Syrian Army convoys withdrawing towards Homs, seizing control of the town's checkpoint and burning it following pro-government forces withdrawal.

context: Syrian civil war > Southern Syria offensive
text: South Syrian rebel groups announce a new offensive on Daraa Governorate and Suwayda Governorate with the goal of implementing a pincer movement on Damascus.

context: Arab–Israeli conflict > Gaza war > Gaza war hostage crisis
text: Hamas releases a propaganda video showing Israeli American hostage Edan Alexander.
An Israeli airstrike on a car in the Gaza Strip kills five people, including employees of World Central Kitchen.
Two people are killed and six others are injured in three airstrikes by Israel in southern Lebanon that occurred despite the ceasefire with Hezbollah.
The Rapid Support Forces announce a civil administration formed by a prime minister and a 90-member legislative council.

At least nine people are killed and four others are injured after an attack in a commercial zone in Apaseo el Grande, Guanajuato, Mexico. Local authorities say the attack relates to the drug sales in the region.
Vietnam approves a US$67 billion high speed rail line from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, which will be an updated version of the North–South express railway proposal.
At least 27 people are killed and more than 100 others are missing when a boat capsizes in the Niger River in Kogi State, Nigeria.

Police arrest eight people linked to an explosion on a canal near Zubin Potok, Mitrovica District, Kosovo, that supplies water to the country's two main power plants. The Kosovar government blames Serbia for the "terrorist" acts, which Serbia denies.

A student attacks his classmates with a hammer and injures two before being subdued by other students at a high school in Guadalajara, Jalisco, México. The attack was streamed on X, where the perpetrator published Nazi views and other violent content.

More than 100 demonstrators are arrested in Tbilisi, Georgia, while protesting against Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze's decision to temporarily suspend the country's accession plans to the European Union to 2028.
Citizens of Iceland vote in a snap election to elect the 63 members of the Althing national parliament.
In association football, Botafogo win their first Copa Libertadores title after defeating Atlético Mineiro 3–1 in an all-Brazilian final at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Battle of Aleppo > 2024 Aleppo University Hospital airstrike
text: Twelve people are killed and 23 others are injured in Russian airstrikes on a hospital in Aleppo, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Battle of Aleppo
text: Turkish-backed militants say that they captured Aleppo's Ramouseh district as well as the city of As-Safira and the town of Khanasir in Aleppo Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives
text: At least nine people are killed and at least 62 others are injured in Russian airstrikes on Idlib.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives
text: The Syrian National Army says that they captured the city of Tell Rifaat and Menagh Air Base in Aleppo Governorate.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: The Rapid Support Forces establish a civilian administration in the Sudanese capital of Khartoum, including the adjacent cities of Omdurman and Khartoum North.
Clashes between FARC dissident groups Raúl Reyes Front and Frontera Commands leave twelve militants dead in Puerto Guzmán, Putumayo Department, Colombia.

context: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sectarian violence in Pakistan
text: The number of people killed during sectarian violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, during the last ten days has increased to 130.
A Malian army drone strike in Tinzaouaten kills eight leaders of the Strategic Framework for the Defense of the People of Azawad coalition.
Nineteen people are killed by Cyclone Fengal in India and Sri Lanka.
U.S. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan says that the United States will not return the nuclear weapons that they dismantled to Ukraine.

At least 56 people are killed during a stampede at a football match in Nzérékoré, Guinea, after the police tear gassed the field as rival fans stormed it following a controversial referee decision. A police station is later set ablaze.

context: Weiss special counsel investigation, Federal pardons in the United States
text: United States President Joe Biden pardons his son Hunter Biden of tax and firearms charges.
Seventy-nine people are injured in football hooliganism clashes between fans of FC Carl Zeiss Jena and BSG Chemie Leipzig following a match in Jena, Thuringia, Germany.
In Iceland, the Social Democratic Alliance wins 15 seats in the Althing elections, with the incumbent Independence Party winning 14 seats. However, no party achieved a majority.
Citizens of Liechtenstein vote in a referendum to form a state pension fund. The vote passes with a 52.6% majority.
Romanians vote for the 330 seats of the Chamber of Deputies and the 136 seats of the Senate.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza war hostage crisis
text: Hamas says that 33 hostages have been killed in the 14 months since the war started.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza war hostage crisis
text: The Israel Defense Forces say that Israeli-American soldier Omer Maxim Neutra, previously believed to be a living hostage, was killed during the October 7 attacks last year and his body was kept in Gaza.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza war hostage crisis
text: U.S. President-elect Donald Trump says there will be "all Hell to pay" if all the hostages are not released prior to the start of his second term.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: The Gaza Health Ministry says that around 37 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in the past 24 hours, increasing the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 44,466.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2024 Lebanon war
text: Despite the ceasefire, Israel and Hezbollah exchange fire, with Israel targeting Talousa and Haris in Lebanon, killing at least eleven people.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom
text: Significant populations of Kurds in Syria are displaced from the northern Aleppo countryside, after factions of the Turkish-backed National Army take control of Kurdish-held territories.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken announces that the United States will provide Ukraine with a $725 million weapons package.

context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency, Kivu conflict
text: At least 10 people are killed during an attack by Allied Democratic Forces gunmen in Batangi-Mbau, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Several houses are burned.
Six suspected New People's Army guerrillas, including two ranking leaders of a regional committee, are killed in an encounter in Las Navas, Northern Samar, Philippines.
Workers of the German metalworkers' union IG Metall begin a labor strike after failed negotiations with Volkswagen following the closure of three automotive manufacturing plants.

context: COVID-19 pandemic > COVID-19 pandemic in the United States
text: The U.S. House of Representatives Oversight and Accountability Committee releases their final reports on the COVID-19 outbreak in the United States investigating the origins of COVID-19, Operation Warp Speed's vaccination program, and mask mandates and lockdowns.
Georgian police arrest opposition leader Zurab Japaridze, accusing his party of "coordinating violence" during the protests against Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze.

Australian Federal Police announces they have arrested thirteen men, including the vice president of the outlaw Comanchero Motorcycle Club and two teenagers, for illegally smuggling 2.34 tonnes of cocaine into the country after their fishing boat broke down off the coast of Urangan, Queensland, Australia.
Forty-four children are injured, including one critically, when a person sprays an unknown gas inside a school in Berlin, Germany.
Three people are killed and eight others are injured after a mass shooting at a gathering in Gage Park, Chicago, Illinois, United States.

In Ireland, Fianna Fáil remains the largest party in Dáil Éireann, increasing its number of seats to 48. Its governing partner Fine Gael wins 38 seats, with the two parties combined winning 86 seats, two shy of a majority.

The Constitutional Court of Romania upholds the results of the first round of the presidential elections following a recount last week after far-right independent candidate Călin Georgescu won a plurality of the vote, triggering a run-off.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: Rebel forces capture the city of Suran, the towns of Halfaya and Taybat al-Imam, and the village of Maardis in Hama Governorate, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) capture seven villages and the town of Khasham in Deir ez-Zor Governorate from pro-government forces. The US-led CJTF–OIR coalition aircraft also launch airstrikes against Syrian government forces in support of the SDF offensive.
The Government of Canada officially designates the Yemen-based Houthi movement as a terrorist organization due to the group's attacks on civilian and military vessels in the Red Sea.

context: 2024–2025 floods in Southeast Asia and South Asia
text: At least 31 people have been killed by flooding in Thailand and Malaysia in the past five days.
Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo announce an investigation into the deaths of 143 people from a flu-like disease in the Province of Kwango.

A court in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, upholds the death penalty for real estate tycoon Trương Mỹ Lan after Lan was found guilty of embezzling $12.5 billion through the Sai Gon Joint Stock Commercial Bank.
The South Korean tourism ministry announces that 38 Vietnamese citizens have gone missing from Jeju Island before their flight back to Vietnam on November 17.

During an emergency address to the nation, South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol declares martial law in order to clear out alleged "threats posed by North Korean communist forces and to eliminate anti-state elements." Yoon says that the decision to declare martial law was made in order to "remove North Korean forces" and to protect South Korea's "liberal constitutional order".

South Korean Army general Park An-su is appointed Martial Law Commander by Yoon Suk Yeol, with Park announcing that media organizations will be subject to military control and that protests will be banned.
Protesters clash with police while attempting to storm the National Assembly building in Seoul.

In defiance of the declaration of martial law, which prohibits political activities, the National Assembly votes unanimously to order Yoon Suk Yeol to lift martial law. Korean soldiers that were guarding the National Assembly building withdraw following the vote.
Yoon Suk Yeol announces that he will lift the martial law that he declared hours earlier amid staunch opposition from both the opposition and his own People Power Party.
Palestinian officials announce that Fatah and Hamas are close to reaching an agreement on appointing a technocratic committee to govern the Gaza Strip following the end of the Gaza war.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > 4 December 2024 al-Mawasi attack
text: Two Israeli Air Force strikes on an evacuation zone in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip kill at least 20 refugees due to explosions and a subsequent fire that destroyed several refugee shelters.

context: Gaza war > Israeli incursions in the West Bank (2023–present) > Israeli settler violence, Legality of Israeli settlements
text: Israeli settlers attack Huwara and Beit Furik in Nablus Governorate, West Bank, and sets fire to several buildings and vehicles. The attacks are in retaliation to Palestinians destroying illegal farming outposts.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: Rebels capture the town of Al-Saan and the villages of Shaykh Hilal and Suruj in Hama Governorate, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: Heavy fighting is reported in and around Hama as rebel forces enter the city and capture three neighbourhoods.

A Russian Navy warship fires warning shots at a German helicopter conducting a routine patrol over the Baltic Sea, forcing the helicopter pilots to make evasive maneuvers. German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock condemns the incident as part of Russia's hybrid warfare against NATO.
The Pakistan Army kills five jihadist insurgents and captures two others in a raid in Lakki Marwat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Another round of blackouts in Cuba leave millions of households without power. The energy ministry says that it is prioritizing restoring electricity to hospitals and water pumping facilities.
An Iranian Air Force training jet crashes in Fars province, Iran, killing both pilots.

Krygyzstan National Security official Kamchybek Tashiev and Tajikistan National Security official Saimumin Yatimov announces that both countries have signed an agreement that would end 33-years of conflict at the border.
German police, French security services, and Interpol conduct coordinated mass raids on an Iraqi-Kurdish human trafficking network in North Rhine-Westphalia and Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany.

The CEO of American health insurance company UnitedHealthcare Brian Thompson is assassinated by a masked gunman while attending a business conference in Manhattan, New York City, New York, United States.

Two kindergarten students are critically injured in a suspected religious hate crime school shooting at a private Protestant school in Palermo, California, United States, before the gunman commits suicide.
Twelve neo-Nazis are arrested in police raids across Italy.
The National Assembly begins impeachment proceedings against Yoon Suk Yeol in response to Yoon's attempt to impose martial law in South Korea.

The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and other professional unions in South Korea announce a labor strike on December 5 and 6 in response to President Yoon Suk Yeol's surprise declaration of martial law yesterday, calling for Yoon's resignation.
The South Korean won drops to a two-year low following Yoon Suk Yeol's declaration of martial law yesterday. Several ETFs on the Korea Exchange also drop to a one-year low.
Foreign embassies in Seoul warn their citizens to stay away from mass demonstrations, citing the possibility of violence and death.

context: 2024 French political crisis > Collapse of the Barnier government
text: In France, the Barnier government collapses after 331 of 577 deputies vote in favor of a no-confidence motion, the first time since 1962 that the government has collapsed following a no-confidence motion. The left subsequently calls on President Emmanuel Macron to resign and hold early presidential elections.

Ahali party leader Nika Gvaramia is arrested in a police raid on his office in Tbilisi, Georgia. The arrest comes as the government continues to crack down on the opposition in response to protests against delaying negotiations to join the European Union. More than 100 demonstrators are also injured during clashes with riot police in Tbilisi.

The Electoral Commission of Namibia certifies the results of the general election, announcing Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah of the ruling SWAPO party as the new President, the first female president in the country's history.
Activists file a second impeachment complaint against Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte over alleged misuse of government funds.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: The Syrian Army says that it has withdrawn from the city of Hama in order to "protect the lives of civilians" after rebel forces enter the city. Rebel forces later begin releasing hundreds of prisoners from Hama's central prison.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: A helicopter is shot down after taking off from Hama Air Base as pro-government forces evacuate the airbase. Another helicopter that took off from the air base makes an emergency landing after being hit. The airbase is later fully captured by the rebels.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: Rebel forces enter the city of Salamiyah in Hama Governorate after reportedly facing no resistance.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Hama offensive
text: Rebels capture the town of Qamhana and Jabal Zayn al-Abidin mountain in Hama Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: Syrian rebel forces capture and take military vehicles and ammunition from a Syrian military engineering battalion facility on the outskirts of the city of al-Rastan in Homs Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: A Russian jet launches an airstrike on the Rastan Bridge over the Orontes River in an attempt to impede the rebel advance on Al-Rastan.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: Rebel forces take control of the town of Talbiseh in Homs Governorate as they advance south toward Homs.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Gaza genocide
text: Amnesty International accuses Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Israel rejects the accusation, referring to Amnesty's statements as "fake news."

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Kamal Adwan Hospital sieges
text: An Israeli airstrike near the Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza kills a 16-year-old Palestinian boy and injures at least 12 others.

context: Piracy off the coast of Somalia
text: The European Union's anti-piracy mission says that heavily armed Somali pirates have hijacked a Chinese fishing vessel off the coast of Puntland, Somalia.
German workers' union IG Metall announces they will go on extended strikes next week leading up to a fourth round of negotiations with Volkswagen.
The value of a Bitcoin surpasses US$100,000 for the first time, after increasing 130% in the past year.
British multinational oil and gas company Shell and Norwegian state-owned company Equinor announce a joint venture to merge their North Sea assets.
A 7.0 magnitude earthquake strikes offshore near the northern coast of California, United States.

context: Winter of 2024–25 in the Gaza Strip
text: Heavy winter rainfall causes extensive flooding across Gaza, with a majority of tents in several refugee camps being destroyed.
Eight people are killed when a cargo truck loaded with fertilizers hits pedestrians and crashes into a house in Makilala, Cotabato, Philippines.

The Mexican health department reports that thirteen children have died from a bloodstream infection caused by Klebsiella oxytoca found in contaminated IV bags in Mexico state, Mexico. Seven children remain hospitalized.
Michel Barnier resigns as Prime Minister of France following the collapse of the Barnier government.

context: European Union Space Programme > Copernicus Programme
text: The European Space Agency (ESA) successfully launches the Vega C rocket carrying the Sentinel-1C satellite to monitor Earth from the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, French Guiana, two years after its failed commercial flight.

ISRO successfully launches the PSLV-XL rocket carrying the European Space Agency's PROBA-3 satellites from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, India, in a solar observatory mission to gather data about the Sun's atmosphere.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: After capturing the town of Talbiseh and the city of Al-Rastan, rebel forces capture several more towns and villages in the northern countryside of Homs Governorate, Syria, reaching the town of Al-Dar al-Kabirah and approaching the outskirts of Homs.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: Russian and Syrian warplanes bombard rebel-held areas in Homs Governorate, killing at least 20 people.

context: Syrian civil war > Southern Syria offensive
text: Syrian Army soldiers from the 8th Armoured Division in Daraa defect to the Syrian opposition as rebels launch attacks on pro-government checkpoints across Daraa Governorate, taking control of several towns, including Inkhil, Ghabaghib, and al-Jiza, as well as the city of Jasim. Rebels later claim near total control of the governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > Southern Syria offensive
text: Rebels take full control of the city of Daraa after agreeing to allow Ba'ath Party officials to leave the city with safe passage to Damascus, and also take full control of the mainly Druze city of Suwayda.

context: Syrian civil war > Southern Syria offensive
text: Jordan closes its border with Syria after rebel forces seize the main Nasib Border Crossing.

context: Syrian civil war > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces take control of Deir ez-Zor and its airport following the withdrawal of pro-government forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: Iraqi militias withdraw from the Syrian side of the Al-Qa'im border crossing on the border with Iraq.
Russia tells its citizens to leave Syria on commercial flights while they still can amid rebel advances in the country.

context: Syrian civil war > Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war
text: Turkey freezes the assets of deceased former commander of Tahrir al-Sham Abu Maria al-Qahtani, who was killed in April, to comply with the United Nations Security Council's policies.
Tahrir al-Sham leader Abu Mohammad al-Julani says that his forces will not end their military campaign until Syrian president Bashar al-Assad is removed from power.
Egypt and Jordan both urge Bashar al-Assad and his family to leave Syria, saying that Assad can no longer stop the rebel offensive.
The Indian Ministry of External Affairs advises its citizens to leave Syria and avoid all travel to the country indefinitely.

context: Gaza war > Kamal Adwan Hospital sieges
text: Israeli drone strikes on the northern and western sides of the Kamal Adwan Hospital in Beit Lahia in the Gaza Strip kill at least 29 Palestinians. Israeli forces subsequently raid the hospital, killing four doctors.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Southern front of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Russian missile strike kills ten civilians in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, and injures four others, including two children. Separately, a missile attack on an administrative building in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, kills two people and injures 16 others.
The European Union and Mercosur trade bloc finalize a free trade deal in Montevideo, Uruguay, after 25 years of negotiations.
Millions of people receive emergency alerts in the United Kingdom as Storm Darragh prepares to make landfall over the British Isles.
Twenty-six people are killed and 28 more injured after a collision between two minibuses in Brokoua, Ivory Coast.
New Zealand Police presume that two Americans and a Canadian are dead after evidence suggests they fell while attempting to summit Mount Cook (Aoraki), suspending search operations.

context: Belarus–Russia relations, Nuclear risk during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko sign an agreement in Minsk, Belarus, offering security guarantees to Belarus including nuclear security and the possible use of Russian nuclear weapons in order to repel aggressions.
Two people are injured in an arson attack on a synagogue in Melbourne, Australia.

context: Restrictions on TikTok in the United States
text: A United States court of appeals upholds the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, which requires China-based company ByteDance to sell TikTok by January 19 or face an effective ban on operations in the United States.
Arubans vote to elect the 21 members of the Parliament. The Aruban People's Party wins nine seats and the People's Electoral Movement wins eight seats, neither parties achieving a majority.

An uncontested election is held for the President of Mauritius, with former minister of education and Labour Party representative Dharam Gokhool winning without contest. Robert Hungley is elected Vice-President.
The Constitutional Court of Romania annuls the first round results of the presidential election vote two days before the second round of the election.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: Turkish-backed Syrian National Army forces conduct extensive drone strikes and artillery shelling on villages near U.S.-backed Kurdish Syrian Democratic Forces positions in the city of Manbij in Aleppo Governorate, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: The Military Operations Command coalition led by Tahrir al-Sham says that a military operation to capture Damascus is underway with rebels reportedly advancing on the capital on several fronts.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: Rebel forces capture the cities of Al-Dumayr and Yabroud and the town of Sa'sa' in Rif Dimashq Governorate as the Syrian Defense Ministry denies reports that its troops are abandoning positions in the Damascus countryside.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: Syrian security officials and Arab officials say that First Lady of Syria Asma al-Assad fled with her three children to Russia last week. However, amid conflicting reports, Syrian state television says that President Bashar al-Assad remains in Damascus.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: United Nations Special Envoy for Syria Geir Otto Pedersen calls for an "orderly political transition" from the collapsing Syrian government to the Syrian opposition in order to end the conflict.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: A statue of former Syrian president Hafez al-Assad is toppled in the Damascus suburb of Jaramana.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Southern Syria offensive
text: The Syrian Armed Forces announce a complete withdrawal from the Daraa and Suwayda Governorates in order to reinforce Damascus.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Southern Syria offensive
text: Rebel forces capture the city of Al-Sanamayn in Daraa Governorate and also capture the city of Quneitra.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > 2024 Homs offensive
text: Rebel forces enter the city of Homs, eventually capturing the city after hours of urban warfare to oust Assad loyalists. Rebels also capture Homs Central Prison and release around 3,500 prisoners.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: More than 1,000 Syrian soldiers seeking refuge cross into Iraq through the Al-Qa'im border crossing according to Iraqi authorities.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Palmyra offensive
text: The U.S.-backed Revolutionary Commando Army takes control of the city of Palmyra in Homs Governorate following heavy fighting with pro-government forces. Rebels also capture the towns of Al-Sukhnah and Al-Qaryatayn in Homs Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives
text: The Syrian Army withdraws from the cities of Al-Hasakah and Qamishli in Al-Hasakah Governorate, transferring control of the Kurdish-majority cities to the Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Iranian intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: Iran begins to evacuate military personnel, diplomatic staff, and civilians from Syria amid rebel advances.

context: Syrian civil war > Refugees of the Syrian civil war
text: The UN World Food Programme reports that the renewed conflict in Syria is estimated to displace around 1.5 million Syrians.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war
text: At least 20 people, including six children, are killed in Israeli airstrikes on the Nuseirat refugee camp in Deir al-Balah Governorate, Gaza.

Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani says at the Doha Forum that his country is seeing a momentum build up for a ceasefire to end the conflict between Israel and Hamas in the Gaza Strip.
Six Pakistan Army soldiers and 22 Tehreek-e-Taliban militants are killed in clashes near the Afghan border.
Six soldiers are killed and seven are injured after a mass shooting at a military checkpoint in Kurram District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Two people are killed by falling trees in England and more than 1.5 million people experience power outages in Ireland and the United Kingdom as Storm Darragh hits the British Isles.
Five people are killed, four others are injured, and several others are missing in an explosion that destroyed several apartments in The Hague, Netherlands.

context: Cross-strait relations, Chinese intelligence activity abroad
text: Prosecutors in Taiwan charge four soldiers with espionage, accusing the soldiers of passing photographs of Taiwan's military capability to Chinese agents in exchange for money between 2022 and 2024.

context: 2024 South Korean martial law crisis > Attempted impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol
text: A vote to impeach South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol fails in the National Assembly due to a boycott of the vote by members of Yoon's People Power Party.
President Yoon Suk Yeol apologizes to the South Korean population, promising that he will not avoid legal sanctions or institute martial law a second time.
Over 100 Indian farmers march from Punjab to the capital city New Delhi to demand for the legal assurance of a minimum support price for all crops as well as loan forgiveness for farmers.
Punjab Police set up barricades and fire tear gas at the marching farmers as they enter Haryana, causing them to turn around and return to Shambhu, Punjab.
Ghanaians vote to elect the President and the 275 members of the Parliament.
Former Workers' Party Secretary-General and longest-serving opposition Member of the Parliament of Singapore Low Thia Khiang announced retirement in politics ahead of the election.
Interim President and military junta leader of Burkina Faso Ibrahim Traoré dismisses Prime Minister Apollinaire J. Kyélem de Tambèla and dissolves the government.

The Iranian Space Agency successfully launches the Simorgh rocket carrying two satellites and the Saman-1 space tug from the Imam Khomeini Space Launch Terminal in Semnan, Iran, the heaviest payload ever launched in Iran.
In association football, the Los Angeles Galaxy defeat the New York Red Bulls 2–1 to win a record 6th championship.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Syrian President Bashar al-Assad leaves the country on a flight from Damascus International Airport to Moscow, Russia.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Russian state media reports that Bashar al-Assad is in Moscow, and that he and his family have been granted asylum by the Russian government.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Senior Syrian government officials are reportedly in talks with the Syrian opposition and are preparing to defect.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Syrian Prime Minister Mohammad Ghazi al-Jalali says that he is not leaving Syria and will commit to a peaceful transition of power to the Syrian opposition. Al-Jalali also calls on rebel forces to not damage state institutions in Damascus or to harm civilians.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: The Syrian Army says that Bashar al-Assad's rule has ended and orders all of its troops to lay down arms and stop fighting.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Syrian rebels seize state television and announce to the nation that Bashar al-Assad has been toppled and that a new government will be formed.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Rebel forces seize the Presidential Palace in Damascus, which is later looted by armed soldiers and civilians.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: Rebel forces take control of Sednaya Prison and begin releasing thousands of prisoners, including many political prisoners.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: Thousands of Damascus residents gather in Umayyad Square to celebrate the collapse of the Assad regime.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: A video posted to X shows Syrians tearing down posters of former Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Qasem Soleimani at the Iranian embassy in Damascus. Statues of former president Hafez al-Assad are also toppled across the city.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: Syrians abroad celebrate the collapse of the Assad regime, with rallies being held in cities across Europe.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Manbij offensive, Operation Dawn of Freedom
text: Turkish security sources claim that 80% of Kurdish-held positions in the city of Manbij in Aleppo Governorate have been taken by the Turkey-backed Syrian National Army.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Manbij offensive, Operation Dawn of Freedom
text: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan threatens "appropriate measures" against Kurdistan Workers' Party-aligned rebel groups, and states that Turkey will never allow these groups control over any part of Syria or its government.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: Syrian regime forces reportedly surrender Deir ez-Zor to opposition forces, according to Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli tanks and troops enter Syria's Quneitra Governorate to reportedly establish a buffer zone, marking Israel's first crossing of the ceasefire line in 50 years.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli forces take control of the towns of Madinat al-Baath and Khan Arnabah in Quneitra Governorate and also capture the Syrian side of Mount Hermon in Rif Dimashq Governorate.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: The Israeli Air Force launches targeted airstrikes on ammunition and equipment depots at Mezzeh Air Base in Damascus and Khalkhalah air base in Suwayda Governorate. An Israeli airstrike also targets the Scientific Research Center in Damascus's security zone, which oversees chemical weapons and ballistic missile programs.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that the 1974 Agreement on Disengagement between Israel and Syria has "collapsed" and orders the Israel Defense Forces to occupy the Syrian side of the Golan Heights.

context: Syrian civil war > US intervention in the Syrian civil war > War against the Islamic State
text: The United States launches airstrikes on ISIL targets in Syria following the collapse of the Assad regime.

context: Syrian civil war > US intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: Outgoing U.S. President Joe Biden praises the end of the Ba'athist Syria regime and announces that the U.S. will support Syria and its neighbors during Syria's political transition.
Turkish forces bombard positions in Syrian Democratic Forces-controlled areas in Al-Hasakah.
The Syrian opposition takes control of the city of Jableh in Latakia Governorate.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 16 Palestinians are killed in Israeli airstrikes across the Gaza Strip, including in Deir al-Balah and the Bureij refugee camp.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Casualties of the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that 43,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022 and that 370,000 soldiers have been injured, while estimating the number of Russian casualties at 198,000 soldiers killed and more than 550,000 soldiers injured.

The Notre-Dame cathedral in Île de la Cité, Paris, France, reopens and holds its first public mass five years after a structural fire damaged the building and destroyed its spire. French President Emmanuel Macron and dozens of world leaders attend the reopening ceremony.
South Korean National Police arrest former national defense minister Kim Yong-hyun and raid his home, alleging that Kim helped President Yoon Suk Yeol institute martial law.

Former Ghanaian President and National Democratic Congress candidate John Mahama wins the presidential election as incumbent vice president and New Patriotic Party candidate Mahamudu Bawumia concedes defeat.
In auto racing, McLaren wins the World Constructors' Championship at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, its first title since 1998.
In professional baseball, the New York Mets sign Dominican outfielder Juan Soto to a $765 million, 15-year contract, the largest contract in Major League Baseball history.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > 2024 Al-Mustariha massacre
text: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that a Turkish drone strike on the village of Al-Mustariha in Raqqa Governorate, Syria, kills eleven family members, including six children.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: The opposition Syrian National Army takes control of the city of Manbij, with 50 people killed in fighting between the Syrian National Army and the Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Lieutenant General Ali Mahmoud, Maher al-Assad's office manager and leader of several Syrian civil war campaigns, is found dead in his office in a suburb of Damascus.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Fall of Damascus
text: The White Helmets civil defense organization announces they have freed over 20,000 prisoners from Sednaya Prison, with over 10,000 others unaccounted for. They report that there are areas of the prison hidden underground that they do not have access codes to, but can see prisoners on security cameras.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz orders the Israeli Defense Forces to quickly occupy the entire Syrian buffer zone and to establish a new security zone further into southern Syria free of all insurgent infrastructure and heavy weapons.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: The Israeli Air Force launches several airstrikes on the city of Daraa and also carries out a series of airstrikes on Syrian Air Force bases, destroying the Syrian Air Force's entire fleet of MiG-29 fighter jets.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip, Blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 50 Palestinians are killed and 84 others are injured in Israeli airstrikes across the Gaza Strip, including ten at a flour distribution zone in Rafah.
The Hamas delegation holds another round of ceasefire talks in Cairo, Egypt, with General Intelligence Service chief Hassan Mahmoud Rashad.
At least 110 elderly people are killed in Cité Soleil, Haiti, following accusations by a gang leader that the people practiced witchcraft against the gang leader's child.
The Arakan Army announces their capture of Maungdaw, Rakhine State, giving them full control over the Bangladesh–Myanmar border.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: Twenty-eight people are killed and 37 others are injured in a bombing on a petrol station in Mayo, Khartoum, Sudan.
PHIVOLCS raises the alert level of the Kanlaon Volcano in the Philippines to Level 3 after an explosive eruption occurred at the summit vent.
The rescue operation at the scene of an explosion at several apartments in The Hague, Netherlands, two days ago, officially ends, with the final toll being six people killed and five others injured.
Five people are killed and 26 others are injured after an explosion at an Eni factory in Calenzano, Metropolitan City of Florence, Italy.
Ten people are killed and two others are missing in floods and landslides in Sukabumi, West Java, Indonesia.
A fishing boat collides with a sand barge near Gyeongju, South Korea, killing seven people with another person missing.
Two military helicopters collide during a training flight in Isparta, Turkey, killing six soldiers.
At least seven people are killed and 42 others are injured when a bus rams into several vehicles and pedestrians in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. The bus driver is detained by local police.

context: Austria–Syria relations, Germany–Syria relations > Refugees of the Syrian civil war
text: Austria and Germany announce that they will freeze all new and ongoing asylum applications by Syrians and will review previous asylum claims by Syrians following the fall of the Assad regime.

Australia and Nauru announce a joint security treaty that will see Australia sending Nauru AU$100 million (US$64 million) in direct support over five years in exchange for Nauru consulting Australia before signing any bilateral agreements with other countries.
A suspect, identified as Luigi Mangione, is arrested in Altoona, Pennsylvania, United States, for the murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
China launches an investigation into American chip manufacturer Nvidia over suspected violations of China's anti-monopoly law.
At least 40 schools in New Delhi, India, receive bomb threats and a $30,000 ransom demand via e-mail on the same day. No evidence of explosives are found.
The local government of Azad Kashmir, Pakistan, repeals an executive order that banned protests following four days of shutter-down demonstrations in May.
The South Korean Corruption Investigation Office imposes a blanket travel ban on President Yoon Suk Yeol for his failed attempt at imposing martial law last week.
Syrian opposition leader Mohammed al-Bashir is appointed Prime Minister of the Syrian transitional government.
Prime Minister of Tonga Siaosi Sovaleni resigns ahead of a vote of no confidence.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR) reports that pro-Turkish factions have begun sectarian reprisal attacks killing at least three Kurdish civilians in Manbij, Aleppo Governorate, Syria, as well as burning and looting civilian homes.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: Pro-Turkish factions impose a siege on several neighborhoods in Manbij, prompting humanitarian concerns of potential massacres and kidnappings.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: The SOHR reports that the Free Syrian Army-affiliated Dawn of Freedom Brigades performed a field execution of dozens of injured pro-Kurdish Manbij Military Council soldiers who had been receiving hospital treatment.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Deir ez-Zor offensive
text: The Military Operations Command says that its forces have taken full control of Deir ez-Zor following days of clashes with the Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Regional security sources report that Israeli troops have reached the city of Qatana in Rif Dimashq Governorate, 10 km into Syrian territory and 25 km southwest of Damascus.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: The Israeli Navy attacks and destroys most of the Syrian Navy's fleet at anchor in the Port of Latakia, including Osa-class missile boats and minesweepers.

context: Syrian civil war > 2024 Syrian opposition offensives > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Qatar, Turkey, Egypt, Iran, and Saudi Arabia condemn Israel's actions in Syria and the United Nations special envoy for Syria calls on Israel to stop its military movements and bombardments inside Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > Eastern Syria insurgency
text: The Islamic State summarily executes 54 Syrian Army soldiers captured near Al-Sukhnah, Homs Governorate.

context: Gaza war > Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: The United Nations reports that humanitarian aid has been blocked from entering the Gaza Strip for at least 66 days, leaving at least 65,000 Palestinians without food, water, electricity, and healthcare.

context: Sudanese civil war > Battle of Khartoum
text: At least 65 people are killed and hundreds of others are injured in Rapid Support Forces artillery shelling on a market in Karary District, Khartoum State, Sudan.
At least 100 people are killed and 37 others are injured in a Sudanese Air Force airstrike on Kabkabiya District, North Darfur, Sudan.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Southern front of the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: A Russian missile strike on a private clinic in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, kills four civilians and injures 20 others.
One Pakistani soldier and 15 separatist militants are killed in an operation in Zhob District, Balochistan, Pakistan
Filipino singer Sofronio Vasquez wins the 26th season of The Voice, becoming the first Filipino and Asian contestant to win a season of the show.

context: Proposed acquisition of Albertsons by Kroger
text: U.S. federal judge Adrienne Nelson of the U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon blocks a $24.6 billion bid by Kroger to acquire stores from Albertsons.
In Malibu, California, United States, the Franklin Fire spreads to more than 2,800 acres, prompting over 20,000 people to evacuate.
A six-story apartment building collapses in Waili, Cairo, Egypt killing eight people and injuring three others.

context: Switzerland–Syria relations > Refugees of the Syrian civil war
text: Switzerland suspends all new and pending asylum requests and announces that they will review their asylum policy following the fall of the Assad regime.

context: Belarus–Russia relations, Nuclear risk during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko confirms the presence of nuclear weapons in his country, including Russia's Oreshnik missile system.
The Russian Federal Security Service arrests a German-Russian man for allegedly planning to sabotage a rail line in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, on behalf of the Security Service of Ukraine.

Kenya Police fire tear gas at hundreds of demonstrators in Nairobi, Kenya, protesting against gender-based violence and femicide. Protests also took place in Mombasa and Lodwar, with at least three people arrested.

context: Somali Civil War > Constitutional crisis in Somalia > 2024 Jubaland presidential election > Battle of Ras Kamboni
text: Somali forces launch a failed attack on Jubaland regional forces, with Jubaland capturing hundreds of Somali soldiers and claiming to have fully taken over Ras Kamboni, Lower Juba, Somalia.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > Siege of North Gaza
text: At least 29 people are killed in Israeli airstrikes on civilian areas in Beit Lahia, North Gaza Governorate, Gaza.
An Israeli boy is killed and three others are injured by a Palestinian gunman attack on a bus in Al-Khader, West Bank.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War > United States and the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The United States Department of State approves a $266.4 million sale of F-16 maintenance equipment to Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian War > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Parliament of Canada approves the allocation of CA$764 million (US$587 million) in military aid to Ukraine.

context: Syrian civil war > Fall of the Assad regime
text: Armed men raid and set fire to the tomb of former president Hafez al-Assad and also conduct attacks on other tombs and graves in Qardaha District, Latakia Governorate, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > Sectarianism and minorities in the Syrian civil war
text: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights urges Syria's military leadership to prevent ongoing sectarian riots, looting, and assaults on civilians from armed groups.
The Federal Foreign Office of Germany announces an additional €8 million (US$8.4 million) in humanitarian aid to Syria following the fall of the Assad regime.
Toussaint Louverture International Airport in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, reopens after it was closed in November when a Spirit Airlines aircraft was struck by gunfire.
Afghanistan's acting Minister of Refugee and Repatriation Khalil Haqqani and five other people are killed in a suicide bombing at the Ministry's headquarters in Kabul, Afghanistan.
Five civilians are killed in Israeli airstrikes in Ainata, Bint Jbeil, and Beit Lif, Lebanon, despite the agreed ceasefire with Hezbollah.
Amnesty International reports that Sudan is currently facing the worst humanitarian crisis in the world, with over 30 million people at risk or in need of humanitarian aid.

context: Proposed acquisition of Albertsons by Kroger
text: American grocery store company Albertsons of Boise, Idaho backs out of a $24.6 billion merger deal between Cincinnati-based grocer Kroger and files a lawsuit against them that includes a $600 million termination fee.
One person is killed in a fire and explosion at a residential high-rise apartment building in Shenzhen, China.
Forty-four people are presumed dead from drowning when a boat carrying refugees from Sierra Leone capsizes on its way from Sfax, Tunisia, to Europe.
Two United States foreign nationals from California are killed in a shooting by unidentified gunmen in Angamacutiro, Michoacán, Mexico.
Iran announces that all government offices, universities, and schools in Tehran province will be closed for two days due to severe air pollution.

A special investigations team conducts a raid on South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol's office, the National Police Agency headquarters, the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency headquarters, and the office of the National Assembly's security service, as part of an investigation into Yoon's failed attempt at imposing martial law last week.
Jailed former national defense minister Kim Yong-hyun, who allegedly helped President Yoon Suk Yeol impose martial law, attempts suicide while in custody.
Hundreds of tractors block Whitehall, City of Westminster, England in protest of Labour government changes to the agricultural inheritance tax.
The Swiss Federal Assembly elects Karin Keller-Sutter, currently a Federal Councillor, as President for 2025.
FIFA announces that Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 FIFA World Cup.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: Large-scale protests occur in Manbij, Aleppo Governorate, Syria, against pro-Turkish Dawn of Freedom Operations Room revenge killings and crimes against civilians.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom > Manbij offensive
text: Pro-Turkish factions are filmed executing dozens of surrendered prisoners of the pro-Kurdish Manbij Military Council and Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom > 2024 Kobani clashes
text: Turkish military forces and the pro-Turkish Dawn of Freedom Operations Room launch an attack with tanks and drones against the Tishrin Dam on the Euphrates river, which the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights warns could trigger a dam failure and a severe humanitarian crisis.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Syrian residents of the villages of Hader, Hamidiya, and Umm Batna in Quneitra Governorate are displaced from their homes after Israeli military forces enter the villages with military vehicles.

context: Syrian civil war > Fall of the Assad regime
text: At least six civilians are reported to have been killed by gunfire in celebration of the fall of the Assad regime.

context: Syrian civil war > Russian intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: Satellite images and MarineTraffic data confirm that the Russian Navy has abandoned its naval base in the port city of Tartus.

context: Syrian civil war > Syrian peace process
text: The Syrian transitional government announces that the constitution and parliament will be suspended during the three-month transitional period.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip > December 2024 Nuseirat refugee camp attack
text: At least 33 Palestinians are killed and 50 others are injured in an Israeli airstrike on the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip.

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: Fifteen people are killed in Israeli airstrikes while guarding humanitarian aid convoys near Rafah and Khan Younis, Gaza.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Four police officers are injured in a drone attack on the barracks of a police regiment building in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia.

The Islamic State – Khorasan Province claims responsibility for yesterday's suicide bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan, which killed acting Minister of Refugee and Repatriation Khalil Haqqani and several other people.
United States president-elect Donald Trump is named Person of the Year by Time magazine.
Astro Bot wins Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2024.
Tropical Cyclone Chido makes landfall over Agaléga, Mauritius.
Seven people, including a child, are killed and 35 others are injured in a fire at a private hospital in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, India.
At least nine people are found dead, six others are missing, and 27 people are rescued when a boat carrying African migrants sinks off the coast of Chebba, Mahdia Governorate, Tunisia.
The European Union approves of Romania and Bulgaria to join the Schengen Area in 2025.
Paraguay reopens its embassy in Jerusalem, Israel.

context: Federal pardons in the United States
text: U.S. President Joe Biden announces pardons for 39 people convicted of non-violent offenses, and commutes the sentences of 1,500 others who had been released from prison to house arrest during the COVID-19 pandemic. It is considered the "largest single-day grant of clemency in modern history".
A Danish court sentences British hedge fund trader Sanjay Shah to 12 years in prison for tax fraud.
The Venezuelan government releases 103 prisoners who were arrested during the protests against the results of the disputed presidential election in July.
In Lithuania, the three-party coalition Government headed by the new appointed Prime Minister Gintautas Paluckas takes over.

Hundreds of protesters, led by university students, gather outside the Radio Television of Serbia headquarters in Belgrade, Serbia, to protest against the state-owned television broadcaster and President Aleksandar Vučić's administration. At least 13 people are detained by Serbian police.
In Somalia, Abdirahman Irro is sworn in as president of Somaliland.
Edith Heard, biologist specialist of epigenetics and director-general of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory, is awarded the CNRS Gold Medal, France's highest research award.
Gukesh Dommaraju defeats Ding Liren to win the World Chess Championship 7½-6½, becoming the youngest ever chess champion at the age of 18 years.

context: Syrian civil war > Israel and the Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Syrian sources report that Israeli forces met with village dignitaries in the Yarmouk Basin area of Daraa Governorate, instructing them to surrender all weapons in the villages and for villagers to comply with home searches.

context: Syrian civil war > US intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: The U.S. military evacuates American citizen Travis Timmerman out of Syria after Timmerman had previously been reported missing in the country.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Moldova and the Russo-Ukrainian War
text: The Parliament of Moldova votes in favor of declaring a 60-day national state of emergency beginning on December 16 due to Ukraine not renewing its transit contract with Gazprom to deliver Russian gas to Moldova.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches one of its largest attacks on the Ukrainian energy infrastructure since the conflict began, with about 290 missiles fired and drones striking multiple regions. The Russian Defense Ministry claims that the attack was in response to a recent Ukrainian ATACMS attack on Taganrog-Central air base in Rostov Oblast, Russia.

context: Gaza war > December 2024 Nuseirat refugee camp attack
text: The number of Palestinians killed in an Israeli airstrike on the Nuseirat refugee camp yesterday increases to 33, most of whom are from the same family. Eighty-four others are reported to be either injured or missing.
Nine people are killed and 20 others are injured in a Rapid Support Forces airstrike on a hospital in Al-Fashir, North Darfur, Sudan.
Cyclone Chido destroys most of Agaléga, Mauritius.
Six people are killed and 66 others are injured in a fire at a nursing home in Amman, Jordan.

context: Opioid epidemic in the United States
text: McKinsey & Company agrees to pay $650 million and enter a deferred prosecution agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice to resolve criminal charges related to its advisory work for Purdue Pharma on increasing OxyContin sales, including conspiracy to misbrand a drug and obstruction of justice.
The British Antarctic Survey reports that A23a, the world's largest iceberg, has exited the Taylor column and is beginning to drift further north through the Southern Ocean.

context: Syria–Ukraine relations > Humanitarian aid during the Syrian civil war
text: The Ukrainian government says that it is ready to supply food to Syria after Russia suspended wheat supplies to Syria amid uncertainty about the new government and payment delays.
A court in The Hague, Netherlands, rejects a request by 10 pro-Palestinian NGOs for the Netherlands to stop arms exports to Israel.
Three people are killed and 48 others are injured in a bombing during a festival in Umphang District, Tak Province, Thailand. Two suspects are arrested.
Former Chinese footballer and coach Li Tie is sentenced to 20 years in prison for bribery and match-fixing.
French President Emmanuel Macron appoints François Bayrou as Prime Minister.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom, Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war > 2024 Kobani clashes
text: The Turkish Armed Forces and pro-Turkish rebel groups amass troops on the Syria–Turkey border outside of Kobani, Aleppo Governorate, Syria, and along the nearby Qarqozak Bridge, following several breaches in an internationally-brokered temporary ceasefire agreement between them and the Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom, Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war > 2024 Kobani clashes
text: Iraqi water experts issue warnings regarding cracks that have formed in the Tishrin Dam in Aleppo Governorate following continuous bombardment by Turkish and pro-Turkish forces and the possibility of further damage causing a dam failure.

context: Somali Civil War > Puntland–Somaliland dispute > Las Anod conflict
text: Two Somaliland troops are killed and eight others are injured in fighting between Somaliland and SSC-Khatumo forces in Erigavo, Sanaag, Somaliland.
At least eight people were killed and ten others injured in a deadly inter-clan conflict in a rural area under the El Buur district of Galgadud region in south-central Somalia

context: Gaza war > Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip
text: At least 52 Palestinians are killed in Israeli airstrikes on two schools in Gaza City and Rafah in the Gaza Strip.

Moody's downgrades France's bond credit rating to "Aa3" from "Aa2" following the collapse of the Barnier government, citing "political fragmentation" as a threat to the country's ability to reduce its public debt and lower its deficit.
Cyclone Chido kills two people and causes "catastrophic" damage to the island of Mayotte, with many more feared dead on the island.
The 24th summit of the Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (ALBA-TCP) is held in Caracas, Venezuela.

Flights are temporarily suspended at Stewart International Airport in New York, United States, after the Federal Aviation Administration alerts them to a drone sighting in the area. The incident prompts Governor Kathy Hochul to call for federal government intervention amid a series of widespread drone sightings across the Northeastern United States.

The Public Service Enterprise Group files a request with the Federal Aviation Administration to close the airspace over two of its nuclear power plants to all aircraft after unidentified drones were spotted hovering over the facilities in New Jersey.
sources: The New York Post via MSN

text: Five people are killed during a shooting spree between Dunkirk and Loon-Plage, in Nord Department, France. A man is detained.

Former Minister of Defence and running mate of Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 Brazilian general election Walter Braga Netto is arrested amid charges with meddling in investigations related to an attempted coup.
One police officer is killed and at least two others are injured in an explosion in Dnipro, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine.

President of Georgia Salome Zourabichvili states that she will not recognize the scheduled presidential election results as legitimate due to the election not being a direct vote, and repeats her intention to remain as president until new parliamentary elections are held.

Georgian Dream candidate Mikheil Kavelashvili is elected as president by the electoral college. Major opposition parties do not participate in the vote, having boycotted Parliament since the parliamentary election in October.
South Korea's National Assembly votes to impeach president Yoon Suk Yeol over his recent attempt to impose martial law.

context: Gaza war > December 2024 Nuseirat refugee camp attack
text: Al Jazeera cameraman Ahmad Al-Louh is killed in an Israeli airstrike on a civil defense point in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli Air Force fighter jets strike surface-to-air missile and weapon depots in Tartus Governorate, Syria, with the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights describing the strikes as the heaviest in the region since the start of the civil war.

context: Free trade agreements of the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom joins the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, becoming the 12th member and the first European member.
Thousands of people are believed to have been killed by Cyclone Chido in the French overseas department of Mayotte, with the cyclone also causing damage in the Comoros and Mozambique.

At least one person is killed when two Russian oil tankers, Volgoneft-212 and Volgoneft-236, are damaged due to bad weather in the Kerch Strait with oil from the tankers actively leaking into the strait.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announces that the remaining five members of the Bali Nine drug-trafficking group, who were serving life sentences in Indonesia, have returned to Australia following an agreement between the two countries to end their imprisonment.
Israel announces that it will close its embassy in Dublin, Ireland, over Ireland's alleged "extreme anti-Israel policies".

White House National Security Council spokesperson John Kirby says that the United States Coast Guard has confirmed that there is no evidence of any "foreign-based involvement" in the unidentified drones that are being sighted over the Northeastern United States.
sources: The Times of India via MSN

text: ABC News settles a defamation lawsuit filed by U.S. President-elect Donald Trump over statements made on air by anchor George Stephanopoulos about the E. Jean Carroll v. Donald J. Trump lawsuits, with ABC agreeing to pay $15 million to the Trump presidential library as well as $1 million for legal fees.

context: Syrian civil war > Fall of the Assad regime > Syrian mass graves
text: A recently created mass grave containing the bodies of 17 executed Syrian Army soldiers is discovered in the Syrian Desert near Deir ez-Zor.

context: Syrian civil war > Fall of the Assad regime
text: In his first public statement since being overthrown, former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad says that he "didn't intend to leave Syria", claiming that he went to Khmeimim Air Base in Latakia Governorate to "oversee combat operations" only to find that the Syrian Army had abandoned their positions and surrendered to rebel forces. Amid "an intensified attack by drone strikes" at the air base, Assad says that Russia decided to airlift him to Moscow.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: The Cabinet of Israel approves a plan proposing to double the occupied Golan Heights' regional Israeli settlers population.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Heavy overnight Israeli airstrikes are reported in Tartus Governorate, Syria.

context: Syrian civil war > Sectarianism and minorities in the Syrian civil war
text: The brother of the imam of the Great Prophet Mosque of Masyaf is assassinated by unidentified gunmen in Hama Governorate, in a potential revenge operation due to the imam being associated with Hezbollah and other Iranian- and Shia-associated militias.

context: Syrian civil war > US intervention in the Syrian civil war
text: The United States Air Force conduct strikes targeting ISIS camps and operatives, killing at least twelve fighters, according to the Pentagon.
The Gaza Health Ministry announces that the death toll in the ongoing war has surpassed 45,000 people.

An improvised explosive device detonates in Cotija de la Paz, Michoacán, leaving two soldiers dead and five others injured. The Secretary of National Defense, Ricardo Trevilla Trejo, blames the Cárteles Unidos for the attack.
Walpeup, Victoria, Australia, reports a temperature of , the hottest temperature reported in the state since 2019. Extreme heat wave and fire risk warnings are also issued for areas across Australia.

U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas calls for state National Guards to be given the authority to shoot down unidentified drones, saying that the federal government is not able to address the issue by themselves.
U.S. officials say that a drone detection system is being deployed in New York following a formal request by Governor Kathy Hochul.

The United States Air Force reports that Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio temporarily suspended air operations for four hours on Friday and Saturday after the airbase reported sightings of unidentified "small unmanned aerial systems".

President-elect Donald Trump cancels a planned visit to Trump National Golf Club Bedminster in New Jersey amid drone sightings in the state. Trump also calls on outgoing President Joe Biden and the U.S. military to reveal the truth about the drones, saying that "the government knows what's happening" and that they know where the drones are coming from.
Two people are killed and six others are injured in a mass shooting at the Abundant Life Christian School in Madison, Wisconsin, United States. The perpetrator is found dead at the scene.
Bolivian prosecutors issue an arrest warrant for former President Evo Morales in connection to sexual abuse allegations that he fathered a child with a 15-year-old girl, a claim he denies.

context: 2024 German government crisis, 2025 German federal election
text: German Chancellor Olaf Scholz loses a vote of confidence, thereby allowing for early elections to be held on February 23.

Chrystia Freeland resigns as Canada's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance amid disagreements with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau on increased government spending and how to handle possible U.S. tariffs imposed by the incoming Trump administration.
President of Kyrgyzstan Sadyr Japarov announces that he has dismissed Akylbek Japarov as Prime Minister.

The Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle expels former Indonesian President Joko Widodo, his son Vice President Gibran Rakabuming and his son-in-law, North Sumatra Governor-elect Bobby Nasution, following a rift over Rakabuming's candidacy as Prabowo Subianto's running mate during the 2024 election.

context: Syrian civil war > War crimes in the Syrian civil war, Fall of the Assad regime > Syrian mass graves
text: Several mass graves are uncovered across Syria following the fall of the Assad regime, with a site in Al-Qutayfah, Rif Dimashq Governorate, estimated to contain the remains of at least 100,000 people.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz visit the summit of Mount Hermon in Syria, which was captured by the Israel Defense Forces last week.

context: Syrian civil war > Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)
text: The Israeli military continue invading Syria beyond the 1974 buffer zone in Quneitra Governorate and take control of the Al-Wehda Dam on the Yarmouk River.

context: Syrian civil war > Operation Dawn of Freedom
text: Senior American officials report that Turkey is building up its forces along the Syrian border, raising fears of a possible ground invasion on territories held by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: Russian Lieutenant General Igor Kirillov, head of the NBC Protection Troops, and his assistant are assassinated by an IED hidden inside of an e-scooter in Moscow, Russia. A Ukrainian source claims that the Security Service of Ukraine is responsible for the killings, after Kirillov was charged in absentia yesterday for the use of chemical weapons, which made him a "legitimate target". Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of the Security Council of Russia, says that the Ukrainian leadership would face an "imminent revenge" for the killings.

context: Russian invasion of Ukraine > Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War, Russia–NATO relations
text: NATO's Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine command center in Wiesbaden, Germany, takes over coordination of Western military support to Ukraine from the United States.
Two police officers are killed and three others are injured in a mass shooting at a security checkpoint in Shangla district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Three police officers are killed and two more are wounded by a roadside bomb targeting a vehicle carrying polio vaccination workers in Dera Ismail Khan District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

Two municipal policemen are killed and three civilians are wounded in an attack near the Jerécuaro-Apaseo el Alto state highway in Jerécuaro, Guanajuato, Mexico. In the same day, four State Public Security Forces officers are killed and two more are wounded after a confrontation with gunmen in the city of Uriangato.
The death toll in Mozambique from Cyclone Chido increase to 34, with more than 23,000 homes destroyed.
A 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes Vanuatu's capital Port Vila, with at least fourteen people killed and more than 200 others injured.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Health Ministry announces that the mystery illness that has left at least 143 people dead in Kwango was a severe form of malaria. The World Health Organization says more malaria vaccines are being sent to its health centres in the region.

The U.S. House Intelligence Committee hold a closed-door classified briefing on drone sightings over the Northeastern United States. The briefing is provided by Federal Bureau of Investigation, the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, according to senior U.S. officials.
A U.S. grand jury indicts Luigi Mangione for the assassination of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
Three foreigners are arrested and one ton of cocaine is seized by the Mexican Navy in an operation off coasts of Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán.
English High Court judge John Cavanagh sentences Urfan Sharif and Beinash Batool to life imprisonment for the murder of Sharif's 10-year-old daughter Sara.
Canadian-American anti-whaling activist Paul Watson is released from prison in Greenland after Denmark declines Japan's extradition request.

context: Second presidential transition of Donald Trump
text: The U.S. Electoral College formally certifies President-elect Donald Trump's victory over Vice President Kamala Harris in the 2024 United States presidential election.
Switzerland's Federal Assembly votes 126–20 with 41 abstentions to outlaw membership or support of Lebanese militant group Hezbollah.

Hadi al-Bahra, President of the National Coalition of Syrian Revolutionary and Opposition Forces, says that the coalition will dissolve once a national conference is convened and a constituent assembly is elected, and demands that the current transitional government be "credible, inclusive and not founded on sectarian bases".
Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev says that arms sent by France to Armenia pose a threat to Azerbaijan.
At least fifteen people are killed after an Indian Navy craft collides with a passenger ferry off the coast of Mumbai, India.

A Bombardier Challenger 300 aircraft flying from Punta del Este, Uruguay, veers off the runway while trying to land at San Fernando International Airport in the Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina, and collides with a house, killing the two pilots onboard.
Thirty-five children are killed and six others are injured in a crowd crush during a Christmas funfair in Ibadan, Nigeria.
Twenty-five people are killed and dozens of others are missing when a boat capsizes on a river in Inongo, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Twenty people are killed and five others are rescued in a shipwreck carrying migrants sinking off the coast of Sfax, Tunisia.

Russian state media agency TASS claims that the nation developed an mRNA cancer vaccine, which is planned to be distributed to patients free of charge beginning next year. However, the Russian Ministry of Health has not provided any evidence to support their claim that the vaccine treats cancer.
The state of California, United States, declares a state of emergency over bird flu.

context: China–United States relations > Chinese espionage in the United States
text: Two Americans of Chinese descent plead guilty to running a covert secret police surveillance station on behalf of the Chinese Ministry of Public Security to monitor, threaten and coerce ethnic Chinese in Chinatown, Manhattan, New York City, New York, United States. At least 100 such stations have been reported worldwide across 53 countries, with human rights monitoring NGOs accusing China of using the outposts to threaten and monitor Chinese nationals abroad.
Mary Jane Veloso, a former inmate on death row in Indonesia, is repatriated to the Philippines following negotiations between the two countries.

The U.S. Department of Defense repatriates two al-Qaeda members, Mohammed Farik Bin Amin and Mohammed Nazir Bin Lep, from Guantanamo Bay to Malaysia, where they will undergo a rehabilitation process before reintegration into society.

In his first direct comments on the issue, president Joe Biden states there is "nothing nefarious, apparently" and "no sense of danger so far" behind the aircraft sightings in the northeastern United States.

context: Legal affairs of the Tate brothers
text: The Westminster Magistrates' Court rules that British police may seize £2.2 million (US$2.5 million) from influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan for allegedly failing to pay taxes on profits from their online ventures.
The Dutch Data Protection Authority fines Netflix €4.75 million ($4.98 million) for failing to properly inform subscribers about the handling of their personal data between 2018 and 2020.
Eleven people are killed and two others are injured in an arson attack on a bar in Hanoi, Vietnam.

context: 2024 Georgian presidential election, 2024 Georgian parliamentary election, 2024 Georgian post-election protests
text: In an address to the European Parliament, Georgian President Salome Zourabichvili urges the European Union to economically and politically pressure the current Georgian government into holding new elections, claiming that recent elections represented a "new form of invasion" by Russia.
Simon Harris submits his resignation as Taoiseach of Ireland to President Michael D Higgins.
The parliament building of Liberia catches on fire amid anti-government protests condemning the attempted removal of House Speaker Jonathan F. Koffa.
In association football, Real Madrid wins the inaugural FIFA Intercontinental Cup after defeating Pachuca 3–0 in the final in Lusail, Qatar. Vinícius Júnior is awarded the Golden Ball.

context: Syrian civil war > Fall of the Assad regime > Deir ez-Zor offensive, Eastern Syria insurgency
