Seven people are killed and 19 others are injured in a blast and fire at a café in Shchuchinsk, Kazakhstan.
Six people are killed and several others are injured after a sleeper bus collides with a trailer on National Highway 25 in Rajasthan, India.
Two people are killed and 49 more injured after a tram derails in Milan, Italy, and crashes into pedestrians and a building.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi says that a potential deal between the United States and Iran is within reach.

A court in Jakarta, Indonesia, sentences nine individuals, including two former chief executives of subsidiaries of state-owned energy company Pertamina, to prison terms ranging from nine to 15 years in a corruption case involving alleged unlawful oil terminal leasing and crude oil imports that prosecutors say caused significant state losses.

context: Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war
text: The Supreme Court of Israel issues an interim order suspending a government ban on 37 foreign non-governmental organizations operating in Gaza and the West Bank, allowing them to continue their operations while the court reviews a petition challenging the revocation of their legal status.

A Tunisian court sentences former prime minister Ali Laarayedh, who has been detained since 2022, to 24 years in prison for facilitating the travel of Tunisian nationals to Syrian conflict zones during his premiership, while seven co-defendants, including former interior ministry officials, receive prison terms ranging from three to 24 years.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rejects a U.S. Department of Defense request to loosen security safeguards on the Claude large language model for potential use in mass surveillance and autonomous weapons systems.
OpenAI announces that it has reached an agreement with the U.S. Department of Defense to deploy its technology on the latter's network.
Israel launches an attack on Iran, calling it a preemptive strike, killing several Iranian high-ranking officials including supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

The United States takes part in the attack on Iran with president Donald Trump announcing a "major U.S. combat operation" targeting Iranian missile facilities and naval assets, and calls on the Iranian military to overthrow Khamenei.

The U.S. Department of Defense announces on X that the codename of the U.S. operation in Iran will be codenamed as Operation Epic Fury. Additionally, Israel announces that the codename of their operation will be Operation Roaring Lion.

Explosions are reported in Tehran, Iran, as U.S.-launched Tomahawk missiles strike Iranian targets, including the supreme leader's office. Satellite imagery confirms the destruction of Khamenei's compound.

Iran launches ballistic missiles at a United States Navy facility in Bahrain, targeting the headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet, and Iranian drones strike residential areas of Manama. The Bahraini interior ministry urges citizens and residents to seek nearest safe locations.

The Cabinet of Israel declares a state of emergency related to the strikes on Iran. Israel closes all border crossings with the Gaza Strip, citing security measures, and suspends the rotation of humanitarian personnel.

Iran launches missiles at Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE state that they have intercepted Iranian missiles. The U.S. embassies in Bahrain and Qatar instruct their personnel to shelter in place.
At least two people are killed and five more are injured when an unidentified airstrike targets the Popular Mobilization Forces headquarters in Jurf al-Nasr, Iraq.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: Iranian Shahed drones strike Kuwait International Airport resulting in minor injures to several airport workers as well as damage to the main airport terminal.

Iran says it has launched a ballistic missile attack on Dubai with reports of multiple missiles striking the city. At least one hotel on the Palm Islands is hit and is ablaze, injuring at least four people. The Burj Khalifa is evacuated. An Iranian drone strikes the luxury hotel Burj Al Arab causing a fire.
Iranian defence minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commander Mohammad Pakpour, and Expediency Discernment Council member Ali Shamkhani are killed by Israeli strikes.
The IRGC Navy announces the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to all vessels.
The Iranian Red Crescent Society reports 201 people have been killed and 747 others have been injured so far in Israeli and American strikes on Iran.
At least 180 people, mostly schoolgirls, are killed in an airstrike on an elementary school in Minab, Hormozgan province, Iran.

At least 21 people, including four children, are killed in an airstrike on a sports hall in Lamerd, Fars province, Iran. BBC Verify and The New York Times determined that a U.S. Precision Strike Missile was used in the attack.
An Iranian missile strikes Tel Aviv, killing a woman, and wounding at least 22 other people, including several seriously, and badly damaging several buildings. Search and rescue efforts are underway.

One person is killed and seven others are wounded in an Iranian airstrike on Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, while four are injured in a similar airstrike on Dubai International Airport.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Yemen's Houthis announce the resumption of attacks on Red Sea shipping routes and on Israel in support of Iran.
Blasts rock Jalalabad, including the Jalalabad Airport in the Nangarhar Province, Afghanistan.
Afghan forces and police say that a Pakistani fighter jet has crashed in Jalalabad, Afghanistan, and that the pilot was captured alive.
The Pakistani Foreign Ministry denies claims that Afghan forces and police downed the pilot. The Pakistani Ministry of Information & Broadcasting confirms on X that no attack took place.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Iran, Iraq, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, and Syria close their respective airspaces to civilian flights as a precautionary measure, while the UAE partially closes its airspace. Later, the UAE indefinitely suspends all flights from the Al Maktoum and Dubai international airports.
At least 21 people are killed and eight others are injured in an explosion at a firecracker factory in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, India.
Six people, including Parliament of Kenya legislator Johana Ng'eno, are killed when an Airbus Helicopters H125 crashes in Nandi County, Kenya.
Five people are killed when an ammunition and missile depot belonging to the National Guard detonates in Suwayda, Sweida Governorate, Syria.

Cuban authorities arrest ten Panamanian nationals in Havana, accusing them of creating anti-government signs in exchange for being paid US$1,000–1,500 and charging them under laws that prohibit propaganda against the constitution, offenses that carry prison terms of three to eight years.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: Anti-war protests are held across the United States in cities such as New York City, Philadelphia, Portland, and Seattle.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: Protests in Detroit, Michigan, are held against the U.S. strikes at Hart Plaza and Wayne State University. Additionally, a protest is held along Jefferson Avenue.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: In Washington, D.C., anti-war protests organized by groups such as 50501 and Code Pink are held near the White House. Additionally, diaspora protests are held near the World War I Memorial with demonstrators holding American and Israeli flags praising the strikes.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: An anti-war protest is held in Los Angeles, California, at the City Hall to call for an end to American military actions in the Middle East. Actress and activist Jane Fonda takes part in the protest.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: Protests are held against the U.S. strikes in Honolulu, Hawaii, including a peace rally at Iolani Palace attended by State Senator Sharon Moriwaki and a separate protest along Ala Moana Boulevard organized by Refuse Fascism Hawaii.
A pro-government demonstration in Tehran, Iran, marches against the Israel and U.S. airstrikes.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: An Iranian drone strikes the Crowne Plaza Hotel in Manama, Bahrain, which houses American embassy personnel. No casualties are reported.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
text: A person is injured in a drone strike on Duqm port in Oman.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Multiple Iranian Shahed drones strike French naval air station Camp de la Paix in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 killings of Iranian officials > Assassination of Ali Khamenei
text: Iran confirms the death of supreme leader Ali Khamenei in an attack yesterday in Tehran by Israel and the United States. Forty days of mourning are declared.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 killings of Iranian officials > Assassination of Ali Khamenei
text: Following Khamenei's death, some Iranians grieve while others in the country celebrated his death. In Galleh Dar, a monument of Islamic founder Ruhollah Khomeini is toppled. Additionally, a statue in Dehloran is toppled.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 killings of Iranian officials
text: Key Iranian officials Abdolrahim Mousavi, Aziz Nasirzadeh, Mohammad Pakpour and Ali Shamkhani are confirmed killed after an airstrike during a meeting yesterday in Tehran.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 killings of Iranian officials
text: Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is allegedly killed along with his bodyguards in an Israeli targeted killing strike on his home in Narmak. However, contrary to reports, a close advisor to him confirmed he is alive.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Cyprus
text: Iran launches two ballistic missiles towards Cyprus, not far from the British military bases on the island. They were both intercepted before reaching Cyprus. Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides states that the country is not a target of Iran.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Cyprus
text: British Royal Air Force base RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus is hit by a drone after declaring a security threat. No casualties are reported.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Nine people are killed and 49 others are wounded in an Iranian ballistic missile strike on a synagogue in Beit Shemesh, Jerusalem District, Israel.
High-ranking clerics in Iran declare jihad against Israel and the U.S., issuing a fatwa against them.
The Israeli Air Force launches a new wave of airstrikes across Tehran, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Basij facilities with multiple explosions reported.
The Palau-flagged oil tanker Skylight is struck by a missile off the Musandam Peninsula in the Gulf of Oman, injuring four crew members.
The IRGC says it has launched missiles at the United States Navy aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln in the Indian Ocean.
Three U.S. service members are killed and five others are seriously wounded in an Iranian missile strike, according to the United States Central Command.
Four Popular Mobilization Forces members are killed in an unidentified airstrike targeting one of their headquarters in Diyala Governorate, Iraq.
The Islamic Republic of Iran Navy's lead Moudge-class frigate IRIS Jamaran is sunk by U.S forces off Chabahar Port.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Southern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russian forces launch artillery strikes on Kherson, Ukraine, killing three people and wounding two others.
Anti-aircraft fire is reported over Kabul, Afghanistan, as Pakistani warplanes launch strikes against Taliban targets.
At least 169 people are killed when insurgents raid a village in Abiemnom County, Ruweng Administrative Area, South Sudan.
The Tatmadaw launches airstrikes against a trading junction in the central Magway Region of Myanmar, killing 25 people and injuring 20 people.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Danish shipping firm Maersk says that it is suspending all vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz until further notice due to the ongoing conflict in the Persian Gulf.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: US-Bangla Airlines announces that they will resume flights to Oman and Saudi Arabia as scheduled. However, they also announce they will temporarily suspend flights to Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
At least 17 people are killed and 18 others are critically injured in an explosion at an explosives factory in Nagpur district, Maharashtra, India.
Four people are killed and ten others are missing after a boat carrying migrants toward Europe capsizes off the coast of Tobruk, Libya, according to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
Six people are killed and seven others are injured when a coach bus collides with a truck near Kyakabuga, Kyankwanzi District, Uganda.
Two Canadian nationals are killed and 18 others are injured in a bus crash near Cumayasa, La Altagracia Province, Dominican Republic.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi says that he has told Oman foreign minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi that Iran is open to serious efforts at de-escalation.

US president Donald Trump claims that the Iranian leadership agreed to talks a day after Israel and the US launched strikes against Iran and stated he has agreed to do so. However, Iranian security council secretary Ali Larijani ruled out any negotiations.
Belgium's special forces, with French Naval assistance, seize a Russian shadow fleet oil tanker in the North Sea.

The Ministerial Council of the Gulf Cooperation Council issues an statement condemning the Iranian attacks targeting GCC countries, reaffirming that their territories won't be used to launch any attacks against Iran and demanding the cessation of those attacks to restore security, peace, and stability in the region.

context: 2026 attack on the United States consulate in Karachi
text: Hundreds of protestors attempted to storm the consulate of the United States in Karachi, Pakistan, leading to clashes with security forces which left at least 22 people dead and multiple others wounded.

Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and 14 others are injured in a mass shooting at a bar in Austin, Texas, United States. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating the attack as potential terrorism.

context: 2026 Iran war > Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran > 2026 Iranian Supreme Leader election
text: Iran appoints Ayatollah Alireza Arafi to the Interim Leadership Council that assumed authority following the assassination of supreme leader Ali Khamenei, with the body set to govern alongside president Masoud Pezeshkian and chief justice Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i until the Assembly of Experts selects a new supreme leader.

context: 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war
text: Over 1,300 demonstrators, mainly affiliated with the Communist Party of Greece, protest in Athens, Greece, with people holding ‌banners and placards reading, "Hands off Iran" and "Close Souda base".

context: 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war
text: A pro-Iran demonstration by the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami is held at the Baitul Mukarram National Mosque condemning Khamenei's death and demanding the intervention of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

context: 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war
text: A anti-war demonstration organized by the People's Solidarity for Participatory Democracy is held at the U.S. Embassy in Seoul, South Korea. The protest is held on the anniversary of the March First Movement.
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado says she will return to the country in the coming weeks.

context: AI boom, Regulation of artificial intelligence
text: Vietnam's artificial intelligence (AI) law takes effect, mandating labeling of AI-generated content and disclosure when users interact with automated systems. The law, which applies to domestic and foreign developers, providers, and deployers operating in the country, also provides for the creation of a national AI data center.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Two Kuwaiti navy members are killed amid Iranian attacks, according to the Kuwaiti defence ministry.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Iranian drones strike the U.S. embassy in Kuwait City.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Iran launches a missile and drone attack on Saudi Aramco's oil refinery in Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia, causing several large fires at the facility, and forcing its closure by Saudi authorities.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Dubai International Airport resumes limited flights for stranded international passengers, with the first flights cleared to depart Dubai.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Cyprus
text: Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides confirms that an Iranian drone struck the British base RAF Akrotiri last night. Paphos International Airport is evacuated after a "drone threat", while Greece deploys two frigates and F-16 fighter jets to Cyprus amid rising tensions.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
text: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer says that the United Kingdom has agreed to a United States request to use British military bases for "defensive" strikes on Iranian missile sites.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
text: NATO secretary general Mark Rutte states that NATO has no plans to be involved in the conflict, while praising Israel and the United States for their strikes against Iran.
The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) reports three more U.S. soldiers have been killed, bringing the death toll among U.S. forces to six, since the start of the conflict with Iran.

Three U.S. Air Force F-15E fighter jets crash in Kuwait during combat operations against Iran after being mistakenly shot down by the Kuwaiti military. All crew members survive. The U.S. CENTCOM confirms the loss of the three aircraft in a friendly fire incident.
U.S. Air Force B-1 Lancer strategic bombers carry out strikes targeting above-ground ballistic missile launch sites and command and control centres in Iran.
The Qatari air force says it shot down two Iranian Su-24 jets over the Persian Gulf.
The U.S. military says it has struck IRGC Navy drone carrier IRIS Shahid Bagheri.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: As a response to Israel's attacks against Iran and Israel's occupation of parts of Lebanon, Hezbollah fired two projectiles targeting an Israeli military base near Haifa. Israel then responded with attacks in Beirut and across many villages in Lebanon. At least 52 people are killed and 149 more are injured.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Lebanese prime minister Nawaf Salam bans Hezbollah’s military activities following an attack on Israel.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukrainian drones strike an oil terminal in the Russian port city of Novorossiysk, Krasnodar Krai. Four residential buildings in the area are reportedly damaged in the attack.

The Taliban says the Afghan military has successfully repelled Pakistani warplanes with surface-to-air missiles that were attacking Bagram Airfield as explosions are reported in several cities, including Kabul.

context: Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran war
text: Iranian semi-official news agency Mehr News Agency reports that the former royal residence and UNESCO World Heritage Site Golestan Palace is damaged by an airstrike.
Qatari-state owned QatarEnergy halts all LNG production at its Ras Laffan Industrial City following an Iranian drone attack.
A floor collapses in an under-construction building in Johannesburg, South Africa, killing nine people.
Save the Children announces that vaccines have arrived in the Sudanese state of South Kordofan, their first in three years since the civil war broke out.
The owner is killed and three others are critically injured in a mass shooting inside a newly launched hotel in Churu district, Rajasthan, India. Three suspects are arrested.

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Indian prime minister Narendra Modi agree to a deal that would strengthen their economic partnership, aimed at boosting ties after two years of strained relationship between the two countries.

context: France and weapons of mass destruction
text: French president Emmanuel Macron announces that France will increase its stockpile of nuclear weapons for the first time in decades citing global threats such as Russia's war on Ukraine, China's growing military power in Asia, and changing U.S. defense priorities as reasons for the nuclear build-up.

context: France and weapons of mass destruction
text: Denmark and France make an agreement on strategic nuclear deterrence. However, French nuclear weapons are not to be located on Danish territory.

context: Rwanda–United States relations, Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
text: The U.S. Department of State imposes sanctions on the Rwandan military for allegedly supporting the March 23 Movement and violating a peace agreement with the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
U.S. military aircraft begin to leave Spain after the Spanish government denied the U.S. permission to use their airbases for military operations against Iran.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: A protest organized by the Party for Socialism and Liberation is held in Phoenix, Arizona near the Arizona State Capitol. Additionally, counter-protests are held in support of the war and praise the Trump administration for the strikes.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: Anti-war protests are held in Des Moines, Iowa, against the US-Israel strikes.
Left-wing parties in India organize protests in Vijayawada against the war and the killing of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

context: 2026 Winter Paralympics > Belarus at the 2026 Winter Paralympics, Russia at the 2026 Winter Paralympics
text: Lithuanian broadcaster Lithuanian National Radio and Television says it will not air the opening ceremony of the upcoming Winter Paralympics, citing the participation of athletes from Belarus and Russia.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: An Iranian drone strike damages Al Minhad Air Base, the headquarters of the Australian military's Joint Task Force 633. Australian defence minister Richard Marles confirms that there were no casualties in the strike.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: A large fire is reported at an oil terminal in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, following an Iranian Shahed drone attack.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: France deploys Rafale fighter jets to the UAE in response to Iranian attacks, according to French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Explosions and fires are reported at the United States embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following a series of Iranian drone strikes.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Qatar announces it has arrested 10 people from two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps cells for espionage and sabotage.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Akrotiri and Dhekelia
text: British prime minister Keir Starmer says he has approved the deployment of Royal Navy warship HMS Dragon to the island of Cyprus to protect the British Overseas Territory of Akrotiri and Dhekelia from further Iranian attacks.
The Iranian Red Crescent Society says the death toll from Israeli and American airstrikes in Iran has risen to 787 with thousands more wounded.
The Israeli Air Force strikes the presidential administration and Supreme National Security Council buildings in Tehran, Iran, with "multiple munitions".

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio discloses that the initial U.S. attack on Iran was due to an Israeli intention to attack Iranian leadership, which would have jeopardized U.S. forces in the region.

The International Atomic Energy Agency confirms the entrances to the underground Natanz Nuclear Facility in Iran have been bombed. However, there are no signs of any increase in radiation at the facility.
Airstrikes hit the Assembly of Experts building in Qom, Iran. The building appears to have been severely damaged in the attack.
Jordan reopens their airspace to civilian aviation traffic, including for transits, arrivals, and departures, after a closure that has been in effect since Monday evening.
U.S. forces destroy Iran's lead Shahid Soleimani-class corvette, the IRIS Shahid Soleimani.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Following a series of drone and rocket attacks by Hezbollah, the Israeli military launch a ground offensive into Lebanon, capturing several positions along the Israel—Lebanon border.

The Taliban confirms 28 Afghan troops have been killed in recent clashes with Pakistani forces along their border. The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan reports at least 42 civilians have been killed.

At least 14 Nigerian Army soldiers and a local imam are killed and several others are injured in two separate attacks by suspected Islamic State – West Africa Province militants on army bases in Gwoza, Borno State, Nigeria.
The U.S. Southern Command announces that the U.S. military has joined the Ecuadorian Armed Forces against narcoterrorists and drug cartels in the country.
Russian liquified natural gas (LNG) tanker Arctic Metagaz catches fire in the Mediterranean Sea after being struck by a Ukrainian naval drone.

More than 200 people are killed, including around 70 minors, when a landslide collapses a mine at the Rubaya mines in Masisi Territory, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. A different landslide collapsed mines at the same site in January, killing over 400.
Two people are killed and three others are critically injured after a helicopter crashes in Pililla, Rizal, Philippines.
Oman Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi renews his push for diplomacy, stating that diplomatic options are still available.

Cuban prosecutors charge six Cuban nationals with "crimes of terrorism" and accuse them of entering Cuba with a US-flagged boat to cause unrest in the country, which was intercepted by the Cuban coast guard, resulting in a shootout.

Trinidad and Tobago declares a new state of emergency in response to a wave of violent crime in the country, including 63 murders since the beginning of the year and a series of gang-related mass shootings.
Purported yakuza leader Takeshi Ebisawa is convicted by a New York federal court and sentenced to 20 years in prison for trafficking nuclear material, drugs, and weapons.

context: Visa policy of the United Kingdom
text: The United Kingdom announces that it will stop issuing student visas to nationals of Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar, and Sudan and suspend work visas for Afghan nationals, citing a rise in asylum applications from individuals entering through legal visa processes.
A total lunar eclipse occurs in eastern Asia, Oceania, Pacific, and the Americas.
Astronomers announce the discovery 1,900 light-years from Earth of TIC 120362137, the tightest known quadruple star system, using data from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Anonymous state intelligence sources tell The New York Times that the Iranian intelligence ministry have signalled to the United States Central Intelligence Agency an openness to talks on ‌bringing an end to the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: An Iranian ballistic missile strikes the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, the largest U.S. military base in the region.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Sinking of IRIS Dena
text: The Iranian frigate is torpedoed and sunk by U.S. Navy submarine USS Charlotte in waters off Sri Lanka, killing at least 87 of the 180 people on board, while 32 others are rescued by the Sri Lanka Navy with 61 remaining missing.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 interceptions of Iranian missiles in Turkey
text: Turkey and NATO forces shoot down a suspected Iranian ballistic missile that was about to enter Turkish airspace.
An Israeli Air Force F-35 shoots down an Iranian Yak-130 fighter jet over Tehran with an air-to-air missile.

U.S. defense secretary Pete Hegseth announces that the U.S. Air Force will have uncontested air supremacy of Iranian airspace within days, and that Iran's military capabilities are "evaporating by the hour" due to constant U.S. and Israeli strikes.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Israeli strikes on a hotel and residential areas in the towns of Aramoun and Saadiyat, in the south of Beirut, kill eleven people and injure four others.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Three people are killed and six more injured during two Israeli strikes on the road to the airport in Beirut.

A task force rescues two minors in an operation against FARC dissidents in Puerto Valencia, El Retorno, Guaviare Department, and arrests four militants and recovers M60 machine guns, assault rifles, explosives, and ammunition.
Five cartel members are killed in a shootout with government forces in Rayones, Nuevo León, Mexico.

A major blackout across much of western Cuba, including Havana, leaves millions without power, following a fault at the Antonio Guiteras power plant in Matanzas. Officials estimate it will last at least 72 hours.
Air France announces the suspension of flights between France and Cuba, starting from March 29 until at least June 15 due to a jet fuel shortage in Cuba.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Several of the United Arab Emirates stock exchanges will resume, including Nasdaq Dubai, Dubai Financial Market, and Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, after being put on pause for two days due to the Iranian strikes.
Four people are injured after an explosion at an oil extraction plant in Logan Township, New Jersey, United States.
At least six people are killed and 15 others are injured when a passenger bus and a semi-trailer truck collide in Tamacine, Touggourt Province, Algeria.
A nationwide blackout occurs in Iraq with the Ministry of Electricity saying the power grid has gone down entirely, and that the cause is under investigation.
The Supreme Court of Brazil orders the arrest of former Banco Master president and major shareholder Daniel Vorcaro in a fraud investigation of potentially up to 12 billion reals in missing funds.

context: Hong Kong–mainland China relations, China–United Kingdom relations, Chinese intelligence activity abroad
text: The Central Criminal Court in London, United Kingdom, charge two British Chinese nationals of violating the National Security Act for spying on diasporic Hong Kongers on behalf of the China-appointed Hong Kong government.
The United States Senate rejects a War Powers Resolution that would check president Donald Trump's power in the Iran war, making it the first vote on the conflict in U.S. Congress.

Taiwanese prosecutors indict 62 people, including Chen Zhi, for their alleged links to the Prince Group, a multinational criminal network that operates scam centers in Cambodia. They also charge 13 companies with offences related to the criminal organization and money laundering.
The Tokyo High Court in Japan orders the dissolution of the Unification Church.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: U.S. Marine veteran Brian McGinnis interrupts a U.S. Senate hearing in protest of the Iran war and is removed by the United States Capitol Police assisted by US Senator Tim Sheehy (R-MT).
A anti-war protest is held in Ottawa, Canada outside a defense conference at the Château Laurier to call for an end to the war and a reduction in defense spending.

Slovak prime minister Robert Fico announces that his government will repeal a law abolishing the country's whistleblower protection office after the Constitutional Court suspended the measure and the European Commission opened infringement proceedings against Slovakia.

The KAIROS rocket developed by private spaceflight company Space One suffers its third launch failure from Spaceport Kii in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, while carrying a small government test satellite. The flight was terminated two minutes after launch.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Akrotiri and Dhekelia
text: Spain announces that the frigate Cristóbal Colón will join French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle and Greek Navy ships to protect the British military bases in Cyprus.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Akrotiri and Dhekelia
text: Italy announces that it will dispatch naval assets to Cyprus. The Dutch navy is also joining the European naval task force.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says that Iran is not seeking a ceasefire or negotiations with the United States.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Azerbaijan
text: Suspected Iranian drones strike Nakhchivan International Airport in Azerbaijan, targeting the passenger terminal. At least two people are injured.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military reports that 74 Iranian missiles and 117 hostile drones have been intercepted and destroyed. A missile hit an oil refinery, causing a fire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Iraq
text: Iraqi forces shoot down a drone that attempted to attack the United States' airbase near Baghdad.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: The Qatari military says that the country was targeted today by 14 ballistic missiles and four drones coming from Iran; all of them were intercepted and no casualties were reported.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates's air defence systems intercept six ballistic missiles and 125 drones launched by Iran. Six people were injured by falling debris over Abu Dhabi.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Kurdish rebellion in Iran
text: United States president Donald Trump says U.S. Air Force jets will provide "extensive air cover" for Kurdish forces in any ground offensive against the Iranian government.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: China is reportedly in talks with Iran to allow crude oil and Qatari liquefied natural gas vessels safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: The Israeli military issues an evacuation order for Dahieh, Beirut, Lebanon, a densely populated suburb which is also a stronghold of Hezbollah, telling residents to "save your lives and evacuate your homes immediately". Thousands of people flee following the warning.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russia and Ukraine exchange prisoners of war, with 200 soldiers returned to each side.
The Ukrainian Navy shoots down a Russian Naval Aviation Kamov Ka-27 helicopter over the Black Sea.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: South Korean president Lee Jae Myung orders the activation of a ₩100 trillion (about US$68 billion) stabilization fund to address volatility in the country's financial markets linked to the Iran war.

context: Tariffs in the second Trump administration
text: Around 24 U.S. states file a lawsuit against the Trump administration after president Trump imposed a 10% global tariff, the first lawsuit challenging those tariffs.
At least six people are killed, eight others are rescued, and six are trapped when a nursing home collapses in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Four people are killed and two others are injured when a Beechcraft 1900 of the Algerian Air Force crashes at Boufarik Airport near Boufarik, Blida Province, Algeria.
An Indian Air Force Su-30MKI fighter jet crashes shortly after taking off from Jorhat Airport in Karbi Anglong district, Assam, India, killing both pilots.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that an explosion struck a tanker anchored in waters about 60 kilometers off the coast of Kuwait, causing an oil spill from a damaged cargo tank.
sources: AFP via The New Zealand Herald

text: Australia and New Zealand deploy military assets, including two RNZAF aircraft, and crisis response teams to the Middle East to assist and evacuate their respective nationals.

The Lebanese cabinet bans activities by members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps within Lebanon and instructs authorities to detain and deport individuals linked to the group. The cabinet also introduces a visa requirement for Iranian nationals entering the country.

French president Emmanuel Macron announces that France will strengthen its cooperation with the Lebanese Armed Forces and provide them with armored transport vehicles as well as operational and logistical support.

Ecuador declares Cuba's ambassador to the country a persona non grata and orders him and all his diplomatic staff to leave the country within 48 hours. Shortly after the announcement, a man was filmed by the Associated Press on the roof of the Cuban embassy in Quito burning a bag of papers.
The United States and Venezuela agree to re-establish diplomatic and consular relations.
Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko pardons 18 political prisoners, including 15 for political charges and three who were convicted of unspecified crimes.
In Kosovo, the 120 members of the Kuvendi fail to elect the president. The Kuvendi is expected to dissolve, with parliamentary elections scheduled to be set within 45 days.
Nepalis vote to elect 275 seats of the House of Representatives nearly six months after the Gen Z protests.
U.S. president Donald Trump dismisses Kristi Noem as Secretary of Homeland Security and nominates Oklahoma senator Markwayne Mullin to replace her.

context: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Texas district 23
text: Brandon Herrera, a gun manufacturer and youtuber presumptively becomes the GOP's nominee for the district, after incumbent representative Tony Gonzales drops from the race following a scandal involving a former aide.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: Iranian diaspora protesters clash with anti-war protesters at a Ali Khamenei vigil at Washington Square Park in New York City, United States.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war
text: Demonstrators in Sanaa, Yemen, rally in solidarity with Iran and Lebanon amidst the conflict.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: The Qatari government announces that its military had intercepted nine Iranian drones, while one drone struck an uninhabited area.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: The Qatar Civil Aviation Authority partially reopens the country's airspace through designated contingency routes with limited capacity. Operations initially included evacuation flights for stranded passengers and air cargo services.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: United States president Donald Trump calls for the "unconditional surrender" of Iran, saying there will be no deal or further talks. This comes after Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that several countries have initiated mediation efforts to end the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Azerbaijan
text: Azerbaijan's State Security Service affirms it has thwarted a terror attack plotted by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including possible strikes against the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military announces that its air defence continue to intercept successive waves of Iranian attacks, with 84 missiles and 147 drones destroyed since the onset of hostilities.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: Drones hit a hotel in Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: An Iranian ballistic missile strikes Prince Sultan Air Base in Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia. The Saudi defense ministry says air defenses intercepted three missiles launched to the base, as well as four drones east of the province.
An Israeli IAI Heron UAV is shot down over Khuzestan province, Iran.
U.S. Army AH-64 Apache helicopters launch air-to-surface missiles at Popular Mobilization Forces positions near Mosul, Iraq.
The Iranian Red Crescent Society reports the death toll from the Israeli and American air campaign in Iran has risen to 1,332.

At least 41 people are killed, including three soldiers, and 40 more injured in Israeli air and ground raids on Al-Nabi Shayth, Beqaa Valley. The Israeli commandos tried unsuccessfully to locate and take away the remains of missing pilot Ron Arad. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/07/israel-strikes-eastern-lebanon-killing-dozens-after-raid-to-recover-idf-pilots-remains-fails (The Guardian)]
Three Ghanaian peacekeepers are injured in an Israeli missile strike in southern Lebanon.

The U.S. defense department says its military has carried out airstrikes on narcoterrorists in Ecuador at the request of the Ecuadorian government, targeting a camp belonging to a faction of the FARC dissidents at the border with Colombia.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees reports at least 100,000 civilians have now been displaced from their homes due to the fighting between Afghanistan and Pakistan, while Afghan forces say they have destroyed 14 more Pakistani military outposts along the border and downed a drone.

The Sudanese military recaptures the town of Barah in North Kordofan, Sudan, following a ground assault backed by airstrikes against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), reportedly inflicting heavy losses on the RSF and destroying 32 RSF combat vehicles.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Russia and Ukraine exchange prisoners of war, with 300 soldiers returned to each side.
A wave of severe weather and a related tornado outbreak, kill at least eight people and cause widespread damage in the central United States.
The Japanese agriculture ministry confirms a H5N1 bird flu outbreak at a poultry farm in Abira, Hokkaido.
Police in Moscow, Russia, detain Iranian nationals who celebrated the killing of former supreme leader Ali Khamenei in public.

context: Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
text: A United States appeals court declines to allow Donald Trump's administration to end temporary protected status for more than 350,000 Haitian nationals, leaving in place a lower court order that blocks the policy while the case proceeds.
Exiled Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi, son of the late former shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, says he is ready to lead a potential transition if the Iranian government falls.

context: 2026 Kosovan presidential election, 2026 Kosovan parliamentary election
text: Kosovan president Vjosa Osmani dissolves the Kuvendi, attempting to set new parliamentary elections within 45 days. The Vetëvendosje party maintains that the constitution allows parliament 60 more days to try to elect a president, seeking to challenge Osmani's decree at the Constitutional Court.

Indonesia announces that it will prohibit social media access for users under the age of 16 and begin deactivating accounts belonging to minors on several major platforms as part of a phased policy intended to address risks such as internet fraud and excessive internet use.
The opening ceremony of the Winter Paralympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo is held in Verona Arena, Verona, Italy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali says that Iran is ready for normal talks but also rejects the current position by the United States.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Dubai International Airport suspends operations after an aerial interception near the airport during Iranian drone and missile attacks in the region. Airport operations later partially resume as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) continues responding to the aerial threats.

Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian apologizes for Iran's attacks on its Middle Eastern neighbors and states that the Interim Leadership Council had agreed not to attack them "unless an attack on Iran originates from those countries". The military later continues the strikes. The governments of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE report attacks targeting their territories.
The United States embassy in Baghdad, Iraq, is attacked with four rockets. Iraqi prime minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani orders the security forces to pursue the perpetrators of the "terrorist act".
The Lebanese health ministry reports that Israeli airstrikes on multiple locations in southern Lebanon killed eight people, including six in Kherbet Selem and two in Kfar Reman.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Kharkiv Oblast governor Oleh Syniehubov says that Russia has launched a barrage of drones and missiles on residential areas in Kharkiv, Ukraine, killing ten people, including two children and injuring ten, as well as damaging the city's power grids.

At least four people are killed, including two policemen, and more than 35 others are injured, including three seriously, in two separate bombings targeting a police patrol van and a market in Wana and Lakki Marwat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
At least 33 people are injured, including three minors and five others seriously, in a bombing at a nightclub in Trujillo, La Libertad Department, Peru. No group has yet claimed responsibility.
At least 45 bandits and three military personnel are killed in a clash between Nigerian troops and armed bandits in Dan Musa, Katsina State, Nigeria.

context: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The Kuwait Petroleum Corporation announces a precautionary reduction in crude oil production and refining operations in response to Iranian attacks and threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Flash floods in Nairobi, Kenya, disrupt flights and result in at least 23 deaths.
Sudan's health ministry announces that the country will launch a hepatitis B vaccine campaign for newborns in 10 states.

United States president Donald Trump meets with leaders from twelve American countries for the launching of a new multinational military cooperation initiative called Shield of the Americas, led by special envoy Kristi Noem. .
At the Shield of the Americas summit, U.S. president Trump says that the United States formally recognizes the Venezuelan government of Delcy Rodríguez.
Child murderer Ian Huntley dies in a hospital nine days after being attacked by a fellow inmate at HM Prison Frankland in County Durham, England, United Kingdom.
An improvised explosive device is detonated during a protest outside the residence of mayor Zohran Mamdani in New York City, United States.

Partial preliminary results in Nepal indicate that the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) won 60 of 165 first-past-the-post seats, while also leading in 61 other consituencies. In Jhapa 5, RSP prime ministerial candidate Balen Shah defeats former prime minister K. P. Sharma Oli.

Guinea dissolves 40 political parties by decree, including the three main opposition groups—the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea, the Rally of the Guinean People, and the Union of Republican Forces—for failing to meet legal requirements, and orders the seizure of their assets.

context: 2026 Winter Paralympics > Russia at the 2026 Winter Paralympics
text: Russia wins their first Winter Paralympics medal since 2014 after Varvara Voronchikhina and Alexey Bugaev each won a bronze medal in para alpine skiing.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: An Iranian drone hits and damages a desalination plant in Bahrain. In addition, falling missile debris injures three people and damages a university building in Manama.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini health ministry reports that an Iranian drone strike on the island of Sitra injured 32 civilians, including four with serious injuries.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: The main building of the Public Institution for Social Security in Kuwait City suffers an airstrike. A large fire breaks out, but no injuries are reported.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: The United States Central Command confirms that a U.S. service member has died of wounds sustained after an Iranian attack on a base in Saudi Arabia on March 1, bringing the confirmed death toll among U.S. forces to seven since the start of the conflict.
Joint airstrikes by Israel and the United States are carried out against oil facilities in Tehran and other Iranian cities, killing at least four truck drivers and causing large fires.

According to Israeli sources, United Arab Emirates (UAE) warplanes carried out airstrikes against Iran, and purportedly struck a desalination plant. However, UAE officials denied any involvement in the alleged attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Four people are killed and 10 more injured in an Israeli airstrike on a Ramada hotel in central Beirut.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Two Israeli soldiers are killed in overnight clashes with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
Israel launches an airstrike and tank shell targeting Hamas members in Gaza City and the Nuseirat refugee camp in the Gaza Strip, killing six Palestinians, including two children.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
text: Two Palestinians are shot dead by Israeli settlers in Abu Falah, in the occupied West Bank. Another Palestinian is killed after Israeli soldiers throw smoke grenades during the attack.
A military projectile struck a residential area in Al-Kharj, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia, killing two people and injuring 12 others.
Civilians flee Akobo, South Sudan, after the military issued an evacuation order to prepare for a military operation.
A bomb exploded at the American embassy in Oslo, Norway, causing minor damage, no one was injured.

context: United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
text: Six people are killed during an American airstrike against a boat in the Pacific Ocean.

context: 2026 New York City protest bombing attempt
text: Two counter-protesters are arrested after throwing improvised explosive devices at an anti-Islam demonstration outside Gracie Mansion in New York City, United States.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The price of oil surpasses US$100 per barrel for the first time in four years.
Five people are killed and 60 others are injured when a bus carrying Zimbabwean nationals collides with a car on N6 near Stutterheim, Eastern Cape, South Africa.
At least four people are killed and several others are trapped after a section of the Bantar Gebang landfill in Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia, collapses amid heavy rainfall.
Two people are killed and 19 people are injured following a mining incident in Samarkandek, Batken Region, Kyrgyzstan.

A fire occurs in a historic building adjoining the Glasgow Central railway station in Scotland, United Kingdom. The building collapses, destroying a number of businesses and shops. The fire also causes the disruption and cancellation of many train services, with Glasgow Central promptly shutting down until further notice.
Peruvian authorities arrest three people following a bombing at a nightclub in Trujillo, La Libertad Department, that injured 44 people.
Colombians vote to elect 183 members of the Chamber of Representatives and 103 members of the Senate.
Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of the late Ali Khamenei, is elected as the next Supreme Leader of Iran.

The Rastriya Swatantra Party wins 124 direct seats and leads in one more from 164 of 165 constituencies reported so far in Nepal. The results from the Dhanusha 1 constituency are withheld pending an order from the Supreme Court.

Swiss voters reject a referendum proposing to reduce the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation's annual licence fee. They also reject a proposal for a climate fund and support efforts to maintain the status of cash and remove individual taxation for married couples.

India wins the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup, beating New Zealand by 96 runs in the final. They become the first team to win back-to-back T20 World Cups, the first team to win the title at home as hosts, and the first team to win the tournament three times.

context: 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup, 2026 Iranian diaspora protests
text: Diaspora protesters surround the bus of the Iranian women's soccer team following their match against the Philippines in Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia, amidst fears of their safety upon returning to Iran after members of the team gave SOS hand signals from the team bus.
Nathan Martin wins the 2026 Los Angeles Marathon in the marathon's closest-ever finish, becoming the second consecutive American to win the event.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
text: The Inter-Services Public Relations announces that the Pakistan Navy has launched Operation Muhafiz-ul-Bahr to safeguard Pakistan's Sea Lines of Communication (SLOC) and ensure the uninterrupted flow of national energy supplies amidst disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: French president Emmanuel Macron announces that France and other states will create a naval escort mission for merchant ships in the framework of Operation Aspides.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 interceptions of Iranian missiles in Turkey
text: Turkey and NATO forces shoot down a suspected Iranian ballistic missile violating Turkish airspace, with debris falling in Gaziantep Province.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Hezbollah–Israel war
text: Lebanese Maronite Catholic priest Father Pierre al-Rahi is killed by an Israeli double strike on a house in the Christian-majority town of Al-Qlayaa, Lebanon.

Islamist militants conduct coordinated overnight attacks on several locations in northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 12 soldiers and three civilians in fighting with government forces. The assaults target military positions in Borno and Yobe states and result in damage to military facilities and nearby homes.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: Bapco Energies declares force majeure on certain refinery operations in Bahrain after damage to its facilities by Iranian strikes, temporarily affecting shipments.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Bangladesh closes all universities by advancing the Eid al-Fitr holidays as part of emergency measures to reduce electricity consumption during an energy crisis linked to the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 rises after United States president Donald Trump says that the war in Iran is “very complete”, hinting that it could end soon. Additionally, oil prices have dipped under $100 following his remarks.
At least fourteen migrants are found drowned and seven others are rescued after their boat collides with a Coast Guard boat off the coast of Demre, Antalya Province, Turkey.
The death toll from floods in Nairobi, Kenya, rises to 42.
Seven workers are killed and four are critically injured after being buried under soil during excavation work at a construction site near Dharuhera in Haryana, India.

context: Azerbaijan–Iran relations > 2026 Iranian strikes on Azerbaijan
text: Azerbaijan reopens its border crossings with Iran to cargo traffic after closing them following a drone incident in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian, who denies Iran's involvement, tells Azerbaijani president Ilham Aliyev that Iran is investigating the incident.

NATO conducts military drills in Greenland involving over 25,000 troops from 14 nations including Denmark and the United States in a effort to de-escalate tensions over efforts by Trump to annex the island. The exercise will last until March 19.

context: Syrian civil war, Syria–United Kingdom relations
text: The Crown Prosecution Service charges a former Syrian soldier from the Air Force Intelligence Directorate with three counts of murder and three counts of torture as crimes against humanity under the International Criminal Court Act for his attacks on civilians in Damascus in 2011.

context: Terrorism in Belgium, Antisemitism in contemporary Belgium
text: A synagogue in Liège, Belgium, is damaged by an explosion. It is being investigated as a potential act of terrorism.

The United States reaches a deferred prosecution agreement with Turkey's state-owned lender Halkbank to resolve criminal charges alleging that the bank helped Iran evade U.S. sanctions. Under the agreement, Halkbank must implement compliance monitoring and avoid transactions that benefit Iran, after which the charges may be dismissed pending court approval.

The ruling Historic Pact coalition wins 25 of 102 seats in the Senate, becoming the largest bloc but falling short of a majority. The Democratic Centre places second with 17 seats, while other seats are distributed among several parties, resulting in a hung parliament that will require coalition negotiations.

The Constitutional Court of Kosovo issues an injunction that freezes President Vjosa Osmani's decree dissolving the Kuvendi, while also preventing both the President from calling snap elections and the Kuvendi from carrying out parliamentary business until the Constitutional Court delivers its final ruling.
António José Seguro is sworn in as President of Portugal, succeeding Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa.
Malagasy president Michael Randrianirina dismisses prime minister Herintsalama Rajaonarivelo and his cabinet.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: The Ruwais refinery in Al Dhannah, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates, shuts down after a drone strike that causes a fire.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: United States intelligence sources report that Iran has started to deploy underwater mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The Central Command says that American forces have sunk several Iranian ships, including 16 minelaying vessels.

context: 2026 Iran war > United Kingdom involvement in the 2026 Iran war
text: Royal Navy warship HMS Dragon leaves Portsmouth and heads to Cyprus in response to a drone strike on the United Kingdom's RAF Akrotiri base.

According to Iran International, American and Israeli airstrikes have killed many Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commanders and generals, including Basij chief Asadollah Badfar. Prior to his reported death, Badfar was involved in crackdowns against the 2025–2026 protests.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Six people are killed and 37 others are injured in a Ukrainian missile attack in Bryansk, Russia.
The Ukrainian Special Operations Forces announce several overnight drone strikes on Russian electronic warfare stations and warehouses in Donetsk and Makiivka, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
Forty people are killed in a drone strike on a truck carrying funeralgoers near Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan.
Seven people, including three children, are killed and 13 others are injured in a Rapid Support Forces drone strike in Dilling, South Kordofan, Sudan.

context: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The price of West Texas Intermediate crude oil rises by more than five percent to US$87.65 per barrel after United States president Donald Trump escalated threats related to the Strait of Hormuz.

context: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Thai prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul orders remote work and the suspension of official international trips for government officials, and reduced electricity use in government buildings amid supply concerns linked to the Iranian war.
At least two are killed and six are injured after a hailstorm and four possible tornadoes strike the vicinity of Kankakee, Illinois, and Wheatfield, Indiana, United States.

The Indonesian rescue agency ends search and rescue operations after a garbage landslide at the Bantar Gebang landfill in Bekasi, West Java, on March 8 killed seven people, with all individuals previously reported missing accounted for.
Five people are killed and eleven others are injured when a bus collides with a truck on the Kampala–Gulu Highway near Bweyale Town, Kiryandongo District, Uganda.

The U.S. National Snow and Ice Data Center reports that Arctic sea ice reached about 14.22 million square kilometers, which is among the lowest yearly high points recorded in more than four decades of satellite monitoring.

context: Australia–Iran relations, Defection of Iran women's national football team
text: Australia grants humanitarian visas to five Iranian women football players who sought asylum, including captain Zahra Ghanbari, Mona Hamoudi, Fatemeh Pasandideh, Atefeh Ramezanizadeh, and Zahra Sarbali, citing fears of persecution after refusing to sing Iran's national anthem before an Asian Cup match in Gold Coast, Queensland.

context: Azerbaijan–Netherlands relations, Iran–Netherlands relations, Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
text: Dutch foreign minister Tom Berendsen announces the temporary relocation of staff and operations of the Netherlands' embassy in Tehran to Baku, Azerbaijan, citing security risks to personnel amid the Iranian war.

context: China–North Korea relations, Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on public transport
text: Train services between Beijing, China, and Pyongyang, North Korea, are announced to resume for the first time since it was suspended six years ago due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Iranian intelligence ministry announces the arrest of 30 individuals, including one unidentified foreign national, on allegations of espionage during the war, accusing the foreign suspect of providing information on the locations and movements of Iranian security forces and military facilities to hostile parties.
Six people are killed and five others are injured in a suspected arson attack on a postal bus in Kerzers, Fribourg Canton, Switzerland.
Shots are fired at the United States consulate in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, with no casualties. Police are investigating the shooting as a national security incident.

context: Reform of the House of Lords
text: Members of the House of Lords vote to pass a bill to remove hereditary peers and heads to King Charles III for royal assent.
Cardinal Louis Sako, the Patriarch of the Chaldean Catholic Church, based in Iraq, retires at the age of 76.

Malagasy interim president and military leader Michael Randrianirina removes prime minister Herintsalama Rajaonarivelo from power and dissolves the entire Cabinet without explanation, five months after they were assigned following the 2025 protests.
Tibetans protest worldwide after 67 years of China's occupation of Tibet.

In basketball, Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo scores 83 points in a 150–129 win over the Washington Wizards, marking the second-most points in a game in NBA history and most since Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game in 1962. Adebayo’s 36 free throws and 43 attempts also set single-game NBA records.

context: 2026 Winter Paralympics > Brazil at the 2026 Winter Paralympics
text: Brazilian skier Cristian Ribera wins Brazil's, Latin America's and South America's first ever medal at the Winter Paralympics.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian lists preconditions for ending the war between Iran, Israel, and the United States. The conditions include recognizing Iran's legitimate rights, payment of reparations, and firm international guarantees against future aggression.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Thailand-flagged bulk carrier is hit by two Iranian missiles shortly after passing the Strait of Hormuz. Twenty people are rescued and three are reported missing after the vessel catches on fire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Two cargo vessels, the Marshall Islands-flagged Star Gwyneth, operated by Star Bulk Carriers, and the Japan-flagged ONE Majesty, operated by Mitsui OSK Lines, are struck by unknown projectiles, with no casualties reported.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: A bulk carrier is hit by an unknown projectile 50NM northwest of Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
text: Iran drones strike oil storage facilities at the port of Salalah, causing several fuel tanks to burst into flames.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: Two tankers carrying Iraqi oil and gas, Marshall Islands-flagged Safesea Vishnu and Malta-flagged Zefyros, catch fire after being struck in Iraqi territorial waters off Khor Al Zubair Port and near the Al-Faw port area. An Indian member of the first crew is killed in the attack.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Seven people are killed and 23 others are injured after an Israeli strike on Temnine Et Tahta, Baalbek-Hermel Governorate, Lebanon. Five people are also injured after a strike on the nearby village of Aali en Nahri.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah launches over 100 rockets at Israel, injuring five civilians in Upper Galilee.
Four people are injured in the United Arab Emirates after two drones fall near Dubai International Airport.

A United Nations aid worker from France is killed in a series of explosions caused by drone strikes in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the occupying M23 rebels blaming the Congolese government.

At least 17 people are killed in a drone strike on a secondary school and a health center in Shukeiri, White Nile State, Sudan. Local authorities and the Sudan Doctors Union blame the Rapid Support Forces.
Over 20 people are killed and 23 others injured in a Sudanese Armed Forces drone strike in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan.
Norwegian police arrest three brothers on suspicion of involvement in a bombing outside the U.S. embassy in Oslo on 8 March that caused minor damage but no injuries. A terrorist motive is suspected.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The International Energy Agency agrees to discharge 400 million barrels of oil from its members’ strategic reserves, its largest-ever release, to counter soaring global energy prices due to the war. Despite the measure, the price of the crude barrel rises above US$100 again in international markets.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Wynn Resorts says it plans to resume construction on the upcoming Al Marjan Island resort in Ras Al Khaimah following a short pause amidst the war.
Spain permanently withdraws its ambassador to Israel and terminates the position after bilateral diplomatic relations worsened this week.

The United Nations Security Council approves a resolution condemning Iran's attacks on the Gulf Cooperation Council states and Jordan. The text, presented by Bahrain and co-sponsored by 135 countries, is passed with 13 votes in favor and the abstentions of Russia and China.

Romania authorizes the United States to use its air bases to refuel aircraft and deploy monitoring and satellite communications equipment in support of military operations related to the Iran war, following approval by the Romanian parliament and the Supreme Council of National Defence.

context: Censorship of TikTok, Mass media in Albania
text: The Albanian constitutional court rules that the government's ban on the social media platform TikTok violated constitutional protections for freedom of expression and press freedom, after authorities blocked the service in 2025 following a fatal stabbing linked to a dispute on the platform.

Europol reports that more than 330 people in 70 countries have been arrested during an international operation against organized networks suspected of trafficking illegal waste within Europe and exporting it to Africa, Asia, and Latin America, with large quantities of dangerous goods and nearly €10 million (US$11.6 million) in assets seized.
José Antonio Kast is sworn in as President of Chile, succeeding Gabriel Boric.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup, Iran at the FIFA World Cup
text: Iranian sports minister Ahmad Donyamali states that Iran will not participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup to be hosted by Canada, Mexico, and the United States, citing security concerns amid the Iran war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei issues his first public message since his election in which he says that Iran should continue blocking the Strait of Hormuz and advises neighboring countries to close American military bases in their territory. Khamenei also vows to "avenge the blood of our martyrs".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: German shipping company Hapag-Lloyd says that projectile ​fragments ​hit the Liberia-flagged container vessel Source Blessing ⁠near the ​Strait.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Oman orders the evacuation of vessels from the Mina Al Fahal oil port.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: An Iranian strike hits fuel storage tanks at a facility in Muharraq Governorate, Bahrain.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait International Airport is targeted by several drones, causing material damage but no injuries.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: The Saudi defense ministry announces the interception of two missiles and the destruction of seven drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: A French soldier is killed and six others are injured in an Iranian drone attack on a military base in Erbil, Iraq.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Eight people are killed and 31 more injured by an Israeli airstrike on the Ramlet al-Baida beach in central Beirut, Lebanon. Seven more people are also killed in other attacks in the country.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah launches over 200 rockets and 20 UAVs at northern Israel, injuring two people.
At least 20 people are killed in an airstrike targeting a Popular Mobilization Forces building in Akashat, Iraq.
Four people are killed and over 24 others are injured, including seven children, in a drone strike on a market near the Chad–Sudan border in Darfur, Sudan.
The Italian military base in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, is struck by a missile, with no casualties of injuries reported.
Chilean architect Smiljan Radić receives the 2026 Pritzker Architecture Prize, recognizing his contributions to contemporary architecture.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war, Embargo of Russian oil during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The United States treasury department issues a temporary license permitting the delivery and sale of Russian oil and petroleum products already loaded onto vessels before March 12, easing sanctions on such shipments until April 11 amid rising global energy prices.
The Lufthansa pilot union announces a 48-hour strike for all flights departing German airports until Saturday over ongoing disputes about pensions, causing major delays.
At least 102 people are killed and one person is rescued after a series of landslides in the Gamo Zone of Ethiopia.
Eight people are killed after an artisanal mine collapses in Ouham-Pendé, Central African Republic.
At least four crew members are killed when a United States Air Force Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker carrying six crew members crashes after an incident involving another aircraft in western Iraq.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: Iceland and the Netherlands announce they will both intervene on the side of South Africa in the International Court of Justice's genocide case against Israel.

context: Arctic policy of Canada, NATO Arctic Sentry, Polar Icebreaker Project
text: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney announces nearly CAN$35 billion (US$25.7 ‌billion) in funding to strengthen Canada's Arctic infrastructure, including upgrades to military facilities and the construction of new icebreakers to expand the country's operational capacity in the region.

context: Brazil–United States relations, Arrest of Jair Bolsonaro
text: Brazilian Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes denies a request by imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro to receive a visit from American diplomat Darren Beattie, ruling that the meeting falls outside the diplomatic purposes stated in Beattie's visa authorization.
Cuba announces plans to release 51 prisoners following discussions with the Holy See, stating that the detainees have served most of their sentences and demonstrated good conduct.
Hungary returns two seized armored cars to Ukraine but retains approximately US$82 million in cash and gold as authorities investigate suspected money laundering.

context: Iran–Thailand relations, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Thailand summons Iran's ambassador, demanding an apology and an explanation for the attack on the bulk carrier in the waters of the Strait the previous day.
Two people are killed, including the perpetrator, and two other people are critically injured in a school shooting at Old Dominion University in Norfolk, Virginia, United States.

A Russian military court sentences 19 people for their involvement in the terrorist attack at the Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, Moscow Oblast, in 2024. Fifteen of those are sentenced to life in prison while the other four are given between 19 and 22 years in prison.
Two unidentified men assault and injure the deputy director of KontraS, an Indonesian human rights organization, in an acid attack in central Jakarta.
The perpetrator is killed and 31 others are injured in a shooting and vehicle-ramming attack at the Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield Township, Michigan, United States.
The International Criminal Court at The Hague dismisses an investigation into whether U.S. sanctions against Venezuelan officials qualify as crimes against humanity.
A rabbi is seriously injured in a stabbing in Ramat Gan, Israel, as local police suspect a terrorist motive.
The Israeli military drops charges against five soldiers accused of raping a Palestinian prisoner at the Sde Teiman detention camp.

The Nepalese election commission releases the official results of the recent election, with Balen Shah's Rastriya Swatantra Party winning 182 seats in the 275-member House of Representatives. The result gives the party a majority in the House and places it two seats short of a supermajority.

Polish president Karol Nawrocki announces that he will veto legislation enabling Poland to access €43.7 billion (US$50.3 billion) in European Union loans under the Security Action for Europe program to fund military spending.
In basketball, Oklahoma City Thunder player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander breaks the NBA record set by Wilt Chamberlain for most consecutive 20-point games with 127 games.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 interceptions of Iranian missiles in Turkey
text: Turkey intercepts an Iranian ballistic missile violating its airspace.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: At least 58 people are injured by an Iranian ballistic missile strike on northern Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
