text: United States president Donald Trump says that U.S. forces conducted airstrikes on military targets on Kharg Island, Iran, and warns that the U.S. may also target the island's oil infrastructure if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Sinking of IRIS Dena
text: Sri Lanka repatriates the bodies of 84 Iranian sailors killed when the frigate IRIS Dena was sunk by a United States submarine off the coast of Galle on 4 March. Thirty-two rescued sailors remain in Sri Lanka while authorities continue to host other Iranian naval personnel under humanitarian arrangements.
U.S. officials say a marine expeditionary unit of 5,000 marines and sailors will deploy to the Persian Gulf to reinforce existing forces stationed in the region.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Twelve medical staff members, including doctors, nurses and paramedics, are killed in an Israeli airstrike against a medical facility in Burj Qalaouiyah, Bint Jbeil District, Lebanon.
Two migrant workers are killed and several other people are injured after security forces intercept a drone in an industrial area in Sohar, Oman.
The Saudi Arabian defense ministry reports that air defenses intercepted and destroyed 56 hostile drones targeting several areas across the country.
Six people are killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike on a residential area in Kabul, Afghanistan. A fuel depot in Kandahar is also bombed.
Eleven people are killed and 20 others are injured in a drone strike on a fuel reserve in western Sudan.
Armed men ambush and kill twenty security personnel, including two senior military officers, in Plateau State, Nigeria.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Saudi Arabia cuts oil production by 20% after the shutdown of two offshore oil fields, including Safaniya.
The United States military confirms that all six crew members aboard an Air Force Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker died when the aircraft crashed in western Iraq yesterday.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: Cuban president Miguel Díaz-Canel confirms that Cuba is in talks with the U.S. to find solutions to the oil blockade in his country.

context: El Salvador–United States relations, Nuclear power in El Salvador
text: El Salvador and the United States sign Agreement 123 under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to build a nuclear power plant in El Salvador that is planned to be operational by 2030.

context: Illegal drug trade in Latin America
text: Bolivian authorities arrest suspected Uruguayan drug cartel leader during a police operation in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Marset, who is wanted by several countries and has a US$2 million reward linked to money laundering allegations, is detained along with four other individuals.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warns of a stronger response than in January if new protests against the regime erupt.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Five U.S. warplanes are damaged in an Iranian drone strike on Prince Sultan Air Base, Saudi Arabia.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: United States president Donald Trump calls on the country's allies to help lift the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
Fifteen people are killed in a reported Israeli and United States missile strike on an HVAC factory in Isfahan, Iran.
Three Kuwaiti soldiers are injured after two drones struck Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base, damaging the facility.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: The port of Fujairah, a bunkering hub and export terminal in the Emirate of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, suffers a drone attack. UAE authorities report that its air defence intercepted nine ballistic missiles and 33 drones.
The U.S. embassy in Baghdad, Iraq, is hit by a missile from an unknown origin.
Palestinian militant group Hamas calls for Iran to cease their attacks on Middle East neighbors during the war. They also reaffirm Tehran's right to defend itself from Israel and the United States.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israel and Lebanon are expected to hold direct talks in the coming days amidst the reignited war between Israel and Hezbollah.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Five people are killed and three others are injured in Russian drone strikes on residential areas and critical infrastructure across Ukraine.

According to Taliban officials, fourteen Pakistani soldiers are killed and eleven others are injured by Afghan fighters during the capture of a Pakistani guard post along the Durand Line in Kunar Province, Afghanistan.
Seven Indian pilgrims are killed and eight others are injured when a minibus returning from the Manakamana Temple veers off a road and plunges down a slope in Gandaki Province, Nepal.

Cuban authorities arrest five people after a small group of protesters damaged and set fire to a Communist Party office in Morón, Ciego de Ávila Province, during demonstrations over prolonged blackouts and shortages of basic goods.
An explosion lightly damages a Jewish school in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with no reported injuries, making it the third attack against Jewish buildings in the Low Countries this week.

Ecuador begins enforcing a curfew from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. in the provinces of El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos, and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas to support military operations against criminal organizations.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Spain in the 2026 Iran war, Gaza war protests
text: Anti-war protests are held across Spain, including in Madrid, Barcelona, and Valencia, against both the Iran war and the Gaza war, reviving the "No to war" movement.
Protests are held in Italy against the war, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, and upcoming constitutional referendum in the country.

Belarusian opposition activist Maria Kolesnikova receives the Charlemagne Prize in Aachen, Germany, which had been awarded to her in 2022 for her role in advocating for democracy, human rights, and free elections in Belarus while she was imprisoned for her role in the 2020 Belarusian protests against President Alexander Lukashenko.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Formula One World Championship
text: In auto racing, the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile cancels the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, both scheduled to occur in April, due to safety concerns amid the Iran war.

In association football, English attacking midfielder Max Dowman scores for Arsenal in a 2–0 win over Everton to become the youngest ever goal scorer in Premier League history at 16 years and 73 days old.
In rugby union, France defeats England 48–46 to win the Six Nations Championship in the final.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war
text: Eight police officers, including the police chief of the Deir al-Balah Governorate, are killed by an Israeli attack on a police vehicle in Az-Zawayda, Palestine.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
text: Four people are killed and two others are injured when Israel Defense Forces soldiers open fire on a civilian car in northern Israeli-occupied West Bank.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: An Italian MQ-9 Reaper is destroyed in an Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
Afghan forces launch mortars into Pakistan, with one hitting a residential property in Bajaur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing four members of the same family and wounding two others.

The South Sudan People's Defence Forces announces that they have deployed troops in Akobo, South Sudan to secure full control of the area for the first time since the outbreak of the civil war in the country after having previously recapturing the area from opposition forces.
At the Academy Awards, One Battle After Another wins six Academy Awards, including Best Picture and the inaugural Achievement in Casting award.

Sinners wins four Academy Awards following a record 16 nominations, with Ryan Coogler for original screenplay, Michael B. Jordan for lead actor, Autumn Durald Arkapaw for cinematography, and Ludwig Göransson for score.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Japan announces it will start releasing 80 million barrels of oil from its reserves, the largest such release in the country's history, in response to disruptions in the oil supply caused by the conflict.
The death toll from severe flooding in Kenya rises to 66, according to the Kenya Red Cross Society.
Two people are killed and eleven others are hospitalized in serious condition following a meningitis outbreak at the University of Kent in Canterbury, Kent, England.
The first round of municipal elections takes place in France.
Kazakhstanis vote in a referendum to approve a new constitution.
North Koreans vote to elect the 687 members of the 15th Supreme People's Assembly.

context: 2026 Republic of the Congo presidential election
text: Congolese people vote to elect a president, with incumbent Denis Sassou Nguesso seeking a fifth consecutive term.
Vietnamese citizens vote to elect the 500 members of the 16th National Assembly. The sole legal party contesting the election is the Communist Party.

context: 2026 Winter Paralympics > 2026 Winter Paralympics closing ceremony
text: The Winter Paralympics conclude in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, with China as the highest-ranked team in the medal table. The Paralympic flag is handed over to the organizers of the 2030 Winter Paralympics to be held in the French Alps.
In para ice hockey, the United States defeats Canada 6–2, completing the three-peat of hockey championships at the Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Italy.

context: 2026 Formula One World Championship > 2026 Chinese Grand Prix
text: In auto racing, Mercedes-Benz driver Kimi Antonelli wins his first Formula One Grand Prix after also setting his maiden pole position at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix. He becomes the second-youngest Grand Prix winner at 19 years old.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup > Iran at the FIFA World Cup
text: Asian Football Confederation secretary general Windsor John says that the Iran national football team will still play at the upcoming FIFA World Cup despite remarks from U.S. President Donald Trump that their safety could be at risk.
In association football, Joan Laporta is re-elected president of FC Barcelona.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > Operation Muhafiz-ul-Bahr
text: A Pakistan-bound oil tanker with its Automatic Identification System activated, the Karachi, gets safe passage and crosses the Strait of Hormuz following negotiations between the Pakistani and Iranian governments. According to Senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed, Pakistan agreed to pay the oil shipment, purchased from Abu Dhabi, in Chinese yuan instead of in US dollars.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Several NATO allies of the United States, including Germany, Italy, and Spain, rule out sending warships to lift the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz following a request from U.S. president Donald Trump.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Australia rules out sending warships to lift the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says that Iran is not seeking a ceasefire but also called for the war to end.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Iran launches drone attacks on the United Arab Emirates, killing a Palestinian man in Abu Dhabi and forcing the temporary closure of Dubai International Airport. The port of Fujairah, in the Emirate of Fujairah, already attacked two days ago, is also hit.

The Israeli Air Force strikes and completely destroys the Iranian Space Research Center in central Tehran, stating that it was being used for potential space warfare activities against Israeli satellites.
Kata'ib Hezbollah senior commander Abu Ali al-Askari is killed in an airstrike in Baghdad, Iraq.
The U.S. embassy in Baghdad is reportedly attacked by two suicide drones, causing a powerful explosion.
The Royal Tulip Al Rasheed Hotel in the Green Zone in Baghdad is struck by a drone.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: At least seven people, including four children, are injured by Hezbollah rocket and drone attacks on northern Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Israeli military's 91st Division launches a ground operation against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, expanding a buffer zone along the border.

At least four members of Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are killed and three others are injured in an airstrike on a checkpoint at the entrance to Al-Qa'im, Al Anbar Governorate. A PMF official attributes the strike to the United States.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war, International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
text: The European Union imposes sanctions against nine Russian individuals over their role in the mass murder of civilians committed during Russia's occupation of Bucha during the initial 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Kenyan prime cabinet secretary Musalia Mudavadi says that the government has identified two prisoners of war from Kenya that have been detained by authorities in Ukraine after being involved in Russia's special military operations.

Afghanistan claims Pakistani jets bombed a drug rehabilitation centre in Kabul, killing over 400 people. Pakistan denies the claim, saying it attacked military installations. AFP and BBC journalists confirm at least 30 dead as a result of the bombing.

At least 23 people are killed and 108 others are injured in suspected suicide bombings at three locations, including the Monday Market and University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital, in Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria. No group has claimed responsibility.

context: Nigerian bandit conflict, kidnapping in Nigeria
text: One person is killed and seven others are abducted, including children, in an attack on a community in Chikun, Kaduna State, Nigeria.
A police report in New York formally reveals English street artist Banksy's identity as 51-year-old Robin Gunningham from Bristol, England.
Cuba announces that citizens living abroad will be permitted to invest in and own businesses in the country as the government seeks to expand commercial activity amid an economic crisis.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Sri Lanka introduces a four-day workweek for the public and education sectors to preserve fuel as the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis continues to restrict fuel shipments to the region.
Cuba reports a nationwide power outage following a total electrical grid collapse.
Eleven people are killed and ten others are injured in a massive fire at the Srirama Chandra Bhanja Medical College and Hospital in Cuttack, Odisha, India.
A roof collapses at a shop in Rahim Yar Khan, Punjab, Pakistan, killing eight people and injuring more than 50 others.
At least four people are killed and four others are injured in a building collapse in Nairobi, Kenya.

context: Vaccination policy of the United States
text: United States federal judge Brian E. Murphy blocks the implementation of changes to vaccine policy introduced by health and human services secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., including revisions to the childhood immunization schedule and recommendations issued by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. Murphy rules that the measures likely violate required procedures and halts their enforcement pending further legal proceedings.
The death toll from Lassa fever in Nigeria this year rises to 109.
A woman is killed and over 100 others are hospitalized after getting foodborne illness at a pizzeria in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil.
The European Union imposes sanctions against 16 Iranian individuals and three entities for their role in suppressing protests earlier this year.

Kuwaiti authorities arrest 16 people, including two Lebanese nationals, on suspicion of links to Hezbollah and involvement in a planned sabotage operation, with weapons, drones, and communication equipment seized during the operation.
Nepalese activist and Rastriya Swatantra Party member Bhumika Shrestha is confirmed by the Nepalese Election Commission, becoming the first transgender lawmaker elected in Nepal.
India holds its first phase of elections for 37 seats of the Rajya Sabha.
Modeling suggests the presence of a volatile-rich magma ocean on the exoplanet L 98-59 d, a planet orbiting L 98-59, a red dwarf star 35 light-years away from Earth.

In association football, the Premier League fines Chelsea F.C. £10.75 million and gives them a two-year suspended transfer ban for making secret payments worth £47 million to unregistered agents and third-parties between 2011 and 2018.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: An Iranian Khorramshahr missile strikes Ramat Gan in central Israel, killing two people.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: An oil tanker near Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, is struck by an unknown projectile.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Assassination of Ali Larijani
text: Israeli forces assassinate both Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Ali Larijani and Basij commander Gholamreza Soleimani in two separate airstrikes in Tehran. Iran later confirms their deaths.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Russia is actively sharing military intelligence with Iran, including satellite images of United States military bases and locations of potential targets, as well as improved drone technology.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Three Lebanese soldiers are killed and four more are injured during Israeli airstrikes in the Nabatieh Governorate, Lebanon.
Three people, including a child, are killed and 14 more are injured in an Israeli airstrike in Al-Mawasi, Gaza.

The Ecuadorian government deploys 75,000 soldiers and police officers to four provinces to enforce a nightly curfew. Officials say 253 people have already been detained for breaking curfew, which lasts from 11 pm to 5 am local time.

Colombian president Gustavo Petro accuses the Ecuadorian military of being the perpetrator of an airstrike two days ago inside Colombia, killing 27 people, and orders the deployment of its troops to the border in response.
At least 18 people are killed and several others are injured in an attack by armed bandits in a village in Jibia, Katsina State, Nigeria.
Patriarch Ilia II, head of the Georgian Orthodox Church since 1977, dies at the age of 93.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The United Arab Emirates' offshore Shah gas field suspends operations following a drone attack.
Five people are killed following a fire at the Dos Bocas Refinery in Paraíso, Tabasco, Mexico.
Argentine foreign minister Pablo Quirno announces the country's formal withdrawal from the World Health Organization.

A court in Brussels, Belgium, orders former diplomat Étienne Davignon to stand trial on charges of participation in war crimes in connection with the 1961 killing of former Congolese prime minister Patrice Lumumba. Davignon is the only surviving individual among those accused by Lumumba’s family of involvement in the case.

A Vatican appeals court orders a retrial of Cardinal Giovanni Angelo Becciu, who was convicted of embezzlement in 2023, citing procedural errors in the original proceedings. The court maintains his previously imposed prison sentence pending the outcome of the new trial.

The Legislative Assembly of El Salvador votes 59–1 to approve a constitutional amendment to permit courts to issue sentences of life imprisonment to individuals convicted of murder, rape, or terrorism where the limit was previously 60 years.
One person is killed and another is injured in a shooting at Holloman Air Force Base near Alamogordo, New Mexico, United States.

context: 2026 Republic of the Congo presidential election
text: Provisional results announced by interior minister Raymond Mboulou reported that incumbent president of Congo-Brazzaville Denis Sassou Nguesso will be re-elected with 94.82% of the vote.

U.S. National Counterterrorism Center director Joe Kent resigns in protest of the war with Iran, saying that "Iran posed ​no ​imminent ⁠threat to our ⁠nation" and alleged the U.S. entered into the war due to pressure from Israel and its American lobby.
Prime Minister Denisse Miralles resigns and president José María Balcázar names Luis Arroyo to replace her.

In association football, the Confederation of African Football formally overturns the result of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final in which Senegal won 1–0 over hosts Morocco due to a controversial walk-off by Senegalese players during extra-time. Morocco are awarded the title with a 3–0 win, their second title win.
In baseball, Venezuela defeats the United States 3–2 in the championship game to win their first World Baseball Classic.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 South Pars field attack
text: Israel strikes the Iranian South Pars natural gas field in the Persian Gulf and its neighboring refineries in Asaluyeh. Iran announces it will retaliate against regional energy infrastructure.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: A foreign worker from Thailand is killed by an Iranian cluster bomb in Moshav Adanim, central Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Iran launches a missile attack on Ras Laffan Industrial City in Qatar, the world's largest LNG export facility, causing "extensive damage" according to QatarEnergy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia's air defenses intercept and destroy multiple drones targeting gas and energy facilities in the Eastern Province, with no damage reported. In Riyadh, a refinery is attacked by ballistic missiles.

Kata'ib Hezbollah says that it will cease attacks in Iraq if certain conditions are met including for Israel to halt their military operations in Beirut, making it the first time an Iranian-backed militia group said it is open to ceasing attacks since the US-Israel strikes began on February 28.
The U.S. Air Force uses GBU-72 bunker buster bombs for the first time in combat to destroy underground Iranian anti-ship cruise missile sites used to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Israel assassinates Iranian intelligence minister Esmaeil Khatib in an overnight airstrike in Tehran.
Four Palestinians are killed and six others are injured when falling Iranian missile fragments strike a beauty salon in Beit Awwa, West Bank, Palestine.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: The Foreign Ministers from Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Egypt, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates, met in Riyadh, issue a joint statement calling on Iran "to immediately halt its attacks".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: At least 20 people are killed and dozens injured in an Israeli airstrike on a building in Beirut, Lebanon.
A drone strike attributed to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) kills 17 people, including at a funeral, near the border town of Tine, Chad.
In response to the drone strike, Chad president Mahamat Déby orders the military to retaliate against Sudanese belligerents, including the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces.
The Sudan Doctors Network says that 12 civilians were killed by the RSF in North Kordofan state.
The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have shot down a Bayraktar drone from Ethiopia near North Kordofan.
Pakistan and Afghanistan agree to a temporary "pause" in hostilities during the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Fitr this week.
Over 60 Boko Haram and Islamic State insurgents are killed in an operation by the Nigerian Army in Abadam, Borno State, Nigeria.

Cesar Chavez Day celebrations are cancelled in many communities across the United States after late labor leader and civil rights activist Cesar Chavez was accused by dozens of women and girls, including labor leader Dolores Huerta, of child grooming, sexual assault, and rape.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Aramco restarts operations at Ras Tanura oil refinery, the largest in Saudi Arabia, following a 16-day closure.
At least nine people are killed in a building fire near Palam metro station in Delhi, India.
Seven people are killed and three others are critically injured in an explosion and fire at a residential building in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India.
One person is killed when a cable car cabin crashes down a snowy mountainside in Engelberg, Obwalden, Switzerland.
Rollouts of the meningococcal vaccine begin at the University of Kent in England in the wake of a recent meningococcal outbreak that killed two people amidst a rise in cases.

context: Iran–Qatar relations > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Qatar declares Iran's military and security attachés and their staff personae non gratae and orders them to leave the country within 24 hours following an attack on Ras Laffan Industrial City.
Swedish foreign minister Maria Malmer Stenergard says that Iran has executed a Swedish citizen who was arrested in Iran last June.
Venezuelan president Delcy Rodríguez appoints General Gustavo González López as Minister of Defense, replacing General Vladimir Padrino López who has served since 2014.
Charles H. Bennett and Gilles Brassard are awarded the 2025 Turing Award for their work in quantum information science.

In basketball, the WNBA and its players' union reach a tentative agreement on a new collective bargaining agreement that, if ratified by the league and union, will increase average player salaries and the team salary cap more than fourfold.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: The BAZAN Group refinery in Haifa is struck in an Iranian missile attack, but with "no significant damage", according to Energy Minister Eli Cohen.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: A drone hits Aramco's SAMREF refinery in ‌the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Iranian Shahed drones strike the Mina al-Ahmadi and Mina Abdullah oil refineries and cause large fires, according to the Kuwait National Petroleum Company.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The leaders of France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom issue a joint statement condemning the Iranian attacks on commercial vessels and expressing their "readiness to contribute to appropriate efforts to ensure safe passage through the Strait".
A U.S. Air Force F-35 fighter jet is hit in Iranian airspace forcing the pilot to make an emergency landing at a regional U.S. airbase.
The United States Central Command reports its forces have destroyed a factory in Karaj, Iran, which assembled surface-to-surface missiles for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The United States approves $16.46 billion in military sales to the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait amidst the Iran war.
The Chadian government announces that 17 people have been killed at a funeral late Wednesday in the border town of Tiné following a drone attack originating from Sudan.

A raid kills eleven Sinaloa Cartel members in Sinaloa, Mexico, with a senior cartel leader being captured along with many weapons. The daughter of El Mayo is initially detained and then released due to the lack of arrest warrants.
The King Charles III England Coast Path, the world's longest coastal footpath, is formally opened by Charles III.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: KLM says that they will not resume flights to Dammam, Dubai, Riyadh until May 17, citing safety considerations amid the Iran war.
Seventeen bodies are recovered from a boat that washed ashore in the Comoros. The victims are believed to be migrants from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

context: Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
text: In a joint statement after talks hosted by the United States, DR Congo and Rwanda say they have "agreed to a series of coordinated steps to de-escalate tensions and advance progress on the ground".

context: Egypt–Palestine relations, Egypt–Israel relations, Gaza humanitarian crisis
text: The Rafah Border Crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip reopens for limited movement, allowing a restricted number of Palestinian patients to enter Egypt for medical treatment and some people to return to Gaza under coordinated security procedures, following its closure as a security measure amid the 2026 Iran war.

context: South Africa's genocide case against Israel
text: Germany withdraws from defending Israel in South Africa's International Court of Justice genocide case against Israel, citing their need to defend themselves in a separate case launched against them by Nicaragua.

context: International Criminal Court arrest warrants for Russian leaders
text: The International Criminal Court at The Hague, Netherlands, rules that Tajikistan has violated the Rome Statute after failing to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to the country in October 2025.

context: Reactions to the 2025–2026 Iranian protests, 2026 Iran massacres
text: Iran executes three men arrested during protests last January by hanging.
An Iranian man and a Romanian woman are arrested by Police Scotland for attempting to enter Royal Navy base HMNB Clyde.
The National Assembly of Thailand re-elects Anutin Charnvirakul as prime minister following his Bhumjaithai Party's victory in the recent election.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > United Kingdom–United States relations
text: British prime minister Keir Starmer allows the United States to use British bases to strike Iranian targets near the strait to lift the blockade.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Belgium says that it will consider participating in securing the Strait of Hormuz if a ceasefire is in place and if the operation is conducted within a clear international framework.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says that Iran is ready to help the passage of vessels from Japan in the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: The Iranian army launches strikes against strategic aerial refueling aircraft stationed at the Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
text: A second Marine Expeditionary Unit of 2,200 U.S. Marines is being sent to the region.

U.S. president Donald Trump says that the United States is considering "winding down" military operations in Iran as they "are getting very close to meeting [their] objectives" and urges the countries that "use" Hormuz to safeguard the Strait.
Iran confirms the death of IRGC spokesperson Ali Mohammad Naini in an Israeli airstrike in Tehran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza peace plan
text: Ceasefire mediators in Cairo, Egypt, give Hamas and all armed groups in the Gaza Strip 90 days to hand over their weapons in the coming months, including their missiles and rocket launchers along with their tunnel network.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Syrian conflict > Druze insurgency in Southern Syria
text: Israeli forces strike Syrian military sites, including command and control centres and supply depots, in the country's south, claiming to respond to alleged Syrian government attacks on the local Druze population.

Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz announces the withdrawal of his forces from Iraq, stationed there as part of the CJTF–OIR joint task force against the Islamic State, citing the regional threat from Iran.
United States Air Force general Alexus Grynkewich announces that NATO has withdrawn troops from Iraq and will relocate from the Middle East to Europe amidst the Iran war.

context: Boko Haram insurgency > 2026 Kwara State attacks
text: Government forces arrest three men suspected of participating in the February attacks and mass abductions in two villages in Kaiama, Kwara State, Nigeria. The suspects are cooperating with authorities to locate the kidnapping victims.
At least 64 people are killed, including staff, patients and children, in a strike on a hospital in East Darfur, Sudan.
A drone strike from the Rapid Support Forces targets Al Dabbah, Sudan, including a local power station, causing a power outage in the area and injuring three people.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > International sanctions against Iran
text: U.S. treasury secretary Scott Bessent announces that the U.S. will temporarily lift sanctions on Iranian oil at sea in an effort to ease energy supply pressures. The temporary relief will last for 30 days until April 19.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The U.S. energy department says it has awarded contracts to loan a first batch of 45.2 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Philippine Airlines announces it will halt flights to the Middle East until April 30 due to safety concerns regarding the Iran war.

context: Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk
text: A United States jury in a civil trial finds that X (formerly Twitter) chairperson Elon Musk misled investors in two tweets, but absolves him of some fraud allegations.
Fourteen people are killed and 60 more are injured in a fire at a car parts plant in Daejeon, South Korea.
sources: AFP and Reuters via The Straits Times

context: Foreign relations of Russia since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Foreign relations of the United States > 2026 Cuban crisis, Cuba–Russia relations
text: The United States says it will not allow Cuba to receive any shipments of fuel oil from Russia as two Russian tankers are en route to Havana to deliver around 190,000 barrels of oil amid a critical shortage on the island.

context: Foreign relations of Russia since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Foreign relations of the United States > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia in the 2026 Iran war, Russia–United States relations
text: Politico reports that the United States rejected an offer by Russia to stop providing intelligence to Iran in return for the U.S. ending intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
American actor Kevin Spacey settles out of court with three men at the High Court of Justice in London, England, who accused Spacey of sexually assaulting them between 2000 and 2013.
Two anarchist militants are killed after the accidental explosion of a bomb they were fabricating at a casalis in Rome, Italy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: At least 88 people are injured, including seven seriously, and nine buildings are damaged in an Iranian ballistic missile attack in Arad, Israel. A mass casualty incident is declared.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: At least 78 people are injured, including a 10-year-old, in Dimona, Israel, by Iranian ballistic missile attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: U.S. president Donald Trump issues an ultimatum to Iran to fully open the Strait of Hormuz within the next 48 hours or the U.S. military will "obliterate" their energy infrastructure, including all Iranian power stations.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: A group of 22 countries in a joint statement calls on Iran to cease attacks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Attack on Natanz nuclear facility
text: Israeli and U.S. jets strike the Natanz Nuclear Facility, according to the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Axios reports that the U.S. has reportedly begun initial discussions on the next phase and what peace talks with Iran might look like.

Iran fires two intermediate-range ballistic missiles at the Diego Garcia military base in the Indian Ocean. However, neither missile hits the base, with one of the missiles failing in-flight, and the other having been intercepted by a United States warship using a SM-3 interceptor.
The United States Central Command says that its military has struck over 8,000 targets in Iran, including 130 Iranian Navy vessels, since the start of the war.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claims responsibility for targeting 27 American military bases in Iraq and across the region over the past 24 hours. One police officer is killed in a drone strike on the headquarters of the Iraqi National Intelligence Service in Baghdad.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Zaporizhzhia strikes, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russia launches attacks in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, against energy infrastructure, causing smoke contamination.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Zaporizhzhia strikes, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Two people are killed and six others, including two children, are wounded in a Russian drone attack in Zaporizhzhia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Two people are killed and another is injured in an Ukrainian artillery strike in Belgorod Oblast, Russia.
Cuba reports a nationwide power outage following a total electrical grid collapse, the third major blackout to occur on the island this month.
Seven people are killed when a Qatar Emiri Air Force helicopter crashes after a technical malfunction during a routine mission over Qatar's territorial waters.
Two skiers are killed and 25 others are trapped, including five injured, in an avalanche near Ratschings in South Tyrol, Italy.

Two people are killed in an explosion when a tipper truck and a tank truck collide outside of a gas station on the Lekki-Epe Expressway in Ajah, Lagos State, Nigeria. Several surrounding buildings were destroyed in the initial blast and the ensuing fire.
At least 230 people are rescued, ten of whom are hospitalized for hypothermia, during flooding and storms in Hawaii, United States. Around 5,500 people are evacuated ahead of a second storm.
The 10th CELAC Summit is held in Bogotá, Colombia.
The Iranian parliament says that it is preparing to pass a law that would impose fees on ships for "safe passage" through the Strait of Hormuz.
Large scale protests occurs in Berlin, Germany against the war. Demonstrators call for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve conflicts.
Anti-war protests and diaspora protests against the Iranian regime are held at the Colonial Building in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador.
In South Australia, the Labor Party wins a landslide victory over the Liberal Party. One Nation also secures second place in first-preference votes.

Around 200,000 people gather in Prague, Czech Republic, to express discontent with some steps taken by the current government coalition, including cuts in defence expenditure and proposed changes to the financing of public service media.

context: 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup > 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup final
text: In women's association football, the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup concludes with Japan defeating hosts Australia in the final to win their third title.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Fifteen people are injured in central Israel in Iranian ballistic missile strikes.

Iran threatens to retaliate against the energy and water systems of the Gulf countries if United States president Donald Trump follows through with his 48-hours ultimatum to ​hit Iran's electricity grid.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: One person is killed after a rocket fired from Lebanon struck a vehicle near Israel's northern border, marking the first reported Israeli fatality from cross-border fire since hostilities with Hezbollah resumed earlier in March.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Israeli military destroys the largest bridge crossing the Litani River in southern Lebanon.

context: Terrorism in the United Kingdom > 2026 Hatzola arson attack
text: At least four Hatzalah ambulances are set ablaze and destroyed in an apparent anti-semitic arson attack in Golders Green, London, England. No casualties are reported.
The funeral of Patriarch Ilia II, the former head of the Georgian Orthodox Church, is held at the Holy Trinity Cathedral in Tbilisi, Georgia. He is laid to rest at the Sioni Cathedral.
Cuba restores its power after the power grid collapsed the previous day.

A Bombardier CRJ900LR operating as an Air Canada Express flight from Montreal, Quebec, Canada, collides with a firetruck while landing at LaGuardia Airport in New York City, United States. Both pilots are killed and 41 others are injured.
One person is killed and 10 others are injured, including one critically, when a natural gas explosion collapses two residential buildings in Fatih district, Istanbul, Turkey.
Thieves steal three paintings, one each by artists Henri Matisse, Paul Cézanne, and Pierre-Auguste Renoir, from a private museum in Parma, Italy.
The second round of municipal elections takes place in France.

Italians begin voting on a constitutional amendment that proposes separating the careers of judges and public prosecutors by splitting the High Court of the Judiciary into two bodies, while also establishing a High Disciplinary Court to oversee disciplinary proceedings.

In Germany, the Social Democratic Party declines to second place in Rhineland-Palatinate for the first time since 1991. The Christian Democratic Union party becomes the largest in seats in the Landtag, while Alternative for Germany advances to third place.
Slovenians vote for 90 seats in the National Assembly. A tight race is forecasted between the incumbent prime minister Robert Golob and his predecessor Janez Janša.
Between 200 and 300 National Council of Resistance of Iran-alligned demonstrators of the Iranian opposition gather in Amsterdam, Netherlands, to protest the war and the Iranian government.

Following the March 15 elections to the 15th Supreme People's Assembly of North Korea, Kim Jong Un is reelected chairman of the State Affairs Commission (head of State) and Pak Thae Song is reappointed as premier.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: U.S. president Donald Trump says he is postponing his 48-hour ultimatum for five days before attacking the Iranian power plants as Iran and the U.S. have held "very good and productive conversations" on ending the war. Trump also claims that a "major points of agreement" focused on Iran's renunciation of the nuclear weapon are being talked. Iran denies any dialogue took place.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: Kata'ib Hezbollah says that it will extend its pause on strikes on the United States embassy in Baghdad, Iraq, for five more days.
A person is killed and another is injured in a strike on a transmission site of the Persian Gulf Radio and Television Centre in southern Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: At least one person is killed in an Israeli strike on Hazmieh, Greater Beirut, Lebanon. The Israeli military states that the attack targeted a member of Iran's Quds Force in the area.
At least 15 people are killed and 23 others are injured in strikes on Lagawa District, West Kordofan, Sudan. The Rapid Support Forces attribute the attack to the Sudanese army.
A Sudanese rebel faction led by Yasir Arman calls for the United Nations Security Council to end the use of drones on Sudanese citizens.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Brent crude futures fall 11%, trading just below US$100 a barrel for the first time in days, following the announcement by U.S. president Donald Trump about talks with Iran to end the war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Slovenia becomes first EU country to introduce fuel rationing to cope with extra demand by drivers from neighboring countries.

context: 2026 Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash
text: At least 66 people are killed when a military Lockheed C-130, carrying 125 people, crashes in Puerto Leguízamo, Colombia.
At least one person is killed and several others are injured in an explosion in Kwara State, Nigeria.

In its annual State of the Global Climate report, the World Meteorological Organization states that Earth's energy imbalance and ocean heat content reached record levels in 2025, driven by rising greenhouse gas emissions.
A U.S. civic court finds entertainer Bill Cosby liable for drugging and sexually assaulting a woman in 1972. The woman is awarded $59.25 million.

context: Climate change in Germany, Phase-out of fossil fuel vehicles
text: The Federal Court of Justice of Germany dismisses a lawsuit by Environmental Action Germany to ban BMW and Mercedes Benz from selling new combustion engine vehicles after 2030.

context: Illegal drug trade in Puerto Rico
text: Puerto Rican police seize $12 million worth of cocaine found on a drug smuggling boat off the island's northern coast. Three suspects are arrested.
As a reaction to the 2026 Hatzola arson attack, Belgium deploys (ISTAR) Jagers te Paard Battalion, to guard Jewish "sites" and communities.
In Italy, the constitutional amendment that proposed to select members of the High Council of the Judiciary through sortition is rejected by a 46% to 54% vote.
Following the February 22 elections to the National Assembly of Laos, Thongloun Sisoulith is reelected as President of Laos and Sonexay Siphandone as Prime Minister.

In American football, the Seattle Seahawks signs a four-year deal worth $168 million with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, with at least $120 million guaranteed, making him the highest-paid wide receiver in NFL history.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: The New York Times reports that the United States has sent Iran a 15-point plan to end the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif says that Pakistan is ready and willing to host Iran–U.S. talks to reach a comprehensive deal to end the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Shrapnel from an Iranian ballistic missile wounds three people, including a two-month-old baby, in a Bedouin community in the Negev, Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: Fifteen fighters from Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), including a commander, are killed in an American airstrike on a PMF base in the Al Anbar Governorate.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah rocket fire kills a woman and injures two others in northern Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israeli defense minister Israel Katz states that the military will control a "security zone" up to the Litani River in southern Lebanon until "the threat of Hezbollah" is removed, while also suggesting that Israel will remain in control of the area after the conflict is resolved.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Lebanese government reports that the death toll from Israeli attacks on the country since March 2 has risen to 1,039.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Zaporizhzhia strikes, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
text: Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine kill at least three people, including two in Poltava and one in Zaporizhzhia, and injures several others. The attacks also damage residential buildings and infrastructure in the areas.
A Russian Shahed drone strikes and severely damages the Bernardine Church, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in Lviv, western Ukraine.
The death toll from the March 20 drone strike on the Al Deain Teaching Hospital in East Darfur, Sudan, rises to 70.

context: Sudanese civil war > 2026 Blue Nile campaign
text: A coalition of Rapid Support Forces and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North rebels capture the town of Kurmuk in the Blue Nile region near the Ethopian border.
Suspected Islamic State insurgents kill nine Nigerian troops, one police officer and a civilian during attacks in Kebbi State, Nigeria.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Two concerts by Colombian singer Shakira in Doha, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, scheduled to be held in April are postponed due to safety concerns amidst the Iran war. The Abu Dhabi concert has been rescheduled for November.
The trailer for the upcoming superhero film Spider-Man: Brand New Day released on March 17 reaches 1 billion views on YouTube, becoming the first movie trailer to do so.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Philippine energy crisis
text: Philippine president Bongbong Marcos declares a state of national energy emergency in response to risks to the fuel supply linked to the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: QatarEnergy ‌declares force majeure on some of ⁠its long-term LNG supply contracts for its customers worldwide.

American video game company Epic Games announces that it will lay off more than 1,000 employees along with more than $500 million in savings from cuts to contracting and marketing amid a sharp decline in the number of people playing its flagship video game Fortnite.
Australia and the European Union sign a free trade agreement after eight years of negotiations.
BMW Brilliance recalls nearly 180,000 vehicles in China due to a defect in the air conditioning wiring that may cause a short circuit and increase the risk of fire.
At least 84 people are killed in flash floods across Kenya, including in Kisumu, Uasin Gishu, and Tana River counties.
At least nine people are killed, 266 others are rescued and 45 are reported missing in a shipwreck off Obock, Djibouti.

The Lebanese foreign ministry declares the Iranian ambassador a persona non grata and gives him until March 29 to leave the country, due to Iran's financial and military support of Shia paramilitary group Hezbollah.
The Lebanese foreign ministry says that the decision to expel Mohammad Reza Raouf Sheibani as Iranian ambassador doesn't affect diplomatic relations between the two countries.

The Iranian foreign ministry states that vessels it classifies as non-hostile may pass through the Strait of Hormuz if they comply with its safety and security requirements, while excluding vessels linked to countries it accuses of involvement in the Iran war.
Two people are killed in a school shooting in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán, Mexico. A 15-year-old suspect is arrested.
Danes, Faroe Islanders, and Greenlanders vote to elect 179 seats of the Folketing. Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen seeks a third term in office during the aftermath of the Greenland crisis.
Frederiksen's left-wing bloc wins the most seats but fails to secure a majority.
American technology company OpenAI says it will shut down its Sora app.
The Walt Disney Company and OpenAI's US$1 billion investment deal to allow Disney's intellectual properties to be used with Sora is also cancelled in midst of the shutdown.
NASA states that it plans to pause the Lunar Gateway project and redirect efforts toward developing infrastructure for sustained operations on the Moon's surface, including a future moonbase.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: Jordan's air force intercepts four missiles and one drone launched from Iran.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: A drone strikes a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport, causing a fire at the site.
According to Press TV, Iran has rejected a United States proposal to end the war and sets out five conditions for a ceasefire.
A senior Iranian official says that Iran is still reviewing the proposal despite an initial response that was considered "negative".
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi states that Iran seeks to end the war "on its own terms" but does not plan to enter negotiations with the U.S. and will continue its current policy.
Egyptian foreign minister Badr Abdelatty says that Egypt is ready to host negotiations aimed at ending the Iran war.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: An Iranian cluster bomb wounds nine people, including six children and an elderly woman, in Bnei Brak, Israel.

context: 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: Seven fighters are killed and 13 others are injured in a strike on a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Al Anbar Governorate, Iraq. The attack follows an American strike on the same base yesterday.

Iran says it has received intelligence that the U.S. and an "unnamed regional country" are planning to invade and capture its Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf as thousands of U.S. Marines are due to arrive in the region in the coming days.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: A stray Ukrainian drone strikes a power station in Auvere, Estonia, while another crashes in Latvia during a large-scale drone attack on Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: A Ukrainian drone strike kills two people in Belgorod Oblast, Russia, according to Belgorod governor Vyacheslav Gladkov.

context: Sudanese civil war > El Fasher massacre, Darfur campaign
text: The Sudan Doctors Network says that Rapid Support Forces have killed 16 civilians, including three women, in El Fasher, North Darfur, Sudan.

context: Operation Southern Spear > United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
text: The United States Southern Command (Southcom) says its forces have struck a drug smuggling boat in the Caribbean Sea, killing four occupants. This brings the number of alleged narcoterrorists killed in Operation Southern Spear to 163 since U.S. strikes began.

A ceasefire between Afghanistan and Pakistan collapses with resumed cross-border shelling killing two people in Kunar Province, Afghanistan, while Afghan forces claim to have destroyed three Pakistani military outposts along the border. Both sides accuse each other of breaking the ceasefire first.
Under the in Maastricht, Netherlands, the remains of French musketeer d'Artagnan are believed to be found.
Sarah Mullally is enthroned as the first female primate of the Church of England and Archbishop of Canterbury.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: COSCO Shipping resumes new container shipment bookings from the Far East to several Gulf countries after Iran allowed non-hostile vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz since yesterday.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: India purchases a shipment of liquefied petroleum gas from Iran for the first time since 2019 following a temporary easing of U.S. sanctions, with the cargo set to be distributed among state-run fuel companies, in response to supply disruptions caused by the Strait of Hormuz crisis.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Gold prices in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, rise after a 15-day drop amidst potential diplomacy to end the Iran war.

The International Organization for Migration reports that 922 migrants have died or went missing along the "Eastern Route" from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula in 2025, marking the deadliest year for Red Sea migration and a significant increase from 2024.

At least 26 people are killed, including seven children, 11 others survive and around 13 are reported missing when a passenger bus carrying around 50 people plunges into the Padma River in Goalanda Upazila, Rajbari District, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko visits Pyongyang, North Korea, to meet with its supreme leader Kim Jong Un in a effort to improve relations between the two countries.

context: Hungary–Ukraine relations, Hungary and the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán says Hungary will gradually suspend gas supplies to Ukraine until Russian oil transit through the Druzhba pipeline resumes, citing disruptions to deliveries crossing Ukraine.
British prime minister Keir Starmer authorizes the military to board Russian shadow fleet vessels used by the Russian government to evade international sanctions.

The United Nations General Assembly adopts a resolution proposed by Ghana recognizing the Atlantic slave trade as a crime against humanity and calling for dialogue on reparations, despite opposition and abstentions from Western countries.

A Chinese court sentences former Aviation Industry Corporation chairperson Tan Ruisong to death with a two-year reprieve after convicting him of corruption-related offenses, including bribery, embezzlement, and insider trading, during his tenure as chairperson.

The Indian enforcement directorate says that it has attached in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and has seized villas in the Burj Khalifa as part of the Mahadev online betting app money laundering investigation.
Kuwaiti authorities arrest six individuals suspected of links to Hezbollah over an alleged plot to carry out assassinations targeting state officials.
A jury in California, United States, rules in favor of a woman who sued Google and Meta Platforms for her addictions to websites Instagram and YouTube as a child.

Kosovo's Constitutional Court rules that President Vjosa Osmani's decree to dissolve had no legal effect, giving the Kuvendi 34 more days to elect the next president before automatically moving to new elections within 45 days.

Philippine president Bongbong Marcos signs into law a measure allowing the suspension or reduction of excises on petroleum products when global oil prices reach a specified threshold, subject to time limits and reporting requirements.

After winning her party, the Social Democrats, a reduced majority in the elections, Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen resigns, but is tasked by King Frederik X with leading talks to form a new government.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Pakistan–United States relations
text: U.S. special envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff confirms that the United States has shared a 15-point peace plan to Iran through the Pakistani government.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Pakistan–United States relations
text: Pakistani foreign minister Ishaq Dar confirms that indirect negotiations between Iran and the U.S. are taking place.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: U.S. president Donald Trump extends his deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by ten days, until 6 April, or "face further assassinations of senior officials".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Nine people are injured in Israel after seven salvos of ballistic missiles by Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Two people are killed and three others are injured by falling debris from an intercepted ballistic missile in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Reactions to the 2026 Iran war, Israel–Uganda relations
text: Ugandan military chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba says the country is ready to join the war "on the side of Israel" and says the Ugandan military will enter the war soon if Iranian attacks on Israel do not end soon.
Israel claims to have assassinated Alireza Tangsiri, the commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: One person is killed and 11 are injured by Hezbollah rocket fire in Nahariya, Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Two Israeli soldiers are killed in action in southern Lebanon.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Zimbabwe confirms that 15 of its citizens have been killed after being recruited by Russia to fight in Ukraine, with more than 60 others still on the front line. Cabinet minister Soda Zhemu says that most of them were lured to Russia through social media.
A court in Chelyabinsk Oblast bans the distribution of the documentary film Mr Nobody Against Putin in Russia.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Norway's Storting passes a bill temporarily cutting petrol and diesel taxes in response to surging energy costs amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Mauritius and South Sudan announce measures restricting electricity consumption due to the international energy crisis, with Juba's main electricity distributor saying the capital will start experiencing daily power cuts on a "rotational basis" from today.
At least 14 people are killed and 27 others are injured when a private bus collides head-on with a tipper-truck in Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh, India.
At least 10 people are killed and 35 others are injured when a bus collides with a truck and overturns in Chhindwara district, Madhya Pradesh, India.
Two people are killed, including a child, and at least 90 families are affected in flooding in Kandahar, Afghanistan.

Mexico's navy launches a search and rescue operation in the Caribbean Sea for two sailboats, which departed from Isla Mujeres with nine crew members, carrying humanitarian aid to Cuba after they failed to arrive in Havana as scheduled and lost communication.

A 25-year-old Spanish woman from Barcelona, Catalonia, undergoes euthanasia after her request was approved by authorities and upheld through multiple legal challenges despite opposition from her family.

context: European Union-United States relations > Agreement on Reciprocal, Fair, and Balanced Trade
text: The European Parliament approves legislation to implement the EU-US trade deal adopted in 2025.
Russia says the United Kingdom's decision to board and detain shadow fleet vessels is hostile and vows a "political, legal and asymmetric" response against the UK to protect Russian interests.
British Chief of the General Staff Roland Walker warns that the UK is now on an "inevitable collision course" with Russia and urges the government to prepare.
South Africa says it is no longer invited to the upcoming G7 summit in Haute-Savoie, France, after an initial invitation, with differing statements from its officials on the reasons for the decision.

context: Australia–Iran relations, Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
text: Australia announces a six-month ban on short-term visa applications from Iranian passport holders for tourism and work, citing concerns that some visitors may not depart Australia once their visas expire due to the Iran war. The new policy includes limited exemptions.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: Belarus and North Korea sign a friendship and cooperation treaty after North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un welcomed Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko to Pyongyang.
France and the Philippines sign a visiting forces agreement allowing joint military exercises and cooperation in each other's territory.
Tajik president Emomali Rahmon and Uzbek president Shavkat Mirziyoyev inaugurate the Tajikistan embassy in Tashkent during Rahmon's state visit to Uzbekistan.

context: Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe
text: The Catholic Church in Portugal agrees to compensate 57 victims of sexual abuse with a total of €1.61 million (US$1.86 million) following findings from an independent inquiry into abuse cases over several decades.
Two people are killed, including the perpetrator, in a stabbing attack at a Pokémon Center at Sunshine City in Tokyo, Japan.
Two days after the Danish election, Faroe Islanders vote to elect 33 members of the Løgting.
The People's Party, led by Beinir Johannesen, wins the highest share of votes, receiving nine seats in the Løgting.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup, Iran at the FIFA World Cup
text: The Iranian sports ministry bans the men's national football team from travelling to "hostile countries", placing the team's participation in this year's FIFA World Cup tournament in doubt, which is being held in Canada, Mexico, and the United States. Sports minister Ahmad Donyamali previously stated that Iran will not play in this year's World Cup.

context: 2028 Summer Olympics, Transgender people in sports
text: The International Olympic Committee announces that participation in women's events will be limited to athletes classified as female based on biological criteria, with eligibility determined through a one-time genetic test starting from the 2028 Olympic Games. The policy replaces previous rules that allowed individual sports federations to set their own criteria.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: An Iranian attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia with at least six ballistic missiles and 29 drones injures 15 American soldiers and heavily damages a Boeing E-3 Sentry (AWACS) aircraft.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates report that they have intercepted missile and drone attacks from Iran.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iran's representative in Geneva says that Iran will facilitate and expedite humanitarian aid to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The foreign ministers of the G7 nations reach an agreement to protect passage through the Strait of Hormuz if the war ends.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: One man is killed and several are injured by Iranian ballistic missile attacks on central and southern Israel.
The Israeli Air Force strikes a uranium processing facility in Yazd, Iran. There were no casualties or radiation leaks, according to Iran's Atomic Energy Organization.
Iran has begun recruiting children as young as 12 to man Tehran checkpoints.
The Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North reports that a Sudanese Army airstrike on a funeral gathering in the town of Al Sunut in South Kordofan has killed seven civilians and injured 39 others.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Brent crude oil surpasses US$110 per barrel after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy turned away three container ships and declared the Strait of Hormuz closed.
sources: AFP via South China Morning Post

text: A United States appeals court overturns a $16.1 billion judgment against Argentina related to the 2012 nationalization of oil company YPF, ruling that the shareholders' claims are not valid under Argentine law. The decision reverses a 2023 lower court ruling that had ordered compensation to minority investors.
Landslides triggered by heavy rain kill at least 20 people in Mbeya Region, Tanzania.
Seven people are killed and five others are injured in a landslide on the Zoji La in Ladakh, India.
Three people are killed in a helicopter crash at Kalalau Beach on Kauaʻi, Hawaii, United States.

Two children are killed and at least seven others are injured in a three-vehicle collision involving a dump truck, SUV and school bus on Tennessee State Route 70 in Carroll County, Tennessee, United States.
One person is killed and four others are injured in a mass stabbing at a school in Calama, Antofagasta Region, Chile.
Following his Rastriya Swatantra Party's landslide victory in the general election, Balendra Shah is sworn as Prime Minister of Nepal, succeeding interim prime minister Sushila Karki.

context: Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia
text: Russia designates filmmaker and teacher Pavel Talankin, the co-director and subject of the 2025 documentary film Mr Nobody Against Putin, as a foreign agent after authorities accuse him of spreading disinformation about the government and opposing the war in Ukraine.

Lawmakers from the Jammu & Kashmir National Conference protest outside the legislative assembly of Jammu and Kashmir, India, in solidarity with Iran and against the assassination of former supreme leader Ali Khamenei amidst the Iran war. Additionally, a major confrontation breaks out between INC lawmaker Irfan Hafiz Lone and BJP lawmaker Yudhvir Sethi during the protest.
In Mongolia, the State Great Khural accepts the resignation of Prime Minister Gombojavyn Zandanshatar.
In her last performance before retiring, Japan's Kaori Sakamoto wins the gold medal in the women's singles event of the 2026 Figure Skating Championships.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: Iranian-backed militias launch a drone attack targeting the Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani's private residence in Duhok.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: An airstrike in Kirkuk, Iraq, hits a base of the Popular Mobilization Forces, killing one member and injuring four others.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait International Airport is targeted by multiple drone strikes, causing significant damage to its radar system.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The smelter facility of Aluminium Bahrain in Askar, Southern Governorate, is targeted by Iranian attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Emirates Global Aluminium reports that one of its facilities in Abu Dhabi sustained significant damage and several injuries during missile and drone attacks attributed to Iran.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran University of Science and Technology airstrikes
text: The U.S. and Israel launch airstrikes on the Iran University of Science and Technology (IUST) in the Narmak neighborhood of Tehran, Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
text: The United States Central Command announces the arrival in the Middle East of 3,500 sailors and marines aboard of USS Tripoli.
Iran says it has dismantled a terrorist cell in Gorgan, Golestan and has arrested two suspects.
Five paramedics are killed in an Israeli airstrike in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, Nabatieh Governorate, Lebanon.
Three journalists are killed and several others injured in an Israeli airstrike in Jezzine District, South Governorate, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: The Houthis launch a ballistic missile from their territory in Yemen towards Israel, signifying the group's entrance in the war. The Israeli military says that the missile was successfully intercepted and no injuries were reported. A second attack, also without damage, is reported hours later.
Two people are killed and twelve more are injured in a nighttime Russian drone attack on Odesa. A maternity hospital is also damaged.
A man is detained and another is at large after trying to ignite an improvised explosive device near a Bank of America building in Paris, France. Anti-terrorism prosecutors are investigating.

Twenty-two bodies are recovered from a vessel found adrift off the coast of Crete, Greece, according to the Greek coast guard. Twenty-six people are rescued by Frontex. Several survivors said some people were also thrown overboard into the Mediterranean Sea on the orders of a human trafficker during the journey.
Three people are killed and 23 others are injured, including nine critically, in a fire at a high-rise building in Xiaodian, Taiyuan, Shanxi, China.
Qatar and Ukraine sign a defense pact that includes cooperation on countering missile and drone threats.
Around 18 people are arrested during anti-war protests held across Israel against the Iran war, including 13 in Tel Aviv and 5 in Haifa. Protests are also held in Jerusalem and Beersheba.
Five police officers are killed and three others are injured in an ambush by unidentified gunmen in Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao del Sur, Philippines.
Four people are killed and two others are injured during clashes between insurgent groups in Kamjong district, Manipur, India.
Seven people are injured in a vehicle ramming attack in Derby, Derbyshire, England. An Indian national in his 30s is arrested with counter-terrorism police investigating.
Nepal's former prime minister K. P. Sharma Oli is arrested over his alleged involvement in the crackdown on the 2025 protests.

context: Protests against Donald Trump > 2026 No Kings protests
text: The third No Kings protests are held across the United States against the policies of president Donald Trump's administration including the Iran war, ICE operations, and the killings of Renée Good and Alex Pretti.
Exiled Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi urges the United States not to strike a deal or negotiate for peace with the Iranian regime and also calls for a resurgence in protests.

The South West House of Representatives re-elects incumbent president Abdiaziz Laftagareen for the second time amid tensions with the Somali federal government that resulted in the military being deployed to the Lower Shabelle, Bay and Bakool regions of Somalia.
In Thoroughbred racing, American racehorse Magnitude wins the 30th Dubai World Cup in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, amidst the Iran war.

In chess, the Candidates Tournament 2026 starts in Cyprus. Between 28 March and 16 April, eight players compete in a double round-robin tournament. The winner will face Gukesh Dommaraju for the World Championship.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: Bahrain imposes a nighttime maritime curfew from 6:00pm to 4:00am to restrict sea traffic and strengthen coastal security following reported attacks attributed to Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Ten Kuwaiti soldiers are injured in a new wave of missile and drone attacks on Kuwait.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: The foreign ministers of Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, meet in Islamabad to express their "full support" for potential Iran–United States talks hosted by Pakistan.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: United States president Donald Trump tells Financial Times that the U.S. could seize Kharg Island and "take the oil" in Iran, although "a deal could be made fairly quickly".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: An Iranian missile hits the Makhteshim chemical plant in southern Israel. A warning for the leakage of hazardous materials is issued for the immediate vicinity of the site.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Lamerd sports hall attack
text: A visual evidence released by The New York Times shows that a sports hall in Lamerd in the Fars province of Iran was hit by a untested short-range Precision Strike Missile during the first day of the war on February 28, 2026.
An Indonesian peacekeeper of the UNIFIL mission is killed and a second one is critically injured when a projectile explodes at their position near Aadshit al-Qusayr, Nabatieh Governorate.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: A person is killed by a Ukrainian drone attack in Taganrog, Rostov Oblast, Russia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Several unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are detected across southeastern Finland. One of the UAVs is identified as Ukrainian after it crashes near Kouvola.
Three people are killed and thirteen others are injured in a Russian glide bomb attack on Kramatorsk, Ukraine.
Ten Palestinians are killed, including a 15-year-old boy, and 18 others are injured in artillery fire and airstrikes by the Israel Defense Forces in Gaza City, Palestine.
At least 14 people are killed and 23 others are injured in a drone strike on Dilling, South Kordofan, Sudan.
One person is killed and at least 15 others, including children, are injured in a Pakistani artillery strike in Asadabad, Kunar Province, Afghanistan.
Twelve people are killed by unknown gunmen at a bar in Angwan Rukuba, Plateau State, Nigeria. A mob kills ten additional people in retaliation to the attack.

At least 16 people are killed and 10 others are injured by the Gran Grif gang in Petite-Rivière-de-l'Artibonite, Haiti, during a gun fight with a vigilante group. Human rights activists allege that more than 30 people were killed and dozens were missing.
South Sudanese vice president Riek Machar reports that at least 73 miners were killed and 25 others were seriously injured by unknown gunmen over the weekend after a mining dispute near Juba.

For the first time ever, Israel Police block the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, Pierbattista Pizzaballa, from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre during Palm Sunday, citing heightened risk in the Old City during the Iran war.
At least 45 people are killed and 74 others are injured after five days of severe weather across parts of Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Seven people are killed and two others are injured after a building partially collapses in Hailin, Heilongjiang, China.
