Three people are killed and 20 others are injured when a church collapses in Accra, Ghana.
A nightclub burns down in Kehl, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. All 750 people inside were evacuated, three of whom are treated for shock.

Iran's ambassador to Lebanon, Mojtaba Amani, remains in the country despite being declared persona non grata and ordered to leave. The expulsion order prompts opposition from outlawed Iran-armed group Hezbollah and a cabinet boycott by its ministers and allies.
An unknown number of casualties are reported when a loader is intentionally driven into a crowded market in Fangshan, Beijing, China. A man in his 50s is arrested.
Avi Lewis is elected leader of Canada's New Democratic Party.
In auto racing, Mercedes-Benz's Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest driver to lead the World Championship at 19 years and 216 days old after winning the Japanese Grand Prix.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Israeli strikes on Iran
text: Israeli leaders announce the "completion phase" of war and order the military to strike "economic" targets in Iran to damage the Iranian economy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei says that Iran has not started negotiations with the United States but also says that the U.S. have submitted a negotiation request.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: A missile barrage from Iran and Lebanon causes a fire at the BAZAN oil refinery in Haifa.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: An Iranian attack on a power and water desalination plant in Kuwait kills an Indian worker and damages a building at the site.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Spain in the 2026 Iran war, Spain–United States relations
text: Spain closes its airspace to U.S. aircraft involved in military action against Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Syria in the 2026 Iran war
text: The Syrian Army says that drone attacks have targeted several of their bases near the Iraqi border. However, the Syrian Army also says that several of the drones were shot down and did not say where the drones came from.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza war peace plan
text: Kosovo approves the deployment of troops to Gaza as part of an international peacekeeping force.
Two Indonesian peacekeepers of the UNIFIL mission are killed in Southern Lebanon when a projectile hits their vehicle.

context: Somali Civil War > Constitutional crisis in Somalia
text: At least 10 people are killed, 25 others are injured and more than 45,000 displaced after Somalia's national army ​took control of Baidoa, the capital city of the South West state, two weeks after the state president Abdiaziz Laftagareen said that his administration was severing ties with the federal government and opposed constitutional amendments backed by the Somali federal government.

India says it has ended the Naxalite insurgency after home minister Amit Shah reported that most of the remaining Naxal fighters had been killed, arrested, or had surrendered following intensified security operations.
A human rights organization in Haiti claims that the death toll from the previous day's massacre in the Artibonite department was at least 70 people, higher than official reports.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Brent Crude oil passes US$116 per barrel, the highest it has been since the start of the war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: United States crude oil settles above US$100 per barrel for the first time in four years.

The United Kingdom's Financial Conduct Authority rules that around 12 million people are entitled to financial compensation after being mis-sold motor finance agreements between 2014 and 2024. The compensation scheme will see each motorist awarded around £829, costing car finance lenders a total of £9.1bn.
Five people are killed and three others are injured after a car crashes between Hopefield and Langebaanweg in Western Cape, South Africa.
Four people are killed and nine others are injured in an explosion in an under-construction tunnel in Chongqing, China.
At least 28 people are killed in Afghanistan and 17 in Pakistan after heavy rainfall causes severe flooding.
A study published in the Carcinogenesis journal shows that nicotine vaping can cause lung or oral cancer.
The Russian tanker Anatoly Kolodkin, carrying 100,000 tonnes of crude oil, arrives in Matanzas, Cuba, despite the ongoing U.S. blockade of the island.
The United States resumes operations at its embassy in Caracas after a seven-year closure, aiming to restore direct diplomatic engagement with Venezuela under Delcy Rodríguez's de facto presidency.
The Iranian parliament security approves a series of measures to impose tolls on vessels that pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Knesset passes a bill allowing for mandatory executions of Palestinians convicted of terrorist attacks that kill Israelis.

Victoria Police fatally shoot Dezi Freeman, a self-proclaimed sovereign citizen and fugitive following a seven month manhunt after he killed two police officers and seriously injured another in a shooting in Porepunkah, Victoria, Australia. It was the largest police operation in Australian history.
One person is killed and eight others are injured in a school shooting in San Cristóbal, Santa Fe, Argentina. A 15-year-old suspect is taken into custody.
The Bahraini interior ministry says that three men have been arrested for allegedly trying to form a terrorist cell linked to Hezbollah.
Myanmar military ruler Min Aung Hlaing steps down as army chief to stand as a candidate for president in the upcoming presidential election, the first to be held since the 2021 coup.

Mongolia's parliament appoints Nyam-Osoryn Uchral as prime minister, the third to hold the post within a year, following the resignation of his predecessor, Gombojavyn Zandanshatar, after nine months in office. His appointment follows his removal as parliamentary speaker amid opposition protests and a legislative boycott.
NASA begins the countdown for the launch of Artemis II, set to be the first crewed mission to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972, with liftoff scheduled for 1 April.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup, Iran at the FIFA World Cup
text: FIFA president Gianni Infantino insists that the Iranian soccer team will play in the upcoming World Cup despite the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran has the "necessary will" to end the war, provided that the "guarantees required to prevent repetition of the aggression" are met.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi confirms that direct contacts, although "not negotiations", with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff are under way.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: U.S. president Donald Trump says that U.S. forces plan to end operations in Iran within about two to three weeks while continuing military action, stating that the withdrawal is not contingent on reaching an agreement with Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: U.S. defense secretary Pete Hegseth says that the talks between Iran and the United States "are very real" but also states that the U.S. will "negotiate with bombs" until a ceasefire is reached.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Kuwait Petroleum Corporation claims that oil tanker Al Salmi has been hit by an Iranian drone at a port in Dubai, causing a fire onboard and damage to the vessel. Dubai authorities say that the fire has been contained hours after the incident.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > France–Israel relations
text: The Israeli defense ministry halts sales of defense products to France following president Emmanuel Macron's decision not to allow U.S. aircraft to pass through French airspace en route to Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Italy–United States relations
text: Italy denies the United States Air Force the use of the Sigonella base in Sicily for operations related to the Iran war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Poland–United States relations
text: Poland refuses a request by the United States to relocate its Patriot air defense systems to the Middle East for the Iran war.

China and Pakistan release a five-point peace plan for the Iran war following a meeting between the two countries' foreign ministers, Wang Yi and Ishaq Dar, respectively. The plan includes a ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Israeli defense minister Israel Katz announces that Israel will destroy "all houses" near the Blue Line as part of its creation of a new buffer zone.
Four Israeli soldiers are killed in action while fighting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
American freelance journalist Shelly Kittleson is kidnapped by armed men in Baghdad, Iraq.
Seven dismembered bodies are found on a road in Cualac, Guerrero, Mexico.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: The American Automobile Association reports that the United States national average gas price has reached $4.02 a gallon, the highest since 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surges over 1,000 points and the Nasdaq increases to 3.4% after Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran has signaled it is willing to end the conflict if security guarantees and assurances are met.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Stocks in the U.S. also rise following reports that president Donald Trump has told aides that he is willing to end the war without securing the Strait of Hormuz.
Thirty military personnel are killed when a Russian Air Force Antonov An-26 crashes in Crimea.
Dozens of people are killed and many others are injured after multiple explosions occur at a military ammunition depot in Bujumbura, Burundi, causing extensive damage to nearby residential areas.
Eleven people are killed in a shophouse complex fire in Wamena, Highland Papua, Indonesia.

context: LGBTQ rights in the United States, Legality of conversion therapy > Chiles v. Salazar
text: The U.S. Supreme Court overturns Colorado's ban on conversion therapy in an 8–1 decision, ruling that it infringed on the First Amendment, thereby invalidating similar bans in 22 other states.

Senegalese president Bassirou Diomaye Faye approves a law increasing penalties for same-sex sexual acts to up to 10 years in prison and criminalizing the promotion or financing of such acts. The measure amends existing provisions in the penal code that already penalize these acts.

A court in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, nullifies a fine of more than R$16 million (US$3 million) imposed on football player Neymar in 2023 over alleged environmental violations linked to construction at his Mangaratiba property, citing procedural flaws in the investigation.

Pakistani cricketer Naseem Shah receives a record fine of Rs. 20 million (US$71,500) for a social media post criticizing Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz, while other disciplinary cases arise in the Pakistan Super League, including a fine for Shaheen Shah Afridi and a ball-tampering charge against Fakhar Zaman.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: A fuel storage at Kuwait International Airport in Farwaniya Governorate, Kuwait, is hit by Iranian drones, causing a major fire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Iran fires three ballistic missiles at Qatar, with two intercepted and a third one hitting a oil tanker registered by QatarEnergy.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: A Bangladeshi national is killed by shrapnel during a drone interception in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian releases a letter to the American people and suggests that diplomatic engagement is possible.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: U.S. president Donald Trump, in his first primetime address since the start of the war, says that U.S. forces will soon "finish the job" and that objectives are "nearing completion". However, he also says that the U.S. would hit them "extremely hard" within the next 2–3 weeks if a deal is not reached to end the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Ten civilians are injured, including a girl from Bnei Brak, Israel, who is in critical condition, after a missile barrage from Iran.

A U.S. strike on Tehran reportedly damages the former U.S. embassy, which was converted into a museum following its takeover during the Iranian Revolution. The St. Nicholas Orthodox Church is also damaged.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: As confirmed by the U.S. defense department and international media, two more MQ-9 Reaper unmanned reconnaissance drones have been shot down over Iranian territory.
The Israeli military says that the air force has completed strikes against vital targets in Iran, including military and nuclear targets.
Israeli airstrikes kill seven people, including the Hezbollah commander for Iraq, Youssef Hashem, and injure dozens more in Beirut and nearby Khalde, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: The Israeli military reports a missile launched by Houthi militias is intercepted.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The Russian defence ministry says its forces have taken full control of Luhansk Oblast in eastern Ukraine. The Ukrainian military denies this claim, saying its 3rd Assault Brigade continues to hold a small number of positions near the front line.
A Russian drone strike kills four civilians in Zolotonosha, Cherkasy Oblast, Ukraine.
Talks between Afghanistan and Pakistan are reportedly held in China in an effort to end the current conflict.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Malaysia announces a remote work policy for government officials and employees of state-owned enterprises starting April 15 to reduce fuel consumption amid rising energy costs linked to the Iran war. The government also reduces subsidized fuel quotas while maintaining market-based pricing for unsubsidized fuel.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The Taiwanese transport ministry announces that airlines will increase fuel surcharges on international flights by 157 percent starting April 7, following a rise in global oil prices linked to the Iran war.
A boat carrying Afghan migrants capsizes off the coast of Bodrum, Turkey, leaving at least 19 people dead, according to the Turkish Coast Guard. Twenty other migrants are rescued.
Five people are killed and 21 others are injured, including one critically, when a truck crashes into and sets on fire several vehicles at a tollbooth in Cundinamarca Department, Colombia.
Four people are killed in a roof collapse at a coal mine in Xing County, Shanxi, China.
The United States lifts sanctions on Venezuelan acting president Delcy Rodríguez.

Cambodia extradites the former chairperson of Huione Group to China, where law enforcement authorities accuse him of involvement in a large-scale online fraud and money laundering network linked to Huione. Investigators identify him as an associate of suspected crime leader Chen Zhi, who was previously extradited in connection with the case.
Alice Mina and Vladimiro Selva are sworn in as the new Captains Regent of San Marino.

NASA launches Artemis II from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, United States, carrying astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen, for a flyby of the Moon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain, 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Minor damage is reported near the Kizad area in Abu Dhabi after the United Arab Emirates air defenses successfully intercepts an Iranian missile.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Iran conducts strikes on Amazon Web Services servers in Bahrain and on an Oracle data center in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. However, the Dubai government dismisses any reports the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has targeted the Oracle data center and says it's false.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that Iran and Oman are drafting a protocol to oversee maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The United Kingdom hosts a summit with 40 countries to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Austria–United States relations
text: Austria denies United States aircraft use of its ‌airspace for military operations against Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Karaj B1 bridge attack
text: The B1 highway bridge linking Tehran and Karaj, which was inaugurated earlier this year, is hit by Israeli–U.S. airstrikes. Eight people are killed and 95 others are injured.
sources: Reuters via The Times of Israel

text: The Pasteur Institute of Iran sustains heavy damage in Israeli–U.S. strikes.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza peace plan
text: Delegation from Hamas holds talks in Cairo, Egypt to follow up on the implementation of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Kenya reports at least 16 Kenyans are missing after being recruited to fight for the Russian military in Ukraine, while 38 others are currently in Russian hospitals in unknown conditions as they are under restricted access. Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi says the men were offered a US$2,700 monthly salary by Russian agents for joining the war.
A Russian Antonov An-72 is destroyed in a Ukrainian airstrike on Kirovske Air Base in Kirovske Raion, Russian-occupied Crimea.

context: Sudanese civil war > Aftermath of the Battle of Khartoum
text: The United Nations reopens their headquarters in Khartoum for the first time since 2023 after it was relocated to Port Sudan following the outbreak of the war in mid-April 2023.
Two Rapid Support Forces drones hit the Al-Jabalain hospital in White Nile State killing 10, including seven medical staff.

context: Religion in the United Arab Emirates
text: Dubai moves worship services at churches, temples, and gurdwaras online or suspend in-person services due to the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Air China, China Southern Airlines, and its subsidiary XiamenAir increase fuel surcharges by ¥60–120 (US$8.70–17.50) on domestic flights in response to rising oil prices linked to the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Pakistan increases fuel prices, raising petrol by 42.7 percent and diesel by 54.9 percent in response to higher global energy costs linked to the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: United States crude oil surges to over $113 per barrel.
The Somali Ministry of Ports and Maritime Transport announces that Somalia has registered the Guney (IMO 8230417) ship under the Somali flag, its first national-flagged vessel since 1991.
One person is killed and another is injured when a building in Manado, North Sulawesi, Indonesia, collapses following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia.
One person is killed and hundreds are trapped indoors by flooding in Nea Makri, Attica, Greece, amid gale-force winds along the Mediterranean coast.
Four people are killed when a Cessna 172 crashes into a field in Huejotzingo, Puebla, Mexico.
Both pilots are killed when a Beechcraft Model 18 operating on a cargo flight crashes in Coron, Palawan, Philippines.

Argentina orders Iranian chargé d'affaires Mohsen Soltani Tehrani to leave the country within 48 hours after Iranian officials issued statements that Argentina described as false and offensive. The move follows Argentina's designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization.

context: Moldova–Russia relations, Accession of Moldova to the European Union
text: Moldova's parliament approves the country's withdrawal from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), as the government says CIS's core values and principles are no longer respected, such as territorial integrity and the inviolability of borders, and refers to Russia's actions in the region, including the war against Ukraine and the illegal military presence on Moldovan territory.
Dutch authorities recover the Helmet of Coțofenești and other treasures from the Dacian royal collection, which were stolen from the Drents Museum in Assen, Drenthe, in 2025.
Four children are killed in a mass stabbing at a school in Kampala, Uganda. The suspected perpetrator, an adult man, is arrested.

context: Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia, Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: The Basmanny District Court in Moscow, Russia, sentences German sculptor Jacques Tilly in absentia to eight years and six months in prison for spreading false information about the military and offending religious believers through his public works and statements concerning Russia's actions in Ukraine.

Twelve people are injured when a masked man detonates two pyrotechnic explosives on a train in Siegburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. A 20-year-old man is arrested by Federal Police and charged with attempted murder, aggravated assault, and violation of explosives law. A right-wing political motive is suspected.
Cuba announces the pardon of 2,010 prisoners, with releases scheduled over the coming months based on criteria such as conduct and health.
U.S. president Donald Trump dismisses Pam Bondi as Attorney General, with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche replacing her on an acting basis.
General Randy George, Chief of Staff of the United States Army, steps down upon U.S. defense secretary Pete Hegseth's request.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates intercepts 18 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles, and 47 drones from Iran. Falling debris from the interception kills one person and injures others at the Habshan oil facility in the Abu Dhabi emirate.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Maltese-flagged CMA CGM Kribi, a container ship registered by French shipping company CMA CGM crosses the Strait of Hormuz after departing Dubai, making it the first ship from Western Europe to cross the strait since the war started.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Japanese shipping company Mitsui O.S.K. Lines says that a liquefied natural gas oil tanker registered in Japan crosses the Strait of Hormuz for the first since the beginning of the Iran war. A third ship also crosses the strait.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war
text: Iranian forces shoot down a U.S. F-15E fighter jet in Iranian airspace. U.S. officials say a search is underway for the two crew members, one of whom, the pilot, is rescued. Iran's state media says a reward will be given to any citizen who helps capture an American pilot. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/apr/03/us-fighter-jet-confirmed-shot-down-over-iran (The Guardian]

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war
text: Two U.S. military helicopters are hit with small arms fire while conducting a search and rescue operation for the downed F-15E pilots.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the 2026 Iran war
text: A U.S. A-10 Warthog crashes near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by Iranian anti-aircraft fire. The pilot ejects and is rescued.
At least three people are killed in a strike on a residential area in Tehran, Iran.
The Kyrgyz emergency ministry says that Kyrgyzstan has dispatched over 100 tons of humanitarian aid to Iran. The shipment is ordered by Kyrgyz president Sadyr Japarov.
The U.S. embassy in Beirut warns Americans to leave Lebanon due to the situation in the country.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning says that peace talks between Afghanistan and Pakistan are advancing in an effort to end the war.
Six people are killed and five others, including a child, are injured in Russian drone and missile strikes across Ukraine.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: Pakistan introduces free public transport in Islamabad and Punjab for one month and provides targeted subsidies in other regions to offset the impact of recent fuel price increases.
A 5.8 earthquake hits parts of Afghanistan and Pakistan, killing 12 people and injuring six others in Kabul and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Four people are killed when a small plane crashes into a restaurant in Capão da Canoa, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
One person is killed and at least 47 others are injured when a wall collapses at the Alejandro Villanueva Stadium in Lima, Peru.
At least 35 people are injured after a passenger train derails in Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia.

context: Italy–Saudi Arabia relations, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni visits Saudi Arabia to discuss mitigating the impact of the Strait of Hormuz crisis with Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman. Meloni becomes the first leader from a European Union, G20, and NATO member state to visit the Middle East since the start of the Iran war.
The Swedish Coast Guard boards and seizes an EU-sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker in the Baltic Sea after the vessel caused a 12-kilometer (8-mile) oil spill off the coast of Gotland.

The Central Commission for Discipline Inspection of China announces that former Party Secretary of Xinjiang Ma Xingrui is under investigation over suspected "serious violation of law and discipline", becoming the third member of the Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party to be investigated by the commission.
Cuba begins releasing political prisoners after announcing it will pardon 2,010 inmates amid U.S. pressure on the Cuban government.

Myanmar's military ruler, General Min Aung Hlaing, is elected president by the Electoral College. Min secures 429 votes, against 126 for Nyo Saw and 29 for Nan Ni Ni Aye, who become first and second vice presidents, respectively.

context: Payment and Control Agency for Guidance and Guarantee Community Aid scandal
text: Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis reshuffles his cabinet after several officials were implicated in a European Public Prosecutor's Office investigation into alleged irregularities in the allocation of European Union farm subsidies.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The Jordanian military says that 261 missiles and drones from Iran aimed at Jordan have been intercepted over the past five weeks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait intercepts eight missiles and 19 drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Evacuations during the 2026 Iran war > Russia in the 2026 Iran war
text: Russia evacuates 198 more staff from Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant as an airstrike kills an Iranian security guard at the plant.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war, Iran–Iraq relations
text: Military command spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari says that Iran will allow vessels and ships from Iraq to use the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iran's military command rejects an ultimatum from U.S. president Donald Trump to re-open the Strait of Hormuz in 48 hours or face more attacks on its critical infrastructure.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi rejects reports that Iran has declined to meet American officials in Islamabad, Pakistan, amidst stalled ceasefire efforts. He also reaffirms that Iran remains open for peace talks to end the war.
Five people are killed and 170 others are injured in an Israeli missile strike on a petrochemical complex in Bandar-e Mahshahr, Khuzestan province, Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Israeli military says on Telegram that it has started striking Hezbollah infrastructure in Beirut after destroying a bridge in eastern Lebanon to prevent them from crossing.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israeli airstrikes in Habboûch and al-Hawsh, southern Lebanon, kill at least two girls and injure 40 people, while an Israeli soldier is also killed in action.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Eleven people are injured in an airstrike carried out by Israel in Tyre, southern Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Blockade of the Gaza Strip
text: Around 20 boats from Marseille, Provence, France, set sail with international flotilla in an effort to break the current blockade on the Gaza Strip.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine is willing to hold the next round of peace talks with Russia and the United States.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Five people are killed and 19 others are injured in a Russian drone strike on a market in Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine.
The Somali intelligence and security agency says that security forces have killed nine al-Shabaab militants in Lower Shabelle, Somalia.
Five people are killed in a fire at a gas lighter factory in Keraniganj Upazila, Dhaka District, Bangladesh.
At least four people are killed and 18 others are injured, including two children, when a passenger vehicle plunges off a road near Sojha in Himachal Pradesh, India.
Three people are killed and at least 10 others are reportedly trapped after a four-story hotel collapses in Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh, India.
The Afghanistan National Disaster Management Authority reports 77 deaths and 137 injuries in flooding, landslides and lightning caused by severe weather in the country over the past 10 days.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in Israel
text: The Israeli High Court of Justice orders police to allow anti-war protests in Israel.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in Israel
text: Police clash with anti-war protesters at the Habima Square in Tel Aviv, defying the recent high court order. This comes after protesters defy a previous order by the Israeli military to limit gatherings to 150 people.

Two demonstrators are arrested outside the RAF Lakenheath station near the village of Lakenheath in Suffolk, England, United Kingdom. The protest comes after media reports that a U.S. F-15E fighter jet that was shot down took off from the base.
Protests break out across provinces in Iraq to demand an end to the aggression and end to the war following calls for protests by Shiite National Movement leader Sayyid Muqtada al-Sadr.
A joint operation between the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh police units arrests ISIS recruiter Rizwan in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, India.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announces that the State Department has revoked the green cards of the niece and grandniece of deceased IRGC Quds Force general Qasem Soleimani following their arrest by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
A vehicle crashes into a Lao New Year parade in New Iberia, Louisiana, United States, injuring at least 15 people.

context: 2026 Maldivian constitutional referendum, 2026 Maldivian local elections
text: Maldivians vote to elect members of local councils and decide on a constitutional referendum that proposes holding presidential and parliamentary elections concurrently on the same day in 2028.

context: 2026 Maldivian constitutional referendum, 2026 Maldivian local elections
text: Early provisional results indicate that voters rejected the proposed constitutional amendment, while also allowing the Maldivian Democratic Party to retain five mayoral seats.

Cameroon's parliament approves a constitutional amendment reinstating the position of vice president, who will assume the presidency if the office becomes vacant and will be appointed by the president for the remainder of the term.
The term of Vjosa Osmani as President of Kosovo ends and is succeeded by the speaker of the Assembly, Albulena Haxhiu, who becomes acting president until a new president is elected.

Planet Labs suspends public release of satellite imagery of Iran and surrounding conflict areas at the request of the U.S. government, shifting to restricted, case-by-case distribution for selected uses. The policy applies retroactively to images from March 9 and follows earlier delays imposed to limit potential military use of commercial imagery.
In ice hockey, the NHL's Buffalo Sabres clinch the Stanley Cup playoffs for the first time since the 2010–11 season, ending their 14-year Stanley Cup playoff drought.
sources: The Athletic via The New York Times

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The state-owned energy company Bapco Energies reports an Iranian drone attack on one of its storage facilities. An oil tank caught fire as a result.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: Jordan's military intercepts two missiles and two drones from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: An Iranian drone strikes the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation building, which also houses the Ministry of Oil. The impact triggers a fire, prompting the evacuation of the entire complex.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: An office complex housing government ministries in Kuwait City is struck by a drone, causing significant property damage.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Two power plants and their associated desalination facilities are severely damaged. The electricity and water ministry confirms the failure of two power generation units.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran
text: Iranian media claims an American Lockheed C-130 Hercules was shot down in Isfahan, Iran, while on a search and rescue operation for a missing U.S. airman.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran
text: After heavy fighting, the weapon systems officer from the downed F-15E is successfully recovered by U.S. special forces.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran
text: Two American C-130 transport aircraft and 4 MH-6 Little Bird helicopters are destroyed at a temporary U.S. base in Iran by withdrawing U.S. troops to prevent them from being captured by Iranian forces.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Axios reports that Iran, the U.S., and a group of regional mediators are discussing terms ‌for a potential 45-day ceasefire that could lead to a permanent end to the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The United Arab Emirates declares its willingness to join a U.S.-led international coalition to secure and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blocked by Iran.
An Iranian missile strike hits a residential building in Haifa, Israel, killing two people, injuring nine others, including one seriously, and leaving two others missing.
The Israeli military says that it has killed Mohammad Reza Ashrafi Kahi, the head of trade at the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps's oil headquarters, in an airstrike in Tehran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Lebanese conflict > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah claims its fighters struck an Israeli military vessel off the coast of Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Lebanese conflict > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Five people are killed in an Israeli airstrike on Kfar Hatta, South Governorate, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Lebanese conflict > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: A Lebanese soldier is killed by an Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Lebanese conflict > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: At least four people are killed and forty are injured by Israeli airstrikes on Beirut, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Lebanese conflict > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israeli military chief of staff Eyal Zamir says that all parts of Lebanon south of the Litani River have been turned into an "operational zone" against Hezbollah.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war > Gaza genocide
text: On Palestinian Child's Day, human rights organizations report that approximately 350 Palestinian children are currently being held in Israeli prisons, citing a systematic deterioration in detention conditions and allegations of torture.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war > Gaza genocide
text: A Palestinian is killed and others are injured, including some seriously, in a drone strike on civilians in Gaza City, Palestine.
The Taliban claims six Pakistani soldiers are killed and several others are injured in clashes along the Durand Line in Tani District, Khost Province, Afghanistan.

Nigerian security forces rescue 31 worshippers abducted during Easter services in a village in the Kaduna State, after an attack on churches by armed assailants. The incident results in at least five deaths.
Two people are killed when a cargo ship sinks after being struck by a Ukrainian drone strike in the Sea of Azov near Kerch, Crimea.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: Nepal announces that government and educational institutions will have two days off work during the week instead of one, as part of an effort to save fuel.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: OPEC+ agrees to increase oil production quotas by 206,000 barrels per day for a second consecutive month amid concerns over damage to energy infrastructure and disruptions to maritime routes affecting global supply stability.
Two merchant vessels near the Italian coast rescued 32 migrants from a boat attempting to cross from Libya to Europe over the Easter weekend, and 71 others are still missing at sea.

Fifteen people are killed and fourteen others are injured over the past 24 hours in Angola, due to heavy rains in several regions of the country. Five people have also been reported missing, including three in Luanda and two in Benguela.
Eight people are killed after a bus and a truck collide head-on near Quimistán, Honduras.
Seven people are killed and one injured after a car and a truck collide head-on in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape, South Africa.
Three people, including two children, are killed and another is seriously injured after high winds cause a tree to fall onto an Easter egg hunt in Mittelangeln, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany.
Bangladesh launches an emergency MMR vaccine campaign after new health data shows that at least 130 children have been reported dead from measles in the last six weeks.
Iran executes two men convicted of attempting to storm a military facility and access the armory during the protests in January.

context: 2026 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament > 2026 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game
text: In college basketball, the UCLA Bruins defeat the South Carolina Gamecocks 79-51 to win the 2026 NCAA Division I women's basketball championship game.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Iraq
text: Iraqi security sources say that two people are killed after an Iranian drone strike in the Darashakran District of the Erbil Governorate.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: Debris from a missile defense system falls on a Raneen Systems building in Mussafah, injuring a Ghanaian citizen.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: The United Arab Emirates is targeted by 12 ballistic missiles, two cruise missiles, and 19 drones from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Iran claims to be targeting U.S. satellite equipment and ammunition on Bubiyan Island using drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: The Kuwaiti military responds to 14 ballistic missiles, two cruise missiles, and 46 drones from Iran in Kuwaiti airspace.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Fifteen Americans are wounded in an overnight Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military announces that it has intercepted 188 missiles and 468 drones from Iran since the start of the war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
text: Pakistan proposes a ceasefire plan received by Iran and the United States, reportedly dubbed the Islamabad Accord, which calls for an immediate halt to hostilities, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and a 15–20 day period of negotiations between Iran and the U.S. This comes following reported talks between Pakistani army staff chief Asim Munir, U.S. vice president JD Vance, U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi. The Pakistani foreign ministry says that talks between Iran and the U.S. are ongoing.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
text: U.S. president Donald Trump says that Vance, Witkoff, and senior presidential adviser Jared Kushner are talking to intermediaries in Pakistan on ending the war. He also calls the Iran proposal a "significant step" ahead of his Tuesday deadline.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
text: Iran delivers its response to the United States via Pakistan, rejecting a temporary ceasefire and listing its own 10-point demands, which include a solution to all regional conflicts, lifting of sanctions, reconstruction, and a protocol to re-open the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: An Iranian missile strike hits 15 areas in Israel. A woman is seriously injured in Petah Tikva, while two other people are injured in Tel Aviv. In Haifa, four people are also slightly injured by a cluster bomb.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Israel
text: Four bodies are found during a search and rescue operation in a house in Haifa that had been destroyed by an Iranian missile.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The first vessel from Malaysia passes through the Strait of Hormuz after talks between Malaysian prime minister Anwar Ibrahim and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian aimed at securing clearance for 7 stranded Malaysian vessels in the waterway.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Fars News Agency reports that Iran has allowed 15 vessels to cross the Strait of Hormuz.
The mosque and filling station at the Sharif University of Technology in Tehran, Iran, are damaged in an airstrike, causing a gas outage in the neighbourhood.
At least 13 people are killed in an airstrike on a residential building near Eslamshahr, Tehran Province, Iran.
Explosions, likely from airstrikes, are reported in the South Pars gas field, in southern Iran.
Four people are killed, seven are injured and others are reported missing in a Israeli–U.S. airstrike on a residential area in eastern Tehran, Iran.
Israel claims to have killed Asghar Bakri, the commander of Unit 840 of the Quds Force.
Israeli defense minister Israel Katz states that the military is attacking Iran's most important petrochemical plant in Assaluyeh, causing severe damage.
Strikes hit a petrochemical complex in Marvdasht, Fars province, Iran, causing a fire.
Majid Khademi, head of the IRGC Intelligence Protection, is killed in an American–Israeli airstrike.
Nighttime attacks on Bandar Lengeh and Kong, Iran, kill six people and injured 17 others.
Reports indicate that explosions and attacks occurred early this morning at a military compound in northern Iran and in Khorramshahr.
The Israeli military claims to have attacked Mehrabad International Airport as well as two smaller airfields, destroying dozens of Iranian aircraft and helicopters in the process.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis > 2026 Houthi strikes on Israel
text: The Houthis launch several long-range drones from Yemen at Eilat, Israel, in a coordinated attack with Hezbollah and Iran.

Christian anti-Hezbollah Lebanese Forces Party official Pierre Mouawad, his wife, and another woman are killed in an Israeli airstrike in Ain Saadeh, a predominantly Christian town east of Beirut, Lebanon.
Multiple people are killed by Israeli attacks in towns across southern Lebanon.
The Israeli military orders the evacuation of the southern suburbs of Beirut because Israel will strike "Hezbollah infrastructure".
The Lebanese government reports that there are 1.2 million displaced people in Lebanon due to the war.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Odesa strikes
text: A Russian drone strike kills three civilians in Odesa Oblast, Ukraine, including a woman and her 2-year-old daughter.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Cameroon says Russia has confirmed that 16 Cameroonian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine while fighting alongside Russian forces. Cameroon's foreign ministry says "necessary arrangements" had been made to contact the families of the deceased soldiers.
Sudanese Army says that it has reopened the road linking Dilling, South Kordofan and North Kordofan following battles between the Rapid Support Forces and SPLM-N.
Afghan forces says that they have captured a border post during clashes with Pakistani troops in Khost Province.
One child is killed and three others are injured after a piece of unexploded ordnance detonated in Khost Province, Afghanistan.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: AirAsia says that it plans to open a hub in Bahrain despite the Iran war.
The Afghani National Disaster Management Authority says that the total number of deaths from recent natural disasters in Afghanistan has risen to 110.
One person is killed and four people are injured after a tanker explodes on the Bridge of the Americas near the Panama Canal.

context: Iran–Japan relations, Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
text: Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi says that her government is planning to hold summit talks with Iran amidst the Iran war.
Canadian mining company Vizla Silver confirms nine of the ten workers abducted from a silver mine in Concordia Municipality, Sinaloa, Mexico, in late January, are dead.

A court in Kursk Oblast, Russia, sentences former governor Alexei Smirnov to 14 years in prison for defrauding the government by embezzling public funds intended for building fortifications along the Russia–Ukraine border.

The Philippine National Police announces the detention of four of its officers and the relief of two commanders in relation to the April 3 shootout in Puerto Princesa, Philippines, where two police officers and a personnel of the Bureau of Corrections were killed.
Left-wing activists protest outside the U.S. Embassy in Tel Aviv to call for an end to the war in Iran.

NASA's Artemis II spacecraft carrying four astronauts breaks the record for furthest distance humans have ever travelled from Earth surpassing the previous 248,655 miles (400,171 kilometers) record set by Apollo 13 in April 1970.

context: 2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament
text: In college basketball, the Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team beats UConn, 69–63, to win the national championship. Michigan also becomes the first team to beat UConn past the Sweet 16 or later since Michigan State in the 2009 tournament.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Islamabad Accord
text: United States president Donald Trump announces on his Truth Social that, based on conversations with Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif and field marshal Asim Munir, he has agreed to "suspend the bombing and attacks on Iran for a period of two weeks", subject to Iran agreeing to the "complete, immediate and safe opening" of the Strait of Hormuz, and to allow time for an agreement to be reached.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Islamabad Accord
text: Iranian ambassador to Pakistan Reza Amiri-Moghaddam says that the Pakistan-mediated framework aimed at a ceasefire to end the war has reached a "critical, sensitive stage".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Islamabad Accord
text: Trump tells Fox News that the U.S. is in "heated negotiations" with Iran after being briefed about the proposal.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > Islamabad Accord
text: It is reported that U.S. vice president JD Vance would serve as the U.S. interlocutor in ceasefire talks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Trump warns that "a whole civilization will die tonight" and will "never be brought back" if Iran does not agree to a deal by noon (GMT).

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: The New York Times reports that Iran has ended direct contact with the U.S. in response to Trump's latest threat to "end its civilization". However, Tehran Times denies the reports by stating on X that "diplomatic and indirect channels of talks with [the] U.S. are not closed".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Vance says that the war in Iran will conclude "very shortly", claiming that the U.S. military has achieved all objectives.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia > Saudi Arabia–United States relations
text: The U.S. embassy in Riyadh advises its citizens to reconsider participating in this year's Hajj. The U.S. has raised its travel advisory for Saudi Arabia to Level 3 and warns of security risks such as rocket and drone attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Four people are injured by falling debris in Muraikh, Qatar, after the Qatari military intercepts Iranian missiles.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: Iranian drones strike a SABIC petrochemical complex in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: An Iranian ballistic missile strikes a Thuraya building in the Emirate of Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, injuring two Pakistani nationals.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Iran threatens to launch massive retaliatory strikes against the energy infrastructure of Saudi Arabia and the UAE in the event of a U.S. attack on its power plants.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Saudi Arabia closes the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain for several hours after the Iranian Fars News Agency has published a list of strategic bridges in the Gulf region as potential targets for retaliation.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: China and Russia veto a United Nations Security Council resolution calling on UN member states to "coordinate efforts, defensive in nature" to ensure the safety of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, saying that it was biased against Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war, 2026 United States–Israeli strikes on Iraq
text: Kata'ib Hezbollah announces the release of American journalist Shelly Kittleson, who was kidnapped by gunmen in Baghdad on March 31. The group's condition for Kittleson's freedom is her departure from Iraq.
At least 35 people are killed in airstrikes across Iran.
Reports indicate nighttime attacks in the greater Tehran area, in Ahvaz, Chahbahar, Jask, Shiraz, and Yazd, as well as near Shahid Kalantari Port, Tis Port, and the Imam Ali base.
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that Israel has struck bridges and railways in Iran allegedly used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
U.S. and Israeli warplanes strike Iranian military targets on Kharg Island that results in several massive explosions.
At least five people are killed after a rocket fired from Kuwait landed in Basra, southern Iraq.
Three people are killed and several are injured by an Israeli airstrike in Maarakah, Tyre District, Lebanon.
One person is killed by an Israeli drone strike in Deir ez-Zahrani, Nabatieh District, Lebanon.
One person is killed by an Israeli strike in Zebdin, Nabatieh District, Lebanon.
The Israeli military says that 36 soldiers were injured over the past two days, bringing the total casualties to 411.
Israel deploys the 98th Division to southern Lebanon, raising the force there to five divisions.
The Afghan foreign ministry says that talks between the Taliban–led government of Afghanistan and Pakistan in Ürümqi, China, to end the conflict have been "useful".

context: 2026 attack on Israeli consulate in Istanbul
text: One gunman is killed, while two other perpetrators and two policemen are injured in a shootout outside of the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. The two injured perpetrators have been captured and detained by police.
Armed attackers kill at least 50 people in a village in Shiroro, Niger State, Nigeria, including local hunters, militia members, and civilians.

context: Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran war
text: The semi-official Mehr News Agency reports that a suspected Israeli–U.S. missile struck the Rafi'-Nia synagogue in central Tehran.

This year's Wireless Festival in London, England, is cancelled and all tickets are refunded after its headliner, American rapper Kanye West, is banned from entering the United Kingdom by the Home Office on the grounds that "his presence would not be conducive to the public good" amid controversy over his past antisemitic comments on Jews and Adolf Hitler, and his association with neo-Nazis.
The Japanese House of Councillors enacts the country's largest state budget in history worth ¥122.3 trillion (€664 billion).

The International Organization for Migration reports that at least 990 deaths have been recorded in 2026 across the Mediterranean Sea, making it one of the deadliest starts to a year since 2014, with over 180 people feared dead or missing in the latest shipwrecks since 28 March.
The death toll from a large fire at a petrochemical plant in Tatarstan, Russia, five days ago, rises to 12, including a firefighter. Dozens of others were injured.
Three people are killed and another is reported missing after a scaffolding collapse at a steel plant in Kawasaki, Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan.
A TGV train collides with a military lorry on a level crossing at Nœux-les-Mines, France. The train driver is killed and 27 people are wounded.
The death toll from natural disasters, including heavy rain, storms and floods, rises to 188 in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Cuban president and First Secretary of the Communist Party Miguel Díaz-Canel warns the United States that his forces will wage a guerrilla warfare campaign if the U.S. military invades and occupies the country.
At the invitation of paramount leader Xi Jinping, Kuomintang chairperson Cheng Li-wun begins the first visit to China by a Taiwanese opposition leader since 2016.
Protestors storm the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra, Iraq, after a rocket attack launched from Kuwait killed three people in Basra.

context: Aftermath of the Afghanistan War > War crimes in Afghanistan
text: Australian Army veteran and Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith is arrested by police at Sydney Airport for alleged war crimes committed between 2009 and 2012 during his deployment to Afghanistan.

South Sudan president Salva Kiir Mayardit sacks National Legislative Assembly speaker Jemma Nunu Kumba and her deputy Parmena Awerial Aluong after his ruling party backed a no-confidence vote accusing them of corruption and mismanagement.

context: Protests against the 2026 Iran war > Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
text: A protest is held outside the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., after the ceasefire announcement, calling for President Trump's removal from office and accusing him of war crimes.
Iran calls on the population to form human chains around critical infrastructure such as power stations and bridges ahead of a U.S. deadline that threatens their destruction.
Human chain protests are held across bridge and power plant structures in Iran to protest against Trump's threats against civilian infrastructure.
Citizens in Ilam, Iran, form a human chain protest against Trump's threats against key infrastructure in the country.
The National Assembly of Vietnam re-elects General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Tô Lâm as president for the 2026–2031 tenure, and Lê Minh Hưng as prime minister.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi confirms the two-week ceasefire between Iran and the United States, which includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The ceasefire is ratified by the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC).

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: The SNSC announces that negotiations between Iran and the U.S. will start on Friday in Islamabad, Pakistan, with the U.S. contingent to be led by vice president JD Vance alongside senior presidential adviser Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. president Donald Trump both claim that the ceasefire does not include Lebanon, despite contrary statements from both Iran and Pakistan on their versions of the ceasefire agreement.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt states that Netanyahu and Trump will continue discussions on potentially including Lebanon in a ceasefire arrangement.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: After the announcement, an Israeli military spokesperson states that Israel is still launching attacks on Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says the ceasefire with Israel and the U.S. has been violated as a result of the bombings of Iranian islands and Lebanon. Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf later echoes the remarks, citing the attacks as well as the "denial of Iran to enrich uranium."

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military intercepts six missiles and 31 drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait's interior ministry reports fires at several oil facilities, power plants, and desalination plants after an Iranian drone attack.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: The Qatari military intercepts seven ballistic missiles and multiple drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia's East–West Crude Oil Pipeline is hit in an Iranian attack.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
text: The Emirati military intercepts 17 ballistic missiles and 35 drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: After the announcement of a ceasefire, Iran launches ballistic missiles at Bahrain, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Iranian agencies report explosions from the Lavan and Sirri islands of unknown origin. Iran accuses Kuwait and the UAE of the attacks and launches retaliatory attacks against those countries in response.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Thailand confirms the three crewmen on a vessel that was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in March have died.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: MarineTraffic reports the first ships that have passed through the Strait of Hormuz since the ceasefire announcement, namely the Greek-owned bulk carrier NJ Earth and Liberia-flagged Daytona Beach.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz maritime traffic to oil tankers over Israeli attacks in Lebanon, claiming that Lebanon is included in the ceasefire.
Bahrain, Iraq, and Syria reopen their airspace after weeks of closure. The Damascus International Airport and the Bahrain International Airport begin resuming flights.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war > 2026 Israeli Beirut strikes
text: At least 254 people are killed and 1,165 others are injured in a wave of Israeli strikes on Lebanon, including in southern Lebanon, Beirut, and the Bekaa Valley.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The IDF announces that its strikes in Lebanon are one part of a new operation called "Eternal Darkness".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Israeli military says that it has halted strikes against Iran, but state that they will continue fighting Hezbollah in Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Lebanese army closes a bridge in the Tyre District after receiving a warning of a possible Israeli strike on the structure. The bridge is the last crossing linking areas north and south of the Litani River in the area, where many residents remain despite evacuation notices.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war > Killing of journalists in the Gaza war
text: An Israeli airstrike in Sheikh Ijlin, Gaza City, Palestine, kills two people, including Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning says that Afghanistan and Pakistan has agreed on a comprehensive plan to end tensions after seven days of talks in Ürümqi, China. The two countries also agree to avoid any escalations in their current conflict.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > Tariffs in the second Trump administration
text: U.S. president Donald Trump threatens to impose 50% tariffs on countries that supply military weapons to Iran.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Danish shipping company Maersk says that they will take a "cautious approach" for vessels to cross the Strait of Hormuz despite the ceasefire and says that they have not provided security certainty as to when normal operations would resume.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: German shipping company Hapag-Lloyd says that it still does not plan to resume transiting the Strait of Hormuz despite the two-week ceasefire. They also say that it would need 6–8 weeks for recovery and for normal operations to resume.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Oil prices plunge below US$95 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average surges past 1,000 after the ceasefire announcement.
Belarus plans to open an embassy in North Korea by August 1 after president Alexander Lukashenko visited the country in March following a decree signed by prime minister Alexander Turchin.

context: 2026 attack on Israeli consulate in Istanbul
text: Turkish police arrest 198 suspects across 34 provinces in operations targeting the Islamic State following a fatal shootout outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on April 7. Several suspects are placed in pre-trial detention as part of the investigation.

Rex Heuermann admits in court to killing eight women and discarding their bodies between 1993 and 2010 in New York, United States. Heuermann is expected to receive a sentence of life in prison without parole when he is sentenced on June 17.

context: Illegal drug trade in the United States
text: A U.S. court sentences Jasveen Sangha to 15 years in prison for distributing ketamine that resulted in the death of actor Matthew Perry in 2023, as part of a wider investigation into a network supplying controlled substances. Authorities also charge and sentence other individuals, including medical professionals, in connection with the distribution of the drug.
Anti-war protesters gather outside the U.S. embassy in Ottawa, Canada, to protest against the Iran war despite the ceasefire along with the wars in Lebanon and Gaza.

Around 50,000 protestors across over 150 locations, including around 30,000 outside the National Diet Building in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Japan, protest against the war and proposals by prime minister Sanae Takaichi plan to revise Article 9 of the constitution.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: After pressure from the United States, Israel agrees to hold direct talks with Lebanon in Washington, D.C., but refuses to observe the Iran war ceasefire in Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: German chancellor Friedrich Merz announces that Germany will resume direct negotiations with Iran to support a ceasefire between Iran and the U.S., with talks planned in Islamabad, Pakistan, involving a German delegation.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei had approved the ceasefire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military intercepts seven drones from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: The Kuwaiti military reports that drones attacked several vital facilities and caused significant damage to a national guard base.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy announces alternative routes for ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz, citing risks of sea mines in the main shipping channel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company CEO Sultan Al Jaber says that the strait is still not open because Iran has been restricting and controlling traffic.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Gabon-flagged oil tanker MSG crosses the Strait of Hormuz according to MarineTraffic, making it the first non-Iranian oil tanker to cross the waterway since the ceasefire was announced.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war
text: Former Iranian foreign minister Kamal Kharazi dies from injuries sustained during an Israeli–U.S. airstrike on his home on April 1.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah launches rockets at the Israeli kibbutz of Manara, citing Israeli and American violations of the ceasefire linked to the Iran war.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: At least seven people are killed by a wave of Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling across Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: The Israeli military says that it has killed Lebanese Resistance Brigades commanders Maher Qassem Hamdan and Ali Yusuf Harshi, personal secretary and nephew of Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah says that its fighters are engaged in "point-blank clashes" with Israeli troops in Bint Jbeil, Lebanon.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Lebanese authorities update the losses from the previous day's attacks to 303 killed and 1,150 injured.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russia–United Kingdom relations, Russian sabotage operations in Europe
text: British defence secretary John Healey says three Russian Navy submarines engaged in covert operations against the UK in the North Sea near its undersea cables and says counter-measures are underway.
The Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War says that Russia has returned 1,000 bodies of fallen individuals to Ukraine as part of repatriation efforts.
Russian president Vladimir Putin declares a ceasefire for the weekend in Ukraine for Orthodox Easter.
The Sudan Founding Alliance says that over 56 civilians, including 17 children, are killed and 107 are injured in a Sudanese drone strike on a wedding celebration in Kutum, North Darfur, Sudan.
The World Food Programme announces the return of its Sudan office in Khartoum for the first time in three years amidst a hunger crisis caused by the war.

The Al-Aqsa Mosque, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, the Western Wall, and other holy sites in the Old City of Jerusalem reopen for the first time since the war with Iran started on February 28 after being closed by authorities due to security concerns.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development announces plans to allocate €5 billion to support economies affected by the Iran war, focusing on financial systems, businesses, and infrastructure in Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, and Lebanon.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Gulf Air, the flag carrier of Bahrain, announces a plan to return its operations hub to Bahrain International Airport after having relocated to King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, during the Iran war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Oil prices rebound amidst concerns about the ceasefire, with U.S. and Brent Crude oil back up to nearly US$100 per barrel.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Saudi Arabia reports that the recent Iranian attack on a pumping station of the East–West Crude Oil Pipeline reduced its throughput by 700,000 barrels per day.

Venezuela's National Assembly approves a reform of mining laws that allows greater private investment in the country's mineral sector, with the bill advancing to constitutional review. The measure forms part of broader economic changes aimed at increasing foreign participation in natural resource industries.

context: USAID in the second Trump administration
text: The OECD reports that official development assistance from its member states declined by 23.1 percent in real terms to US$174.3 billion, marking the largest recorded annual decrease, with the reduction largely driven by cuts from the United States.
Four people are killed and 38 are rescued after an inflatable dinghy of migrants capsized near Calais, off the coast of northern France.

Russian deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov meets with Cuban president Miguel Díaz-Canel in Havana to discuss bilateral relations amid ongoing tensions between Cuba and the U.S. over energy and economic measures, and following the recent arrival of a Russian oil shipment to Cuba despite U.S. restrictions.

Indian oil and gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri visits Qatar to discuss the prioritization of energy exports, as the country is India's largest supplier of liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas.
United States deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau summons the ambassador of Iraq to protest the Iraqi government's failure to prevent militia attacks on American personnel.
Nepal issues an arrest warrant for former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba and his wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba, for alleged money laundering.
Pakistan enforces a lockdown in the Capital Territory to prepare for Iran–U.S. ceasefire talks.
The Supreme Court of Russia designates the human rights group Memorial as an extremist organization and bans its activities following a petition by the Ministry of Justice.
Isar Aerospace's "Onward and Upward" mission, which had been due to launch from Andøya Space port in Andøya, Norway, is postponed for a third time due to a possible leak.
A study published in the Science journal finds that 28 chimpanzees, including 19 infants, have been killed during an ongoing chimpanzee war in Kibale National Park, Uganda.

context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
text: The Korean Central News Agency reports that North Korea has tested various military technologies throughout the week, including a surface-to-surface tactical ballistic missile identified as Hwasongpho-11 Ka.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that peace talks with the United States will not begin until there is a ceasefire in Lebanon and Iranian assets are unfrozen.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: The Kuwaiti military reports that several national guard personnel were injured by Iranian drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Pakistani military evacuates the crew of a merchant vessel in the Arabian Sea following a distress call.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israel launches attacks across southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley, killing at least 21 people, including 13 Lebanese State Security personnel in Nabatieh.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Hezbollah fires at least thirty rockets at Kiryat Shmona, Metula, Misgav Am, and Ashdod Naval Base in Israel, saying that it was a response to ceasefire violations.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Israeli chief of staff Eyal Zamir says that the military is in a "state of war" in Lebanon despite the ceasefire with Iran, while visiting Israeli troops deployed near Bint Jbeil.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Hezbollah–Israel conflict > 2026 Lebanon war
text: Preliminary talks between Lebanese and Israeli officials are planned for next week in Washington, D.C., United States.
At least 11 people are killed and several others are injured after gunmen open fire in Injil District, Herat Province, Afghanistan.
Over 100,000 Muslims worship at the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Temple Mount, East Jerusalem, after it reopens for the first time after Israel closed the site at the start of the Gaza war.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: Protests over fuel prices are held in Ireland and Norway.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: The parliament of South Korea approves a supplementary budget worth ₩26.2 trillion (US$17.7 billion) to address the economic effects of the war, which includes cash assistance to 35 million South Koreans.
