text: The Sudanese Army says that it has downed another Chinese-made FH-95 drone near El-Obeid in North Kordofan, making it the fourth drone downed by the army.
Ravindra Ganjhu, a CPI (Maoist) top wanted leader, is confirmed to have been arrested by Jharkhand police in Latehar, India during an anti-Maoist operation.
A Ramesside period tomb that belonged to Theban mayor Paser is discovered in the Theban Necropolis in Egypt.
Danish shipping company Maersk announces that they will resume services through the Red Sea for its WAF6 service.
A fire breaks out at a pub in Chatuchak, Bangkok, Thailand, killing 27 people and wounding 63 more.

South Korea's navy recovers the body of a sailor who disappeared during a patrol near the Northern Limit Line, after South Korea requested North Korean assistance and launched a search involving ships and aircraft.
The University of Oxford begins the first human trial of its ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of the ebolavirus.
The United States says that they will block citizens of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from traveling to the country on commercial flights amidst the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the country.

A cyclosporiasis outbreak, caused by cyclospora cayetanensis, is reported in 31 U.S. states by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reporting 2,640 cases in the state.
Sudan's Khartoum State government reports a shortage in drinking water in neighborhoods in the state including southern Omdurman after a sharp drop is reported in the water levels on the Nile River.
The United Kingdom announces that it will designate Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps as a terrorist organization, and will ban support for the militia group.
The European Union imposes sanctions against Sudan's gold trade, accusing them of financing the civil war in the country.

context: Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war > Anti-war protests in Russia
text: Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin is detained over a video on his social media account featuring the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny, days after he was designated a "foreign agent". He is later released from a police station and will appear in court on July 17.

context: Regime change efforts in the 2026 Iran war
text: The New York Times reports that former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is under house arrest after Iranian authorities reportedly uncovered a significant portion of his contacts with Israel. However, his office denies these reports, including reports that Israel recruited him for regime changing plans.

South Carolina governor Henry McMaster appoints Darline Graham Nordone to temporarily fill the U.S. Senate seat of her brother, Lindsey Graham, after his death last Saturday, with the term ending in 2027.
The Hungarian parliament moves to remove president Tamás Sulyok through a constitutional amendment backed by prime minister Péter Magyar's majority government.

Venezuelan acting president Delcy Rodríguez appoints U.S. envoy Félix Plasencia to a foreign relations and overseas trade post, replacing foreign minister Yván Gil, who becomes science and technology minister.
Astronomers announce that an erythrulose molecule was detected inside a cloud of gas and dust near the center of the Milky Way. It is the first evidence of sugar in interstellar space.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran in an effort to degrade capabilities used to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz ahead of the naval blockade.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Lebanon war > 2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks

context: Iraqi conflict > Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
text: Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi and the U.S. defense department says that all remaining American troops will withdraw from Iraq by September 30, ending a 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion.

context: Sudanese civil war > 2026 Blue Nile campaign
text: The Sudanese Armed Forces say that the 4th Infantry Division's 13th Brigade have taken control of the Blue Nile town of Fashfoun following days of clashes with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North.
Colombia's military says it has rescued 39 civilians kidnapped by the National Liberation Army on a highway in Chocó Department, with two soldiers killed during the operation.
A Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton nicknamed Gus sells for US$50.1 million at Sotheby’s in New York City, United States, setting an auction record for a dinosaur fossil.

Cuba suffers its third nationwide blackout in less than 10 days and fifth of 2026, as the state utility reports a complete grid failure amid fuel shortages caused by the ongoing U.S. imposed blockade, that complicate power restoration.
Seven people are killed and three others are injured after two vehicles collided head-on just outside Ramadi, Iraq.
Six people are killed after a gas-laden truck caught fire and exploded at a checkpoint along a federal highway in Kogi State, Nigeria.
Six workers are killed in a fire at a building under construction in Brussels, Belgium.

The Directorate General of Health Services reports that seven more children have died from measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, bringing the total death toll from the disease in the country to 766.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) announces that it will test the Gilead Sciences antiviral for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.
The World Health Organization reports that 80% of cases of Ebola in eastern DRC are from unknown chains of transmission. Additionally, the death toll from Ebola reaches 700.
The U.S. CDC reports 7,000 cases nationwide of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by cyclospora cayetanensis.
The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports 3,300 cases in the state, up from 2,640 the previous day.

context: Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
text: The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement suspends vehicle stops related to immigration enforcement following the recent fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, Texas, and Joan Sebastian Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine.

context: International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
text: A prosecutor at the International Criminal Court drop charges against former rebel leader Abdallah Banda over his role in a 2007 attack on African Union peacekeepers during Sudan's Darfur conflict.

Japan approves election rules requiring AI-generated images and videos on social media to be labeled and prohibiting false or distorted information about candidates, with the measures taking effect in March.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign > 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that ceasefire negotiations aimed at ending the war have not closed despite renewed fighting between Iran and the U.S.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: The Directorate General of Counter Terrorism of the Kurdistan Region Security Council reports that international coalition forces have intercepted seven drones in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: Three drones are reportedly shot down near the U.S. consulate in Erbil.
CENTCOM announces the U.S. has launched new strikes against Iran for a fifth consecutive day aimed at coastal defense systems, cruise missile storage, and launch sites in the Greater Tunb Island.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Gaza peace plan
text: Morocco signs an agreement with the Board of Peace to join the International Stabilization Force for Gaza.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Nirim attack, Gaza war hostage crisis
text: Israel's military claims to have killed a militant from the Hamas branch Al-Qassam Brigades that participated in the abduction of soldiers Col. Asaf Hamami, St.-Sgt. Tomer Yaakov Ahimas, and Sgt. Kiril Brodski during the October 7 attacks on the Nirim kibbutz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Yemeni civil war > Saudi Arabia–United States relations
text: The U.S. State Department approves a potential US$1.96 billion deal in arms sales to Saudi Arabia amidst the current Iran war and potential re-escalation with the Houthis.
The Sudanese Armed Forces-allied Joint Forces announce that they have recaptured the Orshi Reservoir area in North Darfur, a month after the Rapid Support Forces seized the area.
A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces hits a power station in the town of Al Dabbah in Sudan's Northern State.
Seven people are killed and one person is missing after a rubber dinghy explodes near Liaoning Province, China.
One person is killed and 24 others are missing after a passenger boat sank off the coast of Sulawesi, Indonesia.

IQAir ranks Toronto, Ontario, Canada, as having the worst air quality among major cities worldwide as smoke from wildfires in northwestern Ontario reaches the city, prompting the Canadian environment ministry to advise residents to remain indoors.
The total amount of cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 2,000.
Sudan's health ministry reports that the total amount of cholera cases in north and west Kordofan has increased to 1,547.

context: United Kingdom–European Union relations > Effect of Brexit on Gibraltar
text: The United Kingdom and the European Union remove the land-border fence between Gibraltar and Spain under a post-Brexit treaty, allowing free movement while introducing joint British-Spanish checks at Gibraltar's airport and port.
United Nations secretary-general António Guterres appoints Bangladeshi diplomat Rabab Fatima as the next head of the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan.

Papuan foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko announces the immediate closure of Taiwan's representative office in Port Moresby, citing Papua New Guinea's adherence to the One China policy, while saying the decision does not affect contracts between Taiwan's CPC Corporation and natural gas in Papua New Guinea.

A district court in Kathmandu, Nepal, sentences former deputy prime minister Top Bahadur Rayamajhi to four years in prison and former home minister Bal Krishna Khand to two years for roles in forging documents for a fraudulent Bhutanese refugee resettlement scheme.
Kenya's High Court rejects a Rastafarian petition seeking a religious exemption from cannabis laws, ruling that the group does not show the laws violate religious freedom.

context: Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo establishes a council composed of mostly international war crimes lawyers to advise state institutions seeking accountability and reparations for victims of violence in the country's east.

context: Detention of Craig and Lindsay Foreman
text: The family of British national Craig Foreman says an Iranian court has added two years to his 10-year espionage prison sentence for speaking to the media, as he and his wife Lindsay continue a hunger strike.
Moroccan prosecutors release journalist Ali Lmrabet after questioning him over online posts allegedly defaming unnamed individuals and institutions, while the criminal investigation continues.

U.S. president Donald Trump announces that American citizen Dena Karari has been released from Iran after being detained on espionage charges since 2024. Her lawyer, Jared Genser, also confirmed her release.

France's National Assembly gives final approval to a bill allowing eligible adults with incurable, life-threatening illnesses to obtain lethal medication under strict conditions. The measure awaits Constitutional Council review before taking effect.

Astronomers directly image the exoplanet Beta Pictoris d next to its star, located 63 light-years away, using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope. It is also reported to be fainter than its sibling Beta Pictoris b. The discovery is published in the The Astrophysical Journal.
American technology company Amazon partners with South African internet provider Herotel to launch Amazon Leo satellite internet service in 2027, marking its first such African agreement.

The ESPY Awards is held at the David H. Koch Theater in New York City, U.S., with the 2025–26 New York Knicks winning five awards, including the Best Team award after winning their first NBA championship since 1973, while point guard Jalen Brunson wins the Best Male Athlete and Best Championship Performance awards.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says that Iran is still interested in an agreement with the United States.

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States Central Command launches new strikes against Iran for a sixth consecutive night in an effort to degrade Iranian military capabilities.

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: Explosions are reported in Iran's Qeshm Island, Bushehr, Ahvaz, and Bandar Abbas, including a bridge in Bandar Khamir. A truck on the bridge is reported to be targeted, killing the driver.

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: Tasnim News Agency reports that American fighter jets attacked the Iranshahr Airport in the Sistan and Baluchestan province.

context: 2026 Iran war > Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
text: The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military intercepted and destroyed 32 drones entering the country's airspace.

context: Sudanese civil war > Sudanese refugee crisis
text: Around 1,000 Sudanese returnees in Egypt are reported by a local committee to have returned to Sudan.
The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have destroyed around 205 combat vehicles, military supply trucks, and four strategic drones belonging to the Rapid Support Forces in the past two weeks.
Five insurgents are revealed to have been killed and several others injured in recent clashes last month involving the Mozambican Army and the Islamic State near Catupa, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique.
TotalEnergies and its partners inaugurate the 216 MW Hydra solar-and-battery project in the Northern Cape, South Africa, which is the largest hybrid renewable energy project on the continent.
Twenty-one people are killed and several others are injured after a bus lost control and veered off the road in Kapchorwa, Uganda.
Fourteen people are killed and five others are injured after a minibus plunged into a deep ravine in Cajamarca, Peru.
Eleven people are killed and 19 more injured in a fire at a care facility in Algiers, Algeria.
Six members of a family are killed after a fire engulfed their house in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan.
The Ugandan health ministry reports that Uganda has discharged its last patient diagnosed with Ebola, triggering a 42-day countdown clock on when it can be declared free of the virus.

The Washington Post links the iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms and supplied to American fast food chain Taco Bell as a source of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis.
Taco Bell removes lettuce from some of their restaurants following reports that the Food and Drug Administration has opened an investigation into iceberg lettuce supplied to them.
The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports that the amount of hospitalizations in the state linked to the cyclosporiasis outbreak has surpassed 100 people.
Zambia's health ministry declares an end to its cholera outbreak, which started in August of last year, after four weeks without a case.

Taiwan says that its representative office in Port Moresby will continue operating and assisting Taiwanese nationals, rejecting Papua New Guinea's decision to close it and stating that the move was made without prior consultation. Papuan foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko says that his ministry informed Taiwan of the closure "weeks ago".

context: Sudan–United Arab Emirates relations, War crimes during the Sudanese civil war
text: Sudanese justice minister Abdallah Dirif says that the government will launch lawsuits against the United Arab Emirates in international courts for its role in supporting war crimes by the Rapid Support Forces in the ongoing civil war.

The Thai interior ministry identifies irregularities in the mandatory examination results of 5,814 civil servants and considers suspensions, while police arrest three suspected organizers following a joint investigation with the anti-corruption commission.

context: Huachicol fiscal, Organized crime in Mexico
text: Ernesto Ruffo Appel, former governor of Baja California, Mexico, is arrested on charges related to organized crime and fuel smuggling.

South Korea's Supreme Court upholds People Power Party lawmaker Kweon Seong-dong's two-year prison sentence for accepting ₩100 million (US$67,400) in illegal political funds from the Unification Church, removing him from the National Assembly.

Former Autostrade per l'Italia (ASPI) CEO Giovanni Castellucci is convicted and sentenced to 12 years in prison for his role in the 2018 collapse of the Ponte Morandi in Genoa, Liguria, Italy, which killed 43 people.
Protests take place in Kyiv and other cities across Ukraine against president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's decision to replace defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov with major-general Yevhenii Khmara.
Ukrainian Air Force deputy commander Pavlo Yelizarov resigns from his position in protest of Fedorov's removal as defense minister.

Astronomers report the first observationally confirmed atmosphere around a rocky exoplanet within its star's habitable zone, after detecting helium escaping from the upper atmosphere of LHS 1140 b, a super-Earth approximately 49 light-years from Earth.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: Iran says that it has launched ballistic missile and drone strikes at targets in Bahrain, including a drone vessel depot, an artificial intelligence center used for targeting, and the Al-Sakhir Air Base, as part of the 11th phase of its Saegheh operation.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: Jordan reports having intercepted projectiles fired from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Iranian strikes damage a desalination plant and a power plant in Kuwait, according to the Kuwaiti energy ministry.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy launches attacks on radar facilities in Oman.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Syria
text: Iranian state media reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps have targeted a United States Special Operations Command in Al-Tanf in response to the killing of Iranian soldiers in Iranshahr, Sistan and Baluchestan province.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force launches an attack at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, and claims to have caused damage to equipment there, while Qatar's armed forces claim to have intercepted Iranian attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The U.S. military's Central Command (CENTCOM) confirms that they have destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower in Chabahar Port yesterday, which was allegedly used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for tracking commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: Iranian drone strikes near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, kill eight Kurdish rebels and injure several more.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a seventh consecutive night.
Around eight Palestinians are reported to be killed in an airstrike on a funeral in central Gaza.

The Israeli military and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Hamas commander Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, who served as a "right-hand man" of former Al-Qassam Brigades commander Mohammed Deif, in an airstrike in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip.
An attack on a military deployment in Téra, Tillabéri Region, Niger, kills 16 soldiers and injures 23 others, while state media reports that security forces have killed 15 attackers.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iraq–Syria relations
text: Iraq and Syria sign a memorandum of understanding to rehabilitate the Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline to bypass to the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > Iraq-United States relations
text: The United States Chamber of Commerce announces that Iraq has signed roughly $60 billion worth of agreements and partnerships to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and accelerate American investment in the Iraqi oil sector.

context: Wildfires in 2026 > 2026 United States wildfires > 2026 Minnesota wildfires
text: The United States Forest Service reports that wildfires in northern Minnesota has reached over 77,000 acres, prompting evacuations in the area.
Over 900 wildfires are reported across Canada, including 43 new active blazes, prompting evacuations across the country.
The U.S. state of Connecticut's Department of Energy and Environmental Protection deploys firefighters to assist with wildfire efforts in Quebec, Canada.
A earthquake strikes near the coast of Chiapas, Mexico. Tsunami warnings are issued and at least two people are injured.
The confirmed death toll from the doublet earthquakes that struck northern Venezuela in June rises to 5,069 people.

A large fire breaks out among terraced houses in Krokstadelva, Drammen, Norway, spreading rapidly between multiple housing blocks and prompting mass evacuations. The municipality declares a crisis and calls in fire crews from eight neighboring municipalities.
Eight people are killed, ten others are rescued and 34 are reported missing when a landslide buries multiple houses and residential buildings in Pengshui, Chongqing, China.
Four people are killed and nine others are injured after a head-on collision between two overspeeding cars along the N-25 National Highway in Wadh, Balochistan, Pakistan.
A nine-vehicle pile-up in Deli Serdang, North Sumatra, Indonesia, kills at least four and injures eight others.
A storm in Chile kills three people, injures seven others, damages more than 800 homes, displaces hundreds, and leaves around 400,000 people without electricity across 10 regions.
A nine-story building under construction near Conakry, Guinea, collapses due to heavy rainfall, killing three people and injuring several others.
Two citizens are killed from weather-related incidents and 53,000 homes are reported to be without power during severe thunderstorms across several regions of France.
The death tolls from the measles outbreak in Bangladesh reaches 780 after one child is reported to have died from the disease by the Directorate General of Health Services.
Taylor Farms recalls their iceburg lettuce, traced through a farm in Mexico, amidst the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis.
Michigan, U.S., surpasses 5,000 cases of cyclosporiasis.
The United States allows its national emergency over Hong Kong's national security law to expire while retaining the underlying executive order and most related sanctions.
A civilian dies while a police officer and the suspected gunman are wounded in a shooting in Nørresundby, North Jutland, Denmark, after officers responding to a reported fire are met with gunfire.
The Ontario Court of Appeal finds Canadian far-right activist and Freedom Convoy organizer Pat King guilty of intimidation and orders a re-sentencing.
Japan enacts a law criminalizing public damage, removal or defacement of the national flag, punishable by up to two years in prison or a ¥200,000 (US$1,200) fine.
Turkish authorities detain 67 irregular migrants and five other suspected smugglers following a sailboat interception off the coast of Muğla, Turkey.
Andy Burnham is elected as the new leader of the British Labour Party. He will formally succeed Keir Starmer as prime minister on Monday.

Protests continue for a second day in Kyiv, Ukraine, near the Presidential Office Building, demanding the return of Mykhailo Fedorov as Minister of Defence and the resignation of Oleksandr Syrskyi as the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

Japan's National Diet amends the Imperial Household Law to allow unmarried male descendants of former imperial branches to rejoin the family and permit royal women to retain status after marrying commoners, while preserving male-only succession.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Bahraini military intercepts projectiles fired from Iran.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The U.S. Central ​Command (CENTCOM) reports that two American troops have been "killed in action" in Jordan, bringing the total casualties for American troops to 16.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait says Iranian attacks have struck a second power and desalination plant in two days, causing a fire and shutting several generating units, while other attacks injure firefighters and a worker and temporarily disrupt flights from Kuwait International Airport.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: An oil facility is damaged, according to the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation.

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
text: Axios reports that Iran has launched a ballistic missile at a United States base in Saudi Arabia, making it the first direct attack by Iran on the country since targeting a petrochemical complex in Jubail.
Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that the United States has violated the terms of the Islamabad Memorandum and that Iran is "no longer implementing them".

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, in a statement published by IRNA, report that two oil tankers have exploded after hitting mines south in the Strait of Hormuz. However, the U.S. Central Command disputes the claims on X as "false".

context: 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Philippine foreign affairs department reports that four Philippine-registered vessels carrying 81 seafarers have safely transited through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels are identified as the MV Lyng Trader, MV Western Doncaster, MV Vivian Trader, and MV Eva Fuji.

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: In the seventh day of renewed U.S. strikes, civilian infrastructure, including a desalination plant in Jask, are damaged, cutting off the access to water for 10,000 civilians. [https://www.bbc.com/persian/articles/cd7lx02wjn8o (BBC Persian (in Persian))]

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: Communications services in Iran's Hormozgan province are disrupted after U.S. strikes damaged 116 radio towers there. [https://www.bbc.com/persian/live/c8rnde80d86t (BBC Persian (in Persian))]

context: 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The U.S. CENTCOM launches a new wave of strikes for an eighth consecutive night against IRGC targets in response to two American service members killed in Jordan.
The Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels ambush a Malian military convoy in the Gao Region of Mali.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Moscow Oblast governor Andrey Vorobyov and Tambov Oblast head Yevgeny Pervyshov say Ukrainian drone attacks killed seven workers and injure 49 others at Wildberries warehouses in Kotovsk and Elektrostal, Russia, while another strike ignites an oil facility. Ukraine says the warehouses support Russian drone production.
Arab League secretary general Nabil Fahmy and U.S. envoy Massad Boulos reach an agreement to establish a regular framework for joint coordination for a ceasefire in the ongoing civil war in Sudan.
An insurgent is killed and five others are injured during a counterterrorism operation that foiled a terrorist plot in Wana, South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

context: Belgium–Israel relations, International reactions to the Gaza war
text: Belgium approves an import ban on goods from Israeli settlements.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Kuwait Airways reschedules most of its flights due to the country's airspace being closed amidst ongoing Iranian attacks.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Iran's Hormozgan province water and wastewater company announces that United States airstrikes have damaged desalination equipment, cutting off water to about 10,000 people.
Over 100 houses burn down in a fire in the Krokstadelva municipality of Norway.
Nine people are killed and nine others are injured after an unauthorized firecracker factory explodes in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India.
Five people are killed and two others are injured in a workplace accident in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam.
Five people, including three women, drown in the Godavari River whilst fishing near Polavaram district, India.
Four people are killed, four more are missing, and seven others are injured after torrential rains and flash floods hit a mountainous village in Lai Châu province, Vietnam.
Turkey's interior ministry announces the arrest of 119 people linked to ISIS.
Hungarian president Tamás Sulyok signs the 17th amendment to the nation's constitution, which will end his term in office at midnight the following day.

Jens Spahn resigns as leader of the governing CDU/CSU alliance in Germany's Bundestag amid criticism after he and his husband became parents through surrogacy, despite Germany's ban and his party's opposition to the practice.

Skyroot Aerospace successfully launches Vikram-1, India's first privately built orbital rocket, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh, carrying small satellite payloads into low Earth orbit on its maiden flight.
In association football, England beats France 6–4 in the highest-scoring third-place playoff in FIFA World Cup history, securing their best result since winning the tournament in 1966.

French footballer Kylian Mbappé scores twice to become the highest-scoring player in World Cup history, and the first player to score 10 goals in a single World Cup since Germany's Gerd Müller in 1970.
At the London Athletics Meet, British runner Josh Kerr sets a new world record of 3:42.66 for the mile. The previous record of 3:43.13 by Hicham El Guerrouj had been set in 1999.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire
text: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio says that diplomatic solutions are "still on the table" if Iran ceases attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: The Kurdistan Freedom Party reports that eight Iranian Kurdish rebels have been wounded after a drone strike from Iran hit a camp near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
text: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announces that an American service member has been killed in northern Iraq during a "controlled" detonation of a downed Iranian drone, bringing the total amount of American casualties to 17.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The Israeli military uses the Iron Dome to shoot down fragments from an Iranian missile fired at Aqaba, Jordan, after the Aegis was reportedly used to shoot down the missile.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a ninth consecutive evening amidst a rise in American casualties.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Aftermath of the Syrian civil war > SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes
text: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that 530 people, including 76 civilians, have been killed in clashes between the post-Assad Syrian Army and the Syrian Democratic Forces over the past months.
Around 50 Malian soldiers are reported to have been killed in Anéfis, Mali, by the Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels.

Ukrainian officials say Russian forces struck a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn off Odesa, killing ten crew members from India and Syria. Eight others are rescued, while the vessel continues burning.
At least six people are killed and 21 others are injured when a earthquake strikes the town of Pumpunya in Chongos Bajo District, Chupaca province, Department of Junín, Peru.
Four people are killed, four others are unaccounted for, and several houses are swept away after a landslide triggered by heavy rainfall hits Mon District, Nagaland, India.
Sixty-seven people are rescued and 66 others are reported missing when passenger ferry MV Barima capsizes and sinks near the Pomeroon River in Guyana.
Canada bars foreign nationals who have visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the previous 21 days, citing the Ebola epidemic.

Students hold protests in several cities across India after activist Sonam Wangchuk is arrested and taken to a hospital during his hunger strike calling for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the 2026 NEET exam paper leak, with a march on Parliament planned for the following day.
Santomeans vote to elect the country's president. Incumbent president Carlos Vila Nova seeks a second term in office.

context: 2026 Esports World Cup > League of Legends in esports
text: In esports, Dplus KIA defeats Karmine Corp 3–0 to win the League of Legends title at the 2026 Esports World Cup, extending South Korea's winning streak to three years and securing its first international title since 2020.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup > 2026 FIFA World Cup final
text: In association football, Spain win their second FIFA World Cup title after defeating the defending champions Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States. Spain's captain Rodri is awarded the Golden Ball.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup > Spain at the FIFA World Cup
text: After winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Spain becomes the first country to hold both the men's and women's World Cups, having won the latter in 2023. The men's team extends their international football record of 38 consecutive unbeaten matches, surpassing Italy's record of 37. It also becomes the first team to field two teenagers, Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí, both 19-year-olds, in a FIFA World Cup final.

context: 2026 FIFA World Cup > Spain at the FIFA World Cup
text: Spanish manager Luis de la Fuente also becomes the oldest manager to win a World Cup title at 65 years old.

Mathematician and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge presents an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in three-dimensional space that disproves the n-variable conjecture for n > 2 using the large language model Fable 5. The Jacobian conjecture for n = 1 remains true.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign > 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
text: The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected seven commercial vehicles and disabled one since the blockade on Iranian ports was reinstated on July 14.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Greek shipping company Dynacom Tankers reports that two oil tankers, the Malta-flagged Panamax-sized tanker Kavomaleas and Liberian-flagged crude carrier Acheloos, were attacked off the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by unknown projectiles.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims that two tankers have exploded after passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations > 2026 Iran war ceasefire > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
text: Mediators Pakistan and Qatar propose a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to revive the Islamabad Memorandum signed last month.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran is in a "full-scale war".

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The Jordanian military says air defences intercepted three Iranian missiles targeting Jordan.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The New York Times reports American soldiers were injured and several helicopters were damaged in Iranian strikes against Jordan.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military has intercepted ballistic missiles and drones entering Kuwait's airspace.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The U.S. CENTCOM completes a 10th round of strikes against Iranian military command centers, missile and drone launch sites, maritime capabilities and air defense systems.
The Israeli military says that they have killed two Islamic Jihad militants in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire.
Hamas names Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader, replacing former leader Yahya Sinwar.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Houthi-controlled Yemen declares a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia effective immediately, after accusing it of an "aggressive siege" against Yemen for nearly 12 years.

context: Sudanese civil war > Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war > Saudi Arabia–Sudan relations
text: A plane operated by Saudi Arabia's King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center arrives in Khartoum, Sudan, with aid, food, and medical supplies amidst the civil war.

context: Sudanese civil war > Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war > Sudan–United States relations
text: The United States imposes new sanctions upon the Sudanese military junta, alleging the use of chemical weapons including chlorine gas in the civil war.

context: War against the Islamic State > Iraqi insurgency
text: The Iraqi military say that they have destroyed six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk, Iraq.

context: Canada–United States relations > 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
text: U.S. president Donald Trump signs another executive order imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, including USMCA-covered products, citing alleged discriminatory trade practices. The duties take effect in 30 days, with exemptions for energy, potash, and products under sector-specific tariffs.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: The nationwide gas prices in the United States exceeds US$4 per gallon, the highest since June 17.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
text: Brent Crude oil surpasses US$90 per barrel as oil prices increase amidst the ongoing escalation, while West Texas Intermediate reaches $84.49.
Twenty people are killed, 80 others are injured and more than 100 people remain missing after heavy rains caused flash floods in eastern Afghanistan.

Twelve people are killed and 13 others are missing after a suspected methane explosion collapses part of a tunnel at a hydropower project along the Teesta River in Namchi, Sikkim, India. Rescue teams detect toxic gases while searching for those trapped.
Thousands of fish die in a canal in Sint Maarten in what officials describe as the largest fish kill in the country's history. A critical drop in oxygen levels is being blamed for the deaths.

context: Illegal drug trade in the United States, Mexican drug war
text: A federal court in New York, U.S., sentences Sinaloa Cartel co-founder El Mayo to life imprisonment and orders $15 billion in forfeiture after he pled guilty to charges related to leading the cartel.
Heavy clashes erupt between police and protesters in Bologna, Italy, after a 42-year-old Moroccan man, Abderrahim Fakir, was killed by police while being handcuffed the previous day.

Indian riot police baton-charge protesters marching toward the Parliament House in New Delhi over irregularities involving the NEET. Thousands demand education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, while Delhi Police restrict internet access and say the demonstration lacked permission.
Sir Keir Starmer resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is succeeded by Andy Burnham.
Santomean president Carlos Vila Nova wins re-election with 55.94% of the vote, while his main opposition candidate Nito Abreu comes second with 41.42% of the vote.
Nicaraguan co-president Daniel Ortega announces that the country will hold no further elections in order to "build a wall" against the political opposition.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that they have launched strikes on Amazon's data center in Bahrain.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The U.S. military confirms that a third service member, identified as 28-year-old Sgt. Angel S Rampersad of New York, was killed during a recent attack on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, bringing the total American casualties to 18.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Malta's sustainable mobility ministry confirms that the Greek-owned Malta-flagged oil tanker M/T Kavomaleas was "subject to an attack" in the Strait of Hormuz as it was navigating the southern corridor of the waterway. Additionally, all 23 crew members of the vessel are reported to be rescued.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: A tanker is attacked by Iran in the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the U.S. military conducting strikes for a 10th consecutive night yesterday, forcing crew to abandon ship. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations also confirms the attack.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich says that Israel will not join the United States in striking Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States Central Command confirms that they have launched an 11th round of strikes against Iran, against hangars and military targets such as military logistics infrastructure.

The Israeli military and Shin Bet states that senior Hamas Gaza City Brigade commander Adham Ibrahim Shaaban Nasman, who was involved in directing the October 7, 2023, attacks and taking hostages, has been killed in a Israeli airstrike in the city last weekend, despite the ongoing ceasefire.
Local medics report that 12 Palestinians, including four children, have been killed in airstrikes across Gaza City, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Two oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia, Xin Long Yang and Rodos, turn around in the Red Sea and head for the Suez Canal instead of the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb, after a warning by Houthi-controlled Yemen.
Around 21 people are reported to be killed in a drone strike by Rapid Support Forces in the Tina region of Sudan's North Darfur state near the border with Chad.

context: Communal conflicts in Nigeria > Nigerian bandit conflict
text: A survivor and local official say an armed gang abducted more than 40 people during raids on 11 villages in Maru, Zamfara State, Nigeria, over the weekend. The local government requests additional security forces.

context: Communal conflicts in Nigeria > Nigerian bandit conflict
text: Residents say motorcycle-riding gunmen killed at least 24 farmers and wounded several others in attacks on villages in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State, before stealing livestock and leaving the area.
Three women and a zonal commander are killed, while two youths are injured, as gunmen ambush a youth meeting in Omoku, Rivers State, Nigeria following a local community dispute.

context: Tariffs in the second Trump administration > 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
text: A spokesperson for Canadian infrastructure minister Gregor Robertson announces that Canada has cancelled a joint opening ceremony for the Gordie Howe International Bridge that will connect Detroit, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario, after U.S. president Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods.

context: Tariffs in the second Trump administration
text: Trump announces that imported generic drugs will remain tariff-free until August 2028, face a 100% tariff for one year, and a 200% tariff thereafter, citing efforts to move pharmaceutical production to the country.
Russia stops issuing bonds after recent auctions failed to find buyers.
In Vietnam, a fire on a bus travelling from Lâm Đồng province to Ho Chi Minh City kills seven passengers and injures five others.
The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 53. Seventy-seven others were rescued, while over 55 remain missing.
The Australian reports that Australian doctor Tareq Kamleh, who traveled to Syria to join the Islamic State, is found alive in a prison in Baghdad, Iraq.
The U.S. state of Michigan reports 6,571 cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis.

Venezuela's health ministry reports that the hantavirus killed three people in Anzoátegui, says no evidence indicates human-to-human transmission, and rejects any connection to two unexplained deaths among medical workers in Barinas.
U.S. president Donald Trump authorizes U.S. airlines to resume direct flights to Lebanon, ending a suspension imposed after the 1985 hijacking of TWA Flight 847.

Indian police detain Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi during education-reform protests in New Delhi after he called for prime minister Narendra Modi's resignation. Parliament adjourns as demonstrators demand accountability for examination scandals and education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's removal.
sources: AFP via The New Zealand Herald

text: Two American tourists are injured, including one seriously, in a stabbing attack near the Acropolis in Athens, Greece. A 60-year-old Greek man is taken into custody.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismisses commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi amid protests over the removal of defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov and appoints Joint Forces commander Mykhailo Drapatyi as Syrskyi's replacement.

context: Republican People's Party absolute nullity crisis
text: Özgür Özel, the leader of the Turkish opposition Republican People's Party, who was ousted in May by a judicial ruling, announces that he will establish a new political party.

The French Parliament approves legislation allowing limited use of acetamiprid and flupyradifurone, pesticides banned nationally but permitted in the European Union. Environment minister Monique Barbut says she will resign over the measure.
The wreckage of Pan Am Flight 526A, a Douglas DC-4 that crashed into the sea off Puerto Rico in 1952, killing 52 people, is located by a veteran aviation search team.
sources: The Dallas Express via Yahoo News

text: In association football, Chelsea sign attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for a British record transfer fee of £117 million.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: The Jordanian military reports that air defenses have intercepted 8 out of 10 projectiles fired by Iran against the country in Aqaba near the Israeli border, with two missiles landing in remote areas.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
text: The General Staff of the Kuwait Army reports that Kuwait's military and air defenses have been actively intercepting "hostile drones" from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States military launches Tomahawk missile strikes on Iran's Larak Island.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The U.S. Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran, marking the 12th consecutive day of attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Financial Times reports that the tanker Kavomalaes, belonging to Greek shipowner George Prokopiou, was "highly likely" to have been captured in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran two days earlier.

The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet announces that they have killed three Hamas militants in the northern Gaza Strip, including one in the Hamas military wing that took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Seven oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia's port of Yanbu change course away from the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb after the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports.
Amnesty International calls for an investigation into a Pakistani airstrike against a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, Afghanistan, as a possible war crime.
UNICEF reports that six people, including two children, have been killed and 30 people including children have been injured in a drone strike on a market in Al-Rahad, North Kordofan, Sudan.

A Chadian official reports that a drone attack from Sudanese territory has attacked positions in Chad, injuring civilians and destroying vehicles and several shops. The attack is the fifth in recent months, following an incursion by Rapid Support Forces last January.

Sixteen civilians, most of whom gold miners, are killed during a village attack suspected to have been perpetrated by ADF forces in Mandeite locality, Mambasa, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Five soldiers are killed and six civilians are injured in a mass shooting by ten unknown gunmen at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province, Thailand.
A 35-year-old head constable is shot and killed in a militant attack in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The Resistance Front claims responsibility.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, rise to over US$95 and $86 per barrel, respectively, and the United States average gasoline price rises to $4.06 per gallon, amidst the ongoing conflict.
Seven people are killed after a truck collides with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil.
A Robinson R44 helicopter crashes in Sincan, Ankara, Turkey, killing the pilot and injuring the co-pilot.

In the United States, West Virginia governor Patrick Morrisey declares a state of emergency and announces that 100 National Guard troops have been deployed after flash floods caused by torrential rains were reported across the state, including the northern part.
The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds 800.
African CDC director Jean Kaseya reports that the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached past 1,000.
The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000.

The fire department of Tokyo, Japan, reports 453 heat-related hospitalizations, its highest daily total since records began in 2010, as a severe heat wave kills one person and leaves four critically ill. The country's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reports at least 14 heat-related deaths nationwide over the previous week.

context: Saudi Arabia–United States relations, Nuclear program of Saudi Arabia
text: Saudi Arabia and the United States sign a civil nuclear cooperation agreement allowing Saudi Arabia to use U.S. reactor technology, enrich uranium, and reprocess nuclear waste. The pact excludes the IAEA Additional Protocol and proceeds to U.S. congressional review.

The federal trial against Hadi Matar, the man who attempted to kill author Salman Rushdie in August 2022 in New York, United States, opens. If he is convicted, Matar faces a sentence of life in prison. He is already serving a 25-year state prison sentence in New York.
Unknown gunmen open fire at a police station in Canindeyú Department, Paraguay, killing three officers and wounding another.

Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi is released after police detained him outside prime minister Narendra Modi's residence yesterday during protests demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and changes to the examination system.

Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Joseph Chang Yanfeng as the bishop of Chifeng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China under the 2018 provisional framework, which cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope reports evidence of a possible exomoon-like object orbiting the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B in the CD-35 2722 system, in a study published in the Nature journal.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
text: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) says it has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one since the naval blockade on Iran resumed on July 14.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has stopped three oil tankers from passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The Islamic Republic News Agency reports that the U.S. military struck the Shalamcheh area near the Iran–Iraq border. Two people are reported to be killed and 11 are reported injured.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The U.S. CENTCOM reports on X that they have conducted strikes against Iran for a 13th consecutive night amidst clashes over shipping routes, with explosions reported in Ahvaz, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm Island.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
text: Kuwait's defense ministry reports that a drone has hit the Abdali area near the Iraqi border.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: The Houthis claim to have attacked two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea for their violation of the blockade by Yemen's Houthi-led armed forces. There are no reported casualties.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Shipping data shows that two Chinese very-large crude carriers carrying four million ​barrels of Saudi Arabian oil, the Singaporean-flagged VLCC Xin Long Yang and Chinese-flagged VLCC Cosnew Lake, are heading towards Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Germany's defence ministry moves the Frankenthal-class minehunter Fulda and the replenishment oiler Mosel from the coast of Djibouti to the eastern Mediterranean Sea, citing uncertainty over a planned Strait of Hormuz mission and concerns about prolonged deployment affecting the vessels.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis
text: Reuters reports that Iran sent Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps officers, along with drone- and missile-related equipment, on a Mahan Air flight to Houthi-controlled Yemen on July 13, in preparation for the blockade on Saudi Arabia.

context: Sudanese civil war > 2026 Blue Nile campaign
text: Emergency lawyers report that a drone strike has killed several civilians in the Badia area of Sudan's Blue Nile State.

context: Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
text: Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, increase to over US$101 per barrel and to nearly $93 per barrel, respectively, after the escalation in the Red Sea. The United States gasoline national average increases to $4.09 per gallon.
Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signs a law banning the production and sale of foie gras, citing animal cruelty. The measure effectively ends Brazilian imports of the product.

context: Tariffs in the second Trump administration
text: The United States imposes tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners, citing forced-labor concerns. The duties take effect Friday and exempt USMCA-covered goods and products already subject to sector-specific tariffs.
More than 20,000 people are evacuated from their homes as wildfires spread in Gironde, France. More than 700 firefighters have been deployed to battle the fires.

Taylor Farms temporarily suspend operations at its processing facility in central Mexico after American health officials linked it to a current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S., which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis.

United States federal judge John R. Tunheim sentences Vance Boelter to two life terms plus 40 years without parole for killing Minnesota state representative Melissa Hortman and her husband and wounding state senator John Hoffman and his wife in June 2025.

context: International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
text: The International Criminal Court at The Hague, Netherlands, officially drops charges against former militia leader Abdallah Banda, who was previously charged for his role in a 2007 attack on African Union peacekeepers during Sudan's Darfur conflict.

The United States House of Representatives votes 214–208 to approve war powers legislation attempting to require the president of the United States to halt military action against Iran. The United States Senate votes 47–49 to stop the legislation from advancing.

The International Mathematical Union awards the 2026 Fields Medals to Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman, and Hong Wang at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. Wang becomes the third woman to receive the prize after Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014 and Maryna Viazovska in 2022.
In association football, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger submit joint bids to host the 2032 Africa Cup of Nations under the Alliance of Sahel States.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
text: Bahrain's military says that they have intercepted a number of missiles and drones from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
text: Jordan's military says that they have intercepted seven missiles and six drones launched from Iran. No casualties or damage were reported.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries > 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
text: Kuwait's army says that its air defenses confronted several attacks from Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
text: Iran says it has attacked U.S. military bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, including the Isa Air Base, using Arash drones.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis > 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
text: The U.S. military says its forces fired into a tanker's engine room and disabled the vessel after its crew repeatedly attempted to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports and ignored warnings.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The Indian embassy in Tehran reports that the Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker Disha with 28 Indian nationals on the vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. All 28 crew members were reported safe.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States strikes an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy naval academy in Ziba Kenar, Gilan province, Iran.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
text: Drones target Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, with six drones reported to be intercepted.
The Wall Street Journal reports that Bahraini and Kuwaiti fighter jets attacked military targets inside Iran earlier in July, with air and intelligence support from the United Arab Emirates.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > Gaza war
text: The Israeli military reports that the air force has struck Hamas weapon depots, weapon manufacturing sites and tunnels in the Gaza Strip, and accuses the militant group of violating the ceasefire signed in October 2025.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Israeli–Palestinian conflict > July 2026 West Bank unrest
text: Clashes in Tell, Nablus, kill four Palestinians and two Israelis after a confrontation between settlers and locals in the town. Subsequent settler attacks in the West Bank injure at least 10 Palestinians.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
text: The Houthis deny reports that they have closed the Bab-el-Mandeb and state that they are not seeking to close it, reaffirming that they have only established a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
text: Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah, Yemen, after a long hiatus in response to the movement's attacks on maritime shipping, while the militant group vows to retaliate.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war > Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries warehouses
text: A Wildberries logistic hub in Russia-occupied Crimea is hit by Ukrainian drones and catches fire.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war > Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries warehouses
text: Ukrainian drones also hit Wildberries logistics hubs in Saint Petersburg and Tver, Russia.

Ukrainian officials say a Russian ballistic missile strike on a private training ground hosting a defence-industry event in the Kyiv Oblast killed 10 people and injured nearly 100. Prosecutors investigate possible negligence in organizing the event.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: A Romanian F-16 ​fighter jet shot down a Russian Geran-2 drone near Padina, Buzău County, that had entered its airspace for the first ‌time.
The North Kordofan government reports that 15 civilians in the Burbur area south of El-Obeid, Sudan have been killed by a Rapid Support Forces drone strike.
At least 27 people are killed, including 12 militants, in an attack on a security check post in Tank District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

context: Tariffs in the second Trump administration > 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
text: The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, ceremonially opens, with Canadian officials marking the opening ceremony of the bridge with the absence of American officials amidst ongoing trade tensions.

context: Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
text: Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from twelve U.S. state attorneys general.

French authorities evacuate more than 110,000 people from Cap Ferret, Gironde, by land and sea as an uncontrolled wildfire burns over 19,000 hectares, destroys 80 homes, and threatens the peninsula’s only access road.

Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska declares a national emergency over wildfires in the Community of Madrid and the Province of Ávila, placing the Military Emergencies Unit in command. Authorities evacuate more than 10,000 people as three major fires remain uncontrolled.
The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 72.
Thirteen people are killed and two others are injured after a heavy boulder rolled down a hill and hit moving vehicles in Chamba District, India.
Five people are killed and three others are injured when a soil collapse buries a house in Hongtong County, Shanxi, China.

Oxford University reports the first volunteer that has been injected with the Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain of Ebola that is causing a outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, has spread to an additional four states: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania.
The U.S. state of Michigan surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis.
The Sudan Doctors Union reports a dengue fever outbreak in Sudan's Blue Nile state, killing 39 people and leaving 300 infected.

context: Measles resurgence in the United States
text: The U.S. CDC reports 2,318 confirmed measles cases in the country during the first seven months of 2026, marking the highest annual total since 1991.

context: International sanctions against Iran > Iran–European Union relations
text: The European Union sanctions five Iranian judges over alleged human rights violations and Ashiyane cyber group founder Nima Salehi, whom it accuses of cooperating with Iranian authorities to suppress information.

context: International sanctions against Iran > United States sanctions against Iran
text: The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions against nine firms and four people associated with sanctioned Iranian financer Babak Zanjani after attempting to evade previous sanctions.

context: International Criminal Court investigation in Venezuela
text: Venezuelan foreign minister Félix Plasencia says the country will withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged geographic bias. The ICC says it has not received formal notice and that existing investigations and cooperation obligations remain unaffected.

context: Mexico–United States relations, Mexican war on drugs
text: The U.S. state department, in coordination with the Mexican finance ministry, sanctions over 50 Mexican individuals and companies allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.

A South African court temporarily halts the parliament's impeachment inquiry into president Cyril Ramaphosa over the theft of US$580,000 from his farm, pending his challenge to a report finding possible constitutional violations.
Eight people are killed, including six children, in an arson and shooting attack at a house in Grand Haven Charter Township, Michigan, United States.
Diplomatic sources say International Criminal Court member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan following sexual misconduct allegations.

Prosecutors say thieves stole a 2,500-year-old gold Celtic necklace from the Musée du Pays Châtillonnais in Châtillon-sur-Seine, Côte-d'Or, France, after breaking its display case during opening hours. The artifact belongs to the Vix treasure.

context: Protests against the dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
text: For the ninth consecutive day, thousands continue to protest in Kyiv, Ukraine, demanding Mykhailo Fedorov's reinstatement as Minister of Defence.
Bangladeshi president Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office, citing health reasons.
Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm leave the Law and Justice party as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki.
The SpaceX Starship test flight 13, the first to successfully deploy operational Starlink satellites, successfully lands in the Indian Ocean intact.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war, Killing of health workers in the Gaza war
text: A Israeli airstrike reportedly kills a Palestinian medic at the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip.
sources: Reuters via The Times of Israel

text: An Israeli airstrike reportedly kills senior brigadier general Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the head of the Hamas police force in the North Gaza Governorate, Gaza.

The Israeli military confirms that they have killed several Hamas militants over the past few weeks, including a Nukhba forces cell commander who took part in the Kissufim massacre during the October 7, 2023 attacks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: The naval forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims to have stopped four vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: Iranian health ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reports no U.S. military strikes against Iran, after 13 consecutive nights of strikes by the U.S. Central Command against the country.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
text: The United States halts strikes against Iran after government officials reportedly saw a potential opening to resume diplomatic efforts and talks.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
text: Two people are injured by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, Houthi-controlled Yemen. A Patriot battery operated by the Greek military intercepts two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan, Saudi Arabia.

context: Russo-Ukrainian war > Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
text: Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone strike on a postal facility in Sumy has killed two people.

Darfur Joint Protection Force spokesperson Mutawakkil Ali Wakil confirms that, in coordination with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), that the joint force have retaken control of Umm Sayala, North Kordofan, Sudan, with 38 members of the Rapid Support Forces confirmed to have been killed.
The SAF and Darfur Joint Protection Force recapture Jebrat al Sheikh alongside the North Kordofan towns of Bara and Al-Baraka. Additionally, Darfur governor Minni Arko Minawi confirms the recaptures.
A fourth firefighter dies from injuries sustained in a wildfire at the Colorado–Utah border in the United States on June 27.
The death toll from the flash floods in Assam, India, rises to 62, after fourteen more fatalities are confirmed.
At least 35 people are killed and 30 others are injured when two buses collide on the Deir ez-Zor–Damascus road in Syria.
Two people are killed when a Tecnam P2010 aircraft crashes into a home in Ganderkesee, Lower Saxony, Germany.
sources: DPA via South China Morning Post

text: One person is killed and at least 22 others are injured in a five-alarm fire in Flushing, New York City, United States.

Brazil denies visas to two U.S. state department officials seeking election-related meetings in Brasília, citing risks of "political exploitation". The U.S. state department says the visit concerns electoral integrity and freedom of expression.
Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old Lebanese-German, drives into a crowd at the pride festival in Berlin, Germany, killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run.
Brazil's Liberal Party formally nominates Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro's son, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming election.

Indian education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns after protests over alleged entrance-examination leaks and broader education-system irregularities. His resignation marks the Modi government's first major concession to the demonstrations.

The Bishop of Aberdeen in Scotland declares the sedevacantist Sons of the Most Holy Redeemer religious institute, an order associated with the Society of Saint Pius X, to be excommunicated, after they consecrated a bishop without Vatican approval.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Iran war ceasefire > Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
text: Iran and the United States submit their responses to a proposal by Pakistan and Qatar to resume talks between the two countries.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has prevented six ships from transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
text: Iranian media reports that an oil tanker exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after it has hit a naval mine.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war
text: Five aid convoys from the United Arab Emirates carrying 938 tonnes of humanitarian aid arrive in Gaza as part of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3.
The Israeli military states that an Hamas unmanned aerial vehicle unit commander was killed in an airstrike yesterday in central Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Yemeni civil war > Red Sea crisis
text: Eleven vessels cross the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, according to shipping data from Kpler.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Yemeni civil war > Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
text: The Houthis shoot down a Saudi Arabian reconnaissance drone in northwest Yemen.
sources: AFP via The Times of Israel

text: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan areas of Umm Qarfa and Juraikh. The SAF also seize control of the National Export Highway which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan.
At least 30 people are killed and others are injured in an attack on a community by unknown gunmen in Kaura, Kaduna State, Nigeria.
UNESCO designates the Alamut Castle in Qazvin province, Iran, a World Heritage Site.
Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in the South China Sea along the Vietnamese coast. Forty-five people are rescued while 17 more are still missing.

Brazil recalls its ambassador to Argentina and summons Argentina's ambassador after Argentine president Javier Milei made remarks deemed derogatory about Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes at a political event in São Paulo.

context: Iran–Ukraine relations, Ukraine in the 2026 Iran war
text: The Iranian foreign ministry summons the Ukrainian chargé d'affaires in Tehran over an attack by Ukraine on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea that killed an Iranian sailor, calling it a "hostile and criminal act".

A suspect in a recent vehicle-ramming and mass stabbing attack in Berlin, identified as a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese descent, is shot and killed by police after allegedly rushing toward officers with a weapon.
Three people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting during the annual Bite of Seattle festival in Seattle, Washington, United States.
El Salvador's Nationalist Republican Alliance nominates former legislator Mayteé Iraheta for president, while the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front nominates physician Rafael Aguirre.
Expedition 74, the joint NASA–Roscosmos–ESA expedition aboard the International Space Station, ends after the Soyuz MS-28 undocks and lands on Earth in Kazakhstan.

context: 2026 Formula One World Championship > 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix
text: In auto racing, Formula One announces that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit will host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, under an agreement signed between Bahrain and Malaysia.

context: 2026 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship, Sports-related curses
text: In Gaelic football, the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship concludes with Mayo defeating Kerry in the final to end one of sport's longest-running droughts and a 75-year wait for the title.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Gaza war > Mass detentions in the Gaza war
text: Palestinian media reports that Israel has released 60 Gazan detainees back to the Gaza Strip.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet state that Hamas' internal security head Wael Musa Khaled Ladawi was killed in a airstrike in the Deir al-Balah area of the central Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire.

The IDF claim that Palestinian Islamic Jihad Nukhba militant Amro Abu Alrish and Hamas commander Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh were killed in separate strikes in Gaza, which violated the ongoing ceasefire.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
text: Iran and the United States pause strikes as the U.S. allows additional time for negotiations and Iran suspends retaliatory attacks against U.S. allies.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > 2026 Iran war > Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
text: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry reports intercepting drones fired by Iran-backed Iraqi militias from inside Iraq, which targeted oil facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia and the Riyadh area.

context: Middle Eastern crisis > Yemeni civil war > Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
